articles.title: HBO to Develop Mystery Series ‘Imposter’ From Kalos Chu, ‘Penguin’ Creator Lauren LeFranc to Produce
articles.full_text: Aug 31, 2026 9:30am PT HBO to Develop Mystery Series ‘Imposter’ From Kalos Chu, ‘Penguin’ Creator Lauren LeFranc to Produce By Joe Otterson Plus Icon Joe Otterson TV Reporter joeotterson Latest ‘Scooby-Doo’ Netflix Series Casts Andre Benjamin, Cathy Moriarty 4 days ago ‘Star Trek’ 60th Anniversary Events Include Original Series & Films Screenings, Vulcan Salute World Record Attempt (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago Penn Badgley to Lead ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ Series at Amazon 4 days ago See All Family of Kalos Chu; Maarten de Boer/BAFTA HBO is developing the dark mystery series “Imposter,” Variety has learned. The project hails from writer and executive producer Kalos Chu, with Lauren LeFranc and Rachel Jacobs executive producing via Acid and Tender, which is currently under an overall deal at HBO. “Imposter” marks the first original project developed under that deal. According to sources, “Imposter” was taken out to market in early August and generated significant interest before landing at HBO. The logline states that the show “follows an outsider entering his freshman year at an elite university.” Popular on Variety Related Stories Shannon Wallace, Curtiss Cook, Lauren E. Banks, Liv Symone, Jason Dirden Join Starz Black Rodeo Drama 'The Witcher' Co-Producer Rae Benjamin to Receive Starz #TakeTheLead Award at Humanitas Event, Presented by Russell T Davies Should “Imposter” get picked up to series, it will mark Chu’s first professional screenwriting credit. He graduated from Harvard in 2023 and has interned at multiple companies, including Lucasfilm. LeFranc is best known for developing the hit HBO limited series “The Penguin.” The show, which served as a spinoff of Matt Reeves’ “The Batman,” starred Colin Farrell, Cristin Milioti, Rhenzy Feliz, and Deirdre O’Connell. The show received 24 Emmy nominations in 2025, including best limited series and best actor, actress, and supporting actress in a limited series for Farrell, Milioti, and O’Connell respectively. It ultimately won nine awards, with Milioti picking up the win in her category. Prior to “The Penguin,” LeFranc served as showrunner on the YouTube Premium original series “Impulse.” Her other TV credits include “Agents of SHIELD,” “Chuck,” and “Hemlock Grove.” She signed her overall deal at HBO in 2025, with Jacobs joining as head of TV and film shortly thereafter. Chu is repped by Untitled and Hansen Jacobson. articles.title: ‘Tires’ Renewed for Season 4 at Netflix (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 31, 2026 9:30am PT ‘Tires’ Renewed for Season 4 at Netflix (EXCLUSIVE) By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest Ellen Pompeo to Play Disgraced ER Nurse in ‘Not a Sound’ Drama in the Works at Hulu 4 days ago J. Smith-Cameron Joins ‘Law & Order: SVU’ in Recurring Role 4 days ago ‘Furious’ Renewed for Season 2 at Hulu 4 days ago See All JESSICA KOURKOUNIS/NETFLIX © 2026 “ Tires ” keeps on rolling. The Shane Gillis sitcom has been renewed for Season 4 at Netflix, a few weeks after the third season premiered on the streamer. Hailing from co-creators Gillis, John McKeever and Steve Gerben, “Tires” follows the dysfunctional staff of auto repair chain Valley Forge. The workplace comedy started as a scrappy passion project — Gillis uploaded a pilot to YouTube in 2019 before the trio financed and produced a six-episode first season independently in Pennsylvania. Netflix picked up the show for distribution in 2024 and then renewed and funded future seasons. Related Stories Shannon Wallace, Curtiss Cook, Lauren E. Banks, Liv Symone, Jason Dirden Join Starz Black Rodeo Drama 'The Witcher' Co-Producer Rae Benjamin to Receive Starz #TakeTheLead Award at Humanitas Event, Presented by Russell T Davies “Tires” stars Gillis, Gerben Chris O’Connor, Kilah Fox, Stavros Halkias and Thomas Haden Church. Guest stars include Andrew Schulz, Jamie Lynn Sigler, Billy Magnussen, Taylor Misiak, Sofia Hasmik, Bobby Lee, Dan Soder, Rachel Blanchard, Garret Dillahunt, Anjelica Bette Fellini, Matt Walsh, Tommy Pope, Steph Tolev and H. Foley. Popular on Variety Earlier this year, Variety broke the news that Gillis and McKeever had inked a creative partnership with Netflix to develop new shows and movies. The deal also includes two new stand-up specials from Gillis. Delivering a short and sweet quote about the “Tires” renewal, Gillis said, “It’s cool to get to make another season of ‘Tires.'” McKeever was a tiny bit more expressive: “I love this show and everyone who works on it. Excited to make more.” The “Tires” renewal news comes as the comedy’s recently released third season reached No. 5 on the streamer’s Top 10 English TV list, its highest position yet. Since its 2024 debut, “Tires” has amassed more than 45 million views across three seasons. “‘Tires’ continues to deliver the unapologetic comedy and authentic point of view Shane, John and Steve’s fans know and love, and Season 3 hitting its highest-ever Top 10 ranking proves this fandom just keeps growing,” said Tracey Pakosta, Netflix’s vice president of U.S. comedy. “We love working with this team and can’t wait to see what’s next for the Valley Forge crew in Season 4.” The show is executive produced by Gillis, Gerben and McKeever; Brandon James for Rough House; Brian Stern and Kenneth Slotnick for AGI Entertainment Media & Management; and Becky Astphan. McKeever is the director, and he writes alongside Gillis, Gerben, Chris O’Connor, Amy McLeish, Bobby Telatovich, Sam Mazany, Bobby Telatovich, Amy McLeish-Milligan, Sam Mazany and Grace Cohen. Over the past few years, Gillis has become one of the biggest comedians in the world. In May, he hosted Netflix’s “The Roast of Kevin Hart,” and in July, he sold 76,212 tickets to his stadium show at Lincoln Financial Field, breaking the Guinness World Record for most tickets sold for a solo comedy show. Spider-Man: Brand New Day was in its fifth session, taking its global count to $2.33B ($1.44B int’l, $891.5M domestic), the fourth highest movie ever at the worldwide B.O., while Christopher Nolan’s Odyssey stands at $1.55B ($988.7M int’l, $563.8M domestic). Nolan’s best ever rocketed Universal across the $3B mark overseas, becoming the first studio in 2026 to do so at the foreign B.O. Triple note, the studio already became the first to cross $4 billion worldwide this year. We’re waiting on Uni’s update on their YTD global. It’s the third time that a studio crossed $3B at the international box office since 2019, and it’s the third time that Universal has achieved this milestone as a studio. Universal Pictures; Odyssey ‘s seventh global frame breaks out to $48.6M int’l, -29% from last weekend, at 83 territories, and $14.3M domestic, -27%. The Imax global weekend was $24.6M ($8M domestic, $16.6M int’l) for a running total for the exhibitor on the pic of $449M from 68 countries. China Imax alone did $5.5M this weekend for a running cume of $11.1M. Japan has still to open on Nolan’s Homer epic, that being Sept. 4. Back in the states, this weekend’s performance drove Hollywood’s TCL Chinese Theatre to the highest individual theater performance of any Imax title in history with $4.4M to date. Of note this past weekend, in Korea, The Odyssey passed Brand New Day ‘s gross to become the biggest MPA title of the year there. Weekend 4 added $11.6M with a $70.1M cume, still No. 1 and a 60% market share. Odyssey has taken over Avengers: Infinity War to become the 6th biggest MPA movie of all-time in Korea. China added a third weekend of $10.2M, No. 3 behind local titles Once Upon a Time in the Middle East and V , for a running total of $88.3M. Odyssey has now surpassed the lifetime of Inception and is Nolan’s second biggest in the Middle Kingdom behind Interstellar . That total also puts Odyssey ahead of Jurassic World: Rebirth ‘s total in China. After its sophomore frame, the Philippines is already the No. 4 horror release of all time ($5.4M cume) after a $1.1M weekend. Mexico did $2.1M to lift its cume to $7.7M, while the UK earned $1.8M to raise its cume to $6.6M. France added $1.1M for a market total of $3.3M. Jacob Elordi in ‘The Dog Stars ‘ 20th Century Studios 20th Century Studios’ Dog Stars via Disney which cost $70M to shoot and millions more in marketing was muzzled with a $19.3M global opening ($8M domestic, $11.3M int’l from 49 markets). No China release here. Disney says that within Europe, the Ridley Scott movie opened No. 4 in France ($1.5M) and UK ($1.4M), No. 5 in Italy ($800K), No. 2 Kuwait, No. 3 Bulgaria, No. 5 Finland, No. 4 Netherlands ($300K), No. 5 Norway, No. 4 Switzerland, as well as Bosnia, Croatia, Georgia, Hungary, Iceland, Iraq, Portugal, Romania, Slovenia and Ukraine. Thailand opened to No. 2 MPA, Hong Kong was No. 4 for a MPA, New Zealand and Indonesia was No. 4 for MPA, while Singapore and Malaysia opened to No. 5 for a MPA title. Within Latin America, the Jacob Elordi and Josh Brolin movie opened fifth in Mexico to $900K as well as Colombia (#5), Ecuador (#5), Central America (#5) and Paraguay (#5). Brazil brought in $300K. Paramount’s Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie did $12.7M global this weekend ($4.8M domestic, $7.9M int’l from 59 markets) for a running worldwide of $124.6M ($43.3M domestic, $81.3M overseas). Philippines opened to $115K including paid previews at 132 locations. France was the top holdover with $1.3M, -28% in weekend 4 at 890 locations with a running total just under $13M. articles.title: Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Melanie Goodfellow August 30, 2026 1:34pm Venice jury 2025 Good news. The Venice Film Festival has reinstated its jury press conference, overturning an unusual move to scrap the traditional opening event this year. The festival responded to Deadline’s inquiry on Sunday by confirming that the press conference was now on. A day earlier, the A-list festival, which kicks off on Wednesday, had told Deadline that the press conference was off due to a scheduling conflict. “The opening conference is not being held due to coinciding commitments,” a senior member of the festival’s press team wrote to Deadline Saturday. The cancellation was also confirmed by a top festival executive who noted to Deadline that, as a “remedy”, there would be a “more relaxed welcome cocktail” with some press instead. Related Stories News Venice Film Festival Scraps Jury Press Conference Festivals Nigeria Has Its First Venice Giornate Entry With Damilola Orimogunje's Family Portrait 'Dear Ajayi' -- First-Look Trailer Deadline’s report (which was flagged to the festival ahead of publication) on the matter triggered backlash, leading to the change of course by the festival. Watch on Deadline Ultimately, this is good news for the press, transparency and all those who rightly want to hear from the jury. What it shouldn’t be is an opportunity for point-scoring or denigrating anyone, least of all the press doing their job. Deadline’s questions to the festival about the jury conference had come about following the conference’s clear omission from the festival schedule, which was highly unusual. We asked multiple times why that was, but didn’t hear back. Until we insisted, and then heard back on Saturday. Maybe there was a scheduling conflict concerning the jury head or a number of jury members. It’s possible. But that would also be highly unusual given that this is a staple commitment of all A-list juries. The context here, as we laid out in our piece yesterday, is that festivals have been desperate to diminish the politically charged nature of press conferences all year. The festival has flatly denied that those were its motivations. This year’s Venice Film Festival international jury is headed by Maggie Gyllenhaal with members comprising Tunisian director and screenwriter Kaouther Ben Hania, the English composer and artist Daniel Blumberg, the Italian professor Francesco Casetti, the French director and screenwriter Xavier Giannoli, the Afghan director and screenwriter Shahrbanoo Sadat, and the Hong Kong director and producer Johnnie To. Jury press conferences have become a minefield for those on stage in recent years as journalists ask questions about their views on global politics, especially the Israel-Gaza war. At last year’s Venice jury press conference, jury head Alexander Payne admitted he was “unprepared” to answer questions about Gaza as political issues dominated. This year’s Berlin Film Festival was a highly charged edition with the opening jury press conference proving to be a flashpoint after jury president Wim Wenders said filmmakers should stay out of politics in answer to a question on the Israel-Palestine conflict. Other thorny topics likely to be on the table this Venice include the dearth of female directors in the main competition, the Iran-U.S. conflict and the Russian-Ukraine War. This festival is already shaping up to include a large dose of politics with the addition of Israel-Gaza doc NAZA and the inclusion of Russian film DAU . Last week, Nobel Prize-winning author Annie Ernaux, Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters and filmmakers including Matteo Garrone and Isabel Coixet were among signatories of an open letter urging the Venice Biennale and film festival to take “concrete action in support of Palestine.” The festival will run September 2 – 12, 2026. articles.title: Hollywood Cliffhanger: Can U.S. Summer Box Office Ring Up All-Time Record $4.8 Billion?
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony TIFF Adds Special Screening Of Zack Snyder’s Passion Project ‘The Last Photograph’ ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ & ‘Odyssey’ In Global Brawl Atop Late Summer Frame; Universal First To Cross $3B Overseas YTD – Worldwide Update Dog Eats Dog At Box Office As ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Prevails At No. 2 With $15M+, ‘Dog Stars’ Tanks; Spidey Swings Closer To $900M – Box Office Update View All August 30, 2026 3:34pm The top 4 movies of summer L to R: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day', 'The Odyssey', 'Toy Story 5' and 'Obsession' Jay Maidment/Marvel Entertainment/Columbia Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection/Melinda Sue Gordon/Universal Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection/Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection/Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection The summer domestic box office is so close — so close– to hitting an all-time record, which would surpass the $4.756 billion held by summer 2013. Currently, per Rentrak, the North American box office for the first Friday in May through EOD today stands at $4.598 billion , officially the second-highest summer ever behind 2013. If this summer is going to beat 2013’s all-time high, it has $158M to gross. If this week and next Labor Day weekend over performs, no sweat, but the estimation by some sources is that we could come up $18M-$22M short of 2013’s all-time high. Related Stories News 2026 Domestic Box Office Soars Past $7 Billion, +20% Over 2025 News Summer Domestic Box Office On A Hot Streak, Will Cross $4B By Monday This weekend saw $100M in business from all titles in U.S. and Canada according to Rentrak, +46% over the same frame a year ago. Sony/Marvel Studio’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day came in higher in its fifth No. 1 with $22.2M, while indie distributor Ketchup Entertainment posted its biggest opening ever with $15.4M in its release of Warner Bros Animation’s abandoned Looney Tunes movie, Coyote vs. Acme . That’s right where presales and tracking predicted it. The only new major studio wide entry movie next weekend is Paramount’s Mark Wahlberg crime drama, By Any Means . Look for Spider-Man to do around $18M-$20M over the 4-day holiday. Watch on Deadline Paul Dergarabedian, Rentrak’s Head of Marketplace Trends calls all this nail-biting with summer a “Hollywood Cliffhanger.” At some point in the next couple of days or sooner, Spider-Man: Brand New Day will become the second movie ever to cross $900M at the domestic box office after 2015’s Star Wars: The Force Awakens (currently the highest grossing of all-time in North America with $936.66M). The Destin Daniel Cretton directed movie reps around 20% of the summer’s entire business. If you add in Universal’s The Odyssey, which is Christopher Nolan’s highest grossing ever at $563.8M, then Spidey and Odysseus account for close to 32% of all ticket sales between the first Friday of May and today, Sunday. “No matter where the final number lands, we have to keep the calendar in mind. There are still eight days of box office to be added from Monday, August 31 through Labor Day Monday, Sept. 7, giving this year a full 130-day summer movie season. For a true apples-to-apples comparison, the first 123 days of Summer 2026 should be compared with the 123-day summer of 2013. Based on the current forecast, Summer 2026 should stand at approximately $4.612 billion through Monday, August 31, making it the second-highest-grossing 123-day summer movie season of all time,” Dergarabedian says. He further adds, “I don’t think it really matters at this point whether we beat the record. This has been such a spectacular moviegoing season that the numbers are just that and the incredible mix of films presented to audiences this year has been a game changer, not only for the industry, but for younger moviegoers.” “This could be their version of what Jaws was to audiences in 1975, Star Wars in 1977, and Raiders of the Lost Ark and E.T. in the early ’80s,” he adds, “Think about what those movies meant to audiences and how they changed the way the industry looked at the summer movie season.” Designer John Galliano Pulls Out Of Exhibit Amid Backlash ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: Your Move, Mr. Governor: CA Post Production Tax Incentive Bill Passes State Senate; Moves To Newsom’s Desk
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Tom Tapp , Dominic Patten August 30, 2026 4:31pm Gavin Newsom Tayfun Coskun/Anadolu via Getty Images State support for the contracting L.A. film and TV industry is now in the hands of California Governor Gavin Newsom and some (hoperfully) very creative accountants. With just hours to spare, the California State Senate passed SB 2319 by a vote of 33-5. The legislation creates a separate tax incentive for the post-production industry. The bill now moves on to Newsom’s desk. Related Stories News California Lawmakers Introduce Compromise For Film Industry On Corporate Tax Credit Cap News Sacramento’s Mad Legislative Dash To Fix Tax Credits SNAFU, Get Post-Production Incentive Passed, Or Not Earlier this year, state representatives talked about the post-production credit reaching up to $100 million in allocated incentives across VFX, scoring, mixing and more. That sky-high number is now more realistically envisioned at around $35 million for the first year. It has one big problem: Should Newsom sign SB 2319, there’s no funding for it. Watch on Deadline Yet, as close as the post-production credit might be to being added to the incentives program administered by the California Film Commission , the reality is there is still no actual funding in place for it. The borderline-baroque $352 billion state budget is so tightly wound with its zero-deficit demands that money for such a new credit is nowhere to be seen, no matter how hard Hollywood has advocated for it and, truth be told, desperately needs it to turn the job losses around. Should Newsom — who has aspirations to the White House — sign the bill, the state’s accounting boffins will have to find a way to fund it. The Motion Picture Editor’s Guild issued a statement praising the bill’s passing. On the corporate side of things, State lawmakers on Friday introduced a bill meant to allow studios a few key exemptions from a recently enacted restriction on corporate tax credits. AB136, introduced Friday evening, addresses concerns raised from stakeholders including the Motion Picture Association about the threat of undermining the efforts to expand California’s Film & TV Tax Credit pool to $750 million. Lawmakers have to consider legislation for 72 hours before voting. With that in mind, a vote on AB136 is likely to come Monday evening, hours before the midnight end to the legislative session. articles.title: “I’m Back”: Rams Superstar Aaron Donald Unretires, Will Rejoin Team This Season As It Vies For Super Bowl Berth
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom Dolly Parton Laid To Rest In Same Nashville Cemetery As Late Husband Your Move, Mr. Governor: CA Post Production Tax Incentive Bill Passes State Senate; Moves To Newsom’s Desk Andrea Eastman Dies: ‘Godfather’ Casting Director & Longtime Agent At ICM Was 86 View All August 30, 2026 6:41pm Aaron Donald during Super Bowl LVI in 2022 Rob Carr/Getty Images L.A. Rams fans and TV executives are both smiling today about the same thing. Aaron Donald , the all-world defensive tackle who led the Los Angeles to a Super Bowl victory in 2022, announced today that he will come out of retirement this season. The team confirmed the news by sharing a letter on Rams letterhead addressed to NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, ostensibly from Donald, which read simply, “Dear Commissioner Goodell: I’m Back.” It was signed by Donald. pic.twitter.com/G4Wc6GZVLX — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 30, 2026 DraftKings Sportsbook had the Rams as favorites to win the Super Bowl even before Donald’s announcement. The 2027 championship will be played on the Rams’ home turf at SoFi Stadium. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals NFL Films & HBO's 'Hard Knocks: Offseason' Set For 2027 Return, Replacing 'In-Season' Edition News Taylor Swift Praises The Late Great Dolly Parton's Life & Legacy: "She Was Truly The Gift That Kept On Giving" What’s more, a one-of-one defensive superstar returning to a team in the country’s second-largest media market is a boon to networks and streamers that carry NFL games. The 35-year-old Donald retired prior to the 2024 season, but announced earlier this summer that he was considering a comeback, leading to a couple of workouts with the team in August under the supervision of head coach Sean McVay. Watch on Deadline Tell a friend to tell a friend pic.twitter.com/2DruSoZSI5 — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) August 31, 2026 The Rams did not disclose details of his contract, but ESPN and the NFL Network both reported that it was a one-year, $20 million deal with playoff incentives that could raise the total value of the deal to $30 million. Donald was one of the most dominant defensive lineman in NFL history during his 10 seasons with the Rams, recording 111 sacks, 24 forced fumbles and seven fumble recoveries. He is one of three players in NFL history to have won the Associated Press NFL Defensive Player of the Year Award three times — 2017, 2018 and 2020. If Donald can even approach his previous level of play, his return could give the Rams a devastating pair of pass rushers. The team acquired reigning NFL Defensive Player of the Year Myles Garrett on June 1. Garrett, 30, set the NFL’s single-season record for sacks last year with 23, and was voted the NFL’s Defensive Player of the Year for the second time. He added a league-leading 33 tackles for loss. According to ESPN, that makes L.A. the only team with two active players who won multiple Defensive Player of the Year awards. The Rams’ Opening Night game this Thursday is against longtime NFC West rivals the San Francisco 49ers on Netflix. Donald could play, but no announcement has yet been made. articles.title: Carlos Reygadas’ Long-Awaited Movie ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Sets Sales With Mk2 Films
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’ Carlos Reygadas’ Long-Awaited Movie ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Sets Sales With Mk2 Films Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down View All August 31, 2026 2:45am Heil Jupiter! Carlos Reygadas EXCLUSIVE: Paris-based mk2 films has acquired international sales rights to Carlos Reygadas long-awaited new feature Heil Jupiter! ahead of its world premiere at the New York Film Festival in late September. The radical filmmaker’s first feature since Our Time in 2018, Heil Jupiter! is billed as “a visionary cinematic experience and a nightmarish reflection” on the resistance of love and beauty in our times, no matter how deep the darkness. The official synopsis reads: “Amidst crashing waves and monumental rocks on a distant coast, two young couples open up a realm of shifting realities. Unbeknownst to them, a mysterious entity watches from high above with Godlike judgment. Related Stories News MK2 Films Boards Yuval Abraham & Rachel Szor's Venice Doc 'NAZA' Festivals New York Film Festival Sets Revivals Lineup With Ken Russell's 'The Devils', Powell & Pressburger's 'Gone To Earth' Between these spaces exists a world balanced on the edge of the modern and the primitive, the high-tech and the rural, the corporeal and the mythic. This dreamlike astonishment is a work of feral cinematic expression, splendid in its elemental pleasures, which exist in profound and challenging contrast to its depiction of authoritarian brutality.” Watch on Deadline First announced some eight years ago under the title of Wake of Umbra , Heil Jupiter! has been shot across Poland, Portugal, Sweden, Norway, and Mexico. Giving an update on the project at the Locarno Film Festival last year, Reygadas acknowledged the duration of the production had been long but said the process of making the film had been one of “deep investigation”. Reygadas first broke through in 2002 with debut feature Japón , which garnered a Cannes Caméra d’Or Special Mention. He would go on to win the festival’s Jury Prize for Silent Light in 2007 followed by Best Director for Tenebras Lux in 2012. Our Time premiered in competition in Venice in 2018. Heil Jupiter! is produced by Cristina Velasco for Paloma Negra Films and Carlos Reygadas for No Dream, in co-production with Madants (Poland), Rosa Films (Portugal), Snowglobe (Sweden), Fat City (U.S.), Felix Culpa (U.S.), Board Cadre (Switzerland), Staer (Norway) plus Marco Perego´s Leaf Entertainment (U.S.) and Duende (U.S.). articles.title: TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser-Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender ‘Woman Unknown’ Carlos Reygadas’ Long-Awaited Movie ‘Heil Jupiter!’ Sets Sales With Mk2 Films Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down View All August 31, 2026 3:00am EXCLUSIVE: TrustNordisk has unveiled fresh deals and a teaser-trailer for May el-Toukhy ‘s post-World War II Denmark -set psychological drama Woman Unknown ahead of its world premiere in competition at the Venice Film Festival. Adding to a previously announced sale to Italy (Lucky Red), TrustNordisk has also sealed deals to Benelux (September Films), Latin America (California Filmes), Greece (Neo Films) and the Baltics (Estin Film) with more territories on the verge of being signed. Rising Danish actress Mathilde Arcel ( Second Victims ), stars as Marie, a young nanny and housemaid who is on the cusp of marrying her wealthy, older, widowed employer Christian in the immediate aftermath of the end of World War Two. Related Stories Festivals Venice Film Festival Changes Course To Reinstate Jury Press Conference: How It Went Down News Venice Film Festival Scraps Jury Press Conference Amid the jubilation, there is a darker side to the liberation as woman who fraternized with German soldiers are tracked down and publicly shamed. Marie’s secret past threatens to catch up with her, and she is forced to do everything in her power to preserve her new status as lady of the house in post-war anarchy. Arcel is joined in the cast by Carsten Bjørnlund ( The Legacy ) as the austere figure of Christian; Thorbjørn Hedegaard ( Generations ) as a dangerous, obsessive admirer from Marie’s past and Marina Bouras ( The Idiots ), as the household’s all-seeing housekeeper. Danish Egyptian director el-Toukhy is one of just two female directors in the running for the Golden Lion at Venice this year. Woman Unknown is her third feature film after Long Story Short and Queen of Hearts and continues her co-writing collaboration with screenwriter Maren Louise Käehne. “Even before the film has had its international premiere, it has been an amazing ride – this goes both in terms of festivals, but also in terms of having such a strong group of distributors on board at this early stage and several others currently in talks. We can’t wait for the premiere in Venice on Sunday, where we will for sure be even more busy,” said Susan Wendt, Managing Director at TrustNordisk. Following its Venice premiere, Woman Unknown heads to Toronto , where it will make its North American premiere in the Centrepiece sidebar, before playing in competition at the BFI London Film Festival followed by Riga International Film Festival. Woman Unknown is produced Mikael Rieks ( Land of Mine ) for Nordisk Film Production A/S in co-production with Nafta Films, Nordisk Film Production Sweden and Film i Väst. The film received the support of the Danish Film Institute, Eurimages – Council of Europe, Investment and Development Agency of Latvia, Riga City Council, Nordisk Film & TV Fund, DR, The Swedish Film Institute, SVT, LIAA, Riga Film Fund, TrustNordisk and Zentropa. Local distribution is by Nordisk Film Distribution which has set a February 4, 2027 release date in Denmark. articles.title: Producer Peter Saraf Named Chair Of NYU Tisch’s Undergraduate Film And Television Department
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Mike Fleming Jr Mike Fleming Jr Editor-At-Large @DeadlineMike More Stories By Mike Patricia Clarkson Joins Tom Hanks & Callum Turner In Sony’s ‘The Comebacker’ Netflix Buys ‘Wingmom’ Film Spec By ‘Ghosts’ Co-EP Sam Laybourne Sony’s 3000 Pictures & Temple Hill Land ‘Dolly All The Time’ With Gemma Burgess Set To Adapt View All August 31, 2026 8:00am Peter Saraf Jenae Neeson / Courtesy Sundance Institute EXCLUSIVE : New York University’s Tisch School of the Arts on Monday appointed Peter Saraf as Chair of the Undergraduate Film and Television Department. After forging a career producing such films as Little Miss Sunshine and A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood , this is new terrain for Saraf, a place he hasn’t been since he earned his bachelor’s degree as a theater major at Wesleyan University. School starts today, and so does Saraf. What he lacks in academic bona fides, Saraf brings in more than three decades of experience producing film, television and theater. In addition to being chair, he will be an associate professor in the department and will continue to shepherd his current slate of projects while developing new ones. Related Stories News Sundance Stalwarts Peter Saraf & Eddie Rubin Launch Optimistic Pictures; Awkwafina Pic 'G' Among Their Early Projects News Netflix Acquires Animated Sundance Film 'White Fang' Saraf has produced more than 35 feature films, four episodic series and several theater productions to date. Aside from Little Miss Sunshine and A Beautiful Day in the Neighborhood, his producing credits include The Farewell, Away We Go, Loving, Everything Is Illuminated, Land and Safety Not Guaranteed , as well as the series Nuclear Family, Vida and Sorry for Your Loss . He began his career working with Jonathan Demme and Edward Saxon on films including Beloved, Adaptation and Ulee’s Gold , as well as the documentaries The Agronomist and Mandela . He went on to co-found the independent producing and financing company Big Beach, which he ran for nearly two decades. Watch on Deadline Beyond his production work, Saraf has been an active leader within the industry, having served two terms as Vice President of the PGA and on the Executive Committee of the Producers Branch of the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, as well as on the operating committee of Producers United, and on the boards of directors of the Future Film Coalition and the Woodstock Film Festival. Producing has always been an uphill climb, and it has been made steeper as the business roils with cutbacks and contraction and the infiltration of AI. Saraf saw Tisch as a place to share his experience in initiating projects and seeing them through to completion. “When they called, and my first thought was, why me, I’m not an academic,” Saraf told Deadline. “One of the things that appealed to me was, if I was going to go into academia, it would be good to come at it in a leadership role. I could bring those skills that I’ve built up over the years, being a producer and my experience running companies. It made me feel I could actually do something I know how to do in a meaningful way.” The Tisch Undergraduate Film and Television Department enrolls more than 1,400 students and produces upwards of 6,000 projects each year through a hands-on, “learn by doing” curriculum. “What stood out to me in Peter’s candidacy was not only the breadth of his experience, but the quality of his leadership — collaborative, measured, and forward-looking,” said Rubén Polendo, Dean of NYU Tisch School of the Arts. “He has demonstrated an ability to bring people together across different perspectives while maintaining a clear sense of direction, and he is uniquely positioned to guide the department at this pivotal moment, and to help shape its next chapter.” “Even though I don’t come from academia, I think my experience producing and running companies has prepared me for leading this great film and TV program,” Saraf said. “When considering the job, I realized these young people are the future of the art form and business that I have devoted my professional life to and to have a hand in their development is an incredible gift. Producing is largely about recognizing talent and supporting and enabling that talent to create great work. I’ve been doing that one project at a time; at Tisch, I have the chance to do it one generation at a time.” Designer John Galliano Pulls Out Of Exhibit Amid Backlash ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age Kino Lorber Acquires ‘A Fox Under A Pink Moon,’ Oscar-Contending Doc That’s “A Diary, A Survival Story, An Artistic Manifesto” View All August 31, 2026 8:00am 'Miss Representation: Rise Up' Abramorama EXCLUSIVE: Abramorama has acquired North American distribution rights to Miss Representation: Rise Up , director Jennifer Siebel Newsom ’s examination of the “backlash against women in the age of AI, social media, and rising misogyny.” The company plans to premiere the film at IFC Center in New York City on October 22, before a rollout to theaters across North America. That will qualify the documentary for the Oscar race. Miss Representation: Rise Up , the follow-up to Newsom’s 2011 film Miss Representation , premiered in June at Tribeca Festival in New York. The new film “dives deep into the alarming mental health crisis affecting women’s agency and power,” notes a release. “With the proliferation of AI deepfakes and the online ‘manosphere,’ this new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny towards women and girls in an attempt to objectify, control, and silence them. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Documentary 'The Work In Progress' Trailer: Documentary From E.P. Robert Reich Finds Potent Way To "Help Bridge America's Deepest Divides" Acquisitions Abramorama Takes NA Rights To 'Knife: The Attempted Murder Of Salman Rushdie,' Alex Gibney Film About Author Attacked By Islamic Fanatic Abramorama “Highlighting a new generation of inspiring young women who are actively pushing back, Miss Representation: Rise Up interweaves women’s personal journeys with insights from influential voices across politics, media, technology, advocacy, and academia, including Hillary Rodham Clinton, Nancy Pelosi, Amy Klobuchar, Safiya Noble, Frances Haugen, Reshma Saujani, Jameela Jamil, Gretchen Carlson, and Jim Steyer, to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.” We have your exclusive look at the film in the trailer below. “Jennifer Siebel Newsom has spent over a decade holding up a mirror to how our culture treats women,” said Karol Martesko-Fenster, CEO of AB2 Media Group and Abramorama, and Damon G. Smith, SVP of Creative Strategy and Business Growth. “This timely and incisive film documents a troubling crisis that no one – women, parents, educators, policy makers – can afford to ignore, and introduces us to the young women meeting it head-on. We’re proud to bring this vital, galvanizing work to theaters across North America.” Photo by Cheng Xin/Getty Images The acquisition comes following news of a $17.1 billion dollar settlement of a lawsuit brought by state attorneys general that accused Meta of designing its Facebook and Instagram platforms to addict young people and damage their mental health. Newsom’s film speaks directly to harm inflicted on young women who are routinely denigrated on social media and who face constant scrutiny of their appearance and comportment through online platforms. “We’re dealing with an aggressive predator of misogyny that’s coming at young women online,” actress/activist Jameela Jamil says in the trailer. Another expert reports, “We are putting young women through the most severe mental health crisis that the country has ever experienced.” Director Jennifer Siebel Newsom Courtesy of Andrew Paynter Newsom, who is California’s First Partner, executive produced the Emmy Award-winning and Oscar-nominated The Invisible War (2012), and the Emmy Award-winning documentaries The Hunting Ground (2015) and On the Record (2020). After releasing Miss Representation in 2011, she launched The Representation Project, “a nonprofit organization that uses film, media, and education as catalysts for cultural transformation.” “When I made my first documentary Miss Representation 15 years ago, I wanted my daughter and girls in her generation to use their voices and stand in their power as rightful leaders,” Newsom said in a statement. “Unfortunately, amidst progress for women and girls came extreme backlash. Technology is the newest and most powerful cultural communicator of our time – and it is being weaponized at an unprecedented scale to silence women and girls.” ‘Miss Representation: Rise Up’ Abramorama Newsom continued, “I hope Miss Representation: Rise Up continues to inspire women and girls to use their voice and stand in their power, just as I hope the film encourages boys and men to value women and girls and ensure we all have seats at decision-making tables. Abramorama understands the urgency of getting this story in front of as many people as possible. We are honored to partner with them.” Abramorama and The Representation Project present Miss Representation: Rise Up . Executive producers: Melinda French Gates & Pivotal, Melony & Adam Lewis, Aileen Getty Foundation, Susie Thompkins Buell, Harnisch Foundation, Minderoo Pictures, Jackie Zehner, Maureen Pelton & Charlie Hartwell, Patricia Arquette, Hadley Mullin, Emily Liu Foy, Brenda Robinson, and Barbara Bridges. Original music by Laura Karpman, with cinematography by Mario Furloni. Jessica Congdon and Jennifer Steinman Sternin edited the film. Miss Representation: Rise Up is written and produced by Camille Servan-Schreiber, Gretchen Miller, and Jennifer Siebel Newsom. articles.title: Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age Kino Lorber Acquires ‘A Fox Under A Pink Moon,’ Oscar-Contending Doc That’s “A Diary, A Survival Story, An Artistic Manifesto” View All August 31, 2026 8:00am Documentary filmmakers set for the 2026 Points North Institute Artist Programs Points North Institute EXCLUSIVE: Documentary artists confronting media consolidation, a tightened acquisition market and other challenges are about to get a major lift from the Points North Institute , the nonprofit that puts on the Camden International Film Festival in Maine. On Monday, the institute announced its 2026 Artist Programs, a slate of pitching events, residencies, curated meetings and more that will support talented artists from diverse backgrounds. Prominent mentors, funders, and collaborators will be on hand to work with 40 teams across 27 countries who have documentary projects in development. “Three-quarters of the supported projects are directed or co-directed by filmmakers of color and 60% by women or non-binary filmmakers,” the institute said. Related Stories Documentary 22nd Camden Film Festival To Showcase New Work By Documentary's Leading Lights: Gibney, Kopple, Oppenheimer, Chin, Vasarhelyi, Poitras & More Documentary Ellis-Beauregard Foundation And Points North Institute Announce Major New Award For Documentary Filmmakers PNI also announced details of its annual Points North Forum that “will gather filmmakers and industry leaders for intimate, forward-looking conversations at a moment of profound change.” Several Forum sessions will address the state of public media, which saw deep funding cuts last year pushed by Pres. Trump and passed by the Republican-controlled Congress. Watch on Deadline Both the Artist Programs and the Points North Forum run in tandem with the Camden International Film Festival, set to unfold from Sept. 17-20 in the bucolic towns of Camden and Rockland in Maine’s mid-coast region. Scroll for details on the Artist Programs and Forum. “When so much of the infrastructure that has historically served independent filmmakers is being dismantled,” observed Sean Flynn , artistic director and co-founder of the Points North Institute, “it is more important than ever to create spaces where artists can find the time, resources, and community they need to bring their visions to life. It is an honor to support their journeys and convene the field to imagine and build more durable, abundant systems that will expand the horizons of the documentary form.” Artist Programs Highlights —The 17th annual Points North Pitch , part of the Points North Fellowship and one of North America’s leading documentary pitching forums, will see six feature docs in progress pitching to a panel of funders, producers and executives. Selected filmmakers will be mentored by Sundance Institute ’s Kristin Feeley and program alum Assia Boundaoui . —The second cohort of Diane Weyermann Fellows will gather for their final creative retreat. The program supports three director-producer teams with $100,000 unrestricted grants – one of the largest funds in the US – and an 18-month collaborative fellowship. Advisors include Tabitha Jackson , Kirsten Johnson and Andrea Meditch . —Additional programs include the LEF/CIFF Fellowship , supporting New England-based filmmakers working on feature documentaries, and the year-long 4th World Media Lab, which supports early- and mid-career Indigenous filmmakers from across Turtle Island, in partnership with Big Sky Documentary Festival and Seattle International Film Festival . —Points North will host cohorts from the BAVC MediaMaker Fellowship , CAAM’s Building Bridges Grantees, and the Disabled Nonfiction Producer Apprenticeship run by FWD-DOC and Multitude Films. The festival will serve as the kickoff for the second cycle of a collaboration between American Documentary | POV, Chicken & Egg Films, TIME Studios and Bird Street Productions focused on short documentaries. This cycle’s cohort includes Sierra Ulrich ( Dad Hair ) , Kristine Stolakis ( Hard Labor ), and Alyse Shorland ( Write Me a Letter ) . —Filmmakers will have access to 400+ curated meetings with more than 100 industry professionals through Points North’s 1:1 Meetings , including representatives from Sundance Institute, Hulu, Watermelon Pictures, Chicken & Egg Films, and The New York Times HIghlights From Points North Forum (sponsored by ESPN Films): — Memory Work: Activating Black Archives creates a dialogue between two CIFF selections, Once Upon a Time in Harlem and Windows of Time , and Harvard Black Film Project’s Jackie Glover exploring the significance of community-driven archival practices in the context of the federal government’s erasure and revision of Black histories. —Three sessions take up the current state of public media: *In Field Briefing: Public Interest Media at Risk , Maggie Bowman presents the findings of a new report commissioned by the Ford Foundation, which documents approximately $45 million in direct federal investment in public-interest documentary eliminated by the cuts of 2025. *In Public Media Metamorphosis, executives from FRONTLINE , American Documentary , WXXI and NPR Studios describe how their organizations are expanding into digital distribution as the traditional broadcast model is disrupted. *The Forum closes on Sunday with a regional strategy session convened with Future Film Coalition and the Maine Film Association , asking what it would take to build a more durable media ecosystem in New England. —Magnum photographer Alessandra Sanguinetti , director of the CIFF opener and Locarno winning The Illusion of an Everlasting Summer , will discuss her artistic practice with Cinema Tropical’s Carlos A. Gutiérrez . —Festival alum Keith Wilson brings the fourth episode of Pleased to Announce , his live documentary performance on the financial and emotional costs of awards campaigns, following presentations at CPH:DOX, Cannes and DC/DOX. —Finally, the 5th edition of Points North’s Documentary Town Hall , moderated by Beadie Finzi , will explore how documentary filmmakers and their allies can respond to this moment of uncertainty with vision, ambition and deeper collaboration, building new models for connecting independent work with audiences. Further details about 2026 Points North Institute Artist Programs : Points North Fellowship The Points North Fellowship supports six filmmaking teams as they develop their pitches and publicly present their documentary features-in-progress to a panel of funders and distributors at CIFF’s popular Points North Pitch. Points North’s Executive Director, Elise McCave , will moderate the event. Confirmed pitch panelists include Andrea Alarcón , Sundance Institute; Opal H. Bennett , American Documentary | POV; Daniel J. Chalfen , Naked Edge Films; Nikki Heyman, Doc Society; Eric Hynes , Jacob Burns Film Center; Kiyoko McCrae , Chicken & EggFilms; Anya Rous, Multitude Films; and Paulina Suarez, Ford Foundation. The program’s mentors are Assia Boundaoui , Kristin Feeley, and Andrea Meditch . The program is made possible by sponsorship from the deNovo Initiative. Points North Fellowship Projects Choreography of a Tyrant (France, Syria, USA, Norway, Qatar) Directed by Qutaiba Barhamji. Produced by Anne-Catherine Witt and co-produced by Nesa Azimi. After discovering 14 censored frames showing Hafez al-Assad chasing a fly, a filmmaker investigates how authoritarian power constructs sacred images and how a single flaw can unravel a carefully engineered myth. Hen House (USA) Directed by Julia Rosenheim. Produced by Karen Gaytán & Jazz Szympruch. In Springdale, Arkansas, immigrant poultry workers endure dangerous conditions in silence—until an organizer invites them to turn their experiences into theater. As performing begins to transform how they see themselves, immigration crackdowns force them to decide whether they can afford to keep going. Kamnop: A Treasure is Waiting for You (USA, France, Cambodia, Spain) Directed by Kanitha Heng Snow & Guillermo Roques. Produced by Christian Popp. Kamnop is an exhilarating and transformative road trip, where a mother and daughter travel from Colorado to Cambodia in search of a long-lost treasure, buried during the first days of the Khmer Rouge genocide. Oh Heart, Don’t Be Afraid (Georgia, France, Germany) Directed and produced by Ana Kvichidze. Produced by Mariam Bitsadze, Valerianne Boue and Natalia Imaz. Dachi is a queer person (they/them) from a religious place in Georgia, oppressed by the Archbishop, religious society and even their own family. They find an old witch, taught and empowered with her magic spells and they begin to change reality. Shape of Silence (Canada) Directed and produced by Varun Trikha. Amid changing forests, a blind Polish linguist searches for sounds she believes can express what human language cannot. Untitled Alamo Reenactment Project (USA) Directed by César Martínez Barba. Produced by Henry Kinder & Sean Weiner. Untitled Alamo Reenactment Project explores the construction of the Alamo story. From the voices of reenactors to the ghostly presence of Mexican “soldados” haunting San Antonio, the hybrid film examines how this narrative shapes the landscape of today. 4th World Media Lab Now in its eleventh year, the 4th World Media Lab continues to serve as a vital space for emerging and mid-career Indigenous filmmakers to develop their craft, strengthen their networks and advance projects rooted in cultural integrity and community care. This year’s cohort gathers five visionary artists from across Turtle Island and Pasifika, whose work reflects both artistic rigor and deep relational accountability. The program’s mentors include Yvonne Russo , Tracy Rector , Chris Newell and guest artist Paige Bethmann. The 4th World Media Lab Fellows Noelani Kanuha Auguston is a member of Shx ̌ whá:y Village, with Nooksack and Hawaiian heritage. A wife and mother of two young boys, she and her husband are raising their family in their homelands along the Nooksack River. She earned her BA from the University of Washington and, guided by a deep love of storytelling, went on to earn her MFA in creative writing with a focus in screenwriting from the Institute of American Indian Arts. Noelani currently writes and produces for Children of the Setting Sun Productions. Her work is rooted in an authentic Indigenous worldview, with a particular focus on the peoples of the Salish Sea. She is driven by a commitment to creating hopeful, transformative representations of Native life, especially for youth, offering characters and stories that reflect strength, possibility and self-recognition. Quannah ChasingHorse is a Han Gwich’in and Sicangu/Oglala Lakota land protector and fashion model from Eagle Village, Alaska, and the tribes of South Dakota. Quannah is a fourth-generation land protector; her deep connection to her homelands and her people’s way of life is her grounding and guiding force. She gained prominence through a 2020 Calvin Klein campaign and has since worked with the top global fashion houses; won countless awards; starred in Reservation Dogs and Thin Places ; and graced the covers of numerous magazines, including Vogue , Elle and Harper’s Bazaar . Quannah’s short film, Walking Two Worlds , won awards and streams on The North Face’s channels. Amid Quannah’s accomplishments, her most important work is using her platform to uphold and uplift her Indigenous values and peoples. Montana Cypress is a Los Angeles-based playwright, filmmaker and actor. Originally from the Miccosukee Tribe located in South Florida, he has studied acting at New York Film Academy, the British Academy of Dramatic Acting, and UCLA’s Professional Acting Program. He is a three-time winner of the Von Marie Atchley Excellence in Playwriting Award; winner of Best Native American Directed Short at Phoenix Film Festival; had a full-length comedy stageplay, AChristmas In Ochopee , premiere in Minneapolis, produced by New Native Theatre; and his documentary about alligator wrestling, The Art of Gator Wrestling , can be viewed on PBS North’s YouTube channel. Montana recently played Chief Bromden in the stage adaptation of One Flew Over the Cuckoo’s Nest at the Gainesville Playhouse. He can also be seen in the film Young Washington , released in theaters in July 2026. Banchi Hanuse works across film and radio as a co-founder of Nuxalk Radio, supporting Nuxalk language revitalization, upholding Nuxalk Nationhood and advocating for stewardship of Nuxalk homelands. She directed her first feature documentary, Aitamaako’tamisskapi Natosi: Before the Sun , in 2023. Most recently, Banchi premiered her second feature film, Ceremony , at SXSW in 2026, where it garnered the Documentary Spotlight Audience Award. Lokotah Sanborn is an interdisciplinary artist and filmmaker from the Penobscot Nation Reservation. Lokotah works for Sunlight Media Collective, documenting stories at the intersection of Wabanaki sovereignty and environmental justice. From 2023-25, his video work featured in the traveling exhibition Exploding Native Inevitable , which toured the U.S. He received the Lunder Institute Fellowship (Colby College) and North Star Fellowship (Points North Institute) in 2024 and the David C. Driskell Fellowship (Indigo Arts Alliance) in 2025. His directorial debut, Otherworld , made in collaboration with Odanak Abenaki writer and composer Mali Obomsawin, premiered at BlackStar in August 2025. He co-directed the short Wabanaki Voices in Recovery with Mi’kmaq filmmaker Jared Lank, produced by Points North Institute. His artwork was featured in the MET’s unsanctioned exhibition Encoded , and he won two 2025 Webby Awards. Lokotah is developing his first feature-length documentary. LEF/CIFF Fellowship Points North’s long-standing commitment to supporting regional filmmakers is evident in theLEF/CIFF Fellowship. This program, developed in partnership with the LEF Foundation, offers five New England–based filmmakers with feature documentaries in production or post-production the opportunity to attend CIFF for project development workshops and industry meetings. The LEF/CIFF Fellowship cohort will be mentored by filmmaker Todd Chandler. LEF/CIFF Projects Ancestral Days (USA, Italy) Directed by Bronte Stahl. Produced by Isabella Rinaldi. Francesco leads personalized ancestral tours in Sicily for Americans in search of their roots. Among the bureaucratic, parochial, pastoral and familial spaces his work takes his clients, a reflection on roots, gentrification and the act of remaining emerges. Feu de Lune (Côte d’Ivoire) Directed by Dominic Yarabe. Produced by Eliza Soros, Natalia Almada, Pamela Martinez and Carlo Nasisse. Bobia, a rural village in Côte d’Ivoire, keeps a buried secret. The war has one memory, and it is three generations long. In a place where history was never written down, the memory of this largely erased civil war survives through children’s dreams, adult silences and a mother’s nightly bedtime stories. Patrimony (USA) Directed by Musa Syeed. Produced by Razi Jafri. Dr. Syeed is a retired leader of the Muslim community, a diehard optimist and, at 80, he’s losing his memory and his voice. He’s desperate to find someone to document his eventful life, from serving time as a political prisoner in Kashmir to his pioneering interfaith work in America. But the best he can find is a reluctant, cynical filmmaker who happens to be his youngest son: me. Someone’s Father (USA, Colombia) Directed by Andrea Patiño Contreras. Produced by Gabriela Díaz Arp. Amidst her father’s terminal cancer, a filmmaker interrogates the origins of a family heirloom: a tsantsa, or shrunken human head, acquired by her grandfather in the 1940s. As her father reckons with the question of where to rest his own body, the filmmaker wonders whether the tsantsa deserves the same. Topology of a House (Hong Kong) Directed by Kai Luo. Produced by Sol Ye. After the property crisis cuts off family support, a filmmaker returns from the US to find his home demolished by a bankrupt father who once shaped Shenzhen’s skyline. Drifting in a city in economic retreat, he searches for the meaning of making a family film amid the family’s collapse. Diane Weyermann Fellowship The Diane Weyermann Fellowship at Points North was established to honor the legacy of Diane Weyermann , a prolific producer and pillar of the nonfiction filmmaking community. The Fellowship identifies three advanced career directors and producers working on creatively expansive, cinematic feature-length documentaries that address poignant and urgent themes of our time. The 18-month program is one of the most robust artist development initiatives for documentary filmmakers offered by a U.S.-based organization. The Diane Weyermann Fellowshipprovides $100,000 in unrestricted funding for each project, as well as two creative retreats. The program is tailored to the needs of each film team, giving each project team a creative space to explore and expand possibilities for their films and careers. The Diane Weyermann Fellowship was developed by Points North in partnership with Participant Media and is made possible by seed funding from the Skoll Foundation and major support from the RandomGood Foundation , Ford Foundation’s JustFilms and over 200 individual supporters. The cohort will be joined on their final retreat by creative advisors Kirsten Johnson, Andrea Meditch and Tabitha Jackson . The 2025-2026 Weyermann Fellowship projects and artists follow: Captions Will Be Needed (USA, Mexico) Directed by Natalia Almada. Produced by Esther Robinson and Josh Penn. Captions Will be Needed is filmmaker Natalia Almada’s cinematic response to living with a rare cancer that has reconfigured her relationship to time. Testimony (Australia) Directed and produced by Maya Newell. Produced by Alex Kelly, Larissa Behrendt AO, Sophie Hyde and Lisa Sherrard. As the climate emergency rises before them, Torres Strait Islanders too rise up, suing the government for failing to prevent climate harm. While the court can only hold part of the story, we dance, remember and dream of possible futures with Saibai and her people. This film is their testimony. The Instrument (USA) Directed by Zac Manuel. Produced by Darcy McKinnon. An aging jazz singer sets out with his filmmaker son to use artificial intelligence to resurrect the voice of his late father. articles.title: Barunson E&A Boards ‘Satan’s Slaves: Origin’; Franchise Prequel Billed As Joko Anwar’s Most Ambitious Production
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Rashaana Shah & Manasi Parekh Join $10M AIF Media Fund; Initial Slate Headed By Rick Moody Adaptation ‘Purple America’ Lionsgate Strikes Promotional Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program View All August 31, 2026 8:00am Satan's Slaves: Origin Rapi Films Barunson E&A, the Korean studio behind Bong Joon Ho’s Oscar-winning Parasite , has boarded worldwide sales on Satan’s Slaves: Origin , the latest addition to the blockbuster horror franchise directed by Indonesian filmmaker Joko Anwar . The company will launch the project, which it is billing as “one of the most ambitious genre productions to come out of Southeast Asia”, to international buyers at the inaugural TIFF Market this September. Written and directed by Anwar, Satan’s Slaves: Origin is produced by Rapi Films, in co-production with Anwar’s Come and See Pictures, Sky Media and Legacy Pictures. Related Stories News TrustNordisk Unveils Fresh Deals & Teaser Trailer For Venice Contender 'Woman Unknown' News Alma Har'el's Family Drama 'Wet' Heading To TIFF Market With 193; A-List Cast Circling The film is currently in pre-production and targeting a 2027 theatrical release in Indonesia. Watch on Deadline It marks Anwar’s most ambitious production to date, unfolding across two continents and told in seven languages including Indonesian, Alsatian, Portuguese, Javanese, Dutch, Turkish and Latin. Anwar’s reboot of Rapi Films’ 1980 Indonesian cult classic of the same name started in 2017 with Satan’s Slaves , which became Indonesia’s highest-grossing local film of the year and kickstarted the country’s horror boom. Its sequel, Satan’s Slaves: Communion , became the first Indonesian feature released in IMAX and ranks among the top six highest-grossing local films of all time in Indonesia. The third installment in the franchise, Satan’s Slaves: Origin , is built as a standalone prequel, tracing the origins of the cult and demonic pact that set the first two films in motion. It begins with a mysterious mass hysteria gripping 16th-century Strasbourg – inspired by a real-life incident in 1518 – before arriving at a haunted lighthouse on the southern coast of 17th-century Java, expanding the mythology beyond anything the franchise has attempted before. Anwar also recently directed horror comedy Ghost In The Cell , which premiered at Berlin film festival and is currently the second highest-grossing film of the year at Indonesia’s box office with more than 3.3 million admissions. The film, which is also part of Anwar and Barunson E&A’s two-year exclusive partnership, has been sold to 150 territories worldwide, including Plaion for German rights and Well Go USA for North America. Commenting on Satan’s Slaves: Origins , Anwar said: “This film is everything I didn’t know I was building toward – the one that finally answers where the curse came from, why it never stopped, and what it’s really after. Longtime fans are going to get the answers they’ve waited years for. Newcomers are going to get the ride of their lives.” Yoonhee Choi, CEO of Barunson E&A, said: “Every time we work with Joko Anwar, the scale gets bigger and the ambition gets sharper. Satan’s Slaves: Origin is unlike anything he’s made – a story that moves across centuries and continents. It’s proof of what we’ve believed for years: Indonesian filmmakers are telling some of the boldest genre stories in the world right now, and we’re proud to help this one reach it.” Barunson E&A’s pan-Asian slate also includes Thai horror Inherit from Banjong Pisanthanakun, produced by Thailand’s GDH 559 and selected for this year’s Toronto International Film Festival; Indonesian zombie-apocalypse blockbuster Zona Merah: Dead City ; and Korean occult mystery Stoneborn , from the team behind Exhuma . articles.title: Watch ‘One In A Million’ Trailer, Oscar Contender That Follows Incredible Journey Of Syrian Girl Across Tumultuous Decade
articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Points North Institute Announces 2026 Artist Programs And Points North Forum Ahead of Camden Film Festival Abramorama Acquires ‘Miss Represenation: Rise Up,’ Jennifer Siebel Newsom Documentary About Backlash Against Women In Social Media Age Kino Lorber Acquires ‘A Fox Under A Pink Moon,’ Oscar-Contending Doc That’s “A Diary, A Survival Story, An Artistic Manifesto” View All August 31, 2026 9:00am EXCLUSIVE: The sparkling personality of Israa lights up One in a Million , the Oscar-contending documentary that won two awards at Sundance, including the directing award for Itab Azzam and Jack Macinnes . The film from Frontline Features , PBS Distribution, and BBC Storyville follows Israa from the age of 11 until 21, a decade in which she fled the decimated Aleppo, Syria of her birth, arrived with her family in Turkey, then eventually made it to Germany as one of a million Syrian refugees admitted to that country. The odyssey, which involved incredible peril on the Mediterranean in an inflatable raft, and a brutal journey on foot through Eastern Europe, might remind one of a certain hero from Greek myth (and indeed a mooring on the Greek Island of Samos became a critical stop along the way). Related Stories Documentary DOC NYC Set To Honor Documentary Visionaries Alex Gibney, JT Takagi, Stephen Maing, And Raney Aronson-Rath Documentary Award-Winning 'One In A Million' Makes European Premiere At Thessaloniki Doc Fest Ahead Of CPH:DOX Bow We can share the first trailer for the film above, ahead of the film’s theatrical release in October. Watch on Deadline Israa in ‘One in a Million’ Frontline Features/BBC Storyville After the fall of the Assad regime in Syria, Israa like other Syrian exiles could weigh whether to return. For Israa the decision involved a reckoning with the opportunities afforded in Germany but a lingering sense that true fulfillment might be found back home. “Co-directors Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes bring a palpable blend of sensitivity and nuance to their portrayal of the Syrian refugee Israa and her loved ones, following them across time, borders, and shifting circumstances,” the Sundance program wrote. “It is clear that the filmmakers fully realize the weight of the trust and privilege that comes with undertaking a longitudinal project: to witness the experiences, challenges, and quiet joys of a remarkably resilient family forced to leave their beloved Aleppo.” Frontline Features/BBC Storyville Co-director Itab Azzam is a Syrian native herself. She and MacInness, her filmmaking and life partner, were living in Damascus in 2011 when Syria’s civil war broke out. “We left for London in August of that year planning to return a few months later, but that day never came,” they write in a directors’ statement. “Four years later in 2015, we met Israa selling cigarettes on a street corner in Turkey, as she and her family had just arrived from the devastation of Aleppo. Defiant and brimming with joy, despite the horror around her, we instantly fell in love with her – and felt that her story demanded telling… We knew we wanted to stay in her life. That was when the idea for One in a Million was born.” Directors Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes attend the 2026 Sundance Film Festival Awards Ceremony on January 30, 2026 in Park City, Utah. Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images One in a Million is directed and produced by Itab Azzam and Jack Macinnes and produced by Oscar winner Raney Aronson-Rath ( 20 Day in Mariupol ), Will Anderson, James Bluemel, and Andrew Palmer. Executive producers include David Fialkow and Nina Sing Fialkow, Harriet Gugenheim, Lucie Kon, Jutta Krug, Adam Lewis, Melony Lewis, Patty Quillin, Patty Quillin, and Joseph Schull. articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Your Move, Mr. Governor: CA Post Production Tax Incentive Bill Passes State Senate; Moves To Newsom’s Desk AI Slop Showdown Over Tung Tung Sahur & Italian Brainrot May Offer Glimpse At Hollywood’s Future Jeanie Buss Plays Offense With Her Selling Siblings In Order To Keep Lakers Stake View All August 31, 2026 9:03am Argentina's Lionel Messi celebrates with teammates after their July 7 3-2 victory over Egypt to advance to the World Cup 2026 quarterfinals Justin Setterfield/Getty Images Two days after scoring a stunning four goals in Inter Miami’s 7-1 victory over CF Montreal, Lionel Messi announced Monday that he is retiring from international play. “Now that some time has passed since the final, having thought it over carefully, I want to tell you all that I am retiring from the national team,” he said Monday. In a post, the 2022 World Cup champion made his long anticipated second exit from the national team official. “Time is running short, chapters come to a close, and this is one that hurts me deeply,” Messi wrote six weeks after his Argentina were defeated 1-0 in overtime at the 2026 World Cup Final by Spain. “I love, have loved, and will always love being part of the national team,” he added. Messi had previously retired from playing for Argentina in 2016, but un-retired in time for the 2018 World Cup, where the team was booted out of the Round 16 by France (who went on to win the Final that year). Related Stories Casting 'Doc' Adds Barrett Carnahan, Raffa Virago, Cecilia Lee & Kolton Stewart To Season 3 Cast News Kevin Macdonald On Capturing Pep Guardiola For Prime Video's 'A Beautiful Obsession': "Like Having Robert De Niro Play A Football Coach" View this post on Instagram Playing it forward, the 39-year-old Miami captain continued: “I’ve given it my all, I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some really great young players coming through behind me who deserve their chance.” Watch on Deadline Messi was also the leader of Argentina’s national team this year in what was his sixth appearance at a World Cup. Stunning fans globally and in stadiums this past summer on the Fox broadcast competition with eight goals and four assists after 15 years leading the South American team, Messi became the all-time World Cup goal scorer for a short-time during the tournament. Ultimately, like the World Cup trophy itself, that title was denied to him as France’s Kylian Mbappe moved into the top spot with 22 goals. “The pain is immense and it’s going to take a long time for this wound to heal,” Messi wrote online soon after the loss to Spain, a loss that was further stained by surly and violent behavior by his teammates after the match itself. In addition to what was going on in the World Cup, Messi’s father was ill during the tournament. A close advisor to his record breaking son, Jorge Messi died on August 8 at the age of 68. With his $75 million annual current contract set to run to the end of the 2028 season, Lionel Messi will continue to play for the Florida-based and partially David Beckham-owned team. articles.full_text: Continue to Deadline SKIP AD You will be redirected back to your article in seconds Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Kenan Thompson To Fill In For Simon Cowell As Guest Judge On ‘America’s Got Talent’ ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” ‘Manifest’ Spinoff ‘Arrivals’ Ordered By Netflix View All August 31, 2026 9:30am Kalos Chu and Lauren LeFranc Courtesy/Getty From an assistant desk to a premium HBO development deal: thousands of aspiring writers dream of making that leap. For one, Kalos Chu — who serendipitously works at DreamWorks Animation — that dream became a reality. After a bidding war for his spec Imposter , which started with 10 offers before the field was narrowed down to a three-way battle between HBO, Netflix and Amazon, the drama project landed at HBO for development with an option for a writers room to follow. The Penguin creator/showrunner Lauren LeFranc will executive produce via her banner Acid and Tender Productions under her overall deal at HBO, with her head of TV and fill Rachel Jacobs also exec producing. Related Stories News Everything We Know About 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 So Far Cancellations and Renewals NFL Films & HBO's 'Hard Knocks: Offseason' Set For 2027 Return, Replacing 'In-Season' Edition Written and executive produced by Chu, Imposter is a dark mystery that follows an outsider entering his freshman year at an elite university. Watch on Deadline This is the first writing credit for Chu, a 2023 Harvard graduate with a BA degree in English. “After graduation, I hope to pursue a career in screenwriting — a passion that has developed, in large part, due to my experience in the English department,” he wrote in a 2023 essay about his college tenure. While Imposter makes Chu’s Hollywood writing debut, he had been preparing for it for years. Starting in fall 2020, Chu did a string of stints as a development intern, at Atlas Entertainment, Voltage Pictures, Day Zero Productions, Nickelodeon Animation and DreamWorks Animation. In summer 2022, he interned in physical production at Lucasfilm, to, as he put it in the 2023 essay, address gaps in his filmmaking knowledge of how, exactly, a movie is made and “the practical constraints that screenwriters must grapple with.” A year after graduation, Chu got a job as a feature development assistant at DreamWorks Animation where he has been for the past two years, writing Imposter i n his spare time. With the script selling, Chu will be leaving his DWA job and is currently helping find a replacement. As of now, he doesn’t have an agent; that will likely change soon, too. Paramount has set a June 2, 2028, release date for the follow-up to the 1990 movie, which will also be filmed for Imax and released in theaters in Dolby Cinema, 4DX and premium large formats.
