articles.title: Met Gala Organizers Reportedly Mulling Date Change Amid John Galliano Backlash
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All August 29, 2026 10:56am John Galliano Kevin Tachman/MG19/Getty Images for The Met Museum/Vogue Organizers of the Met Gala are reportedly considering changing the date of the 2027 event amid growing backlash over plans to honor John Galliano. In July, the Metropolitan Museum of Art announced that Galliano’s work would be spotlighted in the Met’s Costume Institute. This exhibition serves as the centerpiece for the annual Met Gala , an event attended by the most elite of the A-list, with one of the most coveted invites. This would make him the third living designer to receive a solo exhibition at the Met, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo in 2017. Related Stories Lifestyle Anna Wintour Wanted the Bezos Back. But She Might Settle for the Clooneys Lifestyle Fashion Keeps Debating John Galliano. It's Ignoring Its Jewish History. At the time, it was announced that the exhibit would feature all the highs and lows, including his antisemitic rant. Galliano is credited with growing luxury-fashion brand Dior into a global giant. However, he was fired by the company in 2011 after video footage surfaced showing the designer, who was inebriated, making antisemitic remarks in a Paris café. Galliano retreated from public life for two years and was found guilty by a Paris court of public insults based on religion, race and ethnicity. He received a fine and was forced to pay damages and court fees. Galliano met with Jewish leaders and rabbis following the scandal and received blessings from groups like the Anti-Defamation League. The exhibit is scheduled to kick off May 3 with the Met Gala, which is overseen by Anna Wintour , Vogue’s global editorial director who also serves as a Met trustee. However, a growing number of voices are criticizing the plan to honor Galliano. According to The New York Times , criticism has grown stronger. “In recent days, opposition to the museum’s plan to honor Galliano has grown among Jewish leaders in New York and beyond,” The Times reported. “Donors have contacted Met executives and threatened to rescind gifts to the museum if the exhibition moves forward as planned.” As a result, Met trustees and board members “have been scrambling to do damage control,” The Times reported. This includes possibly moving the date of the Met Gala, which is always held the first Monday in May, to the following week. The current date of May 3 also happens to be Yom HaShoah, also known as Holocaust and Heroism Remembrance Day, The Times noted. Last week, New York City Council speaker Julie Menin posted a letter to Wintour, Costume Institute curator Andrew Bolton and Met director Max Hollein, saying the decision to honor Galliano was “a serious mistake.” While noting that his influence in the fashion world has been “enormous” and “unquestionable,” Menin added that she had “deep concern” about the decision to honor Galliano. “Mr. Galliano’s long public record of antisemitism, racism and anti-Asian bigotry is deeply troubling,” Menin wrote. “His conduct was repeated and significant. He was criminally convicted in France for racist and antisemitic public insults. He was also captured on video praising Adolf Hitler and telling others that their ancestors would have been ‘gassed.’ That is not behavior that should be easily overlooked or normalized. Recently, there were reports of a similar antisemitic incident that allegedly occurred in 2019. “At a time when our city is confronting a serious rise in antisemitism, anti-Asian hate, and other forms of hatred, I find the decision to so prominently honor someone who has engaged in this behavior to be wholly inappropriate. New York City is one of the most diverse cities in the world.” Menin added that she was “deeply concerned about the process through which this decision was made. Mr. Galliano’s rhetoric and conduct, including the alleged 2019 incident, should have been more thoroughly investigated.” She urged organizers to “reconsider” their decision and suggested other ways Galliano could be honored, including a “contextual exhibit or educational program.” “The Met is one of New York City’s most treasured and visible cultural institutions. Its choices carry enormous weight, both here and around the world,” she continued. “I believe this choice falls short of the standard New Yorkers should expect from it.” View this post on Instagram THR

articles.title: Shailene Woodley Recalls Her “Dream” Role as Mary Jane Being Cut From ‘The Amazing Spider-Man 2’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 29, 2026 1:23pm Shailene Woodley Swan Gallet/WWD via Getty Images Logo text Shailene Woodley is reflecting on the time her “dream” role as Mary Jane Watson was cut from The Amazing Spider-Man 2 . Speaking with the SAG-AFTRA Foundation’s Conversations recently, Woodley shared her reaction to learning that her scenes with Andrew Garfield, who starred as Peter Parker/Spider-Man, had been cut from the final film. The actress said she didn’t find out until about a year after she had finished filming the scenes for the Sony Pictures movie, which was released in theaters in May 2014. “That was a fun phone call,” she joked. Related Stories Movies Jacob Tremblay Doesn't Like the World He Sees in Netflix's 'Unabomber' Trailer Movies 'Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse' Trailer Drops Online, Christopher Miller Slams Leak “I was cast as Mary Jane for Spider-Man , which was my dream. Oh my god, Spider-Man’s my favorite superhero; Mary Jane was my favorite character growing up. So, when I got it, I was like, ‘This is so exciting!'” The Big Little Lies star continued, “We filmed like three scenes together, me and Andrew Garfield. And then, like a year later, they were like, ‘So, you’re not in the movie anymore.’ And I was like, ‘What? What do you mean?’ And they’re like, ‘We’ve introduced a lot of new characters in this last one, and we’re going to wait for whatever happens between [Emma Stone] and Andrew [Garfield].'” Woodley said she was told the filmmakers planned to introduce Mary Jane after Peter’s relationship with Gwen Stacy, played by Stone, came to an end. “They were like, ‘Let’s wait for her to die, and then we’ll introduce Mary Jane.’ Which made sense, but then they didn’t make that film. So, there was no reintroduction,” Woodley said. “That’s what I was told, but again, who knows what the truth is? I could have been terrible, and they were like, ‘We can’t do this.'” The Hollywood Reporter reported in 2013 that Woodley’s scenes had been cut from the film. At the time, director Marc Webb said the decision was made to streamline the story and focus on Peter and Gwen’s relationship. “Shailene is an incredibly talented actress, and while we only shot a few scenes with Mary Jane, we all love working with her,” Webb said. Mary Jane had previously been established as Peter Parker’s main love interest in Sam Raimi’s original Spider-Man trilogy, with Kirsten Dunst playing the character opposite Tobey Maguire. Garfield’s iteration of the franchise instead centered on Peter’s relationship with Gwen Stacy, played by Stone. Bryce Dallas Howard also appeared as Gwen in 2007’s Spider-Man 3 . Sony ultimately shelved plans for a third Amazing Spider-Man movie following the release of The Amazing Spider-Man 2 , which underperformed compared with expectations. Garfield, meanwhile, eventually returned as Spider-Man alongside Maguire in 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home . Garfield has previously described returning to the franchise as “really healing” and has teased that he would be open to reprising Spider-Man “if it was the right thing.” THR

articles.title: Chris Hansen Gives Robert Pattinson Credit for His “Pretty Good Imitation” in ‘Primetime’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 29, 2026 3:36pm Chris Hansen and Robert Pattinson Jason Mendez/Getty Images; Dia Dipasupil/Getty Images Chris Hansen is speaking out again about the upcoming film Primetime , and this time, he’s giving Robert Pattinson some credit for his performance as him. Speaking with Entertainment Tonight , Hansen, the former host of Dateline NBC’s To Catch a Predator , shared his take on The Batman star’s portrayal based on what he’s seen in the trailer. “Obviously he has practiced imitating me, and while I think it’s overly dramatic, I think there is a pretty good imitation there in the trailer,” Hansen said. Related Stories Movies Chris Hansen Buys Ads Before Every Screening of A24's 'Primetime' (Exclusive) Movies Chris Hansen Didn't Watch 'Primetime' Screening Because "A24 Wanted Me to Sign Away My Rights" However, Hansen added that his family has been more receptive to Pattinson’s performance. “It’s not so much what I think; it’s what other people think. And you know, my wife [and] my family seem to think it’s a pretty good imitation,” he said. Still, Hansen pointed out that Pattinson’s character is not an exact portrayal of him. “He’s saying things I never said and doing things I never did, and that’s not who I am. I’m a nice guy, except when it comes to criminals and predators,” Hansen continued. “I think people should remember that it is a work of fiction, only based on real-life events.” The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Pattinson’s reps for comment but did not hear back by the time of publication. Hansen has also been vocal about his lack of involvement in the film, which is inspired by his work investigating suspected child predators. Last week, he told Fox News’ Jesse Watters that he did not attend a screening of Primetime because, he alleged, “The lawyers at A24 wanted me to sign away my rights to my name, image and brand, essentially, as well as any potential legal rights that would come out of the movie.” “I couldn’t sign that, so they didn’t show me the film. I went all the way over there. … But who’s going to sign something like that?” he added. Despite not being involved in the film, Hansen purchased preshow advertising on every screen showing Primetime , directing moviegoers to TruBlu, his streaming network focused on predator investigations, THR exclusively reported . THR

Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Daisy Chain Fields After Olivia Rodrigo announced Friday that Daisy Chain Fields had raised $10 million for women-focused nonprofits, Melinda French Gates has doubled that number, totaling the donation to $20 million. Before her headlining set Saturday night, the “drop dead” singer took the stage to thank all of the musicians who took part in the festival. She began, “The fact that they took the time out of their insanely busy schedules to come and do this festival for free is something I’m so grateful for. Because of that, and because of all of you who came to hang out today, I can stand on the stage and say we are donating $10 million to 10 incredible charities.” Related Stories Music Olivia Rodrigo's Inaugural Daisy Chain Fields Will Be a Showing of Unity -- Even for Photographers Music Olivia Rodrigo's Daisy Chain Fields Raises $10 Million for Women-Focused Nonprofits “I really believe that giving women the tools to decide their own futures and live healthy lives free of violence and discrimination is the most effective tool we have at changing the world for the better,” she began, before introducing French Gates and her donation. “And I don’t know many people who represent that idea more than Melinda French Gates.” “Melinda is one of the most inspiring women I’ve ever met. She’s devoted her life to empowering women and girls that might have otherwise been forgotten,” Rodrigo said. “She’s generous and brave and has done so much good in this world, and I’m totally floored because as well as being in attendance here tonight, she’s pledged to double every dollar that we made here today to a grand total of funds being donated to $20 million. I’m so grateful!” View this post on Instagram The 10 beneficiary organizations, which will equally split the total funds raised, are Baby2Baby, Black Mamas Matter Alliance, Center for Reproductive Rights, FreeFrom, Jhpiego, Johns Hopkins Center for Indigenous Health, National Domestic Workers Alliance, National Institute for Reproductive Health, National Women’s Law Center and Planned Parenthood. 2026 marked the first year of Rodrigo’s Daisy Chain Fields after being announced in June. At a Friday press conference ahead of the weekend, the singer announced that $10 million had been raised for its nonprofit partners. “The organizations we’ve partnered with are doing incredibly important work every single day in the U.S. and globally,” Rodrigo said. “I’m so grateful to every person who bought a ticket, every artist who waived their fee , every sponsor for signing onto a brand new festival and every donation that helped get to $10 million dollars to support women and girls.” Alongside Rodrigo, performers included Chappell Roan, Mitski, Doechii, Bikini Kill, the Breeders, Garbage, Eli, Quiet Light, Rachel Chinouriri, Devon Again and Not For Radio. Stevie Nicks, Karen O and Lilith Fair founder Sarah McLachlan served as special guests. Katseye was originally announced as part of the performance lineup, but dropped out on Thursday due to an injury sustained by member Megan. Nicole Fell contributed to this report. THR

articles.title: Final Emmy Predictions in 116 Categories: HBO Max Poised to Dominate With ‘The Pitt’ as ‘Widow’s Bay’ and ‘Hacks’ Chase Opposite All-Time Records
articles.full_text: Getty / Apple TV / HBO Max / Netflix Variety Awards Circuit section is the home for all awards news and related content throughout the year, featuring the following: the official predictions for the upcoming Oscars , Emmys , Grammys and Tony Awards ceremonies, curated by Variety chief awards editor Clayton Davis. The prediction pages reflect the current standings in the race and do not reflect personal preferences for any individual contender. As other formal (and informal) polls suggest, competitions are fluid and subject to change in response to buzz and events. Predictions are updated every Thursday. Explore Awards Circuit Predictions Pages Oscars | Emmys | Grammys | Tonys Mariska Hargitay Michael Schwartz for Variety Primetime Emmys Predictions Commentary All Categories (Updated: Aug. 29, 2026): “The tribe has spoken.” For the first time in a while, the Emmy race feels genuinely quite settled in the drama race, while the comedy field has a legitimate insurgent, and the limited series category is anyone’s to lose. The ceremony could be a nail-biter. HBO Max’s medical drama and last year’s reigning drama champion “The Pitt” turned a real-time gimmick into the network’s defining series of the year. Apple TV’s horror hit “Widow’s Bay” bulldozed its way into the comedy conversation. At the same time, Netflix’s anthology series “Beef” returned to the fold to take on HBO’s murder-mystery “DTF St. Louis.” If the final predictions hold, the same year “Hacks” set the all-time comedy nomination record with 24 — surpassing the 23-nom mark “The Studio” tied with “The Bear” just last year — the Katie Dippold-created horror gem “Widow’s Bay” is projected to win an astounding 15 Emmys, including outstanding comedy series. That would make it the most awarded comedy series in a single year, breaking the record “The Studio” set only last year with 13. So where does that leave “Hacks?” The fifth and final season of Jean Smart’s Deborah Vance is projected for a single win — a record-setting eighth acting Emmy for Smart — while losing everywhere else. But the margin is razor-thin, and it points at a not-so-great possible record that could be set. If Lisa Kudrow pulls off what many consider to be impossible and eeks out a lead comedy actress win for the final season of “The Comeback” — denying Smart in the one category “Hacks” is otherwise projected to take — and if the show is blanked across the Creative Arts categories as well, the beloved farewell would back into a brutal headline: the most Emmy losses in a single season in history, surpassing the 21 that “The Handmaid’s Tale” lost in 2021. That shouldn’t bum out HBO Max too much, because the network is still projected to dominate the nights overall. “The Pitt” is expected to grow on its freshman tally of five to as many as seven, repeating in drama series and for Noah Wyle, Katherine LaNasa and casting. The limited race looks tighter — HBO’s “DTF St. Louis” is most notably in play — but the second season of Netflix’s anthology “Beef” should squeak it out with six wins, helped by projected acting victories for Oscar Isaac and Carey Mulligan. Thanks to a new “area award” format — voters now judge each nominee against an approval threshold rather than picking one winner — the variety series category can crown more than one show. That could hand a beloved farewell to Stephen Colbert, whose “Late Show” won its first Emmy only last year and signs off in 2026, while simultaneously delivering a long-denied first series trophy to Jimmy Kimmel after a year spent tangling with the president and the F.C.C. In this category, in this format, they don’t have to beat each other. In other variety categories: “The Apple Music Super Bowl LX Halftime Show Starring Bad Bunny” is expected to become the most-awarded Super Bowl halftime show in Emmy history, surpassing the 2022 Dr. Dre/Snoop Dogg/Eminem LVI show, which won three. It would also be the first Spanish-language program to win variety special (live) — and Bad Bunny’s first Emmy. In variety special (pre-recorded), Taylor Swift is expected to win her first competitive Emmy — as a producer of her Disney+ “Eras Tour” special — even as her other awards ambitions play out well beyond television. Her “Toy Story 5″ song “I Knew It, I Knew You” is an early Oscar hopeful in the best original song race, while her album, “The Life of a Showgirl” will be seeking Grammy Awards consideration this cycle. Swift has technically been an Emmy winner since 2015, when “AMEX Unstaged: Taylor Swift Experience” took the juried prize for original interactive program. But a pre-recorded win would be her first competitive Emmy, chipping the asterisk off an EGOT-aspiring résumé. While CBS’ “Survivor,” coming off its landmark 50th season, looked like it could finally win its first statue for competition program, Peacock’s “The Traitors” appears poised to edge it out, though it’s close. A handful of races remain in flux, which only adds pressure to an evening emceed by Emmy winner (and Variety cover star ) Mariska Hargitay, likely to become the first person to hold Emmy wins for acting (thanks “Law and Order”) and documentary, if she wins either doc series or director for “My Mom Jayne.” The Creative Arts ceremonies honoring the artisans, plus the Governors Gala, take place Sept. 5-6. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards air Sept. 14 on NBC. articles.title: ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic
articles.full_text: Aug 29, 2026 2:36pm PT ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic Revered Argentine writer Jose Luis Borges is rendered a colorful, quirky agent to a young writer's creative and romantic awakening in Marc Turteltaub's amiable, loosely biographical film. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic 17 hours ago ‘The Whisper Man’ Review: Diverting Netflix Serial Killer Chiller Doesn’t Demand Much of Robert De Niro 2 days ago Celebrating Tim Curry’s Career in Camp: From ‘Rocky Horror’ to ‘Clue’ to ‘It,’ He Proved You Could Be Serious About Unserious Acting 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Edinburgh American author Jay Parini’s 2020 memoir “ Borges and Me : An Encounter” read as a charming extension of an anecdote any writer would dine out on for the rest of their life: the tale of how Parini, as a college student in the 1970s, was somehow partnered on a winding road trip through the Scottish Highlands with the venerable Argentine literary icon José Luis Borges. Like any good anecdote, it feels healthily embellished — Borges was doubtless a character, but is fashioned on the page into a Character — in ways that director Marc Turtletaub ‘s enjoyable, good-natured screen adaptation appears to build upon. As a feature film, “Borges and Me” is perhaps extended beyond its natural capacity: It feels both a tall story and a thin one. But the charm is still there. Related Stories Taylor Swift Sings Mashup of 'All Too Well,' 'I Knew It, I Knew You' and 'August' in Grammy Museum Video Grammys May Reconsider New Asian Pop Award After BTS Withdrawal: ‘Some Artists Feel This Category Isn’t Representing the Music They Create’ Benefiting considerably from the tawny, textured splendor of its Scottish locations — shot with dewy autumnal crispness by DP Christopher Norr — this is mellow, quietly sentimental fare that was ideally suited to its home-turf world premiere at the Edinburgh Film Festival . It will likely please plenty more crowds on the festival circuit en route to global arthouse-crossover distribution, assisted by the mixture of British, South American and North American drawcards in a transatlantic co-production. Those include its deliberately mismatched leads: Chilean veteran Luis Gnecco (“Neruda”) as the twinkly genius, and Fionn Whitehead (“Dunkirk”), an actor eternally English in his uprightness but appealingly cast an Anglophile American, as his exasperated minder. Popular on Variety As played by White, the young Parini may be fairly advanced in his studies — as an English literature doctoral student at St. Andrew’s University in Scotland — but he exudes an unworldly freshman quality in his just-askew tortoiseshell glasses and oversized duffel coat. A native Pennsylvanian, and still very much a fish out of water, his shy, sweet earnestness makes him an easy target for good-humored ribbing by his breezily bohemian supervisor, the poet Alastair Reid (Alan Cumming, on pleasingly Alan Cumming form). A scholar of South American literature and a leading translator of Borges’ work, he invites the Chilean to stay with him at his ramshackle coastal cottage; joining them for a day, Parini is both bewildered and a little enraptured by the brilliant, eccentric and sightless septuagenarian visitor. He’s not, however, prepared to be Borges’ babysitter — which is precisely what he becomes when Reid heads off on a last-minute trip to London, leaving some pointers regarding the writer’s various medications, but not much else. It also happens to be the week when Parini was planning to drive up into the Highlands to interview his Ph.D subject, the elusive and hermetic poet George Mackay Brown (Peter Mullan, in a mischievous extended cameo). Cue a cross-generational odd-couple road trip, with rather more sightseeing detours than Parini had planned for. Borges may not be able to see the scenery, but delights in every scrap of local color, to a degree that the American — tasked with describing everything to his elder, in suitably lyrical terms — finds quite wearisome. Audiences might relate to some extent. In a sprightly performance rife with oddball mannerisms, Gnecco gives Borges equal parts impish wisdom, earthy vulgarity and childlike wonder, rarely letting a moment’s silence go unfilled with eager chatter. When the virginal Parini — who thus far has read romantic poetry without truly feeling it — hits it off with smart, kindly pub worker Ailith (a wonderful Freya Mavor) and they steal away for a time, the film positively breathes in the old man’s absence. Borges’ presence accounts for some amusing and even poignant adventures: a bumbling boat excursion on Loch Ness, or a fanciful, hallucinatory visit to a long grassed-over battlefield. But the film’s most affecting moments are its quietest ones, largely centered on Parini and his interior anxieties, which include his less academically-inclined brother’s travails as a soldier in Vietnam. Whitehead gives “Borges and Me” the stillness it needs to avoid feeling mawkish or shticky, but screenwriter Oren Moverman (working from an earlier adaptation by Parini and Ross Clarke) pivots between moments of graceful poetry and others of simpler feelgood sentiment. The final balance slightly favors the latter: There’s little engagement with Borges’ own writing, for example, though audiences so inclined have the upcoming five-hour-plus documentary “Life of Jorge Luis Borges” for that. (Perhaps the two films’ eventual distributors could put their heads together and work out a complementary release strategy.) Full of warm feeling and fuzzy nostalgia for the porous, knowledge-gathering naïveté of youth, “Borges and Me” treats the author as a general, buoyant, heavily imagined spirit rather than a historical subject, and likably so. ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic Reviewed at Charlotte Street Hotel screening room, London, July 30, 2026. In Edinburgh Film Festival (Out of Competition). Running time: 109 MIN. Production: (U.K.-U.S.-Belgium-Netherlands) An A Private View, Big Beach, Lemming Films, Ossian Pictures production. articles.full_text: Aug 29, 2026 3:54pm PT Owner of ‘Heated Rivalry’ Cabin Needed to Do Some ‘Soul Searching’ Before Inviting the Show Back for Season 2 By Jack Dunn Plus Icon Jack Dunn Latest Owner of ‘Heated Rivalry’ Cabin Needed to Do Some ‘Soul Searching’ Before Inviting the Show Back for Season 2 14 hours ago Chris Hansen Says Robert Pattinson’s ‘Primetime’ Performance Is ‘Overly Dramatic,’ But His Wife and Kids Think It’s a ‘Pretty Good Imitation’ 16 hours ago Venice Film Festival Jury Press Conference ‘Probably Not’ Happening Due to Scheduling, Will Replace Event With Welcome Cocktails for Journalists 17 hours ago See All sabrina lantos Michael Kutryk, the owner of the now-famous cabin featured in “ Heated Rivalry ” Season 1, said he needed to do some “soul searching” before allowing the HBO production to come back for Season 2. “I did a little bit of soul searching about allowing them to come back,” Kutryk told HGTV . “I know they need it, and I realize I [could] be difficult and try to squeeze them, but I [couldn’t] bring myself to do that.” Related Stories Netflix Orders 'Manifest' Spinoff 'Arrivals,' With a New Mystery and Cast — Announced on 8/28, Of Course How 'The Pitt' Production Designer Expanded the Emergency Room for Season 2 He continued, “When they called, they said, ‘How much do you want?’ First, I told them they scratched my table, then I named a very reasonable price. They were shocked and appreciative. I actually didn’t even get them to replace my table.” Popular on Variety Kutryk’s house was featured in the “Heated Rivalry” Season 1 finale, titled “The Cottage,” in which Shane Hollander ( Hudson Williams ) brings Ilya Rozanov ( Connor Storrie ) to his remote family cabin for a private getaway. Kutryk, a Toronto doctor, said he was shocked when he first listened to Rachel Reid’s “Game Changer,” on which the show is based, on audiobook. “My jaw just dropped as I listened. The pretty explicit nature of the book made me wonder just what they’d be filming … and showing!” Kutryk said. “I just thought, OK, they’re gonna film what they’re gonna film. What’s done is done.” “We’ll see after Season 2 airs what demand is like,” he added. “It’s still true: I’m a private guy. This is my retreat. I built this to get away from the world, so I don’t know how much longer I’ll continue to share it.” “Heated Rivalry” Season 2, which was greenlit in December 2025 , is expected to release in April 2027. The HBO Max and Crave series follows up-and-coming professional hockey stars Shane Hollander and Ilya Rozanov, who maintain a facade as fierce competitors on the ice while engaging in a secret romance. articles.title: Inside the Global Rise of CJ ENM’s ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier’
articles.full_text: Aug 30, 2026 12:56am PT Inside the Global Rise of CJ ENM’s ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Inside the Global Rise of CJ ENM’s ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier’ 6 hours ago ‘The Song of Scorpions,’ ‘Qissa’ Director Anup Singh Sets Mumbai Film ‘Lasya: The Gentle Dance’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Kartik Aaryan’s ‘Captain India’ Sets September London Shoot (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All CJ ENM When “ The Legend of Kitchen Soldier ” was selected as the only K-drama in the Special Screening section at Series Mania in Lille earlier this year, it marked an early signal that something unusual was happening with a show that had started life as a calculated creative gamble. By July 31, when the series took best drama series at the Fifth Blue Dragon Series Awards, that signal had become a verdict. The 12-episode series – produced by Studio Dragon and released as a TVING original on CJ ENM ‘s Korean streaming platform – follows Kang Seong-jae, played by Park Ji-hoon, a young man who joins the military to escape a difficult reality. His trajectory shifts when a virtual quest screen appears before him, redirecting him toward life as an army cook. As he completes each mission, buried secrets within the military base begin to surface. Related Stories Taylor Swift Sings Mashup of 'All Too Well,' 'I Knew It, I Knew You' and 'August' in Grammy Museum Video Grammys May Reconsider New Asian Pop Award After BTS Withdrawal: ‘Some Artists Feel This Category Isn’t Representing the Music They Create’ The show’s international performance has been striking across multiple platforms. It reached No. 2 overall on Disney+ Japan, ranked among the top three Korean drama titles on HBO Max across 17 countries and territories – performing especially strongly in Indonesia, Malaysia and the Philippines – and landed in the Rakuten Viki top five across the Americas, Europe, Oceania and MENA. On Sept. 15, chief producer Kim Tae-hoon will take part in a creator talk at K-Brand Week in Poland, extending the show’s reach into a new European market. Popular on Variety None of this was treated as a foregone conclusion during production. The creative team at Studio Dragon made a series of deliberate formal choices that broke with K-drama convention, and they knew it. Central among them was the editing. Rather than using visual style as a background element, the production foregrounded it as part of the show’s identity – building the virtual quest screen into the fabric of the series, and adopting a lo-fi, high-energy aesthetic that amplified the comedy rather than simply serving the narrative. “I believe the success of ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier’ revolves around how experimental it was, especially in its direction and never-before-seen editing style, which hooks audiences instantly,” said Lee Hye-young, executive producer of “The Legend of Kitchen Soldier” at Studio Dragon. “However, it was also important for us to maintain depth in the show’s narrative. That’s why we incorporated the ‘over-the-top’ elements to an extent that would not interfere with the story’s cohesiveness.” The challenge of holding that balance extended to the cast. Led by Park and Lee Sang-yi, both of whom carry established international fanbases, the ensemble also includes Han Dong-hee as Lieutenant Cho Ye-rin and Lee Hong-nae as Senior Sergeant Yoon Dong-hyun. “While maintaining the extreme editing style, we also wanted to make sure the cast was not overwhelmed by these elements,” said Kim Tae-hoon, chief producer at Studio Dragon. “Thanks to all the cast members’ remarkable performances, we were able to bring our creative vision to life.” The show also made a structural bet that distinguished it from the bulk of globally travelling K-drama: it placed comedy at the centre without a romance narrative to anchor it. K-drama’s international rise has been built substantially on romantic melodrama, and a straight comedy with no rom-com scaffolding represented a genuine departure. The series made that departure without sacrificing character depth – each member of the ensemble was given distinct motivation and a narrative arc, allowing audiences to build investment across the run. The IP extended beyond the screen through Migak Boys, an in-universe K-pop group formed around the drama’s characters and their reactions to Kang Seong-jae’s cooking. The device brought together K-drama, K-pop and food culture within a single property, adding a layer of audience engagement beyond conventional viewership. “The success of the TVING original ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier’ demonstrates that fresh genres and original storytelling can resonate with audiences both in Korea and around the world,” said Choi Bo-hyun, chief contents officer at TVING. “Building on TVING’s bold creative vision and CJ ENM’s content capabilities, we will continue to expand the diversity and global competitiveness of K-content.” The Blue Dragon win and the Poland screening suggest the show’s impact is still accumulating. Sebastian Kim, head of the content business Unit at CJ ENM, said the series had opened a door the company intends to keep pushing through. “The success of ‘The Legend of Kitchen Soldier’ is proof that diverse genres of K-dramas can succeed in the global entertainment market, opening a new era in which global audiences are ready to embrace unconventional storytelling,” Kim said. “Standing at the forefront of K-culture’s global expansion, CJ ENM will continue to challenge ourselves to develop stories that are different, unique, and unexpected for global fans, delivering consistent surprises and new experiences to audiences around the world.” ‘Harry Potter’ Series Star Bel Powley Says ‘I Strongly Disagree With J.K. articles.title: ‘Sea of Glass’ Review: A Widow’s Coastal Healing Retreat Turns Into a Stately, Moody Greek Tragedy
articles.full_text: Aug 30, 2026 1:31am PT ‘Sea of Glass’ Review: A Widow’s Coastal Healing Retreat Turns Into a Stately, Moody Greek Tragedy Eleven years after his stylish crime drama 'Wednesday 04:45,' Greek writer-director Alexis Alexiou returns with another intriguing blend of neo-noir tropes and anguished character study. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Borges and Me’ Review: Gentle, Nostalgic Literary Road Movie Is More Perky Than Poetic 16 hours ago ‘The Whisper Man’ Review: Diverting Netflix Serial Killer Chiller Doesn’t Demand Much of Robert De Niro 2 days ago Celebrating Tim Curry’s Career in Camp: From ‘Rocky Horror’ to ‘Clue’ to ‘It,’ He Proved You Could Be Serious About Unserious Acting 3 days ago See All Tugo Tugo Productions There are Greek waves aplenty lapping at the forlorn beachside setting of “ Sea of Glass ,” though they’re not especially weird ones. Amid a national cinema that has become internationally recognized for perverse plotting and deadpan absurdism, writer-director Alexis Alexiou ‘s third feature stands out for its stark storytelling and earnest emotional intensity. There is more than a nod to classical Greek tragedy here, and the film — a contemporary tale of dysfunctional parent-child relationships with escalatingly brutal consequences — doesn’t wear it lightly. But a spirit of feminist independence also infiltrates these dark proceedings: Alexiou namechecks “Thelma and Louise” among his inspirations, and though “Sea of Glass” is never quite so rousing or rowdy, it’s finally a moving study of female allyship across generations. Related Stories Dolly Parton, Queen of Country Music, Dies at 80 Dolly Parton, 1946-2026, In Appreciation: A Life of Many Colors It’s been 11 years since Alexiou’s last feature “Wednesday 04:45,” a sleek, Michael Mann-indebted thriller that, despite its ticking-clock narrative setup, really led with heavy neon-nights ambience — and toured the festival circuit extensively following its Tribeca premiere. “Sea of Glass,” which recently bowed out of competition at Edinburgh, is similarly stern with its neo-noir inflections, though its script, by Alexiou with Afroditi Nikolaidou, branches out effectively into raging family melodrama. The results are absorbing, but at 130 minutes, could stand some tightening: A slow-burning setup takes rather too long to segue into the stirring, high-stakes female friendship portrait at the film’s heart. Popular on Variety Though the louring atmospherics here are a leading attraction, “Sea of Glass” also serves as a strong showcase for veteran actress Evangelia Andreadaki (recently seen in last year’s Greek Oscar submission “Arcadia”), who’s charged with telling much of her character’s backstory in weary silence. In her mid-sixties, Vangelio’s days are spent caring for her older, bedridden husband, with little time or thought for herself, beyond perusing old tourist guidebooks with idle yearning; one introductory scene limns a life of under-appreciated, routine-bound service. When the old man dies, her numb reaction appears caught between grief and relief, though her two adult sons show little understanding of her emotional state. Impulsively, Vangelio decides on some alone time, on her own terms — booking an off-season vacation at a coastal resort on the Greek island of Evia. Presumably overrun with holidaymakers in the summer, it’s chilly and dolefully quiet when she arrives, as is the shabby hotel she checks into: Excellent sound design, in particular, captures the lonesome reverberations of weather and water in this wintry limbo. Still, the rundown mood of the place suits Vangelio’s own. Here, at last, is somewhere she can productively do nothing. Or it would be, if the hotel didn’t have its own drama of oppression and liberation brewing downstairs. 23-year-old Vicky (Christiana Matelska Toka) runs the establishment thanklessly and almost single-handedly, with little help from its owner, her boorish father (Michalis Iatropoulos). Dad is an abusive alcoholic, prone to berating and even assaulting his daughter in front of guests, of which Vangelio is currently the only one. That draws her into this domestic crisis whether she likes it or not; she soon forms a tacit bond with the desperately withdrawn Vicky, who’s visibly grateful for a maternal figure to confide in. Women have little voice in this community of stale, disappointed men, including the local cops who are her father’s best friends. Vicky could run away, but feels an unconditional obligation to look after the man holding her down; Vangelio, recognizing something of the life she just escaped in the young woman’s plight, in turn feels duty bound to help her out of it. Freedom, when it comes, comes violently, cuing a final act that exhilaratingly changes the pace, location and emotional scale of proceedings. It’s Andreadaki’s weathered, keenly watchful performance, and her galvanizing connection with her younger, more recessive co-star, that keep things grounded as the story ramps up in severity and consequence. The biblical title, drawn from a description in the Book of Revelation of the passage to heaven, also fittingly conjures the film’s aesthetic: DP Simos Sarketzis shoots in the softly frosted blues, greens and browns of glass shards faded and rounded by time and tide. Alexiou’s film feels defined by water, as the characters increasingly take to the ocean and stormy weather sets in from above. There is much pain, dirt and blood here to be washed away. ‘Sea of Glass’ Review: A Widow’s Coastal Healing Retreat Turns Into a Stately, Moody Greek Tragedy Reviewed at Soho Screening Rooms, London, July 31, 2026. Running time: 130 MIN. Production: (Greece-Bulgaria-Cyprus) A Tugo Tugo Prods. production in co-production with Portokal, Bark Like a Cat Films. Producers: Alexis Alexiou, Tonia Mishiali, Victoria Mitreva, Afroditi Nikolaidou, Elina Psykou, Vanya Rainova. Executive producer: Nikos Smpiliris. Co-producers: Mina Dreki, Stelios Kammitsis, Theodora Valenti, Ivica Vidanovic. Crew: Director: Alexis Alexiou. Screenplay: Alexiou, Afroditi Nikolaidou. Camera: Simos Sarketzis. Editors: Lambis Haralambidis, Marios Kleftakis. Music: Lefteris Moumtzis. articles.title: ’17’ Review: Harrowing Teen Pregnancy Drama from Macedonia Could Be the Feel-Bad Movie of the Year
articles.full_text: Aug 30, 2026 3:13am PT ’17’ Review: Harrowing Teen Pregnancy Drama from Macedonia Could Be the Feel-Bad Movie of the Year Sarajevo Best Actress winner Eva Kostić captivates in this unflinching portrait of peer pressure and sexual shame by first time writer-director Kosara Mitić. By Beatrice Loayza Plus Icon Beatrice Loayza Latest ‘Small Things’ Review: Zvonimir Jurić’s Island-Set Chamber Drama Unfolds a Quietly Devastating Family Reunion 6 days ago ‘Everything That’s Wrong With You’ Review: A Luminous Two-Hander from Slovenia About Online Pals Navigating the Waters of IRL Friendship 1 week ago ‘Good People’ Review: Milcho Manchevski’s Haunting Documentary Revisits the Kočani Nightclub Fire Through Survivors’ Eyes 1 week ago See All Courtesy of Berlinale From the first frame, Kosara Mitić’s “ 17 ” refuses to pull any punches, plunging us immediately into the traumatic moment when a hookup between high-school student Sara (Eva Kostić) and two boys takes a violent turn. From here, this nervy teen drama from Macedonia picks up several months later and follows the withdrawn Sara over the first two days of a class trip to Greece, where one of her assailants is among the unruly group of youngsters. Winner of the Best Actress prize at Sarajevo after premiering in the Berlinale’s Perspectives section, the film has a bleak, unflinching gaze that sometimes skims the edges of shock-value miserablism. In the end, however, Mitić’s intrepid approach is undeniably bracing, and held together at its core by Kostić’s simmering performance. Related Stories Dolly Parton Skips Dollywood Ride Opening Amid Ongoing Health Problems: 'My Nashville Doctor Has Kinda Clipped My Wings' AMC, Regal Theaters Set Dolly Parton Retrospectives With 'Steel Magnolias' and 'The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas' In the most superficial sense, “17” resembles one of this year’s more auspicious festival breakouts “La Gradiva”: Both follow a raucous senior class to a foreign country and in the process unearth dark truths about the gang via restlessly fluid camerawork that, in extended close-ups, mercilessly lays bare its protagonist’s anxieties. Also partly filled with nonprofessional young actors, Mitić’s hair-raising debut makes that French first feature look sunny by comparison. There’s a practical reason for this darkness beyond the obvious Eastern European somberness: The first day of the trip, and the bulk of the film, takes place in a stopover hotel in Bitola that cinematographer Naum Doksevski casts in dim jaundiced lights and long shadows. Popular on Variety When the group arrives by bus, Sara is a conspicuously surly presence in her baggy sweatshirt and dragging jeans; her classmates, brusque, yappy, and shockingly entitled as they constantly talk back to their two teacher-chaperones, both grossly resigned to their students’ insolence. Denied the private room she paid double for because of a mix-up by hotel management, Sara must room with her guileless, overly eager friend Lina (Martina Danilovska) and her cool-girl ex bestie Nina (Eva Stojcevska). Nina is now dating the apish Filip (Dame Joveski), Sara’s ex and one of her rapists — unbeknownst to everyone, of course. By teasing out the dynamics between Sara, her classmates and her teachers, the script by Mitić and Ognjen Sviličić highlights a culture of shame and straight masculine privilege; a don’t-ask-don’t-tell world where girls, especially, are peer-pressured to party and surrender their bodies to (often brutal) male whims. Worse yet, in these girls’ heads, is the slut-shaming and bullying that would ensue should this cruel code of silence be broken. And so, there’s a reason Sara is cagey, though Kostić’s remarkable breakout performance adds to this frayed reticence a coiled rage that comes out each time she lays eyes on Filip. That explodes into action in one startlingly seedy scene involving a rape in full view of revelers at a hotel party. When a hotel worker gets a beating from the sociopathic Filip and his juiced-up cronies, this sadism pushes the limits of credulity, though a comment from a teacher — that the kids better behave in Greece, a civilized country with real rules — reveals that Mitić might somewhat be thinking in metaphors. In any case, it’s not just that Sara, whose terrible secret is concealed by the straps cinched around her rounded belly, feels dirtied and disgraced; there are layers to her knowing gaze. A smirk she gives to Nina, who chalks up Sara’s bad attitude to jealousy over Filip, conveys the pity of a veteran soldier talking down to a fresh recruit. But because Sara is indeed only 17, wisdom is tempered by a quivering vulnerability as the reality of her pregnancy presses upon her, body and soul, forcing her to open up to Lina and discover the possibility of solidarity. Along with a brief moment of tenderness Sara experiences with her class’s resident dork, this feminine camaraderie makes for a nugget of niceness in a sea of despair. And at a border control checkpoint, a symbolic crossroads if there ever was one, Mitic has Sara decide in a bracing, breath-held final scene: Bury her truth at all costs or embrace it, haters be damned. ’17’ Review: Harrowing Teen Pregnancy Drama from Macedonia Could Be the Feel-Bad Movie of the Year Reviewed at Sarajevo Film Festival (Competition), Aug. 17, 2026. (Also in Berlin Film Festival — Perspectives.) Running time: 105 MIN. Production: (North Macedonia-Serbia-Slovenia) A Black Cat Production production in co-production with Art & Popcorn, December. (World sales: Totem Film, Paris.) Producer: Tomi Salkovski. Co-producers: Miroslav Mogorovic, Vlado Bulajic, Lija Pogacnik. Crew: Director: Kosara Mitic. Screenplay: Mitic, Ognjen Svilicic. Camera: Naum Doksevski. Editor: Vladimir Pavlovski. With: Eva Kostic, Martina Danilovska, Dame Joveski, Eva Stojchevska, Petar Manic. articles.title: Laura Dern to Give George Clooney Venice Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement
articles.full_text: Aug 30, 2026 6:48am PT Laura Dern to Give George Clooney Venice Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Pink Floyd’s Roger Waters, Nobel Prize Winner Annie Ernaux and More Sign Open Letter Calling for Venice Film Festival to Take ‘Concrete Action’ in Support of Palestine 2 days ago Who’s Afraid of Film Festivals? After Politics Rattled Berlin and Shook Up Cannes, Venice Braces for Impact 2 days ago Italy’s RAI Cinema International Boards Edoardo De Angelis’ ‘The Fire Within You’ Ahead of Venice Launch, Reveals First Clip (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago See All Getty Laura Dern is set to give the Laudatio speech honoring George Clooney at Venice Film Festival where, as previously announced, he will be honored on Wed., Sept. 2, with a Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement. Clooney – who is one of only three people to have been nominated in six different Oscar categories throughout his career (best picture, director, lead actor, supporting actor, original screenplay and adapted screenplay) – will be celebrated on the Lido on the evening of Sept. 2 during the festival’s opening ceremony in his triple guise as actor, director and producer. articles.title: Venice Film Festival Scraps Jury Press Conference
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Melanie Goodfellow August 29, 2026 11:02am Venice Film Festival international jury 2025 Getty The Venice Film Festival has taken the unusual step of scrapping its main jury press conference this year, we can reveal. The festival, which gets underway next week, hasn’t made a public statement to confirm the break from protocol but confirmed the move to us after multiple requests to know if it was going ahead. The move comes at a time of highly charged press conferences at A-list festivals with jurors and talent being quizzed by journalists repeatedly about global politics, especially the Israel-Gaza war. Related Stories Festivals Nigeria Has Its First Venice Giornate Entry With Damilola Orimogunje's Family Portrait 'Dear Ajayi' -- First-Look Trailer Festivals Venice: Palestine-Israel Conflict Set To Be Hot-Button Topic As Open Letter Calls For Festival To Take Concrete Action In Support Of Palestine The festival denied that the move was made with those considerations in mind and said instead it was a result of a “scheduling conflict”. This year’s Venice Film Festival international jury is headed by Maggie Gyllenhaal with members comprising Tunisian director and screenwriter Kaouther Ben Hania, the English composer and artist Daniel Blumberg, the Italian professor Francesco Casetti, the French director and screenwriter Xavier Giannoli, the Afghan director and screenwriter Shahrbanoo Sadat, and the Hong Kong director and producer Johnnie To. Watch on Deadline Ben Hania was at the festival last year with acclaimed drama The Voice Of Hind Rajab , about the tragic killing of five-year-old Palestinian girl Hind Rajab. At last year’s Venice jury press conference, jury head Alexander Payne admitted he was “unprepared” to answer questions about Gaza as political issues dominated. This year’s Berlin Film Festival was a highly charged edition with the opening jury press conference proving to be a flashpoint after jury president Wim Wenders said filmmakers should stay out of politics in answer to a question on the Israel-Palestine conflict. The festival had to publicly defend jury members and call for a different approach to press conferences following them being dominated by questions about politics. The subject of censorship was brought up by press at this year’s Cannes jury presser and dominated column inches for the event. This year’s Venice festival is already shaping up to include a large dose of politics with the addition of Israel-Gaza doc NAZA and the inclusion of Russian film DAU . This week, Nobel Prize-winning author Annie Ernaux, Pink Floyd co-founder Roger Waters and filmmakers including Matteo Garrone and Isabel Coixet were among signatories of an open letter urging the Venice Biennale and film festival to take “concrete action in support of Palestine.” The festival will run September 2 – 12, 2026 Spidey Winning Again; ‘Coyote Vs. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Liza Minnelli Pays Tribute To Friend Dolly Parton: “When I Was In Trouble? Dolly Knew It.” ‘Paranormal Activity’ Broadway Review: Stage Adaptation Of Film Franchise Is A Frightfully Good Time Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller’s ‘Incident At Vichy’ Revival To Off Broadway Next Year View All August 29, 2026 12:12pm 'Downstate' at Playwrights Horizons Joan Marcus The marquee at Broadway ‘s Booth Theatre appears to confirm the rumors: Bruce Norris ‘ acclaimed and controversial play Downstate will take up residence at the venue in an upcoming production directed by Joe Mantello . The news was first reported by the Chicago Tribune – the play premiered in 2018 at Chicago’s Steppenwolf Theatre Company – with the newspaper noting that the Broadway staging will be produced by Scott Rudin and feature at least two members of the original Chicago cast: Francis Guinan and K. Todd Freeman. The Chicago staging was followed by an Off Broadway production at Playwrights Horizons in 2022. Both of those productions were directed by Pam MacKinnon, not Mantello. Related Stories Reviews 'Paranormal Activity' Broadway Review: Stage Adaptation Of Film Franchise Is A Frightfully Good Time Obituaries James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of 'The Heidi Chronicles' & 'I'm Not Rappaport' Was 89 The play, set in a group home for people convicted of sex crimes, received overwhelmingly positive reviews for the Off Broadway production, winning the 2023 New York Drama Critics’ Circle Award for Best Play. Watch on Deadline Specifically, the plot follows four men who have been convicted of sex offenses and have completed their prison sentences but remain on the sex offender registry and live in a group home in downstate Illinois. During the course of the play, one of the men is confronted by a former student. The Rudin-Mantello pairing would reunite the two following their massively successful, Tony-winning 2026 revival of Death of a Salesman starring Nathan Lane and Laurie Metcalf. Rudin, Mantello and Metcalf also collaborated on Samuel D. Hunter’s play Little Bear Ridge Road last season following its premiere at Steppenwolf (the Chicago company did not participate in the Broadway staging of that play). The Broadway premiere of Downstate has not been officially announced, and aside from the marquee lights no Downstate signage on the Booth is evident. Deadline has reached out to sources for confirmation of the plans. The play, which has also been staged in the West End and Washington, D.C., came under fire from right-wing commentators and U.S. Senator Ted Cruz, who responded to a favorable review in the Washington Post by tweeting, “So now the corporate media is praising pedophilia.” Norris, whose play Clybourne Park won the 2012 Tony Award for Best Play, responded to the controversy prior to its Off Broadway engagement in a statement quoted by Playbill: “A depiction of something is not an endorsement. But, I do think that witnessing the lives of characters on stage encourages identification, and if you spend two hours in the company of a group of sex offenders, do you emerge from the experience with your certainty about them momentarily disrupted? The goal is not to forgive, but rather to complicate an easy and casually cruel response.” In addition to the New York Drama Critics’ Circle Award, the Off Broadway production won the Obie Award for Playwriting. Michael Kutryk, the Toronto doctor who owns the Muskoka home that served as Shane’s (Hudson Williams) cottage in the Season 1 finale “The Cottage”, recalled that the show had a “very small budget” when he agreed to “almost nothing” to let them film at the lakefront property. “I did a little bit of soul searching about allowing them to come back,” he told HGTV of Season 2. “I know they need it, and I realize I [could] be difficult and try to squeeze them, but I [couldn’t] bring myself to do that.” Related Stories News ‘Heated Rivalry’ Creator Explains Why Finale’s Sex Scenes Are His Favorite, Teases Season 2 & Beyond “Will Always Be Centered Around” Shane & Ilya News What To Expect For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2: Everything We Know So Far Kutryk added, “When they called, they said, ‘How much do you want?’ First, I told them they scratched my table, then I named a very reasonable price. A producer told him the series was based on a book by Rachel Reid and it’s about hockey, so he listened to the audiobook. “My jaw just dropped as I listened. The pretty explicit nature of the book made me wonder just what they’d be filming … and showing!” said Kutryk. “I just thought, OK, they’re gonna film what they’re gonna film. What’s done is done.” After Airbnb was “desperate to get it as a booking,” Kutryk ultimately agreed to “an offer too good to refuse” from another rental company. But he’s not sure if he’ll rent it out again after Season 2. “We’ll see after Season 2 airs what demand is like,” he explained. “It’s still true: I’m a private guy. This is my retreat. I built this to get away from the world, so I don’t know how much longer I’ll continue to share it.” Deadline recently reported that Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Daniel Diemer, Shaheen Jafargholi, Emily Hampshire, Edvin Ryding, Robert Naylor, Sabrina Jalees and Priyanka have been cast in Season 2 of the Crave Original, which is set to premiere in spring 2027. Randy Holmes/Disney After Jelly Roll avoided discussing his politics at the Grammy Awards in February, he peeled off the band-aid this week with a heartfelt speech. During his final night as Jimmy Kimmel Live ! guest host on Friday, the 3x Grammy winner opened up about watching “people decide who I am, what I am, what I believe, what I support and what I don’t support” after he “fumbled my words” when a reporter asked about his political stance at the awards show. “Looking back, I don’t necessarily regret asking for more time before I spoke. I wish more people took more time before they spoke,” he explained. “But I do wish I had found the words to express my heart just a little bit sooner. But I was afraid that anything I was going to say was going to be immediately taken as a political statement. And ironically, by trying so hard not to make a political statement, I became one.” Related Stories Late Night TV ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’ Reveals Summer Guest Hosts Including Diego Luna & Jelly Roll Politics Rosie O’Donnell Ends ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live’ Guest Run With Trump-Roasting Song: “Use That Stable Genius Brain” Jelly Roll continued, “I spent my entire career trying not to belong to a political party, partly because until March of this year, I wasn’t even allowed to vote. But now that I have that right, it’s one I plan to exercise this coming November.” Watch on Deadline Having been convicted of several felonies in his life, Jelly Roll was pardoned by Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee for his crimes in the state last December, restoring his voting rights. Jelly Roll explained that he wants to be “a voice for the voiceless because I know those people. Those are my people. I try to speak for the unspoken,” adding, “That night at the Grammys, I had an opportunity to speak up for people who were scared, hurting and felt like nobody was speaking for them. I had a microphone and I didn’t use it the right way. “But my daddy always told me, it is never too late to do the right thing,” he continued. “So, I’m going to try to do the right thing, right now, because human dignity isn’t Republican nor Democrat. Compassion isn’t left-wing and mercy isn’t right-wing. Pain and healing knows no partisanship. Hurting hearts are more important than poll numbers. And there are no boundaries or borders for broken families.” After shaking Donald Trump ‘s hand at UFC 309 at Madison Square Garden in November 2024, Jelly Roll also stressed that “a handshake is not an endorsement, a conversation is not an allegiance, and a joke is not a political point of view.” Noting that his dad, a USMC veteran who died in 2019, was “one of my best friends,” Jelly Roll said, “This might be a hot take, but out of respect for him and everybody who has ever served or continues to serve this country, I will always shake the hand of the sitting president of the United States when asked. My father would have been disappointed had I done anything other than that. I’m proud that I was able to shake the president of the United States’ hand. I’m also proud I live in a country where I can make jokes about him. Ain’t that what’s great about being an American? The democracy, the freedom of speech?” Jelly Roll concluded his monologue, “While everything else I’ve said this week has been a complete joke, this is not. Our leaders on both sides of the aisle are doing an absolute sh*t job of trying to bring us together, y’all. … We may disagree, we may argue, may vote completely differently. But let’s try not to let the couple of things we disagree about forget the hundreds and hundreds of things we have in common.” Spidey Winning Again; ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: Leanne Morgan Had To Give LA Writers “Grace” To Capture Her Southern Voice: “They’re In A Bubble Out There”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Jelly Roll Slams Politicians On Both Sides For “Sh*t Job,” Addresses 2024 Trump Photo: “A Handshake Is Not An Endorsement” Tom Hardy’s Debut Rap Album Features Busta Rhymes, Method Man & A Bane Cameo ‘Ali G: Who Iz I?’ Sparks Calls For Theater Boycott, Trailer Slammed Over Racist Stereotypes View All August 29, 2026 8:25pm Star and executive producer Leanne Morgan on 'Leanne' (2026) Courtesy of Netflix With Season 2 of her namesake series now available to stream on Netflix , Leanne Morgan is praising her writers for capturing her Southern voice. The Leanne star recently discussed the culture shock of relocating from Tennessee to Los Angeles to film the sitcom, noting that she was worried her writers room would “stereotype the South and church people.” “I have got a wonderful writing staff, and they have got my voice,” she said on The Women of Joy Show . “But at first, I was like, ‘They’re stereotyping the South, they’re stereotyping Christians.'” Related Stories News Netflix Sets ‘Leanne’ Season 2 Premiere Date; Tyne Daly To Guest On Series That Stars Brother Tim Daly Cancellations and Renewals Leanne Morgan & Chuck Lorre Comedy ‘Leanne’ Renewed For Season 2 By Netflix Morgan continued, “So, at first, I thought, ‘Are they gonna get this right?’ Cause people stereotype the South and church people and all of that, so that was very important to me. And I realized I had to give them grace, because a lot of my writers were not raised in church, and I think they’ve done a really good job.” Watch on Deadline The comedian explained that her “brilliant” writers will draft an episode before she infuses her own voice. “I rewrite what I would really, what we really say in the South. ‘We use Dukes Mayonnaise, not Miracle Whip.’ Even something simple like that,” she said. “But they’re very wonderful to me, because it is based on my comedy and all of that,” added Morgan. “I can do whatever I want to, I’m an executive producer, and they’re very good to me about that.” Later in the show, Morgan stressed that Hollywood has left the market for Christian entertainment untapped, instead opting for over-sexualized projects. “Honest to goodness, I think in the secular world, I think a lot of people don’t want to see all that,” said Morgan. “I think a lot of people don’t want to see all that, and I think they’re in a bubble out there. And they think people want to see that, but they’re not in the middle of the United States.” In Leanne , the eponymous Southern matriarch is faced with starting over when her husband of 33 years leaves her for another woman.
