articles.title: ‘Paranormal Activity’ Broadway Review: Stage Adaptation Of Film Franchise Is A Frightfully Good Time
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Alex Winter Bringing Arthur Miller’s ‘Incident At Vichy’ Revival To Off Broadway Next Year Amid Growing Galliano Backlash, Met Gala Mulls Date Change – Report James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of ‘The Heidi Chronicles’ & ‘I’m Not Rappaport’ Was 89 View All August 29, 2026 7:00am Travis A. Knight, Cher Álvarez, 'Paranormal Activity' Matthew Murphy There are plenty of laughs in Paranormal Activity , a play that just might be Broadway ‘s scariest horror story ever, but they’re not the lighthearted jolly chuckles of, say, Titanique or the gut-bucket guffaws of Oh, Mary! No, the laughs in Levi Holloway ‘s chiller are more along the lines of those recalled from sharing a movie theater showing The Exorcist : Relief-fueled roars spurred on by the embarrassment of having just shrieked out loud like Jamie Lee Curtis in Halloween . The movie references, of course, are intentional: Holloway’s Paranormal Activity, unerringly directed by Felix Barrett (the Punchdrunk founder and artistic director behind the popular immersive Sleep No More ) and starring two Broadway newcomers who by all rights should by now be overnight stars, is based (in spirit, as it were, if not plot) on the durable Paramount Pictures film franchise of the same name. Related Stories Obituaries James Walsh Dies: Tony-Winning Broadway Producer Of 'The Heidi Chronicles' & 'I'm Not Rappaport' Was 89 News Tim Curry Remembered By 'Rocky Horror Show' Playwright Richard O'Brien & The Broadway Revival And while the production borrows just about every worthwhile horror movie trope and scare tactic ever committed to film, this Paranormal Activity feels entirely (and idiosyncratically) of the stage , as if Holloway and Barrett worked some voodoo magic to have us all forget that we’ve ever so much as heard of, much less seen, slamming doors, impossible shadows, glitchy television sets with minds of their own and lamps that flicker like so much lightning. This play uses ’em all – to just about perfect effect – along with only-in-the-theater elements like stage lighting and sound designs that amp up the scare volume (literally) to shattering results (and not just on your eardrums, though that too.) Watch on Deadline Ditching the films’ plotlines for something new, if, obviously, related, Paranormal Activity follows young American couple Lou ( Cher Álvarez ) and James ( Travis A. Knight ) who have recently relocated from Chicago – where some strange, vaguely described things involving “lost time” and black-outs bedeviled poor Lou. So right from the start we have a time-honored set up: A young wife who might be haunted or maybe just unbalanced, and won’t be entirely trusted by the men in her life one way or the other. That’s a trope as socially relevant today as it was when Gaslight (a film that gets name-checked here) owned it, and Rosemary’s Baby perfected it and Let’s Scare Jessica To Death took it to the drive-in. Let the man pretend to be the hero. We know the truth. Well, we think we do, anyway. Playwright Holloway has all sorts of tricks up his many sleeves, turning misdirection (visual, narrative, aural or otherwise) into a symphony of look-here! no look-there! shifts. There’s a shocking moment early on in which writing, directing, acting, the illusions by Chris Fisher, the lighting by Anna Watson and sound design by Gareth Fry come together so seamlessly and impactfully that the audience response is a mix of serious what- was -that gasps and very loud shrieks. Followed by that embarrassed laughter, naturally enough. The play opens on Fly Davis’ two-tiered set – a largish but comfy and lived-in London flat, bedrooms upstairs and always on view so we see what the couple downstairs doesn’t – with the sound of a podcast filling the theater. The podcaster is a thick-accented medium, of sorts, who reminds us that houses aren’t haunted, people are. Remember that. Álvarez in ‘Paranormal Activity’ Matthew Murphy The anticipated spine-tingles begin almost immediately, when buzzy light fixtures and TV static make nuisances of themselves, and dazed Lou is wont to stare into a middle-distance at a presence only she can sense. James, though loving and well-intentioned, can’t help but show his skepticism, repeatedly (and blithely unaware of his condescension) asking if his wife remembered to take her meds today. Audiences don’t need to fret about some prolonged is-she-or-isn’t-she red herring though: Soon enough, James is met with incontrovertible proof that, no indeed, they are most definitely not alone. Even the podcast medium, making a house call (perhaps the only truly unbelievable moment in a tale that by all rights should be stocked with them), freaks out when she comes face-to-face with something she probably never really believed could exist. To give more away would be to spoil the good, scary fun that unspools over the two-hour running time, a running time, by the way, that is filled with long, tense moments of quiet anticipation expertly broken by very loud blasts of everything from rock music to slamming doors, burglar alarms, doorbells, the proverbial bumps in the night and an intensely unsettling, nearly incomprehensible voice from the ether. Old, carefully guarded secrets are revealed, shames are exposed, blame is tossed and no one is safe from the past, the predictions or one another (especially when the other isn’t all he or she appears to be). Newcomers Álvarez and Knight couldn’t be better in their newlywed roles, convincing in their giddy love scenes, their casual affections, their unwanted suspicions and, most of all, their terror at whatever is lurking in the air and in their souls. In supporting roles, Eva Kaminsky as the gorgeously-named spiritualist Etheline Cotgrave does well to keep us on our toes, and Shannon Cochran, as James’ Southern Christian evangelical mom, is both funny and suitably creepy whether she’s moralizing in person or via long-distance video screen chats. The mom’s name, not so incidentally, is Carolanne, just a tiny space away from “they’re heeere” Carol Anne of Poltergeist . Yes, a bit on the nose, but who could begrudge Holloway for indulging in some fun for himself? Having perfected this whole stage fright business since his underrated 2019 outing Grey House, which now seems like a practice run, the playwright, along with his director, cast and creative and technical teams, have gifted us a smashingly diverting entertainment to kick off the Broadway fall season with a big, loud bang. Or several. Title: Paranormal Activity Venue: Broadway’s August Wilson Theatre Written By: Levi Holloway Directed By: Felix Barrett Cast: Cher Álvarez, Travis A. articles.title: Alma Har’el’s Family Drama ‘Wet’ Heading To TIFF Market With 193; A-List Cast Circling
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Jason Statham Buyers Ponder Whether Amazon Leak Caused ‘Mutiny’ At Box Office: “There’s Been Plenty Of Finger-Pointing” ‘Lord Of The Rings’ Producer Lines Up New “Large-Scale” Fantasy Movie ‘Wars Of The Drakons’ AI Sci-Fi Series ‘Kira’ Heads To MIPCOM For Ex Machina & K5, First Look Images View All August 29, 2026 7:17am Alma Har'el Getty Honey Boy director Alma Har’el’s next project Wet is heading to the TIFF market with Patrick Wachsberger’s 193 and is attracting what could be a killer cast. News of the project broke online last month via Page Six who reported that Oscar winner Javier Bardem was in talks. Bardem remains in early talks for the project, and we can reveal that Mission Impossible and Dune star Rebecca Ferguson, Heated Rivalry ‘s Connor Storrie and Marty Supreme breakout Odessa A’zion are also in very early discussions. No deals are done and as is often the case with market packages, there’s a chance they change or don’t come together at all, but buyers are likely to spark to this cast. Related Stories Festivals 'Krux' Trailer: Toronto-Bound WWII Drama Captures True Story Of Disintegration Of Order In German Village Casting Odette Annable Leads Cast In Horror 'Postmortem'; Sublimity Launches Sales For TIFF As First Look Revealed Little has been revealed about the plot but we can confirm it’s an original script from Har’el and Christian Stangeby that is said to be in the vein of HBO’s Succession and the Oscar nominated Palme d’Or winner Triangle of Sadness . If the script gets close to those projects, buyers will likely be in thrall. Watch on Deadline Wachsberger’s 193 is handling international sales. Fifth Season is due to finance and produce alongside Chris Leggett, Riva Marker, and Har’el. The hope is to shoot in Spain early next year. Har’el’s last feature was her debut, Honey Boy , which was written by and starred Shia LaBeouf. The 2019 film, which was picked up by Amazon, garnered largely positive notices and played at festivals including Sundance and TIFF. Har’el was in development on an adaptation of dystopian science-fiction novel Mockingbird for Searchlight. In the meantime, she has also directed TV. Bardem had great write-ups for his turn in Spanish movie The Beloved at Cannes and U.S. distributor Kino Lorber is aiming for a fifth Oscar nomination for the actor. Reps and 193 declined to comment. articles.title: Spotify Names Joe Hadley VP of Global Music Content and Partnerships
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 28, 2026 10:15am Joe Hadley Courtesy of Spotify Spotify has promoted Joe Hadley to vice president of global music content and partnerships, the company announced on Friday. Hadley, who has been at Spotify since 2022, will now oversee both the streaming service’s music editorial and partnerships teams, and he’ll work directly with artists, labels and music publishers. Hadley will report to Charlie Hellman, Spotify’s SVP and Global Head of Music. Previously, Hadley’s title was global head of music partnerships and audience. “Editorial is a key part of bringing an essential human touch to Spotify,” Hellman said in a statement. “The team’s judgment and taste is what fans and artists rely on. Joe’s capable leadership will keep artist advocacy at the center of our work and bring even more impact to the programming we do.” Along with Hadley’s promotion, J.J. Italiano has also been named of Head of Editorial. He will report to Hadley. Prior to joining Spotify, Hadley was a prolific booking agent, serving as the head of hip-hop and R&B at CAA, where his clients included Beyoncé and A$AP Rocky. Before then, he was an agent at Windish. Italiano had his first stint at Spotify from 2017 to 2019 before heading to YouTube in 2020. He came back to Spotify in 2022. THR

articles.title: Pokémon Stop-Motion Series Set at Disney+ as Part of Larger Distribution Deal
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 11:40am 'Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu' Courtesy of Disney Logo text Disney and The Pokémon Company International have struck a distribution deal that will bring both a new and a classic animated series to Disney+ . The streamer, and sibling cable channel Disney XD, have picked up a stop-motion series called Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu for a 2027 premiere. The deal also includes rights to Pokémon the Series: The Beginning , the first animated series featuring Ash, Pikachu and the rest of the foundational Pokémon characters. It’s now streaming on Disney+ and began airing on Disney XD earlier in August. Related Stories TV 'Alice and Steve' Renewed for Season 2 at Disney+ TV Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Opens Up About 'Wonder Man' Un-Renewal: "It's a Lesson in Life" Disney and The Pokémon Company announced the deal Friday at Pokémon XP, a fan convention in San Francisco. Aardman, the acclaimed studio behind Wallace & Gromit and Shaun the Sheep , is making The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu with The Pokémon Company. Aardman’s team for the show includes director Tom Parkinson, creative director — IP development Nat McKay and model making creative lead James Young. “Pokémon has that rare ability to mean something to longtime fans while continuing to feel completely relevant to young audiences today,” said Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids & Family. “ Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu brings Aardman’s signature stop-motion artistry with a bold, playful new perspective to this beloved world, giving audiences a fresh way to experience the characters they know and love.” The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu will follow the two characters through the Galar Region as they seek to help and protect the Pokémon living there. “ These stories, full of adventure and heroism, all told from the perspective of Pokémon is made even more exciting through the lens of the incredible filmmakers at Aardman,” said Phil Rynda, Pokémon’s director of original animation. “Audiences will be delighted getting to know the Sirfetch’d & Pichu, and wonderful cast of Pokémon, featured in this series. Aardman has brought Galar to life in a way that makes you feel like you can smell the air, touch the tree bark, and want to adventure alongside our series heroes.” THR

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Still in More Theaters Than Any Other Movie 5 Weekends Later
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By James Hibberd Plus Icon James Hibberd Writer-at-Large JamesHibberd Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 11:43am Tom Holland in 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day.' Jay Maidment/Sony Pictures Logo text Stop us if you’ve heard this before: That Spider-Man: Brand New Day movie? It’s doing pretty darn well. Insanely well. Like $2.24 billion and counting worth of well. Now, going into its fifth weekend, the Sony-Marvel blockbuster is quietly showing another type of strength: Even with two new major films opening, exhibitors are keeping Brand New Day in more theaters than any other movie. It’s close, mind you, but still: Brand New Day will be in 3,678 theaters, more than any other title, just barely dropping from last weekend’s 4,006. The Looney Tunes legal comedy, Coyote vs. Acme is opening in slightly fewer theaters — 3,575 — despite very strong reviews (95 percent critics score on Rotten Tomatoes; read The Hollywood Reporter ‘s review ) and strong audience scores (92 percent). Coyote vs. Acme is tracking for a somewhat modest $14 million to $22 million domestic opening. While it might not prove to be a hit, its overall reception is certainly making the case that it was a movie worth releasing rather than shelving for a tax write-down, as Warner Bros. originally planned. Then there’s Ridley Scott’s post-apocalyptic thriller The Dog Stars opening right behind Coyote in 3,330 theaters (the film has largely negative reviews from critics — though THR ‘s review was positive — with a domestic opening predicted around $9 million to $14 million). But back to Brand New Day , which has been the gift that keeps on giving for Sony-Marvel and theater owners since its July 31 release. The records have piled up: Biggest opening day ($169 million), biggest domestic opening weekend ($360 million), biggest Monday ever ($47 million), the fastest movie to hit $500 million (seven days), the second-biggest movie ever domestically and, currently, the highest grossing movie of 2026. Brand New Day is expected to rack up yet another $22 million to $27 million domestically this weekend, which should put it past Titanic on the list of the highest-grossing movies of all time. THR

Adults star Amita Rao feels the sentiment’s true for the FX comedy, which returned for its second season yesterday (Aug. 27). The 27-year-old actress and comedian plays Issa, the delightfully confident and outrageously funny member of the core Adults gang. When season one ended, Issa’s boyfriend Paul Baker, played by Jack Innanen, marries another member of the group Anton, played by Owen Thiele, in order to stay in the country — Paul Baker, always first and last name, is Canadian much like Innanen. Related Stories Next Big Thing 'The Last Sunrise' Star Maia Reficco Is Finally Facing Her Fears Next Big Thing Jonathan Daviss Thinks You Will Be Surprised With His Post-'Outer Banks' Role The only problem is that Paul Baker and Anton have palpable chemistry with one another that even Issa can’t deny, and that dynamic plays big into the wildly funny second season of the show. The love triangle has been done before in comedies, and Rao’s more interested in dynamics outside of the romantic relationship. “What was always been interesting to me was the tension between Issa and Anton as best friends,” Rao tells The Hollywood Reporter on a recent Zoom. “Me and Owen had a lot of fun talking about what was said and unsaid behind the scenes because it never really made sense to us that they wouldn’t have debriefed about this.” Rao knew that Adults was special from moment one. “I hadn’t seen a show that really encapsulated a Gen Z ethos [like Adults did],” she says. When the show premiered, she and her co-star Malik Elassal called each other to talk about the “energy shift” that happened. It was different than she was used to working as a stand-up comedian. articles.title: Top Toronto Fest Party Host Expects More Studio Bashes, Tighter Budgets: “No One Is Throwing Money Around”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All August 28, 2026 12:27pm TIFF Lightbox headquarters Zou Zheng/Xinhua via Getty Images Restaurant and nightclub kingpin Charles Khabouth, a top party host for major studio and streamer movie premieres at the Toronto Film Festival each year, expects to feed and honor more Hollywood A-stars in town this year for the 2026 edition. “Last year we did 46 events. This year we’re at 51 (parties) and counting,” Khabouth told The Hollywood Reporter on Friday, ahead of TIFF getting underway on Sept. 10 for an 11-day run. That’s good news for the wait and bar staff at his downtown Toronto venues around TIFF Lightbox like Vinny, Bisha Hotel, STORYS Building, Portland Room, Animl Steakhouse & Cocktail Den, Kost, Byblos and Bar Romy as prime locations for Hollywood star-watchers during the festival’s 51 st edition. Related Stories Movies Late F1 Icon Gilles Villeneuve Drives For Speed, Trophies in 'Rise of a Legend' Trailer (Exclusive) Guest Column Keep Your Opinions Off Celebrities' Bodies (Unless It's Time to Intervene) And Khabouth expects even more American players to call about late-party bookings, or to upgrade cocktail events or intimate dinners to full-blown movie premiere parties. “With last-minute changes, I estimate we will hit 60 events this year,” he added, with around 35 of those expected to be parties with an average of 200 attendees. That’s also good news for local food and alcohol suppliers, limo drivers, security personnel, tablecloth and glassware suppliers. And Toronto launching its inaugural TIFF: The Market is also predicted to offer even more business for local party suppliers, including those installing drapery, lighting and red carpets. Khabouth cautions, however, party spending by Hollywood studios and streamers this year will continue to come down in Toronto, as it has since COVID. “There’s nobody throwing money around like they used to,” the top restaurateur, who has been in business in Toronto with his Ink Entertainment banner since 1983, reported as the Hollywood bean counters are now in charge. That’s made lavish Hollywood premiere parties in Toronto, where the champagne flowed to help toast or tout upcoming award season contenders, a thing of the past. “It’s all budgeted. It’s all calculated. The studios are no longer doing what they used to. Budgets have been cut back everywhere and we understand,” Khabouth argued. That means his restaurant and nightclub venues will continue to work within the budgets of the major American players, while still offering a superior product to ensure repeat business. “It’s still important to deliver that great experience. It showcases that we’re doing a good job,” Khabouth insisted. The Toronto Film Festival is set to run Sept. 10 to 20 this year. THR

articles.title: Dave Franco Says Raunchy ‘Idiots’ Scene Is “Craziest Thing” He’s Done on Camera
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Brian Davids Plus Icon Brian Davids Writer PickYourBrian Follow Sign Up View All August 28, 2026 1:19pm Dave Franco attends the premiere of "Idiots" presented by IFC at Vidiots on August 10, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. Emma McIntyre/Getty Images Logo text If you’re an emerging director, chances are you’ll hear a word of encouragement from Dave Franco . Jeremy Saulnier certainly did after the actor saw the filmmaker’s breakout self- and crowd-funded revenge thriller, Blue Ruin (2013), starring his childhood best friend Macon Blair . When Blair himself took a crack at the director’s chair a few years later, Franco also reached out to compliment his Sundance-winning I Don’t Feel at Home in This World Anymore . The Palo Alto native admits his generosity is partly motivated by a desire to get on talented directors’ radars for future roles, but it’s mainly about softening the industry’s competitiveness. Related Stories Movies 'Idiots' Filmmaker Macon Blair Talks Surviving 13 Years of Setbacks, Recastings and a Title Change Movies What Happened to '23 Jump Street'? “We don’t tell each other enough how much we enjoy each other’s work. There’s such a competitive spirit within the industry that I just want to put out some good vibes, especially if it’s someone’s first time putting out a movie,” Franco tells The Hollywood Reporter in support of Idiots ’ Aug. 28 theatrical release. “So I guess I play the long game sometimes, but it doesn’t normally lead to collaboration. More often than not, it has led to friendship.” In Blair’s case, Franco’s overture in 2017 led to both friendship and eventual collaboration. The writer-director quickly returned the favor by sending Franco his road comedy script called The Shitheads . Franco soon realized, however, that he was too young to play the then-40-something Mark Southard, an aging slacker who, along with another underachiever named Davis Hench, winds up transporting a reprehensible trust-fund teen named Sheridan to rehab. The film would nearly go in 2017 and 2018 with a couple different combinations of actors, particularly Luke Wilson and Tracy Morgan, but then its financing came crashing down, shelving the picture until Franco wrote another one of his patented emails around 2024. At this point, he’d not only aged into the role of Mark, but he’d also directed and/or produced a number of projects to where he could be equally beneficial behind the camera. “I said, ‘No pressure, but I’m here. If I can help in any way as a producer, I’d love to come in and help find the money,’” Franco recalls. “So I’ve basically been stalking Macon for the past ten years in trying to collaborate with him.” The Shitheads did indeed find funding in 2025 en route to a fall shoot in Georgia. Franco even proved instrumental on the casting side of things by recommending O’Shea Jackson Jr. as Davis. The two actors had previously worked together on a series for the short-lived short-form platform, Quibi. And when it came time to find the despicable teenage influencer named Sheridan, Franco suggested Mason Thames from their 2025 film Regretting You . Before being retitled to Idiots , the film’s original title of The Shitheads wasn’t just a reference to Mark and Davis’ gross incompetence at life. It also had to do with the film’s signature scene in which Sheridan spikes his handlers’ generic colas, causing Mark to produce a geyser of diarrhea in their motel room. “It’s a top-three poo scene in cinematic history. It’s up there with Jeff Daniels in Dumb and Dumber ,” Franco states. “I remember calling my wife [Alison Brie] after that day and telling her I just did the craziest thing I’ve ever done on camera, which is saying a lot because I’ve done so many fucked-up things on camera. But I hold to that statement, and I’m pretty confident that it’s a violent moment people will talk about afterward.” The pic premiered at 2026’s Sundance Film Festival before securing theatrical distribution from IFC the following month. The deal was not contingent on a title change, but Team Shitheads , once they learned about the realities of promotion, realized that they’d only be making it harder for their small throwback comedy to gain traction. Thus, they landed on Idiots to keep the tontal spirit of the original intact. All in all, Franco hopes Idiots can do its part to bring back a brand of comedy that has largely disappeared from multiplexes. “ Idiots hearkens back to comedies from the early 2000s: The Hangover , Superbad , Pineapple Express , Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle ,” Franco says. “There are other moments besides the diarrhea scene that’ll shock audiences. I have personally missed these types of comedies. So I hope people check it out because, for us to be able to make more comedies again, people need to see the rare ones that do get made.” Below, during a recent conversation with THR , Franco also discusses his future as a director, before updating his status on 24 Jump Street and Now You See Me 4 . *** You don’t look like Alison Brie. ( Franco is using his wife’s Zoom account. ) I like to get people’s hopes up and then slash them when I finally appear on screen. You look more like the French Dip-hating Dave Franco . ( Laughs .) Wow, you’ve done your research. Dave Franco as Mark in Macon Blair’s Idiots Courtesy of IFC I keep tabs on the situation. So a script called The Shitheads shows up in your inbox one day. It’s from Macon Blair of Blue Ruin fame. Were you already familiar with the work he and Jeremy Saulnier have done together? Big time. I re-watch Blue Ruin every single year. It’s probably the movie I recommend to people more than any other. It was made for less than half a million dollars, and it’s a perfect, taut thriller. So that was my introduction to Macon as an actor. Then I saw the first movie he wrote and directed, I Don’t Feel at Home in This World Anymore , and that’s when I reached out to Macon to say, “I love your shit. I will do anything with you.” This was nearly 10 years ago now [in 2017], and at the time, he sent me the script for The Shitheads . But I was too young to play the Mark role that I ultimately played. So it wasn’t meant to be, and we amicably parted ways Eight years then passed, and I reached out to him again to say, “Hey man, I’m old now. Let’s go! Whatever happened to that project?” Then he told me that it almost went, but it fell apart. So I said, “No pressure, but I’m here. If I can help in any way as a producer, I’d love to come in and help find the money.” And he said, “Alright, let’s give it a shot.” So I’ve basically been stalking Macon for the past ten years in trying to collaborate with him. Do you often play the long game? If I see a movie that I love, especially by a first-time director, I will reach out to them and let them know how much I love their work. Part of that is obviously wanting to work with them myself, but another part is that we don’t tell each other enough how much we enjoy each other’s work. There’s such a competitive spirit within the industry that I just want to put out some good vibes, especially if it’s someone’s first time putting out a movie. I just want to send them some love. So I guess I play the long game sometimes, but it doesn’t normally lead to collaboration. More often than not, it has led to friendship. I’ll meet up with people every once in a while to talk film, and one of those people is Jeremy Saulnier. I reached out to him about Blue Ruin . As you mentioned, the Shitheads script has had quite a history the last 13 years. It once had Luke Wilson and Tracy Morgan attached to it in 2017. Macon did tell me that he aged the piece down a little bit because you and O’Shea Jackson Jr. are still younger than that combo would’ve been at the time. But how noticeable were those changes from your perspective? If I’m being honest, not a ton changed. It was more just practicalities like, “Hey, we don’t have enough time or money to do some set piece, so we had to cut it.” But for the most part, the script has remained untouched, which speaks to just how timeless this story is and how iconic these characters are. It stood the test of time, and there weren’t a bunch of rewrites just to make it more modern. You’ve always been able to play younger, and I still think you can play younger. Has that been a blessing for the most part? Or has it worked against you like it originally did with The Shitheads in 2017? It’s a tough question to answer. I’m sure it’s gone both ways where it’s benefited me in certain circumstances and then been detrimental in others. But for this film, I did want to look slightly older than I typically do. I did my absolute best to grow out my facial hair, and it came in nice and scraggly. I learned that I can grow a pretty strong goatee, but the sides are nasty and patchy. So it worked beautifully for this character who’s a full-on shithead. Dave Franco as Mark in Macon Blair’s Idiots Courtesy of IFC 6 Balloons (2018) was the more dramatic portrayal, but coming out of The Studio season one’s penultimate drug episode, were you hesitant at all to play another character who’s drugged out of his mind? You’re the first person to ever connect 6 Balloons to The Studio , and I appreciate that. I played a heroin addict in 6 Balloons , and it’s a hardcore drama. Leading up to filming, I lost 20 pounds in a month. I’m not a very big guy as is, so that was a significant portion of my body weight. I was not a happy person, as you can imagine. But I wanted to take myself out of my comfort zone in order to try something new. And even though it’s a very small movie that not a ton of people have seen, it’s interesting how much it still comes up. It usually happens when directors are reaching out to me about slightly more serious projects that they’re working on, and then they’ll point to my performance in that. So it means a lot just because we put a lot into that one. But when I’m playing “Dave Franco” on The Studio — and I’m inebriated on alcohol, weed, cocaine and mushrooms at the same time — I can push the boundaries a little bit more. I can be a little sillier and a little more over the top. It’s a more manic version of being drugged out. In Idiots , my character partakes in drugs as well, but it’s a different kind of drug trip. This is more of a sink-into-the-couch type of trip. If someone says the wrong trigger word, it sends Mark spiraling into hell. So I like to believe that I have a lot of range when it comes to playing drug addicts. The funniest part of Idiots to me is how Mark is constantly trying to relate to people that he has absolutely nothing in common with, such as the scene in the bathroom with Sheridan (Mason Thames) or the scene coming out of the bathroom with the motel clerk: “You’re a man who takes pride in what he does; I am too.” Like you said, he truly is full of shit. Yeah, he really likes to believe he’s a hero, and he has a strong lack of self-awareness. He means well, but he just doesn’t know how he’s coming across to others. He says to Sheridan, “Guys like you and me, we’re used to being up in the high steel.” So there’s nothing more fun to play than a cocky fucking idiot — someone so convinced he’s a great person, and the smartest guy in the room, when in reality, he’s just a shithead. Macon explained the title saga to me, but did you fully expect the Shitheads title to change at some point? If I’m being totally honest, once we got through Sundance with that title, I had hopes that we could somehow take it to the finish line. But we had a very open, honest conversation with our distributor, IFC. And to their credit, they said, “Hey, we’re willing to ride this title. If you guys want to go punk rock, we are right there with you. But we have to let you know that it limits us in terms of where we can market this film. You can’t just have the word shit on a giant billboard in Hollywood.” Ultimately, we put so much work into this film, and because we want as many people to see it as possible, that’s why we pivoted. There’s a Lars von Trier movie called The Idiots , but no one had taken the cleaner version of Idiots , so we jumped on it. Yeah, it’s now the movie’s second Lars von Trier reference. You gotta love the double Lars von Trier reference. O’Shea Jackson Jr.’s Davis, Dave Franco’s Mark and Mason Thames’ Sheridan in Macon Blair’s Idiots Courtesy of IFC Entertainment I’m glad they kept Sheridan’s “shitheads” line in the movie as a nod to the former title and the explosive motel scene. I know they changed the line to “idiots” in the trailer, but if you were forced to do so in the movie, would you have protested that choice to ADR the new title? Yeah, there’s no reason to change that line just because that’s how it’s represented in the trailer. Just let it play out the way we intended when we shot it. O’Shea’s character goes off on Mason’s character after that “shitheads” line, and Mark quietly laughs as this mostly measured guy finally loses his cool. But I did wonder if you actually broke ever so slightly there given how sudden and strong the outburst is. That was definitely intentional. That was my character being so giddy and pleased by the fact that Sheridan is finally being put in his place. He’s also entertained by the idea of this man of God stepping outside of his comfort zone and swearing in a way that he probably never has before. So there’s a lot for Mark to be titillated by in that moment. I have to tell you a story about the time I saw Together . I was standing behind a critic as he was giving his comment to the studio rep. And he remarked, “I liked the movie, but the two leads had absolutely no chemistry.” And then the rep and I both responded in unison: “Dude, they’re married.” Hilarity then ensued once he realized his oversight, and I still tease him about it to this day. I appreciate you standing up for me, but to be fair, there are married couples that don’t have chemistry together on screen. We actually feared that that might be the case. And while I’m never one to pat myself on the back, that is not an issue with that film. The chemistry is fucking there. ( Laughs .) I think some people mistake chemistry for characters just not liking each other. So our characters are definitely at odds for most of that film, but we’re flowing off each other in an objectively smooth and electric way. Dave Franco and Alison Brie in Together Germain McMicking/Courtesy of NEON You’ve probably been told that you’ve got good chemistry with other actors throughout your career. But I always hesitate to make that assumption because only the scene partners truly know whether they have good chemistry or not. What percentage of the time is it actually good chemistry versus good acting and good editing? There’s been situations where it’s known that certain people hated each other on set, and then they have “great chemistry” when you see the final product. So there are cases like that, but more often than not, if they have good chemistry on set, you’re going to feel it when you see them on the big screen. For me, I’ve made a conscious effort, especially in the last decade, to surround myself with people that I know and love, whether that’s my best friends or my wife. When I’m surrounded by people that I feel comfortable with, that allows me to be free and open and take risks. I know I’m going to fall on my face sometimes, but I also know that no one is going to judge me. They’ll keep encouraging me to try weird shit, and that’s when the best stuff comes. I last spoke to you for The Rental , so what’s up with writer-director Dave Franco? Have Obsession and Backrooms motivated you to make another horror movie? I definitely will direct again, and I really believe that the next movie I direct will be a horror film. That said, when you’re directing something, you’re focused on that project for years at a time, and it takes everything out of you. So I’m just not currently in the state of mind to dedicate myself to one project like that. But I’ve been able to scratch that itch by being a producer on films like Idiots that I’m also acting in. I can still be a part of all the conversations from the ground up and through the release of the film. So that’s been really fun and satisfying for me, and it still allows me to bounce around to many different projects. Do you know yet if you’re going to be in 24 Jump Street ? The truth is I don’t know yet. I have let them know how much I adore the franchise and that I’m here if they need me — but if Eric Molson doesn’t naturally fit into the story, I understand. Do you think Now You 4 Me is going to happen? I think it’s going under the name of 4 Now You See Me: 4 Now You Don’t. ( Laughs .) You’ve clearly workshopped this title. ( Laughs .) I’ve heard that there’s a script in the works, but I haven’t seen anything. That’s as much as I know at this point. For the sake of inspiration, The Studio welcomed any and all industry stories from the cast and crew. Did you ever offer up your experience on the 2019 motion picture 6 Underground ? ( Laughs and responds sarcastically. ) Why do you assume that movie spawned production stories? Well, I asked you about it during The Rental , and while you said it was 50 times crazier than I could possibly imagine, you also said it was better suited for an off-the-record dinner conversation. ( Laughs .) With The Studio , the truth is I wasn’t on that set long enough for them to be mining stories from me. I wasn’t around during pre-production or the whole writing process. But 6 Underground was a whirlwind. I played a [getaway] driver who drives around the streets of Florence, Italy, but I didn’t expect to actually do a lot of the driving with Ryan Reynolds in the passenger seat — plus Mélanie Laurent and Adria Arjona in the backseat. There was a moment when I was doing donuts next to a world-famous museum in Florence, and if I hit something, I could have literally destroyed a piece of history. Looking back, it was a slightly idiotic thing to do, and I blame myself. I should have just handed the wheel over to my stunt double. Decades from now, when you and your wife are swapping set stories like the one you just shared, what day on Idiots will you likely bring up first? You know it has to be the day of the diarrhea scene. It’s a top-three poo scene in cinematic history. It’s up there with Jeff Daniels in Dumb and Dumber . I remember calling my wife after that day and telling her I just did the craziest thing I’ve ever done on camera, which is saying a lot because I’ve done so many fucked-up things on camera. But I hold to that statement, and I’m pretty confident that it’s a violent moment people will talk about afterward. The cast and crew experienced it for the first time together. We never tested the rig before cameras rolled on the day, and it was so volcanic that everyone on set immediately started cracking up. But the camera was still on me as I was losing my faculties in this delirious state, so I had to stay in character and pretend like nothing was happening. We did two takes, and on the second take, we decided to add a little texture with some mashed-up Cocoa Krispies. Raunchy comedies like this used to be common. Yeah, Idiots is meant to be a throwback comedy. It hearkens back to comedies from the early 2000s: The Hangover , Superbad , Pineapple Express , Harold & Kumar Go to White Castle . It’s a movie that goes hard. There are other moments besides the diarrhea scene that’ll shock audiences. They won’t believe how far we push things in this. I have personally missed these types of comedies, and I have heard from many other people who feel the same way. So I hope people check it out because, for us to be able to make more comedies again, people need to see the rare ones that do get made. Did the MPA force Macon to cut the diarrhea scene down at all? There was no conversation about that. They were like, “Get rid of the title Shitheads , but show the gnarliest shit scene possible.” Respect. *** Idiots is now playing in movie theaters nationwide. THR

articles.title: Meg Stalter on ‘Oh, Mary’, Advice for Bowen Yang and Preparing Her Emmys Red Carpet Look With Paul Downs: ‘It’s in the Works’
articles.full_text: If you purchase an independently reviewed product or service through a link on our website, Variety may receive an affiliate commission. Meg Stalter is never not in character. This summer alone, the comedian has spent eight shows a week playing a boozy, bratty Mary Todd Lincoln in Cole Escola’s “Oh, Mary!,” taking over Broadway’s starry title role after Maya Rudolph and following previous Marys including Escola and Jinkx Monsoon. Her 10-week run, which ends in September, comes just months after “Hacks” wrapped its five-season run — and earned a record-breaking 24 Emmy nominations for its final season, including Stalter’s first individual nod for supporting actress in a comedy for playing Kayla. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It While Escola’s catastrophically theatrical first lady has now been played by a growing roster of performers (Bowen Yang is set to replace Stalter next month), the comedian has put her own distinctly juvenile stamp on Mary. “I definitely feel like my Mary’s very childish,” she says. “There’s a lot of sticking my tongue out, I feel like I’m doing a lot of tongue choreography.” Somewhere amid eight-show weeks and an upcoming trip to the Emmys, Stalter has also apparently become a home cook. That newfound hobby made her an apt partner for the food brand Knorr, which tapped the comedian this summer for its “Ultimate Chicken Roast,” a new campaign built around its Chicken Bouillon and Premium Flavor Base . The partnership included a “Chicken Roast” event in New York earlier this month, where guests were served Knorr-seasoned dishes by partner chef Sohla El-Waylly while Stalter took the mic. Following the roast, Variety caught up with Stalter to talk her newfound love for cooking, “Oh, Mary” and what we can expect from her Emmys red carpet look: What advice did the previous Marys, like Maya Rudolph or Cole Escola, give you? May and I were just talking about how it’s a lot of lines — that before you even go into rehearsal, memorizing as much as possible is really helpful. Which is really practical, but really important. It helped me a lot to memorize it before I got to New York. I’m shocked that you even had to audition. What was the audition experience like? I really loved auditioning because it felt like a movie moment when I got it. And also, I wanted them to know what they were getting. People know my comedy, but I’ve never really sung on…well, maybe we shouldn’t say that. But you had to sing in the audition, and I think they wanted to make sure they knew what my take was. It made me feel really confident because it was like, okay, they know what they’re getting, and I have proven that I understand the play and the character. So it was really fun, and I worked with a vocal coach. When you first saw ‘Oh, Mary!’, did you immediately know it was something you wanted to do? I saw Jinkx do it, and I love Cole, and I’ve always wanted to see Cole do it. When I was in New York, I finally got to see Jinkx, and I just have never felt more seen in a character. Which is so funny, because I’m not the president’s wife and an alcoholic, but the way that she loves to perform. I just fell in love with it. I asked my team if I could audition, and they talked to them about it. So I really, really wanted to audition and do the play after “Hacks.” I feel so lucky to get to do it. How would you describe the most unique aspect that you brought to the character? I definitely feel like my Mary is very childish. I know she’s childish in general, but there’s a lot of sticking my tongue out and being really…I feel very young when I’m playing Mary. Of course, everyone plays her as bratty because she just is bratty. But I think I’m doing a lot of tongue choreography. Are they recording it or anything? I’m so sad that I’m not going to be able to see it. I think you’ll have to imagine me. Unless you can get ahold of some sort of theater tape. Have you given Bowen any advice yet? I’ve told him that I’m so excited that he’s going to do it, but I haven’t given any advice because I think he’s going to be so perfect. Is there anyone you want to see next in the role? I want to see Cole do it again. And I’d also like to see just a regular person off the street do it. It should literally be someone who’s not acting at all. Just some random person who works at a company, like at an office, and then they’re chosen out of the office. They have to do it within two weeks. Heckling has become more common in Broadway audiences, especially when people come for a specific performer What has your experience been with Broadway audience behavior? We’re so lucky that we don’t get a ton of heckling. But I can tell when people have seen it before because they start laughing a little bit before the punchline. Once in a while, there’s a part where they might say what the punchline is. I’ve had that happen maybe once. But we’re lucky that we don’t get too much. It’s not heckling like, “I hate this.” It’s more like they’re laughing because they know it. Broadway is such a crazy schedule. How has that affected your eating schedule and home cooking? I was actually talking to people in the cast about this. I feel like when you’re doing a show every night, you have to find food that tastes good but also gives you energy and isn’t going to make you feel sick. Chicken is actually one of the foods that all of us have said doesn’t make us feel sick and gives you energy. I definitely have to think through the times when I’m eating more than if I were just at home. You want to eat a good meal before the show, but you don’t want to eat too much because then you’ll feel so low-energy. Have you always enjoyed cooking? I actually feel like I’ve learned how to cook in the last two years, and I love cooking so much. I used to not really cook, but now I cook a lot. I just think it’s really relaxing and really fun, and also a way to show someone that you love them back when you get to cook for them. At the Knorr Chicken Roast, I did get stocked up on the Knorr Chicken Bouillon so I have a lot of it. But it’s going fast because I use it so much. It does help make cooking easier because I’m not an expert chef, but I am getting good, and I do know how to do it now, which is really fun. I’m always looking for ways to make it easier and get flavor fast. Have you cooked the cast your Knorr-seasoned chicken? I haven’t cooked for the cast yet, but I need to. I really do. You’ll have to host them for your last show. Have them over and do another chicken roast, I guess. Yeah, definitely going to do that. I’m definitely going to have the cast over, and everyone should bring a side dish. Should I make the chicken? Lastly, congratulations on your Emmy nomination. Do you have your red carpet look planned out? Well, it’s in the works. It’s in the works… Is it coordinated with Paul [Downs]? I don’t know. [Laughs] Loading comments... articles.title: Payal Kapadia, Neeraj Churi, Subhadra Mahajan Among Talent Behind SASO, IFFSA-Backed South Asian Toronto Market Projects (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 9:15am PT Payal Kapadia, Neeraj Churi, Subhadra Mahajan Among Talent Behind SASO, IFFSA-Backed South Asian Toronto Market Projects (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Payal Kapadia, Neeraj Churi, Subhadra Mahajan Among Talent Behind SASO, IFFSA-Backed South Asian Toronto Market Projects (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago Sabu Unpacks ‘Arrested Memory’ Ahead of Venice, Toronto Bows as Trailer Debuts (EXCLUSIVE) 11 hours ago Fan Bingbing, Kim Jeewoon, Hong Kyung-pyo Curate Busan’s Carte Blanche as Festival’s Story Market Adds Thai Remake, Hong Kong Titles 14 hours ago See All SASO/IFFSA The South Asian Screen Office of Canada and IFFSA Toronto, in collaboration with Storiculture, have selected eight South Asian feature film projects for a new pathway to financiers and industry partners at the Toronto Film Festival ‘s inugural market, under an initiative called South Asian Screen Futures. The slate includes talent tied to recent Sundance, Cannes and Toronto honors, among them “All We Imagine as Light” director Payal Kapadia , “Cactus Pears” producer Neeraj Churi and “Second Chance” writer-director Subhadra Mahajan. Related Stories Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' The lineup includes six single-country projects from Canada and India, plus one additional entry co-produced across Saudi Arabia, the Netherlands and Canada. Popular on Variety “A Varnam in Silence” (Canada, India) is written and directed by Kalainithan Kalaichelvan, produced by Shaista Roshan and Alison Almeida. The film follows a woman who loses her voice after her mother’s funeral and her family’s belief that it was stolen. Kalaichelvan’s short “Karupy,” about a Tamil matriarch who announces plans to end her life at her own birthday party, premiered at Toronto in 2025 and was nominated for best live action short drama at the 14th Canadian Screen Awards. Roshan produced that short as well as “Unbraided,” below, while Almeida is currently producing “The Temple,” directed by Calvin Thomas and Yonah Lewis, and has associate-produced titles including Reza Dahya’s “Boxcutter” and Durga Chew-Bose’s “Bonjour Tristesse.” “Moh” (India), from writer-director Subhadra Mahajan, follows an Indian widow and her late husband’s lover as a shared trip reshapes their bond. Mahajan’s feature debut “Second Chance” premiered in competition at the Karlovy Vary Film Festival’s Proxima section in 2024 and traveled to more than 40 festivals, including Busan and AFI Fest, before a 2025 Indian theatrical release. She previously co-wrote Pan Nalin’s “Angry Indian Goddesses,” which premiered at Toronto, and served as second unit director on “Last Film Show,” India’s 2023 Oscar submission. “Pink City Skies” (Canada), directed by Maya Bastian and produced by Leslie Hope and Tina Vacalopoulos for Parallila Pictures, centers on a teenager who leaves home after being discovered with his boyfriend. Bastian’s short “Tigress,” backed by the Netflix/CFC Calling Card Accelerator, screened at Reel Asian and Reykjavik and was nominated for a Canadian Cinema Editors award. Hope, a Nova Scotia-born actress known for playing Teri Bauer on “24,” has directed television episodes including “Snowpiercer” and “Star Trek: Strange New Worlds” and produced the 2019 feature “Lie Exposed.” “A Suitable Wife for Her Husband” (Canada), written and produced by Avi Grewal and Sunny Gill, follows an Afghan-Canadian salon owner secretly seeking a second wife for her husband. “Soma Helang” (India), co-written and co-directed by Shubham Negi and Sourav Yadav and produced by Neeraj Churi and Beesham A. Seecharan, follows a woman working to hold her polyandrous Himalayan family together after a hailstorm destroys their harvest. Negi’s short “Hills Don’t Dance Alone” won a Netflix TakeTen grant and premiered at BFI Flare, while Yadav’s short “Malwa Khushan” won the Kashish QDrishti Grant and screened at the BAFTA-qualifying Iris Prize. Churi produced “Cactus Pears” (Sabar Bonda), which became the first Indian fiction feature to win the World Cinema Grand Jury Prize: Dramatic at Sundance in 2025 and opened in U.K. and Ireland cinemas in June this year. Seecharan’s credits include co-executive producing the PGA-nominated “Mediha” and the BAFTA- and Emmy-nominated “Beyond Utopia.” “Lefty” (Canada) comes from writer-producer Seth Mohan and director-producer Esther Caszo, and follows a young man finding recovery from anxiety and addiction through cricket. “Unbraided” (Saudi Arabia, Netherlands, Canada), written and directed by Razan Alsoghayer and produced by Shaista Roshan, tracks two childhood friends navigating a changing Saudi Arabia. Alsoghayer, who trained at La Femis in Paris and the British Film Institute, has screened short films at the Red Sea International Film Festival; her short “A Breath” was nominated for best student film at the 2020 Saudi Film Festival. Roshan’s other producing credits include “Karupy” and “Queen Mother,” and she is a 2026 participant in the Red Sea Feature Films Program. “Swarnapuchhri” (India), from writer-director Ritwik Goswami and producer Nidhi Girish Salian, follows a mother’s search for answers after her son vanishes amid protests against a nuclear power plant. Goswami’s screenplay won the West Meets East Screenplay Lab at the Dhaka International Film Festival. Salian, a former lawyer who was part of Vice India’s founding team, oversaw Prime Video’s GLAAD-nominated “Rainbow Rishta” as creative director at VICE Studios Asia-Pacific. Payal Kapadia serves as executive producer; her fiction feature debut “All We Imagine as Light” won the Grand Prix at the 2024 Cannes Film Festival and was nominated for best director and best foreign language film at the 2025 Golden Globes, while her documentary “A Night of Knowing Nothing” won the Golden Eye at Cannes in 2021. Screen Futures links the projects to sales agents, distributors and other prospective partners rather than functioning as a lab or mentorship program. Organizers describe it as project-first, tailoring outreach to the specific opportunities available to each film. The push forms part of a wider Canada–South Asia Screen Corridor, an effort organizers say will help stories and talent move more freely between Canada, South Asia and other international markets. articles.title: SCAD Savannah Film Festival Returns for 29th Year
articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 10:15am PT SCAD Savannah Film Festival Returns for 29th Year By Isabelle Farina Plus Icon Isabelle Farina Latest SCAD Savannah Film Festival Returns for 29th Year 3 hours ago ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Gameplay Trailer Shows Weapons Destroying Planet in the Series’ Finale (Gaming News Roundup) 1 day ago Dolly Parton Has One Last Song Buried in a Time Capsule: ‘My Place In History’ 2 days ago See All Getty Images for SCAD SCAD Savannah Film Festival returns for its 29th year on Oct. 24 through Oct. 31. The eight-day university-led festival in Georgia will host exclusive screenings, competition films, feature films, documentaries, shorts, animated films, panel discussions and workshops. Visiting industry professionals and students of SCAD School of Film and Acting and School of Animation and Motion Media can get to know each other through master classes, coffee talks, portfolio reviews and more. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It Variety returns with its “Artisans to Watch” hosted by Jazz Tangcay and “Pixels and Pencils” hosted by Clayton Davis. Popular on Variety Returning programs also include The “Docs to Watch” series, hosted by Scott Feinberg of The Hollywood Reporter, spotlighting the 10 best documentaries of the year. Entertainment Weekly will host its “Breaking Big” panel recognizing the next generation of Hollywood talent. Deadline is also set to return with its “TV Sidebar” highlighting new series on television. Last year, Davis’ panel hosted the directors of “KPop Demon Hunters,” “Elio” and “TMNT,” as well as the helmer of “In Your Dreams,” “Arco” and “Little Amélie.” Chris Appelhans and Maggie Kang spoke about the global phenomenon that is “KPop Demon Hunters” and discussed the collaborative process behind the film while celebrating the freedom to present Korean culture in a bold, fresh way. “Let’s make these characters real — ugly at times, silly, and real hot,” Kang said with a laugh. Tangcay’s 10 artisans to watch panel featured “One Battle After Another” editor Andy Jurgensen, “Sinners” cinematographer Autumn Durald Arkapaw and “Golden” singer and songwriter EJAE, all of whom went on to win Oscars. Durald Arkapaw made Oscar history by becoming the first woman to win in the best cinematography category. Speaking about working with director Ryan Coogler — the pair are reuniting for “The X-Files” reboot — she said, “We support each other. I’ve learned how to read the story through [Ryan’s] eyes, to understand what he needs to tell it and what is important to him.” As the first woman to shoot on 65mm, Durald Arkapaw said she was also grateful for the opportunity to continue opening doors for more representation in cinematography and to be an inspiration for female cinematographers. “It means the world when young girls, or film students of similar heritage, come up to me and express their gratitude, not just for the work, but for the fact that they can see someone like themselves behind the camera.” SCAD Savannah Film Festival is one of the largest in the Southeast U.S. with more than 74,000 people in attendance. Last year, SCAD screened 26 Oscar-nominated films, including eight of the Best Picture nominees. Stars who attended in 2025 included Best Actress Rose Byrne (“If I Had Legs I’d Kick You”), Best Supporting Actress Inga Ibsdotter Lilleaas (“Sentimental Value”) and Best Casting winner Cassandra Kulukundis (“One Battle After Another”). Over 200 SCAD alumni also worked on 21 of the films nominated for Oscars including seven of the 10 Best Picture Nominees, three nominees for Best Animated Feature, and every nominee for Best Visual Effects. Festival passes for 2026 are available now. Individual event tickets will go on sale Oct. 2 online at filmfest.scad.edu or in person at the SCAD Box Office at 216 E. Broughton St. in Savannah. articles.title: How ‘Idiots’ Director Macon Blair Conjures Big Laughs From the Year’s Cruelest Villain: ‘He’s Actually a Monster That Has to Be Captured Before More People Get Hurt’
articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 10:15am PT How ‘Idiots’ Director Macon Blair Conjures Big Laughs From the Year’s Cruelest Villain: ‘He’s Actually a Monster That Has to Be Captured Before More People Get Hurt’ By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest Tom Hardy Gets X-Rated About Kathy Bates, Raps About Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin and Recites Shakespeare on His Wild New Album 3 hours ago How ‘Idiots’ Director Macon Blair Conjures Big Laughs From the Year’s Cruelest Villain: ‘He’s Actually a Monster That Has to Be Captured Before More People Get Hurt’ 3 hours ago FilmQuest Announces 2026 Lineup: Jamie Lee Curtis, Britt Lower and Rhea Seehorn Among Stars of Genre Films at Utah Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Steve Swisher; Courtesy of IFC Entertainment “This guy really does need to be contained, because he’s got such potential for danger and violence and mayhem.” Macon Blair is describing the antagonist of his latest movie. He’s no stranger to menacing genre fare, as evidenced by the two other films he wrote and directed: 2017’s “I Don’t Feel at Home in This World Anymore” and 2023’s “Toxic Avenger” reimagining. But despite pitch-black elements, “ Idiots ,” in theaters Friday via Independent Film Company, is a rollicking comedy. In it, two knuckleheads — the well-intentioned and religious Davis (O’Shea Jackson Jr.) and sleazy bro Mark (Dave Franco) — get a job chauffeuring troubled teens to rehab. While their first ward, Sheridan Kimberley (Mason Thames), appears to be just another troubled rich kid, he turns out to be way too dangerous for his clueless caretakers. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It Having Sheridan actually be a cruel person was one of the key audience expectations the writer-director hoped to flip in the pursuit of laughs. Popular on Variety “It was about wanting to have the most formidable villain possible for these guys to go up against, and just play off the idea that audiences are smart and they’ve seen a lot of movies,” Blair says. “If you see a premise like this … ‘There’s two dumbbells that have a kid in the car.’ Your expectations are probably going to be that at some point along the way they will give him some advice or wisdom or a hug and he will be redeemed. He’ll get straightened out sooner or later. I really like the idea of taking the wheel in the complete opposite direction, where at a certain point you realize, ‘No, he’s actually a monster that has to be captured before more people get hurt,’ and playing off people’s expectations.” Sheridan’s cruelty also fueled the film’s oft-shifting tone, which keeps audiences uncomfortably guessing what cringy situation comes next. Without giving away too much, the film’s grossest scatological joke happens right before Sheridan has a sinister scene with a sex worker (Kiernan Shipka). “There’s this big, extremely over-the-top gross-out comedy punchline, and then about 10 seconds later, it goes 100 degrees in the opposite direction,” Blair says. “It’s meant to be whiplash that resets the tone of the movie. As soon as that happens, we’re back into the jokes, but in theory, that clenched feeling from that one moment remains, and that’s how you feel about Sheridan for the rest of the movie. When they’re running around the block trying to capture him, it’s not as cartoonish as it otherwise would be.” “Idiots” takes the structure of a road trip movie, as Davis and Mark work desperately to keep Sheridan under control and bring him to rehab. But along the way they reckon with Mark’s busted car, a werewolf-obsessed rapper (Nicholas Braun, in an outrageous role), a militant kidnapper (Peter Dinklage), bad drug trips and more. Beyond the plot, Blair and his DP Guillermo Garza hoped to give the comedy a dynamic visual style. Despite the tight indie schedule, Blair says all of this pressure helped make the movie stronger due to creative problem solving. “Because the schedule was so short, there were a lot of times where we had a very detailed shot listed/storyboarded plan going in. But we would get in the day, and there wasn’t going to be enough time to get all of it,” Blair says. “So a lot of times on the fly, Guillermo and I would redistill the scene and say, ‘OK, if we thought we were going to do this moment in three shots, what’s the version of it where it’s one shot and we just do it with a move?’ It was one of those things where the limitations of time or light or whatever forced us to … I don’t mean ‘not be precious about it.’ It’s kind of the opposite of that. To really drill down on: ‘gun to my head, what can we afford to lose?’ So the scenes become as specific as possible, because it’s really just the bare bones of what you very essentially need. I’m not saying, ‘I would go into another movie asking for fewer days.’ I wouldn’t. But I loved how that happened, because if we had the luxury of ‘you can shoot as much as you want,’ I don’t think we would have come up with the same solutions, and it would have felt different. It would have felt a little less sharp.” The one comedic element Blair didn’t want to stick his neck out for? The much-discussed original title. The film premiered at this year’s Sundance Film Festival as “The Shitheads,” but was renamed “Idiots” once Independent Film Company acquired and dated the film. It wasn’t a war Blair felt like waging. “That was part of the conversation we had internally about changing the title: It wasn’t so much a full ‘You’re not allowed to do this.’ It was just a list of limitations,” he says. “It was a lot of things that had to do with where posters could be displayed in public, and how you could obscure the names. It started to feel like it was going to be an uphill battle promotion-wise with this movie. Given that it’s a smaller movie and it’s coming out in the summertime, and there are a ton of movies to compete with, we didn’t want to hamstring ourselves with, yes, it’s a funny title, but to cross your arms and say, ‘By God, I’ll have fewer people see the movie to hold on to this title.’ It seemed like cutting off your nose to spite your face. So we said, ‘Let’s just pivot to something that’s not going to give us that hassle.’” Watch the trailer for “Idiots” below. articles.title: Tom Hardy Gets X-Rated About Kathy Bates, Raps About Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin and Recites Shakespeare on His Wild New Album
articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 10:25am PT Tom Hardy Gets X-Rated About Kathy Bates, Raps About Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin and Recites Shakespeare on His Wild New Album By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest Tom Hardy Gets X-Rated About Kathy Bates, Raps About Willem Dafoe’s Green Goblin and Recites Shakespeare on His Wild New Album 3 hours ago FilmQuest Announces 2026 Lineup: Jamie Lee Curtis, Britt Lower and Rhea Seehorn Among Stars of Genre Films at Utah Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Mark Lazarus, Hannah Storm, Fareed Zakaria and More Added to Paley International Council Summit 1 day ago See All Kristina Bumphrey/Variety Tom Hardy is best known as a movie star who plays rough-and-tumble characters, and he’s brought that energy to the mic on his latest project. The actor who records music under the alias Frankie Pulitzer just dropped a collaborative album called “Czarface Meets Frankie Pulitzer” with underground rap supergroup Czarface, which consists of duo 7L & Esoteric and Wu-Tang Clan’s Inspectah Deck. For fans of Hardy’s Hollywood work, he peppers in plenty of film and comic book references into his lyrics. The actor is no stranger to comic lore, as he played the villainous Bane in 2012’s “The Dark Knight Rises,” as well as portrayed Spider-Man antihero Venom in three standalone movies and a cameo appearance in “Spider-Man: No Way Home.” Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It In the song “Raw Forever,” Hardy loads his verse with references to Martin Scorsese’s 1999 film “Bringing Out the Dead,” Willem Dafoe ’s portrayal of baddie Green Goblin from 2002’s “Spider-Man,” Marvel evildoer Doctor Doom, DC Comics hero Sergeant Rock and Sidney Lumet’s classic 1975 film “Dog Day Afternoon.” Popular on Variety I’m Bringing Out the Dead like a paramedic out the Cage, directed by Marty Frank Pierce the gang’s here welcome to the party I be somewhat of a scientist like Willem Dafoe If you know then you know Goblin up crumbs Hit ’em with the fly kill ’em with the low Profile, no smile, exile the old style So vile, exhale the smoke cloud, blow trial Dog Day Afternoon When I talk Sgt. Rock on the block with the Glock aftershock from the boom Rip you out your costume Stuff you in the smallest locker, lock you in the locker room Doctor Doom how I’m the Victor the Scripture In the song “Mad Technology,” Hardy namechecks two Stephen King books-turned-movies (“Cujo” and “Misery”), and says something wild about the star of the latter, Kathy Bates . Elsewhere in his verse, he shouts out Marvel hero Thor, and later references Shameik Moore, who voices Miles Morales in the “Spider-Verse” films and starred in the drama “Dope.” You shit-for-brain no-name lame, that bites like Cujo I’d rather masturbate to Kathy Bates than hear you flow And you know that Misery, it loves company … Beatin’ P is not an easy chore like defeating Thor … Sprinkle Dope Across the Verse, shout to Shameik Moore At the end of “Grim-Visaged War,” Hardy recites Shakespeare ‘s famous “Richard III” monologue in a voice very reminiscent of his Bane performance. Lastly, there’s a “Titanic” reference on “Gnawing at My Rhyme Like a Poisonous Rat.” Yo, you act amused like DiCaprio scratching his pencils To capture your figure you love the attention that’s all clear Although Hardy has not spoken publicly about his work as Frankie Pulitzer, he is no stranger to rapping, having previously appeared on other Czarface albums as well as dropping a few loose collaborative singles. Hardy also recorded an album at the turn of the millennium called “Falling on Your Arse in 1999″ under the moniker Tommy No 1, along with his producer friend Edward Tracy, aka Eddie Too Tall. The record was never properly released, but it appeared online in 2018. articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 11:01am PT Music Industry Moves: Warner Music and Blavatnik Family Foundation Announce 2026 Grantees; Spotify Ups Joe Hadley By Jem Aswad Plus Icon Jem Aswad Executive Editor, Music jemaswad Latest Music Industry Moves: Warner Music and Blavatnik Family Foundation Announce 2026 Grantees; Spotify Ups Joe Hadley 2 hours ago Nile Rodgers & Chic to Headline DKMS Cancer Benefit Gala in New York 2 days ago Warner Chappell Music Promotes Gabz Landman to Executive VP of A&R 4 days ago See All The Warner Music Group / Blavatnik Family Foundation Social Justice Fund has announced its first slate of 2026 grantees – a docket that includes 17 organizations and an investment of almost $6 million. Since its launch in 2020, the $100 million fund has committed more than $52 million to organizations that focus on criminal justice reform, education, and arts and culture to help advance equity. This latest docket includes six new grantees, with a focus on organizations using music as a tool to drive social progress. First-time grantees include Atlanta Music Project ,which provides tuition-free music training, performance opportunities, and college and career preparation to students in under-resourced Atlanta neighborhoods; Brooklyn Youth Sports Club ’s VOICES (Vibrations Of Inner-City Excellence and Success), which helps Black and Latino youth express themselves through songwriting, performing, and sound engineering; Classical Pride , a music festival celebrating LGBTQAI+ composers and musicians across classical music; and Generator , the music development organization that ensures that artists, talent, and creative professionals across the North of England have the opportunities, connections, and support to build sustainable careers. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It The fund also remains committed to the pursuit of social justice through education. Over the next five years, it will support the creation and maintenance of 75 new prison libraries in the United States through new grantee Freedom Reads . The fund will also provide education to voters in the criminal legal system through another new grantee, Global Black Economic Forum , which works toward economic freedom for Black and marginalized communities worldwide through leadership development, conferences and summits, policy advocacy, and litigation. economic freedom for Black and marginalized communities worldwide through leadership development, conferences and summits, and policy advocacy and litigation + Spotify has promoted Joe Hadley to VP of Global Music Content and Partnerships and expanding his leadership in the music organization, the company announced on Friday. Hadley will now run both the Music Editorial & Partnerships teams, bringing his expertise and leadership to both. “Editorial is a key part of bringing an essential human touch to Spotify. The team’s judgment and taste is what fans and artists rely on. Joe’s capable leadership will keep artist advocacy at the center of our work and bring even more impact to the programming we do.” says Charlie Hellman, SVP and Global Head of Music at Spotify. J.J. Italiano will also become Head of Editorial, encompassing Global Music Curation, North American Editorial as well as overall editorial strategy and will report to Hadley. + Concord Music Publishing has signed Mercury Prize-nominated electronic-music composer and producer Floating Points (Sam Shepherd) to a worldwide publishing agreement covering future works including his forthcoming album “Mere Mortals,” due for release on 28 August. The project, a musical retelling of the ancient Greek myth of Pandora, will be performed at the Edinburgh International Festival on 28, 29 and 30 August, followed by a four-night run at Sadler’s Wells Theatre in London from 9–12 September. In a joint statement from Tom Deffee and Carol Crabtree at Solar Management: “We’re delighted to join forces with Concord. Sam’s creative world spans wide from electronic to orchestral composition, film scoring and everything in between, so finding a publishing partner with the global scale and artistic vision to match that was essential.
