The project will be A&R’d by Justin Bieber’s longtime DJ and collaborator Tay James and produced and co-written by Harv (Bieber, Skrillex, Summer Walker, Post Malone). Maguire first built her career as an actress and television personality, with credits including Netflix’s “Insatiable,” “Fear Street Part One: 1994” and “Are You There God? It’s Me, Margaret.” She launched her music career earlier this year with debut single “Passenger,” followed by “Kiss Me While I Cry.” + Lighthouse Management + Media has signed actress and recording artist Liamani Segura , who stars in Disney’s “Descendants: Wicked Wonderland” and “Camp Rock 3,” out August 13. The 17-year-old singer-songwriter signed with Def Jam Recordings and also scored a lead role on Disney’s “High School Musical: The Musical: The Series,” and released her debut EP, “Dear Little Me,” last year. Lighthouse also manages Jennifer Aniston, Towa Bird, Selena Gomez, Jason Bateman, H.E.R., Nina Dobrev, Gwyneth Paltrow, Paul Rudd and Mark Ruffalo, among others. + WME has elevated Sara Williams to Head of Music Marketing. Williams will oversee the 20-person music marketing team and continue to be based in Nashville and will now report to Kirk Sommer, Global Head of Music for WME. She joined the company in 2019 and has worked closely with Luke Combs, Duran Duran, Zach Bryan, Kane Brown, Jason Isbell and more. Previously, she led the marketing department at AEG Presents Rocky Mountains in Denver. Levi Jackson, who previously oversaw WME’s music marketing division, has moved onto WME’s Brand Strategy team as VP of Music, reporting in to group head Robbie Henchman. “Since joining WME, Sara has been an inspiring and trusted presence, built terrific relationships across the agency, and brought fresh thinking to our artists’ touring business,” said Sommer. “She is a natural fit to run our music marketing group and we’re excited to continue growing this offering under her leadership.” + PRG (Production Resource Group) , an entertainment and live event technology solutions company, has named Joe Simon chief technology & information officer, reporting to CEO Lawrence Burian. He most recently worked as an advisor to media and entertainment companies on technology modernization and AI strategy, and previously held roles at Entain, Encompass Digital Media, Vice Media, Univision, Condé Nast, and Viacom. “We are building PRG for a bigger future, and that means investing across every part of this business: our leadership, crews, talent development, and the equipment, technology and systems that fuel and connect our operations worldwide. Exceptional leadership is one of the most important ways we position the company for long-term success,” said Burian. Tuesday August 25 Grammy-winning singer-songwriter Meghan Trainor has signed with United Talent Agency for global representation across live touring, filmed entertainment, digital media, theatre, brand partnerships, and more. The signing follows Trainor’s on-screen acting debut in Ryan Murphy’s FX series “The Beauty,” and the April release of her seventh studio album “Toy With Me,” although she canceled a North American arena tour slated for earlier this year amid low ticket sales, citing the challenges of balancing work, family and a new baby. She also has appeared as a judge, coach, mentor and advisor on “The Voice,” “The Voice UK,” “The Four” and “Australian Idol.” She also published the motherhood memoir “Dear Future Mama: A TMI Guide to Pregnancy, Birth, and Motherhood from Your Bestie.” Trainor is managed by Nikola Barisic for Bond Artist Management and represented by Aaron Rosenberg for Myman Greenspan Fox Rosenberg Mobasser Younger & Light LLP. + The Guitar Center Music Foundation has named Valeisha Butterfield as its CEO & Executive Director, effective immediately. She will work closely with GCMF’s Board of Directors to advance the Foundation’s strategic plan, grow fundraising and donor engagement, develop partnerships with schools and community organizations and strengthen the reach and visibility of its programs. She was previously co-president of the Recording Academy and VP of global partnerships at Google; she currently serves on the Grammys’ Television Committee and is the founder of Seed Media. “Valeisha brings the rare combination of nonprofit leadership, music industry experience and operational expertise that GCMF needs for its next stage of growth,” said board president and chair Curtis Heath. “She has spent her career building organizations, developing partnerships and bringing people together around a shared purpose.” + Songwriter Phil Barton has announces a global publishing deal with BMG in partnership with Liz Rose Music , marking the next chapter in a career that has produced more than 900 songs. Barton first broke through with Lee Brice’s No. 1 hit “A Woman Like You,” and has had songs recorded by artists including Sara Evans, Gabby Barrett, Dustin Lynch, Eli Young Band, Priscilla Block, Matt Stell, Alison Krauss, Ashley McBryde and others. “We couldn’t be happier to welcome Phil to BMG,” says BMG’s Amy Hendon Scott. “I’ve believed in Phil since the beginning, so getting the opportunity to work together again makes this partnership especially meaningful. Phil is the kind of songwriter every publisher hopes to work with. His songs are honest, memorable and beautifully crafted, but just as importantly, he’s someone artists love writing with. He brings curiosity, consistency and an incredible work ethic to every room, and we’re proud to partner with Liz Rose Music as we help champion the next chapter of his remarkable career.” + BBR Music Group/BMG Nashville has signed award-winning Canadian country artist Jade Eagleson , whose track record includes four Juno Award nominations, 2025 Canadian Country Music Association’s Male Artist of the Year, 2024 CCMA Album of the Year, and 2023 CCMA Entertainer of the Year and Male Artist of the Year honors. In addition to signing with the label, Eagleson also expanded his team signing with Range Music for management, CAA for booking and Spirit Music, in a joint venture with Alliance Music Partners, for publishing. “I’m incredibly excited to begin my journey with BBR Music Group/BMG Nashville,” Eagleson said. “I have always had a profound respect for their team and the way they love and elevate their artists. The whole team feels like family and I’m so very proud to call this label my home. Regarding Range, that team has already been such a strong support for me, and we’re only just getting started. In addition, I love my agents at CAA, and I am so grateful that they rolled the dice on me and my obsession with steel and fiddle. For the Spirit Music team, I remember coming to Nashville close to 10 years ago exploring publishing options, and most folks politely turned me away because what I was doing at the time was too country.” + Independent distribution and services company Amuse has named Mark Mitchell general manager and Tim Cronin senior VP and head of music. Amuse is also announcing a new London office, located in Farringdon, from which Mitchell and Cronin will lead Amuse’s London, New York and Stockholm teams. Mitchell joins from Parlophone Records, where he served as Co-President for five years and worked closely with such artists as Coldplay, Iron Maiden, Gorillaz, Pink Pantheress and David Guetta. He most recently spent a year at 0207 Def Jam/Universal Music Group, and prior to Parlophone, served as GM at Atlantic Records UK. Cronin joins from FUGA, where he served as Senior Director of Business Development, leading business development and sales across the UK and Ireland. Amuse combines a human approach and data with the scale only a distributor can offer. Mark and Tim bring more than 40 years of combined industry experience between them, and will be able to bring Amuse’s unique offering to artists and labels alike.” Hook, AI-Powered Music Remixing App, Strikes UMG Deal as It Takes Social-Forward Approach to Fan-Created Remixes (EXCLUSIVE) AI Music Companies Udio and GRAI License Swath of Patents From UMG-Backed Music IP Holdings (EXCLUSIVE) Stability AI Raises $76 Million in Funding Round Backed by Universal Music Group, Warner Music Group, Sony Music Group and Electronic Arts (EXCLUSIVE) Music Companies Demand More Scrutiny of AI-Generated Tracks Before Chart Debuts Loading comments... articles.title: Owen Thiele on Portraying Queer Friendship in ‘Adults,’ Working With Connor Storrie and Being a ‘Nepo Grandchild’
articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 11:01am PT Owen Thiele on Portraying Queer Friendship in ‘Adults,’ Working With Connor Storrie and Being a ‘Nepo Grandchild’ By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Meg Stalter on ‘Oh, Mary’, Advice for Bowen Yang and Preparing Her Emmys Red Carpet Look With Paul Downs: ‘It’s in the Works’ 5 hours ago Jemima Kirke on Her Marc Jacobs Campaign, Fashion Week Chaos and Why Jessa’s Style in ‘Girls’ ‘Doesn’t Appeal’ to Her 23 hours ago The Best Celebrity Fragrance Campaigns in 2026: Zendaya, Dakota Johnson, Alexander Skarsgård and More 1 day ago See All Getty Images for Meta Owen Thiele has a lot more riding on “ Adults ” this time around. The FX comedy returned for its second season Aug. 27 with an audience now invested in its messy, co-dependent group of twentysomethings. Thiele, who plays Anton, says the cast spent much of the wait for renewal worried the show might not come back at all. “But I feel like now we have a little, tiny, beautiful cult following that hopefully will stick by us and get us that third season..” Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It That was the mood when Thiele sat down with Variety at an Instagram-hosted dinner at Palma in New York celebrating the new season. It can be hard to wrangle even the closest friends to a weeknight event, especially only one day after a booze-heavy premiere the previous night. But Thiele is unquestionably popular. Bowen Yang, Molly Gordon and Mary Beth Barone were just a few of his bold-faced friends who made their way to the West Village for a multi-course Italian meal and many, many dirty martinis. Popular on Variety Instagram also used the dinner to spotlight Instants, its newer feature for sending spontaneous photos through DMs, while Thiele is set to share behind-the-scenes content from the event on the platform’s @notfit4main account. Getty Images for Meta Getty Images for Meta Getty Images for Meta One reason for Thiele’s bursting-at-the-seams friend group is his growing list of Imdb credits. The 29 year-old also appears in Prime Video’s “Overcompensating,” where his character George represents a very different kind of queer friendship than Anton does, and he’s headed to the big screen in “Peaked,” Molly Gordon’s upcoming comedy, alongside Connor Storrie and Dua Lipa. He’s also writing “Off Color,” a semi-autobiographical Amazon comedy inspired by his experience growing up Black and gay in a white Jewish family. The project pulls from his fascinating family history: Thiele is the son of music producer Bob Thiele Jr. and the grandson of iconic record producer Bob Thiele (“What a Wonderful World,” which Thiele co-wrote for Louis Armstrong, might ring a bell.) Susie Essman, known for her iconic role in “Curb Your Enthiusiasm,” is set to play Owen’s mother. Below, Thiele talks to Variety about portraying queer friendship on screen, being a “nepo grandchild” and working with Connor Storrie and Dua Lipa: What can we expect from Season 2 of “Adults” — and Anton and Paul? Well, a lot happened. A lot happened. So I’m invested too. When I got those scripts, I was immediately reading. I was hoping that the kiss was addressed and it is but it’s addressed in a way that I think people wouldn’t expect. Like avoidant-attachment vibes? Sort of, sort of. It’s sort of like me in a relationship. I feel like you pull from your own life a lot for the character. Yes, I do, I do, I do. A lot of people would say I can’t act because of that. But the writers did such a brilliant job crafting this season because it doesn’t feel at all expected, and there are so many twists and turns that when I was filming it, I was like, “What? This is happening?” I couldn’t believe it. You’re in “Overcompensating”, too: the two shows reflect very different types of queer friendships. What do you think might have been missing in representations of queer friendship before, and what do those two separate arcs bring to it? I think “Overcompensating” does such a brilliant job of showing someone who isn’t comfortable with themselves finding solace and space in people who are comfortable with themselves. And I think what “Adults” does is show this immediate comfortability and coziness. Sexuality isn’t even uttered. But I think they’re two very important stories to tell. One is what I felt in high school. I came out in high school, and I was very much looking for somebody who I could relate to in that way, which is Benny [Benito Skinner] to George [Thiele]. And I feel like in “Adults,” I’m kind of where I am now, where it’s just unspoken and unsaid and it doesn’t really matter. I have to ask about “Off Color.” I imagine the “nepo baby” conversation is going to come up. How are you feeling about putting something this personal out there? One hundred percent. Everyone thinks I’m a nepo baby. I don’t think my dad was successful enough for me to be a nepo baby. But your grandpa was successful. I was on his Wikipedia today! No, my grandpa — I am. No, no, he was successful. I am a nepo grandchild, for sure. I’m scared, and I’m also ready. I’m like, you know what? I want to put myself out there in every way possible and see what happens. Some things will not be received well, and I’m ready for that. And hopefully other things will be. What have the conversations with your family been like while writing? It’s hilarious. It feels like therapy. It’s family therapy. My mom will be like, “I never said that.” And I’m like, “You definitely said that.” We’re all working through things, and I’m working through things as I write this show. I’m not running things by them. I’m more like sending them scripts, and my mom being like, “Why’d you make me a bitch?” Susan Essman is playing her. How did she get involved? I met with her. I sat with her and explained my life story to her, and she, for some reason, wanted to be involved, which is so crazy to me still. She’s Jewish, my parents are Jewish. But more than that, she’s an idol. She’s one of my comedy idols. She’s a comedy legend. So I feel very lucky. I can only think of her as her character in “Curb Your Enthusiasm.” What kind of energy does she bring playing your mom? My mom is a helicopter mom, but Owen in the show is front seat in the helicopter. He is obsessed with her being that way. So it’s the back-and-forth. It’s the enabling. It’s the codependency. She’s not really a yeller. She’s definitely a crier. She cries at everything. It’s a lack of boundaries. I haven’t seen Susie play this, which I think will be fun. Going back to “Peaked,” what was it like working with Connor Storrie? Connor is a dream. He is not only a very attractive man, he is so beyond talented. I interviewed him for my podcast, and afterward I was like, “Oh God, you are a dream.” And then I got to work with him after that. He was just down to play. Everyone on “Peaked” was just down to fucking clown. We were all down to do whatever Molly [Gordon] wanted us to do. Molly has such a great, beautiful, clear vision. What was it like being directed by Molly, who you’re so close to? She’s my best friend. It felt like we were kids again. I’ve known her since I was two. I’ve been in plays with her. She has directed me before. When I auditioned for “SNL,” she was very involved and was kind of directing my [audition] sketches for “SNL.” She’s been directing me for years, so this just felt like a natural progression. What’s your overall vibe with posting on social media? Oh my God, I love Instagram. I posted on Instagram twice today. In-feed. I think people are sick of me. I think people are unfollowing. I’m also like, who the fuck cares? Post when you have a hot photo. You have a hot photo, you want people to see it — post that shit. Who cares? Let’s not be precious with our dumps. Let’s just post when we like something. I want to go back to 2016 Instagram, where you’re posting a photo of something you like. articles.title: Rafael Manuel on Why the Golf Course in ‘Filipiñana’ Is a Metaphor for Inequality in the Philippines
articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 11:15am PT Rafael Manuel on Why the Golf Course in ‘Filipiñana’ Is a Metaphor for Inequality in the Philippines By Jazz Tangcay Plus Icon Jazz Tangcay Artisans Editor @jazzt Latest Rafael Manuel on Why the Golf Course in ‘Filipiñana’ Is a Metaphor for Inequality in the Philippines 2 hours ago Dolly Parton’s Musical Will Still Open on Broadway ‘As Was Dolly’s Wish’ 3 days ago Dolly Parton Honored by Kacey Musgraves, Keith Urban, Reba McEntire: ‘We Will Always Love Her’ 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Divergent PR Rafael Manuel ’s new indie feature “ Filipiñana ,” which opens Friday in New York, is set against a backdrop of oppressive heat and drought. The narrative follows Isabel, a 17-year-old from the provinces of the Philippines, who gets a job at a prestigious golf resort. Manuel felt the golf course was the perfect setting for the film to explore societal inequities in the country. With the very first courses established on American military bases, the local elite eventually took over, making the golf course a center of power. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It In his framing, the country club members are presented high in the frame to show the hierarchy structure, and the servants are presented low in the frame — an early shot shows Isabel sitting on the grass as she places a ball on the tee for a club member. Popular on Variety Manuel says, “That’s what attracted me to the golf course.” He adds, “When you think about it, it’s a good metaphor for the country in that it’s very large and situated on a very fertile plot of land that’s toiled on and worked on by so many people, but ultimately enjoyed and profited from by only a select few.” That, Manuel says, illustrates the class divide that has been so ingrained in the Philippines. Manuel spoke with Variety about how the film relates to the colonial past of the country, and the metaphorical symbolism of the golf course. He also talks about reflecting that through Isabel’s gaze and why she represents an awakening. Can you talk about your main characters Isable and Clara and what they represent and what you wanted their gaze to say? I very much get the notion that Clara is an outsider in all of this. The first image you see of Isabel is of her opening her eyes, and the last image you see of Clara is of her closing her eyes. For me, that’s very much representative of their narrative arcs. Isabel’s journey is one of awakening and remembering the past, seeing it and hearing it. Whereas Clara’s journey is one into slumber, inaction, passivity, and perpetuating the system. Clara is a tragic character. Isabel, on the other hand, is a heroic character because I feel like Isabel moves towards action, and Clara moves towards inaction.” What went into that casting process and finding Jorrybell Agoto as Isabel and Carmen Castellanos as Clara? Clara is a non-actor, but Isabel was in the short. It was only her second time acting, and she was a very inexperienced actor. My directing style is to try to get out of the way as much as possible, so I spent a lot of time building the world of the character and of the film. When it comes to being on set, I try to direct them as little as possible because I trust all the work that we both did in pre-production. Freedom is such an important part of acting because every single decision and gesture that they make, they have to freely choose it. That’s how you get good acting. What I really look for in actors is playfulness because I see playfulness as a sort of resistance. What we try to do is build all these restrictions around them and then see how their playfulness and their autonomy express themselves through the parameters we’ve set. Can you talk about working with your production designer Tatjana Honegge and cinematographer Xenia Patricia in terms of establishing the film’s visual language. What did you want to say? It was very much a team effort. I’d also like to mention Vincent Villa. He’s a French sound designer based in Cambodia, and I feel like sound has a very important role to play in this film — even in the visual aesthetic — because sound guides the eye on where to look. I feel like the conversations we had were about developing an oral grammar that could give shape, texture, color, and sound to this invisible violence that we were very interested in exploring. A lot of the conversations I had with Xenia were about my obsession with landscape photography and how it’s been used in different contexts as a colonial tool. Susan Sontag’s “On Photography” talks about how the American West was colonized through landscape photography. If you go through the Philippine archive of the turn of the 20th century — around the 1800s and 1900s — you’ll see that the Philippines was also colonized through photography. Simon Schama writes about this in his book “Landscape and Power.” He talks about how landscape is a projection of man’s imagination onto rock, grass, and water. So the question naturally arises: Whose imagination is being projected? These colonial themes — this dreamwork of imperialism — very much inform the visual language of “Filipiñana.” You’re constantly seeing characters framed in these wide landscapes, and their small actions become a form of resistance to the colonizing gaze. A lot of the film is slow in terms of pacing, allowing moments to breathe. What was behind this choice? The slowness, for me, has a twofold purpose. First, it really helps communicate the heat and lethargy — the kind of lethargy that the Filipino humidity and the stifling 50-degree heat of a Filipino summer can induce. When you think about why the Philippines has stayed the same for so long — why the country has struggled with the same problems for so long — I think the heat has a part to play in that. If you’ve ever been in heat like that, so humid and sticky, you realize quite quickly that it’s like a quagmire. It makes action so hard to do because all you want to do is lie down. The slow pacing of the film was meant to communicate that. The second reason behind the deliberate pacing of the film was that I really wanted to capture this Filipino experience of waiting for change. What do you want people to take away from watching this? I feel like so much of what we’re trying to do is create a space for the viewer to exercise their autonomy—autonomy of sight, hearing and feeling. I say that because the way the drama is structured is very minimal. I feel like conventional narrative, in a way, is a form of gentrification. When you take into consideration how so many spaces — not just in the Philippines but around the world — are privatized, you realize you can step out of your house and, in five seconds, you’re being sold something by a billboard. Actually, you don’t even need to step out of your house; you can just go on Instagram. So, we really tried not to be didactic and instead create an autonomous space for viewers to practice their autonomy — or to be autonomous, if they choose to be. So when you ask me what I want them to take away, it’s hard to say because they can take away whatever it is they want to take away. The film’s designed like that. I guess for me, one of the main things I’m interested in hearing from audiences after a screening is: How did they view the ending? Did they view it as an optimistic ending, or did they view it as a pessimistic one? This interview has been edited and condensed. articles.full_text: Aug 28, 2026 11:19am PT Disney+, Pokemon Company Ink Global Distribution Deal, Including New Stop-Motion Series By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Disney+, Pokemon Company Ink Global Distribution Deal, Including New Stop-Motion Series 2 hours ago What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ 1 day ago New York Comic Con Unveils 2026 Professional Schedule Lineup, Including ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Author-NBCUniversal TV Panel (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Disney+/The Pokémon Company International Disney+ has set a global distribution deal with the Pokémon Company International that will include a new stop-motion series coming in 2027. The announcement comes on the heels of “Pokémon the Series: The Beginning” beginning to air on Disney XD earlier this month, marking it as the first title to launch under the new global distribution agreement. The show, which follows Ash and Pikachu as they embark on adventures throughout the Pokémon world, is now available for streaming on Disney+ in the U.S. and some international markets. Related Stories Instagram Head of Product Design Explains Thinking Behind That New Logo and Responds to Critics: 'It's Important for Us to Embrace the Future' Instagram Unveils 'More Modern' New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It Titled “Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu,” the new stop-motion project hails from animation studio Aardman and will debut on Disney XD and stream exclusively on Disney+. Popular on Variety Per the description for the new series, “Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu”: Sirfetch’d and Pichu embark on an epic journey through the Galar Region. Together, they set out on a gallant quest to help and protect Pokémon across the region. Their missions rarely go as planned, but their noble deeds forge their friendship as they step bravely into the unknown where peril, alliances, rivalries, extraordinary Pokémon, and endless laughs await them. “Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu” creative team at Aardman includes director Tom Parkinson, creative director of IP development Nat McKay and model making creative lead James Young. The Pokémon-Disney distribution deal news was announced during a panel at Pokémon XP Friday, which is taking place over the next three days at the Moscone Center in San Francisco. “Pokémon has that rare ability to mean something to longtime fans while continuing to feel completely relevant to young audiences today,” Ayo Davis, president of Disney Kids and Family. “This new series ‘Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu’ brings Aardman’s signature stop-motion artistry with a bold, playful new perspective to this beloved world, giving audiences a fresh way to experience the characters they know and love. Along with ‘Pokémon the Series: The Beginning,’ these series are powerful additions to Disney XD and Disney+.” “These stories, full of adventure and heroism, all told from the perspective of Pokémon is made even more exciting through the lens of the incredible filmmakers at Aardman,” Pokémon director of original animation Phil Rynda added. “Audiences will be delighted getting to know the Sirfetch’d & Pichu, and wonderful cast of Pokémon, featured in this series. Aardman has brought Galar to life in a way that makes you feel like you can smell the air, touch the tree bark, and want to adventure alongside our series heroes.” Watch the trailer for the upcoming stop-motion series “Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu” below. articles.title: ‘Doctor Who’ On Prime Video? Amazon Execs Say They “Welcome Any Conversation Around IP”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Doctor Who’ On Prime Video? Amazon Execs Say They “Welcome Any Conversation Around IP” Edinburgh TV Festival Diary: Farewell To The Great City; YouTube Takeover; Channel 4’s Next Content Chief & Paramount Mischief Apple TV Buys Mackenzie Crook’s Comedy-Drama ‘Small Prophets’ View All August 28, 2026 7:57am The 15th Doctor regenerates into Billie Piper on 'Doctor Who' Disney+ Could The Doctor come calling at Prime Video ? Oliver Jones, Senior Commissioner for UK Scripted at the Amazon -owned streamer, set tongues wagging at the Edinburgh TV Festival when questioned if Prime Video could become the new international home for Doctor Who . “I love Doctor Who , and we welcome any conversations around IP,” said Jones, as he and Nicole Clemens , Amazon MGM Studios’ London-based VP of International Originals, spoke about a plan to significantly increase spend on UK content. While there’s no indication Prime Video is exploring a deal for the show, many at the festival later remarked the idea had not been dismissed out of hand. Related Stories News Donald Trump's Latest Financial Disclosure Shows Significant Sales Of Netflix Securities; Disney, WBD And Comcast Transactions News Prime Video Sets Series Adaptation Of Stephen King Short Story 'Crouch End' Disney+ was the previous international home for The Doctor, but it exited its deal with BBC Studios after two seasons of the show and spin-off The War Between Land and Sea . This came amid extremely high per-episode costs and the disappointing ratings for the second Disney-backed run. Watch on Deadline For Prime Video, the chatter came amid a busy week in which it has announced several UK originals, including docu-series on Lando Norris, and Peter Crouch and Abby Clancy and Stephen King drama series Crouch End , along with casting for Season 3 of LOL: Last One Laughing UK . Clemens revealed yesterday that investment in British content was increasing “across the board,” effectively sending a come-and-talk call to the UK production community. She made clear commissioning power was in London, adding further fuel to the fire. “The UK budget now sits in the UK, and the decision-making sits with me,” said Clemens. “I wanted to let people know that we’re open for business.” Cash will be made available for scripted and unscripted programs. Jones, the former Apple exec who recently re-joined Amazon, padded out the programming wish list. “We want broadly commercial shows, but they still need to have a sense of authorship, originality, with deep, multi-faceted characters and a real sense of lean and propulsion. “We’re a local UK team, we’re programming for UK audiences, and we’re programming across all of the regions,” said Jones. “Ideally, they also have universal themes, universal subject matters, which mean that they could travel and get bigger audiences.” Clemens added: “If it doesn’t work in the UK, it won’t travel.” Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: ‘Manifest’ Spinoff ‘Arrivals’ Ordered By Netflix
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” Tracy Oliver & Issa Rae Open Marriage Drama Heats Up TV Marketplace – The Dish Ellen Pompeo To Star In ‘Not A Sound’ Drama In Works At Hulu From David E. Kelley Productions View All August 28, 2026 8:28am L-R: Jeff Rake, Margaret Easley and Laura Putney Netflix/Becca Light Rake/Elizabeth DeCicco It’s 8/28, time for Manifest news. Exactly five years to the minute after Netflix announced it was reviving Manifest for a fourth and final season following its NBC cancellation, the streamer is resurrecting the series again, this time with a spinoff. Netflix has greenlighted Arrivals: A New Manifest Mystery , a sci-fi drama set in the universe of Manifest featuring a new cast of characters and storylines. The offshoot comes from Manifest creator, executive producer and showrunner Jeff Rake and co-executive producers Margaret Easley and Laura Putney; the trio serves as co-creators, executive producers and showrunners of Arrivals , with Warner Bros. TV back as studio. Related Stories Executives Chris Sussman To Become BBC's Comedy Chief Trailers Netflix Drops 'Unabomber' Trailer Starring Jacob Tremblay In Arrivals , when a mysterious plane crash-lands in Denver, the passengers emerge with no memory of who they are, where they came from, or why they’re here. A young social worker and a novice Homeland Security agent team up with the new arrivals in an attempt to stop a humanity-ending catastrophe, discovering along the way that they are all part of the very puzzle they’re trying to solve. Watch on Deadline Rumors about Netflix exploring a Manifest spinoff started circulating soon after Season 4 Part 2 was released in June 2023. By end of 2024, the project was in development at the streamer. By end of 2025, the spinoff had opened a writers room. And earlier this month, the series had started meeting with directors. Every step of the way, Netflix would not confirm the spinoff’s status — or even its existence — until this morning, on “828 Day,” when fans celebrate the series about the mystery of Flight 828, at 8:28 AM PT. Netflix has been leaning heavily into that tradition the way it did with Stranger Things Day on Nov. 6, announcing the Season 4 order for Manifest on 8/28/2021 at 8:28 AM PT and releasing the season’s premiere date and trailer on 8/28/2022 at the same time. With the Arrivals: A New Manifest Mystery title, the streamer seems to be taking a page off its playbook on another franchise, Knives Out , whose followups were tiled Glass Onion: A Knives Out Mystery and Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery. It is unclear from the logline what exactly the spinoff’s connection to the original series would be, including whether it would keep the 828 flight number to fit into the existing annual Manifest celebration. “Manifest” (l-r) Josh Dallas as Ben Stone, Melissa Roxburgh as Michaela Stone Photo by: Peter Kramer/Warner Brothers On Manifest , there was a time jump, not amnesia involved: after Montego Air Flight 828 landed safely in New York following a turbulent but routine flight that lasted a few hours for everybody onboard, they realized that for everyone else, five years had passed. “When the idea for Manifest first crash-landed in my head, I never imagined where it would lead. What started as a wild concept became something much bigger – a story that connected with millions of people around the globe,” Rake said of the series starring Melissa Roxburgh and Josh Dallas. “And thanks to Netflix, we were able to finish the journey and give those fans the ending they deserved.” He went on to tease Arrivals. “But the world of Manifest has more stories to tell. To now bring fans a brand-new mystery from that world is quite simply beyond my wildest dreams,” Rake said. “ Arrivals co-creators and co-showrunners Laura Putney and Margaret Easley have been my trusted colleagues for over a decade. Their contribution to the Manifest mothership cannot be overstated. It was a no-brainer to make them my partners on this spinoff. Together we’ve set out to create something bold, surprising, deeply human, and full of the kind of big ideas that spark conversations long after the credits roll. We can’t wait for a whole new audience – and longtime Manifest fans – to discover Arrivals .” The spinoff is designed to give Manifest fans more of what they want but also be accessible to new viewers. Netflix stepped in to save the original series following its cancellation by NBC after three seasons when viewership for the first two seasons kept surging on the platform in the U.S.. Since H1 2023, when Netflix started its semi-annual data dumps, the four seasons of Manifest combined have amassed more than 130M views on the streamer. Manifest Season 4 spent 9 weeks in the Global Top 10 English TV list and hit #1 in over 90 countries, though the number of weeks comes with an asterisk as the season was split into two parts, a move that typically prolongs a series’ stay in the Top 10. “We are thrilled to expand the Manifest universe with Arrivals, led by the original creative team of Jeff Rake, Margaret Easley, and Laura Putney,” said Jinny Howe, Netflix’s Head of Scripted Series, US & Canada. “Their return ensures the creative continuity essential to this franchise, allowing us to honor what made the original a phenomenon while introducing a fresh perspective for fans worldwide.” Rake, Easley and Putney executive produce alongside the original series EPs Robert Zemeckis and Jack Rapke of Compari Entertainment; Len Goldstein of Tall Baby Productions and Jacqueline Levine. Warner Bros. Television is the studio. Rake is repped by WME and Johnson Shapiro Slewett & Kole. Putney and Easley are repped by WME, Kaplan/Perrone Entertainment and attorney Jamie Feldman. articles.title: Gladys Knight Taking Break From Stage Amid Health Concerns And Worrying Performance Videos
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Gladys Knight Taking Break From Stage Amid Health Concerns And Worrying Performance Videos Tim Curry Remembered By ‘Rocky Horror Show’ Playwright Richard O’Brien & The Broadway Revival Anna Louizos Dies: Broadway Scenic Designer Of ‘In The Heights’ & ‘Avenue Q’ Was 69 View All August 28, 2026 8:54am Gladys Knight performs in Las Vegas last year Ethan Miller/Getty Images The great Gladys Knight will take a step back from the relentless touring that’s marked her 75 years in show business. In a new Instagram post – see it below – the 82-year-old “Midnight Train to Georgia” singer writes, “After much soul searching I’ve decided that I will be easing into fewer performances while focusing on transitioning into the next stage of my career and life moving forward,” her statement reads. “I’ll be spending more time on projects with my husband and visiting with my grandbabies and am looking forward to this new era.” Related Stories News American Music Awards 50th Anniversary Special Sets Performers Including Brad Paisley, Gladys Knight, Green Day, More News Barry Manilow Postpones Vegas Residency After Surgery For Lung Cancer: “What The Doctor Ordered” The announcement last night came as Knight was in the midst of a 2026 solo tour and a year after she participated in The Queens Tour with Chaka Khan, Patti LaBelle and Stephanie Mills. It was during the Queens Tour that her son Shanga Hankerson publicly expressed concern for his mother’s well-being, telling People magazine that the busy road schedule, encouraged by her husband William McDowell, was “detrimental” to her health. Watch on Deadline Knight refuted Hankerson’s claims, saying that her health and her performances had been “misrepresented” by her son. A spokesperson told People at the time that Knight’s attorneys were exploring “any and all legal remedies due to Shanga’s defamatory comments.” But more recently, cell phone videos taken by audience members at Knight performances, including one from a July 25 Hollywood Bowl concert, show the singer wandering the stage, her back to the audience and seeming to miss singing cues. Backup singers appear to be performing the vocals traditionally handled by Knight. Knight concludes her Instagram post by saying, “I’d like to take a moment in advance to thank all my fans over these last three quarters of a century for making a little girls’s dream come true and supporting her every stop of the way. I am immensely grateful to all of you and send my eternal love back to you. “I hope to see your smiling faces out and about and on the road,” she continues. “God bless all of you and hope to see you soon.” The Instagram post was greeted with a steady stream of praise and thanks from such artists as Busta Rhymes (“God Bless you and thank you Queen”), Jackee Harry (“We love you, Gladys!!!”), Andy Cohen (“You have given us so much!”), Kelly Rowland (“You have given us your ALL, Thank You a million times over! I love you Ms. Gladys”) and Holly Robinson Peete (“I love you @msgladysknight”). Knight is generally acknowledged to be one of the most powerful and poignant vocalists of the rock-and-R&B era with hits spanning decades, from her work with her siblings and cousins the Pips (“Midnight Train to Georgia,” “Neither One of Us Wants to Be the First to Say Goodbye,” “Best Thing That Ever Happened to Me,” “I’ve Got to Use My Imagination,” “I Heard It Through the Grapevine” and “Love Overboard” to her later solo work. Among her hits without the Pips was “That’s What Friends Are For,” the 1985 #1 smash with Dionne Warwick, Elton John and Stevie Wonder that raised money and awareness for AIDS research and prevention. articles.title: ‘Lord Of The Rings’ Producer Lines Up New “Large-Scale” Fantasy Movie ‘Wars Of The Drakons’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas AI Sci-Fi Series ‘Kira’ Heads To MIPCOM For Ex Machina & K5, First Look Images Welsh Hit & UK Oscar Hopeful ‘Effi O Blaenau’ Gets International Sales Deal Ahead Of TIFF Market Alliance Cinema Backs David Mamet’s ‘Speed The Plow’ & Lines Up Brazilian YA Adaptation ‘Diary Of A Weird Girl’ View All August 28, 2026 9:31am Barrie M. Osborne, Lord Of The Rings Getty, New Line EXCLUSIVE : Oscar-winner Barrie M. Osborne , one of only three producers credited with producing each of the original Lord Of The Rings movies, is lining up a new ambitious fantasy project called Wars Of The Drakons . The U.S. vet, also known for producing Face/Off and as an executive-producer on The Matrix , The Great Gatsby , The Meg and the live-action Mulan , is set to produce the movie alongside Jeanette B. Milio and Jim Milio of My Big Fat Greek Wedding outfit Alliance Cinema. Wars of the Drakons: The Seer’s Prophecy , which is conceived as the beginning of a franchise, is “set in the war-torn world of Aerion, where kingdoms battle for power with the aid of Drakons — formidable dragon-like creatures possessing extraordinary supernatural abilities. At the center of the story is legendary warrior and Drakon master Kale D’Sar, whose loyalty to a ruthless king is shattered when a mysterious Seer reveals a prophecy: the King’s own daughter, Princess Kahrie, is destined to become a great warrior, unite the divided kingdoms of Aerion, and ultimately bring an end to his brutal Blood Regime.” Related Stories News 'The Lord Of The Rings: The Hunt For Gollum': Everything We Know So Far News 'Lord Of The Rings' & 'Tomb Raider' To Be Housed At Fellowship Entertainment After Embracer Spin-Off The synopsis continues: “When the King moves to eliminate the child, Kale becomes part of a dangerous conspiracy to save her, forcing him to choose between duty, family and the future of an entire world. What follows is a sweeping journey of war, forbidden love, betrayal, magic and spectacular Drakon battles, as ancient secrets are revealed and the struggle for Aerion’s future begins.” Watch on Deadline The original story, which has been in development for more than six months, is being written and also produced by newcomer Carla Romero. The “large-scale fantasy adventure will combine immersive world-building with emotionally driven storytelling and have broad international appeal,” we’re told. Osborne, who produced the LOTR trilogy with writer-director Peter Jackson and Fran Walsh, told us: “I am always attracted to dramatic fantasy films spearheaded by collaborative, passionate, and committed writers and producers. Over the last six months of development, Carla has certainly proved to be a passionate writer and producer. Joined by Jeanette B. Milio and Jim Milio, we have an unbeatable producing team. I am confident that the film we will create will attract a four-quadrant audience. The cast, crew, and locations we are considering will add to the scope and grandeur this screenplay deserves. I look forward to including all of you on our journey.” The project marks the first producing gig for 82 year-old Osborne in more than a decade. He was most recently an executive-producer on Francis Ford Coppola’s Megalopolis , a film that reunited the two after they first worked together almost fifty years earlier on Apocalypse Now , with Osborne serving as a production manager on Coppola’s classic. Before becoming a producer, New Zealand-based Osborne served as a production manager on other classics including Bond movie Octopussy and TV series Kojak . Writer-producer Carla Romero added: “ Wars Of The Drakons is a passion project years in the making. I’ve always loved fantasy adventures that transport audiences to extraordinary worlds filled with wonder and discovery, and I’m honored to partner with producer Barrie M. Osborne and executive producers Jeanette B. Milio and Jim Milio to bring this vision to life. Through Wars of the Drakons , I explore the enduring power of loyalty and the choices that reveal who we truly are. My hope is that audiences lose themselves in its world, fall in love with its characters, and carry its story with them long after the journey ends.” Alliance Cinema most recently helped finance David Mamet’s return to filmmaking, Speed The Plow , with Anthony Mackie, Sharon Stone, and Ben Mendelsohn. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Netflix Drops ‘Unabomber’ Trailer Starring Jacob Tremblay Danny Ramirez Joins Michael B. Jordan And Austin Butler In ‘Miami Vice ’85’ ‘Heat 2’: Odessa Young In Talks For Charlene Role In Sequel; María Cid Top Choice For Role Of Gabi View All August 28, 2026 10:00am L-R: Josh Stern and the Duffer Brothers Courtesy Matt and Ross Duffer have appointed Josh Stern as president of Upside Down Pictures , the production company under their exclusive deal with Paramount . “We are beyond thrilled that Josh is joining us at Upside Down,” said Matt and Ross Duffer. “Not five minutes into our first meeting, we knew we had found the perfect partner to help lead our company — Josh has impeccable taste, a track record that speaks for itself, and a shared ambition to bring bold new stories to both film and television. It’s going to be a busy few years, and we can’t wait to share with you what’s coming…” Related Stories News Duffer Brothers Close 4-Year Film, TV & Streaming Megadeal With Paramount, Set Netflix Exit Executives Peter Chernin’s The North Road Sets TV Creative Exec Team Under Amy Israel Led By Josh Stern Under their four-year overall deal at Paramount that began in April, the Duffers will develop projects across film, TV and direct-to-consumer through Upside Down. Watch on Deadline “Ten years ago, Matt and Ross Duffer made a show that felt both wholly original and deeply nostalgic, and came to define an entire era of streaming,” said Stern of the brothers’ Stranger Things . “I’m honored to be partnering with these visionary filmmakers, and with Dana, Josh, Cindy, Matt, Jane, Don, and the amazing team at Paramount. As we begin this exciting new chapter of Upside Down Pictures, we’re eager to collaborate with world-class filmmakers on boldly imaginative and wildly entertaining movies and television series that seize on the power of genre yet are deeply grounded in authentic emotion and character. I’m thrilled to be joining the team and for this chance to tell stories that will connect with audiences around the globe.” Prior to joining Upside Down Pictures, Josh Stern was EVP Television for Peter Chernin’s North Road, and he executive produced Quinn Shephard’s upcoming drama series The Body, premiering in November on Netflix. “I’m grateful to Peter, Scott, Amy, and the entire North Road and Mediawan team for the extraordinary experience of working together and for their support as I take this next step,” he said. Prior to North Road, Stern was the New York City-based creative lead at wiip, where he developed the upcoming Apple TV series The Off Weeks, created by Alissa Nutting and starring Ben Stiller and Jessica Chastain; and Safe Houses, created by Gideon Raff and starring Ana de Armas and Jennifer Connelly. Stern also executive produced the Peabody-winning series Dickinson , created by Alena Smith, one of Apple TV’s first original series. He was also Director of Development at Darren Aronofsky’s Protozoa, where he oversaw development of Aronofsky’s films The Whale and Mother! , on which he was an executive producer, and also developed and executive produced Pablo Larraín’s Jackie and Tobias Lindholm’s The Good Nurse . “The Duffers have redefined what it means to build immersive, genre-defining universes for audiences everywhere, and our expansive partnership with them across film, television and streaming marks the start of a new creative era for Paramount,” said Matt Thunell, President of Paramount Television Studios and Don Granger, President of Paramount Pictures’ Motion Picture Group, “Josh’s remarkable track record collaborating with some of the most visionary artists working today makes him the ideal partner to help elevate and execute the Duffers’ boldest ambitions. We couldn’t be more excited to work closely with him in his new role at Upside Down Pictures.” Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Michelle MacLaren To Direct & EP James Marsden-Led Apple TV Series ‘Disavowed’ ABC Developing Drama Series ‘The Undertaker’ From Gabriel Garza, Hanelle M. Culpepper, 20th Television & Elevate Entertainment ‘Acapulco’ Star Camila Perez To Reprise Role Of Young Angie From ‘Power’ In ‘Origins’ Spinoff View All August 28, 2026 10:00am L-R: Gabe Garza, 'The Undertaker' and Hanelle Culpepper Bobbi Whitney/Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: ABC is developing The Undertaker , a police procedural based on the Swiss series Der Bestatter, from writer Gabriel Garza ( The Winchesters , The Flash ), director Hanelle M. Culpepper ( Paradise, Star Trek: Picard ), 20th Television and Elevate Entertainment. The Undertaker will follow Luke Conrad, a former police detective who takes over his family’s funeral home business and can’t resist investigating the deaths that come through the door. The award-winning Der Bestatter, created by Hartmut Block, ran for seven seasons on Schweizer Radio und Fernsehen in Switzerland. Related Stories News 'The View' Confirms Season 30 Cast In Promo, Teasing Big Premiere Surprise News 'Who Wants To Be A Millionaire' Summer Finale Scores Ratings Wins For ABC Garza will serve as writer and executive producer of The Undertaker, with Culpepper directing and executive producing. Exec producers also include Alex Cole and Joe Wiggins of Elevate Entertainment, and Michael Wenning. One Gate Media is the rights holder for Der Bestatter . Watch on Deadline Garza began his career as a writer in animation, followed by creating a comedy sitcom, and then becoming an executive producer on the CW’s The Flash . On the series, Garza ran the writers’ room and helped produce more than 100 episodes before moving on to write and produce for the prequel to the Supernatural series, The Winchesters. Garza is repped by WME and MetaMorphic Entertainment. Emmy nominee Culpepper has directed episodes of some of the most popular shows on TV: American Crime , Gotham , How to Get Away with Murder and Star Trek: Discovery . Most recently, she directed episodes of the Hulu series Paradise . For her work on the Season 2 finale, Culpepper received an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Directing. Her upcoming projects include Apple TV+’s adaptation of William Gibson’s science-fiction novel Neuromancer . She is also attached to direct feature adaptations of Amari and the Night Brothers and 1000 Miles . Culpepper is repped by WME and MetaMorphic Entertainment. Wenning is repped by Artists First. articles.title: Dan Stevens Hopes Prime Video’s ‘RoboCop’ Series “Preserves” Elements Of “Extreme Violence & Also Satire”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Dan Stevens Hopes Prime Video’s ‘RoboCop’ Series “Preserves” Elements Of “Extreme Violence & Also Satire” ‘Vanderpump Villa’ Renewed For Season 4 At Hulu CBS Shuts Down ‘Big Brother’ Live Feeds To Avoid Spoilers In “Unprecedented Twist”: “Go Outside, Smell The Flowers” View All August 28, 2026 10:10am Dan Stevens and RoboCop Getty Images / Orion Dan Stevens has been cast as the titular hero in Prime Video’s RoboCop series and is sharing what he would like the show to feature. In a new interview, Stevens opened up about what he’s looking forward to the most in the sci-fi series and hopes it “preserves” two particular elements from the original films. “Oh my god, I mean so many things,” Stevens told ComicBook about what has him excited about his new role. “That original is one of my favorite films of all time. For me and so many of my friends, it was such an iconic movie.” He continued, “I think maybe one of the first exposures to extreme violence and also satire. I think that’s what I’m most looking forward to, hopefully preserving those elements.” Watch on Deadline Stevens will take on the role of Alex Murphy and his cyborg alter ego in the show based on the MGM movie franchise. The eight-episode series, written by Peter Ocko, follows a giant tech conglomerate that persuades the city to place a powerful robot on its police force – a robot implanted with the consciousness of a beloved fallen officer, Alex Murphy (Stevens). Peter Weller originally played Alex Murphy in RoboCop (1987) and its sequel, RoboCop 2 (1990). Robert Burke took over the role for the third installment in 1993. A 2014 remake of the 1987 film had Joel Kinnaman play Officer Murphy. Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Renewed For Season 2 By HBO Max
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” Tracy Oliver & Issa Rae Open Marriage Drama Heats Up TV Marketplace – The Dish Ellen Pompeo To Star In ‘Not A Sound’ Drama In Works At Hulu From David E. Kelley Productions View All August 14, 2026 12:07pm Story Arc 'Stuart Fails to Save The Universe' HBO Max Stuart will continue to fail in his efforts to save the universe as HBO Max has renewed The Big Bang Theory spinoff for a second season. From creators Chuck Lorre, Zak Penn, and Bill Prady and Warner Bros. TV, the first season of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe is HBO Max’s second-biggest comedy launch ever globally, per the streamer. Not surprisingly, HBO Max’s biggest launch also was a followup to a hugely popular comedy series, Sex and the City sequel And Just Like That … The achievement comes with an asterisk because HBO Max had not debuted a new original comedy series in almost three years, since Lorre’s Bookie premiered in November 2023. Also, the streamer has had a gradual international rollout over the past five years and was not available in Western Europe until 2024 and in some countries, including the U.K. and Germany, until 2026, skewing global viewership comparisons. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery News ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’: Here Is Why Episodes Of ‘Big Bang Theory’ Spinoff Are So Short The renewal comes four episodes into Stuart Fails To Save the Universe ‘ Season 1 run; episodes drop weekly every Thursday. The spinoff lives on HBO Max alongside the mothership series; both are exclusive to the Warner Bros. Discovery platform (in the case of The Big Bang Theory, for streaming only). Watch on Deadline “We’re delighted with how this hilarious, genre-bending show from Chuck, Zak, and Bill has connected with the audience, both devotees of The Big Bang Theory and new fans alike,” said Amy Gravitt, EVP, HBO Programming, Head of HBO & HBO Max Comedy Series. “Along with everyone else, we can’t wait to see the worlds they conjure for these beloved characters next season.” A single-camera, sci-fi take on The Big Bang Theory, the spinoff stars four alums from the hit CBS sitcom. It follows comic book store owner Stuart Bloom (Kevin Sussman) who is tasked with restoring reality after he breaks a device built by Sheldon and Leonard, accidentally bringing about a multiverse Armageddon. Stuart is aided in this quest by his girlfriend Denise (Lauren Lapkus), geologist friend Bert (Brian Posehn), and quantum physicist/all-around pain in the ass Barry Kripke (John Ross Bowie). Along the way, they meet alternate-universe versions of characters we’ve come to know and love from The Big Bang Theory. As the title implies, things don’t go well. Those playing alternate versions of themselves so far have included Big Bang stars Kaley Cuoco, Kunal Nayyar and Mayim Bialik. “Chuck, Zak, and Bill delivered something truly special with Stuart Fails To Save the Universe — a completely original take on one of the most beloved franchises of all time that captures the unique essence that made The Big Bang Theory so special,” said Channing Dungey, Chairman and CEO, Warner Bros. Television Group and WBD US Networks. “It’s been an absolute joy to see audiences embrace this next iteration so passionately, and we can’t wait to continue exploring the multiverse in season two.” The series stars Kevin Sussman (Stuart), Lauren Lapkus (Denise), Brian Posehn (Bert), and John Ross Bowie (Kripke). Stuart Fails To Save the Universe , from Chuck Lorre Productions in association with Warner Bros. Television, is created, written, and executive produced by Big Bang creators Lorre & Prady and Penn. Kyle Newacheck is executive producer and directs multiple episodes. Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: Ron Perlman, Shohreh Aghdashloo & Cuba Gooding Jr. Set For Golden Dunes Jury Duty In Dubai
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Ron Perlman, Shohreh Aghdashloo & Cuba Gooding Jr. Set For Golden Dunes Jury Duty In Dubai Venice: Palestine-Israel Conflict Set To Be Hot-Button Topic As Open Letter Calls For Festival To Take Concrete Action In Support Of Palestine ‘Fjord’ Trailer: Neon Unveils Cristian Mungiu’s Palme D’Or Winner With Renate Reinsve & Sebastian Stan View All August 28, 2026 10:15am Ron Perlman, Shohreh Aghdashloo & Cuba Gooding Jr. Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Dubai ’s reputation as a travel and entertainment destination has taken a battering in recent months as the emirate got caught in the crosshairs of the U.S.-Iran war but this has not put a stop to the fledgeling Golden Dunes Festival. Ali and Zeus Zamani , the L.A.-based filmmaking duo behind AZ Filmz , are pushing on with a second edition of the event they spearheaded last year in partnership with Ben Coen, Scott Carlson and Don Worley. After an inaugural edition revolving around an awards ceremony, the second edition has been expanded to three days and will feature a program of screenings, panels and workshops. Related Stories Casting Ron Perlman Latest To Join Amazon MGM's Horror Film 'Seasons' From Drew Hancock Casting Charlie Hunnam Gets 'Sons Of Anarchy' Gang Back Together For FX Meta-Series 'Legends' The event announced on Friday that Hellboy star Ron Perlman , Oscar-nominated actress Shohreh Aghdashloo ( House of Sand and Fog ) and Jerry Maguire Oscar winner Cuba Gooding Jr. have signed on as the first wave of jurors for the second edition. Watch on Deadline Perlman and Aghdashloo will take particularly active roles, joining panels and workshops alongside fellow jurors and invited industry guests. “Movies don’t really recognize borders. A great story can come from Los Angeles, Tehran, Seoul or Dubai, and if it’s truthful, it reaches you. That’s what festivals can do at their best, bring filmmakers into the same room and let audiences discover voices they might never otherwise encounter,” said Perlman. Gooding Jr. added, “Cinema has always been one of the great bridges between cultures. Having participated in Golden Dunes in its first year, I saw firsthand the kind of international exchange that Dubai can create. It is a city where filmmakers and audiences from different parts of the world naturally come together, and there is real value in creating a space where voices from East and West can meet through storytelling.” The second edition will run from November 28 to 30, with the Golden Dunes Awards taking place on November 29th at the Belcanto at Dubai Opera rooftop venue in downtown Dubai. “Our first year was about establishing Golden Dunes. Year two is about opening it up. We want filmmakers coming to Dubai for three days, not simply attending an awards ceremony sitting in a room with people like Ron and Shohreh,” said Ali Zamani . “It’s about their experiences, discovering films from other countries and building relationships with filmmakers they might never otherwise meet.” The first wave of the jury panel combines several generations and areas of filmmaking. Perlman’s credits include Hellboy , Sons of Anarchy , Nightmare Alley and Guillermo del Toro’s Pinocchio . Aghdashloo received an Academy Award nomination for House of Sand and Fog and won an Emmy for House of Saddam , with subsequent credits including The Expanse and The Flight Attendant . Gooding Jr. won the Best Supporting Actor Oscar for Jerry Maguire after breaking through in John Singleton’s Boyz n the Hood , with additional credits including A Few Good Men , Men of Honor and The People v. O.J. Simpson: American Crime Story . Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Stuart Fails’ Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene “Was Terrifying” Tracy Oliver & Issa Rae Open Marriage Drama Heats Up TV Marketplace – The Dish Ellen Pompeo To Star In ‘Not A Sound’ Drama In Works At Hulu From David E. Kelley Productions View All August 28, 2026 10:22am Story Arc (L-R): Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus in 'Stuart Fails To Save the Universe' HBO Max SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 6 of HBO Max ‘s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . In Episode 6 of HBO Max’s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe, the quartet of accidental heroes Stuart Bloom ( Kevin Sussman ), Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), Bert (Brian Posehn) and Barry Kripke (John Ross Bowie) find themselves in a universe where people have descended from cows; they eat plants and chew their cud. Kripke and Bert want to leave, Stuart and Denise opt to stay, leading to the former duo being stuck falling in an endless void in-between universes. After meeting a new version of Raj (Kunal Nayyar) — who does not mention the broken device his post-apocalyptic self almost fixed in the first episode — and getting scolded by Stuart from another dimension, Stuart and Denise somehow order a second copy of the machine and soon find themselves falling through the void alongside Kripke and Bert. Related Stories News Everything We Know About 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 So Far News 'Backrooms': A24's Highest Grossing Pic Ever Sets Fall Streaming Date On HBO Max Turns out the horror on their faces was not just acting but the screams were hard to muster, Sussman and Lapkus told Deadline. “There were so many things that were crazy, I think being in the Matrix was insane, we were all with our bald caps in goo pods, and then we were on high wires, like flying, being dropped 30 feet in the air to shoot the falling-through-the-void scene, that was very scary,” Lapkus said about their experience filming Season 1 of the Big Bang Theory spinoff. “The high wire one in particular, the scene was we’re being dropped, falling through the air, and we’re supposed to be screaming,” Sussman said. “And what Lauren and I discovered both simultaneously the first time we were dropped, it was so much faster and scarier than we thought that neither of us were able to scream.” Added Lapkus, “When you’re actually scared, you can’t scream. It’s kind of like those nightmares that I’ve had over and over again, where I’m trying to scream and I can’t. When you’re falling and you’re actually scared, you just swallow it, we’re choking. Yeah, it was terrifying.” (You can watch the video below.) Speaking of choking, there was a lot of that in the episode with all the food regurgitating. “Lots of hay, lots of grass, yeah, lots of choking,” Lapkus said. Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. He will star opposite series leads Téa Leoni and Tim Daly, as well as recurring guest star Jamie Lee Curtis. Newlyweds is a later-in-life love story about a free-spirited woman, Jeanie (Leoni), and a buttoned-up professor, James (Daly), who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship. Recently divorced, James accidentally runs into Jeanie at a valet stand and is so taken with her beauty and spirit that they wind up having dinner together anyway. Tony soon realizes that his life with Jeanie is not going to be the quiet, stay-at-home lifestyle he enjoys, but he also knows he’d rather change his ways than live without her. Related Stories Casting NBC's 'Line Of Fire' Adds Sam Waterston, Campbell Scott & Chris Chalk As Guest Stars News Ariana Madix Sets 'St. Denis Medical' Season 3 Return Madrigal will play Dan, James’ divorced best friend whose plans for single life are derailed by James and Jeanie’s impulsive wedding. articles.title: ‘Hooters: The Movie’ In The Works About Chicken-Wing Eatery’s Origins
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Starburns Industries’ Tom Hanks Pic ‘Lincoln In The Bardo’ Adds Willem Dafoe, Jonathan Bailey & Peter Dinklage Melissa Hirschenson Exits Innovative, Launches The Hirschenson Group ‘Hooters: The Movie’ In The Works About Chicken-Wing Eatery’s Origins View All August 28, 2026 11:08am Original Hooters Archives EXCLUSIVE: It’s about to get spicy on the big screen — there’s a movie about famous chicken-wing chain Hooters in the works. Hooters: The Movie is being independently produced by the chain’s original founding partners and is being directed by Emmy-nominated filmmaker Jon Rosenbaum ( Woody Woodpecker Goes to Camp, Benchwarmers 2: Breaking Balls ) off a screenplay by Ed Droste, Phil Olson and Chuck Melcher. Casting is underway, led by casting directors Lisa London and Catherine Stroud of London/Stroud Casting. Based on the real events behind Hooters’ founding, Hooters: The Movie centers on Ted and Lenny, two lifelong friends from a small town in Iowa who accidentally launch a national restaurant empire, only to find everything they built threatened by the federal government. The adventure begins when Ted becomes infatuated with Diane, whom he first sees from afar when featured in a spring break commercial. Determined to find her in real life, Ted talks a hesitant Lenny into joining him on a road trip to Clearwater Beach, FL. Diane would later become the very first Hooters Girl. Related Stories Casting Al Madrigal Joins Cast Of NBC's 'Newlyweds' News 'Stuart Fails' Stars Kevin Sussman & Lauren Lapkus Reveal Filming Episode 6 Scene "Was Terrifying" “I think people are going to enjoy watching how we were really just some guys who didn’t know what we were doing, but had a great time doing it,” said Droste, a Hooters co-founder and producer. “There’s a lot of drama, but a lot of heart and fun too. And of course, our world-famous Hooters Girls are the real stars. For over 40 years Hooters has been America’s oasis in good times and bad. It’s time to deliver a taste of our big-hearted culture and famous humor to the world.” Watch on Deadline Said Rosenbaum: “From the moment I first learned the Hooters origin story, I knew it would make an incredible movie. It’s the perfect combination of a hilarious buddy comedy and an inspiring biopic for a beloved American brand: Two lifelong friends with no idea what they’re getting themselves into, a crazy idea they’re willing to bet everything on, and a wild journey that culminates in the creation of something bigger than they could ever have imagined. It’s not at all what people will be expecting – and it’s mostly true! I can’t wait to bring this story to life.” Production is being eyed for November, filming primarily in the Tampa/Clearwater area, where the original Hooters restaurant opened in 1983. Rosenbaum is represented by Ross Fineman at Fineman Entertainment and Brent Jordan Sherman at the Characters Talent Agency. Dog Days Of August: ‘Coyote Vs. articles.title: ‘The Dog Stars’: 6 Of The Biggest Changes Between Peter Heller’s Book And The Ridley Scott Film
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi All The Songs In ‘The Dog Stars’: From Hozier To Caamp ‘The Dog Stars’: 6 Of The Biggest Changes Between Peter Heller’s Book And The Ridley Scott Film ‘In A Holidaze’ Film Adaptation Of Christina Lauren’s Novel Sets Release Date At Netflix View All August 28, 2026 11:26am Jacob Elordi as Hig in 20th Century Studios' THE DOG STARS. Fabio Lovino/20th Century Studios SPOILER ALERT: This post contains spoilers for The Dog Stars now out in theaters. Ridley Scott ’s newest film, The Dog Stars , is based on Peter Heller’s 2012 novel of the same name. Mark L. Smith’s screenplay made several noticeable changes to the story, some of which provide more action in the plot and propel the film forward. The Dog Stars centers Jacob Elordi ’s mechanic-turned-pilot Hig, who is one of the lone survivors of a flu pandemic and follow-up blood disease, as he navigates post-apocalyptic Colorado and neighboring states. Related Stories Red Carpet Premieres ‘The Dog Stars’ World Premiere Red Carpet: Jacob Elordi, Margaret Qualley, Rak The Dog & More Reviews ‘The Dog Stars’ Review: Jacob Elordi Searches For Last Gasp Of Humanity In Ridley Scott’s Sharp Postapocalyptic Thriller He only has ex-military misanthrope, Bruce Bangley ( Josh Brolin ) and his German shepherd dog Jasper to keep him company, and when Hig needs space from Bangley, he flies out in his yellow Cessna plane to visit Mennonite families, whose leader is played by Benedict Wong, and provide them with medical supplies from a hospital in Denver. Hig risks contagion by the children and their parents to help them out. Watch on Deadline For differences — big and small — in the book, which generated a surge in the library app Libby demand by 268.5% the week of release, versus The Dog Stars film, read on. The Plane The 1956 Cessna 182 is described as cream and blue in the book. Hig nicknames her The Beast, which seems more of an inner monologue moniker. He uses it to fly the perimeter of his and Bangley’s little haven where they’ve survived trespassers and other threats mostly because Bangley picks them off with his long-range rifle. In the film, the plane is yellow. Jasper’s Death L-R: Jasper and Jacob Elordi as Hig in 20th Century Studios’ THE DOG STARS Fabio Lovino/ 20th Century Studios In Heller’s book, Jasper passes somewhat peacefully in his sleep when Hig takes him up to the mountains to camp and fish. The dog had gone mostly deaf, and he was getting old, so Hig’s decision to camp out under some frost ended up being too much for the canine. In the film, Jasper dies after Bangley waits until the last minute to pick off some invaders that target Hig and his dog. Bangley does this because Hig wasn’t thorough with his air surveillance and missed the people that came at him and Bangley. One of their errant gunshots found the canine’s heart. In both the book and the film, this is what ultimately galvanizes Hig to go fly beyond their shelter and search for more. He had received a signal from Grand Junction airport years ago, so he wanted to see if anything could be found behind that transmission. How Hig Meets Cima & Pops When Hig touches down in the book near Cima’s ( Margaret Qualley ) and Pops’ (Guy Pearce) farm, tucked away like his shelter with Bangley, he meets an aggressive Pops right away who shoots at him a couple of times. Hig doesn’t help by provoking him with scrawled messages on paper, but eventually they get past it and he stays with them. In the film, Sarah the donkey leads Hig to their ranch of sorts, and he sees Cima first, but Pops is behind him in the shadows with a rifle and quickly descends on Hig, telling him to unload his weapons and stand slowly. Pops does not want Hig anywhere on their property, but Cima engages in some conversation with the pilot. (L-R) Jacob Elordi as Hig and Margaret Qualley as Cima in 20th Century Studios’ THE DOG STARS Fabio Lovino/20th Century Studios How Cima & Pops Leave With Hig In the book, Pops and Hig slowly come to the conclusion that they can leave the farm all together in the plane. After working through the equations to balance cargo, fuel and the plane’s weight, it’s concluded that Pops will drive out onto the highway and then join his daughter and Hig in the Cessna after they’ve taken off to burn some of the fuel. The film sees them hastily get in the plane when a large group of hostile people find their farm and attack them. Both Pops and Cima get in the plane after they’ve helped Hig clear a path for takeoff by chopping down trees and throwing rocks out of the way. The Reapers In Heller’s novel, the looming new threat were referred to as “The A-rabs” who had somehow gotten to the country and were causing trouble. The film describes them as Reapers. Hig captured their graffiti in the beginning of the film, and a hoard of them — covered in facepaint — attack both Cima and Pops’ camp as well as Bangley, who is left alone when Hig goes out to find Cima and Pops. In the book, readers don’t get to fully see the attack on Bangley because it’s told from Hig’s perspective and he’s gone, but the film expands to show the scene, parts in night vision radar. Bangley’s relieving survival is part of both the book and film. Grand Junction Cima, Pops and Hig explore Grand Junction both in the book and in the movie, but what goes down there is wildly different in the movie. They both involve prompting by a transmission from an older woman’s voice. In the book, when Hig tries to land there, a trip wire almost snags the Cessna and pulls them down to their deaths in a crash. They then land still and discover an old couple, who they kill, living in the radio tower with way too many cats. The film took this part up a notch with a surprise appearance from Allison Janney as Darlene, voice heard on the radio and leader of a strange cult-like group who have been living at the airport for a while. Darlene used to be a flight attendant, and she still dresses the part. She only deems Cima fit to “keep” in their strange compound because she has doctorial skills.

Smith-Cameron As Recurring For Season 28 View All August 28, 2026 11:41am Dissney+ has greenlighted Pokémon Tales: The Misadventures of Sirfetch’d & Pichu , a new stop-motion series as part of a just-announced global distribution deal with The Pokémon Company International . Created by animation studio Aardman, the series will debut on Disney XD and stream exclusively on DIsney+ in 2027.
