articles.title: All The Songs In ‘The Dog Stars’: From Hozier To Caamp
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi All The Songs In ‘The Dog Stars’: From Hozier To Caamp ‘The Dog Stars’: 6 Of The Biggest Changes Between Peter Heller’s Book And The Ridley Scott Film ‘In A Holidaze’ Film Adaptation Of Christina Lauren’s Novel Sets Release Date At Netflix View All August 28, 2026 12:04pm (L-R) Jacob Elordi as Hig and Margaret Qualley as Cima in 20th Century Studios' THE DOG STARS Fabio Lovino/20th Century Studios The Jacob Elordi -starring and Ridley Scott -directed The Dog Stars adapation of Peter Heller’s novel features a soundtrack that fits the folk and rock themes and tones of the movie. Based on Heller’s 2012 from a script by Mark L. Smith, The Dog Stars follows mechanic-turned-pilot Hig (Jacob Elordi), who goes in search of survivors of a deadly flu pandemic and blood virus after living quietly in an abandoned airship with Bangley ( Josh Brolin ), who does not have as much hope in humanity as Hig. Related Stories Books ‘The Dog Stars’: 6 Of The Biggest Changes Between Peter Heller’s Book And The Ridley Scott Film Reviews ‘The Dog Stars’ Review: Jacob Elordi Searches For Last Gasp Of Humanity In Ridley Scott’s Sharp Postapocalyptic Thriller The film opens with Hozier ’s “Like Real People Do,” and later on, when Hig meets Cima (Margaret Qualley), he plays Caamp’s “By and By” for her on headphones because she says she misses music and dancing in the post-pandemic world. Alongside these folk songs, there are needle drops from Van Morrison, Dean Martin and Mick Jagger. Hozier’s “Like Real People Do” comes back around at the end to book end the story. For the all the songs in The Dog Stars , read on: Watch on Deadline “Like Real People Do” by Hozier “Heroes” Written by Jess Cates, Ty Kelly Lacy and Dennis Joseph Matkosky “Tupelo Honey” Written and Performed by Van Morrison “By and By” Performed by Caamp “Charmaine” Performed by Jack Nitzshe “Memories Are Made of This” Performed by Dean Martin “Fly Me To The Moon (In Other Words)” Written by Bart Howard (Sung by Allison Janney) “The Long Black Veil” Performed by The Chieftains with Mick Jagger

articles.title: Dark Comedy ‘Buddy’, Thriller ‘Colony’, John Boorman Doc Hit Theaters – Specialty Preview
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Apple TV Hikes Price, Will Now Cost $14.99 A Month In U.S. Producer Manny Halley Takes Over L.A.’s Pacoima Studios With Long-Term Lease DAZN Acquiring EverPass Media In U.S. Expansion View All August 28, 2026 12:30pm 'Buddy' Roadside Attractions New comedies mark the penultimate weekend of summer from Buddy to Idiots to Finding Emily . Korean zombie thriller Colony , from the director of Train to Busan , and superhero film Legend of the White Dragon (both from Well Go USA) join a handful of limited releases including docs Boorman and the Devil , The Cycle of Love and Hanging By a Wire . Horror comedy Buddy from Roadside Attractions, by Chris “Casper” Kelly, hits 1,258 screens. Set in the colorful world of It’s Buddy! , a fictional 1990s kids’ television show starring a bright orange unicorn and a group of children who spend their days singing, dancing and helping Buddy (voiced by Keegan-Michael Key) spread happiness. But when one child refuses to play along, Buddy is not pleased and cracks begin to appear in this seemingly perfect world. Certified Fresh at 87% on Rotten Tomatoes. A promotional video of Buddy playfully ambushing a movie theater employee has gone viral on social media ahead of the opening. Premiered at Sundance; see Deadline review. Related Stories News 'Coyote Vs. Acme' & 'Dog Stars' Barking Up 'Spider-Man's Tree With Summer End Near - Weekend Preview News 'Tony', 'Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma' Go Wide After Ace Debuts; Andrew Garfield In 'The Magic Faraway Tree', 'It Ends' - Specialty Preview IFC opens raunchy road-trip romp Idiots on 1,100 screens. From filmmaker Macon Blair ( The Toxic Avenger ), it stars Dave Franco, O’Shea Jackson Jr, Mason Thames, Kiernan Shipka, Nicholas Braun and Peter Dinklage. Premiered at Sundance; Deadline review here under its previous title, Sh*theads . Two unqualified bozos (Franco and Jackson) are hired to transfer a rich teen (Thames) to rehab when their straightforward gig quickly spirals into dangerous mayhem. Watch on Deadline Also from IFC, The Sun Never Sets by Joe Swanberg debuts at the Music Box in Chicago, expanding next weekend. Stars Dakota Fanning as a woman whose relationship with her boyfriend hits a rough patch just as her ex reappears in her life, leading to messy entanglements in the Alaskan wilderness. Premiered at SXSW; see Deadline’s interview with Swanberg. Well Go USA Entertainment is out with Korean zombie thriller Colony by Yeon Sang-ho ( Train To Busan ) on 411 screens. Stars Gianna Jun as Professor Se-jeong, who is thrust into a bloody nightmare when a rapidly mutating virus is released during a biotech conference, causing authorities to seal the facility. Trapped inside with no escape, Se-jeong and a small group of survivors must fight to stay alive while the infected undergo horrific transformations. Premiered at Cannes Midnight Screenings section. Well Go released a remastered Train To Busan earlier this month for the hit’s 10 th anniversary. The distributor is also debuting long gestating Legend Of The White Dragon as an event release for the three-day weekend and Wednesday, one showtime daily, on 596 screens. Directed by Sean and Aaron Schoenke, the film reunites the late Jason David Frank with fellow Power Rangers Jason Faunt, Cerina Vincent and Ciara Hanna. Forced to hide in the shadows, superhero fugitive hero Erik Reed/the White Dragon (Frank) must clear his name to reunite with his family. Standing in his way is a mysterious villain intent on his destruction. The release is timed to National Power Rangers Day marking the premiere of the original Mighty Morphin Power Rangers TV series in 1993. Rom-com Finding Emily from Focus Features and the producers of Bridget Jones’s Diary and Notting Hill , debuts at 678 locations. The feature directorial debut of Alicia MacDonald, written by Rachel Hirons and produced by Tim Bevan, Eric Fellner and Olivier Kaempfer. It stars Angourie Rice, Spike Fearn and Minnie Driver. When a lovesick musician is given the wrong number for his dream girl, he teams up with a driven psychology student to find her, sparking a campus-wide frenzy. Billboards in L.A. and New York have been offering “Emily-only” advance screenings at AMC Century City and AMC Empire 25 open only to people named Emily or their friends. Kino Lorber is out with Filipiñana , the feature debut Rafael Manuel, at the Film Forum in NYC. The scathing look at class hierarchy set within an exclusive private golf club in Manila premiered at Sundance, where it won a Special Jury Award for Creative Vision before going on to play Berlin and other fests. Manuel is in town for three sold-out Q&As. The Cycle Of Love by Oscar-winning filmmaker Orlando von Einsiedel ( The White Helmets, The Lost Children, Evelyn, Virunga ), executive produced by Priyanka Chopra Jonas, opens at the Angelika in NYC. The doc from Variance Films adds L.A. next weekend with more cities to follow Sept 1, kicking off an Academy campaign for the fall. Premiered at Telluride and has since played CPH:DOX, Sheffield DocFest and DC/DOX. The 1977 real-life adventure of PK, a 23-year-old Delhi street artist who picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile cross-continent mission to find Lotta, a woman who had captured his heart during a visit to India. David Kittredge documentary Boorman And The Devil from Yellow Veil Pictures opens in limited release at The Quad in NYC. Adds the Laemmle LA and additional markets September 4. After directing Point Blank and Deliverance , John Boorman was offered to direct Exorcist II: The Heretic . The film became a massive failure, nearly ending his career. Years later, cast and filmmakers discuss its ambition and artistic value. Includes interviews with Boorman and actresses Linda Blair and Louise Fletcher. In Mohammed Ali Naqvi’s Sundance-premiering Hanging By A Wire from Abramorama, opening at the Village East in NYC, a routine school commute turns terrifying when a cable car’s wire snaps, leaving eight passengers — including six schoolboys — dangling 900 feet above a ravine in the remote Himalayan foothills. With no margin for error and a cable that could fail at any moment, an unlikely alliance of rescuers must improvise under intense public scrutiny, racing against an invisible clock before disaster strikes live on television. Disposable Humanity opens for a weeklong Oscar-qualifying run at the Laemmle Monica Film Center. Explores the Hitler’s “Aktion T4” program that resulted in the deaths of over 300,000 disabled people The murders, arranged and executed by doctors in cooperation with the German state from 1939 to 1941, targeting those that the T4 program deemed “life unworthy of living.” Directed by Cameron S. Mitchell, produced by David Mitchell. Winner of the Slamdance Audience Award, RiverRun International Film Festival’s Director’s Award for Community Impact, and the Ridgway Independent Film Festival Director’s Choice Award, and nominated for Best Documentary of the Year by the Midwest Film Journalists. articles.title: Tom Hanks Movie ‘Lincoln In The Bardo’ From Starburns Industries Adds Willem Dafoe, Jonathan Bailey & Peter Dinklage
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Tom Hanks Movie ‘Lincoln In The Bardo’ From Starburns Industries Adds Willem Dafoe, Jonathan Bailey & Peter Dinklage Melissa Hirschenson Exits Innovative, Launches The Hirschenson Group ‘Hooters: The Movie’ In The Works About Chicken-Wing Eatery’s Origins View All August 28, 2026 12:48pm L-R: Willem Dafoe, Peter Dinklage and Jonathan Bailey Brad Trent/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: We can tell you that Willem Dafoe , Jonathan Bailey and Peter Dinklage have boarded the voice cast of Starburns Industries’ Lincoln in the Bardo , based on George Saunders’ New York Times bestseller and 2017 Booker Prize winner. Deadline broke the news that two-time Oscar winner Tom Hanks is playing Abraham Lincoln in the live-action portion of the Duke Johnson-directed pic. Related Stories Casting Tom Hanks To Play Abraham Lincoln In Starburns Industries’ ‘Lincoln In The Bardo’; Playtone Producing News ‘Late Fame’ Review: Willem Dafoe And Greta Lee Superb In Wonderful Indie Film About Art And Rediscovery In A New York Long Gone Saunders adapted his own novel for the screen for the hybrid stop-motion animation/live-action title. Lincoln in the Bardo explores one of the most intimate moments of Lincoln’s life, centering on his relationship with his recently deceased 11-year-old son. The feature mixes history and imagination in a story that unfolds through an ensemble of characters – living and dead, historical and invented – to explore themes of love, empathy and the human capacity for connection in the face of unimaginable grief. Watch on Deadline Dafoe will play Reverend Everly Thomas, the ghost of a minister who died believing he would go to heaven, but, to his dismay, found out otherwise. Bailey is voicing Roger Bevins, the ghost of a young gay man who took his own life over a failed love affair and instantly regretted it. Dinklage is voicing Hans Vollman, a ghost obsessed with his dream of being reunited with his much younger wife. Four-time Oscar nominee Dafoe’s credits include animated films Finding Nemo , Fantastic Mr. Fox and The Boy and the Heron , as well as At Eternity’s Gate , The Florida Project , Shadow of the Vampire and the Oscar-winning pic Platoon . He is repped by WME, The Artists Partnership and Circle Management. Emmy-nominated Bailey’s credits include the Wicked franchise, Jurassic World: Rebirth , the limited series Fellow Travelers and the Netflix hit Bridgerton . Next he will star in the untitled John Lee Hancock film about Monsanto. He is repped by CAA, Conway van Gelder Grant, Anonymous Content and attorneys at Hansen Jacobson Teller. Four-time Emmy winner Dinklage’s credits include the upcoming Black Bear title Wicker , Roofman , director Joe Wright’s Cyrano and the HBO global phenomenon Game of Thrones . He is repped by CAA and attorneys at Jackoway Austen Tyerman. Johnson, Paul Young and Devon Young Rabinowitz produce through Starburns Industries, alongside Hanks and Gary Goetzman producing for Playtone. Steven Shareshian, Aaron Mitchell and Saunders are executive producers. CAA Media Finance and WME Independent are handling sales at the upcoming Toronto Film Festival market. articles.title: ‘The Big Break’ Reboot’s Debut Season Shelved By The Golf Channel After Good Good Withdraws Title Sponsorship
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Disney+ Greenlights New Pokémon Stop-Motion Series As Part Of Global Distribution Deal ‘Law & Order: SVU’ Adds J. Smith-Cameron As Recurring For Season 28 Anonymous Content Names Steve Shikiya Chief Operating Officer View All August 28, 2026 1:10pm Scottie Scheffler on the 18th hole during the first round of the Tour Championship 2026 at East Lake Golf Club, August 27, 2026, in Atlanta, GA Getty Images A major scandal that has rocked the golf world has impacted the debut season of The Golf Channel ‘s reboot of The Big Break reality competition series. The new season, which was due to premiere Tuesday, August 25, has been canceled after Good Good announced it would be stepping away as title sponsor of the Good Good Championship, a new PGA Tour event set for November in Austin, Texas. The winner of the reboot’s debut season was supposed to receive a sponsor exemption to compete in the Austin event. Since Good Good pulled out, there was no prize to be given, hence the season cancellation. Related Stories News Kai Trump To Join Golf Channel Broadcast Crew Next Weekend News The Golf Channel Picks Up Chad Mumm & Wells Adams' 'Vanity Index' As It Takes A Swing At Video Podcasts The controversy erupted a week ago when Good Good posted on its social channels a 60-second ad, which has since been taken down, depicting one of Good Good’s members knocking down a female member reaching for his golf bag and then standing over her, saying, “Do not touch my new driver.” Watch on Deadline Shortly thereafter, Callaway Golf Company, a leading American sports equipment manufacturer based in Carlsbad, CA, cut ties with Good Good amidst the outcry over the ad. Good Good then announced it was withdrawing its sponsorship for the Austin event. Golf Channel had initially postponed the series premiere, originally scheduled for this past Tuesday night, to Sept. 1. The Versant cable network then followed with a statement Thursday on social media: “Following recent developments involving Good Good, and including the fact that the intended outcome of the series can no longer be fulfilled, Golf Channel will not be able to complete this season of Big Break as planned,” Golf Channel said in the statement. “While we are disappointed for the 12 competitors, our production team that worked tirelessly on the season, and the show’s passionate fans, we look forward to Big Break’s return to Golf Channel in 2027.” The Big Break aired from 2003-2015, when the series was canceled amid cuts by Golf Channel’s then-owner NBCUniversal. In October 2025, Golf Channel announced that The Big Break would be revived for a 24th season, in collaboration with the golf-oriented media company Good Good. articles.title: ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Director Celebrates Film Release, Saying “We Won” & “It’s Proof That Movies Don’t Just Go Away”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Dan Stevens Hopes Prime Video’s ‘RoboCop’ Series “Preserves” Elements Of “Extreme Violence & Also Satire” ‘Vanderpump Villa’ Renewed For Season 4 At Hulu CBS Shuts Down ‘Big Brother’ Live Feeds To Avoid Spoilers In “Unprecedented Twist”: “Go Outside, Smell The Flowers” View All August 28, 2026 1:23pm 'Coyote vs. Acme' Warner Bros. Coyote vs. Acme has made its way to theaters, and director Dave Green is expressing his gratitude. “COYOTE VS. ACME IS FINALLY, GLORIOUSLY, IN THEATERS NOW. Which means one thing. WE WON,” Green shared on Instagram. “You can go see this movie. In a theater. In your favorite seat. With your favorite snacks. With your favorite people. You can head into a dark room and laugh with strangers. Together. Congratulations to everyone who made this happen.” Green noted that the “victory” was a “shared experience,” adding, “It’s a record of the cast and crew, post, prep, and animation teams who poured so much love and passion into it over years and years.” Related Stories News 'Coyote Vs. Acme' $1.7M Previews, 'Dog Stars' $850K As Canines Rule Thursday - Box Office News 'Coyote Vs. Acme' & 'Dog Stars' Barking Up 'Spider-Man's Tree With Summer End Near - Weekend Preview “It’s shared, permanently, with the audience who fought so hard for its survival. Your fight is the reason this film finally made it to the big screen. Thank you @ketchupentertainment for hearing the audience. We’re so grateful that you did,” he continued. Watch on Deadline Coyote vs. Acme was originally set to premiere July 21, 2023, but Warner Bros. moved it to make way for Barbie . However, in November of that same year, the studio shelved the movie and instead took a $30 million tax write-off . In March 2025, Warner Bros. completed the sale of the Looney Tunes hybrid to Ketchup Entertainment, with Forte recently revealing that they plan to release the film on August 28, 2026. Green championed the effort to keep Coyote vs. Acme from remaining shelved, finding a way for audiences to finally see the movie in theaters. “This is a celebration, it’s proof that movies don’t just go away. We make work so it can be seen and shared — that’s the whole reason we do what we do,” Green said. “Persistence and resilience have truly won the day. Enjoy Coyote vs. Acm e on the big screen. Where it was always meant to be seen!” Coyote vs. Acme was written by Samy Burch, based on a story by James Gunn, Jeremy Slater, and Burch. The film follows Wile E. Coyote as he hires a billboard attorney to sue the Acme Corporation for selling faulty products. Will Forte, Lana Condor, John Cena, Luis Guzmán, and Kenneth Choi are among the actors in the cast. articles.title: Will Forte Says Glowing Reviews for ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ “Make It Feel Like You’re Not Crazy,” Admits “I Felt Gaslit For a While”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 10:42am Will Forte at the 'Coyote vs. Acme' premiere at Westwood Village Theater on Wednesday night. Eric Charbonneau/Ketchup Entertainment via Getty Images After several years in limbo, Coyote vs. Acme finally got its moment in the sun on Wednesday at its L.A. premiere. It was a night that for a long time did not seem possible, after Warner Bros. Discovery shelved the film in November 2023 in favor of a tax write-off. Fans rallied around the project, though, refusing to let it die — until in March 2025, Ketchup Entertainment saved the film and set it up for a summer 2026 theatrical release. Star Will Forte looks back at that period as “an emotional roller coaster,” admitting that despite how vocal people were being online to revive the film, “I didn’t think it would do anything.” Related Stories TV Tom Colicchio Says 'Top Chef' Has Become as Important as a James Beard Award Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Hits No. 2 on All-Time Domestic Chart, Topping 'Avengers: Endgame' “I was just like, ‘They’re not hearing you, it’s not going to make a difference.’ And then they just kept going and it’s because of them the movie’s out,” Forte told The Hollywood Reporter on the carpet. “I had given up on it and I can’t thank these people enough. I always thought this movie was super special and the support from the community has meant so much. It’s made me feel sane; I felt gaslit for a while and their support, now the positive reviews coming out — [they] just make it feel like you’re not crazy.” Coyote vs. Acme is a hybrid live-action and animation movie set in the Looney Tunes universe. It sees Wile E. Coyote deciding to sue the Acme Corporation after their products fail him one too many times in his relentless pursuit of the Roadrunner, with Forte as his inexperienced lawyer and John Cena as Acme’s attorney. And as Forte mentioned, the film is being released amid glowing reviews and very positive audience buzz. “It’s so validating. I’ve been a part of a lot of projects that haven’t gotten great reviews that I have loved — MacGruber . I love it. People may hate it, but I love it, I’m so proud of it,” the actor said, noting that reviews are not everything but “in this case, I am accepting positive reviews and saying they do mean something, I’m doing a flip around.” He continued that much like Wile E. Coyote going up against a big corporation, the film itself is an underdog, “so we need all the help we can get, and it feels like all these voices, the voices that helped us get the movie into the theaters, are helping spread the word about it being in the theaters. Hopefully people will listen to them and see these positive views and go like, ‘This movie deserves to be seen.'” Cena echoed, “We’re here, we’re coming out in theaters, I just hope that everyone who used their voice shows up to see this thing.” Wile E. Coyote makes a grand entrance at the #CoyoteVsAcme premiere pic.twitter.com/4CjPnYTOcH — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 27, 2026 That appreciation for the fans was clear at the event as well, as a costumed Wile E. Coyote character marched down the carpet with the UCLA marching band, carrying a sign that read “Absolute Cinema.” It’s a reference to a viral video of a fan who picketed outside of the Warner Bros. lot, in the rain, following the film’s cancellation; the character also appeared inside the screening, with another sign that read, “Thank you fans.” “We feel so lucky,” emphasized director Dave Green . “Every single person that spoke out and tweeted and wrote a message, and for our brave costumed Coyote who stood out in the rain, we’re grateful for every single individual who was there for us.” The filmmaker also brushed off any initial sequel plans as “I’ve not thought beyond this day,” but noted, “We made a movie that we thought was funny and worked for us and we internally thought was a blast. It’s so validating and kind to see the audience responding.” Coyote vs. Acme, which also stars Lana Condor , Eric Bauza and Martha Kelly, hits theaters on Friday. THR

articles.title: How Dolly Parton Crossed Over Into Hollywood — and America’s Hearts
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By David Kamp Plus Icon David Kamp David Kamp | The Hollywood Reporter View All August 27, 2026 10:42am Nine to Five (1980): from left, Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton, Jane Fonda. 20th Century Fox Film Corp./Courtesy Everett Collection Dolly Parton was perfect for her breakout decade, the 1970s. Color TVs outsold black-and-white sets for the first time in 1972, the annus mirabilis in which she composed “Jolene” and “I Will Always Love You,” allegedly on the same day. With her huge yellow hair, chambray-blue wardrobe, and sunshiny radiance, Parton was engineered to beam straight through the screen into every American home. Both of those songs became number-one country hits, in ’73 and ’74, respectively, and Dolly, Porter Wagoner’s girl singer no more, became America’s rhinestone superstar. The 70s were also the last golden age of an American monoculture, when most of us experienced the same programs, movies, and records at the same time. Country crossover wasn’t so much crossover as happy coexistence. Roy Clark could show up at Felix and Oscar’s New York apartment in The Odd Couple to demonstrate his virtuoso pickin’ skills and be summoned to Burbank to sub in for Johnny Carson as a guest host of The Tonight Show . Cliff Arquette’s hayseed character Charlie Weaver reliably occupied the lower left corner on Hollywood Squares . Hee Haw , the variety show Clark co-hosted with Buck Owens, thrived on TV in first-run syndication — it’s where this writer, like millions of other impressionable kids, first saw Parton perform “Coat of Many Colors,” her affecting song about the coat her mother sewed for her “from a box of rags that someone gave us.” Young Dolly wore the coat proudly to school, only to be ridiculed by mean kids who laughed at the sight of it. Dolly, unbowed, told off the poverty-shamers by saying she was actually rich, because of “the love my mama sewed in every stitch.” You couldn’t not be moved or besotted. Related Stories Music Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton at Madison Square Garden Residency Opening Night: "We Love You" Music Dolly Parton's Spotify Streams Spiked Over 1,200 Percent Following Icon's Death Of all the artists flying the country flag in this era, Dolly was the most transcendent, rivaled only by the great Johnny Cash. (Whereas Cash was known for his gravity and underrated comedically, Parton was known for her levity and underrated artistically.) Dolly was simply irresistible to everyone, no matter their background or cultural prejudices. Even the rock snobs at Rolling Stone loved her, flying her to New York in ’77 for an extraordinary photo shoot in which Annie Leibovitz paired Parton with an emerging Austrian bodybuilding star. While a naked Arnold Schwarzenegger stood with legs wide apart and biceps flexed, Parton, a pink bow in her hair, joyfully posed in front of him, her hips obscuring his naughty bits, her ginormously bewigged head blocking out his, eclipse-style. Parton, conversely, seemed to embrace all comers without wariness. In her successful bid to achieve crossover pop stardom, she sublimated her writer’s ego and turned to two old Brill Building hands, Barry Mann and Cynthia Weil, for “Here You Come Again,” which shot to number three on the Billboard Hot 100. When the Bee Gees were lying low in the post-disco backlash of the early 1980s, she and Kenny Rogers took their song “Islands in the Stream” to number one. On Dolly , her short-lived 1976 variety show, she gamely performed with collaborators both likely (e.g. Linda Ronstadt and Emmylou Harris, later to rejoin Parton for their triumphant 1987 album Trio ) and perhaps not so much (e.g. The Hues Corporation, of “Rock the Boat” fame, and KC and the Sunshine Band). In 1978, a writer named Colin Irwin, of the British publication Melody Maker , described the process of having his snide-journo defenses dissolved by Parton in real time: For ten minutes I just gawp, unable to comprehend the vision, but she — o bviously well-acquainted with such a reaction — accepts it gracefully, perhaps even with relish, and rattles on… “Been a hectic day but ah’m pretty used t’that nahw an’ ah enjoy meetin’ new people cos ah get a lota ideas for songs because of certain personalities that ah meet. Mahbe ah’ll wraht a song ’bout yew. Ah’ll call it ‘Laughing Eyes.’” Sigh. I think I’m in love. Unquestionably, she manipulates the press . And yet you still love her. Because she admits it. Where others of the ilk make you cringe with their synthetic sincerity, Dolly is disarmingly honest about it all, constantly sending herself up, mockingly talking about her wigs and her figure. She admits that her bizarre stage act and her appearance are merely means to an end, and you can even forgive the weepy sentiment of so much of her material, born out of the stifling poverty in which she was brought up. “Coat Of Many Colors,” for example — which she has often cited as her favorite song — reconstructed the Joseph story in the Bible, but was also based on a traumatic experience she herself had as a child. How can anyone with a heart knock that? The great monoculture of which Parton was the apogee began to fall apart with the advent of cable television in the 1980s and was eventually atomized completely by the internet. Today we live in a world where someone named Ella Langley can occupy the upper reaches of the Billboard charts alongside someone named Lil Baby, the fans of one having no idea of what the other’s music even sounds like. But Dolly kept on Dollying, decade after decade, holding us all together when very little else did. At the dawn of the 80s, she effortlessly translated her talents to film, starring alongside Jane Fonda and Lily Tomlin in 9 to 5 and writing and performing its infectious title song. In 1986, she formed a production company, Sandollar Productions, with her former manager, Sandy Gallin, a gay, Jewish, very tan show-business macher . “Nobody could quite get how the Christian Southern girl and New York Jewish boy could have so much in common,” she told the New York Times when Gallin died, in 2017. “But it was real. My husband didn’t love to travel, and Sandy was gay and did.” Together, Parton and Gallin produced the Father of the Bride movies and the millennially revered Buffy the Vampire Slayer TV series. Dolly Parton and producer Sandy Gallin at the Beverly Hills Hotel in 1992. Ron Galella, Ltd./Ron Galella Collection/Getty Images With Gallin’s help, she also launched the theme park Dollywood, situated just outside her native Great Smoky Mountains, in Pigeon Forge, Tennessee. There, she turned her heritage, warts and all, into a celebration, complete with a museum of Partonian artifacts literally called Rags to Riches: The Dolly Parton Story. (It has since evolved into a formidable multimedia complex called The Dolly Parton Experience.) Unlike certain other claimants of Appalachian background, Parton related her stories of hillbilly hardship without grievance. Over and over, she chose positivity. She often related the story of how taken she was, as a small child, with the scarlet woman of her little town, “with this yellow hair piled on her head, bright red lipstick, red nails, and high-heeled shoes. I thought she was the prettiest thing I’d ever seen. I used to say to my mama, ‘Oh, she’s so pretty!’” When Dolly’s mother derided the woman as “trash,” Parton recalled, “I just thought, ‘That’s what I want to be when I grow up: trash!’” Opry-style humor aside, Parton took her platform as an odds-beater seriously. Convinced that her sharecropper father’s illiteracy prevented him from realizing his dreams, she founded a nonprofit called The Imagination Library that mails free books to children every month from birth to the age of five. Founded in 1995, the program has distributed more than 300 million books. Lee Parton was still alive when The Imagination Library was founded. “I had the idea to do something special for him,” Parton said in 2018. “In the bible, where it talks about ‘Honor your father and your mother,’ I don’t think that necessarily means just to obey them. It means to bring honor to their name if you can. So I got my daddy involved in this program. I wanted him to feel like he was part of something special. He took such pride in the fact that the little kids called me ‘The Book Lady.’ He was prouder of that than anything.” How can anyone with a heart knock that? Parton was studiedly apolitical yet anything but gutless. In 2020, in the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, she donated $1 million to Vanderbilt University Medical Center to seed the research that led to the development of the Moderna vaccine. In her words and deeds, she supported gay rights and marriage equality, arguing for the latter with the characteristic zinger, “Why can’t they be as miserable as us heterosexuals in their marriages?” Coming from someone else — really, anyone else — these pro-queer, pro-vax, and pro-literacy stances would likely have been critiqued in some quarters as “woke.” But you never hear anyone carping on TV or social media about “Dollyweird.” Parton was a uniter. She commanded a wonderfully anachronistic monocultural respect, attributable to all the goodwill she had accumulated and the positivity she never stopped projecting. We’ll truly never see Dolly’s like again, though you can see certain individuals modeling themselves in her likeness. Sabrina Carpenter paid explicit homage to Parton’s comic-blond-minx persona by inviting the woman herself to record a duet, 2024’s “Please Please Please,” complete with a caper video that finds the pair sweetly harmonizing while a man they’ve abducted lies bound in the back of their pickup truck. Sabrina is no Dolly, which isn’t a knock but a comment on the impossibility of any new artist ever enjoying the level of admiration and adoration that Parton did for most of her life. But it’s great that Dolly remains, fifty-plus years after “Jolene” and the glory days of Hee Haw , an aspirational model. Her motto was, “Dream more, learn more, care more, and be more.” She more than lived up to it. THR

articles.title: Billy Porter Set to Receive Legacy Award From Elizabeth Taylor AIDS Foundation
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 10:52am Billy Porter Credit: Afshin Feiz/Courtesy of Subject The Elizabeth Taylor AIDS Foundation is finalizing the program for its Los Angeles fundraiser, a Night of Compassion, by drafting Billy Porter to receive one of the top awards. The Emmy-winning actor and activist will receive the Elizabeth Taylor Legacy Award, while Vanity Fair will receive some shine by taking home the the Elizabeth Taylor Commitment to End AIDS Award. CNN’s Laura Coates is confirmed to host the whole affair from inside a Beverly Hills Hotel ballroom on Sept. 17. Deborah Cox, who broke out with her 1998 smash “Nobody’s Supposed to be Here,” will take the stage to perform at the Gilead Sciences-sponsored event. Related Stories Business John Waters, Billy Porter and Julio Torres Set for Second Season of 'Finding Fire Island' Series Lifestyle Elton John Impact Awards to Honor LGBTQ+ Icons and Trailblazers Including Jonathan Bailey and Chappell Roan “ETAF is honored to celebrate Billy Porter and Vanity Fair at this year’s Elizabeth Taylor Night of Compassion. Both have used their platforms to raise awareness, inspire change and stand up for communities affected by HIV and AIDS,” said ETAF executive director Catherine Brown. “At a time when so many people living with and at risk of HIV are facing uncertainty, their voices, advocacy and support are more important than ever. We are proud to recognize their commitment and to continue Elizabeth’s legacy of compassion and action.” Porter, the multi-hyphenate actor, singer, director, producer, composer and playwright, won an Emmy for his work on Ryan Murphy’s FX’s drama Pose . Porter originated the role of Lola in the Broadway musical Kinky Boots , which won him a Tony Award, Drama Desk Award and Outer Critics Circle Award, as well as a Grammy for best musical theater album. He won a second Tony as a producer on A Strange Loop . Porter will be seen in The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping . He broke his silence on his HIV status with a profile in The Hollywood Reporter , published in May 2021, by breaking the shame of his diagnosis. “The truth is the healing,” he said at the time. Vanity Fair is being singled out for its coverage, dating back to a November 1992 that featured Taylor holding a condom. Most recently, in February, they partnered with ETAF to take over its online homepage. More information on the event can be found here . Laura Coates of CNN. Courtesy of CNN/Subject Deborah Cox attends the 79th Tony Awards at New York’s Radio City Music Hall on June 7, 2026. (Photo by Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images) THR

articles.title: Penn Badgley to Star in Murder Mystery ‘Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone’ at Prime Video
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 11:00am Penn Badgley and David Hemingson Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images; Luke Fontana Logo text Penn Badgley just can’t seem to get away from killers. The You star will topline a murder mystery at Prime Video called Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone . Prime has placed a series order for the project from showrunner David Hemingson, Fifth Season and Made Up Stories. The series is based on a novel of the same name by Benjamin Stevenson. “I’m thrilled to be partnered with Fifth Season and Made Up Stories in bringing Ben’s heartfelt and darkly hilarious whodunit to life,” said Hemingson ( The Holdovers ). “And we are so lucky to have Penn as our lead. I can’t think of any actor better suited to bring Ern’s intensity, brilliance and hilariously dry sense of humor to life.” Related Stories TV Carina Walker Named Head of YA at Amazon MGM Studios Beyond the Book Anna Todd's Post-'After' Era: Inside Her Next Chapter With 'The Last Sunrise' Romance Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone follows Ern Cunningham (Badgley), a “mystery-writing expert” who heads to Vermont for family reunion “to welcome his brother Michael home from prison — the same brother Ern helped convict,” the show’s logline reads. “When a frozen body appears and a snowstorm traps everyone inside, the deaths begin to mount. Everyone in Ern’s family has already killed someone — either by accident or otherwise.” Hemingson will executive produce the series with Bruna Papandrea , Steve Hutensky and Jeanne Snow of Made Up Stories, Molly Allen, Badgley and Stevenson. “I am blown away by the vision and enthusiasm everyone has for bringing this book, and Ernest Cunningham, to the screen,” said Stevenson. “Penn perfectly captures Ern’s clueyness and cleverness, and David has brought bags of wit and heart to the script. With the passion of Amazon MGM Studios, Bruna and Steve behind us we have an absolutely killer team, and I can’t wait to solve a murder with them.” Stevenson’s 2022 novel kicked off a best-selling series — there are currently four Ernest Cunningham mysteries, and the author is writing a fifth. “We’re beyond excited to bring Ben’s sensational book to life in Dave Hemingson’s brilliant hands,” said Papandrea and Hutensky. “We’ve found the perfect Ern in Penn and it’s a dream to be making this series with our amazing partners Amazon MGM Studios and Fifth Season.” Added Peter Friedlander, head of global TV at Amazon MGM, “ Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone is a brilliantly inventive series that subverts the murder mystery genre in the most unexpected and entertaining ways. Ben created a world that is darkly funny and wickedly clever. Paired with David’s sharp storytelling and Penn’s magnetic presence, and with our incredible partners at Fifth season and Made Up Stories, this series is going to be something truly special for Prime Video.” Badgley is repped by Brillstein Entertainment Partners, CAA, The Lede Company and Hansen Jacobson. Hemingson is with by 3 Arts, WME, and McKuin Frankel. Stevenson is repped by Intellectual Property Group and Curtis Brown Australia. THR

articles.title: Dolly Parton’s Sister Stella Says Late Icon Offered to Test Experimental Drugs to Help Battle Cancer
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Etan Vlessing Plus Icon Etan Vlessing Canada Bureau Chief View All August 27, 2026 11:58am Stella and Dolly Parton Terry Wyatt/Getty Images Dolly Parton ’s little sister Stella Parton has revealed the country music icon asked her medical team to try experimental drugs on her to help future cancer patients battle their own health struggles. “What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future, Stella Parton said in an emotional Facebook tribute. She insisted the late icon got to heaven “right on time” on Tuesday, when Dolly Parton’s death after a brief battle with cancer was revealed. The music legend was admitted to the hospital in Nashville late last week after dealing with kidney and autoimmune issues. Related Stories Music Harry Styles Pays Tribute to Dolly Parton at Madison Square Garden Residency Opening Night: "We Love You" Music Dolly Parton's Spotify Streams Spiked Over 1,200 Percent Following Icon's Death Stella Parton said her sister’s 11th hour medical request that her doctors be allowed to test possibly future drugs to battle cancer was in keeping with her lifetime of trying to help others. “My sister was always thinking of others, and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources as she continued to do to the very end,” Stella Parton wrote. The elder Parton revealed in September that she was postponing a set of Las Vegas concerts to deal with “some health challenges.” In the past few months, the country music legend put on a brave front, telling her fans that she was OK. Her husband of nearly 58 years, businessman Carl Dean, died at age 82 on March 3, 2025. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to The Dolly Parton Estate for comment on Stella Parton’s social media tribute. Stella Parton’s tribute to her sister follows in full: My big sister Dolly got her wings this past Tuesday. If anyone gets to heaven I’m sure she made it right on time. I know she’s showing out big time, in all her sparkles and shine. That was my sister’s way. Every Tuesday about this time, before the sun came up and the world was still asleep, she and I for many years had our coffee together over the phone. Being little farm girls we’ve continued to be early risers. As she liked to say; “shoot Tedda we get more work done before the sun comes up than most folks do all day long!” We would catch up on gossip, as sisters do, and drink coffee and make plans as it has always been our way. My sister was one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known. What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future. My sister was always thinking of others and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up and give more of your time and resources as she continued to do to the very end. I want to personally thank all of you for the out pouring of love and respect you are showing my sister. Your love and respect for her is deeply felt by all of us who loved her first and it helps as we grieve her passing through our lives! My Tuesday morning coffee time will never be the same but her love, respect and goodness will remain. Dolly loved the world and everyone in it. I would criticize and complain about it and she would laugh and say; “shoot Tedda, we’ve got more important things to do than worry about their silly asses.” She was right and she proved it everyday. She left the world a better place by being in it so let’s follow her example. Love and respect to all of you. Stella THR

articles.title: ‘Furious’ Renewed for Second Season at Hulu
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 12:00pm Emmy Rossum in Hulu's 'Furious' Sarah Shatz/Disney Logo text Hulu is still feeling Furious . The Disney-owned streamer has renewed Furious , a serial killer thriller starring Emmy Rossum , for a second season. The pickup comes a few days ahead of the first season finale, which debuts Aug. 31. Loosely based on the 1987 movie Black Widow and created by Elizabeth Meriwether , Furious stars Rossum as Alice Black, an FBI agent who is tracking a serial killer (played by Lola Petticrew). “Both walk their own paths toward justice,” the show’s logline reads, “and as their lives start to intertwine, the line between right and wrong begins to blur.” Related Stories TV 'The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives' Season 5 Trailer Teases Leadup to Taylor Frankie Paul's 'Bachelorette' Season Being Pulled TV Mindy Kaling and 'Not Suitable for Work' Cast React to Cancellation: "I Loved Making This Show" The second season is likely to follow Rossum’s Alice on a new case, though it’s still very early in the development process. Furious has received strong reviews; The Hollywood Reporter critic Daniel Fienberg wrote that “especially in its home stretch, [the series] becomes a complex, well-acted and even funny thriller about the ongoing toll of trauma, the psychic cost of revenge and the danger of a life driven by anger.” Sources say the show is also likely to appear in Nielsen’s top 10 streaming charts for its premiere week; that data is due for release later Thursday. Season one of Furious also stars Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Scoot McNairy. Jake Lacy, Rob Delaney, Hope Davis, Rob Yang and Steve Way have recurring roles. “I love serial killer shows, but I’d never seen one with a female serial killer other than Killing Eve ,” Meriwether said on THR’ s podcast I’m Having an Episode earlier this month. “I wanted to dive into that character and [ Black Widow ] seemed like a good framework. This sounds insane, but the more I learned about female serial killers, the more I was drawn in — especially learning that most female serial killers have been victims of violence. That idea began forming in my head, just the cycle of violence and how misunderstood it is when it comes to women.” The series comes from 20th Television and Searchlight Television. Meriwether ( The Dropout, Dying for Sex, New Girl ) is the showrunner and executive produces with Rossum (via her Composition 8 banner), Ronald Bass, Matt Olmstead, Sam Hoffman and Brian Kirk, who also directed the first two episodes. THR

articles.title: Andrea Eastman, Casting Director on ‘The Godfather’ and Former ICM Agent, Dies at 86
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 27, 2026 12:15pm Andrea Eastman Patrick McMullan/Getty Images Andrea Eastman, who as the head of casting at Paramount Pictures brought Ali MacGraw to Goodbye, Columbus and James Caan to The Godfather before serving as a manager and longtime ICM agent, has died. She was 86. Eastman died Wednesday in her sleep at her home in Santa Barbara, a family spokesperson told The Hollywood Reporter . A real straight-shooter, Eastman discovered Jaclyn Smith, got Steven Spielberg and Roy Scheider together for Jaws (1975), managed Sylvester Stallone in his Rocky heyday and talked Rob Reiner into hiring her client — and his best friend — Billy Crystal for When Harry Met Sally … (1989). Related Stories Movies Samuel Monroe Jr., 'Menace II Society' Star, Dies at 52 Movies Peter Cullen, Voice of Optimus Prime in 'Transformers,' Dies at 85 With a long stint at ICM in Los Angeles and New York, she also repped and/or managed Barbra Streisand, Burt Reynolds , Peter Boyle, Chevy Chase, Henry Winkler, Jamie Lee Curtis, Christopher Reeve, Katharine Ross, Christopher Plummer , James Brolin, Dustin Hoffman, Dyan Cannon, Gabriel Byrne, Brenda Vaccaro, Richard Gere, Kim Basinger, Kathleen Turner, Stockard Channing, Tony Danza, Wes Craven, Katherine Heigl, Katie Couric, Elle MacPherson, Marshall Brickman and Charlie Rose, among many others over the years. Eastman fought to cast MacGraw, then a 30-year-old photographer’s assistant and model new to acting, for the role of the younger Jewish-American princess Brenda Patimkin opposite Richard Benjamin as her romantic interest Neil Klugman in Goodbye, Columbus (1969), directed by Larry Peerce. Natalie Wood had already turned down the part, and the studio had looked at hundreds of other actresses before MacGraw came aboard. (The year the movie hit theaters, MacGraw wed Paramount Studios chief Robert Evans .) Eastman initiated the casting for Francis Ford Coppola’s The Godfather (1972) and worked with Fred Roos to hire actors for the eventual Oscar winner for best picture. “You make endless lists when you are a casting director,” she said in 2023. “When you do a movie, you try to think out of the box. For The Godfather , it was endless casting. We worked seven days a week. I was dreaming of Italians all night every night.” Eastman thought Italian producer Carlo Ponti would make a great Vito Corleone before Godfather author Mario Puzo came up with the idea to cast Marlon Brando . Caan had excelled in his screen test for the film and was slated to play Michael Corleone opposite the hulking Carmine Caridi as Sonny Corleone (Coppola had offered him the role in a bar). But when Al Pacino was hired to play Michael, Caan was out of the movie. Caridi “was a big guy but not menacing. He was like a big Saint Bernard,” Eastman said. “Luckily, he’d never formally signed a deal, and Coppola trusted me. He was leaving for Sicily [to scout locations], so he told me, ‘Just cast my fucking movie!’” After getting Charlie Bluhdorn, head of Paramount parent Gulf + Western, and Evans to sign off on Caan as Sonny and Pacino as Michael, Eastman hurriedly got Caan to sign a contract before someone changed their mind. “We all worked as a team, but I am responsible for Jimmy Caan getting the part of Sonny,” she said. This era was the happiest time in her career, she often noted, but she would quit the studio in early 1973. Born on June 15, 1940, Eastman grew up in Westport, Connecticut, where she attended Staples High School. She graduated from Ohio State University and married producer and backgammon expert Bruce Becker; after they divorced, she moved to California. In summer 1968, she was working as an assistant for $150 a week for Paramount head of casting Joyce Selznick when the niece of Gone With the Wind producer David O. Selznick was fired. Eastman, then 28, took her place and made $300 a week. She first spotted Smith when both were in the audience at the stage musical Hallelujah, Baby! “She was gorgeous,” Eastman said in an interview last year. “I walked up to her and gave her my card. She looked at me like, ‘Who is this person? She’s my age.’ And then I brought her in and she met Charlie Bluhdorn and Bob Evans and we put her under contract.” (Smith would play as a wedding guest in Goodbye, Columbus. ) Eastman’s tenure at Paramount also saw the release of such notable films as True Grit (1969), Downhill Racer (1969), the box office sensation (and MacGraw-starring) Love Story (1970), Catch 22 (1970), T.R. Baskin (1971) and Play It Again, Sam (1972). She said she quit Paramount when Frank Yablans , who had recently replaced Stanley R. Jaffe as studio chief, threatened to fire her if she attended the 1973 Academy Awards, where The Godfather was nominated for 11 Oscars. She took a job at double her previous salary as an agent at International Famous Agency; her clients back then included Ross, Boyle, Curtis, Benjamin and Paula Prentiss. She left to become Stallone’s manager, and that led to her agreeing in 1977 to form a joint personal management company with Jeff Wald , Ron DiBlasio and Herb Nanas. But soon after introducing Stallone to Wald, she was told by DiBlasio that “we don’t want to go forward with you, Jeff’s going to have his own company,” she recalled in 2023. She said she was offered $25,000 but turned that down, and she would file a $1 million suit against Wald and DiBlasio for damages. She formed her own company, Andrea Eastman Management, before joining ICM in 1983. She said Spielberg offered Scheider the role of police chief Martin Brody in Jaws at one of her dinner parties and that Reiner gave Crystal his script to When Harry Met Sally at one of her weddings. Later, she convinced Streisand to appear in an unglamorous role in Meet the Frockers (2004). Eastman moved to Bozeman, Montana, full-time in 2005 and retired from ICM in 2010. Her husbands also included attorney Richard Wilsker and producer Paul N. Lazarus III ( Westworld , Capricorn One ). In the 2022 Paramount+ miniseries The Offer , Eastman was portrayed by Stephanie Koenig. She said she did not appreciate that she and Godfather producer Al Ruddy were depicted as having a one-night stand when it fact they had love affair that lasted more than a year. She established a sanctuary in Montana near Big Sky Resort dedicated to rescuing, rehabilitating and sheltering maltreated, abandoned and abused horses and dogs, and her impact as an animal advocate was chronicled in Jill Rappaport’s 2004 book, People We Know, Horses They Love . In the late 1990s, she enlisted Robert Redford ’s help in getting the nation’s first state initiative to ban the slaughter of horses for human consumption passed. She spent three months in 2020 at the Beverly Hills Hotel recovering from open-heart surgery. Her late golden retriever had the run of the place, which was operating at a limited capacity during COVID, and a kids picture book written from the pooch’s perspective, Trooper at the Beverly Hills Hotel , was published in 2022. After some tough early years in Hollywood, Eastman proved to be as tough as they come. “One of the things [you learn] being an agent is you don’t give up,” she said in 2014. “You never take no for an answer.” THR

articles.title: Tim Curry Honored by Past and Present Frank-N-Furters With “I’m Going Home” Performance
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All August 27, 2026 12:20pm The 'Rocky Horror Show' Broadway cast pays tribute to Tim Curry. Rocky Horror Broadway/Instagram Luke Evans, Paul Soileau and Jake Shears paid tribute to late Rocky Horror Show star Tim Curry on Wednesday following news of his death at age 80. Following Wednesday‘s Broadway performance of The Rocky Horror Show , Paul Soileau — who is currently starring as Dr. Frank-N-Furter, the role Curry originated — honored the late actor after the curtain call. In videos shared online, Soileau told the audience, “The role of Frank-N-Furter is a marvelous beast. Frank-N-Furter inhabits spaces and sneaks in spaces and places and old theater houses and old theaters like this, movie theaters, teenagers’ bedrooms.“ Related Stories Lifestyle Pulitzer Prize Finalist 'Here There Are Blueberries' Set For Broadway Lifestyle 'Six' Will End Five-Year Broadway Run in January He added, “The way Frank-N-Furter survives is that he finds vessels and he goes into them and he takes them over and he keeps moving and moving and moving all around. And many people in this room, on this stage, have been a vessel for Frank-N-Furter over the years. But if you trace it all back, 53 years ago, there’s one home and one vessel. One mothership that Frank-N-Furter could actually call home, and it’s Tim Curry.” Curry first took on the Frank-N-Furter role in the original 1973 London production of Richard O’Brien’s The Rocky Horror Show , following a turn on Broadway in 1975 and in the 1975 film adaptation, The Rocky Horror Picture Show . “53 years ago, Richard O’Brien laid a piece of paper in front of Tim Curry with ingredients on it,” Soileau also said. “And he took all those ingredients and he created this beast that everyone found something within it and could see a piece of themselves inside of it.” Soileau later welcomed Luke Evans , who portrayed Frank-N-Furter in the current revival and played his final performance just three days prior, and Jake Shears, who will take over the role starting Sept. 11. Together, the past and present Frank-N-Furters performed the song “I’m Going Home,” from the musical. The performance was shared on the official social media accounts for the production. View this post on Instagram Rocky Horror creator Richard O’Brien also paid tribute to Curry in a message shared by his son online. “Tim Curry was a wonderful man by nature who was also a wonderful performer and understood the difference between such delightful achievements. He never sought attention and never put himself before the roles that he played. He was, in short, a good egg and class act,“ O’Brien said. “It was both a privilege and delight to have known him and worked with him. Rest in peace dear Tim.” On Wednesday, a tribute to Curry was also set up at Rocky Horror ‘s Studio 54 Broadway theater. Tribute to Tim Curry in lobby of Broadway Theater THR Staff THR

articles.title: Oscars: 7 Films That Could Define the Awards Season, From ‘The Odyssey’ to ‘Michael’
articles.full_text: Focus Features; A24; Lionsgate The frontrunners have a head start. The festivals have contenders ready to run them down. Let the games begin. The film year has already delivered, led by Christopher Nolan’s “ The Odyssey ,” a July event picture that doubled as the first true best picture launch of 2026. Back in May, Cannes fired the opening shots, sending Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” Netflix-acquired Spanish-language epic “La Bola Negra” and Russian drama “Minotaur” down the Croisette with buzz that will trail them into the fall. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 But a frontrunner in August is just a film with an earlier release date. Over the next six weeks, the Oscars race will unspool in waves — the thin air of Telluride, the carpets of Venice’s Lido, the crowds of Toronto, the tastemakers of New York — with a single afternoon screening able to rewrite the whole narrative. Popular on Variety The festivals are set, and the year is loaded. And a moonwalk, a Homeric voyage and a Pixar goodbye are all in play at the same time. Here’s where the race stands. PROJECT HAIL MARY, Ryan Gosling, 2026. © Amazon MGM Studios /Courtesy Everett Collection ©MGM/Courtesy Everett Collection “Project Hail Mary” (Amazon MGM Studios) Ryan Gosling has three Oscar nominations — for “Half Nelson,” “La La Land” and “Barbie” — and no wins, and this adaptation of Andy Weir’s novel could hand him another shot. It also marks the live-action sci-fi leap of Phil Lord and Christopher Miller, the “Lego Movie” and “21 Jump Street” duo. Oscar history isn’t usually kind to directing partnerships: Only a handful have been nominated, most recently the Daniels for “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” Lord and Miller could join that short list, if Amazon MGM builds a friendly reminder campaign around them. “The Odyssey” (Universal Pictures) No surprise, Nolan is the man to beat, and “The Odyssey” is exactly the kind of feat the Academy’s directors branch loves to reward. His adaptation of Homer’s epic arrived to a wave of critical love, the rare summer tentpole with awards ambition built into its foundation: mythic source material, a starry ensemble and a theatrical approach designed to make the format itself part of the conversation. Two years after the “Oppenheimer” sweep — his first directing Oscar and a best picture win shared with wife and producing partner Emma Thomas — Nolan enters this campaign with a lot of Academy goodwill. Matt Damon’s Odysseus could put him in serious play in the actor race after winning a screenwriting Oscar nearly 30 years ago for “Good Will Hunting.” At the same time, John Leguizamo, Robert Pattinson, Anne Hathaway and Samantha Morton crowd a supporting field. Jaafar Jackson as Michael Jackson in Michael. Photo Credit: Courtesy of Lionsgate Courtesy of Lionsgate “Michael” (Lionsgate) Every season has an unofficial Oscar “villain” — think “Green Book,” “Bohemian Rhapsody” and “Emilia Pérez.” This year has a moonwalk. “Michael” doesn’t need critics (it has a 38% Rotten score, but a 97% Certified Fresh rating); it needs the Academy’s populist wing, the same bloc that widened best picture to 10 slots after the 2008 “Dark Knight” snub to make room for films the public embraced. Jaafar Jackson’s transformation into the King of Pop will be the main talking point, and two-time Oscar nominee Colman Domingo’s chilling turn as family patriarch Joe Jackson lends the film gravity. Factor in the craft branches — editing, sound and makeup and hairstyling — and voters have plenty of boxes to check. Olivia Wilde, Seth Rogen, Penélope Cruz and Edward Norton appear in The Invite by Olivia Wilde, an official selection of the 2026 Sundance Film Festival. Courtesy of Sundance Institute | photo c/o The Invite The Invite “The Invite” (A24) Olivia Wilde’s third feature is her sleekest, most assured work behind the camera, and A24 is mounting a full fall campaign. An English-language remake of Cesc Gay’s “The People Upstairs,” it boasts one of the year’s most impeccable ensembles: Seth Rogen, Wilde, four-time nominee Edward Norton and Oscar winner Penélope Cruz (a triple threat this year, with “La Bola Negra” and “Bunker” still to come). The engine is a crackling script by Rashida Jones and Will McCormack (reunited after “Celeste and Jesse Forever”) that offers sharp dialogue, a merciless structure and relentless laughs. In a season that rewards originals and adaptations alike, this is writing voters will likely remember in January and a cast the actors branch can get behind. OBSESSION, Inde Navarrette, 2025. © Focus Features /Courtesy Everett Collection ©Focus Features/Courtesy Everett Collection “Obsession” (Focus Features) If “Get Out” had Daniel Kaluuya, “Obsession” has Inde Navarrette. The horror breakout — the highest-grossing film in Focus Features history — lives and dies by its star, who plays a hypnotized co-worker and love interest with fearless physicality. Destined to be one of the year’s signature discoveries, as proven by her casting as Rogue in the upcoming “X-Men” movie, Navarrette could emerge as a critics’ awards darling, and Focus has every reason to push hard — perhaps even for writer-director-editor Curry Barker and a best picture slot. “I Swear” Graeme Hunter Pictures “I Swear” (Sony Pictures Classics) The N-word outburst at the BAFTA Awards put “I Swear” in the headlines and buried the real story: Robert Aramayo deserved that surprise win for lead actor. As a man living with Tourette’s syndrome, the 33-year-old English actor delivered an invigorating, deeply human turn that topped Timothée Chalamet’s in “Marty Supreme” and Michael B. Jordan’s in “Sinners.” The film’s U.S. release date makes it eligible for the Golden Globes, Critics Choice and the Oscars. If enough voters see it, they’ll understand why Aramayo won the BAFTA — and the film could get other Oscar nominations, including original screenplay. TOY STORY 5 , from left: Bullseye, Jessie (voice: Joan Cusack), 2026. © Walt Disney Studios Motion Pictures / Courtesy Everett Collection ©Walt Disney Co./Courtesy Everett Collection “Toy Story 5” (Pixar) “Toy Story 5” is a $1 billion juggernaut and the kind of overwhelming favorite the category bends around; Pixar sequels lock up nominations before the competition has finished storyboarding. The film also gets a boost from legendary composer Randy Newman and superstar Taylor Swift. The franchise carries a perfect Oscar record: All four previous “Toy Story” films earned best original song nominations, the only series with a flawless mark in the category. Pixar could extend the streak with “I Knew It, I Knew You,” written by Swift and Jack Antonoff — which would also hand Swift, a record four-time album of the year Grammy winner, her first Oscar bid after two near misses. In a franchise built on goodbyes, one more song may be all it takes. articles.title: What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’
articles.full_text: Aug 27, 2026 11:32am PT What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks 27 minutes ago What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ 1 hour ago New York Comic Con Unveils 2026 Professional Schedule Lineup, Including ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Author-NBCUniversal TV Panel (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago See All Audible More than half of Americans aged 18 and older, an estimated 157 million people, have listened to an audiobook, according to the Audio Publishers Association. Back in May, Audible likely added a few more to the fold with its Story House experience, which the Amazon-owned audiobook company proclaimed to be the first ever “bookless bookstore.” Following a pop-up during the return of BookCon at NYC’s Javits Convention Center in April, the Audible Story House operated for a month (from May 1-May 31) in lower Manhattan and saw more than 7,000 unique visitors come through its free-to-enter doors. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 “What I was excited about was the opportunity to learn a lot more about customers and their experiences in that space,” Audible’s global head of brand content marketing James Finn tells Variety . “And oftentimes, I don’t have a sample size like that, and I don’t have a situation where we show up for an entire month in a city like New York and really learn more about our existing customers and new listeners.” Popular on Variety Nick Castle Located at 260 Bowery, the three-floor audiobook space offered guests the chance to browse titles using physical “Story Tiles” (blocks with RFID chips that made listening to samples via speakers, headphones or through your own phone and earbuds a quick business) throughout seven distinct listening spaces. It housed an immersive listening theater with Dolby Atmos surround sound and a “Listening Bar” with a dedicated “Story Tender” staffer offering up personalized recommendations for sampling. There were creator programming and panels, book clubs, hands-on crafting activities, a pop-up cafe from Brooklyn’s Land to Sea and tons of merch. But come June, it was all gone. “It was very hard when we closed the doors, I will be honest,” Finn says. “And a lot of people assumed that it was going to be there permanently, which was a nice compliment to the team that built the space.” Out of the 301 titles that were on offer in Audible’s Story House (“We never say what the one title is because everybody had an opinion — but we wanted to add that one more,” Finn says) 98% of the audiobooks were listened to “to any degree” over the course of the month in operation. The most popular included “Project Hail Mary,” “The Hive: A Thriller,” “George Orwell’s 1984,” “Just Kiss Already,” and Audible’s full-cast recording of “Harry Potter and the Sorcerer’s Stone.” Photo by Bryan Bedder/Getty Images for Audible Getty Images for Audible There was also a lot of interest in Matt Dinniman’s “Dungeon Crawler Carl” LitRPG series, which released new book, “A Parade of Horribles” on May 12. “People were coming in, and they had already listened to it, and the eighth book had only come out a couple days ahead of time, and they were still tapping it, and they still were excited about that,” Finn says. But it wasn’t just the “Carl” fans that were sticking around. Audible says it counted more than 15,000 “deep engagement” experiences among its Story House guests, meaning the person did more than simply enter the space and browse. “People weren’t just coming in and then leaving, or coming in and listening to a sample and leaving,” Finn says. “They genuinely were staying around, going to the different areas, or coming to the community sessions where we had different activities, or going up to the cafe and buying an AudiBuddy and that was really interesting.” Finn says the Audible team has also been looking at “what are the learnings from the actual experience in New York that we can adapt to the experience within the app and within the service.” The biggest takeaway: “removing friction and allowing more engagement and allowing more of an opportunity for personalization, so that they have the opportunity to go to what’s interesting to them, but to sample and to try.” Audible Audible now has those 13,000 leftover “Story Tiles,” so there are some plans for what to do with those tactile representations of audiobooks. “We created that technology and that item. It didn’t exist,” Finn says. “The ambition was, how do we take something invisible and make it tangible? So the RFID component with it, we were able to see what people were listening to, and it was fantastic because everybody has different tastes and we saw such an interesting read across the entire slate of content there.” Finn adds: “But after the fact, what we’ve been doing is assessing what does Audible Story House look like in our plans for ’27. Right now, what we’re doing is similar to what you saw at BookCon. We’re going to bring a version of that with the core fundamentals to Guadalajara Book Festival, and then Frankfurt Book Fair.” Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Gameplay Trailer Shows Weapons Destroying Planet in the Series’ Finale (Gaming News Roundup)
articles.full_text: Aug 27, 2026 11:45am PT ‘Final Fantasy VII Revelation’ Gameplay Trailer Shows Weapons Destroying Planet in the Series’ Finale (Gaming News Roundup) By Tanya Fedak , Isabelle Farina , Mya Copeland “ Final Fantasy VII ” received a new gameplay trailer during gamescom Opening Night Live. The third and final entry in the “Final Fantasy VII” remake series sees hostile giants called Weapons arriving to save a world undergoing a crisis. But, unable to determine who’s a true threat, the Weapons ultimately cause mass destruction on anyone or anything who stands in their way. It’s up to Cloud and his friends to fend off the giants and save the world from Sephiroth. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 Also revealed in the trailer are Chocobo mounts, a grappling hook and the new Summon Typhon and open-world exploration via parachute. Cloud and Tifa are also seen in their new FITS, which is a new system of “Final Fantasy VII Revelation” that introduces unique outfits with increased power and new abilities. Popular on Variety “Final Fantasy VII Revelation” will release in spring 2027 on all platforms. Watch the trailer below. See more gaming news below. TRAILERS “Sesame Street: Friends & Fun” has released its first gameplay trailer. The Big Block Party is almost here on Sesame Street, and it’s up to players to help residents like Elmo, Cookie Monster, Big Bird, Abby Cadabby, Grover and Tango prepare. Designed for preschool players and families, the game allows users to explore the neighborhood through educational experiences. Each character offers unique activities across landmarks such as the Community Garden, Bandstand and Farm. Whether it’s cooking with Cookie Monster or helping Abby with magical tasks, players have more than 50 story activities and mini-games to explore. “Sesame Street: Friends & Fun” releases Oct. 9 from Outright Games, in collaboration with Sesame Workshop. Watch the trailer below. NEW LY ANNOUNCED GAMES Attention all Atari fans! Atari is bringing back 39 Atari 2600 titles on physical cartridges, including Pitfall!, River Raid and Kaboom. Celebrating the reunion of Atari and Activision after nearly 50 years, the Atari x Activision Collection consists of three physical offerings. The Standard Edition cartridges of a dozen popular titles will begin shipping in November for $34.99 each. Four Deluxe Box sets – Treasure, Speed, Secrets and Victory – expand the collection to 39 total games, with the first set shipping in late November and the rest to follow in Spring, Summer and Fall 2027. Each set will be sold via pre-order for $249.99. A Complete Collection, which includes all four Deluxe Sets and a to-be-announced collectible item, will be sold via pre-order for $999.96. Pre-orders for the standard edition cartridges, the Treasure Deluxe Set and the Atari x Activision Ultimate Deluxe Set are available today at atari.com Atari is an interactive entertainment company and gaming industry brand that provides multi-platform, interactive entertainment and licensed products. Atari brands includes game developers Coatsink, Digital Eclipse, Early Morning Studios, Implicit Conversions, Infogrames, Nightdive Studios, Stormteller Games and the community-based sites AtariAge and MobyGames. * “The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt” remastered is launching on Sept. 29, along with a new expansion, “Songs of the Past.” The expansion will take players to the brand new realm of Letten — an idyllic land of rural tradition that hides a dark secret just below the surface. The remaster will bring upgrades and enhancements to visuals, performance, gameplay and more when it launches on PC, PlayStation 5, and Xbox Series X|S. It will also be available on Nintendo Switch 2 and Battle.net . “Songs of the Past” launches in 2027 as a paid expansion for “The Witcher 3” on PC, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, and Nintendo Switch 2. It is available to wishlist now across select platforms. NEW RELEASES Star Wars Zero Company, a single-player turn-based tactics game set in the twilight of the Clone Wars, is now available for PC via the EA app, Steam, and Epic Games Store, and PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series consoles. In the new game, former Republic officer Hawks and Zero Company, a squad of unconventional professionals for hire, are recruited for an operation by Republic Intelligence. From ex-nobles to ex-cons, they now share one mission: stop the Infinite Coil, a Separatist-aligned cult, and their leader Kundri Fathom before the deadly Shadow Plague consumes the galaxy. Players must strategically navigate tactical operations, investigations and other missions through the original story. Star Wars Zero Company is now available in retail and digital storefronts for PC via the EA app, Steam, Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5 and XBOX Series consoles. The Digital Deluxe Edition, featuring unique cosmetic items inspired by the Clone Wars era, is available for $59.99 SRP on PC and SRP $69.99 on consoles. The Collector’s Edition is available for $299.99 SRP and features a Star Wars Zero Company-themed Hasbro Black Series Thermal Detonator, Steelbook, Desk Mat and more. Alongside the game’s launch, the soundtrack for Star Wars Zero Company, featuring an original score by GRAMMY® award-winning composer Gordy Haab, is available via Walt Disney Records. IN-GAME EVENTS Snoop Dogg lent his likeness and voice to a new Elusive Target mission in “Hitman World of Assassination,” playable now through Sept. 26 free in-game and via the Free Demo. The mission follows Agent 47 as he targets Dr. Cyrus Cane, whose cookie brand Morsizzles is set for a worldwide launch despite evidence linking it to several deaths during product testing. To stop the launch, Cane and the product must disappear. Agent 47 has the perfect opportunity to strike at a pre-launch party on Haven Island. Snoop Dogg’s son, Cordell C. Broadus, joins him as a party guest in the game. The two are the first father-son duo to appear together in the franchise. The Herbalist Pack, themed after the mission, is also available on all platforms. It includes permanent access to The Visionary two-level arcade contract, The Herbalist Assignment featuring Snoop Dogg and cosmetic items inspired by Snoop Dogg and the mission. ‘Nanny McPhee’ Musical Written by Emma Thompson to Open in London Next Summer Hulu Cancels Mindy Kaling-Created Comedy ‘Not Suitable for Work’ After One Season (EXCLUSIVE) Phyllida Law, Scottish Actress and Mother of Emma and Sophie Thompson, Dies at 94 Loading comments... articles.title: Dolly Parton Was Willing to Take Experimental Cancer Drugs In Order to Help Others in the Future, Her Sister Says in Online Tribute
articles.full_text: Aug 27, 2026 11:46am PT Dolly Parton Was Willing to Take Experimental Cancer Drugs In Order to Help Others in the Future, Her Sister Says in Online Tribute By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest Dolly Parton Was Willing to Take Experimental Cancer Drugs In Order to Help Others in the Future, Her Sister Says in Online Tribute 51 minutes ago Jon Stewart, Bruce Springsteen and Hasan Minhaj to Perform at New York’s Stand Up for Heroes Event 22 hours ago Miley Cyrus Honors Godmother Dolly Parton: ‘I Have an Angel by My Side. I Always Have’ 1 day ago See All Getty Images In addition to her tremendous country music career, Dolly Parton was known for her big heart. According to her sister, Stella Parton , Dolly’s desire to help others extended into her final days battling cancer. In a message posted to social media , Stella Parton wrote of Dolly, “My sister was one of the most generous, thoughtful and kind people I’ve ever known. What the world saw is exactly who she was, so much so, she told me recently that if there was no hope for her, she would still allow her medical team to try experimental drugs in the hope of helping others in the future.” Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 The tribute continued, “My sister was always thinking of others, and if you want to honor her legacy, show more kindness, lift others up, and give more of your time and resources, as she continued to do to the very end.” Popular on Variety Dolly Parton died of cancer on Aug. 25 at age 80. Her health struggles began to make headlines in the fall of 2025, when she announced that she would no longer be able to perform at a Las Vegas residency in December 2025 due to “some health challenges.” The queen of country music’s death had a profound impact on people across the country and around the world, with tributes pouring in from Taylor Swift, her goddaughter Miley Cyrus and even Donald Trump. “My big sister Dolly got her wings this past Tuesday. If anyone gets to heaven I’m sure she made it right on time. I know she’s showing out big time, in all her sparkles and shine. That was my sister’s way,” Stella Parton, a country singer-songwriter in her own right, also wrote. “Every Tuesday about this time, before the sun came up and the world was still asleep, she and I, for many years, had our coffee together over the phone. Being little farm girls, we’ve continued to be early risers. As she liked to say, ‘shoot Tedda, we get more work done before the sun comes up than most folks do all day long!’ We would catch up on gossip, as sisters do, and drink coffee and make plans, as it has always been our way.” Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist Loading comments...
