articles.full_text: Aug 27, 2026 12:00pm PT ‘Furious’ Renewed for Season 2 at Hulu By Ethan Shanfeld Plus Icon Ethan Shanfeld @ethanshanfeld Latest ‘Furious’ Renewed for Season 2 at Hulu 31 minutes ago Dolly Parton Was Willing to Take Experimental Cancer Drugs In Order to Help Others in the Future, Her Sister Says in Online Tribute 44 minutes ago Jon Stewart, Bruce Springsteen and Hasan Minhaj to Perform at New York’s Stand Up for Heroes Event 22 hours ago See All Hulu “ Furious ” has been renewed for Season 2 at Hulu. The thriller series starring Emmy Rossum has become a breakout hit for the streamer, with viewership growing week over week since its July 27 premiere date. The finale of the eight-episode Season 1 of “Furious” airs on Monday, Aug. 31. From Elizabeth Meriwether — the mind behind “New Girl,” “The Dropout” and “Dying for Sex” — “Furious” follows an FBI agent named Alice Black (Rossum), who is chasing down a mysterious and calculating female serial killer (Lola Petticrew). Variety chief TV critic Alison Herman gave the first season a positive review , praising the “stellar cast” and writing that the show “delivers a compelling study of female victimhood and what happens when women break our culture’s limited scripts for it.” “Furious” was created, written and executive produced by Meriwether. Rossum executive produced for Composition 8 along with Ronald Bass, Matt Olmstead and Sam Hoffman. Brian Kirk executive produced and directed the first two episodes. articles.title: ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks
articles.full_text: Aug 27, 2026 12:14pm PT ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest ‘GTA 6’ Drops 27 Minutes of New In-Game Footage on Netflix Amid Ongoing Rockstar Games Leaks 29 minutes ago What Audible Learned About 7,000 Listeners From Its NYC Bookless Bookstore: ‘How Do We Take Something Invisible and Make It Tangible?’ 1 hour ago New York Comic Con Unveils 2026 Professional Schedule Lineup, Including ‘Dungeon Crawler Carl’ Author-NBCUniversal TV Panel (EXCLUSIVE) 4 hours ago See All Rockstar Games Netflix dropped 27 minutes of new “Grand Theft Auto 6” content Thursday at 3 p.m. ET in a collaboration with Rockstar Games ahead of the highly anticipated title’s November release. The event, which was first announced earlier this month, comes as Rockstar continues to suffer ongoing “ GTA 6 ” gameplay leaks. The content was captured entirely from in-game footage on PlayStation 5 (the game will be released for PS5 and Xbox Series X and S on Nov. 19), per Netflix and Take-Two Interactive-owned publisher Rockstar. It marks the lengthiest look fans have gotten at “GTA 6” thus far, following two trailers released over the past three years. Related Stories Ben Jones, Actor Turned Politician Who Played Cooter Davenport in 'The Dukes of Hazzard,' Dies at 84 The official description for “GTA 6” reads: “Jason and Lucia have always known the deck is stacked against them. But when an easy score goes wrong, they find themselves on the darkest side of the sunniest place in America, in the middle of a criminal conspiracy stretching across the state of Leonida – forced to rely on each other more than ever if they want to make it out alive.” Popular on Variety Rockstar has stated Netflix will be the exclusive home of the “Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look” special for six hours before the content is released on YouTube and across other platforms. It seems that exclusivity has had an impact as user error reports for Netflix spiked just prior to the Netflix “GTA 6” reveal, hitting 3,129 at 2:49 p.m. ET, according to service-monitoring website Downdetector.com. Netflix says the “GTA 6” “extended look” event represents “the next evolution of storytelling and content” on the streaming platform: “This trailblazing partnership with Rockstar Games elevates games to the center of modern culture — bringing an in-depth look at one of the most anticipated releases in the history of entertainment to Netflix subscribers first.” Rockstar Games — which last week filed subpoenas related to the leaks — issued its first statement about the situation on Wednesday: “Dear all, We know that many of you have been waiting to hear from us regarding the events of the past week. It would be an understatement to say that having videos of Grand Theft Auto VI gameplay leak in this way has been heartbreaking for our team, and this is obviously not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time. We are very sorry that everything has taken as long as it has — from getting the game finished (nearly there!) to sharing more details and official gameplay, and providing the community with everything you want to know. We are very excited for everyone to see the extended look tomorrow. It has taken longer than we wanted to get it ready, but as with everything we do, we know we need to exceed your expectations, and we are determined to deliver at the level you expect and deserve. While it is unfortunate that the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers, we hope that everyone will wait a bit longer to experience the game for themselves on November 19. We want to thank everyone in the community who has reached out with messages of support this past week — your words meant more to this team than you can imagine. Ultimately, we are making this game for you, and without you, we would not have the privilege of making games. We look forward to sharing more with you soon. Sincerely, Rockstar Games” Later that day, Rockstar posted two messages on X noting its preferences regarding how fans go about creating content based on the Netflix event amid the outside leaks, writing: “Once Grand Theft Auto VI: An Extended Look debuts on Netflix, creators can share their reaction content across social and video platforms.” In a followup, Rockstar added: “Quick clarification: you are free to livestream An Extended Look from 3 p.m. ET on August 27 providing you adhere to platform-specific guidance and you do not simply restream or repost the unedited video in full without context or commentary.” More to come… Paul McCartney, Olivia Dean and Raye Make Mercury Prize Shortlist Loading comments... articles.title: Miley Cyrus Remembers Godmother Dolly Parton: “I Have An Angel By My Side”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine Writers Guild Foundation Taps 2026 Veterans Fellowship Cohort Miley Cyrus Remembers Godmother Dolly Parton: “I Have An Angel By My Side” ‘The Secret Lives Of Mormon Wives’: Taylor Frankie Paul Faces ‘Bachelorette’ Backlash & Jen Affleck Confronts Whitney Leavitt In Season 5 Trailer View All August 26, 2026 9:52am Story Arc HANNAH MONTANA, Miley Cyrus, Dolly Parton, 'Good Golly, Miss Dolly', (Season 1, aired Sept. 29, 2006), 2006-, © Disney Channel / Courtesy Everett Collection Miley Cyrus mourned the loss of her godmother and mentor Dolly Parton , who died Tuesday at the age of 80 , writing in an Instagram post the following morning that “the feeling of losing my Aunt Dolly is beyond what feels right to share.” “Our most sacred moments were private and they’ll stay there behind the stage, beneath the glamour & between our hearts,” she wrote. “What I KNOW is Dolly would want me to feel it, write a song about it, and then continue on and be strong. I have an angel by my side. I always have. One of our last conversations was about music and metamorphosis. 🦋” Cyrus concluded her emotional post: “I will always love her and want to make her proud. My heart breaks for the world, her family and friends who will miss her deeply. We’re in this loss together and we will see her in all of the most beautiful things. 💖” Watch on Deadline View this post on Instagram Related Stories Culture Remembering Dolly Parton: A Career in Photos News Dolly Parton: Keke Palmer, Pedro Pascal, Kacey Musgraves & More Pay Tribute To “One Of One” Country Music Legend Cyrus has extremely close familial and creative ties to Parton, who had been part of the younger star’s life since she was born. “I’ve known her since she was a baby,” Parton told Good Morning America in 2009. “Her father’s a friend of mine, and when she was born, he said, ‘You just have to be her godmother,’ and I said, ‘I accept.’ We never did do a big ceremony, but I’m so proud of her, love her, and she’s just like one of my own.” In a post of his own on Tuesday, after news of Parton’s death broke, the Cyrus patriarch honored Parton: “Like every little boy, I grew up loving Dolly Parton. She was a part of our lives, on our TV’s, right in our living rooms,” he wrote, adding: “Dolly recently sent me a beautiful message, telling me she loved me with her whole heart. I will always love her in the same way ….. with my whole heart … and I always will.” Parton also played Cyrus’ on-screen godmother, occasionally appearing on Hannah Montana across its four seasons. They have taken to stage and screen together at various points over the years since. In 2022, the pair co-hosted NBC’s Miley’s New Year’s Eve Party from Miami, Florida, featuring joint performances of some of their hits including “Wrecking Ball” and “I Will Always Love You.” Cyrus and Parton also collaborated musically several times. Cyrus joined Parton in 2010 at the 25th anniversary of Dollywood to sing “Jolene” — a song she has performed many times over since then. They performed it again together in 2019 at the Grammy Awards. Cyrus also co-wrote a track on her 2017 album Younger Now with Parton, titled “Rainbowland,” and the elder singer recruited her goddaughter to appear on her A Holly Dolly Christmas album in 2020. Set to air at 8 p.m. ET, the special will be hosted by Kevin Frazier and Nischelle Turner. It will feature interviews from ET , including her first appearance on the show in 1982. It also will feature interviews and new tributes from Dionne Warwick, Melissa Etheridge, Diane Warren, Debbie Allen and Jennifer Nettles. Since her death on Tuesday , all of the broadcast networks have aired primetime specials in tribute. CBS News and ABC News aired primetime specials that evening, and an NBC News special aired on Wednesday. PREVIOUSLY: CBS News and ABC News will air specials on Tuesday paying tribute to Dolly Parton, who died today at the age of 80. Watch on Deadline NBC plans a news special on Wednesday. A CBS News Special: Dolly Parton — An American Icon will air at 10 p.m. ET, with Gayle King and Tony Dokoupil along with a team of CBS News journalists commemorating Parton’s life. They will be joined by Anthony Mason, CBS News’ senior culture and senior national correspondent, and a correspondent in Dollywood in Tennessee. articles.title: Tyler Perry’s ‘Divorced Sistas’ & ‘Zatima’ Among 4 Former BET+ Series Renewed By Paramount+
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Tyler Perry’s ‘Divorced Sistas’ & ‘Zatima’ Among 4 Former BET+ Series Renewed By Paramount+ Rafe Judkins Inks Overall Deal With Paramount Television Studios As Paramount+ Ramps Up Worldbuilding Efforts Amazon MGM Studios Names Carina Walker Head Of YA View All August 27, 2026 10:30am Paramount+ EXCLUSIVE : Two months after BET+ was folded into Paramount+ , with its programming migrating to the larger streamer, four of the former BET+ original series have been renewed by Paramount+. They include Tyler Perry’s Divorced Sistas , picked up for Season 3, and Zatima (Season 6), as well as Carl Weber’s The Black Hamptons (Season 3) and The Family Business (Season 7). Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery News 2026 Premiere Dates For New & Returning Series On Broadcast, Streaming & Cable Divorced Sistas and Zatima ‘s orders are for 16 episodes, which is typical for Perry shows, running in two eight-episode installments. That has been the pattern for Divorced Sistas while Zatima ‘s seasons to date have consisted of 20 episodes, split in two batches of 10. That includes upcoming seasons of both series that had not been announced but had been quietly filming: a 20-episode fifth season of Zatima , and 16-episode second season of Divorced Sistas . The latter, a spinoff from Perry’s popular BET series Sistas , last summer logged the most watched series premiere on BET+. Watch on Deadline The Family Business and The Black Hamptons ’ pickups are for 10 episodes each. They are somewhat surprising given the large gap between seasons, especially for The Black Hamptons, whose renewal comes more than two and a half years after the series’ eight-episode second season ended its run on BET+. The Family Business ‘ 10-episode sixth season released its finale on Dec. 18 last year. It is possible that the renewals had been done unofficially awhile ago and are now being announced. The pickups for Divorced Sistas, Zatima, The Family Business and The Black Hamptons join the March Season 6 renewal for BET+ original comedy Ms. Pat Show, which was done ahead of BET+’s slate transition to Paramount+ in June. ‘We feel the migration was very successful, the audiences are showing up for sure, Paramount+ Head of Originals Jane Wiseman told Deadline last week, noting that the volume of originals that BET+ was known for is not going to go down now that the shows are on Paramount+. The integration of BET+ into Paramount+ involved Paramount buying out Tyler Perry Studios’ stake in BET+. He remains one of Paramount’s most prolific creators/producers across BET and Paramount+. “Our relationship with Tyler Perry is very strong, and I’m excited for more content from him, as well as working closely with our friends at BET Studios,” Wiseman said last week. BET Studios also works across Divorced Sistas, Zatima, The Family Business and The Black Hamptons . Here are details on the newly renewed series: Title: The Black Hamptons Season: 3 EPs: Carl Weber, ND Brown Jones, Trey Haley Logline: In this adaptation of Carl Weber’s novel, the Britton family faces high tensions with the newly arrived Johnsons in the upscale Black town of Sag Harbor, NY. Talent: Lamman Rucker, Vanessa Bell Calloway, Elise Neal, Brian White, Karon Riley, and Mike Merrill Episode count: 10 Eps Title: The Family Business Season: 7 EPs: Carl Weber, ND Brown Jones, Trey Haley, Ernie Hudson Logline: The wealthy Duncans run their lucrative New York-based criminal enterprise with iron fists, and family always comes first. Talent: Ernie Hudson, Valarie Pettiford, Darrin Dewitt, Javicia Leslie, Tami Roman, Sean Ringgold, Michael Jai White, Arrington Foster and Lisa Raye McCoy. Episode count: 10 Eps Title: Tyler Perry’s Divorced Sistas Season: 3 EPs: Created, directed, written and executive produced by Tyler Perry. Logline: What begins as one confession cracks open everything this group of women thought they were protecting. Years of deception, half-truths, and emotional compromises finally surface, forcing Rasheda, Geneva, Naomi, Tiffany, and Bridgette to confront not just the men in their lives, but one another. Talent: LeToya Luckett, Khadeen Indréa, Porscha Coleman, Briana Price, Jennifer Sears, DeVon Franklin, Ronreaco Lee, and Robert Christopher Riley. Episode count: 16 Eps Title: Tyler Perry’s Zatima Season: 6 EPs: Created and executive produced by Tyler Perry. Logline: Revelations are birthed from misunderstandings, lessons of love and loss are painstakingly learned, and forgiveness and reconciliation dominate. For Zac and Fatima, the fight to protect their family becomes the center of everything as they learn what it truly takes to hold a life and a future… Together. Talent: DeVale Ellis, Crystal Reneé Hayslett, Nzinga Imani, Remington Hoffman, Cameron Fuller and Guyviaud Joseph. articles.title: BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style “Public Service Algorithm” Propelled By Creators
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style “Public Service Algorithm” Propelled By Creators Prime Video Sets Access Doc Series On Peter Crouch & Abby Clancy Prime Video Revs Up Doc Series About F1 Driver Lando Norris View All August 27, 2026 10:37am BBC boss Matt Brittin BBC The BBC ‘s Director General, Matt Brittin , has said the British broadcaster’s streaming service could benefit from a “public service algorithm” that allows it to function more like YouTube. The striking plans, which Brittin warned was not “policy” at this stage, would see the BBC iPlayer opened up to creators and make the service more like YouTube, the platform that the exec oversaw in EMEA before joining the BBC. Related Stories News BBC Files New Motion To Dismiss Donald Trump’s $10 Billion Lawsuit, Challenges Claims Of U.S. Viewership Via VPN News Donald Trump Waging $10B Legal War Against BBC On Basis “Doctored” Documentary May Have Been Viewed 285 Times In America In his first address to the industry today at the Edinburgh TV Festival, the former Google exec once again warned the BBC iPlayer had “fallen behind” rivals due to a focus on content spend over technology in recent years. He first made similar noise in a town hall speech to staff in May soon after he became DG. Brittin was careful to say this was “no fault of the team” at the BBC and that the content spend meant he “inherited incredible audience reach,” but leaves a puzzle over the iPlayer’s future and an immediate challenge in improving the iPlayer recommendations functionality. Watch on Deadline His blue-sky solution was for the iPlayer to function more like YouTube by hosting creators from around the UK – “providing they stick to the guidelines we choose to set.” He didn’t detail how this would be achieved, what the remuneration offer would be or why creators would choose to opt for BBC digital services over YouTube or other social media platforms, but it is still one of the more tantalizing ideas to be floated by a director general of the BBC for some time. Brittin also called for the BBC to be “a more open platform” and that there was a need to “create sovereign media public space,” while adding the UK could build something “unadulterated by commercial interests, by algorithms that have other interests at heart.” The service, which he dubbed ‘iPlayer 2.0″, would be based around “educating, informing and entertaining the public here and ideally around the world,” he said, adding it should be created “it in a way that’s not biased towards the incentives of a U.S. tech company or commercial interests. It should be biased towards what we want public service to be all about.” It is likely the BBC, which is in the midst of cutting 2,000 roles to save around £500M ($679M), will have to cut programs to pay for improvements to the iPlayer. He noted that the BBC had shed £1.3B over the past decade and services and programs would inevitably come under pressure. Brittin has spent his first 100 days at the BBC travelling to different parts of the mammoth organization to identify where to prioritize his efforts and how to wrestle with the type of existential crisis that outgoing BBC presenter Amol Rajan described earlier today. Brittin admitted he had not “understood quite the severity” of the financial pressure heaped on the BBC. “Obviously, to get to that scale of savings, there’s uncertainty hanging over a lot more colleagues than those who will eventually leave the organization,” he added. “That’s really hard to deal with. articles.title: Amazon MGM Orders Penn Badgley Murder Mystery Series ‘Everyone In My Family Has Killed Someone’ From David Hemingson
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Andrew Bachelor Directs & Stars In Supernatural Horror Film ‘Tap Twice’ Amazon MGM Orders Penn Badgley Murder Mystery Series ‘Everyone In My Family Has Killed Someone’ From David Hemingson Jamie Dornan Joins Zoë Kravitz In Megan Park’s Mystery Apple Film View All August 27, 2026 11:00am Penn Badgley Slaven Vlasic/Getty Images Amazon MGM Studios has announced a series order for Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone , a darkly comedic murder mystery from Fifth Season and Made Up Stories, based on the bestselling book series by Benjamin Stevenson . You ‘s Penn Badgley will star, with David Hemingson ( The Holdovers ) set as showrunner and executive producer. Badgley returns to Amazon after wrapping a starring role opposite Meghann Fahy in their forthcoming rom-com You Deserve Each Other — also from Fifth Season, along with Likely Story. The project gets off the ground at Amazon MGM after an attempt at series development of the book at HBO. Related Stories Casting Elizabeth McGovern Joins Amazon MGM Horror Film 'Seasons' Executives Amazon MGM Studios Names Carina Walker Head Of YA Set deep in the dense mountains of Vermont’s Northeast Kingdom, Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone follows Ern Cunningham (Badgley), a mystery-writing expert who reluctantly attends a family reunion to welcome his brother Michael home from prison — the same brother Ern helped convict. When a frozen body appears and a snowstorm traps everyone inside, the deaths begin to mount. Everyone in his family has already killed someone — either by accident or otherwise. Watch on Deadline Mariner Books published the book in 2022. It’s Stevenson’s first in an internationally bestselling series, dubbed Ernest Cunningham Mysteries , whose fifth installment is currently in the works. Hemingson exec produces alongside Bruna Papandrea, Steve Hutensky and Jeanne Snow of Made Up Stories, Molly Allen, Badgley and Stevenson. Fifth Season and Made Up Stories are producing and will together serve as the studio. Fifth Season and Made Up Stories reteam following collaborations on series including The Good Daughter and Wolf Like Me for Peacock, Roar for Apple TV+, Nine Perfect Strangers for Hulu, Pieces of Her and Anatomy of a Scandal for Netflix, The Last Anniversary for AMC and The Lost Flowers of Alice Hart for Prime Video. In a statement on the series order, author Stevenson shared, “I am blown away by the vision and enthusiasm everyone has for bringing this book, and Ernest Cunningham, to the screen. Penn perfectly captures Ern’s clueyness and cleverness, and David has brought bags of wit and heart to the script. With the passion of Amazon MGM Studios, Bruna and Steve behind us we have an absolutely killer team, and I can’t wait to solve a murder with them!” Peter Friedlander, Amazon MGM’s Head of Global Television, added: “ Everyone in My Family Has Killed Someone is a brilliantly inventive series that subverts the murder mystery genre in the most unexpected and entertaining ways. Ben created a world that is darkly funny and wickedly clever. Paired with David’s sharp storytelling and Penn’s magnetic presence, and with our incredible partners at Fifth Season and Made Up Stories, this series is going to be something truly special for Prime Video.” No stranger to murder, nor successful book adaptations, Badgley is coming off of a starring turn as serial killer Joe Goldberg in the hit thriller series You , based on the book series by Caroline Kepnes, which originated at Lifetime before moving to Netflix for its final four seasons. Otherwise best known for starring in The CW’s Gossip Girl , his upcoming slate includes the Bleecker Street thriller NDA , in addition to You Deserve Each Other . He is repped by Brillstein Entertainment Partners, CAA, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller. Oscar-nominated for his script The Holdovers , the holiday dramedy directed for Focus Features by Alexander Payne, Hemingson also produced that film, marking the screen debut of Tony ‘s Dominic Sessa. Otherwise best known for creating the ABC series Whiskey Cavalier , the writer-producer has also worked on The Catch , Don’t Trust the B—- in Apartment 23 , Kitchen Confidential and myriad other series. He is repped by 3 Arts, WME, and McKuin Frankel & Whitehead. A stand-up comic, as well as an author, Stevenson’s books have sold over a million copies in 29 territories. The latest in his Ernest Cunningham series, Everyone in This Bank Is a Thief , released in March. articles.title: New Edinburgh TV Event Confirmed At Launch Event Attended By Richard Gadd
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style “Public Service Algorithm” Propelled By Creators Prime Video Sets Access Doc Series On Peter Crouch & Abby Clancy Prime Video Revs Up Doc Series About F1 Driver Lando Norris View All August 27, 2026 11:15am Richard Gadd and Phoebe Waller-Bridge were discovered in Edinburgh Josh Telles for Deadline/Getty Edinburgh will have a TV festival in August after all. Scotland’s Cabinet Secretary for Education, Culture and Gaelic, Màiri McAllan, has today confirmed an initiative aimed at developing a new festival that will sit alongside the other Edinburgh festivals, including the film and comedy events. This confirms Deadline’s scoop from last month . This outlined how Screen Scotland had commissioned a piece of work aimed at exploring an industry event that would replace the Edinburgh TV Festival , which is next year moving to Manchester after 51 years. Related Stories News 'The Pitt' & 'The Celebrity Traitors' Win Prizes At Edinburgh TV Festival Awards News BBC Boss Matt Brittin Outlines Concept For YouTube-Style "Public Service Algorithm" Propelled By Creators A launch event attended by Baby Reindeer and Half Man creator Richard Gadd was held today in Scotland’s capital, as many of the UK’s TV sector attended the final Edinburgh TV Festival, which is held at the Edinburgh International Conference Centre. Gadd and the likes of Fleabag creator Phoebe Waller-Bridge were discovered by the TV industry while performing their shows in the city during August. Watch on Deadline As we previously reported, the initial development work was funded by Screen Scotland and completed in early summer 2026. Per a news release today, this was undertaken “with fresh eyes” and explored “how Edinburgh’s August festivals partner to present a new offer to the global content industries, in response to the increasingly blurred boundaries between the different creative artforms and the way creative talent, IP and ideas move fluidly between them.” Former Edinburgh TV Festival Creative Director Rowan Woods , who oversaw the initial development, has been appointed to lead the next stage of development, which will again be funded by Screen Scotland and delivered through The Fringe Society. Working with the Fringe Society, Screen Scotland and a broader advisory group, she will consult widely across the August festivals and with venues, broadcasters, platforms, content creators, publishers and other potential participants and audiences to establish the shape of the new initiative. This will include “how it can best support the connection of new talent and IP to content commissioners worldwide.” This consultation phase is expected to conclude in early spring 2027, with an initial pilot planned for next August. This will likely place it in direct competition with the Manchester event, whose details haven’t yet been announced. Edinburgh is awash with energy during August, with the Fringe attracting hundreds of comedy acts, who perform in venues across the city during the month. Alongside that is the Edinburght Film Festival, the Edinburgh TV Festival and the Edinburgh International Book Festival, making the city a hive of activity. Many TV professional bemoaned the plan to move the TV fest out, even though costs have become prohibitively high in many cases. The Scottish Government is providing funding support for the new event’s development via Screen Scotland. More details will follow next year. David Smith, Director of Screen Scotland, said: “Edinburgh has a unique role to play in bringing together the people, ideas and creative work that will shape the future of the screen and wider creative industries. Every August, the city becomes a remarkable meeting place for talent from around the world, alongside audiences, producers, commissioners, artists and creative thinkers. “We have an opportunity to build on that extraordinary concentration of talent and energy and create something new, ambitious and genuinely distinctive for the global industry.” Separately, Screen Scotland is establish the Lynda Myles Debate as a keynote element of the August festivals from from next. This will “honour the contribution” of Lynda Myles, formerly Director of the Edinburgh International Film Festival and co-creator of the Edinburgh TV Festival, to the city’s festival month. “I’m deeply touched and honoured to have the debate named after me,” said Myles. It’s exciting to see the importance of ideas and discussion being recognised in the plans for the new event, especially as this was the initial intention of the creation of the Edinburgh Television Festival in 1976.” Odessa Young In Talks For Charlene Role In ‘Heat 2’; María Cid Top Choice For Gabi Paramount+ Renews Tyler Perry’s ‘Zatima’ & ‘Divorced Sistas,’ 2 Other Ex-BET+ Shows Optimus Prime Voice Actor Peter Cullen, 85; ‘Menace II Society’s Samuel Monroe Jr, 52 Danny Ramirez Set For ‘Miami Vice ’85’ With Michael B. articles.title: Tim Curry Remembered By ‘Rocky Horror Show’ Playwright Richard O’Brien & The Broadway Revival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Anna Louizos Dies: Broadway Scenic Designer Of ‘In The Heights’ & ‘Avenue Q’ Was 69 Samuel Monroe Jr. Dies: ‘Menace II Society’ Actor Was 52 Rosie O’Donnell Joins Producing Team Of London-Bound Musical ‘Indigo’ About Autistic Teenager View All August 27, 2026 11:51am Tim Curry, 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' (1975) 20th Century Fox Film Corp./Everett Collection UPDATE, with tribute from playwright Richard O’Brien: Richard O’Brien, who wrote The Rocky Horror Show and cast his friend Tim Curry in the central role of Frank-N-Furter back in the ’70s, joined the current Broadway revival in offering up a heartfelt tribute to the late actor who died Tuesday at the age of 80. In a message written by O’Brien (who also played Riff Raff in both the stage musical and film) and posted on Instagram by his son Linus O’Brien, the playwright writes, “It is with an exceptionally sad heart and misted-up eyes that I share these words with you. Tim Curry was a wonderful man by nature who was also a wonderful performer and understood the difference between such delightful achievements. He never sought attention and never put himself before the roles that he played. He was, in short, a good egg and class act. It was both a privilege and delight to have known him and worked with him. Rest in peace dear Tim.” Related Stories News Tim Curry Dies: ‘The Rocky Horror Picture Show’ Actor Was 80 News Luke Evans, ‘Clue’ Stars, Carol Burnett, Josh Gad & More Pay Tribute To Tim Curry Broadway’s hit Tony-nominated revival of The Rocky Horror Show also remembered the man who made Frank-N-Furter a style icon in high heels, garter-supported fishnets and skin-tight bodice and who embodied one of the most beloved, campiest characters to ever grace a midnight movie. Watch on Deadline Richard O’Brien, Tim Curry and Patricia Quinn in ‘ The Rocky Horror Picture Show ‘ (1975) 20th Century Fox/Everett Collection In a post on the production’s Instagram page, the show writes, alongside a photo of Curry in character from The Rocky Horror Picture Show , “Remembering the legendary Tim Curry, who first brought Frank-N-Furter to life. We are heartbroken by his passing and grateful for the unforgettable legacy he leaves behind. Thank you, Tim, for giving the world a little more freedom, a little more fearlessness, and through the tears in our eyes, the courage to BE IT. We love you.” The “BE IT” line references one of Rocky Horror ‘s most famous catchphrases: “Don’t dream it, be it.” Although a flop when Curry led the cast in its original 1975 Broadway staging, panned by critics and closing after just 45 performances, the musical was revived for a more successful run in a 2002 Circle in the Square staging starring Tom Hewitt, Lea DeLaria, Jarrod Emick and Joan Jett. An even bigger hit revival arrived at Broadway’s Studio 54 venue last March in the Sam Pinkleton-directed staging starring Luke Evans (in the Frank-N-Furter role), Rachel Dratch, Andrew Durand, Amber Gray, Stephanie Hsu and Juliette Lewis. Last week, The Rocky Horror Show grossed a big $949,446 for the final week or original cast members Evans, Hsu and Durand. Jake Shears takes over for Evans on September 11, with Lorna Courtney and Kevin McHale joining the cast August 25. articles.title: ‘Furious’ Renewed For Season 2 By Hulu Ahead Of Season 1 Finale
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Tyler Perry’s ‘Divorced Sistas’ & ‘Zatima’ Among 4 Former BET+ Series Renewed By Paramount+ Rafe Judkins Inks Overall Deal With Paramount Television Studios As Paramount+ Ramps Up Worldbuilding Efforts Amazon MGM Studios Names Carina Walker Head Of YA View All August 27, 2026 12:00pm (L-R): Lola Petticrew, Emily Rossum in Hulu's 'Furious' Disney/Sarah Shatz Hulu has renewed Liz Meriwether ‘s thriller Furious , starring Emmy Rossum , for a second season. It is an unusually early pickup by the Disney streamer which (like other platforms) usually waits for long-tail viewership data before making renewal decision. Furious is still rolling out its first season, with the season finale, written by Meriwether, premiering Aug. 31. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Series Renewals Photo Gallery Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Cancellations Photo Gallery: Series Ending This Year & Beyond The pickup of Furious follows t he cancellation earlier this week of another freshman Hulu origina l, comedy Not Suitable For Work , which was done two months after that series’ finale. Hulu has not released ratings data for Furious yet but noted in the renewal announcement that viewership has been growing week over week. Watch on Deadline Nielsen’s reporting is delayed, with numbers for Furious ‘ launch week coming out later today. Despite premiering with only three episodes vs. full-season drops for many streaming series, Furious is rumored to have cracked the Top 10 for streaming originals, which is based on total minutes consumed. Despite its staggered release, Furious also has been a consistent presence on Luminate’s weekly rankings, peaking at No.5 with 2.43M U.S. views for its first full week of release. Additionally, Furious is believed to be the #1 series on Disney+/Hulu worldwide for the month of August and the #2 freshman drama on Hulu in the U.S. year to date, with 4B cross-media impressions. Furious ‘ solid performance, coupled with its 98% critics score on Rotten Tomatoes and reasonable cost by streaming standards likely tipped the scale for an early renewal. From creator and executive producer Meriwether, 20th Television and Searchlight Television, Furious follows an FBI agent, Alice Black (Emmy Rossum) on the hunt for a mysterious and calculating female serial killer (Lola Petticrew). Both walk their own paths toward justice, and as their lives start to intertwine, the line between right and wrong begins to blur. Quincy Tyler Bernstine and Scoot McNairy star alongside Rossum and Petticrew; Jake Lacy, Rob Delaney, Hope Davis, Rob Yang and Steve Way guest starred in Season 1, which was also executive produced by Rossum for Composition 8, along with Ronald Bass, Matt Olmstead, and Sam Hoffman. Brian Kirk executive produced and directed episodes 101 and 102. Furious is now streaming on Hulu and Hulu on Disney+ in the US for bundle subscribers and on Disney+ internationally. articles.title: Jelly Roll Takes Jabs at Donald Trump While Guest Hosting ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 7:42pm Jelly Roll on 'Jimmy Kimmel Live!' Disney Logo text During Jelly Roll ‘s return as guest host of Jimmy Kimmel Live! on Monday night , the country singer took several opportunities to throw jabs at President Donald Trump . During his opening monologue, the country singer-rapper started with the “main event of America this weekend” — the IndyCar race in Washington, D.C., dubbed the Freedom 250 Grand Prix. “The cars drove through the streets of D.C., and there’s Donald Trump, who apparently has never held a flag before,” he said, as a video played of the president waving a green flag. “What a shit job. How do you fuck up waving a flag?” Related Stories Music Trump Orders Flags to Fly at Half-Staff in Wake of Dolly Parton's Death: "The World Loves You" TV Rosie O'Donnell Joke About Trump and Natalie Harp Draws Gasps From 'Kimmel' Crowd As the audience broke out in laughter, Jelly Roll continued, “But the president seemed to enjoy the IndyCar race, which was a real switch up for him, because normally he only likes his own race.” “Trump also drove around the track in his motorcade doing what they call the lap of honor, which sounds like a loyalty program at a strip club,” the singer quipped. “Five percent cash back in the champagne room for all Lap of Honor members. Sadly, those are the only laps Trump’s been doing lately.” Jelly Roll’s “laps” joke was only the beginning of several more digs directed at Trump’s physical fitness during the monologue. “According to the Washington Post , a lot of doctors are worried about the president’s weight. After his last physical, we found out Trump gained 14 pounds, which means he’s now tipping the scales at almost 240. It’s crazy. Think about this, y’all. In the last few years, I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump,” the “Save Me” artist said, prompting laughter from the studio crowd. He added, “And let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing.” Jelly Roll told the audience they should “take it easy” on Trump because “we shouldn’t be making fun of the president for his weight because we know that he would never do that to other people.” That’s when a video montage started to play of the president talking about people’s weight and appearance on many different occasions, calling others a “big fat slob,” “fat pig” and “fatter than ever,” among other terms. “Well, if that ain’t the pot calling the kettle fat,” the singer said. “Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you’ll be happy to see your penis again.” Jelly Roll first guest hosted Jimmy Kimmel Live! in July 2025 before returning this week while regular host Jimmy Kimmel is on his summer hiatus. The country star has been open about maintaining an apolitical public stance . Despite being criticized for avoiding politics, Jelly Roll told reporters backstage at the 2026 Grammys that “people shouldn’t care” about his political opinions because “I’m a dumb redneck.” THR

For more color payoff and matte finish options, look for products marketed as “skin tints” or “tinted moisturizers” — just be sure they have SPF in the mix. Alternatively, skip the search and see our five tried-and-tested favorites below. And because Tarte’s formula has more color payoff, it’s available in a wider range of shades than the category’s sheerer alternatives. best serum Ilia Super Serum Skin Tint SPF 40 $48 at ilia Ilia’s fan-favorite skin tint is another multi-hyphenate miracle worker that prioritizes a wide shade range, deep moisture and sun care as skin care (and vise versa). Parton died Tuesday in Nashville at 80, her family announced. She died after a “brief battle with cancer,” her reps told People . “A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” Swift began in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter . “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one.” Related Stories Music Beyoncé Remembers Dolly Parton as "Bold and Brilliant" in Touching Tribute TV '20/20' Sets Dolly Parton Special Tribute: Where to Watch Online “She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously,” Swift continued. “She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist.” She concluded, “Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too. Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.” Last September, the “Jolene” singer announced she was postponing a set of Las Vegas concerts to deal with “some health challenges.” In May, she canceled her Las Vegas residency, but continued to put on a brave front, telling her fans that she was OK. In July, just ahead of her Madison Square Garden wedding, Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to varying organizations, including to Dolly Parton”s Imagination Library. Parton shared an Instagram video thanking the married couple for their donation, where she said she was “blown away and overjoyed with that gratitude.” “Now, it’s evident, that you have made giving back a key part of your lives, so hey, when you have you firstborn, can I have it?” she joked. “Because that is gonna be one special baby!” The 14-time Grammy Award winner also reflected on the two-time Oscar nominee’s legacy in Parton’s 2023 profile with The Hollywood Reporter . “Dolly is a force of evolution and transformation in our industry, but she does it with such playful levity it almost looks effortless. Her sense of humor and mischief are easily my favorite things about her, because I think it forces the world to reconcile that a woman can be a serious artist and writer who also has raucous fun with it, can make people laugh and be in on every joke,” Swift told THR . “She’s never stopped challenging herself to clear new hurdles and explore new territory artistically, and I think that speaks to her great curiosity about the human condition. She’s a legendary empath and the storyteller for the ages. She’s also having the most fun doing it.” THR

articles.title: Dolly Parton, a Hollywood Treasure Who Lit Up the Screen With Her Authentic Self
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By David Rooney Plus Icon David Rooney Chief Film Critic DavidCRooney1 Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 7:58pm From left: Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton and Jane Fonda in '9 to 5.' 20th Century Fox Film Corp./Courtesy Everett Collection When Jane Fonda was developing the rollicking 1980 workplace farce 9 to 5 , inspired by a real-life women’s rights organization of that name, at some point the project shape-shifted from the serious drama that was originally planned to a comedy, enlisting the brilliant Colin Higgins to direct and work on the screenplay with Patricia Resnick. Having cast Lily Tomlin as her acerbic ally in the secretarial pool, Fonda and producer Bruce Gilbert wanted to broaden the film’s appeal, landing on the idea of a third lead who might push beyond urban liberals to reach mainstream, conservative and Southern audiences. From that commercially-driven demographic strategy, Dolly Parton the Movie Star was born. Related Stories Movies James Lew, Stuntman and 'Hot Shots! Part Deux' Actor, Dies at 73 Movies Rene Malo, 'Decline of the American Empire' Producer, Dies at 84 As Doralee Rhodes, the happily married secretary of Dabney Coleman’s lecherous corporate vice president, kept busy dodging his unwelcome advances, Parton was a natural. Her luminosity, effervescence, folksy delivery and innate comic timing infused the film with livewire energy, whether she was fantasizing about hog-tieing and spit-roasting the boss or bringing that fantasy to life, like a seasoned rodeo queen. The movie became a massive hit, grossing more than $103 million at a time when a women-centric, empowerment-minded blockbuster was almost unimaginable. Every one of the predominantly female ensemble comedies that became pop cultural fixtures in later decades — The First Wives Club , Sister Act , The Devil Wears Prada , Bridesmaids — owes 9 to 5 a debt. The eternally catchy country pop theme song Parton wrote and recorded for the film left its own mark, reaching number one on Billboard ’s Country, Hot 100 and Adult Contemporary charts. Parton often said in interviews that she came up with the song’s tapping typewriter-key rhythm by clicking her long acrylic fingernails together. The death of a global superstar is invariably a sad event, but the loss of Parton today at age 80 is an uncommonly crushing blow to many of us. For gay men, she was our North Star, a beacon of inclusivity in a world of persistent intolerance. Her theme park near the Great Smoky Mountains, Dollywood, was a pilgrimage destination on the queer-tourism map. If gays ran the Oval Office, her birthday would be a national holiday. Parton frequently mined self-deprecating humor from her almost cartoonish appearance — the boobs, the big blonde wigs, the bejeweled outfits, the cosmetic surgeries — and yet she remained unequivocally real. I saw her perform just once at a Radio City Music Hall concert in 2005 as part of her Vintage Tour, along with a sea of gay men who had resurrected their Westernwear from Madonna’s “Don’t Tell Me” period for the occasion. When an elaborate piece of stage scenery malfunctioned and failed to descend from the flies during her opening number, Parton quipped that a little old country girl from East Tennessee should never have even attempted something so fancy. The iconic look and larger-than-life persona were an inextricable part of her sui generis screen presence in a handful of beloved movies. She was never an actress with significant range, but the thing is, she never had to be. The sweetness, the sense of humor and the old-fashioned goodness that epitomized who she was in her many walks of life made her incandescent. From her very first entrance, we knew exactly who her character was, almost all of them a mirror to who Parton was in real life. In The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas , starring as Miss Mona Stangley alongside Burt Reynolds, she made being the madam of a brothel — or as she puts it in one of her songs, “A Lil’ Ole Bitty Pissant Country Place” — seem wholesome, caring for her “girls” like they were her own children. Rewatching that cornbread musical in a Houston gay bar in the early ‘80s was a hootenanny I’ll never forget, Stetsons constantly flying up in the air in jubilant appreciation. In Steel Magnolias , an all-star tear-jerker about the fortitude to be drawn from female friendship in times of sadness, Parton played the big-haired, open-hearted small-town Louisiana beauty parlor owner, Truvy Jones. (Her character names alone are divine.) Her salon was a social hub, a place for harmless gossip and friendly banter, and a respite for its regulars from their frequently exasperating husbands and sons. Watching Parton hold her own alongside pros like Sally Field, Olympia Dukakis and Shirley MacLaine was bliss, not to mention seeing her character in a loving marriage with the coolest — OK, and sexiest — of modern-day cowboys, Sam Shepard. It’s doubtful that anyone would try to make a case for the 1984 Sylvester Stallone vehicle, Rhinestone ; I wonder if there’s even a living soul who managed to get through it. But Parton could sew a silk purse out of a sow’s ear, introducing two top 10 country hits in the movie. Her gifts were put to more memorable use in the cheesy but disarming comedy Straight Talk , as Shirlee Kenyon, a Southern transplant looking to rebuild her life in Chicago, where she becomes an accidental talk radio call-in advice show host. And Parton brought her signature warmth and wit to the guilty pleasure Joyful Noise , playing G.G. Sparrow, a feisty widow wrestling for control of her small Georgia town’s choir with Queen Latifah’s Vi Rose Hill. When Vi Rose gets her in a headlock, G.G. squawks, “Oow, you’re breakin’ my hair!” Putting aside her many cameos and popular TV movies, Parton’s filmography was by most standards meager. But she inhabited every role with spirit, vigor, compassion and charm for days, qualities entirely true to herself. Her death leaves the world a much poorer place. THR

articles.title: Haim Saban, Lawrence Bender and Teddy Schwarzman Among Industry Group Accusing Mark Ruffalo of “Antisemitism” in Attack on Paramount Leadership
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 9:31pm Mark Ruffalo Monica Schipper/Getty Images An entertainment industry group that includes Hollywood producers Haim Saban , Lawrence Bender and Teddy Schwarzman has released a statement condemning the alleged “antisemitic tropes” underpinning Mark Ruffalo ‘s opposition to Paramount’s leadership amid its proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). The statement comes from a group calling itself The Brigade, which describes itself as “a group of nearly 1,000 members, friends, and allies of the Jewish community who are proud to be working in film, television, music, Broadway, social and digital, and other platforms in and around the entertainment industry.” Related Stories News Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo From Paramount "Antisemitism" Claim: "All of Us Artists Could Stand to Be More Like Mark" Business Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Calls Out Mark Ruffalo's Paramount Remarks: "Obsession and Demonization" As well as Power Rangers media mogul Saban, Reservoir Dogs and Pulp Fiction producer Bender and Black Bear founder and CEO Schwarzman, the Brigade includes amongst its ranks Ram Bergman, Matti Leshem, Anthony Bregman, Micah Green and Lynn Harris. The Brigade’s statement comes in the wake of Ruffalo’s Aug. 21 Instagram post that spotlighted Oracle’s ties to the Israeli military — specifically a viral clip of former Oracle CEO Safra Catz at the Israeli-American Council National Summit in 2024 as it related to Israel’s war effort in Gaza. “Singling out Jewish executives and describing them in terms lifted from centuries-old antisemitic conspiracy theories, while invoking Israel as the frame for that attack, is antisemitic,” reads the statement. “It is unacceptable to introduce Jews, antizionism, or antisemitism into conversations about business transactions, simply because those involved are Jewish.” Ruffalo has long opposed both the Paramount-WBD merger over concerns about Hollywood jobs and has also long campaigned for Palestinian rights and condemned Israel’s actions in Gaza and the West Bank. The actor’s post called out Oracle founder Larry Ellison, Paramount’s controlling shareholder through a family trust, and the father of Paramount CEO David Ellison. Larry Ellison is also the key financial backstop behind Paramount’s merger attempt with WBD. The statement added: “This is a callous continuation of the ongoing campaign by the same individuals and groups targeting Jewish people and the state of Israel, a pattern of antisemitism and misinformation that puts our community in grave danger.” After Ruffalo’s initial Instagram post, a Paramount spokesperson issued a reply to the four-time Oscar-nominated and two-time Emmy-winning actor that called for the temperature of the debate around the WBD deal to be lowered and characterized Ruffalo’s remarks as “antisemitic.” In a viral X post, Ruffalo fired back that the “accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest.” The Brigade joins the Simon Wiesenthal Center in condemning Ruffalo’s Paramount posts. But in her own statement , Emmy-winning Hacks actress Hannah Einbinder described the “antisemitism” claims against Ruffalo as “ludicrous,” and implored more in Hollywood to “be more like Mark.” Read the full statement from The Brigade below: We are writing on behalf of a group of nearly 1000 members, friends, and allies of the Jewish community who are proud to be working in film, television, music, Broadway, social and digital, and other platforms in and around the entertainment industry. It is unfortunate that we are yet again forced to state our unequivocal condemnation of the use of antisemitic tropes and narratives by those who use their platform for targeted hate speech toward Jews. Singling out Jewish executives and describing them in terms lifted from centuries-old antisemitic conspiracy theories, while invoking Israel as the frame for that attack, is antisemitic. It is unacceptable to introduce Jews, antizionism, or antisemitism into conversations about business transactions, simply because those involved are Jewish. There is nothing “strange” about a Jewish executive discussing substantive issues about tech. This is not commentary on a merger. It is not a criticism of a government. It is simple antisemitism, where Jewish executives are portrayed as a secretive and powerful wealth-hoarding elite delighting in mass death. This is the same rhetoric that Nazis, Soviets, and the Klan weaponized against Jews, and its consequences are not only historical: they show up today in attacks against Jews in our streets, our synagogues, and our schools. This is a callous continuation of the ongoing campaign by the same individuals and groups targeting Jewish people and the state of Israel, a pattern of antisemitism and misinformation that puts our community in grave danger. There is no excuse and no defense for this rhetoric, including the “I have Jewish friends” rationale, and there are many questions that demand an answer — including, is there someone behind the funding of this campaign that is continuously perpetrated by the same individuals? We will keep standing up against this hatred. Because when we say, NEVER AGAIN, we mean it. THR
