articles.title: Marlo Miazga Launches M Media With CBC Order For “Deeply Personal” Doc ‘Ground Control’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse British Hulu Original ‘Raising Chelsea’ Returning For Second Season On Disney+ Marlo Miazga Launches M Media With CBC Order For “Deeply Personal” Doc ‘Ground Control’ ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role In Trailer For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Comedy-Drama View All August 26, 2026 12:00am Marlo Miazga M Media EXCLUSIVE: Canadian producer and showrunner Marlo Miazga is launching a production company with a “deeply personal” documentary for CBC about her death of her teenage child. M Media will operate out of Toronto, as a IP-focused media business making scripted and unscripted content, with former Sphere Media boss Miazga at the helm. Miazga’s debut commission, Ground Control , is a feature documentary that has been in development alongside a memoir she is writing for Random House Canada titled Ground Control : Losing My Child to Suicide . The book, co-written with journalist Katrina Onstad, details her tragic story of losing Miazga’s 14-year-old child, Mars, to suicide in 2020 and the aftermath. Related Stories News 'Son Of A Critch': Trailer For Final Season Of Canadian Sitcom Sees Mark Having A Midlife Crisis At 17 Casting Assaad Bouab & Caroline Dhavernas Join CBC's 'Saint-Pierre'; First Look At Season 3 Canadian pubcaster CBC has now greenlit production. This will begin in October with delivery aligned for spring next year following the official launch of the book on January 26, 2027. Production finance is in place with Telefilm Canada’s Theatrical Documentary Program, the Canada Media Fund’s POV program and the Roger Documentary Fund all contributing. Watch on Deadline Directing the film is Chase Joynt ( No Ordinary Man ), with Greg Beer and Onstad the writers. Miazga will be joined as an executive producer by Catalyst founder Julie Bristow, who is a long-time colleague and an advocate for mental health, with Ryan Dias also an exec. Ground Control will have a theatrical run in Canada, which is being handled by Eyesteel Films. Worldwide rights are being shopped. Miazga is one of Canada’s premiere producers, and was most recently President and exec producer at Sphere Media’s Unscripted and Kids & Family arms. At Sphere, she oversaw docs such as Monkey on a Stick: Murder, Madness and the Hare Krishnas , an adaptation of Anne Allan’s book Dancing with Diana: A Memoir and a doc series based on Sophie Grégoire Trudeau’s memoir-cum-manifesto Closer Together: Knowing Ourselves, Loving Each Other. Return to entrepreneurial roots The launch of M returns Miazga to her entrepreneurial roots, having co-founder her first company, NewroadMedia, in 2011 with CBC exec Ann Marie Redmond. She went on to work with Bristow, another former CBC exec, at Bristow Global Media (BGM), where she developed, created and produced several shows. BGM was ultimately sold to Kew Media, and later became part of Sphere (then Datsit Sphere) when Kew went into administration over six years ago. She left Sphere in July last year, at which point she began work on her new venture. “As M Media officially launches, the greenlight for Ground Control marks a deeply personal and professional turning point,” said Miazga. “After this period of reflection and planning, I’ve built the foundations of a company rooted in resilience, creativity, and ethical storytelling. “We know how to make great shows, that has been proven countless times. The secret now is how to make them whilst experimenting, learning, adapting and remaining open, curious and kind. I’m now ready to tell the most important story of my life and to bring other stories that matter to audiences worldwide.’” Lionsgate Inks Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Tributes, Career Gallery & Obituary For Music, Humanitarian Icon Ryan Gosling And WB Eye Live-Acton ‘Flintstones’ Pic About Bamm-Bamm ‘Bel-Air’ Spinoff ‘Hilary’ Starring Coco Jones In Works At Peacock Read More About: Comments

articles.title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Stars Juno Temple & Hannah Waddingham Detail Firework Scene They Were “Chomping At The Bit “ To Do In Season 4
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Dolly Parton: Beyoncé, Pedro Pascal, Sabrina Carpenter & More Pay Tribute To “One Of One” Country Music Legend HBO Sets ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Premiere Date; Unveils Teaser Everything We Know About Amazon MGM & Sony Pictures TV’s ‘God Of War’ Adaptation So Far View All August 26, 2026 12:01am L-R: Juno Temple and Rebecca Waddingham in ' Ted Lasso' Season 4 Apple TV SPOILER ALERT: This post spoils Ted Lasso Season 4 Episode 4 , titled “Greyhounds’ Day Off.” Getting a women’s soccer team off the ground takes its challenges, which Keeley Jones ( Juno Temple ) and Rebecca Welton ( Hannah Waddingham ) have begun to realize four episodes into the fourth season of Ted Lasso . From the “Higgins Report” disclosing some devastating numbers and probabilities about whether the team could profit to their different mindsets of going about business, the pair have clashed over decisions. Rebecca has had to say no to many a Keeley pitch, and Keeley has, in turn, had to get creative. Related Stories News All The Songs In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 So Far News Meet The Lady Greyhounds: Key Players & Staff For AFC Richmond’s Women’s Team In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 In Episode 4, Keeley’s eagnerness is on full display when she and Rebecca witness Zelda Southport (Tracy Ullman) speak at a conference. Rebecca’s desire to remain demure and not show their cards wins out, and she ends up googling Zelda and finding some red flag results. Rebecca accidentally calls Keeley “naïve” after the publicist and burgeoning businesswoman wants to enlist Zelda in their mission of getting the women’s team more funding and attention, but the pair make up in the Nelson Road stadium seats one night. Watch on Deadline “We were chomping at the bit to go into that scene, weren’t we?” Waddingham said of the reconciliation between the female friends. “Totally. It’s so interesting when I think about that now. We didn’t even have to talk about what it was. We just had to run our lines together” Temple added. “Which is such an interesting and a beautiful thing to be able to say.” Complete with pink fuzzy blankets and thermos mugs, Rebecca apologizes and voices how she feels bad that she has to shut down many of Keeley’s ideas, but Keeley takes it in stride and says it’s okay, embracing the way it makes her think of another way to “get things done.” @deadline #JunoTemple on the transformation of Keeley’s style throughout #TedLasso ♬ original sound – Deadline “We played it, and then we had to go back over it because it was Diwali when we were shooting it, and so we were really shut down by the fireworks,” Waddingham continued, with Temple chiming in that they “weren’t supposed to actually pay attention to” the pyrotechnics. The distracting Diwali fireworks distracted led to reshoots of the pivotal moment. “You were guilty of this too. I won’t let that slide,” Temple said in response to her costar. “I kept being distracted because I’m like Keeley. I like anything that glitters, that’s sparkly, and I kept looking at them, then being like, “Oh my god, they’re not supposed to be there.’” In the show, Keeley has also tasked Kenneth the Bus Driver (Mark Kempner), who sources drugs and now, fireworks, apparently, to test out different hues of the colorful smoke that is popularly used opening women’s soccer games. The explosions provide different interruptions, punctuating the moment as one of Keeley’s ideas plays out in real time.

articles.title: ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Lionsgate Strikes Promotional Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows View All August 26, 2026 12:08am Rahasia Kelam Kakak Tiriku Vidio ReelShort has struck a deal with Indonesian streaming platform Vidio to bring hundreds of microdramas to local audiences, as well as co-produce new short dramas with Indonesian production houses. ReelShort catalogue titles will be available on Vidio starting on September 1 through the dedicated Short Drama tab, launched by Vidio last year, for subscribers on the TV Extra, Platinum, Platinum Extra, and Ultimate packages. The initial offering will include more than 200 titles across popular genres including romance, billionaire romance, fantasy and family drama, with a wide selection of titles available with Indonesian dubbing and subtitles. Related Stories News International Insider: Australia's Attention Battle; Vertical Video Rises; Kevin Macdonald On Pep Guardiola News FlareFlow & Europe's Shorts Strike Four-Title Microdrama Pact In addition, a “sizable” slate of short drama series co-produced with Indonesian production houses will be made available across both platforms. In a statement, Vidio said the collaboration “creates opportunities for Indonesian creative talent to gain production expertise and knowledge from ReelShort’s global short-drama experience”. Watch on Deadline The partnership, brokered by AR Global Media Network, is ReelShort’s first in Indonesia and is part of a wider expansion across Southeast Asia that has also included strategic partnerships with AIS in Thailand and Globe in the Philippines. According to recent data from Media Partners Asia (MPA), ReelShort currently leads the short-form drama market with an estimated 29% global market revenue share. In Q2 2026, Vidio reached 5.8 million paid subscribers across Southeast Asia, ranking third regionally. MPA data also shows that Indonesia has emerged as Asia-Pacific’s largest market for short-form drama consumption, accounting for 39% of the region’s total audience. Sutanto Hartono, CEO of Vidio, said: “Vidio continues to evolve alongside the changing ways Indonesians consume entertainment. As audiences increasingly look for content that fits seamlessly into their daily lives, we want to ensure they can find every type of entertainment they love on a single platform, from live sports, local originals, global entertainment to now, the rapidly growing format of short dramas. “Our partnership with ReelShort not only responds to this emerging audience demand but also strengthens Vidio’s position as Indonesia’s most comprehensive entertainment platform, offering more choice, greater convenience, and an even richer viewing experience for our subscribers.” Joey Jia, Founder and CEO of Crazy Maple Studio, owner of ReelShort, said: “Our partnership with Vidio marks a significant milestone in ReelShort’s Southeast Asia growth strategy and reflects a fundamental shift in how audiences are consuming entertainment. “Indonesia is one of the region’s most dynamic entertainment markets. We see tremendous potential not only to expand access to our global catalogue, but also to create original stories for Indonesian audiences. Through our planned local productions with Vidio and Indonesian production partners, we look forward to combining ReelShort’s global experience in developing high-performing short-drama IP with local creative talent to build stories and franchises that resonate locally while reaching audiences across the region and beyond.” Lionsgate Inks Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Tributes, Career Gallery & Obituary For Music, Humanitarian Icon Ryan Gosling And WB Eye Live-Acton ‘Flintstones’ Pic About Bamm-Bamm ‘Bel-Air’ Spinoff ‘Hilary’ Starring Coco Jones In Works At Peacock Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Ted Hodgkinson To Leave Southbank Centre & Join Hay Festival As Creative Director
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Ted Hodgkinson To Leave Southbank Centre & Join Hay Festival As Creative Director Janus Films & Criterion Acquire Paul Thomas Anderson’s Cameron Winter Concert Film Oscars: Belgium Selects Lukas Dhont’s ‘Coward’ For International Feature Film Race View All August 26, 2026 1:07am Ted Hodgkinson Photo credit: Pete Woodhead. Ted Hodgkinson, the Southbank Centre ’s longtime director of literature and spoken word, is leaving the London institution to join Hay Festival in the newly created role of creative director. Hodgkinson will officially join the Hay Festival team in the autumn. In the new role, Hodgkinson will be responsible for leading the event’s artistic and creative strategy and public programming. He joins Hay’s executive team, led by Chief Executive Julie Finch. The wider executive team also includes International Director and co-Deputy CEO, Cristina Fuentes La Roche; Executive Producer and co-Deputy CEO, Adrian Lambert; Director of Communications and External Affairs, Christopher Bone; Finance Director Amanda Cartwright; Production Director Georgie Cooke; and Commercial Director Penny Compton. Related Stories News Hay Literary Festival: Jesse Armstrong Among Headliners Of Inaugural Cinema Lineup, Screening Programme Includes 'Dahomey', 'Priscilla' & 'The Worst Person In The World' News Mubi To Launch Screening Series At Hay Literary Festival “We’re delighted to welcome Ted Hodgkinson to Hay Festival Global as our new Creative Director,” Finch said in a statement. “Ted joins us at a pivotal moment, as we build towards our 40th anniversary in 2027 and respond to growing demand for Hay Festival platforms in the UK and around the world.” Watch on Deadline Discussing his new role, Hodgkinson said he aims to build on the event’s “exceptionally strong foundations while being bold and ambitious in reimagining the programme for audiences in Hay-on-Wye and around the world, fired by the belief that its brightest years are still ahead.” Across his decades-long tenure at the Southbank, Hodgkinson programmed more than 3,000 events, including the now-buzzy London Literature Festival, and expanded the Southbank’s cultural relevance with ambitious programming that mixed the institution’s classical literature programming with contemporary flourishes, like the partnership with Dua Lipa’s Service95 Book Club. He is an Honorary Fellow of the Royal Society of Literature and a Fellow of the Royal Society of Arts (FRSA). He also serves as a trustee of English PEN, New Writing North and The Arts Foundation. articles.title: Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Lionsgate Strikes Promotional Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows View All August 26, 2026 1:18am Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) Busan International Film Festival Major tech companies including Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Kling AI and Alibaba Group have signed up to participate in the InnoAsia program of this year’s Asian Contents & Film Market ( ACFM ). The official market of Busan International Film Festival, ACFM says it is expanding its scope around the vision of “an innovative ecosystem in which cinema and technology co-evolve.” InnoAsia aims to connect storytelling with emerging technologies, including AI and the rapidly growing microdrama ecosystem. As part of this, ACFM is partnering with global marketing and advertising agency Innocean to co-host the ‘Cinema by Brand 2026’ competition, with the Producers Guild of Korea (PGK) responsible for the selection process and production supervision. Related Stories News YouTube Ad Revenue Rises 13% In Q2 To Surpass $11 Billion, Boosting Parent Alphabet's Performance News A24 Defends Google AI Partnership, Studio Doesn't "Necessarily Love" GenAI Content But "We'd Rather Have A Seat At The Table" Cinema by Brand is described as “an innovative investment and production support platform that connects client brands with film creators worldwide to develop and produce new film content.” Watch on Deadline This year, the competition is seeking 20-minute short film projects featuring Hanwha Group’s ‘Space Solar Power’. The first-round selections will be announced in early September, followed by final pitching in late September, with final selections announced during ACFM. Each selected project will receive production funding, and the selected projects will then be produced and presented to audiences in Korea and worldwide. A session during the market will also explore the significance and potential of branded content in the content business. Meanwhile, in addition to Google, Kling AI and Alibaba, other AI-driven tech companies attending InnoAsia will include BytePlus, Netflix’s VFX studio Eyeline Studios, MegazoneCloud, OPIM Digital, the Korean Film Archive’s VFX asset trading platform i.AM, and InShorts. AI-driven content production companies joining the program include France-based AI/XR content studio Atlas V, Korea’s Mateo AI Studio, MBC C&I, Climax Studio, For Entertainment, K-Dragon and MooAm. Microdrama platforms Mango TV, FlickReels and Vigloo have also confirmed their participation. Kling AI will co-host ‘New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI’ and ‘Kling AI Networking Reception: From Production Needs Across Asia to Industry Partnerships’ with ACFM. AWS and MegazoneCloud will launch the ‘AWS Awards’, linked to startup pitching. Winning companies will be selected following a PoC (proof of concept) process and receive AWS cloud vouchers. InnoAsia will also continue its partnerships with international markets, including Berlin film festival’s European Film Market (EFM). Lux AI, an EFM-participating startup developing an intelligent lighting solution for virtual production, and Tanja Meissner, Director Berlinale Pro and EFM, are set to visit Busan. Through collaboration with TAICCA School under the Taiwan Creative Content Agency, imCore, a startup developing an AI solution to improve VFX production efficiency, will also participate. ACFM and InnoAsia 2026 are taking place October 10-13 at the BEXO exhibition centre, during Busan International Film Festival, which is running October 6-15. articles.title: Oscars: Japan Selects Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s ‘All Of A Sudden’ For International Feature Film Race

The Japanese-French-language drama premiered to an 11-minute standing ovation at Cannes and went on to win a Best Actress prize for both of its stars, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto. Set in France and Japan, All of a Sudden follows Marie-Lou (Efira), the director of a care facility for the elderly, who is determined to introduce an innovative philosophy of care rooted in listening and respect for residents’ dignity, despite resistance from members of her staff. Her path is profoundly reshaped by an encounter with Mari (Okamoto), a Japanese theater director battling cancer. As the two women form a deep friendship, they join forces in a shared struggle to make the impossible possible. articles.title: Brenda Song Loves the Los Angeles Rams So Much She Ended Up in a Broadcast Booth at SoFi Stadium
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All August 24, 2026 3:49pm Macaulay Culkin and Brenda Song pose inside SoFi Stadium as the Los Angeles Rams played a pre-season game against the New Orleans Saints on Aug. 22, 2026. Credit: Los Angeles Rams A dream came true for Brenda Song on Saturday inside SoFi Stadium. The veteran star is such a diehard Los Angeles Rams fan that the team not only invited Song (and longtime partner Macaulay Culkin ) to a preseason matchup with the New Orleans Saints, they welcomed her into a broadcast booth to offer color commentary on CBS L.A. Song happened to be on the air during the third quarter for one of the game’s most thrilling moments when Alex Cook returned an interception 100 yards to the end zone as the Rams dropped an exclamation point on the Saints with a 34-0 victory. Related Stories Movies 'Brady vs. Manning': Documentary Film in the Works About NFL Rivalry (Exclusive) Movies 'Madden' Biopic Sets Fall Release Date, With Nicolas Cage Teasing Role as "Highlight for Me" It was a coup for Song, who is as passionate about defense as she is rattling off the names and stats of some of favorite players. Even those in her inner circle are surprised by how knowledgeable and passionate she is about the hometown team. “For our opening game last season against the Colts, I actually brought Dave Stassen and Scott MacArthur, our showrunner and one of the stars of Running Point, and they said they saw a different side of me from the opening kick-off,'” Song told The Hollywood Reporter immediately after Saturday’s game. “They said, ‘You were a different person. You didn’t speak to us. You were on the edge of your seat from the first play.’ I said, ‘Yes because every play matters. Every inch matters. There’s no other game like it.’ That’s why I love it so much.” The team loves her back. “Brenda is one of our most loved and invested fans,” said Rams chief marketing officer Kathryn Kai-ling Frederick. “Between her deep knowledge of the game, her on-camera presence and the enthusiasm she brings to everything she does, we knew she would add a fresh perspective and fun energy to the broadcast.” THR got to quiz Song on the the roots of that love, her predictions for the coming season and why she and Culkin regularly decline VIP suites in favor of sitting in the stands. Brenda Song, we are sitting in a golf cart in the bowels of SoFi Stadium moments after you made your broadcast debut. How did that feel? I’m on a high. I’m not joking when I say it was my dream. I grew up loving sports but I’m 5’2” — my feet barely touch the ground when I’m sitting in a chair — so I just love watching from the sidelines as a couch analyst. I’m just so grateful to the Ramily for letting me go up there and live out my dream and call the game. Sitting next to Rob Havenstein, an incredible right tackle, was insane. Viewers got to hear how passionate you are about defense, which I think people might be surprised by because offense is always seen as such a sexy part of the sport. Why defense? I’ve always loved defense. Before Kobe Bryant was in the league, my parents, my dad and my brother always watched the Chicago Bulls. Dennis Rodman was my favorite player. Watching defense is so fun because the smallest hand movement or slide can create such a big moment. When I started watching football, I got to see Aaron Donald play — Aaron Donald is my GOAT, the GOAT — and seeing him do the chop to get around someone was incredible. Yes, offense is sexy and sparkly but I love a shutdown defense. When I’m watching a game, I really enjoy when our defense is out there because there’s something spectacular about it, especially when you’re playing a team known for its offense and you can just shut them down. It’s amazing. Don’t get me wrong, I love watching [Matthew Stafford], [Puka Nacua] and our receivers — they’re amazing. But our defense is really special, and I’m very, very excited to see Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson play this season. You’ve said in multiple interviews that your dream was also to be a defensive coordinator … Yes, truly. As a defensive coordinator, you’re watching the offense line up at the line of scrimmage it’s your job to say, “What can I do to stop this?” You have to be three steps ahead to spoil someone’s fun. I love watching a game at the stadium because you get to see a lot of plays off the ball. One of my favorite things is watching the defensive coordinator swap out players and put people in if it’s a run play versus passing. I won’t say which game this was because it still hurts, but we’ve watched games when we’re giving our A-guys a break and other teams take advantage of that. They see the weak spots. There’s so much more to football than a crazy 60-yard throw and a fun touchdown. I love defense so much. I could talk about it all day. It’s my favorite thing. Song with Rob Havenstein inside SoFi Stadium on Aug. 22, 2026. Credit: Los Angeles Rams You mentioned Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson. Who else on the roster are you excited about? When you have a shutdown corner like Trent, you can’t help but be excited, because you look at the numbers and realize that no one is even throwing in his direction. He’s also so versatile. Of course how could you not be excited about Myles Garrett, the reigning defensive player of the year? He’s the only person aside from Aaron Donald that would make you say, “I don’t want to line up across from him.” And he’s now a Ram! I feel so very lucky to have a Hall of Famer on our team. I feel very spoiled. What’s the history of your Rams fandom? It all started because I’m a huge Lakers fan. I grew up watching basketball and the Chicago Bulls, but when Kobe got traded to the Lakers in 1996, I became a Kobe fan. I can genuinely say that I’ve seen almost every game Kobe Bryant ever played. When he retired in 2016, I couldn’t watch basketball anymore. It was too devastating. Kobe Bryant was basketball to me, so I took a break from sports. Then when I started dating Mac — we were about a year into dating — I came out to the living room one Sunday morning and he was watching a Rams-Seahawks game during the Russell Wilson days. I jokingly said, “Let’s football.” He started walking me through the downs and explaining things to me. We’d watched the Super Bowl but L.A. hadn’t had a staple team. Once he started explaining it all to me, I became obsessed. Very fortunately, we also went to the Super Bowl that year. Song with Rob Havenstein. Credit: Los Angeles Rams When they played the Patriots? Yeah, that was in 2019, after the 2018 season. I was locked in. I kept asking myself, “How have I spent so many years not watching football?” Now, anytime between August and February, you won’t find me doing anything on Sundays, Mondays or Thursdays aside from reading books. We literally have a TV just for sports. We have two young boys, and when they’re home, they get the big TV. But on Sundays, Mondays and Thursdays … That’s where Mom and Dad are? Yes. It’s nice that you can do this as a couple, and get so into it. I mean, he’s wearing a Rams jersey with Culkin on the back. A thousand percent. We come here a lot. I like being in the stands with the fans because I come here to watch a game. I love meeting everyone, but I’m here to watch the game. Mac knows we are only talking ball for the whole time that we’re here. I’ve been able to reconnect with a lot of people that I haven’t seen in a long time just because of the games. Dylan Sprouse texted me that he saw me on the big screen. It’s also been really fun to bring friends to games and show them my love. This is my passion. Culkin and Song in SoFi Stadium as the Rams played a pre-season matchup with the Saints on Saturday. Credit: Los Angeles Rams It’s also nice that it’s so organic and the fans have really responded to you becoming so invested. I was just saying to Mac as we were driving here that I couldn’t believe I was getting to sit in the booth and do color. I truly am just a huge fan. Anytime they ask me to come, I’m in. “Just tickets, please, I’ll sit anywhere.” There’s no bad seat in SoFi, so I’ll sit anywhere. I’ll be anywhere. It feels really surreal because I genuinely love this game so much. Mac will tell you, the only time I ever really get starstruck is when I’m around these players. It’s nice to see you both lean into the attention in a way as well because I know you’re pretty private about your lives. To be honest, it’s just really organic. We show up at places that we love. We love sports, so we want to come and watch a game. We want to enjoy these things, and we don’t want anything to hold us back. We love our lives, and we’re so proud of the life that we’ve built. One of the things that I love so much about our relationship is that he is the first significant other in my life who has allowed me to truly be me. People always ask, “What is one of the first things you connected on?” It wasn’t about us being child actors. It was sports. I never would have thought Macaulay Culkin liked sports, and I don’t think he ever thought I would like sports. But once we started talking, we both realized how important it was to one another. Then we started testing each other about how much the other knew. Even today, we were talking about Ty Simpson’s last game and I said he went 21 of 25 but Mac said, “No, he was 22 of 24.” He looked it up, and I was like, “Why would you even question me?” That’s what we were kind of doing when we first met, but about basketball. We realized that we had so much in common, and sports was a huge part of that. We love football, we love basketball, we love boxing. These are things that I feel like I never got to really enjoy with a significant other. I don’t want to speak for him, obviously, but it’s something that we very much enjoy. And it’s important for our relationship to find things outside of work and family that we like to do together. For us, it’s coming to Rams games, which is an absolute buzz. I feel really proud that even though he’s a native New Yorker, he always says the Rams are our team. Now he roots harder for the Rams than any other team. Let’s talk about your career for a second. Running Point has been renewed for a third season, and you’re continuing to show a diversity of performances from TV to film, like with the recent The Last Showgirl. I read how you were apprehensive about fans seeing that performance with you swearing up a storm, but it landed really well for you. How are you feeling about these last couple of years? I’m always waiting for the other shoe to drop. I feel so incredibly grateful. Truly, I have been doing this since I was 3 years old, and I must be a crazy person because I love it so much. And I still love it so much. I’m always just so grateful that I get to wake up every day and do the thing that I’ve dreamed of doing my entire life with people who I love, respect and admire, and want to continuously work with. There was a shift after having two kids. It was really hard, and I was such a different person in the way that I looked at my career. My priorities were so different. It was really scary because it felt unknown for the first time. Instead of being scared of that, I tried to embrace it by realizing that I was in a new phase of my life, and I was ready. I feel like a big ball of clay, and I’m scared in the best way possible. We’re about to start filming season 3 of Running Point , and it’s like my family there. I love showing up to set every single day. We’re making a show that we’re so proud of and having the best time doing it. I just wrapped a Netflix film [ The Fifth Wheel ] with Nikki Glaser, Fortune Feimster and Kim Kardashian, directed by Eva Longoria and written by Paula Pell and Janine Brito. We had the best time making it. I just feel so lucky that I continuously get to work with people I love so much, doing something that I’ve always wanted to do. I wake up every day like, “Is this real life?” I think about that all the time. I feel really grateful, and I hope that I just continuously move in the right direction and challenge myself. Song, Kate Hudson and Mindy Kaling at the second season premiere of Running Point in Los Angeles. Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for Netflix Back to the Rams. Expectations are sky-high for next season. What are your predictions? The best thing that can happen is that we have confetti blowing everywhere on Valentine’s Day here at SoFi. We’ll have the best off season next year because we’ll be celebrating for months. That is my expectation, and also my prediction is that we’ll be celebrating with #99 on the field with us. We can continue this conversation. I’m going to meet you in this golf cart here at SoFi. Let’s do it. THR

articles.title: Guillermo del Toro, James Gunn Join Crunchyroll’s Inaugural Anime Future Forum

Courtesy of Crunchyroll Crunchyroll has lined up Guillermo del Toro, James Gunn and senior executives from some of Japan’s biggest anime and manga companies for the inaugural Crunchyroll Anime Future Forum, an invitation-only industry summit set for Oct. 7 in New York. The first slate of speakers includes MAPPA president and CEO Manabu Otsuka; Toho executive officer Taichi Ueda; Shueisha’s Yuta Momiyama, an editor-in-chief overseeing the digital side of Shonen Jump+; and Sony Music Entertainment Japan president Atsuhiro Iwakami, who is also chairman of Aniplex. In the anime world, these are some of the true heavy-hitters. Related Stories Business Trump Trade War With Canada Puts Film, TV Spending Rules in Crosshairs Movies Saoirse Ronan Is "Dead Serious" About Playing a James Bond Villain Sony Pictures Animation president Kristine Belson will also moderate a panel with Bob Persichetti and Justin K. Thompson, the directors of the upcoming Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse . Olympic gold medalist figure skater Amber Glenn, rapper and author Big Sean and content creator Jordan Howlett will also participate in the forum from a fan perspective. The one-day event, themed “Designing for Anime’s Future,” will organize discussions around fandom, technology, storytelling and intellectual property protection. Planned sessions include conversations on transmedia storytelling across anime, gaming and live action; the changing theatrical experience; the future of manga; and the role of influencers in expanding anime fandom. Sony Group president and CEO Hiroki Totoki will deliver opening remarks, Sony Pictures Entertainment chairman and CEO Ravi Ahuja will speak during the day and Crunchyroll president Rahul Purini will close the forum with remarks and news. Sony first announced plans for the forum in May, describing anime as an important growth sector for the company and the event as a way to deepen ties with Japanese publishers and creators while bringing them together with partners from other industries. At the same corporate strategy briefing, Sony said Crunchyroll had surpassed 21 million paid subscribers worldwide as of the end of March. Crunchyroll says more than 400 industry figures will attend the forum, which will be held at the Jacob K. Javits Convention Center on Wednesday, Oct. 7, before New York Comic Con begins at the same venue. NYCC runs Oct. 8-11. THR

articles.title: Taylor Swift on Dealing With Public Perception and Deciding Not to Opt Out Before Her Career “Got Unmanageably Big”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All August 24, 2026 5:30pm Taylor Swift attends the Songwriters Hall of Fame 55th annual Induction and Awards Gala on June 11 in New York City. Jamie McCarthy/Getty Images After a very busy summer that included being inducted into the Songwriters Hall of Fame , releasing an original song for Toy Story 5 and, of course, getting married , Taylor Swift made a stop at the Grammy Museum in Los Angeles for a wide-ranging conversation about her career. “The Icon Sessions with Taylor Swift: A 20-Year Retrospective” event, presented by the Recording Academy ‘s Songwriters & Composers Wing, took place earlier this month and was released online on Monday, featuring Swift sitting down with Recording Academy CEO Harvey Mason Jr. Related Stories Music Meet Tuide, Your New Favorite Girl Group (Exclusive) Music Madonna Tops U.K. Dance Charts a Record Fifth Time in 15 Weeks Early on in the chat, Mason Jr. asked the superstar how she learned to trust her instincts when sharing her music with the public, as Swift explained, “I’m making music because I’m playing for the fans. I’m putting this out for people who care about it and who look to music as a way to cope with their life in the way that I did; I think that if you can actually go through all those checkpoints, you realize that putting out music you’ve made that you love so much is not the path to universal validation. If you’re still doing it, then you love it for the right reasons.” She added that dealing with the public perception and analysis of her lyrics “sometimes fuels [her songwriting]. Sometimes when people are mocking me, it’s really fun to mock them back. Sometimes I like to just use words that they have to look up in order to talk shit about.” Swift also acknowledged that she has several “coping mechanisms” that she’s used throughout the years, and “one of them is saying, ‘You chose this. You chose this every day. You could have opted out of this any day before it got unmanageably big,’ and I decided not to because I love it that much. And that’s just where it begins and where it ends. Everything that comes with this ultimately is worth it, as long as I get to still make music.” The discussion touched on a number of her albums, including her Reputation era, which she described as “a time in my life when — for the very first time, not the last — people had really actively tried to misunderstand me, just in general, and to misunderstand what I was trying to say and to purposely misinterpret it.” Reflecting now on the 2017 album, Swift said, “I’m very proud of it when I look back on it. I think the things that I look back on now is when I’ve gone through something that was sort of an attempt to drive me insane — when you when you don’t allow that to happen, and you use art and music as a way to like barrel roll out of that, those are the moments I’m the most proud of.” Elsewhere in the conversation, Swift explained how she’s “not a big mood board artist” and usually decides on the aesthetics of an album as the last piece. She explained that she identifies as a “confessional songwriter,” but “I think it’s important to specify that not all shocking revelations you make about yourself are deep. Like just saying something dramatic, shocking and wild doesn’t make it something that’s going to help people, resonate with people, be an important story that sits in people’s minds, hearts and souls.” “We have to be purposeful. You can’t just like scream something crazy and be like, ‘I’m a confessional songwriter,'” she continued. “Just for the same exact reason why details should not be strictly decorative. Like let’s not be haphazard with these things, let’s make them count.” Swift also touched on the process of her Taylor’s Version album re-records, saying, “At first, it’s like when the dog actually did eat your homework, and you’re like, ‘Now I have to redo it all?’ And then I have to go in to the teacher and be like, ‘The dog ate my homework.’ The public and the media — since it hadn’t really been done before in that way and I guess on like such a big scale and so loudly and obnoxiously — the public kind of did a little bit side-eye me the way that a teacher would if you did say the dog had eaten your homework. That was an interesting place to start from and I had to sort of get myself from the place of being like everyone says this isn’t going to work and everyone’s saying like nobody’s gonna want to hear my new take on the same work.” In closing, Swift gave an acknowledgement to her early days as a country star, noting, “I love my country roots more and more the further along this path I get. I want to honor them more and more, and I feel more and more tied and more loyal to them, the people that shaped who I am as an artist and as a writer. That all happened in Nashville.” She finished with some advice to young songwriters in the audience, telling them, “I hope that you will show up to work even when the idea fairy doesn’t. I hope that you will not be the person who shoots down everyone’s ideas in the room, but has not brought any of your own. I hope that you will remember the ‘yes, and’ of the improv session that is your recording sessions and that is life as well. And I hope you remember that in the music industry, as wild and ever-changing as it is, enthusiasm can protect you from anything. I would know.” THR

articles.title: Hulu Cancels ‘Not Suitable for Work’ After One Season

The comedy series, which premiered in June and ran for nine episodes, starred Ella Hunt (AJ), Avantika Vandanapu (Abby), Will Angus (Davis), Jack Martin (Josh), Nicholas Duvernay (Kel) and Jay Ellis (Bill). It centered on “five work-obsessed 20-somethings striving for professional success and, if they have time, personal happiness in Manhattan’s most glamorous neighborhood, Murray Hill,” per the show’s logline. Related Stories TV 'The Girls': Khloé Kardashian Wanted Her Friends to Have Their Own Show. Then Things Got Complicated TV 'The Drop' Trailer Sees 'Snowfall' Characters Go After "New Gold Rush" of West Coast Rap Warner Bros. Television, which produced Not Suitable for Work , plans to shop the show around for a potential new home. As for Hunt, after getting the role of AJ, she told THR , “Being part of the Mindy-verse was exciting to me.” When Duvernay, who scored the role of Kel, first read the pilot, he “thought it was hilarious and refreshing” because “a lot of the comedies put out nowadays are so angled at Gen Z to the point where it’s like scrolling on Instagram.” “It has that vintage … not to make the comparison, but from the jump, it’s always had a bit of a Friends vibe,” he added during a previous interview with THR . “That’s a giant to compare it to, but that’s initially how I felt being part of it. articles.title: Foo Fighters Rock Hollywood Bowl Debut as Gustavo Dudamel Says Goodbye to L.A. Philharmonic
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All August 24, 2026 9:42pm Gustavo Dudamel (standing, left) and Foo Fighters singer Dave Grohl (center) at the Hollywood Bowl. Courtesy of L.A. Phil Dave Grohl appeared unsure whether anything could ever be this good again as he took the stage for a unique Foo Fighters concert at the Hollywood Bowl on Saturday. Not only did the musician and his Grammy Award-winning band perform at the storied venue for the first time ever, but they did so with accompaniment from the Los Angeles Philharmonic. Leading the full orchestra was departing conductor Gustavo Dudamel , who celebrated his farewell weekend with the L.A. Phil at the Bowl before his tenure as music and artistic director of the New York Philharmonic begins next month. Related Stories Music Taylor Swift on Dealing With Public Perception and Deciding Not to Opt Out Before Her Career "Got Unmanageably Big" Music Meet Tuide, Your New Favorite Girl Group (Exclusive) “Tonight, we’re going to play as many things as we can before we have to stop,” Grohl told the crowd during the 15-song set. “We usually play for three hours a night, but tonight, we picked the best songs that we can perform with our friends in the L.A. Phil and Mr. Gustavo Dudamel. Some of these you may have never heard before, so sit back and enjoy.” Indeed, the rock band dusted off some deep cuts to go along with staple singles “Times Like These,” “All My Life,” “The Pretender,” “My Hero” and “Best of You.” Also included within the set were such tunes as “Razor,” which the band had not performed live since 2006, and “Home,” which they last played in 2007. Gustavo Dudamel (third from left) joins the Foo Fighters at the end of their Hollywood Bowl performance. Courtesy of L.A. Phil “Gustavo, how you doing?” Grohl asked at one point of Dudamel, who has led the L.A. Phil since 2009. The former Nirvana drummer went on to quip about the orchestra and choir, “So I figure we just get 14 more buses and take them on tour for the rest of our lives. Good plan?” As he has done lately, Grohl dedicated the performance of “Aurora” to late drummer Taylor Hawkins , who died in 2022 at age 50 . “He would have loved this,” Grohl said with a fond laugh about his longtime friend and collaborator. View this post on Instagram Foo Fighters, who are currently on tour in support of recent album Your Favorite Toy , ended the night with their standard closing song and signature hit “Everlong.” This particular rendition included a fireworks show. “I wish that we could do this every fucking night for the rest of our lives with all of these amazing people,” Grohl said ahead of the final song. “What an honor to be invited to this hallowed ground, this special place, to be able to give Gustavo one more big rock show before he has to leave this wonderful city. And then to share this experience with all of you guys, it’s so amazing.” THR

articles.title: Dominic Monaghan to Join ‘Lord of the Rings’ 25th Anniversary Reunion With Elijah Wood, More at CCXP

Courtesy of Everett Collection Frodo and Merry are plotting new adventures to honor the 25th anniversary of the Lord of the Rings film franchise. Dominic Monaghan is the second confirmed guest for the forthcoming CCXP26 fan event that takes place later this year in São Paulo, Brazil , following the previous announcement that Elijah Wood , aka Frodo Baggins himself, will attend. With the theme of “Fellowship Forever,” this year’s CCXP is held Dec. 3-6, and its full lineup will be announced soon. Monaghan made his feature acting debut as Meriadoc “Merry” Brandybuck in The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring , which was released in theaters Dec. 19, 2001, and also starred Ian McKellen, Liv Tyler, Viggo Mortensen, Sean Astin, Cate Blanchett and Orlando Bloom. Based on the writing of J.R.R. Tolkien, the New Line movie was the first in director Peter Jackson ‘s trilogy that collectively surpassed $2.9 billion at the global box office and scored 17 Oscars. Related Stories Business Guillermo del Toro, James Gunn Join Crunchyroll's Inaugural Anime Future Forum Business Trump Trade War With Canada Puts Film, TV Spending Rules in Crosshairs “CCXP has a tradition of bringing together the iconic names who have shaped pop culture history, and Fellowship Forever is the celebration that The Lord of the Rings fans truly deserved. Having Merry alongside Frodo on the CCXP26 stage is one of those moments that captures the very essence of the festival — epic, in the most literal sense of the word,” says CCXP vp of content Roberto Fabri. Monaghan returns to CCXP after attending last year’s edition, where he participated in panels and met with fans for autographs and photos. The British actor is also known for playing Charlie on Lost , along with his roles in the Star Wars and X-Men franchises. Last year’s CCXP included a viral moment when Timothée Chalamet showed off his dance moves to “Crank That (Soulja Boy)” while promoting his film Marty Supreme . Other notable presentations in 2025 included a Supernatural reunion ; conversations with such stars as Kathryn Newton, Selton Mello and Game of Thrones standout Tom Wlaschiha; and panels for projects like It: Welcome to Derry , The Boys , A Knight of the Seven Kingdoms , Anaconda , The Secret Agent and Percy Jackson and the Olympians . articles.title: Meet Mestiza, the Female Duo From Spain Mixing Flamenco and Electronic Music
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 25, 2026 12:01am Mestiza Courtesy of Mestiza Spanish DJs Belah Sánchez and Patricia “Pitty” Bernad had their own careers. But in 2021, they teamed up under the moniker Mestiza . Since then, the Spanish DJ and producer duo has been finding a growing fan base with its combination of electronic music with flamenco influences. “We are the culture of flamenco mixed with the hypnotic energy of electronic music, creating a bridge between the ancestral and the futuristic,” their website says. In December 2023, Mestiza released the debut album Quëreles via their independent label Sacro Music, which also reimagined flamenco traditions through a club lens. In 2025, Mestiza became the first female DJ duo to get a residency at the Hï Ibiza club on the Spanish island known as a destination for electronic music lovers. Related Stories Movies Dominic Monaghan to Join 'Lord of the Rings' 25th Anniversary Reunion With Elijah Wood, More at CCXP Business Guillermo del Toro, James Gunn Join Crunchyroll's Inaugural Anime Future Forum After playing Coachella earlier this year, this fall, the women behind Mestiza are bringing their high-energy act, as part of its Sacro event series, to New York, where they will rock the Brooklyn outdoor venue Creekside – Under The K Bridge, and London, where the duo will bring its sounds to the legendary Roundhouse in Camden on Oct. 30. THR , in an email Q&A, asked Mestiza about the duo’s history, music and aesthetics, their respect for flamenco, which comes from Andalusia in southern Spain, and what’s next for them, including a possible cinema project. How and when did you two decide to become a duo rather than continuing your solo work? PATRICIA “PITTY” BERNAD Before Mestiza, we had both been DJing individually for around 15 years, so we each had our own careers, experiences and musical identities. When we started working together, we quickly realized there was something much more powerful in what we could create together. We shared a similar vision of music, while bringing different personalities and influences to it. At some point, it stopped feeling like a collaboration and started feeling like a project with its own identity. That was really the beginning of Mestiza. Mestiza, courtesy of Jorge Foley Can you tell me why you chose the name Mestiza, which I hear means “mixed,” and what it symbolizes? And what does “Sacro” mean and why did you choose that name for your label and events? BELAH SÁNCHEZ Mestiza comes from the idea of mixture, which is really at the heart of everything we do. We bring together different worlds: electronic music and flamenco, tradition and modernity, our Spanish roots and a much more global sound. We liked that the name could represent all of that naturally. Sacro means “sacred” in Spanish. When we created it, we wanted it to feel like more than just another electronic music event. There is something almost ritualistic about people gathering around music, dancing together and sharing the same energy. Sacro was born from that idea and has gradually become its own universe. I love electronic music and have heard and enjoyed flamenco music. Why did you want to mix them? PITTY For us, it was never about mixing flamenco and electronic music simply because it was an interesting combination. Flamenco is part of the culture we grew up surrounded by, and electronic music is the language through which we express ourselves as artists. The interesting part for us is finding the point where those two worlds can coexist naturally. We have enormous respect for flamenco and everything it represents, so the intention has never been to disguise it or turn it into a trend. It is about taking elements from our roots and allowing them to have a conversation with contemporary electronic music. Maybe that is also why it can connect with people in completely different parts of the world, even if they haven’t grown up with flamenco. How excited are you for your upcoming London and New York performances and the venues you get to play at? BELAH We are incredibly excited about both shows. In London, we’ll be performing at the Roundhouse, the iconic venue in Camden where artists like Amy Winehouse, Adele and Lady Gaga have performed. Bringing Mestiza to a stage with so much history is very special for us. Mestiza, courtesy of Leshea Lewis In New York, we’ve played many times before, but this will be the first time we perform for such a large crowd at an outdoor venue, so it feels like a very important moment for us. What role do fashion and style play for Mestiza? It feels like you are an “experience” that goes beyond music? PITTY Fashion has always been another form of expression for us. We don’t really separate the music from the visual side of Mestiza – what we wear, the stage design, the lighting and the imagery are all part of the same identity. Music will always be at the center, but we love creating an entire world around it. How key is female representation and empowerment for you and your work? BELAH We are very proud of what we’ve achieved as two women in a scene that has historically been very male-dominated, but we also want our work to speak for itself. Femininity is an important part of our identity, and for us, empowerment means being ambitious, being in control of our project and embracing who we are. If that inspires other women to do the same, it’s something we’re very proud of. Mestiza at Coachella, courtesy of Mestiza Courtesy of Mestiza Your live shows have a reputation for being very visual. Why? And do you have any interest in making movies or series – or making music for them? PITTY We think very visually when we create. We’re inspired by cinema, fashion, architecture and Spanish iconography, so naturally those references become part of our shows. We both love cinema and the whole cinematic world. In fact, we’re currently involved in a project we can’t talk about yet, but there’s a possibility that Mestiza’s music might be making its way to the big screen very soon. Is there anything else you would like to share? BELAH Mestiza is still evolving. What started as a way of bringing our roots into electronic music has become a much bigger creative universe. We want to keep exploring that through our music, our shows and Sacro, while always staying connected to where we come from. We still feel there is so much we haven’t shown yet. THR

articles.title: Hilary Strong Steps Down as CEO of John Gore Studios
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 25, 2026 1:17am John Gore (L), Hilary Strong. John Gore Organization/Sean Gleason London-based film and TV studio John Gore Studios , which is behind the likes of the Toronto-bound Onwards and Sideways , with Laura Linney and Rhys Ifans starring as two people being diagnosed with Parkinson’s, said on Tuesday that Hilary Strong is stepping down as CEO and that it will reorganize. The firm will be “joining forces with its U.S.-based sister company, The John Gore Organization, under the common control of a single holding company,” it said. “This will facilitate coordination between the companies and will bring their respective film, television and theatrical businesses under a common strategic vision that will enable them to reach an even broader audience on screens and stages worldwide.” Each of the companies will be under the executive leadership of owner and founder Gore. Related Stories Music Meet Mestiza, the Female Duo From Spain Mixing Flamenco and Electronic Music Movies Dominic Monaghan to Join 'Lord of the Rings' 25th Anniversary Reunion With Elijah Wood, More at CCXP British-born Gore, a two-time Emmy and Olivier award winner, has served as executive chairman of John Gore Studios, with Strong, whose previous roles included chief at Agatha Christie Ltd. and commercial director at Hat Trick Productions, as CEO. Said Gore: “Hilary and the team took the business from zero to seven feature films in 18 months, which must be a record – all the while burnishing the legacy of Hammer Films and expanding into new technologies and complementary businesses to pave a path for the future. I am extremely grateful to Hilary for the significant role she has played in the launch of John Gore Studios and excited about this next chapter.” Strong served as an executive producer on each of the first six feature films developed during her tenure. “I have adored my time working with John and the wonderful team we have put together to create John Gore Studios, and I will always be grateful to John for the opportunity, but we have both agreed that, with the reshaping of the global business, my work here is done,” she said. THR

articles.title: Ridley Scott’s ‘The Dog Stars’: First Reactions
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 1:48am (L-R) Jacob Elordi as Hig and Josh Brolin as Bangley in 20th Century Studios' The Dog Stars. Fabio Lovino/20th Century Studios Ridley Scott is back! The visionary filmmaker’s latest feature The Dog Stars hits theaters globally on Aug. 28. and early social media reaction suggests the post-apocalyptic sci-fi film has plenty of Scott’s visual flair but feelings were mixed over the script. The Dog Stars held its world premiere in London on Aug. 20 and 20th Century Studios held a series of press screenings for the film over the last week. Attendees were allowed to post brief reactions on social media after screenings. Full critics reviews for the film are embargoed till Aug. 25. Related Stories Movies 'Possession' Remake With Callum Turner, Margaret Qualley Sets Summer 2027 Release Movies Danny Boyle's Rupert Murdoch Movie 'Ink' Sets December Theatrical Release From Netflix The feature has an all-star cast, including Jacob Elordi , Josh Brolin , Margaret Qualley , Alison Janney , Guy Pearce and Benedict Wong and is based on the 2012 novel by Peter Heller. The Dog Stars is set in a time after a flu pandemic has wiped out most of humanity and tells the story of a former civlian pilot named Hig (Elordi) and his ex-Marine companion Bangley (Brolin) as they try to survive the dangers of a fallen world. Scott directed the film from a script by Mark L. Smith ( Vacancy, The Revenant, Overlord, The Midnight Sky, The Boys in the Boat and Twisters ). The Dog Stars is the prolific Scott’s next film after 2024’s Gladiator II , and also follows Napoleon (2023), House of Gucci (2021) and The Last Duel (2021) as the 88-year-old British auteur’s other films in the 2020s. He is next scheduled to helm Treasure Island from a script by Adolescence co-creator Jack Thorne, with Hugh Jackman starring in the feature based on Robert Louis Stevenson’s work. articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ ‘The Odyssey’ Extend Battle Atop U.K. and Ireland Box Office as ‘Insidious’ Makes Strong Debut
articles.full_text: Aug 25, 2026 12:00am PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ ‘The Odyssey’ Extend Battle Atop U.K. and Ireland Box Office as ‘Insidious’ Makes Strong Debut By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Oscars: South Korea Selects Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’ for International Feature Race 21 minutes ago ‘Pride’ Musical to Transfer to Bridge Theatre From November; Director Says Bigger Venue Means the ‘Comedy Will Really Benefit From More People Watching’ 34 minutes ago Epstein Files Documentary ‘Diabolical’ Lands at HBO Max in International Deal 42 minutes ago See All Everett Collection Sony’s “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ” retained the No. 1 spot at the U.K. and Ireland box office for a fourth consecutive week, collecting £3.6 million ($4.8 million), according to Rentrak. The superhero blockbuster pushed its running cumulative gross to $117.9 million. Universal’s “ The Odyssey ,” directed by Christopher Nolan, held firmly in second place during its sixth frame, grossing $3.7 million to cross the $100 million milestone with a local total of $101.4 million. Related Stories 'Josephine' Trailer: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan Star as Struggling Parents in Sundance Award-Winning Psychological Thriller Horror sequel “ Insidious: Out of the Further ,” distributed by Sony, arrived in third place with an opening weekend of $2.9 million. Warner Bros.’ “The End of Oak Street” followed in fourth position in its second weekend, adding $1.2 million for a running total of $6.2 million. Popular on Variety Black Bear’s comedy “ Spa Weekend ” rounded out the top five with an opening haul of $668,191. articles.title: Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope,’ Netflix’s ‘Dead-End Job’ and ‘Blue Road,’ Disney+’s ‘The Remarried Empress’ Among Selections as Busan Unveils Korean Cinema Today, On Screen Lineups
articles.full_text: Aug 25, 2026 12:25am PT Na Hong-Jin’s ‘Hope,’ Netflix’s ‘Dead-End Job’ and ‘Blue Road,’ Disney+’s ‘The Remarried Empress’ Among Selections as Busan Unveils Korean Cinema Today, On Screen Lineups By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Oscars: South Korea Selects Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’ for International Feature Race 28 minutes ago ‘Pride’ Musical to Transfer to Bridge Theatre From November; Director Says Bigger Venue Means the ‘Comedy Will Really Benefit From More People Watching’ 41 minutes ago Epstein Files Documentary ‘Diabolical’ Lands at HBO Max in International Deal 49 minutes ago See All ©2026 PLUS M ENTERTAINMENT, FORGED FILMS CO LTD, AND NA HONG-JIN The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has unveiled its Korean Cinema Today and On Screen selections, with Na Hong-Jin ‘s “ Hope ” among a nine-film lineup spanning Panorama and Special Premiere. “Hope,” Na’s latest feature, drew global attention ahead of release on the strength of its large-scale production and a cast including Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Hoyeon, Taylor Russell, Cameron Britton, Alicia Vikander and Michael Fassbender. The film was selected in competition at this year’s Cannes Film Festival and will screen at BIFF as part of Korean Cinema Today – Panorama, which rounds out its six-title lineup with four world premieres. Related Stories 'Josephine' Trailer: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan Star as Struggling Parents in Sundance Award-Winning Psychological Thriller Among the Panorama selections, “The World Before” marks director Yoon Dan-bi’s return to Busan with her second feature, following a 17-year-old girl navigating unfamiliar feelings across an island summer; the film will world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival before its Asian premiere in Busan. Yoon’s 2020 debut, “Moving On,” won four prizes at BIFF in 2019, including the Netpac Award. Veteran actor Kim Hye-ja returns to the screen for the first time in nine years in “Still Shining,” the latest from director Song Il-gon, whose credits include “Spider Forest” (2004), “The Magicians” (2006) and BIFF’s 2011 Opening Film “Always.” The Panorama slate also includes Hong Sung-min’s directorial debut “Sinner,” starring Jung Sung-il and Park Ji-hyun; Lee Yong-jae’s directorial debut “Ugly Duckling Ms. Maeng,” pairing Lee Sun-bin with veteran actor You Chea-myung; and Kim Joung-hoon’s ensemble mystery “Final Interview,” led by Cho Yi-hyun, Kim Jae-won, Shin Seung-ho, Kang You-seok, Kwak Dong-yeon and Bae Gang-hee. Popular on Variety BIFF’s Korean Cinema Today – Special Premiere section, dedicated to prominent contemporary Korean commercial films, will feature three world premieres. “Cattle Run,” from first-time feature director Kim Ji-hyun, teams Ryu Seung-ryong and Park Hae-jun as estranged brothers who unite to protect a newborn calf during a village crisis. “Sapiens,” the feature debut of Lee Hu-bin, casts Jung Sung-il and You Chea-myung as a suspect and attorney working through conflicting testimony in a kidnapping case. “The Sorry Generation,” from Kim Sung-yoon, whose “Fragment” won the CGV Award and the Chorokbaem Media Award at BIFF in 2024, follows a comic family clash between an exorcism and an ancestral spirit, led by Jung Jae-young and Lee Yi-kyung. BIFF’s On Screen section, launched in 2021 to give audiences an early theatrical look at the year’s most anticipated drama series, will present three selections this year, each screening a portion of its episode order. Netflix’s “Dead-End Job,” directed by Kim Da-min, whose “FAQ” won the Aurora Media Award at BIFF in 2023, stars Lee Jae-wook, Ko Min-si, Kim Min-ha and Lee Hee-jun in a mystery centered on a suspicious part-time job; four of its eight episodes will screen. Disney+’s “The Remarried Empress,” an adaptation already drawing attention for its cast, brings Shin Mina, Ju Jihoon, Lee Jongsuk and Lee Seyoung to a romantic fantasy directed by Cho Suwon, known for “I Can Hear Your Voice” (2013) and “Still 17” (2018); three of its 10 episodes will screen. Netflix’s “Blue Road,” from Han Jun-hee, whose “Coin Locker Girl” played Cannes’ Critics’ Week in 2015 and whose series “D.P.” won Best Drama at the 2022 Baeksang Arts Awards, stars Son Suk-ku, Nagayama Eita and Kim Shin-rok in a cross-border murder mystery, with three of its eight episodes screening. The 31st Busan International Film Festival will run Oct. 6-15, in and around the Busan Cinema Center, with the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market held Oct. 10-13. articles.title: ‘Cairo Conspiracy’s’ Tawfeek Barhom to Star in Les Valseurs’ ‘Borderline’ by Oscar-Nominated Yves Piat (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 25, 2026 12:38am PT ‘Cairo Conspiracy’s’ Tawfeek Barhom to Star in Les Valseurs’ ‘Borderline’ by Oscar-Nominated Yves Piat (EXCLUSIVE) The drama-comedy, set to start filming in the spring 2027, will be pitched at Haugesund’s Nordic Co-Production Market By Annika Pham Plus Icon Annika Pham Latest ‘Game of Thrones’ Star Kristofer Hivju Turns to Rom-Com With ‘True Love’ by ‘Little Did I Know’s’ Martina Haag (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Icelandic Producer Hlín Jóhannsdóttir Sets ‘Just a Kid’ With Alief Ahead of Haugesund and Reunites With ‘Driving Mum’ Team (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago Haugesund New Nordic Films Reveals Standout 36 Nordic Projects and 15 Fresh Pics Set to Woo 300 Industry Attendees 2 weeks ago See All Tawfeek Barhom Courtesy of Les Valseurs Palestinian actor Tawfeek Barhom , best known for Tarik Saleh’s Cannes winner “ Cairo Conspiracy ” in 2022 and Palme d’Or winner 2025 for his short film “ I’m Glad You’re Dead Now ,” is set to headline the French pic “Borderline” by first-timer Yves Piat. A very loose feature-length version of Piat’s Oscar-nominated live action short “ Nefta Football Club ,” “Borderline” (Sur la ligne”) reunites Piat with producer Damien Megherbi , co-founder of French outfit Les Valseurs with Justin Pechberty. Popular on Variety Related Stories 'Josephine' Trailer: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan Star as Struggling Parents in Sundance Award-Winning Psychological Thriller Joining the cast are Samir Guesmi (“Ibrahim,” “A Prophet”) and Lyes Salem (“ Nefta Football Club ,” “The Man from Oran,” “Munich”). In the Arabic-speaking pic, Barhom stars as Hichem, a customs officer on the Algerian-Tunisian border, who tries to provide a decent life for his wife Leila and little daughter Zineb. Caught up in a corrupt system, his integrity is put to test when he meets Tesla, a music-loving donkey lost in the desert with headphones over his ears and bags full of cocaine on his back. “During my research, I often had in mind the actor who played the lead role in Matteo Garrone’s “Dogman.” When Tawfeek accepted the role, I knew I had found my ‘dogman’: with his accuracy, fragility, and determination, he will be the perfect anchor for this film, which features colorful characters struggling in the chaos of their world,“ said Piat in a statement. Speaking with Variety , ahead of the film’s pitch tomorrow at the Nordic Co-Production Market in Haugesund, Merghebi said “there’s something undeniably compelling about Tawfeek’s acting style. “The film which sits between the cinematic universes of Elia Suleiman and the Coen brothers, navigates between realism and absurdity. The character of Hichem is an upright and honest man, who encounters financial hurdles. When he finds the donkey carrying the cocaine, he is faced with a moral dilemma: should he sell it on the black market or turn it over to the authorities? Tawfik will be perfect to portray the character’s inner struggle. “ “He’s also very hard working,” the producer added. “We want the film to feel authentic, particularly regarding the Arabic language; Tawfeek speaks Palestinian Arabic, but he is capable of fully immersing himself in a role and honing the specific Arabic dialect required here.” Digging into “Borderline”’s narrative, Megherbi believes the overarching theme of borders both real and moral, should play strongly internationally. “Together with Yves and co-writer Alaa Eddine Aljem, our idea was to approach the concept of borders in a cinematic and metaphorical way,” he explained. “On one hand, you have the running theme of the moral boundary. Will Hichem stay clean, on the right track when he’s surrounded by people involved in illicit deal-making? “ “Then you have the setting on the Algerian-Tunisian border. There is something inherently absurd about the very notion of a border, especially in the middle of the Sahara,” Megherbi observed. “Borders are human inventions. In North Africa in particular, they’ve been drawn practically with a ruler by colonial powers, yet they have real consequences for people’s lives. In the film we take them very seriously, and challenge viewers to reflect on them. But their inherent absurdity is also what triggers the humour.” Spanish Co-production The project is being co-produced by Les Valseurs with Spain’s Sumendi and BTeam, partners to the French outlet on Diego Céspedes’ “ The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo ,” (Un Certain Regard top winner in 2025), with funding from Catalonia’s ICEC, France’s CNC, Region Nouvelle-Aquitaine and Pays de la Loire. At this week’s Haugesund New Nordic Films market, Megherbi is hoping to add Nordic co-producers, especially from Norway. “We’ve already co-produced “ Elephants in the Fog ” (this year’s Jury Prize winner at Cannes Un Certain Regard) with Storm Films in Norway. I believe the kind of deadpan, absurd humor tends to resonate well in Scandinavia. “Nordic people also know what it means to be tiny in front of a huge, indifferent landscape, even if the temperature is a little lower in comparison with the Sahara!” he quipped. Part of a delegation attending the French Focus in Haugesund , Megherbi will also bring to the Nordic Co-Production the animation project “All the Softness in the World,” feature debut of Turkish helmer Ayçe Kartal, multi-awarded for the short “Wicked Girl.” The sweeping story is set from the early 1950s in Turkey, through to the disco era in Paris. A boy raised as a girl in Turkey to protect him from a family vendetta, flees to Paris. There he resumes his life as a young man, and overcomes his trauma through creativity as he enters the real of Haute couture. “We’re in early stages of financing,” said Les Valseurs co-founder who is looking for equity and technical partners. Both “Borderline” and “All the Softness in the World” are vying for the Storyline Award, Best Pitch and Midpoint Talent Award, to be handed out on Thursday. The move, it claims, will “facilitate coordination between the companies and will bring their respective film, television and theatrical businesses under a common strategic vision.” Related Stories 'Josephine' Trailer: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan Star as Struggling Parents in Sundance Award-Winning Psychological Thriller Each of the companies will be under the executive leadership of owner-founder Gore, who has spent more than $100 million in building John Gore Studios , acquiring production, IP, distribution and sales business, as well as the famed Angels Costumes. Popular on Variety As part of the move, Hilary Strong will step down as CEO of John Gore Studios. Strong, an established industry veteran, joined in Jan. 2025 after leading Agatha Christie Ltd, where she helped revamp the writer’s literary estate in to a major film and TV property. “Hilary and the team took the business from zero to seven feature films in 18 months, which must be a record — all the while burnishing the legacy of Hammer Films and expanding into new technologies and complementary businesses to pave a path for the future,” said Gore. “I am extremely grateful to Hilary for the significant role she has played in the launch of John Gore Studios and excited about this next chapter.” Added Strong: “I have adored my time working with John and the wonderful team we have put together to create John Gore Studios, and I will always be grateful to John for the opportunity, but we have both agreed that, with the reshaping of the global business, my work here is done. articles.title: Epstein Files Documentary ‘Diabolical’ Lands at HBO Max in International Deal
articles.full_text: Aug 25, 2026 1:51am PT Epstein Files Documentary ‘Diabolical’ Lands at HBO Max in International Deal By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Oscars: South Korea Selects Lee Chang-dong’s ‘Possible Love’ for International Feature Race 10 minutes ago ‘Pride’ Musical to Transfer to Bridge Theatre From November; Director Says Bigger Venue Means the ‘Comedy Will Really Benefit From More People Watching’ 23 minutes ago Epstein Files Documentary ‘Diabolical’ Lands at HBO Max in International Deal 31 minutes ago See All Warner Bros. Discovery Warner Bros. Discovery has acquired international distribution rights to “Diabolical: The Epstein Files” for HBO Max , with the documentary rolling out across international territories from Sept. 3, marking its premiere in the U.K., Italy and the Netherlands. The documentary, produced and distributed by Australian Broadcasting Corporation, charts Jeffrey Epstein ‘s ascent, his trafficking network and his ultimate collapse. Epstein was convicted of sex offenses and is accused of orchestrating a sustained abuse and trafficking scheme that preyed on underage girls for years. Related Stories 'Josephine' Trailer: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan Star as Struggling Parents in Sundance Award-Winning Psychological Thriller The film also scrutinizes the failures across policing, the courts and social institutions that critics say let his abuse persist largely undetected for so long. Popular on Variety Investigators, legal experts, journalists and others tied to the case contribute first-hand testimony throughout the documentary. Interviewees include Epstein survivors Lisa Phillips and Ashley Rubright, along with his brother, Mark Epstein, and attorney David Schoen. “‘Diabolical: The Epstein Files’ is a timely examination of a case that not only shook international headlines but profoundly affected perceptions of power and influence,” said Myriam Lopez-Otazu, senior VP international unscripted content and global networks EMEA at Warner Bros. Discovery EMEA. “By exploring the scale and consequences of these crimes, the documentary provides our audiences with insight into one of the most significant and disturbing abuse cases in recent history.” HBO Max holds exclusive all-television and SVOD rights in the U.K. and Italy (including Italian-speaking Switzerland), and exclusive non-standard television and SVOD rights in the Netherlands. The platform has also secured exclusive SVOD rights across the CEE territory, Spain, Portugal, Greece, Turkey, Iceland, Cyprus, the Baltics, the CIS, Malta, Israel and Ukraine. “Diabolical: The Epstein Files” was produced by Australian Broadcasting Corporation’s Jennifer Feller and executive produced by Caitlin Shea. articles.title: Liza Soberano Joins Jury for Golden Globes Impact Prize for Documentary, Presented During Venice Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 25, 2026 1:54am PT Liza Soberano Joins Jury for Golden Globes Impact Prize for Documentary, Presented During Venice Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Liza Soberano Joins Jury for Golden Globes Impact Prize for Documentary, Presented During Venice Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) 45 minutes ago Orlando Bloom to Be Honored During Venice Film Festival With Filming Italy Award 19 hours ago Fulvio Lucisano, Italian Producer of ‘Planet of the Vampires’ and ‘What Have You Done to Solange?,’ Dies at 98 7 days ago See All Courtesy TK Filipino-American star Liza Soberano has joined the jury for the Golden Globes Impact Prize for Documentary, which will be presented by Artemis Rising Foundation during the upcoming Venice Film Festival . The prize, founded by the Golden Globes and Artemis Rising Foundation with support from Think-Film Impact Production, honors a documentary feature film in the festival’s official selection — either in or out of competition — “that exemplifies the extraordinary power of documentary filmmaking to illuminate important social issues through compelling storytelling,” according to a statement. Related Stories 'Josephine' Trailer: Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan Star as Struggling Parents in Sundance Award-Winning Psychological Thriller Soberano, who moved from California to the the Philippines as a child, built a stellar career there before crossing over to make her Hollywood debut in Focus Features’ “Lisa Frankenstein” in 2024. She has a lead voice role in DreamWorks Animation upcoming “Forgotten Island” that will be released in September. Along with her creative work, Soberano is an active ambassador for Save the Children Philippines as well as an advocate for women and children’s rights, protection of children from online sexual exploitation and mental health. Popular on Variety “I’ve always believed that film has the power to do more than entertain — it can challenge injustice, offer safety, inspire hope and remind us of our shared humanity,” Soberano said. “Documentary filmmaking is where some of the most courageous and unforgettable storytelling is happening today. I’m honored to serve on this jury, because celebrating documentary filmmakers isn’t only about recognizing extraordinary talent; it’s where the future of cinema is heading,” she added. The Golden Globes Impact Prize for Documentary Award’s full jury will comprise Golden Globes president Helen Hoehne; Oscar-winning producer and founder of Artemis Rising Foundation, Regina K. Scully; Oscar-winning producer and co-founder of Impact Partners, Geralyn White Dreyfous; and founder and CEO of Think-Film Impact Production, Danielle Turkov Wilson. The winner will receive a cash prize of $10,000 from Artemis Rising Foundation. The Golden Globes, Artemis Rising Foundation and Think-Film Impact Production first partnered to launch a documentary prize at the 2025 Cannes Film Festival and then expanded the partnership to Venice last year. “Documentaries have become some of the defining cinematic experiences of our time,” said Golden Globes president Hoehne, noting that in the Venice documentaries selection “we see creatives continuing to expand what the genre can do.” Regina K. Scully, founder of Artemis Rising Foundation, said: “We are thrilled to continue our partnership with the Golden Globes and the Venice Film Festival to celebrate cinematic excellence and see documentary storytelling receiving the prominence and recognition it has long earned.” Commented Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera: “Venice has always been a home for filmmakers who expand the possibilities of cinema, and documentary has become one of the defining creative forces in contemporary filmmaking.” “As this art form continues to grow in creative ambition and global reach, it is only natural that its place within the international awards landscape continues to evolve. We are proud to host and support the Golden Globes Impact Prize for Documentary; we welcome every initiative that elevates this [type of] work and reflects its growing importance within our industry’s highest honors.” The 83rd Venice Film Festival runs from Sept. 2 to 12.
