articles.title: Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children” View All August 23, 2026 8:04pm (L-R) Mark Curry, Raquel Lee, Dawnn Lewis, Tahj Mowry in 2001's The Proof Point Disney The Proof Point’ s Raquel Lee claims in a extremely graphic negligence suit against the Walt Disney Company she was “repeatedly raped, sexually assaulted, sexually abused and sexually harassed” on the Utah set of the 2001 movie. The House of Mouse knew about it and did nothing to stop the violence, the Quiet on Set: The Dark Side of Kids TV participant adds. “John Doe (“Mr. Doe”), an on-set, adult, middle-aged, male employee of Disney who was involved in the filming of the movie,” the August 21 filing in LA Superior Court for the now Raquel Lee Boileau from NYC-based Wigdor LLP says with intentional vagueness about the alleged predator. “Mr. Doe’s sexual abuse of Ms. Boileau was apparent to the adults on Disney’s set. Defendant Disney repeatedly failed Ms. Boileau. Disney facilitated and concealed Mr. Doe’s severe sexual abuse of Ms. Boileau.” Related Stories News 'National Treasure 3' In Works, Franchise Director Reveals: "It's Finally Real" News Disney Inks Creator Content Deal With Dhar Mann Studios “Disney’s set was not safe for children,” the unspecified “money judgement” seeking complaint states of what the 14-year-old Lee faced on the Mark Curry-led and Neal Israel-directed Disney Channel film. A case of kooky scientists ( Hangin With Mr Copper’s Curry and Dawnn Lewis) their kids (Lee and Tahj Mowry), the time traveling Proof Point debuted on September 14, 2001. Watch on Deadline Claiming the “visibly disheveled” teen was also at the receiving end of tirades from Disney execs at the time over her performance, the filing strategically invokes the much accused, much convicted and Incarcerated Harvey Weinstein , among others. With the ex-Miramax kingpin in mind, the now nearly 40-year-old actress’ jury trial desiring filing adds: “This is not the first time that Disney has enabled a sexual predator to target and abuse vulnerable victims. Disney has a longstanding and horrifying history of protecting sexual abusers that began well before 2001-and continued after 2001.” “Disney has caused irreparable and devastating harm, and must be held accountable,” the action claims for its client. “Defendant failed to use reasonable care in investigating the circumstances on set and did nothing to reasonably investigate, supervise or monitor and/or terminate Mr. Doe to ensure the safety of child actors,” it also bluntly says. Contacted by Deadline, Disney today had no comment on the suit or the accusations within it. That’s not surprising all things litigious considered – even more so with the amount of time that has passed and people involved who are no longer at Disney. In terms of a situation specific timeline, the first the Josh D’Aamaro-led company heard about this sordid case was back in June, sources say. That was when Doug Wigdor and Jame Kim approached Disney in the hopes of settling this out of court. Clearly, the parties couldn’t reach a satisfactory deal. What is also clear is that while Disney may or may not have first heard of the horrors Lee went through in 2001 just a few months ago, this four-claim action is not the first time the actress has had lawyers involved fallout from Poof Point . Deadline has learned that in 2015 a Gloria Allred -represented Lee negotiated a confidential settlement for “a small amount of money” with a male who worked on Proof Point. The male in question was represented by Venable partner William Biggs, II. Allred had no comment on any settlement or anything to do with it when contacted by Deadline. Biggs did not response to Deadline’s request for comment on that matter of over a decade ago. Details of that settlement and the exact sum paid out are under lock and key – – hence likely the “John Doe “in this new civil complaint. However, the presence of Allred, well known for her work for sexual assault survivors, could be an indication of the nature of the core case back in 2015. As for this latest action, the law has changed in Lee’s favor. Whereas in the past Lee would have long exhausted the statute of limitations, under a 2020 California measure, survivors of childhood sexual abuse now have up until their 40th birthday to file a civil claim. Actually, an 2023 addition to that 2020 law removed any statute of limitations for civil claims of childhood sexual assault survivors that occurred on or after January 1, 2024. Under the law as it stands now, a plaintiff can claims triple actual damages if it is proven a company (like Disney), institution or persons(s) were aware of the assaults and abuse and choose to conceal what was happening. A state of affairs that is precisely what Lee is saying Disney did in her case on Poof Point. It is worth noting that former Real Husbands of Hollywood regular Raquel Lee Boileau has worked with Disney on several occasions since The Poof Point . She did voiceover on Disney+’s The Proud Family: Louder and Proude r . Debuting in 2022, the animated series was a revival of Disney Channel’s The Proud Family , which Raquel Lee Boileau was also on from 2001-2005. Raquel Lee Boileau’s attorneys had nothing to say whatsoever today on any 2015 settlement, but they were not silent about what they filed this weekend. “Over the last decade, countless child actors have come forward to bravely share their experiences of abuse by adults in entertainment,” said Doug Wigdor and Jane Kim. “As former government prosecutors, our message to the entertainment industry is simple: This conduct is inexcusable, and those involved—directly or indirectly—must be held accountable.” It is also worth noting Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV’s Broadcast Arm Sony’s One-Two Punch: $39M For ‘Spider-Man’ & $25M+ For ‘Insidious’ Settlement Talks With State AGs This Week; Newsom Weighs In On Merger Karoline Leavitt Reveals Post-White House Press Secretary Job Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children” View All August 23, 2026 11:16pm Paramount & Warner Bros water towers Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: A meeting Monday between Paramount brass and state Attorneys General over sussing out settlement talks between the parties in David Ellison ‘s contested $111 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery has turned into a “game of PR chicken,” an industry insider says. “Ellison and Makan Delrahim think they can force Rob Bonta into backing off with threats and intimidation,” a Tinseltown mandarin points out, as leaks out of Paramount insist the company is considering leaving California if the antitrust suit filed by the Golden State’s AG Bonta and 11 others ends up going to trial in March 2027. “That’s not going to work. He’s more determined that ever to take them to court, the rest is all for show, to take the pressure off.” Related Stories News Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Calls Out Mark Ruffalo For "Antisemitism" & "Demonization" News Mark Ruffalo Blasts Paramount For Calling Him "Antisemitic" Over Merger Criticism: "Appalling And Fundamentally Dishonest" A part of that so-called show and responding to settlement calls from corporate and political stakeholders are some pretty audacious proposals that were discussed in August 21 communications between the AGs’ offices, their Milbank outside counsel, and the Melrose lot. Watch on Deadline It wasn’t quite the drama of Reagan and Gorbachev in Reykjavík in 1986, but there certainly were landmines. Setting the stage for the August 24 conference with promised “structural remedies,” Team AG are asking Paramount to sell off several of WBD’s cable channels. The Wall Street Journal first reported the potential conditions earlier Sunday. Doubting Ellison’s repeated promise to release 30 movies a year in cinemas is real or even possible, the states’ also want the movie studios kept separate, Deadline has confirmed. Bonta, New York’s Letitia James and the other blue state AGs have said they will bring a codicil of sort to the table for the August 24 huddle. In what is both a boss move and a poison pill, the AGs want Donald Trump’s “good friend” David Ellison agree to not have any day-to-day oversight or control of WB, I’m told. California Attorney General Rob Bonta left, Paramount CEO David Ellison Getty Images “David’s not going to go along with any of that, and Bonta knows it,” a studio exec told Deadline Sunday of stipulations that would neuter the mogul aspiring Para CEO and gut most of any immediate revenue streams for a $80 billion debt carrying ParaBros combo. Using terms like “performative” to describe Bonta and the other AGs staff agenda items, the exec asserts: “Ellison needs those cable channels, that’s still where the money is.” Though the object of much chatter and always in Trump’s bad books, sparkly CNN does not appear to be among the cable jewels the AGs want Oracle founder Larry Ellison’s son to divest himself of to get the merger done. HBO and HBO Max are not part of the talking points for the meeting, to no surprise. Individuals from different corners of the corporate, political and legal arena as well as with co-plaintiffs the Writers Guild of America, tell Deadline that expectations are “intentionally low” for that Monday’s meeting. “No one trusts anyone on the other side, it’s obvious,” the industry insider claims of the big law firms feeding frenzy, the big stakes and big personalities involved. “The states’ think Paramount’s going to say whatever they need to say to close the merger and avoid paying fees. Paramount think this is all partisan politics. Both sides are wrong and right, not willing to give anything big up. That’s not going to work if you want a deal.” While Paramount has made some minor M&A and ownership concessions outside the US and the UK for regulatory approval of the merger, the agenda items the AGs are throwing down are on a whole other level. A de facto obligation under the mediation proceedings routinely initiated in federal civil cases to prevent costly and time consuming trials, the perfunctory August 24 gathering took on exalted status in past 55 hours. After placed items that a Red State could become Para’s new HQ, and a tactical but punted Hail Mary request for the states to pony up a $1.88 billion bond to offset the “extraordinary losses” the states’ case could cause home of The Godfather , increasingly lame duck Governor Gavin Newsom suddenly joined the chorus of exhibitors , gubernatorial candidates , the DGA, IATSE and flipping and then flopping again LA Mayor Karen Bass to break his Sphinx-like silence last week. Newsom said he believed “there’s some universal settlement there, if that’s possible” between his close colleague Bonta and his reported pal Ellison. Stressing on August 21 he took “seriously” the threats Paramount may leave California, the probable 2028 POTUS contender threw some Red media meat into the mix, adding: “I know there are many meetings that are going on, and there’s a lot of conversation.” Paramount had no comment Sunday on any proposals put forth late last week for discussion in Monday’s part face-to-face, part virtual meeting. The CA AG’s office, the NY AG’s office and the WGA did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment tonight. However, in what could be the first conversation between Ellison and Bonta since the AGs filed their now WGA joined antitrust action on July 13, there is hope on both sides that the principals can at least lower the temperature a tad. To that, Ellison may need to get much more directly involved Monday and going forward as a backlash is growing against Para’s chief legal officer and merger field marshal Delrahim. “It’s not just he says one thing in public, another in private,” a source close to events tells Deadline of the “frustrated” opinion officials have of the former Trump Assistant Attorney General and antitrust boss. “He seems to want to provoke a conflict for conflict’s sake.” Back in court, Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin last week set August 26 as the date a Magistrate judge will be selected for mediation between Para and the AGs/WGA. An amended proposed scheduling order is due from the parties the same day. Besides leaks, tweets and the usual spin from the participant Monday, that order may prove to be the best indication what direction this all could really be going. articles.title: Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV For First Time
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV For First Time Meghan Markle Could Resume Acting Career After Return To UK – Report International Insider: Australia’s Attention Battle; Vertical Video Rises; Kevin Macdonald On Pep Guardiola View All August 24, 2026 12:43am 'Baby Reindeer' Netflix Netflix just hit a major milestone in the UK. The global streamer has posted £2.06B ($2.81B) revenues for full-year 2025, meaning it generated more cash than the country’s leading commercial broadcaster, ITV , and is well ahead of smaller PSB rivals Channel 4 (£1B) and Paramount-owned 5 (£318M). The BBC ‘s is funded by the licence fee and does not account in a comparable way. Netflix’s revenue grew 11.3% from the £1.85B posted in 2024, according to a Companies House filing, with the growth pegged primarily to 7% growth in the average number of paying customers and “higher average monthly revenue” per paying member. Related Stories Casting 'One Piece: The Battle Of Alabasta' Adds Four To Season 3 Cast In Roles Of Koza, Toto, Pell & Chaka News 'Hercule': BritBox Unveils First Look At Edward Bluemel As Title Character In Poirot Origin Series The 2025 figure compares with the £1.9B ITV’s media and entertainment made in its latest full-year results . The division, which houses ITV’s channel suite and streamer ITVX, is being sold to Sky. When production wing ITV Studios is added in, ITV plc posted revenues of £4.12B. Watch on Deadline Netflix UK ‘s operating profit for the financial year ended December 31, 2025, was £44.9M, up slightly on the £43.2M the year before, with profit after tax coming in at £53.3M, up 11.5%. The news will surely be a big talking point at the final Edinburgh Television Festival this week in the Scottish capital, where Netflix and the UK’s other major streamers and broadcasters will take to stage to talk to the industry. Netflix UK’s Doc Series boss, Adam Hawkins, is the fest’s advisory chair this year. Netflix launched in the UK in 2012 as part of its first expansion into Europe, and has since grown into one of the dominating forces in British broadcasting through shows such as Baby Reindeer , The Gentlemen and Adolescence . With the BBC’s licence fee model in crisis, the idea of forcing streamers to support the UK’s leading public broadcaster in collecting its funding. The Motion Picture Association, which represents Netflix and the U.S. studios, has slammed the idea and even BBC Director General Matt Brittin has admitted the plan would be “difficult” to enforce. Earlier this year, regulator Ofcom’s Media Nations report revealed Netflix was ahead of the BBC, ITV and YouTube as the service viewers first thought of when deciding what to watch. The number of 16-24s choosing the streamer first was further ahead of rivals. The filing to Companies House showed that Netflix Services UK Limited, the company Netflix uses to house its earnings in Britain, distributed interim dividends of £30M on July 21, 2025. It also increased the amount loaned from Netflix to nearly £400M, with an extended maturity date of August 1, 2028, and became a subsidiary of Amsterdam-based Netflix International, which merged with Netflix Services Holdings in May last year. According to the filing, Netflix employed an average of 342 staff in the UK in 2025, up from 263 the year before. articles.title: Hayley Atwell Says Peggy Carter Getting “Frisbeed To Death” In ‘Doctor Strange’ Was “A Complete Disservice To The Character”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake ‘Free Nelson Mandela’ Maker Rogan Productions Opens South Africa Office & Tweaks Management Set Up Patchway Studios, Which Supported ‘Rivals’ & ‘A Good Girl’s Guide To Murder’ Shoots, Fights Closure Threat From Investor ITN Journalist Exited With “Significant” Payoff After Review Found He Suffered Mental Health Discrimination View All August 24, 2026 12:57am Hayley Atwell as Captain Carter in 'Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness' Marvel Studios Hayley Atwell was disappointed about the demise of Peggy Carter. In an interview at the For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi convention in London, Atwell told attendees that she was frustrated by Captain Carter’s storyline in 2022’s Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . Cameoing in the film as an alternate to Captain America, Carter — an MCU fixture since 2011 — was apparently killed off by Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen) with her own shield. Atwell said: “If I’m really like brutally honest, I was so disappointed with how they positioned her and what happened to her in that scene. It’s so small, and she gets frisbeed to death.” Related Stories News Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Says "Optics Are Obvious" Of 'Wonder Man' Cancellation & 'Blade' Reboot Delays: "It Should Be A Priority To Change That Narrative" News Everything We Know About Marvel's Upcoming 'X-Men' Movie So Far The actress said she pleaded with colleagues on set to make changes to the scene. “I tried on set to kind of go, ‘Can I just add? Can I just suggest?’ And they were like, ‘Sure, but no.'” Watch on Deadline She continued: “I felt that was like a bum steer and a complete disservice to the character.” View this post on Instagram Atwell, who is expected to return as Carter in Avengers: Doomsday later this year, said the character was having “fun” in the Captain Carter guise — and she hopes for more of the same. “I hope maybe one day in the future they’ll give her more in that capacity,” she teased. It’s not the first time Atwell has discussed her misgivings about Carter’s cameo in Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness . In 2023, she told the Happy Sad Confused podcast: “When she was like, ‘I could do this all day’ and then followed by she’s immediately cut in half by a frisbee. And the audience being like, ‘She can’t do it all day. Apparently you can’t, so, egg on your face.’ That doesn’t really serve Peggy very well.” Earlier in the For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi interview, Atwell revealed that she uses Carter’s line “I know my value” in her contract negotiations with Marvel . “If I’m able to say these lines with conviction, I’ve got to embody them myself,” she added. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison’s Power Put On The Table Disney Knew About On-Set Rapes & Did Nothing, ‘Poof Point’ Actress’ Negligence Suit Asserts: “Not Safe For Children” View All August 24, 2026 1:11am California Attorney General Rob Bonta Getty There will be no settlement talks meeting Monday between Paramount and a coalition of state Attorneys General after all. California AG Rob Bonta cancelled the scheduled sit-down late Sunday after reports of an August 21 meeting with the David Ellison -led company oozed out. More galling to Bonta is that what was discussed at that meeting about a meeting slipped out into the public sphere. “Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” the AG said in a statement provided to Deadline in the midnight hour. “As soon as Paramount stops playing games and engages sincerely, my office is happy to meet again.” Related Stories Acquisitions Paramount & AGs Settlement Meeting Monday More Show Than Substance As Cable Channel Sell-Offs & Curbing Ellison's Power Put On The Table News Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Calls Out Mark Ruffalo For "Antisemitism" & "Demonization" News of behind the scenes talks in the bitter battle over Paramount’s $111 billion merger with Warner Bros Discovery were actually first confirmed publicly by none other than Gov. Gavin Newsom . “I know there are many meetings that are going on, and there’s a lot of conversation,” the presumed 2028 presidential candidate said on August 21. Watch on Deadline It should be noted that Deadline actually heard details of the August 21 preliminary gathering to set the agenda for the August 24 meeting from a variety of sources, if you know what I mean? Though expectations for the August 24 meeting were “intentionally low,” sources told Deadline Sunday, there seemed to be several hot ticket items on the table for the parties. Specifically, representatives of the 12 state AGs who sued Paramount and Warner Bros Discovery in an antitrust action on July 13 wanted CEO Ellison to sell a swath of WBD’s still lucrative cable channel stable. As well, the elected officials sought to have Paramount and WB remain two separate studios, with Donald Trump pal Ellison ( and to some extent his father and backer Larry Ellison) practically cordoned off from running the place he just bought. “David’s not going to go along with any of that, and Bonta knows it,” a studio exec told Deadline Sunday of the discussion points put on the table. Clear non-starters with Ellison and Para execs, the agenda points also reflect the wide figurative and literal distance between the AGs, their lawsuit partners the WGA and the Melrose lot. Paramount did not respond early Monday to request for comment on Bonta’s pulling of the meeting plug. The New York Times first reported the meeting cancellation. Urged by the likes of Gov. Newsom, flip-flopping L.A. Mayor Karen Bass, the DGA, IATSE , Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra, and others to sit down and hammer out a settlement, the AGs and Paramount/WBD have been set by a federal judge to go to trial on March 2, 2027. David Ellison, Chairman & CEO, Paramount Skydance Getty With Bonta decrying leaks of Ellison moving Paramount Skydance to Georgia, Texas or Tennessee if the ParaBros merger doesn’t see significant talks or resolution by October 1 as “blackmail,” the bitterness between the two has become as much a corporate and political showdown as a legal one. The CEO penning NYT op-eds i nsisting it is all about CNN, didn’t help the healing process. The already reinforced battlefronts became all the more stark over the past week with Paramount ignoring federal Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin’s earlier implied rejection of any bond from the states and asking for a $1.88 billion bond to offset the “extraordinary losses” the suit could cost the company. Add to that another report submitted to the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors on August 19 spotlighting “about 4,500 TV and film jobs ..could be lost.” The L.A. County Department of Economic Opportunity also estimates thousands of more indirect and industry adjacent jobs will be wiped out by the more than $80 billion debt carry ParaBros. The bigger picture puts another consequence of the merger being the loss of wages in the billions and the region losing $547 million in tax revenue. No further settlement meetings had been put on the calender beyond today. One source said to Deadline the fight between Paramount and Bonta is all a “game of PR chicken.” If so, then someone just blinked. articles.title: Venice Adds Competition Film From ‘No Other Land’ Directors, Jim Wilson & Jonathan Glazer About “Systems Behind Israel’s Calculated Killing Of Palestinian Civilians”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Pamela Anderson To Be Honored At AmfAR During Venice Film Festival Terrence Terrell, Jayne Taini, Sachin Bhatt, Mario Cantone & William Sadler Lead Dramedy ‘The Summer They Came’ SXSW True Crime Doc ‘I Got Bombed At Harvey’s’ Scores North American Deal View All August 24, 2026 2:15am Naza Venice Film Festival The Venice Film Festival has added a hot-button documentary to its Competition lineup. The synopsis for new film NAZA (we’re told this is an acronym relating to the Israeli military) reads: “Shot at night on the rooftops of Tel Aviv, the film reveals in detail the systems behind Israel’s calculated mass killing of Palestinian civilians in Gaza”. The film heralds from Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor, two of the four co-directors of the 2025 Oscar-winning documentary No Other Land . It has been produced by UK news outlet The Guardian , and James Wilson (JW Films) and executive-produced by Jonathan Glazer . Wilson and Glazer are the Oscar-winning team behind The Zone of Interest . The duo’s speech at the Oscars following their win was the source of a considerable amount of chatter in the days following. Related Stories News Pamela Anderson To Be Honored At AmfAR During Venice Film Festival News Martin Scorsese Joins Paul Schrader's Venice Drama 'The Basics Of Philosophy' As EP; Noora Films Boards Sales The film will be screened in the Sala Grande (Palazzo del Cinema) on 10 September at 5.15pm, in the presence of the directors, the producers, Guardian journalists and the official delegation. Watch on Deadline Yuval Abraham and Rachel Szor join nine other directors (across 21 films) making their debut in the Venice Film Festival’s Competition, alongside Casey Affleck, Alì Asgari, Danny Boyle, May el-Toukhy, Cédric Kahn, Ilya Khrzhanovsky, Lance Oppenheim, Nicolas Pariser and Paolo Strippoli. Oscar winner No Other Land showed the destruction of a Palestinian community in the occupied West Bank, which had been resisting forced displacement after an Israeli “firing zone” was declared on their land. Israel’s settlement policies in the occupied West Bank have drawn condemnation from the UK, France, Germany, Italy and Canada in recent days. All settlements are illegal under international law. Wilson and Glazer were recently producer and executive producer respectively on Venice 2025 drama and Oscar nominee The Voice Of Hind Rajab , about the final hours of a six-year-old Palestinian girl trapped in a car under fire in Gaza in January 2024. Israeli authorities last week opened a criminal investigation into her death. The subject of the Israel-Gaza conflict has once again been to the fore this weekend in Hollywood following a verbal skirmish between actor Mark Ruffalo and Paramount leadership . articles.title: Gaumont Unveils First Deals On Stéphane Brizé’s Venice & TIFF-Bound ‘A Good Little Soldier’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Emile Hirsch Joins Anthony Michael Hall, Claire Forlani & Stephen Lang Set In Sci-Fi Thriller ‘Final Invasion’ Ahead Of TIFF Market Launch Supernatural Thriller ‘Snapshot’ Gets Sales Deal Ahead Of Edinburgh & Frightfest Bows, Watch First Clip Canada’s Rodeo FX Taps Former MPC Film Montreal Exec For Key Corporate Role View All August 24, 2026 2:29am A Good Little Soldier Gaumont, France 3 Cinéma EXCLUSIVE: Stéphane Brizé’s A Good Little Soldier , starring Alba Rohrwacher as a high-powered exec confronted with a case of toxic management, has sold to a number of key territories ahead of its world premiere in competition in Venice and North American debut in Toronto . Gaumont has sealed deals for Australia (Palace Films), Switzerland (Xenix), Spain (BTeam Pictures), Greece (Rosebud), Italy (I Wonder Pictures), Benelux (Cinéart), Portugal (Alambique), former Yugoslavia (MCF) and Turkey (Mars Film). Brizé’s 11th fiction feature, A Good Little Soldier sees the director return to his exploration of the workplace at the heart of previous dramas The Measure of a Man , At War and Another World . Related Stories News Venice Adds Competition Film From 'No Other Land' Directors, The Guardian & Jonathan Glazer About "Systems Behind Israel's Calculated Killing Of Palestinian Civilians" News Pamela Anderson To Be Honored At AmfAR During Venice Film Festival It Brizé’s fourth time in competition at Venice after the Fipresci Prize winning A Woman’s Life as well as Another World and romantic interlude Out of Season , starring Guillaume Canet and Rohrwacher. Watch on Deadline In her second collaboration with Brizé, Rohrwacher plays 43 years old Carla Moretti, a high-performing and devoted business executive, whose polished exterior conceals deep insecurities. Hired as the HR manager of a major corporation with a mission to promote employee well-being while maintaining demanding performance goals, she comes up against toxic management practices. Compromises become unavoidable, threatening to push her to breaking point. The film also reunites Brizé with longtime collaborator Vincent Lindon in the role of the corporation’s pushy CEO. It marks their sixth film together, with their past collaborations including The Measure of a Man , for which Lindon won Best Actor in Cannes in 2015. “Anger was the dominant feeling throughout the making of The Measure of a Man, At War and Another World . That anger has never entirely left me, but over time, it has given way to something closer to disgust. Partly because I now understand more clearly the mechanisms of a system that arrogantly ignores the signs of suffering among employees. And partly because I have become more acutely aware of the grotesque charade of corporate communication,” says Brizé of the new film. “As a result, this film has a much sharper edge. Without ever concealing the violence of the system, it shows a kind of casual, shameless indecency that makes us laugh, as though the film were tipping into farce.” The film is a Gaumont production, lead produced by Sidonie Dumas, in coproduction with France 3 Cinéma and with the support of Canal+. Gaumont handles international sales and distribution in France where the film launches in cinemas on November 25. A Good Little Soldier plays in competition at Venice in the second half of the festival and then heads to TIFF where it will screen as a Special Presentation. articles.title: Netflix, Disney+ & Amazon Rein In Price Rises As Customers Near Financial “Limits” – Ampere
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks Read the full story By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV For First Time Meghan Markle Could Resume Acting Career After Return To UK – Report International Insider: Australia’s Attention Battle; Vertical Video Rises; Kevin Macdonald On Pep Guardiola View All August 24, 2026 2:47am Prime Video's 'Sterling Point' Prime Video Streamer price hikes are taking consumers nearer to the limit of what they’re willing to spend, according to Ampere Analysis . As such, Netflix , Disney+ and Prime Video owner Amazon have been reducing the size of average price increases from 24% per subscription in 2023/24 to 14% in 2025/26. In dollar terms, the average has increased, albeit more modestly from $1.67 per month to $1.54, over the same period. Ad-free tiers have seen larger price rises than ad-supported tiers ($1.61 versus $1.21), and the price gap between the two options has grown, Ampere’s report showed. Related Stories News Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV For First Time Casting 'One Piece: The Battle Of Alabasta' Adds Four To Season 3 Cast In Roles Of Koza, Toto, Pell & Chaka This points to global streaming services nearing a precipice for cost increases, as the proliferation of services available and a general caution around spending mean consumers are becoming less likely to accept higher and higher demands. Watch on Deadline “As streaming markets mature and become increasingly competitive and saturated, Ampere believes the trend could indicate that streamers are moving closer to the limits of consumers’ willingness to pay, leaving less headroom for larger price increases in the future,” said the research house in its latest report. With advertising now a key revenue driver for most global streamers, they are being incentivized to keep price rises down on ad-supported tiers, while increases on paid-for tiers are larger. Western Europe has seen the largest average price rises over the past three years at $1.86 or 16%, ahead of North America ($1.79/15%) and Central and Eastern Europe ($1.68/18%). Of the three serviced tracked, Netflix’s price increases have “remained broadly stable,” while Disney+ has “seen the clearest shift towards more modest increases.” Amazon made the fewest, which is “likely reflecting the broader role of the Prime subscription within Amazon’s retail business.” “The decline in price increases comes as streamers diversify how they monetise their audiences. Advertising is an increasingly important revenue stream, reducing reliance on subscription pricing alone, while password-sharing crackdowns allow streamers to generate more value from existing audiences through extra member slots. As streaming businesses mature, revenue growth is becoming less reliant on price increases, while intense competition is also making streamers increasingly mindful of how they are positioned against rivals.” Netflix Posts $2.8B Revenues In UK To Overtake ITV’s Broadcast Arm Sony’s One-Two Punch: $39M For ‘Spider-Man’ & $25M+ For ‘Insidious’ Settlement Talks With State AGs This Week; Newsom Weighs In On Merger Karoline Leavitt Reveals Post-White House Press Secretary Job Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Michael Wright, Star of ‘The Five Heartbeats’ and ‘Sugar Hill,’ Dies at 70
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 22, 2026 8:18am Michael Wright Mark Von Holden/WireImage Michael Wright, who starred as the lead vocalist Eddie King Jr. in Robert Townsend’s The Five Heartbeats and as Wesley Snipes’ brother in Sugar Hill , has died. He was 70. Wright died Wednesday in Los Angeles of heart failure and complications from Marchiafava-Bignami disease, a rare degenerative neurological disorder, TMZ reported . “Our family is grieving an enormous and deeply personal loss,” his wife, Susan, wrote on Instagram. “Michael, your work will live forever, but your love will live even longer in the hearts of those who knew you best. Rest peacefully, my love. You will be missed beyond words.” Related Stories Movies Paul M. Pollard, Camera Man on 'Bound for Glory' and 'Heaven's Gate,' Dies at 84 Music Frank Beard, ZZ Top Drummer, Dies at 77 The lanky Wright also stood out as the Resistance fighter Elias Taylor on the popular NBC miniseries and series V in the mid-1980s and as the drug-addled inmate Omar White on 22 episodes of HBO’s Oz over three seasons from 2001-03. In The Five Heartbeats (1991), written by Townsend and Keenen Ivory Wayans, Wright sparkled as the leader of the Motown-inspired R&B group that struggles to deal with success over the years (his King character battled drugs and alcohol). The group also featured Townsend as Duck Matthews, Tico Wells as Anthony “Choirboy” Stone, Leon as J.T. Matthews and Harry J. Lennix as Terrence “Dresser” Williams. Wright was excellent again as Raynathan Skuggs, brother of Snipes’ Roemello Skuggs, in the gritty Sugar Hill (1994), written by Barry Michael Cooper in the second film of his “Harlem Trilogy.” From left: Leon, Robert Townsend, Tico Wells, Harry J. Lennix and Michael Wright in ‘The Five Heartbeats.’ 20th Century Fox Film / courtesy Everett Collection Wright was born in New York City on April 30, 1956. His mother, Alberta, owned Jezebel, a Southern restaurant in the theater district, and that’s where he met Townsend for the first time. “I never go out,” Townsend told New York magazine in 1991. “But before I knew it, we were club-hopping. Then we ended up in Michael’s apartment at 3 a.m. watching this Japanese film [ Bedtime Lies ] he’d made.” Wright had started out in a work study program at the Lee Strasberg Institute, where he “mopped floors, I answered phones, I did all kinds of tasks in exchange for my classes,” he told Sheen magazine in a 2021 interview. He then appeared in his first film as Clinton, the leader of The Del Bombers gang, in The Wanderers (1979), directed by Philip Kaufman, followed by a turn as a volatile young soldier named Carlyle in Robert Altman ’s Streamers (1983). Six months after their first meeting, Townsend sent him the script for The Five Heartbeats for the role that had been designed with Denzel Washington in mind. He noted that after Cooper had written the part of Raynathan for him in Sugar Hill , he was sitting in a coffee shop in Manhattan when Snipes walked in “with an entourage of about 10 people.” “I just stood up and got him by the lapels and said, ‘Man, I got a movie and I want you to make it with me,’” he said. “He wanted me to tell him more about it. We got in his limo. Wesley had a three-picture deal with Fox, I think. I got Wes to commit to making that film. That’s how that film got made. “That was an authentic New York role, and it was made for me. A lot of it was commiserate with my own personal journey. I improvised the whole film.” Wright’s résumé also included the films The Principal (1987), Money Talks (1997), Piñero (2001), The Interpreter (2005) and Dope King (2025) and the TV series Miami Vice , New York Undercover and Black Lightning . Survivors include five children and a grandchild. “The greatest sin an actor can commit is to fail to be interesting,” he said in his Sheen interview. “I always try to make my characters interesting. I want you to be riveted and wonder what’s going on behind my eyes. I want the audience to think along with me and go on an internal journey.” View this post on Instagram THR

articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swinging to Fourth Box Office Victory as It Tops ‘Insidious’ Sequel
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ryan Gajewski Plus Icon Ryan Gajewski Senior Entertainment Reporter View All August 22, 2026 8:55am Tom Holland stars in 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day.' Sony Pictures Logo text Spider-Man: Brand New Day continues to deliver in its fourth weekend at the box office as it faces off against newcomers Insidious: Out of the Further and the Jason Statham -led Mutiny . Sony Pictures ‘ releases are set to claim the top two spots at the domestic box office, as Spider-Man: Brand New Day grossed $9.8 million on Friday, with the studio projecting it to add $36.5 million for the weekend amid its historic run . This would bring its domestic cume to $852.4 million through Sunday, surpassing 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home to become the No. 3 highest-grossing film ever at the domestic box office. This will also put Brand New Day as Sony’s highest-grossing domestic film after it set the record last weekend for the top global release in the studio’s history. Related Stories Beyond the Book How 'The Magic Faraway Tree' Embraced Its Dated Source Material to Deliver a Humble Yet Epic Adaptation Movies 'Insidious: Out of the Further' Hunts Down $3M in Box Office Previews Insidious: Out of the Further occupies second place with $10.6 million on Friday, including Thursday previews . Sony projects an opening weekend of $23.7 million for the sixth installment in the horror franchise that hails from Screen Gems , Stage 6 Films and Blumhouse Atomic Monster and kicked off with 2011’s original Insidious . Out of the Further earned a C+ CinemaScore, tying 2023’s Insidious: The Red Door for the series’ lowest grade. Debuting in 3,330 North American theaters, Out of the Further stars Amelia Eve, Brandon Perea and Lin Shaye and centers on a young mother who can bring spirits back with her to the real world. It follows The Red Door , which saw the return of original series stars Patrick Wilson and Rose Byrne. That one opened to an impressive $33 million domestically before grossing $189 million worldwide throughout its run. Amelia Eve in Insidious: Out of the Further. Sony Pictures With an $18 million production budget, Out of the Further holds a 60 percent approval rating from critics on Rotten Tomatoes and a 70 percent audience score. Critic Frank Scheck wrote in his review for The Hollywood Reporter that the film “proves routine in its elaborate plot machinations.” Also opening this weekend is Mutiny , as Lionsgate’s film notched $2.8 million domestically on Friday, including Thursday previews. Earning a B+ CinemaScore from audiences, Statham’s latest action title looks to pick up $7.4 million for the frame to land in sixth place from 2,600 North American screens. MadRiver Pictures and Punch Palace Productions produced the project that carries a $40 million production budget. Director Jean-François Richet’s feature stars Statham as a former Marine who sets out to prove his innocence after getting framed for murder. It holds a 50 percent approval score from critics on Rotten Tomatoes but an 80 percent score from audiences. Mutiny follows Statham’s Shelter , which opened with $5.5 million domestically earlier this year for Black Bear. Jason Statham as Cole Reed in Mutiny. Dan Smith/Lionsgate Universal’s The Odyssey is finding a home in third place with an estimated $18.5 million for its sixth weekend to bring its domestic total to $538 million. Starring Matt Damon as Odysseus, Christopher Nolan’s mythological epic surpassed Deadpool & Wolverine during the week to stand as the highest-grossing R-rated title globally. In its sophomore frame, director David Robert Mitchell’s dinosaur-focused The End of Oak Street looks to scarf down around $8 million to bring the Warner Bros. release’s two-week domestic total to $37 million. Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor star in the survival feature, which is set to decline by around 62 percent. The weekend’s top-earning dinosaur film has yet to be determined, as PAW Patrol : The Dino Movie is battling with The End of Oak Street for fourth place. Also in its second weekend, Paramount Pictures’ animated sequel is similarly targeting roughly $8 million to decline around 61 percent and bring its domestic tally to an estimated $34 million. Expanding to a wide release in its third weekend is A24’s Tony , starring Dominic Sessa as a teenage Anthony Bourdain. The feature serves up an estimated $4.8 million from 1,600 North American screens to claim seventh place and bring its domestic cume to around $6.4 million. The 25th-anniversary rerelease of Universal’s The Fast and the Furious pulls into eighth place with an estimated $3.3 million. The Vin Diesel vehicle grossed $207 million globally in its initial run to kick off the franchise that has a long-awaited eleventh installment in the works . Black Bear’s comedy Spa Weekend is currently in ninth place with an estimated $3 million domestically from 2,000 locations. Earning a B+ CinemaScore, directors Jon Lucas and Scott Moore’s movie stars Leslie Mann, Isla Fisher, Michelle Buteau and Anna Faris. Starring Andrew Garfield , The Magic Faraway Tree is heading for an estimated $1.15 million from 1,600 North American screens to land on the outskirts of the top 10. Vertical releases director Ben Gregor’s literary adaptation that also stars Claire Foy. Director Destin Daniel Cretton ‘s blockbuster Spider-Man: Brand New Day keeps spinning to historic heights. Tom Holland , Zendaya , Sadie Sink and Jon Bernthal star in the film that recently set the record as the fastest movie to hit $800 million domestically . After the weekend is over, only 2015’s Star Wars: Episode VII — The Force Awakens and 2019’s Avengers: Endgame will hold bigger domestic cumes. THR

articles.title: Janie Bradford, “Money (That’s What I Want)” Songwriter, Dies at 87
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 22, 2026 10:02am Janie Bradford Leon Bennett/Getty Images Janie Bradford, the onetime receptionist for Berry Gordy who co-wrote the R&B classic “Money (That’s What I Want),” the first big hit for the founder of Motown Records, has died. She was 87. Bradford died Friday at Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in Los Angeles after an extended illness, her family announced. Bradford also co-wrote “Too Busy Thinking About My Baby,” which Marvin Gaye took to No. 4 on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1969, and songs for other artists including Mary Wells, Stevie Wonder, The Temptations, the Four Tops and Martha & the Vandellas. Related Stories Movies Michael Wright, Star of 'The Five Heartbeats' and 'Sugar Hill,' Dies at 70 Movies Paul M. Pollard, Camera Man on 'Bound for Glory' and 'Heaven's Gate,' Dies at 84 She later served as head of writer relations for the Motown publishing company Jobete. Born on June 2, 1939, in Charleston, Missouri, Bradford was inspired to be a writer after her idol, poet Robert Frost, visited her high school. While living in Detroit with her sister, Clea, she became neighborhood friends with singer Jackie Wilson, who had just charted with his first solo single, the 1957 party anthem “Reet Petite.” Wilson invited her to meet Gordy, one of the song’s writers, and she gave him a collection of her poetry. After Gordy had launched the Tamla and Motown labels in 1959, he hired Bradford as a receptionist. One day, as Gordy was working on a song, Bradford joined him at the piano to add her own verse — “Your love gives me such a thrill, but your love don’t pay my bills. Gimme some money, baby!” The song, of course, would become “Money (That’s What I Want).” First recorded by Barrett Strong, it peaked at No. 23 on the Hot 100 and helped cement Tamla/Motown as hit-makers. It would be covered by The Beatles, The Rolling Stones, The Flying Lizards, The Supremes, Boyz II Men and Charli XCX, among many others. “Janie was there with me from the very beginning, before there was even a Motown, and she will always hold a very special place in my heart and in the Motown family,” Gordy said in a statement. “Janie was smart, clever, witty and fun. She was also talented and determined. In those early days, everybody did what was needed to be done, and Janie was no exception. She became Motown’s first receptionist, but her talents quickly took her far beyond that desk.” Bradford’s credits also included “Contract on Love,” recorded by Little Stevie Wonder, Wells’ “Your Old Standby,” Diana Ross’s “I Am Me” and The Supremes’ “Time Changes Things” and “We Should Be Closer Together.” After some 25 years at Motown, Bradford in the 1990s founded the Heroes and Legends Awards, an event that over 30 years honored music icons and presented scholarships to those pursuing higher education. “Her annual gatherings always felt like old home week because Janie kept that wonderful sense of family alive,” Gordy said. In June, she was inducted into the Women Songwriters Hall of Fame. Survivors include her husband of 55 years, Wardean; her children, Lance and Nicole; her daughter-in-law, Carolyn; and her grandsons, Bradford and Austin. THR

articles.title: Before ‘The Pitt,’ There Was ‘St. Elsewhere’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 22, 2026 11:30am From left: Ed Begley Jr., Cindy Pickett, Bruce Greenwood, David Morse and Denzel Washington on St. Elsewhere, which ran from 1982 to 1988 and won six Emmys in 1986. Courtesy Everett Collection Though it was never an outright hit, St. Elsewhere punched way above its weight in terms of the careers it helped launch and a style that set the template for medical dramas that followed it. The show can also boast one of the more memorable series finales in TV history. Created by Joshua Brand and John Falsey, St. Elsewhere followed the staff and patients at a struggling Boston hospital over six seasons on NBC, from 1982 to 1988. Like its fellow NBC show Hill Street Blues (both were from MTM Enterprises), St. Elsewhere pioneered a new kind of storytelling. Hospital dramas that came before it focused mainly on a lead character whose personal struggles didn’t interfere with their work and presented the health care system as orderly and well functioning (see Marcus Welby, M.D. , Trapper John, M.D. ). St. Elsewhere instead took a grittier tack, with overlapping, serialized stories and medical professionals who had complicated lives and sometimes could not save patients ­— traits that are recognizable in its successors, from ER to Grey’s Anatomy to The Pitt . Related Stories 'Awards Chatter' Podcast Emmy Nominee Patrick Ball on His Rollercoaster Journey to 'The Pitt' and How His Own Addiction Battle Has Informed His Performance TV 'Palm Royale' Went Full 'Dynasty' for Its Biggest Fight Yet When the series debuted, that style was seen as a barrier to success: Reviewing the show in November 1982, THR critic Richard Hack wrote, “So real and graphic is the drama being presented here that we cannot believe that 20 million people across this country will find it entertaining enough to flip to.” Nonetheless, St. Elsewhere would win 13 Emmys over its run, including six for its fourth season in 1986. It was nominated for best drama series in all six seasons, though it never took home that honor. Three of the show’s regulars — William Daniels, Bonnie Bartlett and Ed Flanders — won acting Emmys for their roles. Equally impressive was the show’s eye for emerging talent: It helped kick-start the careers of Denzel Washington, Mark Harmon and David Morse, as well as comedian Howie Mandel, playing against type in a dramatic role. The 1988 series finale cemented St. Elsewhere ’s place in TV lore by suggesting that the entire show may have taken place inside the imagination of Tommy Westphall (played by Chad Allen), the autistic son of Flanders’ Dr. Donald Westphall. It was perhaps the most audacious choice an already groundbreaking show ever made. This story first appeared in an August stand-alone issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. articles.title: Meghan Markle Reportedly Dropped From Consideration to Join Guy Ritchie’s ‘The Gentlemen’

Jonathan Brady-Pool/Getty Images; Matthew Towers/Netflix Meghan Markle has been dropped from consideration to join Guy Ritchie ‘s The Gentlemen , according to Tina Brown, who reported that the decision came after intense backlash in the U.K. In a column published Saturday on Substack , Brown, the former editor-in-chief of Vanity Fair and The New Yorker , wrote, “I learned this morning that the casting of Meghan Markle in season 3 of Guy Ritchie’s Netflix series The Gentlemen has been withdrawn. The backlash in the UK was so intense, it became untenable to go forward. This does not bode well for Meghan’s acting comeback in the UK.” Related Stories General News Meghan McCain Criticizes Prince Harry and Meghan Markle's U.K. Move TV Meghan Markle in Advanced Talks to Join Guy Ritchie's 'The Gentlemen' After She and Prince Harry Move Back to the U.K. The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Markle’s representative and WME, which represents both Markle and Ritchie and didn’t receive a response. THR also reached out to Brown, who said she stands by her reporting. Brown is the author of two bestselling books about the British royal family. The report comes a day after THR learned that the Duchess of Sussex was in advanced discussions to join season three of The Gentlemen , which films in the U.K. Her role was being written for the third season, which has not yet been renewed. Season two of The Gentlemen premieres Sept. 3 and stars Theo James. Ritchie, who created the series, which was adapted from his 2019 film of the same name, met Markle through mutual acquaintances, THR was told. Netflix declined to comment. Markle’s potential role in The Gentlemen would have marked the Suits star’s return to acting after she stepped away from the profession in 2017 when she got engaged to Prince Harry. The couple recently revealed that they are moving back to the U.K., with Brown reporting that Markle’s potential acting role was a significant factor in the decision. The couple also have a history with Netflix. After moving to California in 2020, Prince Harry and Markle signed an overall deal with the company, resulting in several docuseries, including Harry & Meghan , Polo, and With Love, Meghan . articles.title: Bunny Levine, Librarian Turned Actress in ‘Gilmore Girls,’ Thelma’ and ‘You Don’t Mess With the Zohan,’ Dies at 97
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 22, 2026 4:40pm Bunny Levine at the 'Thelma' premiere in 2024. Amanda Edwards/Getty Images Bunny Levine, an actress who appeared in Gilmore Girls, You Don’t Mess With the Zohan, Thelma and numerous other TV shows and films, has died. She was 97. Levine died peacefully in her sleep, her manager confirmed to The Hollywood Reporter , with NBC Los Angeles reporting that she died Thursday at her home in Tarzana, California. Born on Dec. 22, 1928, in East Orange, New Jersey, Levine developed an interest in acting at a young age. But after graduating from high school, she put those dreams on hold for 25 years while working as a school librarian and raising her three children, according to her IMDB biography . After retiring, Levine began taking acting classes and auditioning for roles. Following the death of her husband, Bernard Levine, in 2003, she moved to Los Angeles. Related Stories Music Janie Bradford, "Money (That's What I Want)" Songwriter, Dies at 87 Movies Michael Wright, Star of 'The Five Heartbeats' and 'Sugar Hill,' Dies at 70 Levine went on to build an extensive résumé of television appearances, including roles on Law & Order, Everybody Loves Raymond, Gilmore Girls , Ugly Betty, Private Practice, Criminal Minds, 2 Broke Girls, Raising Hope, Southland, New Girl, Getting On, The Mindy Project, Fuller House, Shameless and Dave. Her film credits included Slime City, The Jimmy Show, A Thousand Words, La La Land and the Adam Sandler-starring comedy You Don’t Mess With the Zohan in 2008. Levine later reunited with Sandler for Sandy Wexler in 2017 and the 2023 Netflix film You Are So Not Invited to My Bat Mitzvah . Levine continued acting into her 90s. Her more recent credits include The Invisible Raptor (2023); Michael Angarano’s Sacramento (2024), starring Kristen Stewart and Michael Cera; and Thelma (2024), starring June Squibb . She also appeared in projects released this year, including the final season of The Upshaws and The Cure. THR

articles.title: Mark Ruffalo Rejects Paramount’s Claim His Anti-Merger Comments Were “Antisemitic”: “My Views Should Never Be Interpreted as Hostility Toward Jewish People”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All August 22, 2026 5:10pm Mark Ruffalo at the AFI Awards in January. Rodin Eckenroth/Getty Images for AFI Mark Ruffalo is rejecting Paramount ‘s claim that his recent comments highlighting the role Larry Ellison’s Oracle played in the Israel-Gaza war were “antisemitic.” “The accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest,” Ruffalo wrote on X Saturday morning . “Criticizing the actions of the Israeli prime minister, a military technology contract or the executives who supply it is not the same as criticizing Jewish people. This critical and necessary dialogue is then dishonestly framed as being anti-Israel. To be clear, my views come from my own political convictions and should never be interpreted as hostility toward Jewish people, for whom I have deep love and respect. Everything I know about acting, activism and humanism has been profoundly shaped by the Jewish friends, colleagues and loved ones who have been integral and family throughout every point of my life.” Related Stories Business Mark Ruffalo Links Paramount to Oracle's Israeli Military Ties. The Studio Calls Remarks "Antisemitic" Business Gavin Newsom Says Paramount Settlement Talks Happening in "Real Time," Signals He'd Like a Deal Ruffalo, a staunch opponent to Paramount’s $111 billion deal for Warner Bros. , had recently shared on social media a clip from 2024 of former Oracle chief Safra Catz talking about “profoundly scary technologies” Oracle had built as Catz was speaking about Oracle’s tech in relation to the Israel-Gaza war. Ruffalo went on to call the war a “genocide” that “was built on an apartheid system of oppression powered by Oracle.” He added in his Instagram story that these “profoundly scary technologies” “will most likely be merged into one of the largest media conglomerates in the world” and criticized the planned Paramount-WB merger, saying moguls “are crushing workers and consolidating the wealth of the world for their own power and concentrated dominance.” Paramount issued a lengthy reply in which the company called for the temperature of the debate to be lowered and called Ruffalo’s remarks “antisemitic.” “We are, as always, troubled when antisemitic tropes are invoked in purported service of a business dispute,” the Paramount rep stated. “Words like ‘genocide’ and ‘apartheid,’ applied to a corporate transaction, aren’t just wrong — they’re a bridge too far, and they cheapen the very real suffering those words are meant to describe. This doesn’t deserve a response in kind — and to be clear, we don’t tolerate prejudice of any kind, against anyone.” Paramount added, “We understand people feel strongly about this merger and are hopeful and expect that it will be judged based on the legal merits, not underlying bias. We’re asking for the same good faith we’re extending: less rhetoric, more understanding. Paramount’s future is being written for everyone who wants to make and watch great stories.” In his response Saturday, Ruffalo sought to make a distinction between his objections to the Israeli military and his views about the Jewish people. He also argued that the merger “has real consequences for real people and for the entire country” and deserved serious scrutiny, particularly given what the deal would mean for control of CNN, HBO and other Warner Bros. assets. “Scrutinizing the Ellisons, including Oracle’s business built on data, surveillance technology and government contracts and the serious threat to editorial freedom and the loss of a livelihood for thousands of families, is fair and necessary,” Ruffalo wrote. “The $111 billion deal would hand one family control over CNN, HBO and Warner Bros., backed in part by foreign money whose influence on editorial decisions has never been fully explained to the public. Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have called for serious national security review, and regulators still haven’t given the public a real answer. Until they do, the merger shouldn’t move forward. Now is the time to dive boldly into all these issues, not step back or concede.” In his Instagram story about Oracle’s “profoundly scary technologies,” Ruffalo mentioned the ongoing antitrust lawsuit filed by 12 attorneys general, which Paramount said last week is the only thing stopping the deal from being done , now that the merger has been cleared by all global regulators. Still a number of officials, including California Governor Gavin Newsom , Attorney General Rob Bonta , California Democratic gubernatorial candidate Xavier Becerra and L.A. mayor Karen Bass , have expressed support for settlement talks, which Newsom said Friday were happening “in real time.” THR

articles.title: ‘Spa Weekend’ Review: Leslie Mann and Isla Fisher Go Underserved in a Lukewarm Bath of a Comedy
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Angie Han Plus Icon Angie Han Television Critic ajhan Follow Sign Up View All August 22, 2026 5:21pm 'Spa Weekend' Black Bear Pictures Have you ever had the experience of booking a trip that promised to be a blissful getaway, only to find once there that you’re having…not the worst time, but definitely a disappointing one? That the food that looked so pretty online tastes bland in person, that the overstuffed pillows give you neck pains, that — come to think of it — there’s not really that much to do at this resort beyond linger beside a lukewarm pool? If so, the aura of letdown surrounding Spa Weekend , the latest outing from writer-directors Jon Lucas and Scott Moore, ought to feel familiar. On paper, it’s a variation on the “R-rated hijinks plus heartfelt emotion plus beloved cast” equation that’s worked so well for Bridesmaids and Girls Trip and Lucas and Moore’s own commercially successful though creatively uninspired Bad Moms . In execution, the hijinks feel awfully tame, the emotion shallow, the stars underserved. Related Stories Movies 'Insidious: Out of the Further' Hunts Down $3M in Box Office Previews Movies Anna Faris Reveals Melania Trump Joke Cut From 'Scary Movie' Spa Weekend The Bottom Line A likable cast let down by uninteresting hijinks. Release date: Friday, Aug. 21 Cast: Leslie Mann, Isla Fisher, Michelle Buteau, Anna Faris, Adam Demos, Dominic Ona-Ariki, Erika Heynatz Director-screenwriters: Jon Lucas, Scott Moore Rated R, 1 hour 37 minutes The premise is the title, not much more and not much less. On the occasion of her she’s-not-saying-which birthday, overworked Los Angeles lawyer Jane ( Leslie Mann ) books a two-night stay at a wellness retreat seemingly around Malibu, though the Australia-shot production avoids getting too geographically specific. (Wherever it is, the sunsets are very pretty.) Along with her for the ride are her two childhood besties — sweet-natured Sophie ( Anna Faris ), who’s withering under a boss so spoiled he can’t even buy his own Skittles, and hot-tempered Coco ( Michelle Buteau ), who’s working through a painful divorce while stubbornly not working through the anger management issues that led to it. The trip promises to be precisely the break all three of them desperately need but cannot ever seem to take, because as working moms pulled every which way by ailing parents, needy kids and demanding jobs, these women cannot imagine planning so much as a date night less than three months in advance. They could certainly never do something so self-indulgent as book a whole trip on a whim — except that that’s exactly what we’ve just seen them do, within five minutes of Coco floating the idea over brunch. I presume the whiplash-inducing speed with which the trio go from “Oh, I couldn’t possibly” to “We’ve booked the room” is meant to be aspirational: Here are women finally saying “screw it” to a society that demands they put everyone else first, and taking care of themselves for once! But it has the condescending effect of suggesting that their struggles were never real to begin with. The only thing ever actually holding them back, apparently, was their own lack of willpower. Well, that and, in some roundabout way, their lack of appreciation for the unwanted fourth member of their circle. Mel ( Isla Fisher ), who’s only scored a last-minute pity invite thanks to Sophie’s guilty conscience, is “the one woman all the others secretly cannot stand” — you know, that thing Spa Weekend assures us every female friend group always has. If you can’t identify who that might be in your own girl gang, maybe that’s because it’s you. Or maybe it’s because Spa Weekend has a habit of treating all its characters’ problems as universal and therefore inherently relatable and interesting. You can practically hear the “Am I right, ladies?” after every such observation. In fairness to Jane, Coco and Sophie, their distaste initially proves warranted. From the moment Mel bursts onto the property — boobs spilling out of her pushup bra, dildos spilling out of her suitcase, inappropriate language spilling out of her mouth — she brings nothing but chaos. When she’s around, a guided meditation session devolves into a shouting match, a chill evening into a cocaine-fueled rager, a short walk between spa treatments into, somehow, a wild golf cart chase. None of it is anything you haven’t seen before, and in Lucas and Scott’s ineffectual hands, none of it gets as nasty or raunchy or destructive as those descriptions suggest. What’s more, Mel can’t seem to stop meddling in her friends’ live. She swipes Sophie’s phone to scream at her shitty boss. She tricks Coco’s ex (Dominic Ora-Ariki’s Roger) into rushing to her side. She baldly propositions Adam Demos’ hot yoga instructor on Jane’s behalf (“Obviously she’s on the older side, but she’s got a porno body!”). Her behavior is upsetting and mortifying and potentially life-destroying to all her friends until it’s not, as Spa Weekend slowly but predictably gets around to the argument that the world needs Mels — the hot messes who force everyone else out of their miserable but societally approved ruts. It would be a very nice message, if not for the fact that the script undercuts it by keeping all its characters too vague and one-dimensional to care much about in any direction; I couldn’t even tell you what Coco does for a living or why Jane’s raising her kids alone. To the extent that there are any genuine chuckles or warm fuzzies to be found in Spa Weekend , it’s thanks to skills this talented core cast have deployed more effectively elsewhere. A pretty funny scene in which Jane tries very hard to pretend she’s not extremely turned on by Demos’ Kai giving her a hand massage called to my mind the even funnier ones of Mann smiling through her tears in Blockers . Coco’s smooth, sexy chemistry with Roger made me want to revisit Buteau’s winsome turn as a heartbroken stylist in Netflix’s Survival of the Thickest . Fisher earns most of the film’s few real laughs by channeling the upbeat yet unhinged energy that’s served her so well since her breakout in Wedding Crashers . Even Faris’ miscast turn as awkward, mousy Sophie served to remind me how much more delightful she is when she gets to go weird and messy, as in The House Bunny or Smiley Face . But the ability to occasionally evoke other, better projects does not a good film make. Spa Weekend has nothing fresh or insightful or even all that amusing to add to the familiar formula it’s borrowing — and for all its apparent good intentions, nothing much more meaningful to offer the overworked, overstressed moms of the world than the suggestion that maybe they could, like, try taking a vacation sometime. If this is what a big relaxing escape looks like, you’re better off saving the money and chilling at home. Full credits Distributor: Black Bear Pictures Production company: Black Bear Pictures Cast: Leslie Mann, Isla Fisher, Michelle Buteau, Anna Faris, Adam Demos, Dominic Ona-Ariki, Erika Heynatz Director-screenwriters: Jon Lucas, Scott Moore Producers: Suzanne Todd, John Friedberg, Teddy Schwarzman, Michael Heimler Executive producers: Troy Lum, Andrew Mason Director of photography: Danny Ruhlmann Production designer: Michelle McGahey Costume designer: Vanessa Loh Editor: James Thomas Music: Philip White Casting director: Kirsty McGregor Rated R, 1 hour 37 minutes THR

articles.title: ‘National Treasure 3’ Is “Finally Real” and “We Have a Script,” Director Says
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 22, 2026 6:11pm From left: Diane Kruger, Justin Bartha and Nicolas Cage in 'National Treasure: Book of Secrets.' Walt Disney Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Get ready for another treasure hunt: A third National Treasure movie is happening, according to director Jon Turteltaub. Speaking at a live taping of the National Treasure Hunt podcast Friday night in Philadelphia, Turteltaub said, “It’s happening. You’re the first people I’ve said this out loud to. I have not said anything before this, but you deserve to have the scoop. It’s finally real. Now, it’s ‘Hollywood real,’ meaning things could happen. Nic [Cage] gets hit by a bus, there’s no National Treasure 3. If I get hit by a bus, there’s probably a National Treasure 3. Welcome to Hollywood.” Related Stories Business Disney Strikes Content Deal With Dhar Mann Studios TV ABC Sues FCC Over Threats to Broadcast Licenses in First Amendment Case “We finally have a script that I like,” he said before adding before revealing that Disney said, “OK, this sounds like a movie we can make.” The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Disney for comment and they declined. The franchise later expanded to television with National Treasure: Edge of History , which premiered on Disney+ in 2022 but was canceled after one season. Catherine Zeta-Jones joined the cast, while Bartha and Keitel reprised their roles. As for the third feature, no casting has been announced. THR reached out to Cage’s representative for comment.
