articles.title: ‘Outer Banks’ Creators Break Down Season 5’s “Earned” Ending, Supernatural Lean & JJ’s Presence
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News California Film & TV Tax Credits In Peril As Sacramento Deal Falls Apart: Exclusive Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Trouble In Paradise: John Ross Bowie & Brian Posehn On Who Ruined Utopia In ‘Stuart Fails’ E5 ‘Outer Banks’ Creators Break Down Season 5’s “Earned” Ending, Supernatural Lean & JJ’s Presence Dave Bautista Set To Play Kratos In ‘God Of War’ As Amazon Series Recasts Lead View All August 20, 2026 3:35pm From left: Carlacia Grant, Jonathan Daviss, Madelyn Cline, Drew Starkey, Madison Bailey and Chase Stokes in 'Outer Banks' Netflix SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Season 5 of Netflix ‘s Outer Banks . There were a lot of full-circle elements in the fifth and final season of Outer Banks . The series ended the way it started, with a hurricane. Sarah (Madelyn Cline) wore a version of her iconic Midsummers white dress from Season 1 to her wedding to John B (Chase Stokes) in the series finale where the two recited the vows she used for their impromptu nuptials on the open seas in Season 2. And the Pogues, in the same lineup as their very first treasure hunt (sans the late JJ), went on one final adventure together in Azerbaijan. Related Stories News All The Songs In ‘Outer Banks’ Season 5: Tame Impala, Stevie Wonder & More News ‘Outer Banks’ Season 5 Finale: How Things End For Pogues, Kooks & Twinkie As John B & Co Sign Off It wasn’t your typical Outer Banks season: there were three proposals — two by Pope (Jonathan Daviss) to Cleo (Carlacia Grant), one by Rafe (Drew Starkey) to Sofia (Fiona Palomo), a wedding (Sarah and John B) and a baby, as the couple welcomed a son whom, as expected, they named JJ, after their beloved friend who was supposed to be the baby’s godfather. Watch on Deadline The show leaned into the supernatural, too, with Kiara, JJ’s father Chandler Groff (J. Anthony Crane) and rich collector Finch all chasing Blackbeard’s Blue Crown to try and resurrect a loved one: JJ; Groff’s wife (and JJ’s mother), whom he had killed; and Finch’s young daughter, respectively. (Groff also senselessly killed JJ, but he didn’t seem to feel remorse over that.) Holding the crown, Kiara did see JJ under a meteor shower, but it was her memories of him. The season also had a revenge thriller vibe as, in her grief, Kiara went full Kill Bill on Groff, chasing him down to murder him, which she did on her second try. Ultimately, it was a happy ending for the Pogues who were able to get back one of the many treasures they had discovered only to see them being taken away – the Royal Merchant gold — which they recovered from the ocean floor after the boat Groff and Kiara were on sunk in the hurricane. Kiara managed to stay afloat while waiting for the Pogues to rescue her as she found herself in calm waters under the eye of the storm. This was the second time she cheated death, having been sent to the bottom of the ocean by Groff in an earlier episode, summoning JJ for help both times. With the money from the gold, the Pogues “rebuilt the island the way it should be so all of us, Kooks and Pogues, could live there… forever,” as John B said at the end of the finale. On the new Kildare, Kooks largely bailed out, Pogues moved in, Pope and Cleo settled into his ancestral home, Tannyhill, and Topper is a bartender. In an interview with Deadline, Outer Banks creators Josh Pate , Jonas Pate and Shannon Burke discuss the ending, what parts of it they had conceived years ago and what elements they had added more recently. They also answer burning questions about the fate of some characters, including what happened to Rafe and Sofia, and whether Sarah and Rafe’s stepmother Rose got any of the gold she had kept until Groff stole it from her. Each Outer Banks character had their own ending, many of which converged at John B and Sarah’s wedding . The trio also explain whether they ever considered bringing JJ back from the dead or have Rudy Pankow reprise his role in any way, if they thought of killing off another Pogue and why Groff was so unredeemable. As part of the interview, Josh and Jonas Pate and Burke also revealed that a prequel set 20 years prior , which features the Outer Banks parents’ generation, is in active development at Netflix. “It really is the story of how the island split — and it’s particularly relevant in our country right now — how it split into the haves and have-nots, how the Kooks and the Pogues started,” Josh Pate said . “How did this rift start?” Below, they tease another possible spinoff. Ending on a Win DEADLINE: Let’s start with with the ending. You said after Season 4 that you’re “bringing it all home.” Is this what you envision, building a Kildare utopia with Kooks and Pogues living in harmony? JONAS PATE : Yes. JOSH PATE : I don’t think the Kooks are there anymore. I think the Kooks have all been kind of driven off. JONAS PATE : No, no, no. There are some, maybe we have a disagreement on that. But I think it’s the happiest ending you could possibly have. Everybody’s there living together. We had lost for 49 straight episodes, so we feel like we earned the happy ending. JOSH PATE : I agree. I think it’s a happy ending, and that’s what we wanted it to be — as happy as we could make it, given everything that had happened in the story. DEADLINE: Is this ending in the ballpark of what you had envisioned from the beginning, from when you created the show? BURKE : It is. Many elements of the final sequence, we discussed at the end of Season 1. DEADLINE: Like Sarah and John B’s wedding? BURKE : Yeah, all that. Tannyhill going to Pope. We sort of knew that it got some traction after Season 1, so we long-arced it from there. So we knew this is where we were going the whole time. JONAS PATE : And bookending with a hurricane, getting an ending with a hurricane. That was pretty much an original idea because [the series] starts with a hurricane. DEADLINE: I thought you were going to end it with the Pogues on the beach after the storm and recreate that power outage photo that became the inspiration for the show. Did you think about ending the series with that shot? JOSH PATE : No, that’s a good question, though. I wish you’d been around. That’s a great idea. JONAS PATE : Do you want to be on the writers staff for the prequel? DEADLINE: Was there anything in the ending that changed from the way you had originally planned it? JOSH PATE : I think Rafe was a big change. I don’t think that at the beginning we had thought that Rafe would be as big a character as he became, as much as we started to really like Drew. Would you guys say that’s fair? I think that evolved. JONAS PATE : Yeah, and I’d say Pope and Cleo. Both of them had real distinct journeys over this year particularly and I would say that that is more reacting to what happened to Pope in the final episode of the last season and just following it through. Drew Starkey as Rafe in ‘Outer Banks’ Season 5 Jackson Lee Davis/Netflix Where in the World Is Rafe? DEADLINE: Speaking of Rafe, was it deliberate that we never heard from him again? He was supposed to send the gang a postcard from Rio, that didn’t happen. He and Sofia left literally with just the shirts on their backs. Where are they? Are they in South America? JOSH PATE : That is another spinoff possibility. JONAS PATE : In the credits, you see a video call from Rafe at the wedding. DEADLINE: Yes, but we still didn’t get an update. Did he and Sofia get a cut from the gold? JOSH PATE : Good question. I don’t know. We sort of felt like just Rafe not being arrested for murder, that’s his win. He’s not in jail for the rest of his life. DEADLINE: Still, it feels sad for him not being able to walk his sister down the aisle. BURKE : The intent was, it felt like as good as you could possibly get for someone who was so bad for a lot of the series. It was as realistic as you can get with him being as bad as he had been, and so we wanted to thread the needle where he had to pay to some extent. He’s exiled, but he does get a second chance. Death Does Not Become Pogues DEADLINE: After JJ’s death in the Season 4 finale, did you consider killing off another Pogue in Season 5? You flirted with Kiara, who came very close to dying twice . JONAS PATE : Josh, we never thought of killing anybody else, do you remember? JOSH PATE : I never recall any. I didn’t want to kill anybody, I don’t want anyone else to die. JONAS PATE : I didn’t think so either. I was just trying to think, like, ‘Did we ever think about it?’ I don’t think so either. Though I would say that something’s thought about at all times. Like, you always consider, everything’s thought of at some point. Madison Bailey as Kiara in ‘Outer Banks’ Sesaon 5 Jackson Lee Davis/Netflix OGs-Only Treasure Hunt DEADLINE: In Season 5, Cleo was sidelined in the Bahamas twice. For the trip to Azerbaijan, Rafe also had a reason to stay, so the Pogues went after the Blue Crown in their original formation (sans JJ). it felt like a throwback to Season 1 and one last adventure for the OGs. Was it intentional? JOSH PATE : Yeah, I think we’re trying to chime some old vibes, classic OBX vibes on some of this season. BURKE : And also it gave Cleo a real singular moment where she did something at the end of eight on the runway, and it also set up finishing the Pope and Cleo story. But yeah, it felt good to have just the OG Pogues on one adventure. Jonas, what do you think about that? JONAS PATE : Yeah, I liked it. I mean, the whole show, honestly, was such a blessing to shoot. The process of making it was so much fun for all of us that I think that we wanted to make sure we experienced all those types of things that we had felt over the course of the season. So it was a little bit of adventure, a little bit of stuff in their home on their home turf. We tried to, as Josh said, chime all the old school, the old versions that we had done in the final season, just to make fans feel satisfied. L-R: Chase Stokes as John B, Madelyn Cline as Sarah Cameron in ‘Outer Banks’ Season 5 Jackson Lee Davis/Netflix Twinkie Lives On DEADLINE: You mentioned Cleo’s heroics, which included blowing up John B’s beloved VW van Twinkie. It made a return , first in the form of Sarah and John B’s wedding cake, and then as their Just Married van. Was this the refurbished original one or a new incarnation of Twinkie? JONAS PATE : Nellie, you really watched this, I appreciate that. It was a new incarnation of Twinkie, which is not easy to find. Over the course of the season, I think there were seven, because they kept breaking down. We had to keep replacing them. Outer Banks or Outer Realm DEADLINE: Blue Crown’s supposed powers. Why did you decide to introduce the element of immortality and did you consider at any point taking a supernatural route and bringing JJ or somebody else back to life? JOSH PATE : Actually, there’s a similar supernatural element in earlier seasons with [Carla] Limbrey. We always knew that the show was not a supernatural show but some people believe supernatural things in the world, and these kids could believe in these myths without us actually crossing the line into actual magic, which we never wanted to do. JONAS PATE : But we felt like, to your point, Josh, it’s human to be superstitious, right? I mean, that’s what a lot of religion is. So we never thought about crossing the line, but we knew that we could have characters that could believe in those types of things, and it could motivate their actions. BURKE : And we wanted to walk right up to the edge of that line, to the point of where some people believed that it was supernatural, and some people didn’t. We wanted to get right up to the edge of that line, but then not cross it. DEADLINE: So the ball of light, was it just a natural phenomenon? Because it wasn’t just Kiara; Finch, Groff and others also believed in the crown’s powers. BURKE : I would say in the staff or the people who are on this phone call that some people here thought it was supernatural, and some people thought it wasn’t. Would you say that’s true, guys? Because I said not supernatural, and I think Jonas said it wasn’t, and Josh, I don’t know what you say. JOSH PATE : I don’t think it was. I mean, it was a meteor shower. But again, two people can see the same thing, like a lightning bolt, and one can take it in a supernatural, spiritual way, as a sign or a message, and someone else can just be like, “Oh, it’s a lightning bolt.” People can interpret those two things differently. So, I think there are characters in the show that are on both sides of that fence, and all you have to do is show. It is coincidental? Well, they knew that there was a meteor shower. There was an incredible video that was captured online of this blue light during a meteor shower that basically was the template for the way we did that. That was real, so we didn’t push it that much if you’ve actually seen this one video of this girl underneath a meteor shower. Chase Stokes as John B, Rudy Pankow as JJ in ‘Outer Banks Jackson Lee Davis/Netflix © 2024 JJ’s Presence DEADLINE: So there was no consideration of bringing back JJ at any point, right? BURKE : Not in any corporeal, like not as a real person, but maybe in a dream sequence, sort of as it was. DEADLINE: But even in the flashbacks, you had younger actors portraying JJ and Kiara’s early years. Was there a conversation with Rudy to come back? JOSH PATE : Honestly, not really. We always knew we wanted to show when they first met. I don’t know, maybe glancingly, but it never got very serious. DEADLINE: In another natural-adjacent phenomenon, Kiara found herself in the eye of a hurricane when she fell overboard, which likely saved her life. It was a beautiful moment but was this supposed to be just symbolic or do we think JJ helped? BURKE : It’s what you think. Like Josh said, it’s walking right up the line, and you can think one thing or the other. Probably everyone is going to look at that and have a different interpretation. Did he really help or was it just that the eye of a storm passed over? DEADLINE: Do you have the answer? JONAS PATE : I guess I know what I think, but that’s not… . JOSH PATE : I think I know what Kara thinks. DEADLINE: What does she think? JOSH PATE : She thinks JJ helped her. Legalizing the Gold DEADLINE: I am a little confused how Rose couldn’t legalize the Royal Merchant gold for so long, and our guys did it in no time, becoming very rich. JOSH PATE : Shan, you want to take that one? Nellie, you’re just grinding us here. BURNE : We’d have to look that up. In maritime law, if you find it on land, there’s different laws. They were saying that before it was found in someone’s house, they didn’t own that house. The gold goes to the person who is from the house, but now that’s a treasure that they found underwater. That’s a maritime treasure, and I think it goes to them. But I’d have to check that to make sure. It’s a good question. But until proven otherwise, it’s because they found it in water, not on land. DEADLINE: Well, they didn’t have witnesses, so I don’t think anybody knows where they found it. And the gold was on land before getting on that boat but OK, I’m not going to go down that rabbit hole. JONAS PATE : In the scene between Rafe and Rose, she says that Ward hadn’t bought the Crain House yet, and they would backdate the sale that so when he found it, that’s his, that it came with the property. Rose Gold DEADLINE: Speaking of Rose, the Pogues rightfully scoffed when she asked them to bring her back some gold for a cut. But then we saw her at the wedding, and she kissed John B. So are they on good terms? Did she get any money out of the gold? JOSH PATE : I love these questions. I don’t think so. What do you think, Shan? BURKE : I don’t think so. I think she has hooked up with another rich guy on Outer Banks, and she’s okay. We wanted to be gracious with everybody. Like, they had some contentious relationships but they still grew up with her, she’s part of Sarah’s family, and it’s a happy ending. Everyone’s more or less on good terms. But yeah, I don’t think she got the gold. Outer Banks. Tony Crane as Groff in ‘Outer Banks’ Season 5 Jackson Lee Davis/Netflix “Seductive Charmer” DEADLINE: Rose seemed like a good, reasonable parental figure until she hooked up with Groff. Who in their right mind would associate themselves with somebody like him? JOSH PATE : I think old Tony is a seductive charmer. JONAS PATE : I mean, If you see watch the whole show, you see all the bad sides of him. JOSH PATE : Shannon and I are, we always described the character of Groff as “tennis handsome.” DEADLINE: Groff is one of the most irredeemable characters I’ve ever seen on TV. Did you try to humanize him, or was he just there for us to hate him? JONAS PATE : We like the good villain, right? JOSH PATE : We toyed with it, and there were elements that we wanted to soften. I think he’s just got a deep psychopathology that’s going on. There was this book called Blood Will Out that our buddy Walter Kirn wrote. It’s about this sociopathic guy who imitates a Rockefeller, he murders somebody, and Walter, who’d befriended him, goes to see him in prison after he’s been convicted of murder. And he’s like, “Okay, man, you lied to me about everything, and you f*cking killed somebody. And the guy looks right at Walter and goes like, “I didn’t kill him.” He’s still lying. That’s what we just kept thinking about. Like, wow, this guy can really go all the way. BURKE : There’s that moment where he has the painting of Larissa, he’s talking to Larissa. I don’t think he’s redeemed, but I think it’s explicable that his original sin is that he married up into Larissa’s family, and then he ends up killing her, and then he’s trying to go back to reverse this thing that he did initially. He’s obviously insane, he’s gone crazy, so not redeemed in any way, but maybe explicable? From left: Austin North as Topper (golfing), Drew Starkey as Rafe, Jason Davis as Dale, Mia Challis as Ruthie in ‘Outer Banks’ Season 5 Jackson Lee Davis/Netflix The Case Of The Disappearing Kooks DEADLINE: Can you explain how the Kooks disappeared somehow, and how in the world is Topper now a bartender? Don’t the Kooks have wealth? BURKE : Well, even wealthy people – they still work as bartenders, they have trouble. The intent was to soften him, to make him more relatable, like he’s actually learned something. JOSH PATE : I think he’s been excommunicated from his parents a little bit too. He’s had a lot of trouble with his mom and dad, so maybe he got cut off and has to support himself now as a bartender. But again, yeah, to make him a little bit more likable, as Shannon would say. DEADLINE: But Kooks still live there, they are just not as rich as they were? There seems to be a clear shift in the dynamic on the island . JOSH PATE : I think the Kooks abandoned the island after the hurricane to a large extent because the island’s destroyed, and what’s happened in the coastal Carolinas is, you can’t get insurance anymore. So they’ll pay you back, but they won’t let you rebuild, and that’s kind of it. Kind of like what’s happening in LA, and so I think, the post-hurricane island returns to more a poorer version of the island. Acknowledgments DEADLINE: Any final thoughts about your Outer Banks journey and ending the show on your own terms? JOSH PATE : We feel really a lot of gratitude to being allowed to end the show in the way we wanted to. A lot of gratitude to Netflix, to Ted [Sarandos] and Bela [Bajaria] and Nne [Ebong], who believed in the show from the beginning, and they largely let us tell the story that we wanted to. So, you’ve been around Hollywood long enough to know that you rarely get to end on your own terms. So, we feel a lot of gratitude for that. Camila Morrone Stars In ‘Miami Vice ’85’ With Michael B. articles.title: Trouble In Paradise: John Ross Bowie & Brian Posehn On Who Ruined Utopia In ‘Stuart Fails’ E5
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Trouble In Paradise: John Ross Bowie & Brian Posehn On Who Ruined Utopia In ‘Stuart Fails’ E5 ‘Outer Banks’ Creators Break Down Season 5’s “Earned” Ending, Supernatural Lean & JJ’s Presence Dave Bautista Set To Play Kratos In ‘God Of War’ As Amazon Series Recasts Lead View All August 20, 2026 6:30pm Brian Posehn, John Ross Bowie, Kevin Sussman in 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' ABC SPOILER ALERT: The story includes details about Episode 5 of HBO Max ‘s Stuart Fails To Save the Universe . In Episode 5 of Big Bang Theory spinoff Stuart Fails To Save the Universe, our quartet of inter-dimensional travelers Stuart Bloom ( Kevin Sussman ), Denise ( Lauren Lapkus ), Bert ( Brian Posehn ) and Barry Kripke ( John Ross Bowie ), land in a tropical paradise inhabited by a primitive tribe of scantly-clothed beautiful people living in a commune where they share everything — food, shelter, and sexual partners. All goes well until Kripke introduces the concept of possession and free market, leading to tribe members, who had been living in harmony, turning on each other and getting into fights, with him feigning innocence that he has no idea how the turmoil started. Related Stories Ratings 'Lanterns' Premieres Among HBO Max's Top Titles, Besting DC Studios Predecessor 'The Penguin' Casting 'The Pitt' Adds 7 To Season 3 Recurring Cast It’s probably fitting that it was Kripke who destroyed utopia. However, “Chuck brought up a point earlier today, saying that Bert has a little hand in that by bringing monogamy into their world, like maybe he should have never done that,” Posehn said in an interview with Deadline, referencing Chuck Lorre, co-creator of Stuart Fails To Save the Universe alongside Bill Prady and Zak Penn. Added Bowie, “Yeah, it’s funny because we have been collectively all blaming Kripke for introducing the free market to paradise, but yeah, Burt holds some responsibility for introducing monogamy as well.” In the episode, Bert is immediately propositioned by one of the gorgeous local women, who quickly becomes his girlfriend, stopping to sleep with others upon Bert’s request as they are headed to the altar. “It felt that episode was incredibly fun to shoot because we like joke-wise, it’s just one killer joke after another in that show,” Bowie said. “But also, it made kind of perfect sense that Kripke would be a big part of bringing down Utopia. And then the way that he completely shirked responsibility at the end — that sense of like, wow, what got into these guys? That was really great. And that cast, oh my God! They found all these beautiful people who were all really funny, all these like gorgeous people who would come in and land jokes, and it was incredible to watch.” Five episodes in, Bert has had the coolest arc of the main characters — from turning commando in Episode 1 to bring mayhem to Caltech and then kicking Kripke’s butt after he’d killed Raj, to doing magic and having a posse of adoring acolytes in Episode 3 to landing a stunning girlfriend in Episode 5. Posehn is loving it. “Well, just getting Bert to do more was already a dream,” he said. “But then the stuff they put me through in the first season was so fun. Every week there was something new, some new thing that I went home to my wife and said, ‘Holy shi*, you won’t believe what Bert’s doing this week.'” Added Bowie, “Well, you were both a fighter and a lover, and that was fun to watch.” Stuart Fails To Save The Universe has been renewed for a second season. articles.title: ‘Outer Banks’ Star Madison Bailey On Show’s “Lack Of Queer Representation,” Desire To Play LGBTQ Role: “I’ve Been Manifesting It”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Chris Hansen Was Turned Away From ‘Primetime’ Screening After Refusing To Sign Standard NDA, Not “Sign Away” His Rights ‘Outer Banks’ Star Madison Bailey On Show’s “Lack Of Queer Representation,” Desire To Play LGBTQ Role: “I’ve Been Manifesting It” ‘Blue Eye Samurai’ Renewed For Third & Final Season At Netflix; Season 2 Gets Premiere Window — Watch The Teaser View All August 20, 2026 7:07pm Madison Bailey attends 'Outer Banks' Season 5 Presents "Pogues For Life: A Fan Farewell" on Aug. 15, 2026 in Los Angeles, California. JC Olivera/PMC With Outer Banks coming to an end, Madison Bailey wants to spread her wings as she contemplates the future of her career. The openly pansexual actress recently discussed the “lack of queer representation” on the Netflix show, which released its fifth and final season on Thursday, revealing that she wishes her character Kiara came out as LGBTQ on the show, and she wants to play a queer character next. “It’s never too late! It’s literally never too late,” she told OUT . “Especially with the lack of queer representation on this show, I’m really happy that people can still connect to it via me in real life and can connect through the actor, and I can represent off-screen.” Related Stories News ‘Outer Banks’ Creators Break Down Season 5’s “Earned” Ending, Supernatural Lean & JJ’s Presence Red Carpet Premieres ‘Outer Banks’ Final Season Red Carpet: Madelyn Cline, Drew Starkey, Madison Bailey & More Bailey added, “There’s definitely themes that are relatable, especially with the found family and choosing your community and rebelling and picking your own friends, there are things to relate to. Your community has and will always have your back through every hardship that we face. Just remember that your community will always protect you and we will always ride for each other.” Watch on Deadline As for whether she’ll get a chance to play an LGBTQ character in the future, Bailey teased, “Can I tease that moodboard might be coming to life right now in real time? It’s on the way! I’ve been manifesting it. ‘Outer Banks’ Netflix “I’ve wanted to represent on-screen for a long time and I think I might have an opportunity to do so,” added Bailey. “I don’t want it to be theatric and sad, and I don’t want it to be a dark sad story. I want happy. I want joy. We need to put the community on screen.” Season 5 of Outer Banks , now streaming on Netflix, finds the Pogues at their absolute breaking point following the tragic loss of JJ (Rudy Pankow) in Morocco. Stranded far from home and mourning the heart of their crew, they’ve lost the Blue Crown and continue to face a gauntlet of familiar threats as they seek to avenge JJ’s death and reclaim their future. articles.title: ‘Free Nelson Mandela’ Maker Rogan Productions Opens South Africa Office & Tweaks Management Set Up
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News California Film & TV Tax Credits In Peril As Sacramento Deal Falls Apart: Exclusive Read the full story By Jesse Whittock , Jake Kanter August 21, 2026 1:35am Soleta and James Rogan Rogan Productions EXCLUSIVE: Fresh off producing Channel 4’s Free Nelson Mandela , Rogan Productions has opened an office in South Africa. The new unit, Rogan South Africa , will be a production base in Johannesburg with close links to Cape Town. This marks the first permanent international expansion for the 13-year-old London-based company. At the same time, Rogan is tweaking its management set-up with founders James and Soleta Rogan taking on co-CEO titles, as well as leading Rogan SA as they search for a local senior producer. The pair has jointly led Rogan since launch, but to this point Soleta Rogan has been Managing Director and James Rogan the Creative Director. Mark Hedgecoe is Head of Rogan Scotland in Glasgow, but is moving to STV in October, with a replacement being sought. Related Stories News David Bowie's Final Decade To Be Celebrated In Documentary Feature From Channel 4, Rogan & Dogwoof News BBC Marking Five Years Since George Floyd's Death With Feature Doc Soleta and James Rogan have close ties with South Africa and their recent three-part doc series Free Nelson Mandela was a well-reviewed look at the life of the anti-apartheid campaigner and political prisoner who became the country’s first Black president in 1992. BBC Studios is shopping it internationally. Watch on Deadline Rogan also produced Original Sin: My Son the Killer for now-defunct South African streamer Showmax. The feature doc, co-produced with fellow UK firm Electric Shadow Company in association with Brazil’s Red Earth and South Africa’s Combined Artists, follows Thea Pretorius, mother of Gerhard Jansen van Vuuren, who murdered his girlfriend Andrea Venter in front of her neighbours, security guards and CCTV cameras in 2011 and then escaped two years later just before his trial. “South Africa has always inspired and captivated us with its deep creativity and extraordinary stories so setting up a base here has been a long-held ambition for us,” said James Rogan. “Whether in drama or documentary, there are world class filmmakers in South Africa, that we are looking forward to working with, and new platforms that are showcasing the brilliance and the potential of African stories. Rogan SA connects us to a storytelling tradition that is hugely powerful and it is an exciting next step on our creative and commercial journey.” Rogan’s productions include Boom Box: Beats and Betrayal for HBO Max, Bowie: The Final Act for Film4/Channel 4, and BAFTA winners Grenfell: Uncovered for Netflix and Uprising for the BBC. “With our broader footprint, Rogan is afforded the scope to deliver more stories in more formats, to more audiences,” said Soleta Rogan. “This has been an aim we have been actively working towards for the past couple of years, with the idea first being ruminated long before that. Opening in a territory that holds a personal connection is a real moment of celebration for us, and we look forward to delivering shows from our widened slate in the future.” Camila Morrone Stars In ‘Miami Vice ’85’ With Michael B. articles.title: ‘Earle Meets World’ Trailer Goes Inside Alix Earle’s Dramatic, Rumor-Filled Year: “Nothing Is Off Limits”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 19, 2026 3:46pm Netflix's 'Earle Meets World' Courtesy of Netflix Logo text “It’s a family business,” reads the tagline for Alix Earle ‘s upcoming reality show, Earle Meets World. Premiering on Netflix next month, the eight-episode series from Fulwell Entertainment follows the influencer as she navigates life with her blended family. The cast includes Ashtin Earle, TJ Earle, Alisa Earle, Ashley Earle, Izabel Earle, Penelope Earle, Thomas Earle, Todd (Alisa’s boyfriend) and Sally Carden (Alix’s best friend). On Wednesday, Netflix released the full trailer for Earle Meets World , following the teaser and first-look photos unveiled last month . The series promises an unfiltered look at Earle’s life after she rose to fame on TikTok in 2022 for posting “Get Ready With Me” videos while attending the University of Miami. Related Stories Next Big Thing Jonathan Daviss Thinks You Will Be Surprised With His Post-'Outer Banks' Role TV Witney Carson Answers Burning 'DWTS' Questions After Pregnancy Announcement, Chats 'Next Pro' The trailer shows Earle dealing with her breakup from ex-boyfriend and NFL player Braxton Berrios, opening up about how she learned of her mother Alisa’s cancer diagnosis and navigating how the family remains close following her father TJ’s affair. “There’s such a different side of my life that people don’t get to see,” Earle says. And the trailer also hints at an answer to questions about Earle’s fallout with Call Her Daddy host Alex Cooper . “She’s trying to paint it as, I’m just this crazy lunatic who is hating her for no reason. There’s a reason,” Earle says in the trailer. Earle signed with Cooper’s Unwell Network in 2023 and launched the Hot Mess podcast under the company. Her departure from Unwell was announced in 2025, sparking speculation about what happened between the two. Cooper addressed Earle in a TikTok posted in April, challenging her to come out and say what happened. Earle later revealed that she planned to discuss the fallout on Earle Meets World rather than on social media. The trailer also pokes fun at the romance rumors surrounding Earle and seven-time Super Bowl champion Tom Brady. Dancing With the Stars pro Jenna Johnson jokes about the speculation, pretending to call Brady and saying, “Tom? Come over, cutie.” Earle and Brady were seen dancing together, with Earle also seen rubbing his back, at a club in St. Barts on New Year’s Eve. They were later spotted dancing together at a Super Bowl party in February. Earle previously teased the possibility of a reality series in an October interview with The Hollywood Reporter , saying, “It’s something we’re talking about a lot as a family. There’s a lot of fun banter and behind the scenes people haven’t seen yet. I love that I get to share experiences with my family. I think they’re such amazing, fun characters that if we ever did something, it would be amazing.” Here’s the official synopsis for Earle Meets World : “Gen-Z’s ultimate It Girl, Alix Earle, is making the next big jump in her career. Can she balance her burgeoning business empire with being that unfiltered, twenty-something, hot mess that America fell in love with? Now she’s taking her candid chaos from your FYP to TV … and nothing is off limits.” Executive producers include Ben Winston, Paul Loban and Charlie Van Vleet for Fulwell Entertainment, as well as Trish Gold and Ally Gasparian. David Grutman’s DGN Studios is also producing, with Evan Rosenfeld serving as an executive producer. Earle Meets World premieres Sept. 4 on Netflix. All eight episodes, which run approximately 45 minutes each, will be released at once. THR

articles.title: Ariana Grande Granted Expedited Subpoena in Lawsuit Over Leaked Music
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 19, 2026 4:05pm Ariana Grande attends the 83rd Annual Golden Globe Awards at The Beverly Hilton on January 11, 2026 in Beverly Hills, California. Monica Schipper/Getty Images Logo text Ariana Grande has been granted expedited discovery in the pop star’s lawsuit over hackers stealing her unreleased music and photos, according to court documents filed in Los Angeles on Wednesday. Grande first filed her lawsuit against unnamed John Does in July , alleging that hackers had targeted devices of people in her inner circle to steal unreleased music, photos and other materials, subsequently selling the content online on the “dark web for significant sums of money.” Grande’s team filed a request for expedited third-party deposition subpoenas shorter than the usual required waiting period, noting that her team has “identified certain Internet platforms and third-party entities whose services were used to perpetrate the illegal dissemination and transactions, and which are believed to have information and data that will allow Plaintiff to identify and unmask these unknown Defendants.” The court granted that request, noting that “it makes little sense to wait” given that Grande doesn’t have any specific defendants to serve. “And on the merits of the motion, good cause is shown,” judge Mark H. Epstein ruled on Wednesday. “The 20 day waiting period will never run because plaintiff cannot — even with reasonable diligence — discovery the defendant’s identity without this discovery, and therefore will never be able to serve defendants.” Grande said she’s been the victim of this hacking campaign for years, noting that in 2023, as many as 45 of her unreleased songs leaked online. Among the songs that have leaked are “Fantasize,” “That Bitch Is Mine” and “White Tee.” THR

articles.title: Jack Coleman Remembers ‘Heroes’ Co-Star Hayden Panettiere, Says He‘s “Filled With Sorrow, Regret and Anger” Over Death
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexy Perez Plus Icon Lexy Perez Senior Digital Editor and Producer View All August 19, 2026 4:09pm Jack Coleman and Hayden Panettiere in ‘Heroes.’ Courtesy Everett Collection Jack Coleman is remembering his Heroes co-star Hayden Panettiere . In a tribute shared on his social media, the actor reflected on working with the actress on the NBC drama series where Colman portrayed Noah Bennet, the father to Panettiere’s Claire. “I’m heartbroken. I couldn’t begin to put my thoughts into words until now, and they will be inadequate. I’ve loved Hayden since day one of the pilot of Heroes , 20 years ago, when she introduced herself by shouting ‘daddy’ and throwing her arms around me. From that day on, she called me daddio. She was Haydini, because she was a magician,“ he wrote. Related Stories News Hayden Panettiere's Ex-Boyfriend and Years-Long Abuser Received a Visit From Police After Her Death Movies Liev Schreiber and 'Ukrainians in Exile' Director Janek Ambros Set for Lakes Noir Film Festival Tribute Coleman went on to describe Panettiere as a “prodigious talent,“ who was just 16 at the time of filming. “During an early scene, a tear rolled down her cheek on the same line, take after take. I marveled at her technique. ‘It’s not technique,‘ she corrected me. ‘I’m not a trained seal. I feel it and the tears just happen to come at that moment.‘ She was 16.“ Given her young age at the time, Colman said she had to endure growing up in the public eye and was “hunted“ by photographers. “By 17 she was #1 on IMDB Pro. She was routinely asked obnoxious questions, mostly some version of ‘when are you going to go off the rails?‘ Today, we’d recognize those questions for the misogynistic provocations they were. She was hunted. Everywhere she went, there were photographers with 300 millimeter lenses—the kind that can make even the most innocent activity look sinister. Once, when she came to our house, paparazzi hid in the bushes behind our yard and drove onto neighbors’ lawns. They were predatory. No one, especially a teenager, should be targeted that way,” he wrote. Despite experiencing the heightened media attention, Coleman says Panettiere “brought joy“ to set and treated everyone with kindness. “She brought joy to the set and a photographic memory. Everyone was in awe of her ability to bring it every take. A tiny colossus who loved to laugh. We laughed a lot. That shining face, that megawatt smile, that wasn’t just for the camera. That was her. She glowed,“ Colman continued. As he‘s still processing the news of Panettiere, who died Sunday at age 36 , Coleman said he‘s “filled with sorrow and regret. And anger. But that’s for another time. Right now I want to remember an extraordinary young woman who was blessed and cursed. She was vulnerable. She felt everything. It made her a remarkable actor and susceptible to the heartache and thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to.” In his parting words, Coleman expressed his love for the actress and his wish that she had been protected and free of suffering. “I love you, Hayden. I’ll miss you. I’m so sorry you suffered. I’ll remember how happy you were on set and on the European press tour; how you championed Tess when she was being bullied; your commitment to animal welfare and the courage to put yourself in harm’s way to protect them. I only wish you had been given that same protection. Good night, sweet girl. And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.” Panettiere is survived by her parents and daughter, Kaya, whom she shares with ex Wladimir Klitschko. The Greenville County Coroner’s Office said the cause and manner of her death remain pending further investigation, and that there were no obvious signs of trauma to her body. View this post on Instagram THR

articles.title: DEA Joins Investigation Into Hayden Panettiere’s Death, Sources Say
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 19, 2026 4:43pm Hayden Panettiere Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images The Drug Enforcement Administration has joined the investigation into the death of Hayden Panettiere , sources familiar with the matter told ABC News on Wednesday. The actress, who was best known for her roles in Heroes , Nashville and the Scream franchise, died on Sunday at age 36 at an apartment complex in Greenville, South Carolina. The Greenville County Coroner’s Office said on Monday that her cause and manner of death remain pending further investigation, and that there were no obvious signs of trauma. However, officials were reportedly heard discussing an “overdose” and “cardiac arrest” on a 911 call at the time of her death. A police report also said her on-again, off-again boyfriend Hickerson and his brother were at the South Carolina townhouse when the actress was pronounced dead by authorities. Hickerson was later visited by police , according to a redacted police report. Related Stories General News Hayden Panettiere's Neighbor Says She Called 911 Multiple Times to Report Disturbances With Star's Boyfriend News Jack Coleman Remembers 'Heroes' Co-Star Hayden Panettiere, Says He's "Filled With Sorrow, Regret and Anger" Over Death Panettiere had been open about her struggles with alcohol and opioid addiction, further detailing her experiences in her memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , released earlier this year. The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to the DEA for more information, but did not hear back at the time of publication. TMZ reported that DEA agents will be assisting the parallel investigations currently underway by the Greenville County Coroner’s Office and the Greenville Police Department, according to sources. Panettiere’s death investigation isn’t the only high-profile celebrity death that the government agency has gotten involved with in recent years. The Los Angeles Police Department also teamed up with the DEA in 2023 after high levels of ketamine were found in Friends star Matthew Perry’s system after he died at age 54. The lengthy multi-agency probe led to five arrests and convictions , including two medical doctors and a supplier dubbed the “Ketamine Queen,” for distributing the drugs that resulted in Perry’s death. Following the star’s death at age 36 on Sunday in Greenville, South Carolina, Mia Terrazzas spoke with Inside Edition on Wednesday about her experience living next to Panettiere and her on-again, off-again boyfriend Brian Hickerson. When asked if she noticed any signs of domestic violence, Terrazzas said, “Oh, absolutely.” “I saw her leaving on a gurney. Brian was right next to her, and I asked her if she was OK, and it looked to me that she had suffered some type of trauma that looked to be battering,” she claimed. “It was clear she was terrified.” Related Stories News DEA Joins Investigation Into Hayden Panettiere's Death, Sources Say News Jack Coleman Remembers 'Heroes' Co-Star Hayden Panettiere, Says He's "Filled With Sorrow, Regret and Anger" Over Death Terrazzas also shared that notices were posted around the property by the Homeowners Association last year, warning residents to call 911 if Hickerson was spotted. However, the signs were removed a week later. Panettiere, best known for her roles in Heroes , Nashville and the Scream franchise, had detailed physical abuse by Hickerson in her memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning , released earlier this year. He was also sentenced to 45 days in jail in 2021 after pleading no contest to two felony counts of injuring the actress. “This predator was in our community. He never stopped living at her place. Amid the investigation into Panettiere’s death, a police report said Hickerson and his brother were at the South Carolina townhouse when the actress was pronounced dead by authorities. articles.title: Did Alex Vindman Just Get Burned by the Larry David Curse?
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Steven Zeitchik Plus Icon Steven Zeitchik Senior Editor, Technology and Politics View All August 19, 2026 7:02pm Florida Democratic Senate candidate, retired Lt. Col. Alex Vindman, concedes to his opponent, Florida State Rep. Angie Nixon, during a primary election-night watch party, held at the American Legion Post 222 event hall on Aug. 18, 2026, in Oakland Park, Florida. Was Vindman Larry David-ed? Joe Raedle/Getty Images Hey let me ask you a question. If I told you about a political candidate with impeccable patriotic bona fides, a compelling backstory and a deep cash reserve, wouldn’t you think he’d win by a landslide or at least turn out a competitive race? That’s what Alex Vindman and his supporters thought. But they underestimated the Larry David factor. Vindman, a Florida Democrat, seemed a lock to win his Senate primary bid on Tuesday. A retired lieutenant colonel in the Army. A Purple Heart-decorated Iraq veteran. A whistleblower on Donald Trump for the 2019 quid pro quo attempt with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy that led to an impeachment trial. Vindman had major name recognition. He raised $16 million ($15 million more than his opponent) and was believed to be a big favorite over said rival, Angie Nixon — a little-known Jacksonville-based member of the Florida House of Representatives. Nixon was a DSA candidate in a state that leans moderate, and then some. No way a million Democrats would give the edge to her. (The pair were battling to take on sitting Senator Ashley Moody, a Republican, to finish out the remaining two years of Marco Rubio’s term.) Yet that’s exactly what unfolded Tuesday. Nixon swamped Vindman by more than 12 points, garnering over 700,000 of the total 1.25 million votes. She pulled off the ultimate chat-and-cut. How could this happen to the retired Army lieutenant colonel and Soviet refugee? What did Vindman do to merit this? Did he not respect wood? I’ll tell you what happened. Larry David happened. Vindman appeared in two episodes of Curb Your Enthusiasm as himself, including the series finale, in which he testifies against Larry in his political bribery case. David even campaigned for the candidate, sending out a fundraising text message earlier this summer (including to people who didn’t live anywhere near Florida). “The man is everything I’m not, which should give you an idea of what a tremendous person he is. Vindman is not a puppet. He loves this country. He loves it so much it’s almost off-putting. I love it too, but come on. Get a life, Vindman!” And David, in addition to schlemieling up everything on the show, has a curse attached to him. A curse that ensures people never get the votes they should. It’s called the Curb curse, and it seeks to explain — because there is no explanation — how David never won a writing or acting Emmy in the entire 12-season, 24-year history of the show. Yes, 120 episodes and he never got a thing. (The show won just two overall, for directing and editing.) A post on Screen Rant after his last strikeout in 2024 said: “ Curb Your Enthusiasm Continues a 24-Year Larry David Curse After The Show’s Ending.” And now that the show is over, it carried over to Vindman. David couldn’t win an Emmy in 2024 and Vindman couldn’t win a primary in 2026. If this was a Curb episode, you could almost imagine Vindman showing up at David’s house. “You cost me the election , Larry.” “What are you talking about? I didn’t cost you the election.” “You cost me the election.” “Get the hell out of here! Cost you the election. Poor Candidate Vindman. Like Al Gore. [Fake crying.] Cost him the election.” And then Vindman would angrily leave, but at the end of the episode happen to be in the Santa Monica restaurant when Larry does something untoward and the camera would pan to him and he’d tip someone off and have his revenge. The curse would be avenged. Of course this may not be a curse so much as, you know, simple irascibility. For the character but also the personality — the real-life David wasn’t one for the glad-handing, even at parties, and it’s not like he kissed the awards ring. He didn’t even show up to the Emmys the last time he was nominated. When you attack Elmo , you don’t get love. That irascibility also may have singed Vindman. Who wants to get a hectoring message from David? Especially asking for money. It’s not cool de la. Sure, if you’re trying to analyze the results of the election, you can talk about the Democrats’ swing to the DSA even in a place like Florida, auguring a new future for the party. Or that many of the moderate Dems in Florida have ditched for the GOP and couldn’t vote in the state’s closed primary. But….eh. It was probably Larry. articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Aims to Swing Past ‘Insidious’ Sequel for Fourth Box Office Win

Sony Pictures Logo text Spider-Man: Brand New Day looks to continue its indefatigable run at the box office against such new challengers as horror sequel Insidious : Out of the Further and the Jason Statham -led Mutiny . Sony Pictures releases Insidious: Out of the Further in roughly 3,000 North American theaters on Friday, with the studio projecting an opening weekend around $23 million. Hailing from Screen Gems, Stage 6 Films and Blumhouse Atomic Monster, Out of the Further is the sixth title in the franchise that kicked off with 2011’s Insidious and carries an $18 million production budget. Out of the Further follows 2023’s Insidious: The Red Door , which saw the return of original series stars Patrick Wilson and Rose Byrne and opened to $33 million domestically before hitting a global total of $189 million for its run. Lionsgate releases the movie that is tracking to open in the high single-digit range and carries a $40 million production budget. MadRiver Pictures and Punch Palace Productions produced the project. Jean-François Richet helmed the feature that holds a 49 percent approval score from reviewers on Rotten Tomatoes. Statham’s recent films include Shelter , which opened to $5.5 million domestically earlier this year, while 2025’s A Working Man launched with an initial weekend of $15.5 million in North America. Next year sees the star leading The Beekeeper 2 . Tom Holland in Spider-Man: Brand New Day. Jay Maidment/Sony Pictures Other new theatrical offerings this weekend include the Andrew Garfield -led The Magic Faraway Tree and Spa Weekend , starring Isla Fisher, Leslie Mann and Anna Faris. Spider-Man: Brand New Day continues its historic run into the waning days of summer, as the Sony Pictures juggernaut that stars Tom Holland and Zendaya is set to lead the box office for its fourth consecutive weekend. Having recently set the record as the fastest movie to hit $800 million domestically , director Destin Daniel Cretton ‘s feature is expected to surpass 2021’s Spider-Man: No Way Home as the No. 3 highest-grossing title ever in North America. articles.title: Naomi Watts to Receive Zurich Fest Golden Eye Award
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All August 19, 2026 9:00pm Naomi Watts JuanKR The Zurich Film Festival (ZFF) will honor two-time Oscar nominee Naomi Watts this year with a Golden Eye Award for her performance in Ben Shirinian’s The Housewife . In the ’60s-set drama, based on a true-story, a young New York Times journalist, played by Tye Sheridan, tracks down a man he suspects of being a Nazi officer living secretly in Queens (Luke Evans). But when the reporter befriends the suspect’s elegant and enigmatic wife (Watts), the implications of his investigation become much more unsettling. The Housewife will have its world premiere at the Toronto Film Festival before heading to Zurich. Watts will accept her Golden Eye honor in person in Zurich on Sept. 26 and take part in a ZFF masterclass. Related Stories Movies Georgian Director Ana Urushadze on Making Her Sarajevo Competition Film Before "A Dead-End Situation" Got Worse Lifestyle How Natalie Portman Got Caught in Novelist Rachel Cusk's Autofiction Trap “Since her breakthrough in David Lynch’s Mulholland Drive , Naomi Watts has been one of the most fascinating actresses of our time,” said Zurich Festival CEO Christian Jungen, announcing the honor on Thursday. “Her greatest performances thrive on the tension between glamour and darkness, between what a character reveals and what she conceals — making her the kind of character actress Hitchcock would have loved.” In The Housewife , said Jungen, Watts “masters this ambiguity as an elegant and mysterious woman [and] delivers one of the most compelling performances of her career.” Watts is a two-time Academy Award nominee, nominated for best actress in 2004 for her turn as a grieving mother in Alejandro González Iñárritu’s 21 Grams ; and in 2013 for her role as a survivor of the 2004 tsunami in J.A. Bayona’s The Impossible . On the small screen, her performance as Baby Paley in the second season of Ryan Murphy’s Feud earned her an Emmy nomination for best actress in a limited/anthology series or TV movie. Previous winners of Zurich’s Golden Eye Award include Kristen Stewart, Jude Law, Benedict Cumberbatch and Dakota Johnson. The 2026 Zurich Film Festival runs Sept. 24 – Oct. 4. THR

articles.title: Jonathan Jackson Shares Touching Tribute to Hayden Panettiere: “She Had Such a Bright Light Within Her”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 19, 2026 11:35pm 'Nashville' Everett Collection Nashville actors Jonathan Jackson and Clare Bowen paid a touching tributes to their late co-star Hayden Panettiere on social media on Wednesday. In a message on Instagram , Jackson, who played Avery Barkley, the bad boy on-again and-off again love interest of Panettiere’s Juliette Barnes in the ABC country music drama, described his co-star as a “sensitive soul” who was “incredibly funny and witty.” Panettiere, who died Sunday in Greenville, South Carolina at 36 , and Jackson starred in Nashville for six seasons, from October 2010 to March 2016. Jackson described how they both “grew up in the industry” and shared that “silent knowing of how intense the struggles can be.” He went on to write that, “she was an absolute joy to work with. Focused, spontaneous and brilliant. The most important thing between friends and coworkers is trust, and we had this.” Related Stories General News Hayden Panettiere's Neighbor Says She Called 911 Multiple Times to Report Disturbances With Star's Boyfriend News DEA Joins Investigation Into Hayden Panettiere's Death, Sources Say He added that it was “not possible to express the shock and grief that so many of us feel right now.” ‘Nashville’ Everett Collection Panettiere’s other Nashville co-star, Australian actress Clare Bowen also posted a tribute on Instagram . Bowen, who played Scarlett O’Connor in the show, wrote a poem set to images of Bowen and Panettiere together from their time working on Nashville together. In one passage, Bowen writes, “I’ll remember you, cheeky in pretty red soles. You said kind things about strangeness, old boots, an old soul. You warned me our monsters only half hid at best…and then fixed the tear in my favorite dress.” In another couplet, Bowen wrote, “We’ll see you someday in your beautiful wings, where vultures and sinners aren’t worthy to sing. Wove from new gold and celestial breath, this isn’t goodbye, it’s just “have a rest.” Following the news of Panettiere’s death, many of her former co-stars on the various film and TV projects she had worked on shared deeply personal and emotional memories of the actress . Nashville alums Connie Britton and Charles Esten , as well as Solange Knowles ( Bring It On: All or Nothing ), Jack Coleman ( Heroes ), Griff Hurst ( A Breed Apart ), Neve Campbell ( Scream ) and Tim Fywell ( Ice Princess ) have all penned tributes to Panettiere. Jonathan Jackson’s full note on Instagram: “I have no words to express the loss of our beloved Hayden. She had such a bright light within her. She was a sensitive soul. Incredibly funny and witty. Amazingly gifted, with a great sense of empathy and compassion. We both grew up in the industry, although she started even younger than me, but we shared that. A silent knowing of how intense the struggles can be. She was an absolute joy to work with. Focused, spontaneous and brilliant. The most important thing between friends and coworkers is trust, and we had this. Elisa and I both love and cherish her deeply, like our own sister. She holds that place in our hearts. My prayer for her every day we worked together was that she would know how loved she is, and that she would find the peace that she was looking for. It’s not possible to express the shock and grief that so many of us feel right now. Our humble prayers are with her family. May God’s angels carry you to your place of rest and true peace. We love you Hayden. You will always be in our hearts. Always. ” Clare Bowen’s poem, posted on Instagram: “It’s been raining in the treehouse for days…for you…you whispered like you’d found the sun, just in June. But you always were full of surprises and dreams pulling at threads and the lines in between. I’ll remember nights side by side in a nest on the same street by fate, that ridiculous bed. The day you got cross that I didn’t scare then by looking glass light cried for everyone there. Thank you for chasing me that day in the dark. I was shattered and bruised, a hollowed out heart. You’d been there. You listened to the bad…and the worst. Our faces painted with the kisses of a good wolf, a good ghost. I’ll remember you, cheeky in pretty red soles. You said kind things about strangeness, old boots, an old soul. You warned me our monsters only half hid at best…and then fixed the tear in my favorite dress. One, in so many in pain, in plain sight, with the last of yourself you kicked on the lights. We’ll see you someday in your beautiful wings, where vultures and sinners aren’t worthy to sing. Wove from new gold and celestial breath, this isn’t goodbye, it’s just “have a rest.” We’ll switch all the coffees, ride our horses too fast…dance with fireflies…and brothers…sisters…friends…under that beautiful blanket of stars. Fly safe, little butterfly. I miss you. Love, Luna Moth.” THR

Related Stories Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief Sinha, known for directing “Mulk,” “Article 15” and “Thappad,” is producing the feature as Mishra’s next directorial effort. The film marks Mishra’s return to a theatrical release after 2023’s “Afwaah,” and it lands as he nears four decades working in Hindi cinema. Mishra has won three Indian National Film Awards, for “Yeh Woh Manzil To Nahin” (best debut film of a director), “Dharavi” (best feature film in Hindi) and “Main Zinda Hoon” (best film on other social issues), and his credits also include “Hazaaron Khwaishein Aisi” and “Is Raat Ki Subah Nahin.” Popular on Variety Bajpayee, a multiple Indian National Film Award winner, takes on the role of Gandhi for the first time in his career. Shukla joins him in the ensemble cast. “This new film focuses on an important yet lesser-known chapter of history – the 21 days in the life of Mahatma Gandhi during India’s independence. At a time when the nation was stepping into freedom, and Delhi was becoming the center of power, Gandhi made an unexpected choice: he chose to walk away. But by walking away, he did not retreat. He reinvented himself. While history books record the surface events of that era, this story explores what lay beneath that famous choice and will depict the personal journey of a leader redefining his path,” Mishra tells Variety . Sinha and Hirawat produce the film through Sinha’s Benaras Mediaworks banner, with NH Studioz presenting. The film joins Hansal Mehta’s own Gandhi series , starring Pratik Gandhi and scored by A.R. Rahman for Applause Entertainment, which has yet to unveil a streaming home. articles.title: Busan Festival Honors Ahn Sung-ki, Market Names Thailand Country of Honor
articles.full_text: Aug 19, 2026 10:32pm PT Busan Festival Honors Ahn Sung-ki, Market Names Thailand Country of Honor By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market 41 minutes ago India’s Epic Studios, Rusk Media Ink 50-Title Vertical Drama Deal (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago Busan Festival Honors Ahn Sung-ki, Market Names Thailand Country of Honor 4 hours ago See All Busan International Film Festival The 31st Busan International Film Festival (BIFF) has unveiled a Special Program in Focus honoring the late Korean screen legend Ahn Sung-ki , while the festival’s market arm has named Thailand the first-ever recipient of a new top-tier country partnership. “Those Beautiful Years, Ahn Sung-ki” serves as the grand finale to the nationwide tributes paid to the actor, who died earlier this year . The six-film lineup was hand-picked by Ahn himself before his passing and centers on his 1980s and 1990s peak, including “A Fine, Windy Day” (1980), “Whale Hunting” (1984), “Chil-su and Man-su” (1988), “Gagman” (1989), “White Badge” (1992) and “Festival” (1996). Each screening will include a guest visit featuring longtime collaborators, among them directors Lee Jang-ho, Bae Chang-ho and Chung Jiyoung, along with actors Kim Bo-Yeon and Bae Jong-ok. BIFF will also publish an essay collection on Ahn’s career and legacy, co-hosted with the Korean Film Archive. Ahn’s screen career stretched nearly seven decades, from his 1957 debut as a child actor through his later years as a UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador and longtime member of the BIFF festival committee. Related Stories Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief Elsewhere at the festival, the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) has launched a Country of Honor program, its highest-tier country partnership, naming Thailand as the inaugural recipient for 2026. The designation builds on a long history of ties between the two markets, including Pen-ek Ratanaruang’s “Ploy,” picked for the Pusan Promotion Plan in 2006, and Aditya Assarat’s “Wonderful Town,” which took the New Currents prize at the festival in 2007. More than 540 foreign film and TV productions shot in Thailand last year, drawn in part by cash rebates of up to 30% for eligible projects. Popular on Variety Chookiat Sakveerakul, president of the Thai Film Directors Association, said, “Thailand is deeply honored to be named the first Country of Honor at ACFM 2026.” He added that the partnership would “open new doors for Thai films and content to reach wider international audiences, while strengthening collaboration between Thailand, South Korea, and partners across the global industry.” The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15, with the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market held Oct. 10-13. articles.title: ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Director Florin Şerban Sets Next Feature After Winning Locarno’s Golden Leopard (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 20, 2026 1:38am PT ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Director Florin Şerban Sets Next Feature After Winning Locarno’s Golden Leopard (EXCLUSIVE) By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘Mother’ Director Teona Mitevska Preps Sequel to Feminist Satirical Drama ‘God Exists, Her Name Is Petrunya’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’ 4 days ago Sarajevo Industry Head on How Building a Talent Pipeline Makes Markets and Festivals More Vital Than Ever 7 days ago See All Courtesy Locarno Film Festival Romanian filmmaker Florin Şerban, whose bleak study of systemic racism and toxic masculinity “You Don’t Belong Here” won the Golden Leopard at the recently wrapped Locarno Film Festival , is prepping his next feature film. Speaking to Variety at the Sarajevo Film Festival , where “You Don’t Belong Here” is playing in the main competition, the director shared details about his next project, “Ela, or the Diary of a Dutiful Daughter From Romania,” for which casting is already underway. Related Stories Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief Written by Adriana Neagoe, “Ela” is “a story about a girl who needs to go away from a family that is very troubled, bounded by alcoholism and violence. She needs to leave before she repeats the story herself, because her life is going in that direction,” said Şerban. Popular on Variety Inspired by the book “Memoirs of a Dutiful Daughter,” by French existentialist philosopher and writer Simone de Beauvoir, the film follows a young Romanian woman who keeps a TikTok diary “where she documents the way she wants her life to be,” said Şerban, “not the way her life actually is.” The film, which has received support from Romania’s CNC, will be produced by Şerban’s Bucharest-based label Fantascope Films, Scharf Film and Avanpost. Şerban is currently searching for international co-producers. The director arrived in Sarajevo fresh off his Locarno triumph, where alongside the top prize, “You Don’t Belong Here” scooped the festival’s Junior Jury and Europa Cinemas Label awards, as well as a special mention for its young star Teodor Butănescu. “The hardest part is the premiere,” the director said, over coffee at Sarajevo’s historic Hotel Europe. “Every single moment watching the film on the huge screen for the first time, literally, it’s like you’ve aged two years. I got out of the cinema drained. I was on the verge of tears.” “You Don’t Belong Here” tells the story of a respected doctor (Adrian Văncică) at a smalltown hospital who’s raising his teenage son, Ioan (Teodor Butănescu), alone after the death of his wife. Unaware that his son is vandalizing cars by night with a gang of masked vigilantes, his world is shaken when he learns that Ioan is a suspect in the murder of a Roma man. Nearly a decade in the making, the film is a somber exploration of masculinity in Southeast Europe, a study of generational divides and a damning portrait of institutionalized racism against Romania’s Roma community. For Şerban, it’s also a personal story inspired by his own experience as a father, and a dawning recognition that fatherhood — and the role of men in society — is rapidly changing in contemporary Europe. “How do we relate to the reality of the world as men in our forties, in our fifties?” the 51-year-old director asked. “There were several changes in the paradigm of how, in this day and age, men should relate to the ones around them. Because this patriarchal model that still exists in the Balkans, that still exists in Europe, little by little, it’s dying. What do we replace it with?” For Marius, there are no easy answers. Middle-aged, hounded by disappointment, he struggles to understand both his son and the generation he represents, never quite finding a way to articulate his love while holding onto “a reality that is vanishing,” according to the director. “For this character, living in this place, there’s no space for love. There’s no time for love,” said Şerban. “You always had this idea that the man had to prove himself. The man had to be a magnet for success, money, fame. He can fail, but he has to get right back up. He cannot shed a tear. He has to be strong. A hero.” “You Don’t Belong Here” marks a return to international festival prominence for the Romanian New Wave veteran, whose debut feature “If I Want to Whistle, I Whistle” premiered in competition at the Berlin Film Festival in 2010, where it won the Grand Prix. Şerban took a break from the director’s chair following the 2018 release of the romantic drama “Love 2. America,” focusing instead on Școala de Film, a Bucharest-based film school he founded in 2010 and later expanded with the help of Romanian actress Cosmina Stratan (“Beyond the Hills”) and the U.S.-based Spanish filmmaker Antonio Méndez Esparza (“Life and Nothing More”). It was among the school’s ranks that the director discovered Butănescu and more than a dozen other actors in “You Don’t Belong Here.” With the school running smoothly in Bucharest, Şerban said he was finally able to return to directing — not least because he also had a story that needed to be told. “It’s a story that’s very close to me. It’s a story that I feel deeply,” he said. “It’s something that I think about a lot. I think it’s the time to raise these questions.” The Sarajevo Film Festival runs Aug. 14 – 21. articles.title: Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market
articles.full_text: Aug 20, 2026 1:48am PT Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Toei, Shochiku, Kadokawa Among IP Holders Set for TIFFCOM’s Tokyo Adaptation and Remake Market 34 minutes ago India’s Epic Studios, Rusk Media Ink 50-Title Vertical Drama Deal (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago Busan Festival Honors Ahn Sung-ki, Market Names Thailand Country of Honor 4 hours ago See All Kawakami Takashi Eight major Japanese publishers, studios and production companies will pitch intellectual property to international buyers at the second edition of Tokyo IP Market: Adaptation & Remake, running Oct. 28-30 at TIFFCOM 2026 in Tokyo. The platform, known as TIPM, will host one-on-one business meetings and open pitching sessions at the Tokyo Metropolitan Industrial Trade Center Hamamatsucho-Kan. Producers from Hollywood, Europe and Asia will attend, seeking to secure rights to adapt and remake Japanese manga, novels and classic films. Related Stories Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) This year’s participants are Amuse Creative Studio, Kadokawa, Nihon Bungeisha, Nippon Animation, Shochiku, Shufu to Seikatsu Sha, Square Enix and Toei. The eight-company roster marks an expansion from the six IP holders at last year’s inaugural TIPM edition. Popular on Variety The market traces its origins to the Tokyo Story Market, a dedicated service for screen adaptation rights covering Japanese manga and novels, which launched at TIFFCOM in 2023. At TIFFCOM 2025, it was rebranded as TIPM and broadened to encompass film studios and production companies. The platform moved beyond Japan for the first time this past May, when seven companies presented at the Cannes Film Market under the Japan IP Market banner. Among this year’s participants, Shochiku brings a library running from Yasujiro Ozu classics to contemporary genre fare. “For 131 years, Shochiku has created stories that transcend generations,” the studio said. “We are ready to bring these stories to audiences around the world and create the next global hit together with global filmmakers.” Toei, which has already seen its IP adapted overseas as “Power Rangers” and “Yolo,” will present alongside Nihon Bungeisha, publisher of the horror hit “Gannibal,” and game developer and manga publisher Square Enix, whose titles including “Fullmetal Alchemist,” “Soul Eater” and “Kakegurui” have already generated anime, television and film adaptations. “Another key strength is our dedicated international production team so we welcome discussions on both remake rights licensing and co-production opportunities,” Toei said. TIFFCOM, now in its 23rd edition, runs alongside the 39th Tokyo International Film Festival , which opens Oct. 26. articles.full_text: Aug 20, 2026 2:00am PT ‘Game of Thrones’ Play ‘The Mad King’ Reveals Behind-The-Scenes Secrets in Stage Transformation Video (EXCLUSIVE) By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest The Beatles Ink Licensing and Merch Deal With Universal Music Ahead of Biopics 1 day ago Phyllida Law, Scottish Actress and Mother of Emma and Sophie Thompson, Dies at 94 2 days ago ‘Slow Horses’ Season 6 Trailer: Olivia Cooke’s Sid Makes a Surprise Return as Gary Oldman Warns Slough House Gang to Go on the Run 2 days ago See All Courtesy of RSC “ Game of Thrones : The Mad King” is sharing some of the magic behind the scenes in a new video that shows how the stage at the Royal Shakespeare Theatre in Stratford-Upon-Avon has been transformed for the show, which launched earlier this month . The show’s production design, overseen by set designer Chloe Lamford, is unlike anything ever seen before at the theatre, which is owned by the Royal Shakespeare Company. As well as excavating two stories down to accommodate stage lifts and scenery pieces measuring up to 20-foot high scenery pieces, the design includes 5,291 oz of rubber crumb chippings to create the textured floor, 1.58 miles of steel (not including the audience seating), and 5,000 individually hand-crafted leaves on the tree (which, for the eagle-eyed, also includes seven hidden faces). It took more than 4,000 hours of carpentry and engineering time to build the set, working with 11 external engineering companies, 19 internal staff and five freelancers. The HBO/Royal Shakespeare Company co-production, which is inspired by George R.R. Martin’s fantasy series, is set before the events in in HBO’s “Game of Thrones” series. It is adapted by Duncan Macmillan and directed by Dominic Cooke. The show opened a week later than planned due to technical difficulties but has almost sold out its entire run. It is due to close on Sept. 5 although fans are hoping for a West End transfer. articles.title: San Sebastián Sets Michaël R. Roskam’s ‘Le Faux Soir’ as Closing Night Film
articles.full_text: Aug 20, 2026 2:16am PT San Sebastián Sets Michaël R. Roskam’s ‘Le Faux Soir’ as Closing Night Film The Belgian-French resistance thriller, sold by Goodfellas, brings the 'Bullhead' director back to San Sebastián 12 years after 'The Drop' By Emiliano de Pablos Plus Icon Emiliano de Pablos Latest Mexico’s Madrefoca Boards ‘Isabel Hernández’ as Zoe Films Builds Festival Momentum (EXCLUSIVE) 3 days ago San Sebastian Adds Jesse Eisenberg, Fred Cavayé, Amanda Kernell Films to Golden Shell Race 6 days ago Bendita Film Sales Picks Up Toronto Discovery Title ‘The Fortunate Isles’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 weeks ago See All 'Le Faux Soir' Courtesy of Goodfellas “ Le Faux Soir ,” a Belgian-French WWII resistance drama from “Bullhead” director Michaël R. Roskam , has been set as the closing night film of this year’s San Sebastián Film Festival. Playing in the festival’s Official Selection out of competition, the film will have its European premiere at San Sebastián after world premiering at Toronto, where it screens in Special Presentations. It will close the festival after the awards ceremony on Sept. 26 at the Kursaal. Related Stories Oscars Budget, 'Engaging' With AI and Hot Memorabilia: Inside the Academy's Annual All-Members Meeting (EXCLUSIVE) Academy Museum Fall Film Events Include 'Marie Antoinette,' 'The Craft,' 'Pan's Labyrinth' - Film News in Brief “Le Faux Soir” is produced by Belgium’s Frakas Productions and Roskam’s Harbor Men Pictures with France’s Rectangle Productions. Goodfellas handles international sales, while Cinéart will release the film in Benelux. Popular on Variety Set in Nazi-occupied Belgium in 1943, the film follows a group of Resistance fighters after the occupying forces turn national daily Le Soir into a propaganda outlet. With commemorations of the 1918 Armistice banned, they hatch a plan to produce a fake edition of the newspaper, reproducing its paper, nameplate and format but filling its pages with articles mocking the German occupiers. The operation has been described as “the world’s first media hack.” Arieh Worthalter (“The Goldman Case”) leads the ensemble, alongside Mélanie Thierry (“Da 5 Bloods”), Karim Leklou (“Jim’s Story”), Mara Taquin (“Zero Fucks Given”), Bouli Lanners (“The Night of the 12th”), Julien Frison (“The Happening”) and François Damiens (“The Bélier Family”). The closing berth brings Roskam back to San Sebastián 12 years after his U.S. crime drama “The Drop,” starring Tom Hardy, Noomi Rapace and James Gandolfini, which won the Jury Prize for Best Screenplay in 2014. Roskam, who previously worked as a journalist for Dutch-language newspaper De Morgen , broke through internationally with feature debut “Bullhead.” After premiering in Berlin’s Panorama section, the film earned an Academy Award nomination for best foreign-language film and landed Roskam on Variety’s Ten Directors to Watch list. He later directed “Racer and the Jailbird,” starring Matthias Schoenaerts and Adèle Exarchopoulos, which screened out of competition at Venice and was selected as Belgium’s Academy Awards entry. He also helmed the first three episodes of Apple TV+ miniseries “Black Bird.” “Le Faux Soir” returns Roskam to the thriller territory that has marked much of his career. Roskam wrote the screenplay, with Bernard Falaise co-credited on dialogue, loosely adapting Marie Istas’ book Le “faux” Soir, 9 novembre 1943 . The 74th San Sebastián Film Festival runs Sept. 18-26.
