articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Charlie Hunnam Gets ‘Sons Of Anarchy’ Gang Back Together For FX Meta-Series ‘Legends’ Curtis Lum Joins ABC’s ‘The Rookie: North’ & Prime Video’s ‘Cross’ For Season 3 Marissa Jo Cerar Developing ‘Drowning In Paper Flowers’ Novel For TV With Jenna Bush Hager & Universal View All August 19, 2026 1:00pm SONS OF ANARCHY, l-r: Tommy Flanagan, Kim Coates, Theo Rossi, David Labrava, Charlie Hunnam in 'Salvage' (Season 6, Episode 6, aired October 15, 2013). FX Emmy nominee Charlie Hunnam ( Monster: The Ed Gein Story , Sons of Anarchy ) is putting the M.C. back together—sort of–for an all-new limited series. FX has ordered Legends , a meta-thriller created, developed and executive produced by Hunnam, who will also star, and Jonathan Groff ( Happy Endings, This Fool ), who will serve as showrunner. Ron Perlman , Katey Sagal , Maggie Siff , Mark Boone Junior , Tommy Flanagan , Kim Coates and Theo Rossi join Hunnam on this new adventure. Additional casting will be announced at a later date. On Legends , when the cast of Sons of Anarchy (who will all play themselves) reunites at a fan convention after more than a decade, the line between life and art blurs as the fractured brotherhood finds itself up against a real-world threat more dangerous than anything they ever faced in their show. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Love Story' Stars On Playing An Iconic Romance: The Fights, The Fashion And The New York Of The '90s - Contenders TV Nominees Studio News 'The Drop: A Snowfall Saga' Trailer Reveals Wanda & Leon Taking On The Music Industry Sons of Anarchy , the biker drama created by Kurt Sutter, ran for 7 seasons on FX, with the series concluding in 2014. Perlman played Clay Morrow, Katey Sagal as Gemma Teller Morrow, Maggie Siff as Tara Knowles, Mark Boone Junior as Bobby Munson, Tommy Flanagan as Chibs, Kim Coates as Tig and Theo Rossi as Juice. The show was a ratings juggernaut for the network, which ordered the spinoff Mayans M.C. in 2018 from Sutter and Elgin James, with Emilio Rivera’s character Marcus Alvarez holding court at the center of the new tale. Sutter had plans for other spinoffs, including the prequel series First Nine , and a sequel series about Hunnam’s character Jax Teller’s sons Abel and Thomas. Sutter is not involved in the project, however, he gave Hunnam his blessing to move forward with the series. In the 12 years since, many of the original cast reconnect for fan conventions on a pretty regular basis, with many maintaining tight relationships. The project has been in development with Hunnam for at least three years at FX, before Groff joined the project more recently. ‘Sons of Anarchy’ FX The greenlight arrives following Hunnam’s rave reviews in the Netflix crime-drama series Monster: The Ed Gein Story , portraying the titular suspected serial killer. For his work, he received his first Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Limited or Anthology Series or Movie. The rest of the cast noted above has gone on to star on major projects across TV and film. Most already had established and successful careers in the industry. “When Charlie brought us this inspired idea, we instantly sparked to his bold and entertaining vision,” said Nick Grad, FX Entertainment President. “Charlie’s talents are on full display as a writer, performer and executive producer, leading the real-life brotherhood on an adventure that is both a love letter to the series and a fun meta twist on what fans think they know.” FX’s Legends is developed and executive produced by Hunnam and Jonathan Groff, with Rob Mac, Nicholas Frenkel and Jackie Cohn also serving as executive producers. The series will be produced by FX Productions and 20th Television and will be available to watch on FX and Hulu. Hunnam is repped by CAA, Brillstein Entertainment, and Sloane Offer Weber & Dern. While they are returning the UK, they will reportedly remain private individuals and non-working members of the royal family. People reports the couple will also keep a home in Montecito. The decision comes after the deal between the pair’s Archewell Productions and Netflix — believed to have been an overall pact — was extended, but as a first look agreement — late last year. After ratings cratered in the second half of 2025, there are no plans for a third season of their cooking show With Love, Meghan. The streamer also withdrew as an investor in Markle’s lifestyle brand As Ever. Watch on Deadline Netflix’s Chief Content Officer Bela pushed back on the idea that the duo was on their way out at the streamer. “We still have a relationship with them. We have movies in development with them. We have an amazing doc with them. They have things in development on the TV and film side. Deals come and go all the time, and we don’t renew so many deals, those just don’t get as much press for obvious reasons. There’s no juicy story there,” Bajaria said earlier this year. Among those projects is a polo-themed drama , which the Sussexes are executive producing under their Netflix deal. Other features in development include The Wedding Date , which, as Deadline revealed in December, Tracy Oliver has come on board to write based on Jasmine Guillory’s book; and an adaptation of Carley Fortune’s Meet Me at the Lake . The Sussex-EP’d documentary Cookie Queens was released two weeks ago by Roadside Attractions. Director Alysa Nahmias’s deep dive into Girl Scout Cookie season had a nice $328k debut on 446 screens. Markle told Deadline at the film’s Sundance premiere in January, “I was a Girl Scout, my mom was a troupe leader. And I think the value of friendship, of being dedicated to a goal as you can see that in Cookie Queens , it’s so reflective of how these girls stick with something that’s important to them and don’t give up. articles.title: ‘Widow’s Bay’ Ups Jeff Hiller To Series Regular For Season 2
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Antonia Blyth Antonia Blyth Executive Editor, Awardsline @antoniablyth More Stories By Antonia ‘Remarkably Bright Creatures’ Star Sally Field Has An Appreciation For Octopuses & Anger Jason Segel Says ‘Shrinking’ Season 4 Will Move Past Acute Grief: “Like A Rom-Com To Me To Try Again At 45 Years Old” – Contenders TV Nominees Studio Octavia Spencer “Felt It Was Incumbent On Me As A Citizen Of The World” To Make ‘Lost Women Of Alaska’ – Contenders TV Nominees Studio View All August 19, 2026 3:31pm Apple TV EXCLUSIVE: Widow’s Bay fans can look forward to a lot more laughs (and possibly screams) with Jeff Hiller in future, Deadline has learned. Come Season 2, Hiller will make the jump from guest star to series regular on the mega-hit much Emmy-nominated show about a haunted Massachusetts island. Hiller, who is repped by Innovative Artists and Odenkirk Provissero Entertainment, met Widow’s Bay creator Katie Dippold in an improv group some 25 years ago. He recently told Deadline that he’d initially sent in a self-tape without telling his old friend. Then, when he was cast, Dippold had warned him that the only role available was a Town Hall staffer who dies. Later, as her script evolved, she called him and said, “Do you mind if I don’t kill you?” Related Stories News All The Songs In 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 So Far Casting 'Murderbot' Adds Steve Buscemi, Wanda Sykes, Patton Oswalt & Many More To Season 2 Cast In the show, Hiller plays Dale, a Town Hall staffer under Matthew Rhys ‘ Mayor Tom Loftis. And in Season 1, Hiller became particularly celebrated for Dale’s iconic scream: “This place is a death trap! RUN!” Watch on Deadline “I have a shorthand with Katie,” Hiller said, recalling their improv years. “She liked when I would melt down and scream. The whole team would always make me do these dramatic monologues where I would end up screaming and crying on the ground. It was a funny bit. And when I read that, I was like, ‘Oh, she wants this .’” Jeff Hiller as Dale and Kate O’Flynn as Patricia in ‘Widow’s Bay’. Apple TV The Apple TV comedy series has garnered a total 19 Emmy nominations, making it the frontrunner of all the new shows this year. And Hiller is Emmy-nominated this year for his guest role of Larry in another Apple TV show, Pluribus — Vince Gilligan’s drama series about a mind-melding pandemic starring Rhea Seehorn as its virus-immune lead. Hiller also won an Emmy last year for his supporting role of Joel in Somebody, Somewhere. This past weekend, Hiller told Deadline that slipping into improv on Widow’s Bay was “actually very tempting. And I didn’t always succeed. They said, ‘We’ll cut around that.’” But one bit made the final cut, he revealed. “One that I think I’m weirdly proud of that literally no one has said that they liked is when Tom is talking and saying, ‘I don’t think this microphone is on.’ And then I say, ‘I can hear you.’” Dale Dickey as Rosemary and Jeff Hiller as Dale in ‘Widow’s Bay’. Dippold is currently in the Widow’s Bay Season 2 writers’ room and has yet to reveal exact plans, but Rhys said the Season 1 finale is “the ultimate setup, I think, for a Season 2. Massive cliffhanger. I’m just talking personally now. A father who now knows the folklore is true. Therefore, if he suddenly leaves the island, his son will die. He realizes he has the Scooby-Doo mission. It’s like, OK, how do we figure this out? What breaks the curse?” The show also stars Stephen Root as local fisherman Wyck. As for what he’d like to see in Season 2, Root told us, “I would love to know more about the backstory. What made Wyck Wyck? What kind of scenes did he see when he was a kid or a young man to make him to want to be a protector of the island to get him to the point where he couldn’t stand it anymore and he said, ‘No, I’m not sitting back anymore. I’m going to tell this mayor that I don’t respect, that I’m going to come out and I’m going to sound the [warning] siren.’” David Ferino/ Deadline And Kate O’Flynn, who has become another fan favorite as Patricia, said, “Next season, I don’t know, but I would love to play a British ancestor of Patricia or something… I like the idea of wigging up and doing a bit of period drama. Why not?” Widow’s Bay Emmy nominees include lead actor Rhys, supporting actors Root, O’Flynn and Dale Dickey as Rosemary, and guest stars Hamish Linklater as the island’s ancient founder Richard Warren and Betty Gilpin as Warren’s wife Sarah, alongside celebrated co-stars Kevin Carroll as Sheriff Bechir, K Callan as secretary June and Kingston Rumi Southwick as Loftis’ son Evan. articles.title: IATSE Local 479 Leadership Suspended Amid Corruption Concerns
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Earle Meets World’ Trailer: Alix Earle Teases Even More “Unfiltered” Look At Her Life, Including Alex Cooper Drama, In Netflix Unscripted Series ‘My Life With The Walter Boys’ Quietly Returns To Netflix For Season 3; Shane Gillis Comedy ‘Tires’ Gets A Boost ‘Hidden Heroes: A Descendants Story’ Adds Darren Criss, Sherry Cola, James Monroe Iglehart & More As Iconic Disney Characters View All August 19, 2026 3:45pm IATSE Getty Images IATSE has suspended leadership at a prominent U.S. local amid allegations of corruption. Local 479, which represents more than 7,000 film and television technicians across Georgia and Alabama, has been temporarily placed under the stewardship of several special representatives after President Matthew Loeb “declared an emergency” at the division last month, according to a letter sent to members and obtained by Deadline. “This decision was the result of an investigation in which reliable and credible information was brought to my knowledge that the property and membership rights of the Local were subject to irreparable injury if there was no temporary intervention,” Loeb’s letter to members read. Related Stories News DGA & IATSE Urge Fast Track On Paramount-WBD Merger Standoff For Fears That Prolonged Court Battle Will Hurt Jobs News TV & Film Scribes Aren't Spinning A Tale This Time: Jobs Really Have Plummeted In The Last Decade In elected leadership’s stead, Loeb has appointed IATSE International Trustee Andrew Oyaas, International Representative Jamie Fry, Special Representatives Daniel Mahoney and Kevin Amick as the Local’s temporary trustees. Watch on Deadline The letter cites Article Seven, Section 16 of the union’s constitution, which bestows Loeb with the power to remove local leadership “where reliable and credible information is brought to the knowledge of the International President indicating that a condition exists in an affiliated local union whereby the actions of the officers or members thereof endanger the property rights or interests of this Alliance…” While the exact nature of the allegations are unclear, Deadline understands that there were financial issues that were recently brought to international leadership’s attention and prompted further investigation. Per the note from Loeb, a hearing on the matter was scheduled for July 20, which is typically a forum for elected officers to plead their own case on the matter and present evidence to contradict international leaders’ claims. Details on the hearing, as well as potential next steps, are scarce. IATSE declined to comment on the internal matter but confirmed to Deadline that Local 479 remains under a conservatorship. International leadership is juggling quite a bit of strife recently. In addition to apparent internal turmoil, the union is also contending with the possible outcomes of Paramount’s $110-billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery. As the antitrust suits move toward a March trial date, Loeb joined forces with DGA executive director Russ Hollander to encourage a quicker reconciliation between Paramount CEO David Ellison and California Attorney General Rob Bonta (who is leading one of the two lawsuits) — whether in court or not. The ongoing merger saga has begun to divide the Hollywood labor community. While DGA and IATSE have expressed a desire to swiftly end the fight, the WGA is also separately suing to block the merger and appears willing to go the distance to do so. SAG-AFTRA has publicly opposed the merger but has not joined the writers in court. Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. articles.title: Hayden Panettiere’s ‘Heroes’ Dad Jack Coleman Pays Tribute To “Extraordinary Young Woman”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Hayden Panettiere’s ‘Heroes’ Dad Jack Coleman Pays Tribute To “Extraordinary Young Woman” ‘Furious’ Actor Steve Way Praises Creator Liz Meriwether For Depicting Disabled Romance In “Beautiful, Healthy Way” Nicola Coughlan On Smaller ‘Bridgerton’ Season 5 Role Amid ‘Only Murders In The Building’ Filming: “I Had Such An Epic Run” View All August 19, 2026 8:12pm Jack Coleman and Hayden Panettiere in 'Heroes' Chris Haston/NBC/Courtesy Everett Collection As Hollywood and fans mourn the death of Hayden Panettiere , her Heroes onscreen dad is recalling the late actress’ talent and heart. Jack Coleman , who starred as Claire’s (Panettiere) father Noah Bennett on the NBC superhero drama, remembered Panettiere as a “prodigious talent” and “extraordinary young woman” in a heartfelt statement after her death at age 36 . “I’m heartbroken. I couldn’t begin to put my thoughts into words until now, and they will be inadequate,” he began on Instagram . “I’ve loved Hayden since day one of the pilot of Heroes , 20 years ago, when she introduced herself by shouting ‘daddy’ and throwing her arms around me. From that day on, she called me daddio. She was Haydini, because she was a magician.” Related Stories Obituaries Hayden Panettiere Dies: “Heroes,’ ‘Nashville’ & ‘Scream’ Star Was 36 News Hayden Panettiere’s ‘Heroes’ Co-Stars Pay Tribute To Actress: Greg Grunberg, Dania Ramirez, Masi Oka & More Coleman continued, “She was a prodigious talent. During an early scene, a tear rolled down her cheek on the same line, take after take. I marveled at her technique. ‘It’s not technique,’ she corrected me. ‘I’m not a trained seal. I feel it and the tears just happen to come at that moment.’ She was 16.” Watch on Deadline The actor took aim at the members of the press who “routinely asked obnoxious questions, mostly some version of ‘when are you going to go off the rails?’ Today, we’d recognize those questions for the misogynistic provocations they were.” View this post on Instagram “She was hunted,” he recalled. “Everywhere she went, there were photographers with 300 millimeter lenses—the kind that can make even the most innocent activity look sinister. Once, when she came to our house, paparazzi hid in the bushes behind our yard and drove onto neighbors’ lawns. They were predatory. No one, especially a teenager, should be targeted that way.” Coleman starred alongside Panettiere for the show’s four-season run from 2006 to 2010, during which she played a high school cheerleader who has regenerative powers. Unbeknownst to Claire, her father Noah works for a secret agency that wants to terminated people with special abilities. “She brought joy to the set and a photographic memory,” Coleman continued. “Everyone was in awe of her ability to bring it every take. A tiny colossus who loved to laugh. We laughed a lot. That shining face, that megawatt smile, that wasn’t just for the camera. That was her. She glowed. “Today I’m filled with sorrow and regret. And anger. But that’s for another time. Right now I want to remember an extraordinary young woman who was blessed and cursed. She was vulnerable. She felt everything. It made her a remarkable actor and susceptible to the heartache and thousand natural shocks that flesh is heir to.” Coleman added, “I love you, Hayden. I’ll miss you. I’m so sorry you suffered. I’ll remember how happy you were on set and on the European press tour; how you championed Tess when she was being bullied; your commitment to animal welfare and the courage to put yourself in harm’s way to protect them. I only wish you had been given that same protection. Good night, sweet girl. And flights of angels sing thee to thy rest.” On Monday, Panettiere’s rep confirmed the actress’ death to Deadline, as police in Greenville, South Carolina initially announced that no foul play was suspected. articles.title: ‘Sons Of Anarchy’ Creator Kurt Sutter Endorses Charlie Hunnam’s FX Series ‘Legends’ That Reunites Cast Of Biker Drama: “I Think You’ll Dig It”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Sons Of Anarchy’ Creator Kurt Sutter Endorses Charlie Hunnam’s FX Series ‘Legends’ That Reunites Cast Of Biker Drama: “I Think You’ll Dig It” ‘Good American Family’ To Take On Lorena Bobbitt As Hulu Orders Second Installment Of Anthology Series From Katie Robbins & Ellen Pompeo ‘Outer Banks’ Prequel Coming Together At Netflix As Hit YA Series Wraps Five-Season Run View All August 19, 2026 10:34pm (L-R): Charlie Hunnam, Kurt Sutter Getty Images Sons of Anarchy creator/executive producer Kurt Sutter took to Instagram to assure his followers that he is OK with series star Charlie Hunnam and FX doing a meta take on his motorcycle gang drama with new limited series Legends . “I’m not involved with Legends at all, nor should I be,” Sutter, wearing a yellow beanie, said in the video filmed in a “hot box”. “It has nothing to do with the characters I created or the mythology. It is really about the show and the legacy of the show, and quite frankly, there are thousands of people who are responsible for that legacy.” Related Stories Casting Charlie Hunnam Gets 'Sons Of Anarchy' Gang Back Together For FX Meta-Series 'Legends' News 'Love Story' Stars On Playing An Iconic Romance: The Fights, The Fashion And The New York Of The '90s - Contenders TV Nominees Studio Developed and executive produced by Hunnam, Legends stars Hunnam and fellow SoA cast members Ron Perlman, Sutter’s wife Katey Sagal, Maggie Siff, Mark Boone Junior, Tommy Flanagan, Kim Coates and Theo Ross. Watch on Deadline Drawing parallels to Galaxy Quest , in Legends , when the cast of Sons of Anarchy (who will all play themselves) reunites at a fan convention after more than a decade, the line between life and art blurs as the fractured brotherhood finds itself up against a real-world threat more dangerous than anything they ever faced in their show. “Just want folks to know that Charlie came to me early on, when he was in the process of pitching this to the network, to ask for my blessing, knowing that the IP would probably not be able to be invoked for various reasons of legalese stuff, and I gave Charlie my full blessing,” Sutter said. “I wish nothing but the best for him in this project. My wife is in the project.” Sutter, who had a recurring role on SoA, was creator executive producer and showrunner of the series, which ran on FX for seven seasons, and co-creator/executive producer of the spinoff Mayans M.C. Sutter was fired from the latter in October 2019 and at the time had some choice parting words for his bosses who let him go after an internal investigation into cast and crew complaints, longtime collaborators John Landgraf and Dana Walden. Time tends to heal wounds. “I have nothing but love for John Landgraf and the folks at FX who have been so good to me, so generous,” Sutter said tonight before giving Legends thumbs-up. “It has my full-blown ‘Watch this motherf*cker’ because I’ve taken a peek at the script that was perhaps just lying on my wife’s knitting table, and it’s so well done, and I think you’ll dig it,” he said. “I love Charlie to death, and I think you will have mad love for this project as well.” Legends is developed and executive produced by Hunnam and Jonathan Groff, who serves as showrunner, with Rob Mac, Nicholas Frenkel and Jackie Cohn also serving as executive producers. The series is produced by FX Productions and 20th Television and will be available to watch on FX and Hulu. Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. articles.title: Naomi Watts Set For Zurich’s Golden Eye Award
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Naomi Watts Set For Zurich’s Golden Eye Award ‘Club Kid’ Trailer: Jordan Firstman Is A Messy Father In His Buzzy Directorial Debut Oscars: Czech Republic Selects Documentary Feature ‘If Pigeons Turned To Gold’ For International Feature Film Race View All August 19, 2026 10:53pm Naomi Watts Juan KR. Naomi Watts will be honored at the Zurich Film Festival with the Golden Eye Award. The festival said Watts is being honored for her “outstanding performance in Ben Shirinian’s The Housewife .” Watts will present the film in Zurich. She stars as the enigmatic wife of a suspected Nazi in the feature. Watts will pick up the award on September 26 and take part in a Zurich masterclass session. “Since her breakthrough in David Lynch’s Mulholland Drive , Naomi Watts has been one of the most fascinating actresses of our time,” Christian Jungen, CEO of the Zurich Film Festival , said in a statement. “Her greatest performances thrive on the tension between glamour and darkness, between what a character reveals and what she conceals – making her the kind of character actress Hitchcock would have loved.” Related Stories Festivals Zurich Film Festival: Peter Farrelly's 'I Play Rocky' & Channing Tatum Starrer 'Josephine' Among Gala Titles News Zurich & El Gouna Film Festivals Strike Strategic Partnership Kicking Off With 'Dolphins: My Close Encounters' Watts was born in 1968 in Shoreham, Kent. She later lived in Wales before moving to Australia with her mother. After working as a model and appearing in smaller roles in Australian television productions, Watts moved to Los Angeles in the 1990s. Some of her screen credits include Alejandro González Iñárritu’s 21 Grams , for which she received her first Academy Award nomination for Best Actress. A second nomination followed in 2013 for her role as a survivor of the 2004 tsunami in The Impossible . Watch on Deadline Jungen added: “ In The Housewife , she masters this ambiguity as an elegant and mysterious woman. At the same time, the film tells a true story that powerfully illustrates how indispensable investigative journalism is in uncovering historical crimes. Naomi Watts delivers one of the most compelling performances of her career, and we are proud to honor her with the Golden Eye Award.” The 2026 Zurich Film Festival runs from September 24 to October 4. articles.title: BFI To Launch Refreshed Film Academy Programme With 12 New Skills Hubs Across The UK
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac BFI To Launch Refreshed Film Academy Programme With 12 New Skills Hubs Across The UK Naomi Watts Set For Zurich’s Golden Eye Award ‘Club Kid’ Trailer: Jordan Firstman Is A Messy Father In His Buzzy Directorial Debut View All August 20, 2026 2:00am BFI Film Academy Photo by Millie Turner/BFI. EXCLUSIVE: The BFI Film Academy, the UK film body’s flagship skills incubator for young people aged 16-25, is expanding with the launch of 12 new BFI Film Academy Hubs across the UK. The BFI has said the scheme will focus on “local provision and devolving funding across the UK.” The 12 hubs will be led by the following organisations: · BFI Film Academy East of England – delivered by 104 Projects CIC · BFI Film Academy East Midlands – delivered by Broadway Nottingham Related Stories Festivals BFI CEO Ben Roberts Gives Keynote Address At Inaugural UK Film Conference: "The Missing Piece, For Me, Is Having Film Firmly In The Classroom" - Edinburgh Film Festival News Isabel Davis Appointed Director Of The BFI Filmmaking Fund · BFI Film Academy London – delivered by CTVC Watch on Deadline · BFI Film Academy North East – delivered by Tyneside Cinema · BFI Film Academy North West – delivered by HOME Manchester · BFI Film Academy South East – delivered by Screen South · BFI Film Academy South West – delivered by Watershed Bristol · BFI Film Academy West Midlands – delivered by Rural Media Charity · BFI Film Academy Yorkshire and The Humber – delivered by Showroom Cinema (Sheffield Media and Exhibition Centre) · BFI Film Academy Northern Ireland – delivered by Nerve Centre · BFI Film Academy Scotland – delivered by Screen Education Edinburgh · BFI Film Academy Wales – delivered by Screen Alliance Wales This new model will run from 2026-29. The BFI has said each BFI Film Academy Hub will engage with schools, youth clubs, colleges and wider community groups to deliver year-round activity to enable local young people aged 16-25 to gain technical and transferable skills, access careers advice and networking opportunities to support them to pursue a career in the screen and wider creative industries. The Hubs will be responsible for curating and delivering introductory courses designed to provide young people with an overview of the film industry with a focus on below-the-line production roles, screen heritage, exhibition and distribution. Ongoing year-round activity – including networking events and masterclasses – will be open to 16-25-year-olds. Each Hub will also have a dedicated Alumni Manager. The BFI Film Academy has been funded through increased investment from the UK Government and ongoing BFI National Lottery Good Cause funding alongside cash from Northern Ireland Screen, Screen Scotland and the Welsh Government. Zakiya Bale, Head of BFI Film Academy Programmes, said the refreshed BFI Film Academy has been “developed to reflect the needs of an ever-changing and fast-paced screen industry.” “BFI Film Academy Hubs will enable young people from across the UK to explore career pathways and develop the skills most in demand across the sector, whatever their background and wherever they’re from,” Bale said. Ian Murray, Minister of State for DCMS, added: “British film is at its best when it tells relatable stories about real lives, and that means the people making those stories need to reflect the country we live in. These nation-spanning BFI Film Academy Hubs will give underrepresented young people the training and connections they need to build a career in film – wherever they live, whatever their background. “Talent is everywhere, but opportunity is not, and we need to put that right. These hubs will help close that gap and build the diverse, skilled workforce our film industry needs for the future, driven through regional delivery partners who know how to best support their local communities.” Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. articles.title: Seriesly Berlin Selects 18 International Projects For New-Look Pitching Competition
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Alison Hurbert-Burns & Bruna Papandrea’s Made Up Stories Launch Australian Production House The Set Up Vertical Video Economy Worth $150B, Even Without China – Owl & Co Report Dutch Kids TV Classic ‘De Fabeltjeskrant’ Getting International Revival View All August 20, 2026 2:18am Seriesly Berlin Deadline The Seriesly Berlin Project Pitches has selected 18 international projects from the likes of Star Trek: Discovery writer Ted Sullivan and British author Robert Wilson. Participants will take to the stage at the Seriesly Berlin Conference on September 15-16 at the Fotografiska Berlin in a new-look format that divides the projects in three – with the Writers’ Pitch introducing projects at a very early stage and the Co-Production Pitch showcasing more advanced projects. A new Vertical Drama strand has also been added to the program. Among the seven titles contesting The Co-Pro Pitch is Have You Seen Sabine? (working title), an Australia- Germany title developed by Australian producer Susan Schmidt and Avenue Road Productions about writer Virginia Peters’ seven-year investigation into the 2005 murder of a German backpacker in Australia. Related Stories News Dutch Kids TV Classic 'De Fabeltjeskrant' Getting International Revival Festivals Seriesly Berlin Sets Disney+'s 'City Of Blood' Among 13 Premieres I Am God brings German director Hanna Doose ( Dust On Our Hearts ) together with Mayana Films producers Zorana Mušikić and May Odeh (Cannes Critics’ Week Grand Prize winner A Useful Ghost ). The story seems a spiritual festival on the German-Polish border become an ensemble dramedy about healing and reinvention. Watch on Deadline Journey to the West – a German, Czech and Slovakian co-pro – is from Czech-Vietnamese filmmaker Dužan Duong ( Summer School ) and is based on oral histories of the Vietnamese diaspora in the former Eastern Bloc. A Czech broadcaster is attached for co-development. Portugal’s Small Death in Lisbon comes from British author Robert Wilson, who adapts his own novel. It’s in developed at SPi, the company behind Glória , Netflix’s first Portuguese original series, with that show’s creator, Pedro Lopes, among the writers. Another from Germany, The Fallen (working title) unites writer Janett Lederer with Milk teeth director Sophia Bösch and Oksuperdanke producers Linda Hartogs and Dominik Eder for a story of female friendship in a Catholic home for unmarried pregnant women in 1978. The Man Behind a Mask comes from Latvia, and has Anna Kalniņa and producer Serge Serpuhovs from Baltic Pine Films attached. It was developed through the Midpoint Series Launch and is a Cold War thriller about the career of Latvian surgeon Viktors Kalnbērzs, who performed the Soviet Union’s first gender-affirming surgery in Riga in the early 1970s. Finally, Vamos from Italy is a sports dramedy from Berlinale Talents 2026 participant and American Film Institute alumnus Fabrizio Muscia. It explores the rise of padel through an ageing tennis pro forced into the one sport he despises. The Writers’ Picth will be contested by Ireland’s Black Valley , which pairs Irish actor-writer Michael Patric ( The Quiet Girl ) with U.S. writer-producer Sullivan ( Star Trek: Discovery , Riverdale ) and producer Mairtín de Barra of Tailored Films for the story of an unlikely friendship between a traumatised former Army Ranger and a refugee from Sierra Leone. Two projects explore Germany’s far right: The Verdict ( Das Urteil ), from Ali Hakim, Max König and Sandra Müller, pairs their Hakim + König Film together with East Gate Filmproduction, ndF’s new Halle-based subsidiary. It follows a defence attorney in Chemnitz taking on a case a whole city has already decided about who is guilty. The Baseball Bat Years ( Baseballjägerjahre ) is also out of Germany but comes from Venezuelan screenwriter Jorge Patiño. It depicts far-right and racist violence in Germany’s post-reunification years, and is billed as a “psychological thriller about a closeted man in a neo-Nazi cell who fathers a son through rape [and] draws a line from the neo-Nazi violence of 1992 to online radicalisation in 2022.” Bloody Bay is from the UK and was developed by London-based writer-producer Olga Rozanova ( Hope ) and sees four fifty-somethings, a new baby and one explosive secret trapped aboard a 48-foot boat. Italy’s Doggy Style is a multilingual mockumentary from German director, writer and photographer Marlon Rüberg about eight dog parents, one threatened park and a revolution nobody is qualified to lead, while Good Godmother from Serbia sees Belgrade-based animation creators Nick Strutinski and Kirill Semiletov sends a former Fairy Godmother become a therapist to fairytale characters. Hands Up , out of the U.S., is from Neta Weiner, Samira Saraya and Israeli showrunner Michal Cooper Keren. It’s a Berlin-set musical drama about an Israeli rapper and a Palestinian singer under growing political pressure. Vertical Drama Pitch The new Vertical Drama Pitch will see in competition Serial Eyes alumna Madeleine Féret-Fleury and Cédriane Fossat’s Deep Fake from France, a 30-part romcom thriller about a French-Korean influencer whose #30DatesIn30Days challenge turns sinister when a fake account takes over her identity; and Germany’s Just Do It ( Einfach Ma Machen ) – from Annekathrin Bach, Sophia Hein and Mirko Muhshoff – about an overconfident influencer who goes into local politics across 20 fast-paced 100-second episodes. Also out of Germany is What We See from Berlin-based journalist and former TV news executive producer Kate Mar. The 50-part social thriller follows what happens when the public reaches a verdict on a suspicious death long before investigators do. Finally, Worth to Know – an Argentinian, German and Spanish co-pro – is from Berlin-based Argentinian Elda Broglio and Luz Orlando Brennan. It turns the awkward questions of two new stepsisters 20 years apart in age into 28 four-minute episodes. The juries comprise among others writer Anna Winger ( Unorthodo , director Mattie Do ( The Long Walk ), agent Silke Bacher from Homebase Künstleragentur and producer Fleur Winter ( The Crash ). Through a new partnership with Cine Chromatix, the winning project presented in the Co-Production Pitch Selection will receive an in-kind post-production award worth €25,000 ($30,000) for colour grading services. The pitching programme is organised in partnership with the European Writers Desk and Creative Europe MEDIA Desk. Elsewhere, the SteinbrennerMüller Award will again honour one German-language project from the Co-Production Pitch and the Writers’ Pitch that, in the opinion of the jury, has the greatest potential to be successful with audiences. This will receive a communications concept from Berlin-based PR agency SteinbrennerMüller worth €2,000 each. “With more than 250 submissions, making this year’s selection was anything but easy,” says Dennis Ruh, Festival Director of Seriesly Berlin. “What stood out was how strongly many of the projects engage with the world we are living in right now. Creators are responding to political and social realities, but they are doing so through deeply personal stories. At the same time, there is plenty of humour and optimism in the selection. These are very different stories, but many of them have the potential to resonate far beyond the places they come from.” Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A. articles.title: Lav Diaz’s Venice Title ‘Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors’ Boarded By Heretic For Sales
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman , Liz Shackleton August 20, 2026 2:38am Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors Venice Film Festival EXCLUSIVE : Lav Diaz ‘s Venice Film Festival title Let Us Through, Dear Ancestors ( Makikiraan Po ) has been boarded by Greek international sales firm Heretic . The film, about Spain’s colonial subjugation of the Philippines, is one of the Filipino auteur’s shorter features running ‘only’ 2 hours 31 minutes. The film, which is playing Out of Competition on the Lido, charts the brutality of Spanish friar Padre Enciso over the population in the 17th century. The synopsis reads: “Spain forcibly transformed the Philippines through sexual violence, exploitation, and religious conversion. Thousands of natives died building 17th-century churches, whose grand architecture stands as monuments to colonization’s brutality.” Related Stories Acquisitions Lightdox Acquires 'Auber 89' Ahead Of Doc's World Premiere at Venice Film Festival Sidebar Giornate Degli Autori News Venice Drama 'I Matter', About Roma Experience, Gets Sales Deal Pic is produced by Bianca Balbuena (Epicmedia Productions Inc) and Montgomery Blencowe (C’est Lovi Productions), with Bradley Liew, Lovi Poe and Louis Wei as executive producers. Watch on Deadline Festival regular Diaz was in Cannes last year with Magalhães ( Magellan ), starring Gael García Bernal, another meditative historical reimagining about colonial legacy and human endurance. This is the latest collaboration between Filipino outfit Epicmedia and Diaz after movies including A Lullaby To The Sorrowful Mystery (Berlinale Silver Bear winner), Berlin Competition entry Season Of The Devil , Venice drama When The Waves Are Gone and Locarno entry Essential Truths of The Lake . Epicmedia is one of the country’s leading arthouse producers and is a regular at major festivals with credits including Rafael Manuel’s Filipiñana , which played at Sundance and Berlin, Truong Minh Quy’s Viet and Nam and Directors Factory Philippines , which both launched at Cannes, Kenneth Dagatan’s In My Mother’s Skin , which played at Sundance and sold to Amazon, and Lorcan Finnegan’s Nocebo, the first Ireland-UK-Philippines coproduction with Eva Green and Mark Strong. That Thing Called Tadhana is one of the highest grossing independent films in Philippine’s box office history. Ioanna Stais, Head of Sales & Acquisitions for Heretic, commented: “We feel incredibly fortunate to be working with Lav Diaz for the first time, a filmmaker whose singular vision and uncompromising body of work we have admired for many years. To be entrusted with bringing his new film to the international market, alongside the brilliant team at Epicmedia, is a real privilege for Heretic.” Bianca Balbuena of producer Epicmedia said: “We are extremely excited to work with Heretic for the first time, especially on a very special project with Lav Diaz. Their energy is so positive! We admire their auteur-driven slate and how they champion unconventional voices. We hope that this becomes a highly fruitful partnership.” Showcases For New ‘SNL’ Cast Members Just Wrapped: Here’s Who Stood Out L.A.
