articles.title: ‘All Her Fault’ Creator On Challenging How Society Views Women & Mothers In Thriller Series
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Industry’ Adds Cary Elwes, Dianna Agron, Sam Riley & More As Season 5 Guests ‘All American’: Tensions High Within The Vortex Amid ICE Raid Aftermath & Fight For Beverly Coach In New Season 8 Clip ‘Lanterns’ Star Kyle Chandler Weighs In On Premiere Twist That Sets In Motion “The Whole Mystery” Of HBO Series View All August 17, 2026 3:15pm 'All Her Fault' showrunner Megan Gallagher at The London in West Hollywood on Sunday Griffin Nagel/Peacock Of all the feedback she’s received on All Her Fault , there is one comment that sticks with creator and showrunner Megan Gallagher : “Those are two of the worst husbands I’ve ever seen on television, and neither one of them were having an affair.” It certainly would’ve been easy (and predictable) to fuel audiences’ distaste for the spouses of Marissa Irvine (Sarah Snook) and Jenny Kaminski (Dakota Fanning), the two women at the center of the thriller who are brought together by the disappearance of the former’s son, by adding an extramarital relationship to the mix — particularly for Jenny’s husband, Richie (Thomas Cocquerel), whose sins amount to far less than Peter’s (Jake Lacy). Related Stories News ‘All Her Fault’ EPs On Creating Riveting Whodunnit Series With An Ending “You Don’t See Coming” – Crew Call Live News Emmy Nominations 2026: The Complete List But, it also would’ve undercut the themes Gallagher wanted to drive home with the limited series, which explores the ways that women and mothers often shoulder the brunt of societal responsibility and therefore get the lion’s share of the blame as well. Watch on Deadline “I don’t think that that’s the worst thing that you can do to your spouse, necessarily. I really don’t,” Gallagher said during an All Her Fault x Women in Entertainment FYC screening at The London in West Hollywood on Sunday. “The truth is, if you are Jenny Kaminsky, and you are miserable every day and asking for help every day, and the person who’s supposed to love you and be your life partner is doing everything within their power to keep you miserable, that’s so much worse, I think, than having an affair. Like, I’d rather have you sleep with your secretary than do that. It meant something to be able to get that on the screen, that look at marriage.” It also gave Gallagher an opportunity to dig into the complexities of a woman like Jenny, someone she says “might seem like [a] pushover” but is far from it. “She’s a people pleaser by nature. She’s very clearly depicted that way, as somebody whose strength is in being empathic and being intuitive and kind of sensing what other people need,” she explained. “And I feel like I know so many people like that, men and women both, but I think that those people often have a very steely core down there.” Gallagher describes the scene where Jenny finally puts her foot down with Richie as the character finally “finding that moment of no.” L-R: Megan Gallagher and Deadline’s Katie Campione onstage Griffin Nagel/Peacock Jenny’s realization is fueled not only by her husband’s actions throughout the series but also by the revelations about Marissa’s missing son and the part her own husband Peter played in his disappearance. At every turn, Marissa blames herself for Milo’s disappearance, as do others, and Peter lets her bear that undue weight for most of the series without explaining his part in any of it. Ultimately, Marissa is a devoted mom who had nothing to do with her son’s disappearance and who was fooled by her own husband. Just like with Jenny, Gallagher says she wanted to challenge expectations for the kind of woman Marissa would be. “I purposefully wrote Marissa as an incredibly accomplished career woman who wasn’t necessarily a lovey-dovey mom,” she said. “She’s got a real edge to her, in a good way, in a way that I find relatable. I’m not a wilting flower. She’s a really strong lady.” Marissa’s devotion to both her son and her own sense of self was an important component to get on screen, Gallagher said, adding: “It’s one thing when society blames you or the media blames you and all that kind of stuff. It’s another thing when women internalize this guilt and we take it on ourselves. To me, that’s the most heartbreaking part.” ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Everything We Know About ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 So Far
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About ‘The Morning Show’ Season 5 So Far Everything We Know About ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 So Far Everything We Know About ‘Percy Jackson And The Olympians’ Season 3 So Far View All August 17, 2026 3:19pm L-R: Carrie Coon and Merritt Wever in 'The Gilded Age' Season 3 HBO Max The culture clash will continue in Season 4 of Julian Fellowes’ HBO period drama The Gilded Age , based on the turn-of-the-century time period in America that lasted between 1870 and 1900 . Some familiar faces have been promoted to series regulars since Season 3, and some new faces are joining the cast to play big-name historical characters, among other new roles for the large ensemble. Related Stories News ‘The Gilded Age’ Cast Throughout The Seasons Of The Period Drama Cancellations and Renewals ‘The Gilded Age’ Renewed For Season 4 By HBO For everything we know about The Gilded Age Season 4, read on: When will The Gilded Age Season 4 come out? Watch on Deadline In a video promotion released in December, HBO hinted that the newest season of the period drama would arrive in 2026 . Is The Gilded Age Season 4 in production? The show’s fourth season has wrapped production. Star Carrie Coon posted the news on her Instagram story. How many episodes of T he Gilded Age Season 4 will there be in total? The Gilded Age ‘s fourth season will have a total of 8 episodes. Will there be new characters in The Gilded Age Season 4? Yes. Deadline broke the news in February that Taylor Trensch ( Bat Boy: The Musical ), James Scully ( You) , Dennis Haysbert ( 24 ), Maggie Kuntz ( John Proctor is the Villain ), Neal Huff ( Mare of Easttown ), and Tony Award-winner Bonnie Milligan ( Search Party ) would be joining the Season 4 cast in recurring roles. Jim Gaffigan ( Chappaquiddick ), Dallas Roberts ( Walk the Line ), Elizabeth Marvel ( Presumed Innocent ), and Andrew Burnap ( Snow White ) have joined as guest stars . Gaffigan will play Grover Cleveland, the 22nd President of the United States, who comes to New York to curry favor with the elite class. Roberts will portray Daniel Manning, a seasoned politician and Secretary of the Treasury under President Grover Cleveland. Marvel will play Nurse Virginia Saville, a kind nurse who works at the Neighborhood Settlement House in the Lower East Side. Burnap will portray Porter, a young gentleman of Society with an Ivy League education and money to invest in exciting new ventures. Who else is coming back to The Gilded Age Season 4? Jordan Donica, who plays Dr. William Kirkland, and Ashlie Atkinson, who portrays Mamie Fish, have been upped to series regulars for the upcoming fourth season. Kelley Curran, who plays Enid Winterton — formerly known as Turner when she served as Bertha’s (Carrie Coon) maid, has also been promoted to series regular . Denée Benton as Peggy Scott and Jordan Donica as Dr. Kirkland in ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 3 HBO Max Series regulars since Season 1 include Carrie Coon, Morgan Spector, Louisa Jacobson, Denee Benton, Cynthia Nixon, Christine Baranski, Harry Richardson, Blake Ritson, Taissa Farmiga, and Audra McDonald, who are all set to return. What happened in Season 3 of The Gilded Age ? Donica’s character, Dr. Kirkland, proposed to Peggy Scott (Benton) in a happy, joyful moment at the end of Season 3. In contrast, George (Spector) and Bertha hit some rough waters in their marriage. This was largely due to Bertha’s rolling full steam ahead by forcing their daughter Gladys (Farmiga) into an arranged marriage . George felt he had no control and was angered by Bertha not wanting her daughter to have a shot at a love match. It’s worth noting that George is upset on Gladys’s behalf; however, she married the Duke of Buckingham and ended up falling in love with him! Bertha’s sister Monica (Merritt Wever) came to town for the wedding, much to the former’s chagrin.

articles.title: Kevin Macdonald On Capturing Pep Guardiola For Prime Video’s ‘A Beautiful Obsession’: “Like Having Robert De Niro Play A Football Coach”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max Kevin Macdonald On Capturing Pep Guardiola For Prime Video’s ‘A Beautiful Obsession’: “Like Having Robert De Niro Play A Football Coach” ‘Small Town Scandal’: ‘Only Murders In The Building’-Inspired Show From New Zealand Comic Royalty Proves Podcasts Can Be Perfect “Proof Of Concept” ‘The Boys’ VFX Firm Untold Hires Film & Episodic Chief View All August 17, 2026 4:01pm Pep Guardiola City Studios “Pep playing himself is a bit like having Robert De Niro play a football coach.” Those are the musings of Oscar-winning director Kevin Macdonald , who has just spent two years charting the exploits of Pep Guardiola and Manchester City for A Beautiful Obsession and yet had barely heard of Guardiola before he was brought on board by Prime Video, Plan B , Workerbee and City Studios . “He wears his heart on his sleeve,” said Macdonald. “He’s just so compelling to watch.” Macdonald, whose subjects have included Whitney Houston and Bob Marley, and who won an Oscar for One Day in September, believes his lack of interest in soccer was advantageous when following one of the greatest managers of all time. The docuseries charts Guardiola’s tumultuous final two seasons after winning an English record four Premier League titles in a row and follows in a long line of Amazon sports docs about soccer teams, although this one isn’t part of the streamer’s successful All or Nothing strand. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Netflix Unveils Live Darts Event With Teenage Sensation Luke Littler News "Remarkable True Story" Of Family Behind World-Famous Panini Stickers Told In Beta-Backed Italian Series 'Album Of Dreams' Asking stupid questions Kevin MacDonald. Image: Deadline via Getty “There’s something quite good about asking stupid questions,” Macdonald told Deadline. “I told him I didn’t know much about football and the weird thing was that really engaged him. He was like, ‘Oh my god I’m so fed up with talking about football.’ So we talked about books, films and all sorts of other things.” Macdonald’s disinterest in the UK’s national sport echoes that of Fisher Stevens, who directed Netflix’s smash hit Beckham documentary several years back and has also said in the past he didn’t know much about soccer when he took up the gig. It allowed Macdonald to get under Guardiola’s skin, the Scottish director explained. “I asked why he was so interested and why the players cared so much,” added Macdonald, who spent hours observing with the legendary Spanish coach, met him five times and interviewed him three times. “We tried to make a series that was emotional and human, and saw these players go through really dramatic events. I hope the series will be enjoyed by people who aren’t football fans, but are just interested in the human drama.” That drama came during the first few months of the period being covered in the doc as Guardiola, fresh off the back of his GOAT-like title quadruple, suddenly found results turning for the worst. Gavin Johnson, Group Media Director at City Football Group, who oversees City Studios, said filming this period was “quite uncomfortable for people internally,” but the team was commited to keeping the cameras rolling. “There is an acceptance at the top of the business that you have to tell deeper stories around the club and to do that you have to open yourself up,” said Johnson. “We’d had this amazing run and then we couldn’t stop losing for a short number of games and it was really really hard. Sometimes it was uncomfortable to watch but that is what makes good drama.” Macdonald said this created “authenticity and honesty,” which contrasts with the “first wave” of popular streaming sports docs from a few years back that “were quite constructed and quite limited” in scope. “Fans see that every Saturday,” he added. “They want something more – a kind of observational, vérité documentary that is quite rare in other worlds.” City Studios’ deep access comes from its unique position as an in-house Manchester City studio, chronicling the team all-year round. “The team we’ve built at City haven’t shied away from any area but have done a wonderful job to build trust, catch all of the content and work within the parameters we have to work within,” said Johnson. “These are top sports individuals [we are following] who have to try and win games for Man City. But also they’re human beings and that is the essence of what Kevin Macdonald has scratched below the surface of.” City Studios has a development deal with Sony Pictures Television for soccer content and Sony international boss Wayne Garvie has previously said he wants to find soccer’s Succession. Updating on the pact, Johnson said there are “three or four projects we are really excited about,” which lean on Garvie’s “expertise, contacts passion and knowledge,” but the world of scripted programming can be “frustratingly slow” compared with docs, he added. “The philosophical underpinning of the series” Image: City Studios So what next for Guardiola? Having won numerous titles at Barcelona, Bayern Munich and Manchester City, the 55-year-old is heading for a rare career break after turning down a job to manage the Italian national team. Macdonald said Guardiola is remarkably philosophical about the future. “He’s coming to terms with the idea that you cannot be the best forever, but you need to understand and communicate to those around you that you have to enjoy life whether you are winning or losing,” added Macdonald. “In a way that is the philosophical underpinning of the series. This feels very authentic coming from Pep. I kept telling him he was a natural Buddhist.” The docuseries launches August 19. It is directed by Macdonald alongside City Studios’ John De Caux and produced by Macdonald for Plan B/KM Films and Banijay UK-owned Workerbee, along with Johnson and Ged Doherty for City Studios. ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Before She Hosts Primetime Emmy Awards, Mariska Hargitay Goes For Gold With Triple Nominee ‘My Mom Jayne’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Lightdox Acquires ‘Auber 89’ Ahead Of Doc’s World Premiere at Venice Film Festival Sidebar Giornate Degli Autori ‘Traces Of Home’ Trailer: Award-Winning Film From EPs Melissa Barrera And John Leguizamo Tells Story Of Love And Forced Displacement ‘First They Came For My College,’ Film About Ron DeSantis-Led “Hostile Takeover” Of Florida School, Announces Theatrical Run View All August 17, 2026 5:05pm Mariska Hargitay in 'My Mom Jayne' HBO As Mariska Hargitay reflects on the past year in her life – a momentous one for the actress and filmmaker – a word comes to her mind to describe it: “cathartic.” She completed her 27 th season starring as Capt. Olivia Benson on Law & Order: SVU and in May made her Broadway debut in the drama Every Brilliant Thing – both exceptional achievements. But the catharsis emerged through an even more personal endeavor: her nonfiction directorial debut My Mom Jayne . The HBO documentary, an intimate exploration of Hargitay’s mother, the late actress Jayne Mansfield , and of a mystery surrounding the identity of Hargitay’s father, has earned three Primetime Emmy nominations, including Outstanding Documentary or Nonfiction Special and Outstanding Directing for a Nonfiction Program. Related Stories News Everything We Know About 'The Gilded Age' Season 4 So Far News Showtime! Buss Family Sells Remaining Lakers Stake To Bob Iger & Josh Kushner “The film has been, for me, the gift that just keeps on giving,” she tells Deadline. “It was an archeological dig of me not knowing what I was going to find, hoping that I had the internal architecture to support myself… Going into the unknown and not knowing what the other side was going to look like, it’s been so extraordinary to come out the other side with the results beyond my even dreams or comprehension, not knowing that the film would resonate with so many people the way it has.” Watch on Deadline Hargitay was just three years old when her mother was tragically killed in an auto accident outside New Orleans in 1967. Mariska and her two older brothers, Zoltán and Miklos (Mickey Jr.), were in the back seat of the vehicle but survived. Mariska and her older siblings were raised by Mickey Hargitay Sr., the man she grew up believing to be her biological father. Jayne Mansfield in 1957. Everett Collection Jayne Mansfield possessed great beauty and talent. She was multilingual and played classical piano and violin, but her exceptional good looks and curvaceous figure limited how the men who ran Hollywood perceived her. Mansfield accommodated herself to the sex symbol persona. In the film, Hargitay recalls growing up without her mom and becoming uncomfortable with how Mansfield had presented on screen. “I didn’t really appreciate the sort of bombshell image and didn’t like some of the [acting] choices she made,” Hargitay told us at the Cannes Film Festival, where My Mom Jayne premiered. “I felt myself being embarrassed by her and just wanting a normal mom and a regular mom and ‘pick me up from school’ and like that… I just felt like I dissociated myself and said, yeah, I don’t want to be part of that, and I want to do it differently.” Executive producer Lauran Bromley, director Mariska Hargitay, and producer and Trish Adlesic pose during the ‘My Mom Jayne: A Film By Mariska Hargitay’ photocall at the 78th annual Cannes Film Festival on May 18, 2025. Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images In the course of the film, Hargitay reevaluates her mom, forming a fuller picture of how Mansfield’s career choices were circumscribed by the egregious sexism of the 1950s and ‘60s. She also explores her mother’s complicated love life, and the blended family Jayne raised that included Mickey Hargitay’s daughter by his first wife. The honesty of the portrayal, coupled with the reality that many people experience blended families or complicated family dynamics has allowed viewers to connect with the film. A young Mariska Hargitay with her mom, Jayne Mansfield. HBO Documentary Films “You could say, ‘Oh, [this story is] about Jayne Mansfield, a movie star in the ’50s and her TV star daughter’; that’s not what the movie is about. It’s a family film. It’s a story about generational trauma, and it’s a story about identity and recovery and reclamation and forgiveness and so many things,” Hargitay says, expressing pride in “the way the film has been received and the way that people have said, ‘That’s my story,’ and the spark that has led people to investigate their own families to uncover their family secrets or just deal with them or just look at them closer.” Hargitay captures on screen her reaction to learning as an adult that Mickey Hargitay in fact wasn’t her biological father. Her dad was Nelson Sardelli, a Brazilian singer with whom Jayne Mansfield became romantically involved during a break from her marriage to Hargitay. That revelation triggered conflicting emotions in Mariska, who felt intensely loyal to Mickey Hargitay as her loving father and didn’t want it to seem as if, somehow, she were turning her back on him. “When we keep secrets, I think that occupies a big part of our psyche — knowingly and unconsciously,” Hargitay observes. “Holding this secret and feeling bad about it and knowing that there was a part of me that just wasn’t clear and allowing myself to be my authentic self — but out of duty thinking this is how it had to be to honor my father. And then when I came to the realization like, no, no, no, that secret isn’t honoring anyone. We have to tell the secret.” She adds, “I wanted to make a love letter for my father, Mickey. That’s what I wanted to do. But in the process, it turned out to really be a love letter to all three of them [Jayne, Nelson, and Mickey] because the film deals with the complexity of the human condition, the real complexities of what it is to be human and how two things can be true at once… I wanted to understand why. Who was the woman behind the pose? Why did my father never admit to me? Why did Nelson never claim me? And I got answers to all of it, and the answers were the most loving.” In My Mom Jayne , Mariska connects with Nelson Sardelli, and the half-sisters she never knew she had. “It was very cathartic and mind-blowing to hear Nelson’s side of the story and understanding why he made the decisions that he made and how complex the decisions were for all three of them in so many ways,” she shares. “I was freed up; I felt like this giant exhale.” Mariska Hargitay acknowledges the audience after making her Broadway debut in ‘Every Brilliant Thing’ at the Hudson Theatre on June 2, 2026. Rob Kim/Getty Images The freeing of psychic space has allowed Hargitay to pursue new avenues of creativity. She made her Broadway debut 40 years after her late mother had done the same. “She was 22 [when she made her debut] and I was 62. That was also a deeply extraordinary feeling for me,” Hargitay affirms. “And when I went to Broadway, one of the things that I took with me was a plaque that she got that said ‘Broadway’s Rising Star 1955.’ And so every night I would hold that before I went [on stage].” Hargitay will continue an extraordinary year by embarking on the 28 th season of Law & Order: SVU and taking on another major challenge – hosting the Primetime Emmy Awards on NBC on Monday, Sept. 14. We’ll have more on Mariska’s plans for hosting the show in a separate piece we’ll publish on Tuesday. articles.title: Technical Foul: Buss Family Dispute Now Leaves Lakers Stake Sale To Bob Iger & Josh Kushner In Purgatory
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Put Up Or Shut Up! Paramount Demands A Very Big Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Antitrust Suit On WBD Merger Nick Reiner Wants His Trust Fund For Top-Notch Defense Lawyers; Britney Spears’ Ex-Trustee Says No As Major Hearing Is Set For Monday Call Her Moving: Alex Cooper In Talks With CAA After UTA Exit Under Cloud View All August 17, 2026 6:15pm Jeannie Buss, Josh Kushner and Bob Iger Getty Images UPDATE: So, maybe Bob Iger and Josh Kushner don’t own 83% of the Los Angeles Lakers after all, or do they? It’s crickets from the Thrive camp today as reps for Jeanie Buss contradicted a earlier assertion from the remaining offspring of Dr. Jerry Buss that it is “time to use this opportunity to move on and exit gracefully while we still can.” Related Stories Executives Bob Iger Buys L.A. Lakers In Record-Setting, $12.5B Post-Disney Move News Bob Iger’s New Magic Kingdom: Fans & Media Wonder If He Can Bring That Disney Sparkle To The Lakers In a move that reeks of a Succession and Running Point crossover for which no one asked, a lawyer for Lakers governor Jeanie Buss insisted later Monday that the so-called sale of the family’s remaining 17.8% stake in the NBA team was all a “years-long pattern” and play by Joey and Jesse Buss to force the hand of their sister (and seemingly Dad’s favorite). Accusing the siblings in a two-page letter to their lawyers of leaking “false, defamatory and pernicious” info to ESPN ‘s Shams Charania “for the malicious purpose of doing harm to the Los Angeles Lakers so long as Dr. Buss’s chosen successor, Jeanie Buss, carries out her father’s wishes,” Adam Streisand further lambasted the so-called sale. Citing a 2017 L.A. Superior Court order obtained to clear up a previous Buss civil war, the Sheppard, Mullin, Richter & Hampton attorney states that “any attempt by the co-trustees to do otherwise, and any attempt to aid or abet the co-trustees as such, would constitute a breach of trust, breach of fiduciary duty and be in contempt of court.” Watch on Deadline He emphasized: “On behalf of Jeanie Buss, I demand that your clients make clear publicly that Jeanie Buss is the Controlling Owner of the Los Angeles Lakers and that your clients shall take no action on this supposed ‘vote’ to sell the 17.8% stake.” Contacted by Deadline this evening, Streisand said that there had been no further developments in the matter. As stated earlier, if the family were to cash out their remaining stake in the 11x NBA Champs, Jeanie Buss would lose her exalted governor status. Under the rules of the Adam Silver-run league, to be a team governor an individual must own at least 15% of said team. If the Busses are actually cashing out with a tag-along to Mark Walter’s sale of the Lakers there would be no family member in charge in any capacity since 1979. That’s an “if,” right now. What is not an “if” is that the NBA Board of Governors has to sign off on the initial sale to ex- Disney CEO Bob Iger and Josh Kushner at their September 15 and 16 meeting in NYC. Add to that Kushner will have to sell his piece of the Miami Heat to be able to take his big Lakers courtside seat. PREVIOUSLY, 1:56 PM: Bob Iger was feted like a Disney Prince at D23 this past weekend, but the ex-CEO looks to be scoring an even greater stake in the L.A. Lakers today. With longtime owners the Buss family voting to tag along with Iger and Josh Kushner’s $12.5 billion purchase last week of the NBA team from Mark Walter, the former House of Mouse boss and brother of Donald Trump ‘s number #1 son-in-law now own 83% of the Lakers. That’s a 17.8% rise over the 65% or so the duo had last week when the purchase from Dodgers owner Walter was made public after a frantic 72-hours of bartering. Kushner’s Thrive Capital did not respond to Deadline’s request for comment on enlarged ownership. However, the Buss family were court side with a statement of their own Monday. “We have decided as a family to sell the remaining Buss Family Trust shares to the Bob Iger group as part of the ongoing transaction,” the Busses said today to ESPN (which Iger used to lord over) after four out of the six siblings voted for the sale. “We love the Lakers, Laker fans and will continue to support Los Angeles; but it is time to use this opportunity to move on and exit gracefully while we still can.” As viewers of HBO ‘s two-season Winning Time: The Rise of the Lakers Dynasty know, Dr. Jerry Buss bought the team (plus the L.A. Kings and the Forum itself) in 1979 and brought some Tinseltown magic (+ Magic Johnson) to the NBA. Under the Buss family, with patriarch Jerry passing away in 2013, the Lakers snagged 11 NBA Championships. Last year, the family sold control of the organization to Walter for $10 billion. Under investigation for alleged dodgy finances, Walter flipped the team to franchise seeking Iger and Kushner almost as fast as a Kobe lay-up. Under both Walter and it seemed Iger and Kushner, Jeanie Buss remained a governor of the team. “We have enormous respect and appreciation for Jeanie, her father and what they’ve contributed to this franchise,” Iger told Rupert Murdoch’s The California Post on August “And we have every intention to honor the agreement that was made between Mark and Jeanie. If things change, they’ll change, but we’re going into this with enormous respect and appreciation for who she is and what she represents in the organization.” That era comes to an end now as NBA rules demand a governor has to own at least 15% of a team. ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: Charles Esten Recounts Sweet First Encounter With Hayden Panettiere During ‘Nashville’ Audition: “What A Great Gift It Was To Act With You”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Charles Esten Recounts Sweet First Encounter With Hayden Panettiere During ‘Nashville’ Audition: “What A Great Gift It Was To Act With You” “Just Heartbreak”: Connie Britton Mourns ‘Nashville’ Co-Star Hayden Panettiere ‘Clueless’ Eyes More OG Cast Returns Alongside Alicia Silverstone For Paramount+ Limited Series View All August 17, 2026 8:28pm Hayden Panettiere and Charles Esten in 'Nashville' Katherine Bombay-Thornton / ABC Following Connie Britton’s heartfelt tribute to Hayden Panettiere , who died Sunday at the age of 36 , fellow Nashville alum Charles Esten also remembered his former co-star. Esten was a late cast addition to the Nashville pilot and the last series regular to be announced in March 2012 on the country music drama about fading Nashville superstar Rayna James (Britton) who is forced to team up with teen sensation Juliette Barnes (Panettiere). In his Instagram post Monday next to a gallery of photos with Panettiere from the show, Esten recounted his first audition for the role of guitarist and songwriter Deacon Claybourne in a soundstage office in Hollywood. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Obituaries "Just Heartbreak": Connie Britton Mourns 'Nashville' Co-Star Hayden Panettiere News Hayden Panettiere Autopsy Shows No Signs Of Trauma “I had read two Deacon scenes before pulling out my guitar and singing two songs. I said my goodbyes and, hoping I’d done well, went to open the door to leave. Instead of swinging all the way out, the door bumped into somebody. Kinda hard,” he wrote. “To my complete surprise, It was Hayden Panettiere , who – in full Juliette Barnes mode – had been listening with her ear to the door. Instead of looking even a little bit caught, her face instantly bloomed into the most beautiful smile. Eyes twinkling, she clapped her hands and said, ‘That was so good!!’ I can promise you that in that moment, there was nothing in the world I needed to hear more than that.” That was the first time Esten met Panettiere who also was auditioning. “It was her turn to go in, so as I went to leave, I said a jokingly cocky, “See you on the set!’,” he recalled. Panettiere landed the role of Juliette weeks before Esten was cast after many rounds of testing. When he showed up in Nashville, where the series was filmed, to start work, Panettiere “walked right up to me, pointed in my face, and with that magical grin said, ‘See you on the set!’,” Esten wrote. “From there, we became fast friends, working very hard to play those 2 troubled Nashvillians, but always having fun and laughing a whole lot along the way.” As they butted heads at the start of Nashville , Rayna and Juliette also fought over Deacon. Rayna’s longtime guitarist, who had always been in love with her, accepted Juliette’s offer to co-write songs together and later joined her on tour. (In an unfortunate plot development, the two also hooked up in the third episode, something Nashville fans prefer to forget.) “She was, of course, extraordinarily talented, infusing her larger-than-life character with all the heart, charisma, humor, whip-smart intelligence, and flat-out magic that were, alongside whatever troubles and pain she carried, a part of her own personal palette,” Esten wrote about Panettiere. “What a great gift it was to act with her, sing with her, and to just be her friend.” On the show, both Deacon and Juliette struggled with alcoholism, something Panettiere had said hit too hold to home for her as it mirrored her real-life addition problems. Esten also recalled Panettiere being “extremely kind” to his wife Patty. “Together, we are heartbroken that she is gone, and praying for her family, and for all those who, like us, will miss and mourn her so dearly,” he wrote. “God bless you, Hayden. Rest In Peace and Light ❤️” Earlier on Monday, Britton posted her own remembrance on IG , which also featured a series of photos from the set of Nashville . “I have no words for this sad song. Just heartbreak,” she wrote. “I love you girl. Sleep easy now. 💔” View this post on Instagram ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Jon Ronson Culture Wars Series ‘Things Fell Apart’ Returns For Third Season On BBC – This Time Exploring David Vs. Goliath Stories
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Hayden Panettiere: Emma Roberts, Melissa Barrera, David Arquette, Viola Davis & More Pay Tribute To “Amazing Talent” Creator Management Firm CMG Talent Unveils Raft Of Hires DramaBox Sets Brazilian Vertical Series From Cimarron & Trio Of Colombian Originals In Latin American Push View All August 18, 2026 1:00am 'Things Fell Apart' BBC EXCLUSIVE: Jon Ronson ‘s audio series Things Fell Apart is returning for a third season next year. The new season, the show’s first in three years, will follow the British-American gonzo journalist as he explores eight stories of outsiders fighting powerful institutions. Per the synopsis, it will include “all too human stories about the moment one person decides to stop accepting the world as it is… stories about what happens when someone attempts to spark that hardest thing – a shift in power. Stories that often have unexpected – and sometimes terrible – consequences.” Related Stories News BBC's 'Vigil' Season 3 Teaser Sees Suranne Jones & Rose Leslie's Detective Pair On An Artic Trek In Search Of Answers News BBC Seeks To Subpoena Ivanka Trump, Jared Kushner & Don Jr. In Defamation Lawsuit BBC Studios Audio is producing for BBC Radio 4 and BBC Sounds , with Sarah Shebbeare the executive producer. The season is planned for an early 2027 launch, nearly three years after Season 2. Watch on Deadline Season 1 of the show, launched in 2021, saw Ronson scour history for the origins on the culture wars, while Season 2 three years later dealt with eight more stories about the new battle lines in the same cultural conflict, which had snowballed during lockdown. However, Ronson has now identified a new trend – individuals declaring war on powerful organizations, and this will be the basis of Season 3. “A new season of Things Fell Apart has become an event in itself, thanks to the creative excellence and hard work of Jon and his team,” said Daniel Clarke, BBC Radio 4 Factual Commissioning Editor. “There is simply no one else working in audio who has the same capacity to combine the epic with the intimate and to tell stories that make us think so hard, as well as evoking such spine-tingling feelings.” “I think we’ve managed to find some extraordinary stories about what happens when an individual takes on a Goliath – a powerful institution or hierarchy or belief system,” added Ronson. “How do these things go right, or wrong? How does a shift in power happen? And how do the institutions snap back? These are nuanced, unfolding human stories, with twists and turns, like mini movies.” ‘Nashville’ & ‘Heroes’ Star Dies At 36; Career In Photos; Tributes Spidey Posts 2nd-Best Third Frame Ever; ‘Oak Street’ Out-Dinos ‘PAW Patrol’ Demands Huge Bond From AGs & WGA Over Costs Of “Roadblock” Suit HBO Renews ‘IT: Welcome To Derry’ For Season 2; Brad Caleb Kane Sole Showrunner Read More About: Comments

articles.title: “She Left This World Far Too Soon”: Wladimir Klitschko Issues Statement On Ex Hayden Panettiere’s Death & Promises To Keep Her Memory Alive For Their Daughter Kaya
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom 2026-27 Awards Season Calendar: Oscars, Emmys, Grammys, Guilds & More Harrison Ford, Robert Downey Jr. & Ellen Pompeo Pay Tribute To Bob Iger As He Becomes A Disney Legend Watch Kevin Costner’s “Field Of Dreams” MLB Game Intro View All August 18, 2026 1:57am Hayden Panettiere and Wladimir Klitschko at HBO's Post Golden Globe Awards Party in 2011 Alberto E. Rodriguez/Getty Images Hayden Panettiere and Wladimir Klitschko split in 2018, but it was always clear that there remained love and respect between the two. Such was the case tonight when former heavyweight champion Klitschko spoke out for the first time about the untimely death of the 36-year-old Heroes actress, with whom he shared daughter Kaya. Related Stories Obituaries Hayden Panettiere Dies: “Heroes,’ ‘Nashville’ & ‘Scream’ Star Was 36 News Charles Esten Recounts Sweet First Encounter With Hayden Panettiere During ‘Nashville’ Audition: “What A Great Gift It Was To Act With You” “Hayden’s tragic death saddens me deeply,” wrote Klitschko, who lives in Ukraine, in a social media post. “She left this world far too soon.
