Panettiere had been open about her struggles with depression and addiction, the latter of which began when she was given “happy pills” at the age of 15. She got Heroes at 16, and graduated to drinking and occasionally taking opioids. Watch on Deadline Kaya’s birth in 2014 brought postpartum depression, which the actress also spoke about publicly.

articles.title: In ‘A Vineyard for A Lobster,’ Snowfall in a Ugandan Village Becomes a Political and Colonial Allegory
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 16, 2026 11:45am 'A Vineyard for A Lobster' Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors Snowfall in Uganda? Welcome to the world of A Vineyard for A Lobster , one of the works-in-progress film projects presented during the 2026 edition of Open Doors , the Locarno Film Festival ‘s co-production platform and talent development program for filmmakers from equity-seeking communities and regions where artistic expression is at risk. It is in the works from Talemwa Pius (short films Engaito , Rations , Bitingu ) and producer Emmanuel Gashumba of Uganda’s Gripmagic Uganda Limited. The team behind the project, presented during the second edition of Open Doors with a focus on films from Africa, was one of the two main winners of the Open Doors Grant. Related Stories Movies "It Was a Bumpy Ride!": Jack Rowan and Director Kieron J. Walsh on the Many Lives of Head-Bopping, Troubles-Set 'Skintown' Locarno Open Doors Spotlight 2026 'Too Much Music' Is a Doc Project About Ghanaian Keyboardist Kiki Gyan - and About Who Controls Artists' Narratives THR has compiled highlights about the movie and insight from Pius about the project and the themes it explores. Synopsis The equatorial village of Rukumba has endured months of drought when suddenly snow falls overnight, an impossible event blanketing the land in white. Kamuturaki (48), a failed trader once mocked for selling winter jackets under the blazing sun, becomes an overnight success. Byeitaka (40), a disgraced preacher, declares the snow divine and sells melted snowflakes as holy water to frightened followers. Kagoro (38), the timid chairman, watches his authority erode as the village reorganizes itself around the miracle. When British envoys arrive, promising support for Rukumba’s independence from Uganda in exchange for access to the snow for scientific research, the village committee embraces the deal as progress. As competing ambitions take hold across the village, tensions rise and unrest erupts, forcing Ugandan military forces to intervene. By the time the snowfall melts, Rukumba is no longer a community but a collection of competing interests each convinced the miracle belongs to them. Director’s note A Vineyard for a Lobster grows out of my interest in how colonial structures continue to shape authority, belief and communal life in Uganda decades after independence. It begins from a question of what happens when something foreign enters a fragile social order and exposes what was already unstable. In the film, an impossible snowfall in a Ugandan village becomes a political allegory, echoing colonial intrusion. Its origin is never explained; what matters is what it reveals. As each character assigns the snow’s meaning according to their needs, the village begins to fracture. I explore how collective failure forms through ordinary self-serving decisions. The arrival of outside interests reflects a pattern that has shaped much of Uganda’s history, where promises of advancement often come tied to the erosion of local agency. I want the film to feel grounded and unsettling, immersing the audience in a community breaking under its own contradictions. What was the inspiration for you to want to make this film? The film came from a question that has been sitting with me for a while. What really changed after colonialism, and what didn’t. Growing up in Uganda, you get used to certain things just being the way they are. But at some point you start feeling that a lot of these colonial systems are still there. The way authority works, even how belief is organized. It looks stable on the surface, but there’s always tension underneath it. The idea of snow falling in a drought-stricken village came as something like a foreign presence entering a place and forcing people to respond to it in different ways. From there, the story became about what that kind of presence would expose in the village. The snow doesn’t break the village. It brings to the surface what was already unstable, so we can finally see it clearly. Almost like putting a face and name to it. And then the question becomes, now what. How do we become responsible to each other? How do we build better systems? I’m interested in how people react to it. Some try to profit from it. Some turn it into belief. Others try to control it. And in the middle of all that, you start to see how weak the sense of collective responsibility really is. That’s where the film comes from for me. Not the event itself, but what it reveals about people when something bigger than them enters their world. How universal are the themes of the film, and why should people outside your home see it? Even though the film is set in a small Ugandan village, it’s really about colonialism across time. Not just what happened in the past, but what carried forward, and what is still happening now in different forms. You can see it in how resources are controlled and how decisions are made for communities from the outside. The film speaks to people who have lived through that kind of history, and also to those who are experiencing it in the present, whether they call it that or not. Because at its core, it’s about what happens when something external or foreign enters a system and begins to reshape it, and how people respond to that kind of pressure. At the same time, it’s also about responsibility. About what happens inside a community when systems are weak, when accountability is not strong, and when people start choosing individual survival over collective responsibility. We are very conscious of that while developing the film. Even though it has a strong commercial direction, we’re also thinking about how it can create impact beyond the screen. We’re already considering an impact campaign that can engage with communities where these questions are still very present, not just in Uganda but in many parts of the world. So the film is not only meant to be watched but it’s meant to start these kinds of conversations. What is the next step for you and your collaborators after Open Doors? Right now the focus is on writing the script. Open Doors helped clarify a lot of things, so the next step is to sit with that and push the project into a solid draft. At the same time, we’re continuing conversations with collaborators we connected with in Locarno, and looking at how to structure the project for the next stage of development and financing. We’re also considering a short film version of the project as a way to further explore the world and tone, and to build momentum around it as part of the larger journey of the feature. So the focus is really just on moving the project forward in a concrete way, both on the page and around it. THR

articles.title: ‘DTF St. Louis’ Creator Steven Conrad Has No Plans to Make More Movies
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By David Canfield Plus Icon David Canfield Senior Entertainment Writer View All August 16, 2026 12:00pm Jason Bateman (left) and David Harbour in the HBO Max limited series. Courtesy of HBO When he was 19 years old, Steven Conrad sold his first screenplay, for Wrestling Ernest Hemingway . In the nearly 40 years since, the Florida native has gone on to write Oscar-nominated films ( The Pursuit of Happyness ) and create acclaimed TV series ( Patriot ), but he’s found a kind of career landmark with DTF St. Louis , his savvy exploration of middle-aged friendship and sexuality among Floyd (David Harbour), his wife, Carol (Linda Cardellini), and his new friend Clark (Jason Bateman). “I don’t think I’d been nominated for anything before,” Conrad says. Now he’s up for Emmys for producing, writing and directing the HBO limited series — which received 13 nominations. “I haven’t made anything that had this kind of attachment to this thing in our business,” he says. “It’s all new, and I don’t know quite what it means. But I’m happy that people are watching the show. That means a lot to me.” Related Stories TV 'The Pitt' Showrunner Admits Season One's Notoriety Amped Up Pressure For Season Two: "We Had to Prove That It Wasn't Just a Fluke" TV 'The Beast in Me' Showrunner Knows That the Violent Murder Scene Was a "Potential Tune-Out Point" For Some Viewers Conrad talks with THR about exploring male friendships, directing his own writing and why he’s focusing on television for now. There’s a lot of admiration for the way that you explored modern male friendship in this show. Can you talk about the approach you took and the conversations it’s sparked? It’s the sort of thing that can go missing from your life — a meaningful friendship, one that you can invest some of your emotional life in, to get good news and then want to share it with this person. When you’re a kid, maybe it just happens a little more regularly, but when you grow up, it can really vanish without you even knowing that it did. There can be periods where you just have a realization that you just don’t have all that many people that you would consider friends. Most of us have colleagues and family members, extended family members. When you are able to absorb the entire run of DTF , it’s positioned initially as this MacGuffin, with this murder case. What it really amounts to between the characters, Clark and Floyd, is some means to organize their friendship around some naughty thing that they can talk about in the fort privately. It had more to do with stimulating their friendship than stimulating their sexual lives. And then I guess it latched on to a period where men were starting to realize in real life that these friendships were not there. There’s also a unique exploration of sexuality among the three of them. What were you hoping to find there? Carol’s sexuality is very different from Clark’s, which is very different from Floyd’s. If you have these things, these appetites like Clark has — to want to do X, Y, Z with an intimate partner, and he hasn’t explored those with his partner — they don’t go away. He doesn’t have the courage to incorporate this into his marriage, so what is your obligation to those kinks? Clark allowed me to write about that type of individual sexuality, the person who has forestalled an exploration of the depths of their sexuality. I don’t think I would’ve felt good about a show if I only had one character who was swimming in those waters because they’re all so different. I felt confident when there was more than one, and that this could be a set of deliverable themes. It became important to me to try to do it in a way that seemed genuine and relatable to anybody who is living and breathing and has grown up. As you mentioned, you open the show with this crime frame that is more familiar to a TV viewer, but it gets more complex and original the deeper you get. What were some core moments for you in understanding that balance? The launching points I have for a story deepening are different from other writers — for me, they’re images. Wanting to install a swing set in your backyard, which is all Clark wanted to do; it’s heavy and he needed his friend to help, but there’s a moment where he just found himself blocked and seated on a swing next to this new friend. When that landed for me, I knew I was going to block that scene that way, then the childish need to be with another person sometimes just to feel safe or to cope. You would think you’d get meaning and then blocking — that you wouldn’t get blocking and then meaning. Being able to direct my own writing, which eluded me for most of my career, now I can explore knowing that I’m going to control the directing part of writing for film. It’s allowed me to discover stuff like that. And then casting is not something anybody really cares to ask a writer’s opinion about generally, but they have to contend with my opinion now. And casting two guys who I just knew that they would be giving off this magnetism and they could draw each other together. You work primarily in TV now, after previously being associated with movies. What’s the appeal of the longer format? If you’re good at making serialized TV, one of the things you then will be good at is delivering episodes and then delivering seasons and then delivering a series. There are three different ways to occupy an audience. There have to be three different approaches to this story. I took that so seriously that in the TV show Patriot — the first one that this crew all made together — when it came time to present the episode titles, we ended up using handcrafted one-off art each time. I treat episodes very differently. They have their own arc; their own payoffs; their own beginnings, middles and endings. Caring to try to be good at doing that at the end of the day leaves you feeling proud about the feat. It’s a lot of work. I haven’t obligated myself to a film or been connected to a film for a few years now, and I don’t have any plans to do it. It just seems it’s kind of gone from my future, this idea that I would make films again. My appetite to continue to make television is really it now because of the length of the engagement. It’s also a longer engagement with the audience. People think about that differently than they do their favorite movie. Films just feel like they’re in frames in a museum to me. Like The Godfather — I admire it. But I feel connected to Succession . I know they’re not my family, but there’s an attachment I have to the extended ordeal that everybody has gone through and the multiple characters that makes me feel like I’m not outside it. That’s what television means to me today. Do you think that the week-to-week release also helps that? This was one show where I observed it gaining this momentum to become appointment Sunday-night viewing. There is something in the ritual of the night. We got lucky that we were on Sunday night because that’s an important night at HBO. Somehow the universe just quiets down over the course of Sunday afternoon into a hush. You’re feeling all this dread — everybody knows the Sunday feelings about school on Monday — so people were in that frame of mind. I like it if a show comes out every Sunday night. I don’t know if I would like it so much if it was Tuesday at 7 p.m. This story first appeared in an August stand-alone issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. To receive the magazine,

articles.title: Karol G Brings Vibrant Vibes to Los Angeles With Her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 16, 2026 12:24pm Karol G performs during the first of three nights headlining the SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California, on Aug. 14, 2026, for her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour. Jill Connelly/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images Coming off of her history-making Coachella headlining set, Karol G had an opportunity to bring the Latin love to the global stage with her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, and she did just that. She delivered an extended version of her festival set during the first of three shows at Inglewood’s SoFi Stadium on Friday night, as the 35-year-old Colombian singer-songwriter had the sold-out crowd on their feet, dancing from the second she appeared on the tropical-inspired stage to the final moment when she said her goodbyes. After emerging from a three-story stone cave structure at the top of the stage, which is a nod to the landscape and prehistoric caves of her native Colombia, she kicked off the show with electrifying vibes, first performing her fan-favorite song “Latina Foreva.” Wearing a gold sequin look, surrounded by backup dancers, she set the tone for what’s to come. Related Stories News Selena Gomez's Attorney Fires Back at Wondermind Lawsuit: "Completely Meritless" Music The Playlist: Seventeen's Vernon on His Hyperpop Roots, K-pop's Evolution and What Inspired 'V8' “We are going to sing very hard; we are going to do it with enthusiasm; we are going to have an incredible time; we are going to do it for Colombia,” she told the audience, speaking in Spanish, at the beginning of the concert. #KarolG opens night one of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour at SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles with hit song “Latina Foreva” pic.twitter.com/T2OCxps0vl — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 15, 2026 Throughout the show, it was clear Karol G wanted to highlight her home country’s beauty and culture, notably with the colorful stage designs and tropical landscapes. It’s also fitting as the tour ‘s supporting album, 2025’s Tropicoqueta , translates to tropical, flirty girl. The night’s vibes were also set when veteran actor Edward James Olmos — who starred in the 1997 film Selena , based on the life of the late Tejano icon, whom Karol G has called her lifelong idol — told the audience in a video message, “Nights like this don’t happen by chance. They’re born from passion, from talent, from hard work and from that unmistakable spirit we call Latino excellence.” Karol G further spotlighted that excellence in the show’s second act, when she performed several songs from her Tropicoqueta album that paid homage to traditional regional Mexican music , including “Tropicoqueta” and “Ese Hombre Es Malo.” She also brought out a mariachi band at one point as well as climbed on top of a massive, brightly colored macaw, a parrot native to the tropical regions of Central and South America. Karol G then slowed things down a bit with tracks from her newly released sixth studio album, No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto , which is an emotional and moody shift from the high-energy Tropicoqueta vibes. During night one, she brought out Cigarettes After Sex frontman Greg Gonzalez to perform their new song, “Después de Ti.” Act three continued to be a standout moment during night two on Saturday, when Bruno Mars also made a surprise cameo to perform his and Karol G’s new song “Still,” as well as record the music video. #KarolG performs new song “Después de ti” with Cigarettes After Sex frontman Greg Gonzalez during night one of Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour in L.A. pic.twitter.com/3iQxnB93Nx — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 15, 2026 The energy was later brought back up, getting fans back on their feet, when Karol G and her dancers started making their way to the illuminated stone pool on the B-stage. While passing by fans, she performed a slew of her hit songs from “Amargura” to “Tu Perfume” to “Dile Luna.” However, “Bandida entrenada” was one of the night’s most lively and sensual moments, when a drenched Karol G transformed into a water goddess and began dancing, rolling and splashing around on the stage, alongside her talented dancers. The love and appreciation that Karol G has for her fans was on full display ahead of the show’s final act, as she took several moments to interact with them. From taking photos to sharing embraces to singing together, the singer made sure to express her gratitude for those who have been supporting her. In one heartfelt moment that evoked cheers from the packed crowd, Karol G made a hand heart with a teary-eyed young fan while snapping a selfie. The singer closed out the unforgettable show with some of her fan-favorite bangers, including “Coleccionando Heridas,” “Si Antes Te Hubiera Conocido,” and lastly, the Tiësto remix of “Provenza,” turning the tropical cave into a rave-like party, while also waving the national flag of Colombia. Karol G next heads to San Francisco for her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour, before making several more stops across North America. After that, she’ll head out on her Latin America and European legs before wrapping up the tour in July 2027 in Milan, Italy. #KarolG closes out night one of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour at SoFi Stadium in L.A. with Tiësto remix of her hit song “Provenza" pic.twitter.com/x9e4JkPJnW — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 15, 2026 THR

articles.title: ‘Love Story’ Producers Didn’t Expect Carolyn Bessette’s TikTok Fan Army to Come for Them
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All August 16, 2026 12:30pm Paul Anthony Kelly and Sarah Pidgeon in FX’s Love Story FX Catalog the ways in which Love Story : John F. Kennedy Jr. & Carolyn Bessette could have gone wrong, and the tally might rival a Thanksgiving grocery list. Pressure on capturing the tragic couple and their time period was high enough before early test photos sent devotees of Bessette’s style into a tizzy and a legion of paparazzi to the FX limited series’ Manhattan shoot. But Love Story ultimately prevailed, commandeering online discourse for its nine-episode run and fetching seven Emmy nominations — including top limited series, one for lead actress Sarah Pidgeon and, shutting down any sartorial naysayers, outstanding period costumes. Power producing duo Nina Jacobson and Brad Simpson know they could make things easier on themselves, but, like with their previous historic collaborations with Ryan Murphy, the fun is in trying to capture a feeling on camera that’s no longer found in real life. Related Stories TV 'DTF St. Louis' Creator Steven Conrad Has No Plans to Make More Movies TV 'The Pitt' Showrunner Admits Season One's Notoriety Amped Up Pressure For Season Two: "We Had to Prove That It Wasn't Just a Fluke" Each true story brings a different minefield to navigate in terms of what’s verifiable information, what’s unknown and the varying public sentiments. Which needle was the most difficult to thread on Love Story ? NINA JACOBSON It’s about understanding both what was known about them and what was not known for so many people. Because, when we were growing up, they were like American royalty. They were icons. But with the subsequent generations, what we found is that people knew her so much better than they knew him. She had become a posthumous influencer. Yet, as much as people knew of her, it was only visual. It didn’t really have anything to do with who she was as a person. BRAD SIMPSON There were lots of recordings of him. He’d get tons of interviews. He was very public. We had to find her voice based on descriptions. And we just knew from all the research that, even though she presented as this WASP ideal and a sort of distant figure, she was incredibly warm and funny. Bringing that to life was one of our biggest challenges. Were you aware of how substantial the Carolyn fan accounts on Instagram and TikTok were? SIMPSON No, but we did know that she’d become this avatar for quiet luxury. Often, when we would get costume designers presenting us styles for actresses in our movies and TV shows, she would appear again and again on wardrobe boards. And we did know that there was a lot on TikTok about her, but we didn’t know how fevered it was when those early photos leaked and the world rained down saying it was going to be a disaster. It showed us the depth of the reach to people who weren’t even alive when she was around. I think you’ve been vindicated by a lot of the aesthetics. How did you capture ’90s New York without going wildly over budget? SIMPSON New York has changed so much more than we’d realized since the 1990s. It’s much easier to shoot period in L.A. New York has huge glass skyscrapers everywhere. There are bike lanes in the streets. It was a city that always stayed the same, and now it looks very different. Luckily, the places that were our main locations, Tribeca and the Upper East Side, had really stayed the same. I recognized quite a few restaurants, too. SIMPSON We were lucky that some of the iconic restaurants that they visited — Indochine, The Odeon, Bubby’s — are still there. We managed to shoot the last surviving restaurant of Sixth Street’s India row [Panna II], which has now been swarmed with people. We were lucky in that some of those places just have that same great aesthetic, but [our production designer] Alex DiGerlando worked really hard with our locations department to find places that looked right and gave us a sense of New York during that time. On a show like The Shards , we’re doing an interpretation of 1981. People wanted Love Story to evoke a well-photographed time. From what I’ve seen of The Shards , it looks very 1980s. Do you two ever do anything that’s just contemporary and easy? SIMPSON Back on [ The People v. O.J. Simpson: American Crime Story ], we didn’t understand. When we got into TV, we were naive. Our first script of O.J. had 110 scenes in it, and I remember the first visual production executive was like, “This is unshootable. There are no standing sets.” You’d think we would’ve learned that lesson by now, which is to write to standing sets and not have so many scenes, but we tend to gravitate toward stories that are a little bit historical and feel cinematic. JACOBSON We came to television as feature producers. So, on the one hand, we’ve learned along the way that a TV show is not just a long movie. There are some tricks to the trade. But at the same time, partly because we tend to alternate between books and historic stories, there’s an ambition to try to capture a feeling. You can never make a book adaptation feel just like the book, but evoking the feeling you had when you read the book or the feeling you had about real people or time, that is our north star. We like having something to try to honor, preserve, capture, embody and get right as an organizing principle in a way that feels honest, even when you take the liberties you have to take in order to tell any story. Looking at each of the eight episodes of Love Story , which was the hardest one to pull off — either logistically or tonally? SIMPSON Everything’s difficult. Even a show that doesn’t work is difficult to pull off. ( Laughs .) But one challenging one was episode eight, “Exit Strategy,” which is just the two of them in a loft as their marriage is falling apart. Ryan had always had an idea to do a bottle episode to show the tensions in the marriage. But that episode proved to be a real challenge — in a great way because we were stripped of all the clothes and other characters. It had to move us through their relationship. The writers, Connor Hines and Juli Weiner, treated it as if it was a play. We rehearsed the actors on weekends and constantly rewrote. Logistically, the hardest episode to pull off was “The Wedding.” We had to live up to the romance and re-create Georgia. And then, of course, the finale. There was the question of how much to show the plane crash, of how to be respectful while giving people the information they need and honoring what the characters went through. It’s been a few months now since the series aired. Has any feedback trickled to you from anyone surrounding the Kennedy camp? JACOBSON No, the Kennedys have not called recently. ( Laughs .) SIMPSON So much has been written about them. They’ve been documented in so many ways. We fell in love with all these characters and wanted to be respectful and make something that was a tribute. As a family, it must be hard to live in a public life. It’s part of what our show is about. But no, nothing has trickled back to us. Looking at a lot of your collaborations with Ryan — Crime Story, Sports Story and Love Story — how do you approach them at this point? How actively are you trying to identify stories that would fit in those franchises? JACOBSON We’re always looking. We’re like truffle pigs, constantly sniffing to find the next thing. What we tend to do is identify a few, put them into the works and wait for something to be good enough to be worth making. That doesn’t always happen at the rate at which we would like. SIMPSON I look at the way we produce as if we’re curating our own magazine. I grew up with Tina Brown’s Vanity Fair . I can imagine Crazy Rich Asians as an article about the rise of Chinese money and the culture of Singapore. You can imagine Pose as a feature about the trans ballroom scene. Every American Crime Story would obviously would fit in. I almost think of ourselves as editors, hoping stories come in well as journalists try to crack them. This story first appeared in an August stand-alone issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. To receive the magazine,

articles.title: Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn, Barry Keoghan and Harris Dickinson Seen Recreating ‘Abbey Road’ Album Cover
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 16, 2026 12:48pm Harris Dickinson (John Lennon), Paul Mescal (Paul McCartney), Barry Keoghan (Ringo Starr) and Joseph Quinn (George Harrison) star in Sony's Beatles movies. John Russo Fans got a sneak peek at Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn, Barry Keoghan and Harris Dickinson filming a legendary moment from The Beatles ‘ career for Sam Mendes’s upcoming films . The four actors, who are each portraying one of the band members, were recently spotted recreating the group’s iconic Abbey Road album cover. The original photo, taken on Aug. 8, 1969, features John Lennon, Ringo Starr, Paul McCartney and George Harrison walking in single file across a crosswalk outside EMI Studios in London. Via videos shared on social media, Mescal as McCartney, Dickinson as Lennon, Quinn as Harrison and Keoghan as Starr were seen recreating the cover photo for Mendes’ four-part Beatles biopic, titled The Beatles – A Four-Film Cinematic Event . Each movie will be told from one of the band members’ points of view, with all four films having interconnected narratives. Related Stories Movies Spider-Man's Next Move? Sony's Tom Rothman on Tom Holland's Future, 'Jumanji' and Beatles Movies Barry Keoghan's Big Cannes Plans: The Irishman Candidly Talks 'Butterfly Jam,' Playing Sir Ringo Starr and Tackling Fatherhood: "It's OK to Be You as a Dad" Harris Dickinson, Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn and Barry Keoghan recreate the iconic Abbey Road album cover for the Beatles Biopics 🎬 #BeatlesBiopics pic.twitter.com/ykRMa0zvpu — Beatles Biopics Updates (@BeatlesBiopics) August 16, 2026 While specific plot details are being kept under wraps, the movie did get access to The Beatles’ full music catalog when the band’s label, Apple Corps, granted music rights for the scripted films. Fans will just have to wait and see how many songs from 1969’s Abbey Road will be featured in the project. The films, via Sony Pictures, will also star David Morrissey as Paul McCartney’s father Jim McCartney; Leanne Best as John Lennon’s Aunt Mimi; James Norton as manager Brian Epstein; Harry Lloyd as producer George Martin; Bobby Schofield as road manager Neil Aspinall; Daniel Hoffman-Gill as roadie Mal Evans; Arthur Darvill as press officer Derek Taylor; Adam Pally as controversial music manager Allen Klein. All four Beatles films are set to hit theaters in April 2028, but the exact date has yet to be revealed. THR

articles.title: Alex Cooper Departing Talent Agency UTA
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Caitlin Huston Plus Icon Caitlin Huston Business Writer hustonca Follow Sign Up View All August 16, 2026 2:27pm Alex Cooper at YouTube's TV Upfront, Brandcast on May 13, 2026, in New York, New York. John Nacion/Variety via Getty Images) Alex Cooper is leaving talent agency UTA, amid a busy week for the Call Her Daddy creator, according to sources familiar with the matter. A source says Cooper is in conversations with other agencies, but nothing is yet signed. The news comes after Cooper announced an investment on Aug. 12 from WTSL, the Silver Lake-backed firm led by Patrick Whitesell, that valued her Unwell media company at $500 million. The plan is to use the investment to grow the company, which includes a slate of podcasts, as well as live events and a film and TV production arm including through acquisition. Related Stories TV Alix Earle Ready to Reveal "Chaotic" Life on Netflix Reality Show: "Filming Season One Was Insane" General News Alix Earle Reveals When She'll Address Alex Cooper Feud: "A Serious Struggle Behind the Scenes" However, amid the planned expansion, a report in Bloomberg last week also said that Cooper’s branded beverage line , Unwell Beverage Co, is shutting down later this year. Cooper has also faced a number of negative headlines after Bloomberg and Vanity Fair both reported claims about staff turnover and uneasiness among the staff, particularly due to the behavior of Matt Kaplan, Cooper’s husband and the company’s co-founder, who is said to have yelled at and berated staff members. Cooper remains one of the most popular podcast hosts thanks to the success of Call Her Daddy , but is now looking to leverage that into more with an expansion of her empire outside of podcasting, which may have prompted the move. A source familiar with the matter says Cooper’s team has spent the past several months planning out its future growth strategy, including representation, related to the funding. UTA declined to comment on reports of Cooper departing. UTA’s Oren Rosenbaum negotiated a $125 million deal with SiriusXM in 2024 for Cooper and the agency also repped Cooper as she launched the Unwell podcast network in 2023. The talent agency represents a number of top creators, including MrBeast, Charli D’Amelio and Alix Earle, who formerly worked with Cooper but left her network, causing speculation about a rift or possible feud between the two creators. That has been raised as a possible reason for the departure, but Earle and Cooper have both been at UTA for more than a year. THR

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere, Actress on ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Kimberly Nordyke , Carly Thomas August 16, 2026 8:06pm Hayden Panettiere Nathan Congleton/NBC via Getty Images Hayden Panettiere , known for her roles on shows such as Heroes and Nashville , has died, her father said in a statement Sunday. She was 36. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen,” her father, Skip Panettiere, said in a statement. “We ask for privacy as our family takes time to process this unimaginable loss.” The details around her death are unknown. Her rep said that an investigation is ongoing. Related Stories Business Kathie Hoops, Longtime Financial Executive at Paramount, Dies at 66 Movies Ian Crafford, Film Editor on 'Hope and Glory' and 'Field of Dreams,' Dies at 82 Panettiere’s credits also include the films I Love You, Beth Cooper (2009), Scream 4 (2011) and Scream VI (2023) and the title role in the 2011 Lifetime telefilm Amanda Knox. Hayden Panettiere and Milo Ventimiglia on NBC’s Heroes . TCDHERO_EC275 She was involved in a relationship with Ukrainian champion heavyweight boxer Wladimir Klitschko from 2009-11 and 2013–18, and they had a daughter, daughter, Kaya, in 2014. Her younger brother, actor Jansen Panettiere, died in February 2023 of aortic valve complications at age 28. In May, Panettiere had published her raw and candid memoir, This Is Me: A Reckoning, where she opened up about growing up in the spotlight as a child star, her battles with addiction, postpartum depression and more. The actress spoke with THR’s Seija Rankin about her biggest revelations from the book, including if she told people she would be writing about the personal stories. “I was fiercely protective of people in my writing,” she said. “I felt very strongly about my ability to tell my stories and make them entertaining enough to put in a book, without having to drag people through the mud. I had members of my team that I would bounce ideas off of, or ask their opinions about things like that I was writing.” She added: “I mean, my publicist is also my dear friend and I trust her, so I leaned on her to know. And then I made sure that Vlad [Klitschko, Panettiere’s ex-fiancé and father of her daughter] wasn’t going to be upset with me. But other than that, I just had to speak my truth — and it’s mine alone.” Hayden Panettiere with Connie Britton (left) on ABC’s Nashville . Everett Panettiere earned her breakout role in 2006, playing the indestructible cheerleader Claire Bennet on the NBC sci-fi series Heroes. She starred on the series for four seasons. She garnered more fame playing Juliette Barnes on the ABC series Nashville from 2012-18 and then as Kirby Reed in the Scream horror franchise. In her memoir, she also opened up about her struggles with Nashville , specifically how Juliette’s storyline started to resemble your own personal strife, such as her character’s postpartum depression and alcoholism. Earlier credits included One Life to Live, Guiding Light, Malcolm in the Middle, The Object of My Affection, A Bug’s Life and Message in a Bottle. Born on Aug. 21, 1989, Panettiere was raised in Palisades, New York, by her parents, actress-producer Lesley R. Vogel, who managed her daughter’s career, and Alan Lee “Skip” Panettiere, a retired captain in the New York City Fire Department. “My introduction to acting was actually at 11 months old,” she told Entertainment Tonight in 2023. “Playskool Toy Train was my first commercial, but, I don’t know if that would really be an introduction to acting, because I don’t think acting was involved at that point. I didn’t have lines, I was just playing.” Hayden Panettiere in Scream VI. Everett Collection She also shared that her favorite experience was playing Sheryl Yoast on Remember the Titans (2000). “This movie was my favorite movie to film; what an incredible time in my life,” she said. “That’s just pure me that look. That is like from, oh my gosh — I mean, I was 10 years old. I had such cute boys around me, I was surrounded by the cutest boys. Kate Bosworth was like my big sister, was close to everyone. … I mean, you have no idea how many times in my life I have wished and prayed — if I had wished to go back to any time in my life, it would be going back to Remember the Titans .” Panettiere earned noms at the Golden Globes, Critics Choice Television Awards, Teen Choice Awards and People’s Choice Awards for her role in Nashville . Her performance in Heroes landed her Teen Choice noms and a Young Artist Award. She also won a Young Artist Award for her role in Remember the Titans. MIke Barnes contributed to this report. THR

articles.title: Bob Iger Takes Victory Lap As He’s Named a Disney Legend, Applauds New CEO Josh D’Amaro: “You’re Wearing That Title Really Well”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All August 16, 2026 8:55pm Bob Iger gets his handprints with Mickey Mouse at the D23 Legends ceremony on Aug. 16 in Anaheim. Kevin Mazur/Getty Images for Disney Bob Iger is having a big week. Just days after it was revealed that the former Disney CEO was joining investor Joshua Kushner to buy the Los Angeles Lakers , Iger was honored as a Disney Legend at the company’s D23 fan event on Sunday. He joined a class that included Chris Berman, Jerry Bruckheimer, Susan Egan, Eric Goldberg, Anne Hathaway , Kim Irvine, Dwayne Johnson , the Jonas Brothers, Lin-Manuel Miranda and Alan Tudyk, in a ceremony at the Honda Center in Anaheim. A number of big names also came out to support the exec, with Al Michaels, Diane Sawyer, Ellen Pompeo, Robert Downey Jr. and Harrison Ford all on hand to present Iger with the final award of the night. Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Hits $2B Globally to Top 'No Way Home' as Sony's Biggest Release Business Disney's Experiences Chief Talks Figment, the Tomorrowland Refresh and All That D23 News “Over the years, I’ve had the privilege of giving this award out to dozens and dozens of truly worthy people, unbelievably talented people who contributed so much to this company, and so it is an incredible honor for me to receive that same award, particularly with this unbelievable class,” Iger told the crowd. “And I must say, following you up here is a little rough — Lin you make me feel talentless, Anne you make me feel stiff, Dwayne you make me feel small. I was going to ask if I could hold the Legends Trophy, but my biceps couldn’t handle it.” He joked that even though the years of giving out the Legends awards were fun, “getting one, it’s even fun.” Iger also took a moment to address new Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro — who has been holding court at D23 events all weekend — saying, “Josh, you’re wearing that title really well, and I am so proud to call you my successor .” Later in his speech, Iger noted, “Having the privilege of entertaining the world the way Disney does is quite a unique experience in life and a lot of responsibility. To have the ability just to make the world a better place is truly an exceptional life experience, and obviously, I am unbelievably grateful to have had that experience.” He went on to thank the company’s talent for their years of partnership as well as “the thousands and thousands of cast members who make this company really what it is.” In closing, Iger reflected on how “20 years ago, I was named CEO of this remarkable company, and I must say, no pun intended, it was a ride of a lifetime,” referencing his memoir of the same name. “Today is a vivid reminder of just what a wonderful ride that was. From the bottom of my heart, to all of you: to our audiences, to our subscribers, to our moviegoers, to our park guests, to our D23 members. Thank you very much.” THR

articles.title: In ‘Oasis,’ a School Spirals Into Violence – and Three Outcasts Take Refuge in a Forest (Exclusive Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Breaking Hayden Panettiere, Actress in ‘Heroes’ and ‘Nashville,’ Dies at 36 close By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 17, 2026 1:00am 'Oasis' Courtesy of Zeitgeist Filmproduktion Adolescent outcasts, identity and violence take center stage in Oasis ( Oase ), the much-anticipated debut feature of German writer-director Jannis Lenz, which will world premiere on Sept. 6 in the Horizons section of the 83rd edition of the Venice Film Festival . This one will be very different from that other Oasis movie at Venice, Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger , a concert documentary about the reunion tour of the famous band that brought Liam and Noel Gallagher back together. If you don’t believe me, just read this synopsis for Oasis . “When a viral video of a student threatening his classmates surfaces online, the school spirals into escalating violence,” it notes. “Crushed by the pressure of teachers and parents, three outcasts take refuge in a nearby forest. There, play hardens into ritual, and pain becomes an escape, until old wounds surface and the boundaries between them are redrawn.” Related Stories Locarno Open Doors Spotlight 2026 In 'A Vineyard for A Lobster,' Snowfall in a Ugandan Village Becomes a Political and Colonial Allegory Movies "It Was a Bumpy Ride!": Jack Rowan and Director Kieron J. Walsh on the Many Lives of Head-Bopping, Troubles-Set 'Skintown' The cinematic drama is an exploration of violence, body and identity – themes that Lenz has also touched on in his previous work. The cast stars up-and-coming German actors Florian Geißelmann ( Sound of Falling , Home Stories ), Anton Petzold ( Home Stories , Ouija ) and Mathilda Smidt ( Almania , Chabos ), as well as veteran Godehard Giese ( Rose , Transit , Babylon Berlin ). Britta Hammelstein ( Murder Mindfully , Woman of the Dead , The Sparrow in the Chimney ) and Ioana Iacob ( Do Not Expect Too Much From the End of the World ) also feature in the cast. Lenz directed Oasis based on a screenplay that he wrote with Alexander Dirninger, who also served as director of photography. The editors are Lenz and Melisa Krasniqi. “Body, space, and identity dissolve into one another, revealing the fragile beauty and quiet brutality of human relationships, while echoing the violence that shapes our contemporary world,” tease the press notes for Oasis . Check out the poster for the film, which THR can exclusively debut, right here. Lenz has previously turned heads with such shorts as Wannabe (2017), which got nominated for the European Film Award, and Soldat Ahmet (2021), which won several awards after its world premiere at the Visions du Réel festival in Switzerland. Oasis is produced by Germany’s Zeitgeist Filmproduktion and co-produced by Austria’s Wega Film and Germany’s Third Picture in collaboration with We Fade to Grey, Ocean Pictures Filmproduktion and Totem Films. The German theatrical release is planned for February 2027 via Mindjazz Pictures. Totem is handling international sales on the German-Austrian co-production. THR can now also exclusively premiere a trailer for the movie. School scenes, one pupil getting questioned about his threat of violence against schoolmates, and images of the protagonists in the forest create unsettling atmosphere. Oh yeah, there are also disturbing drawings. All in all, the audiovisual atmosphere teased here feels unnerving. But check out the trailer for Oasis yourself right here. THR

articles.title: Hayden Panettiere, ‘Heroes’ and ‘Scream’ Star, Dies at 36
articles.full_text: Aug 16, 2026 8:12pm PT Hayden Panettiere, ‘Heroes’ and ‘Scream’ Star, Dies at 36 By Pat Saperstein Plus Icon Pat Saperstein Deputy Editor @Variety_PatS Latest Ian Crafford, Editor of ‘Hope and Glory,’ ‘Field of Dreams,’ Dies at 82 2 days ago Tyler Duckworth, ‘The Challenge’ Reality Show Winner, Dies at 44 3 days ago Fans Remember Jackie the Eagle, Who Became a Social Media Star Worldwide: ‘Regal, Fierce, Deeply Devoted’ 6 days ago See All Getty Images for Paramount Pictu Hayden Panettiere , known for her roles on “Heroes,” “Nashville” and in “Scream 4” and “Scream VI,” died on Sunday, according to ABC News . A cause of death was not immediately known. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen,” her father, Skip Panettiere, told ABC. Related Stories Korea Box Office: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Becomes Second-Fastest Movie to Hit $1 Billion Overseas, Powers to $1.67 Billion Globally Panettiere had been on screen since 1994, at age 5, starting on soap operas “One Life to Live” — appearing on 27 episodes — and later, “Guiding Light,” starring on 45. In 2000, she landed a breakout role in “Remember the Titans,” and in 2006, she joined the cast of “Heroes” as Claire Bennett, portraying the cheerleader in 73 episodes of the NBC drama. Popular on Variety Panettiere later earned two Golden Globe nominations for playing Juliette Barnes on “Nashville.” She starred in 128 episodes from 2012 to 2018. On the film side, she is most known for her role as Kirby in 2011’s “Scream 4.” She became such a fan favorite that she was then asked to return for 2023’s “Scream VI.” She also co-starred with Michelle Trachtenberg in “Ice Princess” and appeared in “Bring It On: All or Nothing.” Raised in Palisades, N.Y., her mother was a soap opera actress and her father was a fire captain. As a child, she appeared on shows including “Ally McBeal” and “Malcolm in the Middle.” Panettiere published her first book, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” in May of this year. In it, she shared many stories from her life in the limelight , including details of her troubled relationship with her mother and abuse she endured through her life in Hollywood. She had also been open through the years about her struggle with alcohol and drugs. In 2020, she spent time at a rehab facility and got sober. In 2023, her younger brother Jansen died unexpectedly of a heart condition at 28. “When something that massive has happened to you, you really learn to pick your fights and just not let the little things upset you,” she told People magazine in 2024 about the death. “Because once something so horrific, so deep, so catastrophic happens in your life, there’s not much that can really rock you.” She made headlines following the People interview, when fans voiced concerns over her slurred speech, something she later spoke about via an Instagram post. “I hadn’t slept for two days prior to the shoot due to one of my dogs who was recovering from an emergency surgical procedure,” she shared at the time, also responding to claims about medication she may be on. “I was exhausted. My rep stopped the interview early as it became obvious that I was fading — especially as the subject matter became heavier… Grief looks different on everyone. Whether or not I am on medication is none of anyone’s business and is between me and my doctor.” She continued, “Mental health is so important, and I hope those reading this now understand that what you say hiding behind a computer screen can have a detrimental impact on someone.” She had a daughter, Kaya, with boxer Wladimir Klitschko, who retained custody due to Panettiere’s struggles with addiction and postpartum depression. articles.title: Hollywood Failed Hayden Panettiere
articles.full_text: Aug 16, 2026 11:03pm PT Hollywood Failed Hayden Panettiere By Marlow Stern Plus Icon Marlow Stern Chief Correspondent Latest John Oliver Brutally Mocks Trump for Sacrificing Staff in Airplane-Swap Incident 6 hours ago Matthew McConaughey’s First Screen Role Helped Catch a Murderer 2 days ago Shannon Elizabeth’s Long, Bumpy Road to OnlyFans Stardom 4 days ago See All Getty Images Hayden Panettiere , the former child actress who grew up onscreen before our very eyes, passed away Sunday at the age of 36 . She died five days before her 37th birthday. “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden,” her father Alan said in a statement. “She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.” Related Stories Box Office: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swings into Second Weekend With $43 Million on Friday Korea Box Office: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut While we are still awaiting a cause of death, Panettiere, who delivered her breakthrough performance at the age of 10 in “Remember the Titans” before starring in the NBC superhero saga “Heroes,” as fan favorite Kirby Reed in the “Scream” films and Juliette Barnes in the country music drama “Nashville,” had struggled for years battling drug addiction, alcoholism and depression, and suffered mightily at the hands of Hollywood. Panettiere chronicled her Hollywood highs and lows in her eye-opening memoir, “This Is Me: A Reckoning,” released May 19 of this year. Popular on Variety In the prologue to her book, she mentions the five stages of grief — and her belief in a sixth, floated by the author David Kessler in his book “Finding Meaning.” That stage is meaning, and Panettiere wrote that “my traumas have offered me meaning through a sense of humor, some ridiculous stories, prioritizing my health, a deeper relationship with my parents, pets I adore, animal rights and environmentalism that gives me purpose, and now, this book.” She continued: “All the heartaches I’ve endured have allowed me to come to a place of empathy and understanding for everything my loved ones have come up against and — most importantly — for myself. They’ve also given me determination. I’m like Dory, the resilient little fish in ‘Finding Nemo,’ who ‘just keeps swimming’ even when she comes face-to-face with a bunch of sharks.” Raised in Palisades, New York, Panettiere landed a series of commercials — the first at only 11 months old — before landing a role in the soap opera “One Life to Live” at the age of 5. She described herself as a “willful child” who wouldn’t be bossed around; a “tomboy” with a big head of curly hair and a “spunky, sassy attitude.” There are plenty of bright moments in her book, like the time she tossed a football around with Denzel Washington on the set of “Remember the Titans” — a movie-making experience she called “the happiest I’d ever felt as an actor” — and disappointing ones, such as losing a role in “Panic Room” to Kristen Stewart after Nicole Kidman backed out of the film due to injury. She shared intimate details about her family life, like the time her mom discovered her father was having an affair and the destructive impact it had on their family dynamic; her complicated relationship with her stage-mom mother, a former soap opera actress; and being overcome with grief after losing her beloved brother and confidant, Jansen, to heart complications in 2023. But the moments from “This Is Me: A Reckoning” that stuck with me the most concerned the many ways she was targeted by Hollywood predators. There was the “important executive at NBC” who kissed her on the lips at a party in 2008 while she starred on his network’s hit show “Heroes,” or the time that a star-studded apartment party in Los Feliz took a turn for the appalling when an “Oscar-winning actor and director” cornered a 19-year-old Panettiere as she was about to leave and tricked her into looking at his exposed testicles with the line, “There’s a big wad of gum on my pants.” “I looked down and recoiled,” she recalled in the book. “This well-respected, award-winning actor’s testicles were hanging out from his unzipped fly… Up to that moment, men in Hollywood had always been kind and respectful around me. There may have been a peck on the lips here and an inappropriate comment there, but nothing had crossed a line.” And that line kept getting crossed, again and again. One of the most shocking incidents occurred when Panettiere was 18 and an actress friend, who she calls Stella in the book, invited her to a yacht party in the South of France. Stella ushered her down into the bowels of the ship and to a cabin where a “famous 30-something British singer-songwriter” lay naked in bed, his bottom half covered in sheets. “I want you to get in bed with him. He has a huge dick,” Stella told Panettiere, who subsequently panicked, writing, “My thoughts were a blur, but I’d spent my life trusting that others had my best interests at heart. Being ‘managed’ was routine, to the point where I lost faith in my intuition. I could feel my heart pounding. As I settled in underneath the sheets, I disassociated. My body no longer felt like my own.” Then, her “survival instinct kicked in” and she managed to escape before anything happened. The Hollywood crowd proved so off-putting to Panettiere that she found herself drawn to the former heavyweight champion boxer Wladimir Klitschko, who is currently helping defend his country of Ukraine against Russia’s invasion, because of how un-Hollywood he is. The two share a daughter, Kaya. As Panettiere told People , when she was only 15, someone on her team began plying her with “happy pills” before she walked red carpets. “They were to make me peppy during interviews,” Panettiere said. “I had no idea that this was not an appropriate thing, or what door that would open for me when it came to my addiction… As I got older, the drugs and alcohol became something I almost couldn’t live without.” Her battle with drugs, alcohol and depression led to an eight-month rehab stint in 2020, where she wrote candidly about the painful effects of withdrawal on her body and mind. “As my nervous system tried to regulate itself without the depressant effects of alcohol, it went into overdrive, and my whole body shook, I couldn’t sleep, and my head pounded like it was pressing against my skull… A doctor told me that if I didn’t stop drinking, I’d be dead within five years,” she recalled in her book. Whatever her cause of death is, one thing is certain: Hollywood failed to protect Hayden Panettiere. Hopefully, her death will serve as a reminder to the industry’s powers that be that young girls and women need to be heard, need to feel safe, and need to be shielded from its more sordid characters. I’ll leave you with a portion of the final chapter of Panettiere’s memoir, which she named “One Final Thought”: “Radical acceptance has taught me to walk hand in hand with my triumphs and my tragedies because they’ve made me who I am. And today, I really love that person. If there’s anything I can offer you with this book, it’s my hope that you do the same.” Miley Cyrus Says She ‘Genuinely’ Wants to Act Again as She Signs With Atlantic Records and Charts Next Chapter: ‘I’d Love to Disappear Into Something Romantic’ Loading comments... articles.title: China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Dominates With $70 Million Weekend as Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Debuts Second
articles.full_text: Aug 16, 2026 11:27pm PT China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Dominates With $70 Million Weekend as Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Debuts Second By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Deluxe Media and Tohokushinsha Film Corporation Set Strategic Asia-Pacific Localization Partnership (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago ‘Heartstopper’ Star Rhea Norwood, ‘Enola Holmes’ Actor Susan Wokoma, ‘Dear England’ Writer James Graham Join U.K. National Youth Theatre’s 70th Anniversary Show (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Korea Box Office: Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Outpaces ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Again in Strong Second Weekend 2 hours ago See All Dirty Monkeys Dirty Monkeys’ war comedy-drama “ Once Upon a Time in the Middle East ” took command of the mainland China box office during the Aug. 14–16 weekend, grossing RMB477.9 million ($70.3 million) over the three-day frame, according to data from Artisan Gateway. Following its Tuesday, Aug. 11 rollout and earlier previews, the production has amassed a cumulative total of $134.1 million. Directed by Wen Muye (“Dying to Survive”) from a screenplay co-written with Lang Qunli and Wei Zhong, the film stars Shen Teng as a Chinese chef who moves to the Middle East to open an eatery to pay off family debts. Alongside his floor manager, played by Jiang Qiming, their business turns into an unexpected sanctuary for local civilians and children when armed conflict erupts. The cast also features Aarif Rahman and Omar Sherif. From the Imax screens left over from the saturation “ The Odyssey ” release, “Once Upon a Time in the Middle East” collected $2.1 million. Related Stories Hollywood Failed Hayden Panettiere Hayden Panettiere, 'Heroes' and 'Scream' Star, Dies at 36 Universal’s Christopher Nolan epic “The Odyssey” debuted in second place, pulling in $28.4 million across its official three-day opening weekend. Bolstered by early previews, the tentpole has reached a cumulative $35.9 million in the territory. The 20,000 screen Middle Kingdom release followed a high-profile Beijing promotional tour and secured an extensive Imax footprint across the country. Including previews, the Imax cume is $19.3 million in China and the company said that this marks the biggest opening weekend ever for a Christopher Nolan film in China, both in Imax box office and Imax indexing. Popular on Variety Pearl Studio’s animated fantasy feature “ All Wishes Come True! ” moved to third position in its fifth weekend, taking in $13.1 million. Directed by Mu Zhengyang, the mythological comedy has accumulated $235.9 million since its July 18 debut, tracking eight ordinary mortals who combine their wit to outsmart celestial deities and earn the mantle of the Eight Immortals. Sony’s “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ” placed fourth in its third full weekend, collecting $9.9 million. The film has reached a cumulative total of $209 million since launching on July 29, continuing its run as the top-grossing Hollywood import in China this year. Enlight Pictures’ animated fantasy romance “To Your Island” held onto fifth place, taking $2.6 million in its sophomore frame for a cumulative total of $15 million. Directed by Zhou Haoran and adapted from Fan Dawang’s popular web novel, the story follows a young woman led by a paper crane to a mysterious island, where she reconnects with her former boyfriend, who has lost his memories and been transformed into a rabbit. Mainland China’s overall weekend grosses reached $132.9 million, while the 2026 year-to-date revenue stands at $3.79 billion, down 30.4% from the same period in 2025. articles.full_text: Aug 16, 2026 11:52pm PT Former Costa Rican Film Commissioner Marysela Zamora: ‘I Believe That the Next Great Chapter in Audiovisual Media Will Be Written in Spanish’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Anna Marie de la Fuente Plus Icon Anna Marie de la Fuente @adelafuente1 Latest Former Costa Rican Film Commissioner Marysela Zamora: ‘I Believe That the Next Great Chapter in Audiovisual Media Will Be Written in Spanish’ (EXCLUSIVE) 3 hours ago Diego Luna, Nicolas Pereda and Rodrigo Plá Set for Competition at Mexico’s Morelia Film Festival 2 days ago ‘Amores Perros’ Exec Producer Francisco González Compean and ‘Counterattack’ Director Chava Cartas Launch Durango Films (EXCLUSIVE) 4 days ago See All (l-r) Carolina Cordero and Marysela Zamora. Courtesy of the Costa Rica Film Commission Former Costa Rican Film Commissioner Marysela Zamora, who was instrumental in reviving the Costa Rica Media Market (CRMM) these past two years, will continue to serve on the Board of Directors of the Ibero-American Network of Film Commissions ( Iberofic ), where she will spearhead a regional agenda aimed at bolstering women’s leadership in the audiovisual sector and help foster Spanish-language content on the global stage. “Marysela has been a key voice in strengthening regional cooperation and positioning Costa Rica within the Ibero-American audiovisual conversation. We are pleased that she continues to be part of our Board of Directors and to lead strategic initiatives for the entire region,” said Carolina Cordero, Iberofic founder and president, who attended CRMM for the first time in July this year. Related Stories ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Sets Box Office Record With $72 Million in Previews, Beating ‘Avengers: Endgame’ 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Crosses $1 Billion in Six Days, Second-Fastest Movie to Hit Milestone “At Iberofic, we understand that the value and experience of professionals transcend the positions they hold at any given time. That is why we seek out and invite the best representatives from each territory—individuals with experience, knowledge, and the ability to build bridges and contribute a strategic vision,” Cordero noted, adding: “Our commitment is to build long-term alliances and opportunities for the audiovisual industry and for the region, beyond institutional cycles. Marysela embodies this spirit and has demonstrated that collaborative work and continuity are essential for building a more integrated, competitive and internationally visible audiovisual industry.” Popular on Variety The leadership change at the film commission, a unit of foreign trade promotion agency Procomer, comes as new conservative populist president Laura Fernandez, who took office in May, consolidates her administration. A creative industries strategist, producer and public policy specialist with more than 12 years of experience advancing Costa Rica’s audiovisual sector, Zamora led efforts to attract international productions and investment as its film commissioner since 2024, overseeing more than 200 projects involving major studios and platforms including Warner Bros. Discovery, NBCUniversal, Hulu, ITV and BBC Studios. During her tenure, film investment tripled in Costa Rica, from roughly $4 million in 2023 to $12 million in 2024, before reaching just over $11 million in 2025. This year, the film commission facilitated the shoot of Abby Fuller’s debut feature “Hope/Esperanza” from Oscar -winning producer Mark Johnson (“ Rain Man ”), an executive producer of the television mega-hit series, “ Breaking Bad .” According to the film’s local l ine producer, Esteban Quesada, a Variety Below-the-Line Talent to Track, this was Johnson’s first time to shoot in Costa Rica. As head of the Costa Rica Media Market, Zamora helped position the country as a regional hub for audiovisual investment and co-production. Her work has earned her more than 30 national and international awards, including a United Nations SDGs and Her Award in 2020. Forbes Central America named her one of the region’s most powerful women in 2026. “I firmly believe that the next great chapter in audiovisual media will be written in Spanish. Our region has the talent, the stories, and the capacity to become one of the world’s great creative engines,” she said. “My commitment to the development of audiovisual media transcends any position and will remain focused on building bridges, attracting opportunities and strengthening an industry that generates culture, identity and economic development for our countries.” Miley Cyrus Says She ‘Genuinely’ Wants to Act Again as She Signs With Atlantic Records and Charts Next Chapter: ‘I’d Love to Disappear Into Something Romantic’ Loading comments... articles.title: Korea Box Office: Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Outpaces ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Again in Strong Second Weekend
articles.full_text: Aug 16, 2026 11:54pm PT Korea Box Office: Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Outpaces ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Again in Strong Second Weekend By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Heartstopper’ Star Rhea Norwood, ‘Enola Holmes’ Actor Susan Wokoma, ‘Dear England’ Writer James Graham Join U.K. National Youth Theatre’s 70th Anniversary Show (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Korea Box Office: Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Outpaces ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Again in Strong Second Weekend 3 hours ago China Box Office: ‘Once Upon a Time in the Middle East’ Dominates With $70 Million Weekend as Christopher Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ Debuts Second 3 hours ago See All Everett Collection “ The Odyssey ” ruled the South Korean box office during the weekend of Aug. 14–16. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the Christopher Nolan-directed tentpole generated $13.2 million from 1,691,744 admissions over the three-day frame across 2,114 screens, capturing 59.07% of the total weekend market. The film grew its sophomore session by nearly 28%, lifting its cumulative South Korean gross to $35.2 million from 4,542,480 total admissions since its Aug. 5 rollout. Related Stories China Box Office: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swings to Massive $121 Million Five-Day Opening 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Hits $2 Billion Worldwide in Three Weeks “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ” held onto second place in its third weekend, bringing in $5.6 million from 767,839 admissions over the frame. The film accounted for 25.47% of the weekend market, pushing its cumulative haul to $53.5 million from 7,279,373 admissions. Popular on Variety “Teenieping: Legend of the Whale Heartstone” retained third place, generating $906,294 from 133,928 admissions over the three-day window. Directed by Kim Soo-hoon, the musical fantasy adventure follows Princess Romi, Heartsping, and their companions exploring an undersea kingdom to rescue Queen Velita. The family feature has accumulated $4.2 million from 633,527 viewers since its Aug. 5 launch. The local action-comedy sequel “Ok! Madam: Bon Voyage” opened in fourth place, pulling in $827,800 from 120,982 admissions over the weekend. Directed by Lee Cheol-ha and starring Uhm Jung-hwa, Park Sung-woong, Lee Sang-yun, and Sooyoung, the comedy tracks a former secret agent turned twisted-doughnut shop owner whose family cruise turns into a hostage crisis orchestrated by international mercenaries. The film has gathered $1.3 million from 203,968 total admissions. Anime mystery entry “ Detective Conan the Movie: Fallen Angel of the Highway” was in fifth place, taking $831,509 from 116,521 admissions. Directed by Takahiro Hasui, the latest installment in the franchise tracks Conan Edogawa investigating high-speed vehicular sabotage on an expressway network. Since opening on Aug. 12, the film has earned $1.5 million from 226,028 admissions. “ Paw Patrol: The Dino Movie ” debuted in sixth place, capturing $272,230 from 39,639 admissions. Since its Aug. 13 release, the title has brought in $330,430 from 47,625 admissions. Sci-fi survival thriller “Hope” was in seventh place, adding $280,866 from 38,708 admissions. Directed by Na Hong-Jin and starring Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Michael Fassbender, and Alicia Vikander, the village-set alien encounter thriller has pushed its cumulative haul to $33.8 million from 4,475,560 ticket buyers. Japanese director Tomoaki Fujino’s personal family documentary “What Should We Have Done?” took eighth place, pulling in $69,362 from 9,499 admissions over the frame to lift its total to $490,387. Faith-based animated feature “David” claimed ninth place, adding $45,188 from 6,714 admissions to bring its gross to $2 million from 298,694 total viewers. Rounding out the top ten was a re-release of the 2018 Queen musical biopic “Bohemian Rhapsody,” which drew $32,941 from 4,234 admissions over the weekend, extending its historic South Korean cumulative gross to $60.9 million from 9,954,658 tickets. The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $22.3 million, almost on par with last week’s $22.9 million. articles.title: Mexico’s Madrefoca Boards ‘Isabel Hernández’ as Zoe Films Builds Festival Momentum (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 17, 2026 12:15am PT Mexico’s Madrefoca Boards ‘Isabel Hernández’ as Zoe Films Builds Festival Momentum (EXCLUSIVE) Italian filmmaker Giorgio Giampà’s feature debut is one of the 15 projects selected for San Sebastián’s 2026 Europe-Latin America Co-Production Forum By Emiliano de Pablos Plus Icon Emiliano de Pablos Latest San Sebastian Adds Jesse Eisenberg, Fred Cavayé, Amanda Kernell Films to Golden Shell Race 3 days ago Goya-Nominated Zoe Bonafonte Leads Spain-Argentina Soccer Pioneer Drama ‘Veleta’ (EXCLUSIVE) 6 days ago Bendita Film Sales Picks Up Toronto Discovery Title ‘The Fortunate Isles’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 weeks ago See All 'Isabel Hernández' Courtesy of Zoe Films Mexico’s Madrefoca Cine has boarded “ Isabel Hernández ,” Italian filmmaker Giorgio Giampà ’s feature debut, joining Zoe Films , LaDoc and Fiasco on the Italy-Mexico co-production. The project is among the 15 titles selected for the 2026 Europe-Latin America Co-Production Forum at the San Sebastián Film Festival. Its San Sebastián berth comes as Zoe Films builds a growing festival presence. The Italian company has Ali Asgari’s “A Bit of Light” in competition at the Venice Film Festival and Shawn Garry’s “After Elena,” starring Alfredo Castro, heading to Toronto’s Centrepiece section. Related Stories Hayden Panettiere, 'Heroes' and 'Scream' Star, Dies at 36 Hollywood Failed Hayden Panettiere The move brings producer Alejandro Saevich into a production team comprising Zoe Films’ Lorenzo Cioffi and Giampà and Fiasco’s Elena Fortes. Madrefoca, co-founded in 2023 by Saevich, is also behind Nathalia Acevedo’s “Salón de Belleza,” selected for competition at Venice Days this year. Popular on Variety Written by Giampà with Melissa Nocetti, “Isabel Hernández” follows a young agronomist living in the Guatemalan jungle who recognizes the father who abandoned her as a child in a documentary about Latin American migrants in the U.S. Her search for answers leads to two men recently deported by ICE who knew him: a young man whom her father raised like a son and a former soldier who claims to know the secret behind his disappearance. Their conflicting accounts force Isabel to confront a past shaped by Guatemala’s civil war and fractured memories of the man she barely knew. “Isabel tries to piece together the past, claim a future of her own, find her own peace,” Giampà said. The film grows out of seven years of research Giampà carried out in Guatemala, living with forest communities and spending time with Mayan survivors of the genocidal massacres of the 1980s, former guerrillas and people deported from the U.S. by ICE. Giampà plans to work largely with non-professional actors “whose own lives resonate with the story,” extending the film’s research-driven approach into its casting. Shooting is planned for autumn 2027. “Isabel Hernández” is part of TorinoFilmLab FeatureLab 2026, previously participated in the EAVE Producers Workshop 2025 and has received development support from Film Commission Regione Campania. Founded in 2023, Zoe Films’ previous productions include Asgari’s “Divine Comedy,” selected for Venice Horizons in 2025, and Alessandro Cassigoli and Casey Kauffman’s “Vittoria,” which played Venice Horizons Extra in 2024. Its short-film slate includes Giampà’s “Astronauta,” selected for Clermont-Ferrand’s 2026 International Competition, and Mel Nocetti’s “I Used to Call That Man Home,” which played Rotterdam earlier this year. The 2026 Europe-Latin America Co-Production Forum will run Sept. 21-23 as part of the 74th San Sebastián Film Festival, which takes place Sept. 18-26.
