articles.title: Netflix Fires Back Against Tyra Banks’ ‘America’s Next Top Model’ Docuseries Defamation Lawsuit
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 15, 2026 8:03pm Tyra Banks in 'Reality Check: Inside America's Next Top Model.' Netflix has filed a motion to strike and dismiss Tyra Banks ‘ defamation lawsuit against Netflix over her portrayal in the streamer’s America’s Next Top Model docuseries, entitled Reality Check . Banks filed a lawsuit against Netflix in June, where she argued she was falsely represented in the docuseries, arguing that her comments were “stripped of context and reassembled to support a false and defamatory narrative unrelated to what she actually expressed.” She participated in a three-and-a-half hour long interview, outlining that just 16 minutes of her footage was used for Reality Check . Related Stories TV Netflix Picks Up YA Series 'Sunshine Girls,' Adds Randall Park to 'Minimum Wage' TV Supernatural YA Romance 'Sid & Zoey' Nabs Netflix Pickup Netflix’s motion, which was filed Friday, argues that Banks’ complaints are “about ordinary editorial decisions.” The motion confirms that Banks sat for a three-and-a-half-hour interview, adding that “After the interview, [Banks] signed an agreement granting the filmmakers the right to edit her interview footage, acknowledging she had ‘no right to review or approve’ the finished documentary, and releasing claims arising from it — including for defamation and false light. She now alleges the documentary, Reality Check: Inside America’s Next Top Model (the ‘Documentary’), defames her — not because it says anything false about her, but because she wanted advance notice of what another interviewee would say, more of her interview included, and her perspective presented differently.” In Banks’ lawsuit, she specifically cited how she was shown in the docuseries responding to cycle two contestant Shandi Sullivan’s alleged sexual assault during filming. She was shown being asked “You remember the story with Shandi?” in Reality Check , to which she responded “um,” before the screen cuts to black, creating a “devastating and deliberate” implication that Banks couldn’t remember the assault, she argued in her suit. “And when Banks is asked whether she remembers Sullivan’s story, the Documentary shows her answer: ‘I do remember her story.’ A documentary expressly showing Banks remembering does not imply that she forgot,” Netflix’s motion reads in response. “Banks understands editorial discretion. She created, hosted, and executive produced 24 seasons of ANTM , making the same kinds of editorial decisions she now attacks — what footage to include, what to omit, and how to present competing narratives,” the motion continues. “The Documentary simply turned that editorial lens back on ANTM and Banks. Her disagreement with the resulting portrayal does not make it defamatory.” A Netflix spokesperson told ABC News in a statement Friday they plan to “vigorously defend” the docuseries and those behind it. “Directors Daniel Sivan and Mor Loushy are respected documentarians who thoroughly interviewed the people behind America’s Next Top Model ,” the statement reads. “Tyra Banks was given the opportunity to speak openly about her experience and the creators fairly presented her perspective alongside those of every other participant shown in this documentary. We stand behind Reality Check: Inside America’s Next Top Model and will continue to vigorously defend it.” The Hollywood Reporter has reached out to Banks’ lawyer for comment. THR

articles.title: Disney’s Experiences Chief Talks Figment, the Tomorrowland Refresh and All That D23 News
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Alex Weprin Plus Icon Alex Weprin Senior Editor alexweprin Follow Sign Up View All August 15, 2026 9:57pm Villains Land concept art Disney Experiences Saturday evening in Anaheim’s Honda Center, The Walt Disney Co. turned to Neil Patrick Harris to serve as a master of ceremonies for what is surely one of its most scrutinized events: The Disney Experiences showcase presentation at D23 . D23 of course is Disney’s in-house fan convention, and the showcase panels are used to reveal new projects and make news. Disney turned to a late night theme for the event, with Harris hosting, joined by a live band, opening the event with a monologue full of Disney-related quips, like noting that the last host of the Experiences was Josh D’Amaro. Related Stories Business Disney and Epic Games Launch Game That Connects Star Wars Theme Park Ride to New Fortnite Adventure Movies 'Frozen 3' "Royal Wedding" Between Anna and Kristoff Is Crashed by New Villain in First-Look “Wait a minute. If my math is correct, I am 24 months away from being CEO, and 48 months away from owning the Lakers,” Harris quipped, before launching into an animatronic-themed, cameo-filled musical number. Of course, it is D23, so it was the announcements that the fans wer eager to see. Saturday’s showcase ended with a pair of showstoppers for Disney theme park fans, a refresh of Figment, one of Epcot’s original rides, including the return of the Dreamfinder character, and a revitalization of Disneyland ‘s Tomorrowland, one of Walt Disney’s original visions. The concept: “New attractions, new open spaces, new places to dream about the future.” “This particular Tomorrowland here at Disneyland was the one that was originally thought of and designed by Walt himself,” says Thomas Mazloum, the chairman of Disney Experiences, in an interview with The Hollywood Reporter . “If you think about it, so much of that at the time was based on optimism: Optimism about the future, and this is going to be our North Star as we approach this particular work. It doesn’t mean we’re not going to change things. It just means we respect where we came from, but we use that optimism to carry us in the future, and in the case of this particular project, I think it proves we are listening carefully to what our guests are telling us while investing also in new generations. “We’ve done a lot, as you know, on Disney California Adventure, and we’re going to continue to do more. But we also know we need to listen equally as carefully and harmonize what this icon, especially Disneyland, did to the world when it first opened,” Mazloum continued. “And so the way I approach this is really not to be beholden by the past, to respect it, but to take Walt’s original positiveness, this optimism, and use that as our inspiration for the creative that we’re going to introduce.” Of course that wasn’t the only news Disney had to share. There were updates on new lands and projects announced two years ago like the Cars -themed area and Villains Land at Magic Kingdom, cruise ship updates, and plenty more. Mazloum spoke to THR ahead of the event to lay the groundwork for what the company is teeing up over the coming months and years, and his first few months leading the division succeeding D’Amaro, who is now Disney’s CEO. “It’s been very simple and very smooth, Alex. Truth be told, even in my prior roles, I’ve reported to Josh D’Amaro, and in this role I continue to report to him. I’m very familiar with our businesses, and it was very exciting for me, frankly speaking, to travel,” Mazloum says, noting that he went to every Disney resort around the world, and many of its cruise ships, after taking the top job. “Recently, I shared a note with our team around the world, and I said to them in my final sentence, and I meant this: ‘This is the privilege of my lifetime.’ “The reason why I feel that way is traveling around the world made me once again realize we truly are having more projects currently happening than at any single point in our history, and it isn’t just the volume — and we’re going to share this obviously with our fans this week — it’s the creativity. And what I always think about is our founder Walt’s quote when he said, ‘Disneyland will never be completed if there is enough imagination left in the world,’ and imagine me traveling all around the world, looking at each side, seeing everything starting to come to life.” While D23 in 2024 served as an unveiling for a barrage of projects that will bring new Disney IP to its theme parks and resorts around the world, this year’s event put more focus on the parks’ own IP. That includes Tomorrowland, of course, but also fan favorites like Figment, the dragon at who has become something of a mascot for Epcot in Orlando, and the yeti animatronic on the Expedition Everest ride at Animal Kingdom, which has been broken since shortly after the ride opened. “What that really means to me is that we’re listening to all of our fans and our guests, and specifically that means harmonizing the various demands,” Mazloum says. “You might be familiar with what we do here at Disneyland, with Avengers Campus, Coco , the first-time attractions and IPs that not only satisfy our existing audience, but I believe will also appeal to new audiences, while harmonizing the need to pay attention also to what our existing fans that have been loyal for many years and often decades demand of us, and to do that is to make sure that we revitalize fan favorites and keep them nice and fresh and new, while also working on new lands, and it’s about really harmonizing these tools. “What you will see is all the new lands and updates on everything that we have announced, and how we follow through, and how we put the creativity at work to create a world-class experience, but then you will also see as we talk about Figment, as we talk about Yeti, as we talk about Tomorrowland, you will see the focus on the existing guests that have been longing for this for a long time,” he added. Things like the yeti animatronic might seem like small potatoes in the grand scheme of things, but Mazloum frames them as a core piece of the Disney magic, getting families to return again and again, generation after generation. “We are immensely focused on attention to details, and our guests, our fans, they genuinely care about our places, our parks, our cruise ships. They genuinely care about the stories,” he says. “They understand our commitment to tell our stories in an authentic way, the way only Disney can, and they hold us to a high standard. And our goal is to meet and exceed that standard. “Whether it’s a nostalgic ride, whether it’s something like the Yeti, it may just be one small thing, but this is really something — a relationship between us and our fans that that we treasure and that is paying off,” he adds. Disney’s Carousel of Progress at Disney World, for example, will be updated next year not only with new scenes, but also new voices, with Jamie Lee Curtis and Bryan Cranston set to voice characters on the attraction. There will also be updates on the Disney Cruise Line, which has become a major source of investment for the company, with a flurry of new ships set to be delivered over the next half decade, including a new lightly smaller class of ships that Mazloum says will enable the company to add new locations in Alaska and Europe to its itineraries. “It gives us a ton of flexibility, which we really want and need as we expand the cruise line both domestically and globally,” Mazloum says. “I always tell everyone it’s three vacations in one. You get the convenience of a cruise, especially for multi-generational travel, you get the Disney stories, and then you get your beach vacation or the beautiful destinations. “So it’s a really incredible value proposition, and with our growing portfolio of parks around the globe — in future years, as you know, we also are working on another park in Abu Dhabi — but when you think about our global portfolio of parks right now, what the ships enable us is to a reach more people in the world that are Disney fans, and at the same time also connect them to our parks,” he adds. “Then you couple that with the fact that there’s still a sizable amount of the population that have never cruised, and on Disney Cruise Line in particular, we attract one of the highest amount of new to cruise guests in the industry.” The next Wish-class ship, the Disney Believe, will include a statue of Moana in its atrium. Ultimately Mazloum is betting that D23 will underscore how the company is leaning into what its theme park fans want, and can set the stage for his own tenure atop the most important experiential entertainment business in the world. “What I’m really hoping that the fans will see, especially at this D23, is the creativity that we’re applying to all the new experiences we’ve announced, and how much we are listening to them, and how important their thoughts and their feelings are to us in in us reimagining some of their most favorite attractions, characters, or lands,” he says. “We’re gonna prove to the world and to our fans that we are following through on all the announcements we made two years ago. That we haven’t just announced it, we’re actually following through.” THR

articles.title: ‘Too Much Music’ Is a Doc Project About Ghanaian Keyboardist Kiki Gyan – and About Who Controls Artists’ Narratives
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 15, 2026 11:59pm 'Too Much Music' Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors Music is a blessing, but maybe it can also be a curse – especially if you are a famous musician who gets remembered mostly for drugs and other negative narratives. Too Much Music , one of the works-in-progress showcased at the 2026 edition of Open Doors , the Locarno Film Festival ‘s co-production platform and talent development program for filmmakers from equity-seeking communities and regions where artistic expression is at risk, wants to explore all these issues. It comes from director Aseye Fiagbe (short The Gentleman , episode 7 of Bad Mama ) and puts a spotlight on a famous keyboardist from Ghana, Kiki Gyan. Related Stories Movies 'Mission' Stars George MacKay and Rosy McEwen on Capitalism, Creative Freedom and the Eternal Allure of British Independent Film Movies Locarno Film Festival Awards Go to 'You Don't Belong Here,' Hong Sangsoo, Monica Bellucci The director is also the producer of the doc via her Aseye Fiagbe Creative Studio in Ghana. She presented the project during the second edition of Open Doors with a focus on films from Africa and won one of three Open Doors Grants . THR has compiled highlights about the movie and insight from Fiagbe about the project and the themes it explores. Synopsis Too Much Music is a feature documentary about Kiki Gyan, a Ghanaian keyboard prodigy who rose to international fame as a teenager with Afro-rock pioneers Osibisa. As his musical contributions expanded without recognition, tensions around credit and ownership led him to leave the band and pursue a solo career across London, Lagos and New York, shaping African disco and funk in the process. Over time, the same system that profited from his brilliance proved indifferent to his vulnerability, and his life became reduced to a singular narrative of addiction and demise. Through archival material and testimonies from family and collaborators, the film reconstructs the forces that shaped his journey and asks how artists are remembered, who controls their stories, and what is lost when brilliance is reframed as failure. Director’s note Music is a blessing, and Kiki Gyan had that gift in abundance. His music is joyful, infectious, technically brilliant, and yet his life story often overshadows the work itself. Many people know how he died long before they encounter the music he made. That imbalance is what pulled me into this film. I grew up with Osibisa as the soundtrack of Sunday afternoons in my home. Years later, I discovered Kiki’s solo work and realized how much of his brilliance had been hidden behind a simplified story of addiction and death. Too Much Music is not about rescuing him or forcing his life into a neat redemption arc. I am interested in complexity: holding brilliance, failure, joy, exploitation, vulnerability, and legacy in the same frame. As a Ghanaian filmmaker, I see this film as part of a larger responsibility to document our cultural history with care. Kiki’s story is about memory and erasure, about who gets remembered for their work and who is remembered only for how they fell. What was the inspiration for you to want to make this film? I grew up with Osibisa as part of the soundtrack of life in Ghana, but the story I knew about Kiki Gyan was basically the story of how he died. He was a brilliant prodigy who became addicted to drugs, lost everything and died in a church bathroom. That was the story. Then, as an adult, I started discovering how much music he had actually made and how little of it I knew. I realized that, like many other Ghanaians, I knew the ending of his life before I really knew the work. That bothered me, and the more I researched him, the more complicated, colorful and human the story became. How universal are the themes of the film, and why should people outside Mozambique see it? For me, the film is ultimately about memory and who gets reduced to what. We do this all the time. A whole person can become one mistake, one tragedy, one headline. Kiki’s story happens within a very particular Ghanaian and African music history, but the questions underneath it feel universal. What happens when talent arrives before someone is ready for everything that comes with it? Who gets credit for creative work? How do we treat people when they fall from the pedestal we put them on? And who gets to decide what remains of someone after they are gone? I don’t think you need to know Kiki Gyan or Osibisa to recognize those questions. What is the next step for you and your collaborators after Open Doors? Open Doors gave the project a real push forward, through the conversations we had, the connections forged and the award, which gives us so much room to continue the development work. The writing and research are still ongoing, particularly around London, Lagos and the U.S., and we are continuing our archival research while building the international production structure around the film. A big focus now is following up with the producers, financiers and other partners I met in Locarno and finding the right co-production relationships. We came to Locarno with a Ghanaian film looking for the right international collaborators. I left feeling much clearer about what those relationships should actually look like. THR

articles.title: ‘Lanterns’ Bosses and Stars on How the Show’s Grounded Approach Ushers in an ‘Entirely Different Kind of Superhero’
articles.full_text: Aug 15, 2026 1:30pm PT ‘Lanterns’ Bosses and Stars on How the Show’s Grounded Approach Ushers in an ‘Entirely Different Kind of Superhero’ By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘The Pitt,’ ‘Hacks’ and ‘Beef’ Among Astra TV Awards Winners 4 hours ago Slipknot Confirms Sid Wilson’s Sudden Exit: ‘We Wish Him the Best’ 12 hours ago ‘Lanterns’ Bosses and Stars on How the Show’s Grounded Approach Ushers in an ‘Entirely Different Kind of Superhero’ 13 hours ago See All Courtesy of Warner Bros. Discovery As part of James Gunn and Peter Safran’s newly expanded DCU, a more grounded take on the “Green Lantern” comics may surprise audiences who associate the character with the Ryan Reynolds film that received poor reviews back in 2011. But for co-creators Chris Mundy , Damon Lindelof and Tom King , “ Lanterns ” is all about going back to the original iteration of the character when he was “an entirely different kind of superhero.” Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) “We’re talking about almost a century’s worth of storytelling, and now we get to carry that baton,” Lindelof told Variety . “But then at the same time, the audience is hungry for something original and relevant, and they want storytellers to take risks. Those risks can’t feel like they’re gimmicks; they have to feel like they have real emotional stakes.” Popular on Variety The show follows Hal Jordan (Kyle Chandler) as he is forced to take John Stewart (Aaron Pierre) under his wing as a backup. As the Green Lantern, Hal has the power to create material items through his ring and acts as an intergalactic space officer. Things take a dark turn after a series of unexplainable deaths draw Hal and John to a small town in Nebraska. As creators, King brings a wealth of experience as a comic book writer, while Lindelof created the “Watchmen” TV series. Mundy, who served as showrunner on “Ozark,” is new to the comic book world. “I know that if Damon didn’t work on this show, I would have used — and I think Tom would say the same — ‘Watchmen’ as a real touchstone of how you do a show and have it be emotional and about real people, while also honoring the comic book part of it,” Mundy said. In addition to the grounded approach that “Watchmen” takes, “Lanterns” also shares similarities in how the show explores race, colonization and justice. King explained how “there’s a wonderful coincidental parallel with comics that ‘Watchmen,’ in the ’80s, set the standard for a generation of comic book writers who were like, ‘Oh, we can talk about those themes using superheroes!'” Poorna Jagannathan, who plays the conniving and mysterious Zoe, hopes that shows like “Lanterns” invite more actors into the DCU who don’t read comic books. “I thought I’d be with a green screen wearing a suit, talking to no one at all, just into the abyss,” she told Variety at Thursday’s premiere on the Paramount lot. “I hesitated because I didn’t know this world at all. I felt like I didn’t belong, actually. I felt bad that I was so ignorant about it.” “I don’t think that only this universe will be affected by it; I think every show in the genre will be affected by what happened on ‘Lanterns,'” she added. “It’ll be a blueprint on how to take something big and keep it with a beating heart.” As the DCU continues to expand and test the waters of audiences, both with the success of films like “Superman” and the underwhelming reception to “Supergirl,” how audiences react to “Lanterns” could determine if early conversations about Season 2 turn into an official renewal. “The one thing that fans hate more than being listened to is fan service and that sort of idea of doing something just to placate them. And so I do think that fandom is not a monolith,” Lindelof said of navigating fandom expectations. “There are some fans who want more risky, edgy sort of revisionist storytelling inside of these adaptations, and some fans who are just basically like, ‘Give me what I love.'” There are certain canonical elements that the “Lanterns” team had to carefully maneuver, such as how the show ties into John Stewart’s involvement in “Man of Tomorrow,” and the return of Guy Gardner (Nathan Fillion), who also appears in “Superman” and “Peacemaker.” But when it comes to what “Lanterns” might signal for the future of the newly revamped DCU, it’s all about creative voices being at the forefront. “You can’t go out of bounds in terms of storylines that James and Peter want to do,” Lindelof said. “But artistically, they’re giving us a lot of freedom to tell the story how we want.” “Lanterns” premieres Sunday, Aug. 16 on HBO Max. articles.title: Director Frieda Luk on Olivia Luccardi’s ‘Sacred Creatures’ Role and the Fine Line Between ‘Crazy’ and ‘Enlightened’
articles.full_text: Aug 15, 2026 1:46pm PT Director Frieda Luk on Olivia Luccardi’s ‘Sacred Creatures’ Role and the Fine Line Between ‘Crazy’ and ‘Enlightened’ By Callum McLennan Plus Icon Callum McLennan Latest Director Frieda Luk on Olivia Luccardi’s ‘Sacred Creatures’ Role and the Fine Line Between ‘Crazy’ and ‘Enlightened’ 13 hours ago ‘How the F— Would You Get This Movie Made in America?’ Christine Vachon, Film4, BBC Film Put ‘Trainspotting,’ ‘Ratcatcher’ and ‘The Wicker Man’ Through the 2026 Greenlight Test 13 hours ago Director Paul Wright Pushes George MacKay to the Edge in ‘Mission’: ‘How Do You Feel Something When You’ve Been Numbed to the Modern World?’ 2 days ago See All Courtesy of Nicolas Villegas For “Sacred Creatures” director Frieda Luk , belief can be comforting, ridiculous, exhilarating and hard to explain. “I’m really fascinated by when people believe in something,” she tells Variety . “One person believes in something, and then a group of people, and then it slowly becomes this massive phenomenon. It goes viral.” That fascination drives Luk’s debut feature, which world premieres in competition at the Edinburgh International Film Festival. Starring Olivia Luccardi , James Cusati-Moyer and Romina D’Ugo, the Canada-Italy production follows three estranged siblings reuniting in rural Italy after middle sister Miriam (Olivia Luccardi) is released from psychiatric treatment following an experience she understands as a spiritual awakening rather than a breakdown. Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) “This movie is my exploration of believing in something and belief,” says Luk. “Miriam has agency. She knows herself and she makes choices. However, when she becomes a figure that people rally around, people are imbuing her with meaning. When she becomes abstract, she no longer controls the message.” Popular on Variety That uncertainty extends to the film itself, which slips between psychological drama, comedy and magical realism without settling comfortably into any of them. For Luk, the tonal slipperiness developed naturally from writing. “I set up the situation and these characters, and as I’m writing, I’m following what they’re doing. What I’m waiting for is how they surprise me,” she says. Courtesy of Nicolás Villegas One influence was Marco Ferreri’s “La Grande Bouffe,” the grotesque story of four men attempting to eat themselves to death. “The comedy is following through that premise in a serious way, because if you actually are going to eat yourself to death, you’re going to have gastrointestinal problems,” Luk says. “It’s also very silly. It never takes itself too seriously.” Italian cinema was integral to “Sacred Creatures” from the start. Luk points to films of the 1970s, admiring their willingness to move between modes contemporary cinema can sometimes keep separate. “A lot of the ’70s movies, especially European ones, are completely in between genres.” Luccardi was similarly keen to avoid reducing Miriam to a diagnosis. “She is healing from the lack of belief from people and everyone thinking that something was wrong with her,” Luccardi explains, adding that Miriam feels “meant for something greater.” There was another, less metaphysical piece of direction that unlocked the character: Luk told her Miriam was like a cat. “She’s very much like: ‘I’m letting you in on my terms. No, I actually don’t want you to touch me. I want to be a pet, but not like that,’” laughs Luccardi. “I did a lot of cat direction,” Luk dryly admits. As Miriam grows more secure in herself, Luccardi subtly changed the physical quality of the performance. “There was more of a calmness in my breath,” she says. “She was more relaxed and calm and just flowed. Before, she may have been a little more stressed and tightly wound.” That growing self-possession becomes visual in the film’s party scene, where Miriam arrives in a voluminous yellow-green dress that immediately separates her from the room around her. There is something of Bette Davis’ party entrance in “All About Eve” to the moment: costume becomes a declaration of presence, allowing Miriam to suddenly occupy a different plane from everyone watching her. Luk wanted the dress to be “kind of ridiculous looking, but also kind of chic,” something that would “take up some space” without seeming entirely out of place. “Miriam is new and a little ridiculous,” she says, with its uncontained “fluffiness” signalling “an irreverence to what has come before.” Luccardi’s relationship with it was rather less reverential by the end of the shoot. “At the beginning, it was great. At the end… I wore it a long time,” she jokes. “As with every costume, you love it at the beginning and then you’re like: ‘Can we burn it, please?’” Courtesy of Nicolás Villegas The surrounding family remain skeptical of their sister’s burgeoning allure to those around her. Luk, an only child who grew up surrounded by cousins, was amused by the way relatives can inhabit incompatible versions of the same history. “They’re always competing,” she says. The instinct of creating a story that makes life easier to comprehend ultimately expands beyond the siblings. Luk grew up without religion, but many childhood friends were religious and invited her to churches and youth groups. Watching from the outside, she was intrigued by their ability to surrender themselves to faith. “I would watch them read a text and believe in that text and treat it like this holy thing,” she recalls. “It was really hard for me to give myself over to something like that.” At Catholic services, she found herself captivated by the incense, clothing and ceremony. “I was like: ‘This is so fun and theatrical.’ I can see how it could be really comforting,” she says. “There’s a community-oriented spirit to it. Being a fan of a big sport is kind of fun. Yelling at a team is fun.” The director began thinking about fandoms, sports and social media with much the same curiosity. What separates a few people who regularly gather from a movement? “What if people hung out, and then that becomes a movement?” she says. “A few people hang out, and then more people hang out. Then you do it regularly, and what happens?” The film is shot in Piedmont and Italy provided a fertile landscape for those questions. Luk recalls seeing reports about a teenage protester and wondering why there couldn’t be a patron saint for protest, and what the origin story of a new saint might look like. But after all that construction of a film, a family history, a faith and perhaps even a saint, the director isn’t interested in providing audiences with a final answer about Miriam. “I want people to come away examining why they believe in something and how,” she says, “and that there is a pleasure in believing something.” “You never know if you are right or you are wrong. You might be wrong.” Or, as Luccardi puts it: “You never know if someone’s crazy or if someone’s enlightened. Who knows?” “It’s a fine line.” Prime Video’s Docuseries ‘Murder 101’ Moves Beyond Crime to Showcase the Power of Community: TV Review Prime Video’s Stunning Drama ’Sterling Point’ Elevates the YA Genre Beyond the Mundane: TV Review Octavia Spencer and Hannah Waddingham Are Badass Besties in Prime Video’s Middling Action Dramedy ‘Ride or Die’: TV Review Loading comments... articles.title: Disney Leaders Talk Streaming Strategy and Growth Drivers: Sports, Local Language, Vertical Media and Emerging Formats
articles.full_text: Aug 15, 2026 4:30pm PT Disney Leaders Talk Streaming Strategy and Growth Drivers: Sports, Local Language, Vertical Media and Emerging Formats By Cynthia Littleton Plus Icon Cynthia Littleton Business Editor @Variety_Cynthia Latest Disney Leaders Talk Streaming Strategy and Growth Drivers: Sports, Local Language, Vertical Media and Emerging Formats 9 hours ago Darren Walker Opens His Home to Friends and Anonymous Content Emmy Nominees in Celebration of ‘Joy, Reflection, Delight and Awe’ 18 hours ago A Bulldog in Business: How Moving into the Booth Opened Other Doors for Dodger Great Orel Hershiser 3 days ago See All The Walt Disney Company Amid a torrent of fan-friendly news about Disney projects across the media spectrum, Disney leadership took time on the first day of the three-day D23 fan fest weekend in Anaheim for panels that offered a behind the scenes look at the Mouse House’s business strategies and vision for driving growth in the streaming era. One of the topics tackled was how to reach next-generation Disney fans with next-generation content formats to keep the company’s many franchises relevant to Gen Alpha and beyond. Disney’s push into the booming vertical media space — aka microdramas and other shortform clips designed to be viewed on mobile phones — was discussed in detail during a session with Eric Schrier , Disney’s president of Direct-to-Consumer International Originals, Strategic Programming and Emerging Media, and Erin Teague , who is executive VP of Product Management for Disney Entertainment and ESPN . Related Stories Peacock to Be Included in YouTube Premium Subscription Bundle Starting in 2027 The conversation was moderated by Jon YouShaei , a YouTube and Instagram executive turned creator and podcaster, and it also featured the perspective of Disney-centric creator Blake Silva as a panelist. Popular on Variety Schrier emphasized that the “Verts” push on Disney+ is a significant investment for the Mouse. The company last week unveiled a pact with TikTok designed to encourage more fans to create clips with authorized Disney IP. This is a big change for the company that has historically vigorously enforced its copyright and trademark rights. “We’ve always looked at making film and television in very finite formats. Half hours, hours, feature length films. And now you can tell any story. Creators are just storytellers,” Schrier said. “We’ve always talked about our creators before there were actually creators. The creator of ‘Paradise,’ Dan Fogelman, he’s a creator. We talk about them as creators. And so they’re just different types of storytellers. So how do we bring those stories to Disney+? How do we complement what we already have on platform? And it’s early days, but we’re really excited about this next generation of storytellers that are out there that are into Disney+.” Teague pointed to examples that demonstrate how smart promotion and word-of-mouth via social media helps drive viewership to Disney’s biggest investments in TV and film. Creator Blake Silva, Disney’s Eric Schrier and Erin Teague and moderator Jon Youshaei speak Aug. 14 at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event in Anaheim. (The Walt Disney Company/Image Group L.A.) The Walt Disney Company “There will never be a replacement for that long-form original content but what is interesting is the way that it is now being supplemented by the shorter form analysis, the clips,” Teague said. As with live game coverage for sports, she said, “the additional commentary and analysis around the game is just as interesting. And so the ways that we can merge those experiences to give people exactly what they want, when they want it in a split second, I think, is the challenge.” Silva asserted that most experienced creators who hone their focus on key brands and franchises know how to plug themselves in to the company’s priorities. He said the TikTok deal and Disney+’s embrace of creator content has been invigorating for the Disney-verse. “We look at social media and clips going viral, about movies or scenes from movies all the time,” Silva said. “So imagine how that would translate and convert when they’re already in the app, to watch it immediately. I really believe in the creator to talent pipeline. It’s really exciting to think how could this create the next Mister Rogers, my idol.” Teague underscored that fans expect to be part of the action in ways that were unimaginable to their parents and grandparents. “Next generations of fans are expecting more from their entertainment experience. They want to be a part of the story. They want to put themselves in the story. They want interactivity. They want to have more agency in the storytelling experience with the democratization of creativity,” Teague said. Teague also took part in a session on how ESPN’s increasingly global sports profile is helping Disney find subscribers and fans. “ESPN is effectively synonymous with sports as a brand. So diehard sports fans know and love ESPN and have forever, that will never change. We will never stop serving the diehard, loyal sports fan because that’s our base,” Teague said during the session moderated by Joe Earley , Co-President of Direct to Consumer for Disney Entertainment. “But two trends are happening. One, the internet and native generations. Gen Alpha, Gen Z, etc. They are now expecting more from their sports fandom and their sports experience,” Teague said. “The technology is evolving and we’re thinking about how to also superserve the casual sports fan, because that fandom is equally as real. And it turns out it looks very similar to Disney fandom. And so we’re thinking about this consistently across our product experiences.” Freddy Rolón , ESPN’s head of global sports and talent office, reeled off the latest stats for ESPN’s reach with 43 linear networks in more than 130 countries and territories, and it is available on Disney+ in more than 100 markets. For the month of June, ESPN reached 640 million digital and social users. “We reach more casual fans, we reach more female fans on Disney+ and then on the flip side, ESPN brings to Disney+ a credibility about sports, authenticity about sports, and then really a recurring reason for fans to come back to the platform. Not just for the games, but for the game around the game,” Rolón said. “When we think about all those platforms, they work in concert. They’re not necessarily individual. We think about the game on Disney+, the coverage, and the social media platforms all working together to reach fans with information when they want it.” Disney’s Erin Teague, Freddy Rolón, Jo Fox and Joe Earley speak Aug. 14 at D23: The Ultimate Disney Fan Event in Anaheim. (The Walt Disney Company/Image Group L.A.) The Walt Disney Company Jo Fox , senior VP of marketing for ESPN, said the tighter connection to Disney+ as the platform has expanded significantly across Europe, Middle East, Asia and Latin America has been hugely beneficial. ESPN has made the strategic decision to make key programs available via Disney+ even for subscribers who don’t get the bundle. “We use the Disney+ platform and their audience, who might be different to our ESPN core audience, and we can talk to them more directly and get them more enthused about sports and ultimately engaging with Disney+ and ESPN as well,” Fox said. “So as an example of that, we will have select college football games and ‘College GameDay’ unlocked on Disney+ coming up. Because the mascots, the pageantry, the tribal nature of it, the excitement around it. It seems like an amazing sport to be able to unlock some of these select games on Disney+ and talk to this new fan base.” Earley also moderated a session on Disney+’s international content strategy for local-language production with Schrier and Carol Choi , Disney Asia Pacific’s executive VP of Integrated Marketing & APAC Original Strategy. It’s a balancing act of leveraging the platform’s worldwide reach with the need to keep subscribers engaged on a consistent basis. Local-language content has long been seen as key to reducing subscriber churn rates. “What we’re really looking to do is tell stories for local audiences and be hyper-local. We call it local for local. So we make French shows for France, Spanish shows for Spain, or Brazilian shows for Brazil. And we do that all over the world,” Schrier said. “We’re going to be increasing that significantly to have local audiences have something that expresses their culture and their sensibility. And what’s happened organically out of that local for local strategy is that those stories are now traveling back to other parts of the world.” Korea and Japan are prime areas of focus for Disney+ and local-language production. “Our local creators and storytellers really appreciate the ability for them to tell stories that are authentic to the local cultures with the support of people who’ve been telling stories like their whole career, like Eric and his team,” Choi said. “With that guidance, we’ve been very fortunate to have produced a number of hits, as well as having audiences outside of APAC discover these stories and content.” Choi pointed to recent buzzy Disney+ series including “Tempest,” “Perfect Crown” and “A Shop For Killers.” Earley added, “Some of those Korean dramas put up numbers that rival or even exceed some of the global originals as well.” (Pictured top: Disney’s Eric Schrier, Carol Choi and Joe Earley speak at D23 in Anaheim on Aug. 14.) articles.title: ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027
articles.full_text: Aug 15, 2026 9:11pm PT ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027 By Jazz Tangcay Plus Icon Jazz Tangcay Artisans Editor @jazzt Latest ‘Monsters, Inc.’ Themed Land Will Open at Disney World in 2027 5 hours ago ‘RuPaul’s Drag Race,’ ‘All Stars’ and ‘Untucked’ Renewed for New Seasons at MTV and Paramount+ 9 hours ago ‘Lilo & Stitch 2’ Drops First Look of Pink Alien Angel in Live-Action Sequel 1 day ago See All Disney THe’Monsters, Inc.’ themed land, Monstropolis is set to open at Disney’s Hollywood Studios at Disney World in 2027. The news was announced Saturday at D23 . Vice President Creative, Walt Disney World Portfolio at Walt Disney Imagineering, Michael Hundgen told Variety , “We’re so excited to bring Monstropolis to life for fans.” Currently under construction, Monstropolis will transport visitors into the world of Sulley and Mike. Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) According to Disney, guests will have the chance to explore the city, meet its citizens, taste unique cuisine, and step into the everyday world of monsters in a totally new way. For the first time, two worlds—once separated—are coming face to face, not through screams, but through laughter. Popular on Variety Hundgen explained, “’Monsters, Inc’ is right up there in terms of iconic locations. The moment you saw it, you thought, ‘I want to go to a world where monsters live and work and play.’ And so, to get to do that at the scale that we’re doing it at is phenomenal. Not only is it about the breadth of the land, but also about creating some of these iconic locations that we’ve seen in the films throughout the years that we’re now getting to realize.’” A central element of Monstropolis is its theatrical experience, which Hundgen emphasized as an important addition to the land. “We knew the door coaster was the cornerstone of the experience,” he said. “It feels like just giving them a coaster would shortchange the experience. So, we embarked on this idea of a theater experience that would really orient our guests to Monsters. We’re inviting folks into this land for the first time, and the monsters are a little skittish around that, so they’re kind of feeling us out. For so long they’ve been sometimes as afraid of us as we are of them, and so this idea that we’re all working in harmony together is new to them.” Hundgen explained that it wouldn’t be a typical theater experience. Collaborating with Pixar and Industrial Light & Magic, the team has developed high-definition panels combined with physical characters. In addition to humor and heart, the show will feature a new original song written exclusively for the park by composer Randy Newman.“It’s the first time Randy has ever written something exclusively for a Disney theme park,” Hundgen revealed, calling the song a perfect complement to the high-thrill rollercoaster that will be located nearby. Disney’s first-ever suspended rollercoaster ride will be a major highlight of the land. “It’s a showstopper,” Hundgen declared. “It’s the first hanging coaster we’ve ever done at Disney anywhere in the world. That opening scene will take you straight into the laugh floor, and guests will be placed into contraptions that Mike has created to harness both laughs and screams. The idea is that if you combine those two things—well, screams are powerful, but laughs are even more powerful.” The ride will take guests 40 feet high in four seconds, he teases. “When you think about show-stopping moments in our canon, that is going to be up there as one of the biggest and best that we’ve ever seen.” The rollercoaster will take guests 40 feet high in just four seconds. “When you think about show-stopping moments in our canon, this will rank as one of the biggest and best,” Hundgen teased. He credited the Imagineering team and their research and development efforts for pushing the boundaries of innovation. “Some of the techniques we’re using in the theater itself come from our partnerships with R&D and ILM,” he said. “More importantly, it’s about using technology to support the story we’re telling. What can we do to deepen the emotional connection guests have with these characters while using tech to enable that?” Hundgen also noted the use of innovative techniques in both the theater and coaster experience. “We’re drawing inspiration from immersive theater and optical illusions that make you feel like things are actually there—paired with physical elements that truly are there,” he explained. “You’ll see plenty of that in the theater experience, as well as a few tricks in the coaster that combine old-school illusions with new tech, all infused with the humor and heart of these characters.” In addition to the theatrical experience and the rollercoaster, Monstropolis will feature merchandise locations and new restaurants—Disney staples. Among them will be Archie’s Scare Pig Pizza, inspired by the mascot from “Monsters University,” and Harryhausen’s, the sushi restaurant featured in the first film where Mike and Celia went on their date. “We’re reimagining Harryhausen’s as a brand-new space,” Hundgen shared. “The menu will be wildly fun. Imagine sushi dishes inspired by the monster world: sushi rolls, tempura satays, all with iconic names that feel straight out of the film.” Guests can also look forward to an animatronic octopus sushi chef. “We’re going to have a full-on animatronic sushi octopus figure, cooking up sushi and playing host,” he confirmed. Monstropolis is scheduled to open in 2027, with restaurants, merchandise experiences, and the theater show debuting alongside the new land. Hundgen expressed excitement about the ambitious project. “Monsters, being one of the first out the gate, will really raise the bar. It’s an incredible project team—passionate and dedicated—and they’ve worked through some pretty gnarly challenges. This will be a fantastic addition to Hollywood Studios and Walt Disney World as a whole. It’s going to be quite the destination.” This AI Startup Made a 24-Hour AI News Channel. Who Wants This? The film is produced by Ananya Birla’s Birla Studios , Hansal Mehta and Sahil Saigal’s True Story Films and Singh’s Maa Kasam Films. Singh, who headlines the project, also serves as a producer on the film, which is directed by Jai Mehta. One of the top stars of Bollywood, Singh takes on a physically demanding role for “Pralay.” This is his next project after the “Dhurandhar” (2025) and “Dhurandhar – The Revenge” (2026) duology, which are among the highest-grossing Indian films of all time. articles.title: ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’
articles.full_text: Aug 16, 2026 1:33am PT ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’ By Christopher Vourlias Plus Icon Christopher Vourlias Latest ‘Shame and Money’ Director on Sundance-Winning Drama About a Kosovo Family in Free Fall: ‘It’s a Look Into the Past and a Warning to the Future’ 33 minutes ago Sarajevo Industry Head on How Building a Talent Pipeline Makes Markets and Festivals More Vital Than Ever 3 days ago Sarajevo Film Festival Head on How Southeast Europe’s Leading Cinematic Showcase Continues to ‘Forge Its Own Way’ 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Vicky Bane, Schuldenberg Films Sundance Grand Jury Prize winner Visar Morina returns to the Sarajevo Film Festival — the scene of a previous triumph — with the biting social drama “Shame and Money,” which won the top prize in Park City earlier this year and is playing in the festival’s main competition. The director’s third feature wowed audiences at Sundance, where Variety ’s chief film critic Guy Lodge praised the “stoic, slowly lacerating look at economic desperation and exploitation in contemporary Europe” as a “keenly observed, sharp-edged portrait of a Kosovo family divided by class.” Related Stories Mubi to Release ‘La Mesías,’ From ‘La Bola Negra’ Cannes Best Director Winners, in the U.K., Germany, Canada, Australia and Beyond (EXCLUSIVE) Morina’s previous film, “ Exile ,” which also premiered in Park City, won the Sarajevo Film Festival in 2020. That film, about a Kosovan immigrant grappling with paranoia after a string of menacing events, was loosely inspired by the director’s own experience. Born in Kosovo, Morina emigrated with his family to Germany in the 1990s, before the war that would ultimately lead to the country’s independence. Popular on Variety “Shame and Money” follows Shaban (Astrit Kabashi) and Hatixhe (Flonja Kodheli), a couple in their forties living with their extended family in rural Kosovo, where they eke out a modest living on their farm. When a family dispute leads to a terrible act of betrayal, their livelihood is suddenly lost. Along with Shaban’s mother and the couple’s young daughters, they are forced to move to Pristina, where the pressure to provide weighs heavily on both husband and wife. Piecing together odd jobs, they do their best to find a way in the hyper-capitalist Kosovan capital, until the relentless struggle of daily life pushes Shaban to the breaking point. Though deeply rooted in the sociopolitical realities of Kosovo, a country that’s largely failed to make good on the promises of the post-war order, Morina sees “Shame and Money” as a parable of modern-day Europe. Across the continent, he notes, the rising cost of living, housing shortages, stagnant wages and a growing rift between the haves and have-nots has spurred widespread pessimism about the direction in which society seems to be heading. “We are actually coming to a point in Germany where it feels like we are going straight to a situation like this in Kosovo,” Morina says. “It’s a look into the past and a warning to the future.” The film provides a bleak portrait of Kosovo, a war-scarred country whose social fabric is fraying at the seams: a society where, as Shaban is reminded by his brother-in-law, Alban (Alban Ukaj), a nouveau riche businessman who reluctantly agrees to take in the struggling family, “Everything has its place. And every person, too.” For the husband and wife duo, that means a succession of low-skilled, low-wage jobs as they scrap to make ends meet. The rigid taxonomy of contemporary urban life couldn’t be more apparent: When Shaban is offered a job as a night watchman at a gated community rising on the city’s outskirts, he explains to Hatixhe that it is a job “to keep out poor people like us.” Gradually, Shaban becomes a ghost of himself, in what comes to feel like a natural outcome in a society where a man’s value can be calculated down to the very last cent. “‘When you’re broke, even your mom doesn’t love you,’” Morina recalls a Kosovan man once telling him. “There is nothing I associate more strongly with the film than this phrase.” “Shame and Money” is written by Morina and Doruntina Basha. It’s produced by Vicky Bane and Schuldenberg Films in co-production with Eagle Eye Films, Vertigo Ljubljana, On Film Production, List Production and Quetzalcoatl. World sales are being handled by The Yellow Affair and Espoo. In both of his most recent features, Morina has been preoccupied with the lives of outsiders — those who, either because of immigration (“Exile”) or class status (“Shame and Money”), are shunted to the periphery of society. Increasingly, it seems those dividing lines have become chasms. At a time when the world (briefly) christened its first trillionaire and the ruling classes build underground bunkers or dream of blasting off into outer space, “Shame and Money” provides a stark warning about the direction in which things are trending — both for our societies and ourselves. “I really believe that people can only take shit to a certain extent. At some point, they go crazy,” says Morina. “There is this German word sozialer Frieden — social harmony. And I think at some point, there is a point of no return.” The Sarajevo Film Festival runs Aug. 14 – 21. This AI Startup Made a 24-Hour AI News Channel. Who Wants This? Loading comments... articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Destiny Jackson , Glenn Garner August 15, 2026 2:26pm 'Your Friendly Neighboorhood Spider-Man' on Disney+ Disney+/Marvel Everyone grab your webshooters because it’s undoubtedly Spidey season. During a Saturday panel at D23 expo, a group of presenters that include Marvel studio’s president Kevin Feige, Spider-Man : Brand New Day actor Jacob Batalon and Disney+’s Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man showrunner Jeff Trammell hit the stage to celebrate 65 years of Spider-Man. Though Peter doesn’t look a day older than his perpetual mid-teens to late 20s, the iconic webslinger has certainly earned his 401k pension and retirement plan these past six decades. Related Stories News Everything Announced At D23: New X-Men Cast, ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Teaser, ‘Coco 2,’ ‘Tangled’ Live Action First Look & More Casting ‘X-Men’ Adds Christopher Abbott, Adam Driver, Inde Navarette & Maya Boyd; Marvel Studios Pic Set for May 2028 – D23 Reflecting on Spider-Man’s ever growing popularity which has now expanded more than ever across the forms of an entire Spider-Verse, several highest grossing films, TV shows, video games and more comics, Feige and Batalon discussed the superhero’s legacy. Watch on Deadline “There is so much story to tell, that even after 65 years, we’re just starting,” said Feige. Marvel Studios President Kevin Feige and ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ actor Jacob Batalon walk out on stage at #D23 to the crowd chanting “C-E-O” at Jacob. The pair also talk about Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s billion dollar impact. pic.twitter.com/XvztgLKjdg — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 15, 2026 After receiving “C.E.O.” chants from the audience and ribbing Feige about getting his “own show,” Batalon added, “Truly just, wherever the story takes us, we’re willing to follow. I feel like we all work with amazing people who make great things and just want to be a part of something you all love.” Although Tom Holland wasn’t present, he graced attendees with a video message. “Playing Peter Parker is my dream, and getting to live that dream has been one of the greatest privileges of my career,” he said. Surprises revealed today on the Premiere stage included the announcement of an interview between Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘s Tom Holland and Destin Daniel Cretton which will be featured in the upcoming milestone comic Amazing Spider-Man #1000 . The several story issue, coming out in September, will follow Spider-Man as he faces his first new fear-inducing and formidable villain in decades named Ravage. It will also mark Noah Hawley’s comic book writing debut. Tom Holland sends a video to #D23 ’s 65 years of Spider-Man panel. Talking about what the role means to him and wishing the fans well. pic.twitter.com/80LekLrywT — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 15, 2026 Disney+’s Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man Season 2, dropping January 2027, teased the introduction of Gwen Stacy and Eddie Brock, working for the Daily Bugle, as Doc Oc attacks a gala and kidnaps Harry Osborn after a brief fight with Spidey, who later in the trailer, is exposed to Venom’s symbiote. Alyssa Sapire, head of Disney Jr. Original Programming confirmed a Season 7 renewal of Spidey and His Amazing Friends alongside debuting a first-look at Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up and casting announcement of guest star musicians Este Haim and Patrick Stump as villains Hallows Eve and Jack O’Latern respectively. #D23 65-years of Spider-Man panel features first look title card for ‘Your Friendly Neighborhood Spider-Man’ Season 2 alongside a villain casting announcement of musicians Este Haim and Patrick Stump for the upcoming special ‘Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up.’ (They… pic.twitter.com/iy4Px0MC8x — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 15, 2026 In 1996, Spider-Man co-creator Stan Lee (sans other co-creator Steve Ditko) told the Chicago Tribune why the character meant so much to him, as well as the rest of the world: “He’s the most famous. He’s the one who’s most like me – nothing ever turns out 100% OK; he’s got a lot of problems, he does things wrong, and I can relate to that… he’s got that feeling of the average guy who turned into a hero and still has problems.” And it seems like with great power and great responsibility that Spider-Man will be enduring plenty more. articles.title: ‘Summer House’ Enters A “New Chapter” After Landing Its First Emmy Recognition – Contenders TV Nominees Studio
articles.full_text: Lindsay Hubbard , one of the stars of Bravo ’s Summer House , was doing an on-camera interview for a different reality show when shocking news broke that two of her Summer House castmates had gotten together. At the end of March, Amanda Batula, who was still married to Kyle Cooke, and West Wilson, who had previously dated Batula’s close friend Ciara Miller, released a statement about their budding relationship. Related Stories News ‘Summer House’ Season 10 Reunion Show Breaks Bravo Ratings Record Ahead Of Final Installment News Emmy Nominations 2026: The Complete List Carl Radke , fellow Summer House star, told Deadline that he saw the pair’s statement when he landed in Los Angeles and realized that Hubbard was in the middle of shooting confessionals for Summer House spinoff In the City . This required a quick pivot from producers, as they revealed during a conversation featuring Hubbard, fellow castmate Carl Radke, executive producer Jamie Jakimo and showrunner Trish Gold for Deadline’s Contenders Television: The Nominees Studio. Watch the conversation below and scroll down for more photos from the event. Jakimo, executive producer and SVP Programming at Summer House producer Truly Original, said, “When some news was put on the internet, we happened to have Lindsay in the studio with us. This is real. We follow what’s real, so we knew we had to camera up. We were on a green screen for a different show. This is happening now. Get the cameras. When something is newsworthy, noteworthy and affecting these cast members, we’re going to capture it.” The only problem was that the show was already in post and the reunion was coming up. “As producers, we’re learning things in real time, much like cast members,” Jakimo added. “We’ve become very nimble over the years where when we see things happening, when we get a call from somebody like Lindsay.” The scandal dominated the internet and continues to do so, and helped Summer House land its first-ever Emmy nomination after 10 seasons. The show is competing against the likes of Love on the Spectrum , America’s Sweethearts: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders , RuPaul’s Drag Race: Untucked and Welcome to Wrexham in the Outstanding Unstructured Reality Program category. Hubbard told Deadline that she was “overwhelmed with excitement” about the nomination and joked that it was “overdue.” “Being recognized after 10 seasons is incredible,” Radke added. “We really are real friends, which of course provides a lot of ups and downs.” While the scandal involving Batula, Wilson and Miller may have got the headlines for Season 10, there were other storylines, including Hubbard and Radke becoming friends again after previously being together. “I was just excited and glad that [Lindsay] and I could continue to kind of grow the friendship, get some closure from the past, kind of try to move on with respect and try to build a new chapter of a friendship. You saw pieces of that like the conversation her and I had at the Labor Day party,” Radke said. “Watching it back was really meaningful and touching. She’s been just cool with me.” “We’re cooler than ever,” added Hubbard. 01 Carl Radke and Lindsay Hubbard Anthony Avellano for Deadline Lindsay Hubbard Anthony Avellano for Deadline L-R: Carl Radke; Jamie Jakimo and Trish Gold Anthony Avellano for Deadline L-R: Lindsay Hubbard, Jamie Jakimo, Trish Gold and Carl Radke Anthony Avellano for Deadline “We really tell these people’s stories,” added Gold. “It’s less about trying to make sure we get every little bit, but really rounding out everybody’s stories and being able to tell a complete story. How do we help move through this when relationships are fractured? One of the things that’s so pivotal is when Summer House is repairing relationships, because they are friends, and I think that’s unique to our show versus some of the other shows that are out there.” The cast is currently filming Season 11 in a new house as well as a crossover with Below Deck Mediterranean . Wilson and Batula are no longer on the show, but Hubbard, Radke, Cooke, Miller, Jesse Solomon, Bailey Taylor, KJ Dillard and Mia Calabrese are. “It feels good to be back. We’re like the little show that could. I feel like we have finally hit our stride. But now, it’s a new chapter,” said Radke. “It’s normal and natural for it to evolve with maybe some new faces or some people graduate or do whatever. It’s a totally new summer, but we have a new house.” Hubbard said that the whole situation “took a lot out of us.” She said, “We spent a lot of time on it, emotionally, mentally, physically. We were all ready to put it behind us and just celebrate a fresh start and a new house with a fun summer.” They’re all single now, as well, Hubbard stressed. “That makes for a fun summer.” Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Scott Foley Returning To ‘Scrubs’ As Sean Kelly In Season 2 Of ABC Revival To Revisit Classic Storyline
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Scott Foley Returning To ‘Scrubs’ As Sean Kelly In Season 2 Of ABC Revival To Revisit Classic Storyline ‘Scrubs’ Adds Keyla Monterroso Mejia As New Nurse In Season 2 Of ABC Revival ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Renewed For Season 2 By HBO Max View All August 15, 2026 2:30pm Scott Foley/'Scrubs' Lebo Lukewarm/Paul Drinkwater/Disney General Entertainment Content via Getty Images EXCLUSIVE : Cue the “Nobody cares, Sean” memes — Scott Foley is coming back to Scrubs . He will reprise his fan-favorite character Sean Kelly on the upcoming second season of the ABC revival. Related Stories Casting ‘Scrubs’ Adds Keyla Monterroso Mejia As New Nurse In Season 2 Of ABC Revival Casting ‘SNL’ Alum John Higgins Joins ‘Scrubs’ For Major Role In Season 2 Of ABC Revival Foley’s return is being announced today at D23’s “Scrubs : Scrubbing Back” panel moderated by Foley and featuring series stars/executive producers Zach Braff (John “J.D.” Dorian), Donald Faison (Christopher Turk) and Sarah Chalke (Elliot Reid), along with showrunner/executive producer Aseem Batra, which also teased more fantasy sequences and the comeback of J.D. beloved blue scooter Sasha next season. Deadline can reveal that Foley will be recurring and, in a full-circle moment, Sean will go back to where his journey on the show started, dating Elliot (Chalke). A Season 2 teaser, which you can watch below, provides a glimpse of Sean and Elliot’s reunion in the hospital cafeteria. Watch on Deadline The duo will be rekindling their romance just as Elliot’s ex-husband J.D. is embarking on a relationship with Charlie (Rachel Bilson), who was introduced in the Season 1 finale . “Scott Foley’s back to be love interest for Sarah, and Rachel has been mine; the dynamic with us all together is just hilarious, and we’re having so much fun,” Braff told Deadline. Added Chalke, “The writers were like, how do we bring back Elliot’s neurosis, and they thought that Scott would be a good way to do that.” She touched on that at D23, with Braff jumping in to announce Foley’s return. Chalke discussed Elliot and Sean’s reunion scene, in which she “falls gracefully” as her heel gets caught on her medical coat. Sarah Chalke is talking about Elliot’s neurosis and a moment she has in Season 2 when Zach Braff chimes in to reveal Scott Foley’s return as Sean Kelly More details here: https://t.co/KYVNyCE5L5 pic.twitter.com/H7d4fjCuyT — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 15, 2026 Foley made his Scrubs debut at the end of Season 1, when Sean, a marine biologist and animal trainer at SeaWorld, was admitted to Sacred Heart with Elliot as his doctor. The two had a brief fling before she dumped him. Sean and Elliot reconnected again in Season 3 and dated for awhile, taking their relationship long-distance when Sean went to New Zealand. Elliot broke things off shortly after Sean returned as her romance with J.D. started to heat up, news Sean did not take well. He eventually moved on with J.D.’s baby mama Kim Briggs (Elizabeth Banks). Foley had been on Scrubs creator Bill Lawrence’s wish list for the revival for awhile. “I really want to have Scott Foley back, I want to have him back on the show just so Zach can say ‘Nobody cares, Sean,'” Lawrence said at PaleyFest in April, referring to the famous dismissive line J.D. uses in conversations with Sean on the original show. The catchphrase took on a life of its own and, two decades later, it continues to haunt Foley, with fans using it to respond to any post he puts up on social media. Foley brought up the infamous line when he came out on stage at D23. “This is personal for me. For those of your who don’t know, I played a character names Sean Kelly. Nobody cares, I heard that,” he said, adding, that he was part of “one of the most complicated love triangles in this show’s history.” Scott Foley takes the stage for the ‘Scrubs’ panel at #D23 to intro Zach Braff, Donald Faison and Sarah Chalke pic.twitter.com/Ha4fi2u6gH — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 15, 2026 In a January interview, Foley revealed that Braff had asked him to return in Season 1 of the new Scrubs and that he had been scheduled for an episode but the schedule could not be worked out. “I’m sure we’ll find the time,” Foley said at the time as he was promoting his Prime Video series It’s Not Like That . The streamer ended up canceling the well received family drama after one season, and Foley’s two-season arc on Will Trent came to an end in May, rendering the Felicity and Scandal alum available . In Season 2 of Scrubs, J.D., Turk and Elliot have leveled up from interns to icons at Sacred Heart. Now, the respected doctors inspire the next generation while balancing the ups and downs of working in a hospital. Together with characters new and old, they are navigating this next chapter with laughter, heart and some surprises along the way. Foley’s return certainly qualifies as one of the surprises. Here is the trailer, which also teases the returns of other OGs from Season 1: In addition to Braff, Faison and Chalke, the Season 2 series regular cast includes Ava Bunn as intern Sam Tosh. The original series’ creator Bill Lawrence serves as executive producer on the revival via his Doozer Productions alongside the company’s Jeff Ingold and Liza Katzer as well as showrunner Batra and stars Braff, Faison and Chalke. In addition to Scrubs , Foley has done three other Bill Lawrence series, Cougar Town, Undateable and Whiskey Cavalier . His upcoming movies include Keep Coming Back and August . articles.title: Rob Rausch Played It Cool On ‘The Traitors’ But His Co-Stars Think “Mr. America” Was A “Bad Boy” – Contenders TV Nominees Studio
articles.full_text: Rob Rausch , a handsome snake-wrangler from Alabama, was standing a few feet away from Maura Higgins , the former Love Islander, next to the Traitors ’ roundtable. Showing little emotion, he finally revealed that he had double-crossed her to win more than $220,000. “I was so fooled by you, you absolute *sshole, you pinky promised,” Higgins says in the Peacock finale. “You’re never going to have a girlfriend after this; you’re such a good liar.” Related Stories News ‘The Traitors’ Hits Record High Audience For Season 4 Finale On The BBC News Emmy Nominations 2026: The Complete List Higgins and the majority of the cast had been fooled all along. “I wish I could sit here and say I knew he was a traitor, but I had no clue,” Higgins said at Deadline’s Contenders Television: The Nominees Studio. “He played the best game in that castle. I genuinely did believe he was a faithful, but you know what? It’s a game, and I was fine with it. I went through all the emotions very quickly, and then I was like, ‘You know what? Fair play.’ I genuinely was so convinced that me and him was winning the show together.” Higgins was joined by Rausch and fellow Season 4 contestants Monét X Change , Tara Lipinski , Lisa Rinna , Rob Cesternino and Eric Nam for the Deadline conversation. Watch the discussion below, and scroll down for photos from the event. Rausch was cold as ice. “I was actually surprised in the edit. I feel like they made me seem a little more nervous than I was,” he said. Rausch, who also became famous on the U.S. version of Love Island , did make it up to Higgins, somewhat, by buying her a Hermès Birkin bag. Rinna, a fellow traitor and the person who helped Rausch secure the bag, had similarly been crossed by him, twice. “I just didn’t see that coming, so I was really genuinely shocked by that because I thought he was a better boy than that, but he wasn’t,” she said. “Everyone wanted him to be Mr. America, and no one wanted to believe that he could possibly be a traitor.” It was a dynamite finale for the Studio Lambert-produced show, which scored six Emmy nominations this year including for Outstanding Reality Competition Program, after winning that category the past two seasons. In addition to those on the Deadline panel, the series starred Ian Terry, Porsha Williams, Donna Kelce, Caroline Stanbury, Tiffany Mitchell, Michael Rapaport, Ron Funches, Yamil ‘Yam Yam’ Arocho, Colton Underwood, Candiace Dillard Bassett, Dorinda Medley, Stephen Colletti, Kristen Kish, Natalie Anderson, Mark Ballas, Johnny Weir and Eric Nam. 01 Tara Lipinski and Maura Higgins Anthony Avellano for Deadline Rob Rausch Anthony Avellano for Deadline Lisa Rinna Anthony Avellano for Deadline Monét X Change Anthony Avellano for Deadline Eric Nam Anthony Avellano for Deadline Rob Cesternino Anthony Avellano for Deadline Nam, who became a traitor after being recruited halfway through the show, was also crossed by Rausch in the finale. “Rob was like ‘We’re going to win this together’ and I was like ‘Cool.’” The singer-songwriter said it was difficult pivoting from being a faithful to becoming a traitor. “Emotionally, it was exhausting,” he said. “We had quickly become friends. I went to bed one night and three hours later, you have to go decide who to kill and that was such a stressful experience.” One moment not shown on screen was when the whole group was going down the stairs: Nam shouted “Traitor,” and Rinna turned her head. She was subsequently banished in episode 7. But she was fine with that. “I had no strategy whatsoever, but the plan that I had was I wanted to wear that Erik Charlotte Couture dress to the banquet, and I didn’t know when the banquet was because they tell you nothing. I was just holding out for that, and so once they got me after that, I was fine because in my mind I had won,” she said. Monét X Change, a faithful murdered in episode 5, said that he had tried to send Higgins “messages from the grave” but she didn’t hear him. Cesternino, a former Survivor star, was murdered in episode 3. He said that The Traitors is more “mentally taxing” than the CBS competition series. Lipinski, an Olympic figure skater, made it to the end but couldn’t convince Higgins or Nam that Rausch was a traitor. “He plays it so cool, at all times,” she said. “You’re constantly surveying everyone, and you just don’t pick up any type of energy of [whether] he even wants to be there. He just did a great job.” Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Mason Thames Reveals He & McKenna Grace Filmed ‘Nimrods’ Before ‘Regretting You’, Talks Possibility Of Doing “Another Job Together”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Outlander’s Caitríona Balfe Joins Live-Action ‘Tangled’ As Queen Arianna Mason Thames Reveals He & McKenna Grace Filmed ‘Nimrods’ Before ‘Regretting You’, Talks Possibility Of Doing “Another Job Together” All Things Spidey At D23: Tom Holland, Anniversary Comic Book, ‘Friendly Neighborhood’ Sneak-Peak, ‘Amazing Friends’ Renewal & Upcoming Special ‘Spidey and the Avengers: Halloween Team-Up!’ View All August 15, 2026 4:03pm Mason Thames discusses filming 'Regretting You' and 'Nimrods' with McKenna Grace. Jessica Miglio/Paramount Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection/Inaugural Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection Nearly a year after they first appeared onscreen together in Regretting You , Mason Thames and McKenna Grace are playing romantic opposites again. Following Colleen Hoover romance’s premiere last October, Thames recently revealed he had already worked with Grace on the Green Day-inspired movie Nimrods , which is now playing in theaters. “So we did Green Da y first. Green Day movie first, and then we did Regretting You right after,” he explained to People . “But it was just so wild. The coincidence of two back-to-back is awesome and we love it.” Related Stories News Green Day’s Billie Joe Armstrong On How His Son Helped Make ‘Nimrods’ Feel “Current,” Potential Of ‘American Idiot’ Movie Musical: “We Talk About It” News Upcoming Mason Thames Movies From ‘Idiots’ To ‘How To Train Your Dragon 2’ Thames added, “I’m so happy that we can finally release it to everybody, because it’s felt like my little secret and my little experience, but I really hope people go to see it and feel the love that was used to make this movie, because I’m really happy with it.” Watch on Deadline After playing romantic opposites twice now, the real-life couple is open to working together again. “If we were ever going to do another job together, we’d want it to be so special and so awesome, so whenever that moment arises, we’re going to snatch it up,” said Thames. Mason Thames and McKenna Grace in ‘Nimrods’ (2025) (Inaugural Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection) In Nimrods , Tommy (Thames) receives a call inviting him and his band Analog Dogs to open for Green Day on New Year’s Eve in Los Angeles. Not realizing it’s his older brother Wayne (Keen Ruffalo) pulling an elaborate prank, Tommy steals Wayne’s car and sets off on a cross-country roadtrip from Kansas City with his bandmates Fred (Kylr Coffman) and Chad (Ryan Foust). Along the way, Tommy meets fellow punk Olivia (Grace) and strikes up a flirtation after seeing her perform live. Both Thames and Grace appear on the movie’s soundtrack. “I mean, those kids are fantastic. They can do anything ,” raved co-writer/director Lee Kirk to Deadline. “And they’re the nicest kids, creative kids, very eager. They were up for whatever we wanted to do. I was so lucky that McKenna wanted to do it and she wanted to put her song in the movie. I just felt like it gave it some authenticity to it, and Mason with his singing, he rehearsed, he worked on those songs, which were written by Billie Joe [Armstrong’s] son, by the way.
