articles.title: ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Review: A Potentially Involving Story Is Weakened by Airless Dialogue and a Misguided Finale
articles.full_text: Aug 14, 2026 1:12am PT ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Review: A Potentially Involving Story Is Weakened by Airless Dialogue and a Misguided Finale A big man in a small city learns that his nonentity of a son killed a Roma man, but as directed, produced, written and edited by Florin Şerban, the film resists sympathy at every turn. By Jay Weissberg Plus Icon Jay Weissberg Latest ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Review: A Potentially Involving Story Is Weakened by Airless Dialogue and a Misguided Finale 2 hours ago ‘Far From the Trees’ Review: A Richly Contemplative Journey of Physical and Mental Meanderings, Beautifully Combining 4K Digital with Super 16 21 hours ago ‘Wandering Trees’ Review: Iconoclastic Director Salvatore Mereu Tries a Newly Minted Fairyale, but Only Fitfully Finds Magic 2 days ago See All Courtesy of Fantascope Films Florin Şerban’s “You Don’t Belong Here” opens with great promise and finishes with a stupefyingly misguided coda: The lengthy minutes in between are rigorously filmed and sharply observed, but would have benefited enormously if the director wasn’t also the producer, writer and editor. Airless pauses between nearly every line of dialogue and a mostly fixed camera allergic to close-ups sink this potentially intriguing story of an upright surgeon in a small city discovering that his teenage son is a racist milksop who killed a Roma man. The static visuals have a certain pedagogical function indicative of scrupulous honesty — no tricks or cuts will interpose on this supposed truthfulness — but the oddly unnatural spaces between every sentence have an artificiality that undercuts the claim to exacting realism. It’s an odd choice from Şerban, whose Berlinale-award 2010 debut “If I Want to Whistle, I Whistle” had a genuinely lively authenticity. Related Stories ‘Reacher’ Star Alan Ritchson Slams ‘F—ing Pedophiles’ in Politics: ‘I Would Get Those Epstein Files Out in Two Seconds … Bitch, Move’ 'Reacher' Spinoff 'Neagley' Trailer Teases Creepy Cult at Center of Murder Mystery Things start auspiciously with Mahler’s 3 rd Symphony accompanying shots of the western city of Reșița, the grand music acting as a counterpoint to the town’s anodyne panorama, suggesting that even in such a nondescript place, something beautiful can exist. That idea is quickly shattered when a stream of masked bike riders armed with baseball bats slap “You Don’t Belong Here” stickers on the cars of the Roma community that they then vandalize. When a man comes out to stop them, he’s beaten to death. Popular on Variety The next morning, Dr. Marius (Adrian Văncică) discovers that some Roma went on a rampage in the hospital morgue, trying to claim the dead man’s body. That same day, the surgeon’s teenage son Ioan (Teodor Butănescu) goes to the school nurse asking to be seen anonymously to check on major bruising he claims to have gotten when he fell off his bike. In a very short time, the story is clearly demarcated, allowing Şerban to focus on character. Marius, approaching 50, is a big doctor in this provincial city, not just a surgeon but the director of the hospital, and a man who prides himself on his directness and honesty. Given how cold he is with most of the people around him, it’s surprising he has a decent bedside manner, but there’s clearly a generational divide between him and junior doctor Tudor (Tudor Vîrgă), who goes out of his way to thank the nursing staff following surgery. For Marius’ friend, police chief Silviu (Alex Conovaru), such solicitude is weak and unmanly. That evening, following a threatening encounter with the dead man’s son (Izdrailă Janir), Marius meets his lover Dana (Cristina Richter), and in a lengthy conversation — more like a monologue à la Nuri Bilge Ceylan — he explains that important men like himself need to crack the whip so others will learn how to behave. “I need to be mean,” he explains, before then revealing his insecurities: “What if I’m not as great as I think I am?” He knows he’s a just person, but what if that’s all? The scene is the only one with some honest introspection and also one of the few times when Marius shows any vulnerability, though the truth is, he’s largely dead inside despite later declarations that his son is his entire world. Had Şerban shown even an iota of that father-son love, the film could have professed some kind of emotional core, but what’s seen on screen are people devoid of affection, and only when Marius’s hardened exterior crumbles on learning that Ioan is suspected of murder does the viewer extend begrudging sympathy to the man. (Though when he admits to not feeling love for Dana, that sympathy goes down another notch.) The problem isn’t the characterization, since the surgeon is extremely well drawn and Văncică’s performance picks up on both the overall inner emptiness and the yearning for something more. What really hampers “You Don’t Belong Here” is the frigid mise-en-scène . Every scene feels inert, and for reasons best known to Şerban, Liviu Mãrghidan’s camera keeps a distance from the characters, making us cold voyeurs unable to get near anyone. At least we regularly see Văncică’s face, unlike Butănescu’s, shot obliquely or in shadow, his perpetual downcast posture making him nothing more than an empty cypher, a babyish teen destined to disappoint any parent. Equally unclear is why every line of dialogue has to have a pause before the next character responds; it’s just one of several directorial and script choices, like the truly unfortunate ending, that will leave audiences wondering how much better the story could have been had a producer and editor cracked the whip that Marius boasts about. ‘You Don’t Belong Here’ Review: A Potentially Involving Story Is Weakened by Airless Dialogue and a Misguided Finale Reviewed at Locarno Film Festival (International Competition), Aug. 8, 2026 (Also in Sarajevo Film Festival.) Running time: 154 MIN. (Original title: ‘Nu e locul tau aici’) Production: (Romania). A Fantascope Films production in co-production with Scharf Film Production, Avanpost, Earlybird, Adrian Văncică, Asociaţia Art-Act 27, Școala de Film. (World sales: REASON8, London). Producer: Florin Şerban. Co-producers: Ruxandra Flonta, Carmen Rizac, Vlad Rădulescu, Marius Leftărache, Sebastian Plămădeală, Adrian Văncică. Executive producer: Minodora Şerban. Crew: Director, screenplay, editor: Florin Şerban. Camera: Liviu Mãrghidan. Music: Marius Leftărache, Nikita Dembinski. With: Adrian Văncică, Teodor Butănescu, Cristina Richter, Alex Conovaru, Izdrailă Janir, Adriana Neagoe, Tudor Vîrgă, Emil Boroghină. articles.title: TV Academy Hall of Fame: Sheila Nevins, Absent Due to COVID, Thanks Dr. Fauci for the Vaccine; Bill Hader Pays Tribute to the ‘South Park’ Creators With a ‘Fish Dick’ Story and More
articles.full_text: Aug 14, 2026 1:16am PT TV Academy Hall of Fame: Sheila Nevins, Absent Due to COVID, Thanks Dr. Fauci for the Vaccine; Bill Hader Pays Tribute to the ‘South Park’ Creators With a ‘Fish Dick’ Story and More By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest TV Academy Hall of Fame: Sheila Nevins, Absent Due to COVID, Thanks Dr. Fauci for the Vaccine; Bill Hader Pays Tribute to the ‘South Park’ Creators With a ‘Fish Dick’ Story and More 2 hours ago Warner Bros. Discovery’s Gerhard Zeiler to Recieve Directorate Award at This Year’s International Emmys 13 hours ago How ‘All Her Fault’ Helped Put Peacock on the Map in Scripted Awards Conversations 15 hours ago See All TV Academy Documentary icon Sheila Nevins — who holds the all-time record for most Emmy wins by an individual (31), thanks to her long run as president of HBO Documentary Films — had to skip Thursday night’s Television Academy Hall of Fame event, after being diagnosed with COVID and pneumonia. Instead, Nevins sent her acceptance speech via video, and kicked off her thank-yous with a special shoutout: Dr. Anthony Fauci. “I’d like to thank a bunch of important people,” she said. “First and foremost, Dr. Fauci. Finally, I got tested, and lo and behold, they said — and they were right — ‘you’re lucky you got the vaccine because you’re going to be over this in five to eight days.’ And it’s true. This is the eighth day, and I’m testing negative. Thank you again, Dr. Fauci.” Related Stories ‘Reacher’ Star Alan Ritchson Slams ‘F—ing Pedophiles’ in Politics: ‘I Would Get Those Epstein Files Out in Two Seconds … Bitch, Move’ 'Reacher' Spinoff 'Neagley' Trailer Teases Creepy Cult at Center of Murder Mystery Nevins was one of six honorees at the Hall of Fame this year, which also included late “60 Minutes” correspondent Ed Bradley, actor Ted Danson ; “ South Park ” co-creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos and “Hacks” star Jean Smart . The event took place at the JW Marriott L.A. Live in downtown Los Angeles — where the TV Academy is set to kick off its annual Televerse conference on Friday. Popular on Variety After her Fauci reference, Nevins wasn’t done. She also had pointed things to say about several of her co-honorees: In the case of Smart, “it’s really quite astounding. Smart, funny, respect for age, beautiful, and most importantly, after so many seasons, able to earn the same amount of money that the men earn.” In the case of Bradley: “I remember those days at ’60 Minutes’ when people could say what they want to say and do what they wanted to do,” she said. “So thank you, man. You were a great newsman, a great reporter.” She thanked “South Park” creators Parker and Stone “for allowing the oligarchy to be punched through animated characters who don’t seem to matter, when, in fact, they can really say Americans are getting fucked.” In the case of late “60 Minutes” anchor Bradley, who died in 2006, his widow, Patricia Blanchet, accepted the award on his behalf. And toward the end of her speech, she acknowledged the troubling times at CBS News, where Bradley was based all those years on the newsmagazine. “In these most troubling of times, when debates abound about what the very nature of the free press is — and when the viability of this most necessary of public services, such a fundamental pillar of our democracy, is at risk — I miss the special skills that Ed brought to the work,” Blanchet said. “The fierce dedication to uncompromising ethics and journalistic standards, the profound compassion and empathy for the voiceless, the deep humanity peppered with great intellect and curiosity, the decency and civility, the wit and grit. “We could all benefit from his mastery now to come to grips with the daunting challenges we currently face as a nation, and indeed as a world,” she added. “Let us learn from and truly uphold Ed’s exceptional legacy. Let us heed Scott Pelley’s warning that CBS News is on fire, and indeed, so are so many of the institutions upon which we rely to uphold our democracy. Let us pick up Ed’s baton and speak truth to power. Let us walk his walk and better safeguard all that is at risk, that we hold so dear in our sacred democracy.” As CBS News’ Leslie Stahl said in her opening tribute to Bradley, “Ed was that the man you saw on television was exactly the man I knew off camera, and he covered a story with compassion. It was because Ed cared so deeply about the powerless. If he covered a story that filled you with joy, it was because Ed himself was so funny and loved to laugh.” For Parker and Stone, Thursday’s ceremony had a bit of serendipity: It was 29 years to the day that “South Park” premiered on Comedy Central — Aug. 13, 1997. Stone started by thanking his family, “because I’ve missed a few birthdays. And also we got the occasional fatwa and security situations.” Stone noted that it’s really deadlines that drive “South Park.” He said: “Trey and I would never have gotten a single episode of television or episode of ‘South Park’ on television without a deadline. And that for me is what television is about. Something going on the air.” Emmy winner Bill Hader, who had briefly worked on “South Park” (and received an Emmy for that time), gave the award to Parker and Stone — and began by telling the story of how the pitch for a “fish dick” storyline on the show came to be. (That anecdote is probably better to hear in person; see it here .) But Hader also wanted to set the record straight about his time on “South Park”: ‘People say ‘you wrote on the show!’ But, I didn’t. I got paid to laugh and watch all these writers and learn from them and how to tell a story. I would not have been able truly to run my own show without watching these guys. That’s where I learned everything.” Accepting her honor, “Hacks” star Jean Smart pointed out that some of her favorite TV moments growing up were when special broadcasts would return for special annual events — like “Peter Pan” with Mary Martin, “The Wizard of Oz” and Charlie Brown specials. “If you missed it, you missed it,” she said. “You had to wait until next year. But now, children can watch whatever they want, whenever they want, as many times as they want. I often wonder what that’s doing to us as a species, not having to ever wait for things, not having to wait for what we want. But that’s a discussion for another day!” Smart was introduced by “Hacks” creators Paul W. Downs, Lucia Aniello and Jen Statsky. “Jean has proven time and time again that she can be funny, dramatic, sexy, vulnerable and strong,” Downs said. “And on ‘Hacks,’ she showed us she can do all of those things, oftentimes in one scene, and sometimes in a single moment.” When it was Ted Danson’s return, he admitted he was a little shy about accepting the honor. “I have a little trouble with acknowledgment,” Danson said. “My mother, during the height of ‘Cheers,’ was asked what she thought of her son’s success, and she said, ‘Well, of course I’m happy for him, but I’ve always believed in the nobility of quiet failure.’ Seriously! So wish me luck.” Danson also paid his respects to the late Jimmy Burrows, who was one of the creators of “Cheers” with Glen and Les Charles. “He was like my dad in show business,” Danson said. “He guided me, taught me what was funny. When he wasn’t around, the few times he wouldn’t direct and someone else was directing, I literally did not know how to play Sam Malone. Because it was all about making Jimmy laugh.” Danson was presented the award by his wife, Mary Steenburgen, who added, “It’s a funny thing to be asked to introduce someone you’re married to. So many temptations. On the one hand, I know Ted Danson, as all of you do, as the charismatic actor whose career has spanned more than four decades. As the man who can make us laugh one minute and break our hearts with something so earnest the next. But I also know the man who has made me coffee every single morning for 31 years.” For Netflix’s co-CEO Ted Sarandos, he noted that he appreciated the honor since he’ll probably never be in line for a regular Emmy: “I have never created, written, or directed a show, so I’m not going to win an Emmy for that. You saw me [as a guest star] on ‘The Studio.’ Clearly, I’m not going to win an Emmy for acting!” Sarandos then made an impassioned support of television: “It is pretty remarkable that with every step of new technology, people still spend a remarkable amount of time watching television,” he said. “It’s incredibly stable, how much time people spend in front of that screen — whatever that screen they choose — and they are looking for those stories that are professionally made by creators with a capital ‘C.’ Because it taps into something deeply human, which is the desire to be told a great story. And television is the best way to tell great stories.” Sarandos gave a shoutout to the producers who have worked on Netflix shows through the years, particularly the early ones like “Arrested Development” creator Mitch Hurwitz. After “Arrested,” Hurwitz was also behind what Sarandos called his favorite Netflix series of all time, “Lady Dynamite.” Comedian Jerry Seinfeld presented the honor to Sarandos. “It’s so wonderful to be at the Academy of Television to induct Ted Sarandos of Netflix into the Hall of Fame. Even though at the same time, it’s hard for me to believe that I am not the one receiving this first,” he quipped. articles.title: Nigel Farage Documentary ‘Where Does the Money Come From?’ Set at U.K. Broadcaster 5 as Parliamentary Standards Watchdog Reopens Finance Probe
articles.full_text: Aug 14, 2026 2:21am PT Nigel Farage Documentary ‘Where Does the Money Come From?’ Set at U.K. Broadcaster 5 as Parliamentary Standards Watchdog Reopens Finance Probe By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Nigel Farage Documentary ‘Where Does the Money Come From?’ Set at U.K. Broadcaster 5 as Parliamentary Standards Watchdog Reopens Finance Probe 25 minutes ago Fukada Koji, Jakrawal Nilthamrong, Boo Junfeng Films Win Busan Co-Production Fund 2 hours ago Rani Mukerji Receives La Trobe Honorary Doctorate, Wins IFFM Special Citation 2 hours ago See All Getty Images ITN Productions has set “ Nigel Farage : Where Does the Money Come From?,” a one-hour documentary examining the Reform U.K. leader’s finances, to air on 5 , part of the Paramount Skydance Corporation, on Aug. 22. The documentary comes amid continuing scrutiny of Farage’s finances, following the Parliamentary Standards Commissioner’s investigation into gifts made to him and the Aug. 13 Clacton by-election that the sitting MP triggered by resigning his seat and standing again. Related Stories ‘Reacher’ Star Alan Ritchson Slams ‘F—ing Pedophiles’ in Politics: ‘I Would Get Those Epstein Files Out in Two Seconds … Bitch, Move’ 'Reacher' Spinoff 'Neagley' Trailer Teases Creepy Cult at Center of Murder Mystery The documentary will examine the donors, companies and payments that ITN said have reportedly brought Farage more than £2 million ($2.7 million) in outside income since he entered Parliament in 2024, along with earnings from broadcasting, after-dinner speaking and reported property interests. A cast of expert contributors will weigh in on reported payments, donations and gifts tied to two crypto financiers, alongside the parliamentary and media scrutiny of Farage’s finances. Popular on Variety Jeremy Daldry, deputy head of U.K. factual at ITN Productions, said Farage’s political reach has the potential to have a huge impact on the nation, adding that the standards commissioner’s investigation makes it the perfect time to unpack the story. “Topical, reactive documentaries are part of our DNA here at 5, and the questions around Farage’s finances really matter to our viewers,” added Federico Ruiz, commissioning editor at 5. “We dig deep into the publicly available information to examine the facts.” Farage announced on July 7 that he would give up his Clacton seat and stand again, framing the vote as a chance for his own constituents to judge him rather than “the establishment.” His resignation, formalized the next day, froze the standards commissioner’s inquiry into a £5 million ($6.7 million) gift from Thailand-based crypto billionaire Christopher Harborne that Farage had not declared. With the Labour, the Conservatives, the Liberal Democrats, the Greens and Restore Britain political parties all boycotting the contest, Farage’s most prominent challenger was Count Binface , a novelty candidate campaigning in a dustbin costume, part of a record field of 34 candidates. Farage won on Aug. 13 with 22,239 votes to Binface’s 9,455, and the standards investigation resumed within hours of his re-election, since such inquiries can only continue while their subject holds a Commons seat. If the commissioner finds Farage breached the MPs’ code of conduct, the case would go to the Committee on Standards, which could recommend sanctions ranging from an apology to a Commons suspension – a suspension of 10 sitting days or more can trigger a recall petition and, if signed by enough constituents, a fresh by-election in the seat. Farage is not the only senior Reform U.K. figure facing scrutiny. Deputy leader Richard Tice is under a separate standards investigation, opened in early August, over an alleged failure to declare a paid-for trip when speaking in a Commons debate. Robert Jenrick, who defected to Reform U.K. earlier this year, has also been referred to the standards commissioner by the Conservatives, while the Electoral Commission and police have separately been investigating donations linked to his 2024 Conservative leadership campaign. ITN Productions is the independent producer within newsmakers ITN, known for premium documentaries responding to major world events, including recent 5 titles “Air India Disaster: The Unanswered Questions” and “The Beckhams’ Billions: How Did They Get So Rich?” “Nigel Farage: Where Does the Money Come From?” is executive produced by Daldry, with Katie Harris and Chris Price-Morgan as producer/directors, Rusen Boztas as production manager and Laura Straker as production coordinator. Post-production was handled in-house at ITN Post. articles.title: ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ Is Drawing Tourists to Milan Prompting an 18% Increase in Visitors to the Film’s Locations in Italy’s Fashion Capital
articles.full_text: Aug 14, 2026 3:00am PT ‘The Devil Wears Prada 2’ Is Drawing Tourists to Milan Prompting an 18% Increase in Visitors to the Film’s Locations in Italy’s Fashion Capital By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Oscars: Switzerland Selects ‘Who is Still Alive’ About Palestinians Who Escaped Humanitarian Crisis in Gaza 19 hours ago Oscars: Turkey Submits ‘Like a Limbless Tree’ for International Feature Race 20 hours ago American Film Market Expands With Launch of AFM House, Site of Its Innovation Hub 2 days ago See All Courtesy Everett Collection “ The Devil Wears Prada 2 ” is making a heavenly impact on Milan. Just a few months after the theatrical release in May of the long-awaited sequel to “The Devil Wears Prada” – that was partly shot in Italy’s fashion capital that serves as a glitzy backdrop for the film’s third act – pedestrian traffic from international visitors at the movie’s main Milan locations has risen by 18% compared with the previous period, according to a study by the Cities Analytics platform. Related Stories 'Reacher' Spinoff 'Neagley' Trailer Teases Creepy Cult at Center of Murder Mystery ‘Reacher’ Star Alan Ritchson Slams ‘F—ing Pedophiles’ in Politics: ‘I Would Get Those Epstein Files Out in Two Seconds … Bitch, Move’ The sequel to the cult classic starring Meryl Streep , Anne Hathaway , Stanley Tucci and Emily Blunt, which features high-profile local cameos, including Donatella Versace and a live-shot Dolce & Gabbana fashion show, is considered the main driver to the influx of approximately 1.5 million international tourists expected to flock to the center of Milan during the summer quarter. More that 451,000 are expected in August alone, says the study released by the local small businesses association Confcommercio Milano, carried out using the Cities Analytics platform. Popular on Variety Confcommercio Milano chief Marco Barbieri said the study “confirms a structural growth trend in international tourism in central Milan,” since the “Devil Wears Prada 2” release, with foreign visitors increasing “by an average of 28,500 per month.” The main visitors to Milan prompted by the “Devil Wears Prada 2” effect are Americans, followed by French and British, according to the study. As for locations, the most notable rise was recorded between the city’s Largo Cairoli square and Palazzo Clerici, within Milan’s quadrilatero della moda luxury shopping district that features in the film (+24%); followed by Galleria Vittorio Emanuele-Duomo (+17%) where Miranda Priestly has a reflective late-night sequence; the Brera Academy (+14%), where Miranda organises one of the film’s most spectacular events, with strobe lights and sequins amidst the Caravaggios; However the interior of Leonardo da Vinci’s Last Supper Museum was replicated on a soundstage, since the lighting from the production would have damaged the real painting; and via Montenapoleone (+13%) the iconic street featuring the dining spot tucked away in a Renaissance courtyard where Emily (Emily Blunt) has lunch with Donatella Versace, played by the designer herself. After becoming a box office hit following its May 1, 2026 release in the United States (and April 29, 2026 in Italy), reaching $220.6 million in the U.S. and $691.4 million globally on a budget of $100 million, “Devil Wears Prada 2” reached 15.2 million views globally in its first five days of streaming since July 29 on Disney+ and Hulu, marking Disney’s biggest live-action movie premiere since “Deadpool & Wolverine.” Meta Suspends AI Image Feature After Days of Backlash Instagram Unveils ‘More Modern’ New Logo, and People Are Already Making Fun of It Meta AI Can Now Use Your Instagram Photos Without Consent. articles.title: ABC And NBC Will Air 90 NBA Games Next Season, Up 14% From The Prior Year
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade ABC And NBC Will Air 90 NBA Games Next Season, Up 14% From The Prior Year Keanu Reeves Motorcycle Racing Series ‘Hooligans’ Renewed For Season 2 On Samsung TV Plus New York Film Festival Currents Lineup To Include World Premiere Of Tala Hadid’s ‘Bardi’ View All August 13, 2026 3:32pm Karl-Anthony Towns of the New York Knicks shoots over the San Antonio Spurs' Stephon Castle during the 2026 NBA Finals. Al Bello/Getty Images ABC and NBC will combine to air 90 NBA games during the 2026-27 season, a 14% increase over the broadcast networks’ total of 79 in the prior season. The uptick will continue the squeeze on general-entertainment programming, extending a long-term shift toward live sports, unscripted fare and news and away from traditional dramas and comedies. More sports also means lower residuals for talent and other stakeholders in entertainment programming. While select games have been announced previously, the NBA revealed its full schedule for next season on Thursday. (Find it HERE .) Tip-off has been set for October 20, when NBC and Peacock will have a triple-header. Games will see the Boston Celtics facing the Detroit Pistons; the Philadelphia 76ers taking on the defending champion New York Knicks; and the Oklahoma City Thunder playing the San Antonio Spurs. Related Stories News Bob Iger's New Magic Kingdom: Fans & Media Wonder If He Can Bring That Disney Sparkle To The Lakers Executives Bob Iger Buys L.A. Lakers In Record-Setting, $12.5B Post-Disney Move Broadcast network games will be on Tuesdays, Saturdays and Sundays. Other games will be on ESPN and certain exclusives are planned on Peacock. Watch on Deadline Disney’s ABC and ESPN will carry five games on Christmas Day, with the slate highlighted by a rematch of last season’s NBA Finals between the Knicks and the Spurs. New York and San Antonio will have the most national games during the season, with 34 out of their 82 contests appearing on one of the three outlets with national rights. Amazon Prime Video joined NBCUniversal and Disney as a rightsholder when 11-year rights deals took effect in 2025. Two games for each team have not been fully scheduled, given that matchups and exact timing will be determined by the outcome of early rounds of the Emirates Cup. The in-season tournament, which was added to the calendar in 2023, streams on Prime Video. All-Star Weekend will start February 19, a few days after the Super Bowl, with ESPN and NBC/Peacock carrying portions of the weekend’s activities. articles.title: threat to leave California
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek Memoir ‘Behind The Castle Walls’ Gets Fall Release Date Neon Sets 36-Hour Screening Of ‘It Ends’ At NYC’s Metro Private Cinema With Payouts For Sticking Around American Film Market 2026 Expands With AFM House, New Indoor-Outdoor Space To Host Innovation Hub View All August 11, 2026 7:31am Story Arc The Paramount lot in Los Angeles Getty Images Paramount CEO David Ellison told a group of the company’s top executives that he will start the process of exiting California on October 1 if the state’s Attorney General Rob Bonta will not negotiate to settle an antitrust suit around the planned merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. Bonta has just responded: “In a span of weeks, Paramount agreed to halt the merger until a court decision or until June 2027, asked for a November trial, and is now back with another attempt to blackmail the state into letting an illegal deal through. Paramount has lost the plot as it continues to lose in court. It didn’t work the first time — on the eve of our July lawsuit — and it won’t work this time.” Ellison made the remarks at a meeting last week. Details were first reported by Puck and confirmed by Deadline. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Commentary Don’t Believe Paramount’s Hype: California AG Rob Bonta Claims David Ellison Muddying WBD Merger Waters With Misinformation & Side Deals; “We Intend To Win” – Guest Column News Paramount Making Deals To Theaters For 30 Films A Year Post-WBD Acquisition; Cinema United Still Anti-Merger Bonta is leading a group of 20 state Attorneys General in the case that is set to go to trial in federal court in the Northern District of California March 2027. October 1 is the day Paramount starts to accrue a so-called ticking fee of $7 million a day agreed to in the WBD deal terms if the transaction hasn’t closed by then. Paramount had asked the judge for a November trial date. Deadline hears that Ellison was emphatic at the meeting that he does not want to relocate but also doesn’t feel welcome in Paramount’s home state as the company and the AG wage a PR battle. The $111 billion merger has been approved by the DOJ and international regulatory agencies, including in the EU and UK. The AGs’ suit is focused on antitrust claims in three areas: wide release films, blockbuster films and cable network programming. Ellison has promised the combined studios will release 30 films a year with significant theatrical windows. He has said he offered to put that in writing for the AG and otherwise engage in settlement talks around potential concessions. A relocation would start with the company’s headquarters, followed by studio jobs. Ellison would move Paramount, or the merged Paramount-WBD , regardless of the outcome of a trial. Beyond the ticking fee, Paramount would owe WBD a $7 billion termination fee (the largest in corporate history) if the deal falls apart unless Warner’s board, led by CEO David Zaslav, agrees to renegotiate. WBD can walk if the deal is not clinched by June 4. Rumors had surfaced months ago that Ellison was considering a California exit if the AG did not soften his stance. Destinations mentioned have included Tennessee, Texas and Georgia. Potential new home states have presumably offered significant incentives if Paramount relocates. In response to previous threats to leave the state, Bonta has called it a “last ditch effort to try to blackmail my office and the attorneys general into allowing an illegal deal.” Paramount has accused Bonta of playing politics. In an op-ed published in Deadline on Monday, the California AG said “Paramount and Warner Bros see the writing on the wall: that they will lose in a court of law. So instead, they are resorting to the court of public opinion. They want to talk about anything but the facts of this case… As disingenuous as it may be, they are welcome to do so.” The California Film Commission on Monday announced that Paramount’s Alicia Silverstone -starring Clueless series and EGOT superstar Viola Davis ‘ corporate fixer series Ascent have been allocated nearly $38 million in Golden State tax incentives under its sweetened package to curb runaway production. In a note this morning, Richard Greenfield at Lightshed Partners wrote that “everything Paramount has done over the past several weeks appears to be inflaming the situation with California Attorney General Rob Bonta and increasing the odds this case goes to trial in March 2027. Given that the merger agreement expires on June 4, 2027, going to trial is a suicide mission that will likely lead to the merger collapsing and the Ellison family being forced to pay the $7 billion breakup fee.” Noting favorable deal commentary by Ari Emanuel, AMC Entertainment CEO Adam Aron and Regal chief Eduardo Acuna, Greenfield said, “Ellison has effectively rallied every major Hollywood ally he can find. What he has not done is offer any form of structural remedy that Bonta and the other State AGs might be willing to accept.” Rather, “Paramount’s PR campaign appears to be strengthening Bonta’s hand rather than weakening it. Bonta was already operating from a position of strength: the judge granted the temporary restraining order and appeared favorably disposed to the State AGs’ antitrust claims, set a March 2027 trial date despite Paramount’s hopes for a November 2026 trial and has shown no inclination to move at Paramount’s preferred pace given the ticking fee and the June 4 merger termination date.” The ope-ed in Deadline, Greenfield said, “makes it crystal clear that Paramount’s approach is making things worse and that the State AGs have no intention of settling this case.” Teamsters Riled Over Merger Promises, Threats; Parties Set Trial-Related Dates ‘End Of Oak Street’ Stomping To $38M-$48M Global Bow; $2M+ U.S. Previews Spidey Sequel Hits $700 Million U.S. Milestone In Record Time Emily Hampshire Among Five New Players Suiting Up For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 More from this Story Arc Paramount WB August 13, 2026 Teamsters Pound Paramount Over WBD Merger Promises & Threats: “Stop Playing Games” August 13, 2026 Parties Lay Out Key Discovery And Other Dates For Pending Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial View All Story Arc Read More About: 99 Comments

articles.title: California AG Rob Bonta Open To Structural Remedies In Paramount-WBD Suit But Calls 30 Movies A…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Former Disney CEO Bob Chapek Memoir ‘Behind The Castle Walls’ Gets Fall Release Date Neon Sets 36-Hour Screening Of ‘It Ends’ At NYC’s Metro Private Cinema With Payouts For Sticking Around American Film Market 2026 Expands With AFM House, New Indoor-Outdoor Space To Host Innovation Hub View All August 11, 2026 3:15pm Story Arc Rob Bonta Riccardo Savi/Getty Images for Concordia Annual Summit California Attorney General Rob Bonta said he’d consider structural remedies to resolve a lawsuit over the Paramount -WBD merger but dismissed “behavioral” remedies that are hard to enforce, like David Ellison ’s pledge that the combined company will release 30 movies a year. “There’s ways where the issue could be resolved with potentially structural remedies, he said at a Politico conference in Sacramento called The California Agenda. “Paramount-Warner Brothers are going to have to make business decisions for themselves.” Related Stories Commentary Don’t Believe Paramount’s Hype: California AG Rob Bonta Claims David Ellison Muddying WBD Merger Waters With Misinformation & Side Deals; “We Intend To Win” – Guest Column News David Ellison Told Top Execs Paramount Will Exit California If AG Refuses To Negotiate On WBD Deal: Rob Bonta Responds Asked if there are settlement talks on currently, he said, “I think they’re eager to enter those talks. And we are very happy with where we are. Literally, in every development in this case, we have won and they have lost. … If they, in good faith and sincerely, want to talk about settlement with us, of course we will be open to any proposals.” Bonta led a group of State Attorneys General in the antitrust suit seeking to block the deal. Set to go to court in March, the case alleges three areas where the $111-billion merger threatens competition – wide releases films, blockbuster films and cable programming. His Politico appearance follows news earlier Tuesday that Ellison plans to start moving Paramount out of California starting Oct. 1 if the AG’s office refuses to start settlement talks by then. Watch on Deadline He defined structural remedies as “keeping certain corporate entities separate … in the markets that we have challenged in our complaint. That’s what we’re interested in. We’ve heard a lot about what we call behavioral remedies … A promise to behave in a certain way in the future. A promise to make a certain amount of movies, for example, in a given year. That’s a behavioral remedy. Those are typically not enforceable in the way that we like. Not particularly good at solving the problem.” Ellison has pledged that the combined company will release 30 films a yea r. “That is an old stale promise. I’ve heard about that before. It doesn’t really vibe, in my humble opinion, with what the market will dictate and what history has shown,” the AG said. Bonta also dismissed having Paramount-WBD divest CNN as a remedy, because “the lawsuit is not political.” The Ellison camp has indicated that that it believes the suit is, in fact, political and aimed at keeping CBS News and CNN from coming together under the Ellisons. “What Mr. Ellison has posited is false. Yesterday, false. Today, false. Tomorrow, false. All day, every day … That is not what this case is about.” He said the suit has “little, if any, mention of CNN.” In an op-ed he published in Deadline Monday, Bonta accused Paramount and Warner Bros of “spearheading a public relations campaign to spin a narrative that is simply false.” “Of course, I am a person who has chosen a life in public service. I am a proud participant in our American democracy. Of course, I care about the free press and independent press. I believe that we need truth seekers and truth tellers in the press. I believe the press should not be bullied by people in power. I believe that the press should be able to hold the powerful accountable, do investigative journalism, tell stories, and inform the American public so they can make decisions for themselves,” he said. “That is a separate view that I have. That is not related to our bread and butter, meat and potatoes, black and white antitrust case.” “This is an antitrust merger to do what antitrust law does, which is make sure that prices are fair, make sure that jobs are not cut, wages aren’t reduced, make sure that there’s choice, quality, competition,” he added. “If Paramount and Warner Brothers wants to propose a settlement that involves real, robust structural remedies that address the concerns in the markets that we’ve identified in our complaint, we will listen.” Bonta declined to comment on a recent report in The Wall Street Journal that California Gov. Gavin Newsom had expressed concerns about the lawsuit and urged the AG to reach a settlement. “I like to keep my private conversations with him private,” he said. “I consider him a friend … I really value my relationship with the Governor. I’m a huge fan. I think he’s incredible. I think he’s an amazing fighter for our democracy, for our state.” Paramount’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim will be speaking at the conference later this afternoon. articles.title: Top House Judiciary Democrat Seeks Transcribed Interview With David Ellison Over Paramount-WBD…
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Parties Lay Out Key Discovery And Other Dates For Pending Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial Kennedy Center Board Votes To Return Donald Trump’s Name To Front Facade Of Complex, Again Approves Plan To Close For Two Years For Renovations Donald Trump Sued By Media Groups Over Sale Of Faster Access To Truth Social Posts View All August 12, 2026 1:49pm Story Arc Jamie Raskin Kevin Dietsch/Getty Images UPDATED: The top Democrat on the House Judiciary Committee wants Paramount CEO to sit for a transcribed interview to answer questions on its proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery. The letter from Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD) is just the latest that Democrats have sent to Ellison, as they amplify their criticisms and opposition to the transaction. In the letter, Raskin cited changes Ellison has made to CBS News and potential changes if Paramount gains control of CNN, accusing the CEO of “colluding with President Trump and his administration to curtail media independence.” The letter referred to a Wall Street Journal report from December, citing unnamed sources, that Ellison offered “assurances to Trump administration officials that if he bought Warner, he’d make sweeping changes to CNN.” Related Stories News Paramount’s Makan Delrahim Says “Everything Is On The Table” In Finding Merger Resolution, Says Leaving California Is A Consideration But Not “Blackmail” News Paramount Making Deals To Theaters For 30 Films A Year Post-WBD Acquisition; Cinema United Still Anti-Merger Later on Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal reported that Paramount has discussed creating an editorial board for CNN when the merger closes. That move would be to try to alleviate concerns over the editorial independence of the network. Watch on Deadline Ellison last week published an op ed in The New York Times defending the proposed merger and claiming that the opposition is fueled by concerns over what will happen to CNN. In his op ed , Ellison wrote that news organizations require independence, while he said that CNN and CBS News, which Paramount already owns, “are here to tell it straight down the middle.” Responding to the report of a potential editorial board for CNN, a Paramount spokesperson said in a statement, “We always remain open to internal improvements to journalistic integrity. However, as we have maintained, using state powers to try to control speech would threaten the protections guaranteed by the First Amendment.” California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading a dozen state attorneys general who are challenging the merger, has denied that CNN is the reason for the lawsuit and has said that a settlement would require structural remedies that would mitigate concerns over the merger’s impact on competition. An editorial board would be unique for a major television news network, and much would depend on the make up of its members. When Skydance sought regulatory approval to purchase Paramount last year, it committed to hiring an ombudsman to take complaints about the news division. The person hired in the role, Kenneth Weinstein, formerly led the conservative Hudson Institute. In his letter, Raskin also raised antitrust concerns, while noting the ongoing state AGs’ lawsuit. Raskin wrote in the letter , “Last week, in a New York Times op-ed, you pledged to tell your story and stay silent ‘no more.’ This is great news. Over the past 12 months, I have sent you four letters. You have responded to none of them. Now that you have vowed to break your long silence, I invite you to a transcribed interview to tell Congress and America your story and answer the Committee’s questions about your Donald Trump -enabled shopping spree to consolidate news organizations, movie studios, cable channels, and streaming services.” He gave Ellison until August 26 to schedule an interview. As the minority party, Democrats cannot compel Ellison to testify. But Raskin and others have suggested that Paramount and other mergers would be under scrutiny should the party regain control of one or more houses of Congress. At a Politico event on Tuesday, Paramount’s chief legal officer Makan Delrahim said, “You can allege all you want. There is no corruption here.” He said that they would be “happy to engage with” Raskin and “provide him, as we have, with information.” “We respect his role and his important role in oversight,” Delrahim said. “But just because he said so doesn’t mean that there’s any corruption.” CNN first reported on Raskin’s letter. The Senate Judiciary antitrust subcommittee held a hearing in February on Netflix’s plans to merge with WBD, with co-CEO Ted Sarandos appearing before lawmakers, weeks before the streamer dropped its bid amid Paramount’s counteroffer. Sen. Cory Booker (D-NJ) said that he invited Ellison to participate in that hearing, but he declined. articles.title: WGA has joined the charge
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Anna Pigeon’ Debuts To 8-Year Ratings High For USA Scripted Originals ‘Chad Powers’: Glen Powell’s Russ Holliday Struggles To Keep Up The Ruse On His College Football Playoff Run In Season 2 Trailer ‘Married At First Sight’ Audience Up 94% For Season 20 On Peacock View All July 14, 2026 12:50pm Story Arc Getty Images The Writers Guild of America has officially entered the ring in the fight to block Paramount Skydance’s pending $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery . The guild’s lawsuit , filed jointly by the WGA East and West in the Northern District of California on Tuesday, seeks to stop the merger on the grounds that it violates federal antitrust law and would cause specific harm to writers. The complaint lays out how the merger would reduce opportunities for writers as well as lead to lower pay and worse working conditions. Related Stories News California And 11 Other States Sue To Block Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery Merger Legal Paramount-WBD Merger Is Competition Killer, State Attorneys General Allege In Proposed Blockbuster Antitrust Action “With fewer competitors, the merged Paramount-Warner Bros. entity would have both the incentive and the ability to lower costs by suppressing writers’ wages and reducing output. Writers will be paid less and have fewer employment opportunities,” the WGA complaint states. Watch on Deadline This development should come as no surprise, given that the writers guild has been critical of any sale of WBD since Netflix first showed interest last year. This new lawsuit comes one day after a dozen state attorneys general sued to block the merger on Monday — a move that was swiftly praised by the WGA . The guild had been working closely with the state attorneys general offices and other federal legislators to sound the alarm on its concerns. Reached for comment by Deadline on Tuesday, a spokesperson for Paramount Skydance said in a statement: “A stronger Hollywood only means something if it’s stronger for the writers who power it. A combined Paramount-WBD will have the scale and resources to reverse the current trends in our industry and expand opportunities for writers, not shrink them: more development slates, more series and film greenlights, and our continued strong commitment to working with the guild’s writers across our brands. “Our clear incentives and pledge to release at least 30 movies a year, with full 45-day windows, continue commissioning from independent production companies, and maintain two distinct film studios reflects our commitment to preserving and boosting creative competition. Combined with our commitment to preserve our iconic brands under independent creative leadership, this will mean more jobs, more writers’ rooms, more staffed positions, and more sustained work across film and television — not less.” The statement concluded with: “As a century-old storytelling company, we have deep respect for the WGA and its members, as evidenced by our commitments in our recently renewed collective bargaining agreement, and we remain committed to building a combined company that expands opportunities for writers and creative talent for generations to come. The alternative to our transaction is a continued decline of the entertainment industry increasingly dominated by big tech companies.” The union’s legal salvo is the latest twist in the long-running saga of Paramount looking to grow much larger under CEO David Ellison. The company outdueled Netflix earlier this year , clinching the Warner Bros. Discovery deal, but the size of it (at $110 billion in debt and equity, one of the largest in corporate history) and the potential impact on the creative community have motivated a lot of opponents. Mark Ruffalo is one of several A-listers to sign a petition against the merger that now has more than 5,000 shares. Paramount has described the state AG suit as being based on a misunderstanding of antitrust case law. The company says its true competitive market includes tech giants like Amazon, Apple and Netflix, and should not be defined as just Hollywood studios. It is notable that the guild opted to file its own lawsuit, rather than join the states. This is likely because the WGA complaint focuses more directly on the labor impacts that the proposed sale will have on writing services provided by guild members. The WGA is represented in this lawsuit by Shinder Cantor Lerner LLP, Cuneo Gilbert Flannery & LaDuca, LLP, and Platkin LLP. Dade Hayes and Ted Johnson contributed to this report. articles.title: play footsie with Paramount
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine ‘Anna Pigeon’ Debuts To 8-Year Ratings High For USA Scripted Originals ‘Chad Powers’: Glen Powell’s Russ Holliday Struggles To Keep Up The Ruse On His College Football Playoff Run In Season 2 Trailer ‘Married At First Sight’ Audience Up 94% For Season 20 On Peacock View All August 12, 2026 5:33pm Story Arc Paramount Skydance-Warner Bros Discovery merger drama continues Getty Images Two of Hollywood’s most powerful unions have a message for California Attorney General Rob Bonta and Paramount Skydance CEO David Ellison : Work it out ASAP, whether in court or otherwise. The DGA and IATSE sent a joint letter to the pair on Wednesday to “raise concerns about the potential for a prolonged timetable for the litigation” and encourage them to make nice after their legal standoff over the proposed merger with Warner Bros Discovery has Ellison threatening to pull his studio out of the state completely. Related Stories News Paramount-Warner Bros Discovery: Emergency Motions, A Showdown Hearing And Next Steps In Challenge To Mega-Merger News DGA & IATSE Urge Fast Track On Paramount-WBD Merger Standoff For Fears That Prolonged Court Battle Will Hurt Jobs At the very least, the unions — which jointly represent nearly 200,000 film and television workers across the U.S. and Canada — want the antitrust case sorted out in court sooner than the current March 2027 trial date. Watch on Deadline “While we have been consistent in our view that mergers, such as this one, historically offer few benefits to workers, we are also particularly concerned about the negative impact a delay in the decision regarding the proposed merger will have on our members and the industry at large,” the letter reads. “We further believe the benefits and detriments of the proposed merger should be measured against the alternative outcomes if it is not approved, especially if the anti-competitive impacts of the proposed merger can be mitigated by a binding agreement.”

articles.title: Parties Lay Out Key Discovery And Other Dates For Pending Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Parties Lay Out Key Discovery And Other Dates For Pending Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial Kennedy Center Board Votes To Return Donald Trump’s Name To Front Facade Of Complex, Again Approves Plan To Close For Two Years For Renovations Donald Trump Sued By Media Groups Over Sale Of Faster Access To Truth Social Posts View All August 13, 2026 3:33pm Story Arc Getty Images This week has been dominated by headlines about Paramount ‘s threat to leave California , by unions and other officials urging a settlement and by Capitol Hill Democrats warning of investigations . But on Thursday, attorneys completed the rather routine step of proposing key dates and deadlines in advance of an antitrust trial over the proposed merger of Paramount with Warner Bros. Discovery . Related Stories News DGA & IATSE Urge Fast Track On Paramount-WBD Merger Standoff For Fears That Prolonged Court Battle Will Hurt Jobs News Paramount’s Makan Delrahim Says “Everything Is On The Table” In Finding Merger Resolution, Says Leaving California Is A Consideration But Not “Blackmail” A joint case management statement was filed by the plaintiffs — 12 state attorneys general and the Writers Guild of America — and the defendants, Paramount and WBD. The fact discovery is proposed to start on Aug. 17, and to close on Jan. 8, a key element of trial preparation that typically generates disputes. Watch on Deadline Last week, U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín set a trial for March 2-19, a timeline that stands to cost Paramount more than $1 billion in “ticking fees” due. As part of their deal, Paramount agreed to pay WBD $7 million for each day that the transaction doesn’t close after Sept. 30. They also face a June 4 deadline for the expiration of a deal, with Paramount on the hook for a $7 billion termination fee. Figures including Xavier Becerra, the Democratic nominee for California governor, have called for a settlement, while the Directors Guild of America and IATSE urged one with a list of proposed conditions on the transaction. Per the latest filing to the judge, the parties say they “are having constructive discussions regarding the identification of two alternative magistrate judges to preside over a settlement conference for the Actions and will provide a further update to the Court as soon as possible.” Such settlement talks also are not unusual before a trial. Among the disputed points, per the filing, are how much time each side will be given during the March proceedings. The state AGs and the WGA propose eight of the 12 trial days, noting that they are two different cases; Paramount and WBD say that time should be split equally. The judge has not said when she would make a decision after the trial, but set a deadline of April 5 for filing of proposed findings of fact and conclusions of law. The final pretrial conference would be on Feb. 24. articles.title: John Cena Made Peace With ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Never Coming Out: “I Don’t Own My Performance”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Julianne Nicholson Was “Concerned” About Reprising ‘Mare of Easttown’ Role In ‘Task’ Season 2: “Do I Know Who This Person Is?” John Cena Made Peace With ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Never Coming Out: “I Don’t Own My Performance” Drew Starkey Stays Mum On Potential ‘American Psycho’ Casting, But Teases: “The Script Is Amazing” View All August 13, 2026 3:41pm John Cena in 'Coyote vs. Acme' Ketchup Entertainment As Coyote vs. Acme finally gets its day in court, John Cena has a pretty levelheaded reaction to the once-shelved movie premiering in theaters. The Emmy nominee explained how he “can accept both the positive and the negative” of the situation after Ketchup Entertainment saved the Dave Green-helmed Looney Tunes movie, which premieres Aug. 28 in theaters, from Warner Bros. Discovery following the newly-merged company’s decision to cancel the release in 2023. “I am hired by an employer to do a task, and it’s my job to prepare as much as I can, be early, be coachable, be passionate, and be reliable. I do that and hope for the best. Those expectations are beyond my control, so it doesn’t make me view the business any differently,” he told Entertainment Weekly. “Keep in mind, it is the movie business. Sometimes, business decisions are things that we don’t see through the same lens.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories Trailers ‘Coyote Vs. Acme’ Final Trailer Gives Wile E. An Action-Packed Legal Fight Ahead Of Comic-Con Screening News ‘Coyote vs. Acme’ Review: The Movie Warner Bros Shelved In 2023 Becomes Its Most Entertaining Film Of 2026 & Best Live Action/Toon Hybrid Since ‘Roger Rabbit’ Cena continued, “Of course, I want my work seen by an audience. That’s how I can accept both the positive and the negative and get better as a performer. But I don’t own my performance. I’m contracted to do a job, and the person who owns it gets to decide what happens with it.” Ultimately, Cena rationalizes, “Even if the movie never saw the light of day, the takeaway I have is that, with the things within my control, I got to be there on the ground with people who made me better and people I care about, and I got to do the thing.” In Coyote vs. Acme , Wile E. Coyote sees an ad for attorney Kevin Avery’s (Will Forte) legal action against the Acme Corporation’s faulty products, deciding to fight back after decades of failed attempts to apprehend his nemesis, Road Runner. The movie also stars Lana Condor, Tone Bell, Martha Kelly, Luis Guzmán and countless beloved Looney Tunes characters. Written by Samy Burch from a story by her, James Gunn and Jeremy Slater, producers include Chris DeFaria and Gunn. In November 2023, Warners shelved the movie, which was based on the 1990 New Yorker article by Ian Frazier, receiving a $30 million tax write-off. The company also shelved Batgirl and Scoob! Holiday Haunt amid the company’s merger. Coyote vs. Acme eventually sold to Ketchup last year in a deal said to be in the $50 million range. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Nick Reiner Faces New Charges In Killing Of Rob Reiner & Michelle Reiner; No Death Penalty Decision Yet, D.A. Says Bob Iger Buys L.A. Lakers In Record-Setting, $12.5B Post-Disney Move Made In L.A., The Paramount Strategy: ‘Clueless’ Series & Viola Davis’ ‘Ascent’ Among Recipients In Latest California TV Tax Credit Allocations View All August 13, 2026 3:50pm Story Arc Teamsters Local 399, David Ellison Teamsters; Getty Images The DGA and IATSE may want to play footsie with Paramount over the state attorneys general antitrust lawsuit and hopes for a settlement. However, as the WGA has joined the charge against David Ellison ‘s currently stalled $111 billion purchase of Warner Bros Discovery , a very strong arm of Hollywood labor has declared it’s time to cut the crap. Related Stories News Parties Lay Out Key Discovery And Other Dates For Pending Paramount-WBD Antitrust Trial Executives Paramount’s Precipice: How David Ellison Could Salvage $111B WBD Merger (Hint – Call Kamala) “At every step of the way, Teamsters have asked for data to show how this merger would be good for our industry, our members and domestic production,” Teamster Local 399’s Lindsay Dougherty told Deadline Thursday. “Touting worker prosperity, without commitments, while simultaneously threatening their livelihood in the press as a bargaining chip begs the question — what is in this deal for American film and television workers?” Watch on Deadline With Paramount leaks threatening to leave California if Golden State AG Rob Bonta and others don’t strike a deal by October 1 clearly in mind, the plain-speaking Dougherty added: “Fast-tracking corporate greed often lends to the creative and skilled workforce losing. Stop playing games, and show us more of your commitment to the workforce.”

articles.title: ‘DTF St. Louis’ Creator Steve Conrad On Tapping Into The Exotica & Underbelly Of The Midwest – Crew Call Podcast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘The End Of Oak Street’ Stomping To $38M-$48M Global Opening; U.S. Previews At $2M+ – Thursday PM Box Office ‘DTF St. Louis’ Creator Steve Conrad On Tapping Into The Exotica & Underbelly Of The Midwest – Crew Call Podcast ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Fastest Movie To Cross $700M At U.S. Box Office View All August 13, 2026 4:30pm L-R: Steve Conrad, Jason Bateman and David Harbour at HBO's 'DTF St. Louis' FYC event in May Phillip Faraone/Getty Images for HBO There’s a 1970s movie sensibility in Steve Conrad ‘s HBO limited series DTF St. Louis , which tells the story of a bromance between two co-workers, a River City TV weatherman played by Jason Bateman and his hearing-impaired interpreter played by David Harbour. The former gets the latter into a kinky dating app. In between them is a love triangle involving Carol, played by Linda Cardellini, the wife of Harbour’s Floyd. The outcome, a weird murder. Or is it suicide? Related Stories News Linda Cardellini On Emmys And ‘DTF St. Louis’, Those Sex Scenes, Playing Jason Voorhees’ Mom And Making Bill Hader’s New Movie – The Actor’s Side News Take Ten: David Harbour Talks ‘DTF St. Louis’, Reuniting With Millie Bobby Brown, Upcoming Film ‘John Rambo’ & The ‘Stranger Things’ Prop He Kept Mike Nichols’ Carnal Knowledge comes to mind when watching DTF St. Louis , but for Conrad it’s more Dog Day Afternoon. On today’s episode of Deadline’s Crew Call podcast, the screenwriter-director tells us about mining melodrama in the Midwest going back to such movies as the 2005 title he wrote, The Weather Man starring Nicolas Cage. “I like the juxtaposition of the electricity when you hear ‘DTF’ — how exotic those three letters sound,” he says. “Then followed by ‘Saint Louis,’ which isn’t always that exciting to hear.” Watch on Deadline “It feels normal. And obviously one of our themes is that nobody’s normal; it just looks that way from across the street. So I thought I would pick a place that people mistakenly think is a little more ordinary than other places, and it is a mistake… there’s freaks galore in the Midwest,” he adds. Some of Conrad’s friends had their lives go a bit sideways with dating apps. It was that inspiration that made him “flirt with the idea that there can be intimacy without consequences. Whatever that promise is ultimately from dating apps that say you can come and experience intimacy and then go back to your normal life, I was skeptical that could be true entirely,” he says. The limited series scored 13 Emmy nominations including for Outstanding Limited or Anthology Series, Harbour and Bateman in Supporting Actor Limited or Anthology Series, Cardellini for Supporting Actress, and Conrad up for writing and directing. Conrad submitted the series finale for Emmy consideration. articles.title: Tyler Duckworth Dies: MTV’s ‘The Challenge’ Alum Was 44
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Tyler Duckworth Dies: MTV’s ‘The Challenge’ Alum Was 44 ‘Task’ Adds Stephanie Sigman, Alaíde, Rocío Guzmán & Regina Nava To Season 2 Cast Stephan James & Colton Ryan Join Nicole Kidman, Elle Fanning & Josh Lucas In Paramount+ Legal Drama ‘Discretion’ As Production Begins View All August 13, 2026 4:45pm Tyler Duckworth MTV Reality TV star Tyler Duckworth , who first appeared on MTV ’s The Real World: Key West and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge , winning twice, has died. He was 44. His mother, Joni, announced her son’s death Thursday on Facebook. “My son, Tyler, passed away earlier this week,” she wrote. “Cause of death has yet to be determined. I will post on Facebook about services as soon as his dad and I figure it out.” Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Cristina Sanz Dies: ‘Born This Way’ Reality Star Was 36 The Sun, which first reported his death , revealed Duckworth was found unresponsive in his bathroom on Tuesday. The publication cited officials in North Dakota as saying the death was classified as unattended, meaning there were no witnesses there at the time. His death came nearly two weeks after he appeared at The Challenge Mania event on July 31 in Minneapolis. He posted a photo of himself alongside fellow Challenge alums on Instagram on August 2. “ @challengemaniapodcast always knows how to bring the BEST of the BEST together!!, he wrote. “So proud to represent my hometown of Minneapolis along with these other challenge legends. The fans are what keep us coming out! Hearing your stories of courage, inspiration & joy that you’ve got being a fan of the franchise is humbling each and every time. Also, pretty sure we nailed the cast photo for the lost season of The Real World: Minneapolis!! Thank you Minneapolis!” Born March 5, 1981, in Atlanta, GA, he grew up in Minneapolis. He appeared on The Real World: Key West in 2006 and went on to compete on six seasons of The Challenge – The Duel , The Gauntlet III , Cutthroat, Rivals , All Stars 2 and All Stars 3 — winning Cutthroat and Rivals. On Cutthroat , he won a bruising, 40-minute elimination round against heavy hitter CT Tamburello after Johnny “Bananas” Devenanzio was eliminated in what has been remember as the “Bananas Backpack” match. After 10 years, he returned to the franchise for All Stars 2. After his run on reality TV. Duckworth became a middle school and high school teacher and was actively pursuing a doctorate degree, according to an interview with Entertainment Weekly . articles.title: ‘Just One Day’ YA Drama Starring Kathryn Newton Moves To Hulu For Development
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Just One Day’ YA Drama Starring Kathryn Newton Moves To Hulu For Development Emilia Jones To Lead The Cast Of Netflix Series ‘The Retrievals’ From Molly Smith Metzler ‘Off Campus’ Casts Shay Rudolph As Dean Di Laurentis’ Sister Summer In Season 2 View All August 13, 2026 4:47pm Kathryn Newton; Jennifer Levin and Sherri Cooper (inset) John Eisendrath / Sherri Cooper / Austin Hargrave EXCLUSIVE : Hulu is developing Just One Day , a series starring Kathryn Newton ( The Devil’s Mouth, Big Little Lies ) based on the Gayle Forman YA romance novels. Patrick Moran executive produces the project, which was originally set up at Amazon under his company PKM Productions’ first-look deal there, with Beauty & the Beast co-creators Sherri Cooper and Jennifer Levin writing the adaptation. That iteration ultimately did not move forward; the concept is now undergoing redevelopment at Hulu with the same writers. Cooper, Levin, Forman and Anna Mastro also executive produce. 20th Television is the studio, marking a homecoming for Moran who once ran its predecessor ABC Studios. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Chad Powers': Glen Powell's Russ Holliday Struggles To Keep Up The Ruse On His College Football Playoff Run In Season 2 Trailer Casting 'Only Murders In The Building' Expands Its Collection Of 'Doctor Who' Stars, Adds Peter Capaldi To Season 6 Cast The Just One Day series spans two books and a followup novella. It centers on Allyson Healey (Newton) whose life is exactly like her suitcase — packed, planned, ordered. Then on the last day of her three-week post-graduation European tour, she meets Willem. A free-spirited, roving actor, Willem is everything she’s not, and when he invites her to abandon her plans and come to Paris with him, Allyson says yes. This uncharacteristic decision leads to a day of risk and romance, liberation and intimacy: 24 hours that will transform Allyson’s life. The first novel, Just One Day, released in August 2013, tells the story from Allyson’s point of view, while Just One Year , published in September 2014, is told from Willem’s POV. The books has been sold into 19 territories and sold almost 1 million copies. YA remains a priority area for Hulu, which continues to develop projects after recently passing on two pilots, including Foster Dade . Newton already is in business with Hulu and 20th TV: she is in their pilot Durango. She currently stars in the Prime Video movie The Devil’s Mouth and recently starred in Ready Or Not 2: Here I Come . Newton, whose upcoming movies also include White Elephant, Somo Lives and Hot Year, is repped by WME, Entertainment 360 and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller, Hoberman. Veteran TV writer-producers Cooper and Levin, who co-created and executive produced the CW’s Beauty and the Beast and worked on Brothers & Sisters, Felicity and Everwood , among other series, are repped by Verve, Mosaic, and McKuin Frankel Whitehead. The film & TV rights for Forman are repped by Katherine Curtis of New Leaf Literary & Media. And spirit is what the night was all about. Kevin Costner provided the narration for an intro to tonight’s Field of Dreams game on Netflix . It’s the third edition of the Hollywood- MLB mashup played on a field near the Iowa farmhouse where the 1989 classic was filmed. And while it wasn’t quite the same as watching Costner walk out of the corn at the 2021 edition, tonight’s video still delivered chills. The original film was more about the connections baseball builds in families, particularly between fathers and sons, and Costner was a key to the emotional and evocative feeling connecting all in attendance and watching on TV. Those stories are important, he said, “to remind us what baseball can make us feel, how deeply it can bring us bring us together and why it’s still worth believing in.” Watch on Deadline You can watch below. The project, written and executive produced by Percy Jackson and the Olympians executive producers/showrunners Jonathan E. Steinberg and Dan Shotz , was set up for development at the Disney streamer about a year and a half ago with sibling 20th Television as the studio. It will not be going past the development stage. According to sources, the reasons for the pass are not so much creative than they are business- (aka budget-) related. Mounting a high-end, live-action superhero series of the caliber of Power Rangers is a major investment, the economics of which are not as favorable when the streamer and/or the producing studio do not own the IP, which is the case here. The Power Rangers brand is owned by Hasbro, which has been looking to get a live-action series adaptation off the ground, with Netflix taking a crack at it several years ago. Once focused entirely on exploiting Disney properties, Disney+ has been increasingly opening up its slate to outside IP, including making development deals for Ella Enchanted and Casper series over the past couple of months. Watch on Deadline Steinberg and Shotz are busy finishing Season 3 of the 20th Television-produced hit Disney+ series Percy Jackson and the Olympians , which premieres on Nov. 20, and developing other projects for the studio under their overall deal there. articles.title: ‘Black Mirror’ Director Ally Pankiw Roasts ‘Harry Potter’ TV Series, Claiming She Turned Down Gig: “Say No To Funding Transphobia”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Top Canadian Screen Bodies & Festivals Urge Government To Stay Strong On Global Streamer Contributions The Harrigans Spiral Out Of Control In ‘MobLand’ Season 2 Trailer Disney+ Signs Content Deal With Gary Neville’s The Overlap To Strike Back Against Netflix’s Football Podcast Play View All August 14, 2026 2:02am Ally Pankiw at a Deadline event and 'Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone' TV series Deadline/Getty, HBO Ally Pankiw certainly won’t be working on HBO ‘s upcoming Harry Potter series. The Black Mirror director shared an Instagram post that appears to show an SMS exchange with her agent in which she emphatically turns down an opportunity to board the series. “I have an instinct on the answer but I feel compelled to ask,” writes the agent. “ Harry Potter ? Hard no?” Pankiw responds, “Absolutely fucking not! lol… (But thank you for asking)”, before the agent writes, “Of course :)… I assumed as much… (And agree).” Related Stories News Julianne Nicholson Was "Concerned" About Reprising 'Mare of Easttown' Role In 'Task' Season 2: "Do I Know Who This Person Is?" News 'House Of The Dragon' Season 3 & 'Life, Larry & The Pursuit Of Unhappiness' Finish As Top Performers For HBO Max The Canadian director, who also has credits for the likes of The Great , shared the post with the caption, “It is simply this easy to say no to funding transphobia,” and added the opportunity was “for directing, not acting… obviously lol”. Watch on Deadline Pankiw’s post drew support from the likes of actor and comedian Vic Michaelis , Welcome to Flatch and Big Mistakes actress Taylor Ortega and Loki , Doctor Who and Sex Education director Kate Herron . The latter wrote in the comments, “They’ve asked me twice and I’ve had to explain my answer is never going to change from a no.” We’ve reached out to HBO for confirmation Pankiw was on its list of directors. Pankiw’s post is a reminder of how the series, Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone , has become toxic in many quarters well before its December launch. This is down to Harry Potter writer and creator J.K. Rowling’s long-held views towards trans people, which have created distance between her and the movie franchise’s stars Daniel Radcliffe, Emma Watson and Rupert Grint. Even the likes of the upcoming series stars Nick Frost, John Lithgow, Paapa Essiedu and Bel Powley have openly disagreed with Rowling. They now face regular online criticism for joining the show. While Rowling has occasionally fought back against those who dub her transphobic – even at one point tweeting, “I respect every trans person’s right to live any way that feels authentic and comfortable to them” – she regularly shares anti-trans posts, antagonizes openly trans people and has celebrated a UK high court ruling that women are defined by biological sex. The Harry Potter series is based on Rowling’s blockbuster books. She is an executive producer alongside Neil Blair, Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV and David Heyman of Heyday Films. Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone , titled the same as the first movie, will debut Christmas Day on HBO and will be available to stream exclusively on HBO Max globally. articles.title: A Movie Theater Didn’t Get Sent ‘Spider-Man’ Posters, So an Employee Drew His Own
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 12, 2026 3:54pm The viral Canadian 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' poster, and the movie's official movie poster. Drake Landon; Columbia Pictures Logo text The promotional materials for Spider-Man : Brand New Day look a bit different in one theater in Canada, and the internet is loving it. A Famous Players theater in Prince George, British Columbia almost certainly has the most unique movie poster for the record-breaking film led by Tom Holland. It features a hand-drawn illustration by employee Drake Landon that was inspired by the Spooder-Man meme , with the title of the movie written in font strikingly similar to the script in the official promotional materials. The movie theater did not receive the official movie poster in time for its release, which led to Landon creating an original drawing to be put in its place in the cinema. That was explained in his now-viral illustration, as a note on the poster reads, “Sorry! We never recieved the real posters! Sorry for any inconviniences!” (Yes, with those exact spelling errors and all, adding to the amusement surrounding the sketch.) Related Stories Movies Frank Miller Talks Arguing with Jim Shooter, Why His Doctor Strange Series Never Happened and 'Sin City' Future Business Cineplex CEO Says Gen Z Is Ready to Go to the Movies: "They're Tired of Looking at Small Screens" Pictures of the poster have gained widespread attention online, with one Reddit post receiving upwards of 51,000 upvotes. Landon tells The Hollywood Reporter the reaction to his Spider-Man poster has been “very unexpected,” and he’s “kinda still not realizing how big it is.” ‘ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ‘ illustration by Drake Landon. Drake Landon Landon adds, “It’s crazy that my art has gone that far for something so simple.” He also confirms that “the inspiration for it was the ‘Spooder-man’ meme that was popular around in the 2010s.” Michelle Saba, vp of communications for Cineplex , owner of Famous Players, also commended the poster in a statement shared with THR . “Our team did have a little fun as they awaited the arrival of their Spider-Man: Brand New Day poster,” she said. It’s no secret that Spider-Man: Brand New Day has been a smash hit — at the box office , and with viewers. The film triumphed over many records originally set by Avengers: Endgame , including by earning the highest-grossing first week in domestic box office history and becoming the fastest title to reach $500 million domestic. Brand New Day hit that milestone in its first seven days; Endgame hit the threshold in eight days. The movie also earned the best-ever domestic box office sums for a Monday and a Tuesday ; is the second-fastest film to achieve $1 billion globally ; and scored the third-best second weekend ever at the box office. Spider-Man related content is hotter than ever, and Famous Players’ viral hand-drawn poster for the film is another piece of media that has proved just that. A Facebook post made by a moviegoer who attended the Canadian theater also shared a photo of the artist, Landon, posing by his now-viral masterpiece. “My son Rogan and I stopped to appreciate this hand drawn movie poster at the theatre today and thought it was awesome. Then we got a chance to meet the artist, Drake. So my son decided to take a picture of the artist with his art work and we thought we should share it for everyone to check out,” wrote Adam Woodrow. “Keep it up Drake!” Cineplex CEO Ellis Jacob commended Gen Z for driving the recent success at the box office in a recent interview with THR . “The big change is Gen Z are coming back to the movies in a big way, and that’s making a difference,” he said. “They’re tired of looking at the small screen. They’re going out on a social basis and having a good time and that to me is very positive.” THR

articles.title: ‘Wizards of Waverly Place’ Actress Jennifer Stone, Who Now Works as a Nurse, Says She Auditioned for ‘The Pitt’

And I remember, because at the end of the pilot episode, the Noah Wyle character, he’s having COVID flashbacks,” she said. “And as I often do, I was reading the script and working on lines while we were waiting for a patient to get admitted, kind of in those brief little pockets of time that you have, so I was working on the lines and reading the script at work.” Related Stories Business Noah Wyle Departs Verve After Two Years TV Jake T. Austin Says He Wasn't Invited to Partake in 'Wizards of Waverly Place' Revival: "Disappointed" Stone began working as an emergency room nurse in 2022; she also began a separate role as a disaster relief registered nurse in 2023, according to her LinkedIn .
