articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten , Jill Goldsmith , Tom Tapp August 12, 2026 7:55am Bob Iger Getty UPDATED with Magic Johnson comments: Fulfilling a long-held dream, Bob Iger has bought himself a big-city major sports franchise. The ex- Disney CEO and Thrive Capital boss Josh Kushner have scored the Los Angeles Lakers at a valuation of $12.5 billion, Deadline has confirmed. That’s the highest valuation for a sports team in U.S. history, topping the record set when current owner owner Mark Walter bought the team just over one year ago. They will be buying out Walter’s 80% stake in the team. Related Stories Sports LeBron James Signs With Philadelphia 76ers As “Last Decision”: “I Am So Excited To Energize A New Fan Base” Sports Donald Trump Says LeBron James Is “Maybe A Racist” After 76ers Move & Prefers Michael Jordan: “I Only Like People Who Like Me” “As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world,” Iger and Kushner said in a statement Wednesday. “We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of Jerry and Jeanie Buss. Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans and the city of Los Angeles.” Of interest to longtime fans is the fate of Jeanie Buss, who under and agreement with Walter is serving as the team’s governor in league meetings. Watch on Deadline “We have enormous respect and appreciation for Jeanie, her father and what they’ve contributed to this franchise,” Iger told The California Post . “And we have every intention to honor the agreement that was made between Mark and Jeanie. If things change, they’ll change, but we’re going into this with enormous respect and appreciation for who she is and what she represents in the organization.” Even as the deal needs to get formal thumbs-up from the NBA Board of Governors, Iger and Kushner got the stamp of approval from Lakers legend Magic Johnson ASAP. “Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners,” Johnson posted online this morning. “I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years — he has always loved the Lakers and basketball, and he will bring championships back to LA” I want to congratulate my good friend Bob Iger and Josh Kushner on their purchase of the Los Angeles Lakers! — Earvin Magic Johnson (@MagicJohnson) August 12, 2026 Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners. I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years – he has always loved the Lakers and basketball and he will bring championships back to LA. — Earvin Magic Johnson (@MagicJohnson) August 12, 2026 The team’s current superstar, Luka Doncic, who was traded to the Lakers in a deal that blindsided not just the league, but Doncic as well, said in part, “I’ve gotten used to big changes over these last few years, but I know that no matter what, there is no limit to the potential of this iconic franchise. I look forward to meeting Josh and Bob so we can get to work building something special in LA together.” Lakers minority owner and current governor Jeanie Buss retweeted Doncic and wrote, “Perfectly said,” alongside gold and purple hear emojis. Perfectly said 💛💜 https://t.co/f7GL4tbG8n — Jeanie Buss (@JeanieBuss) August 12, 2026 After two stints as Disney boss, Iger exited the CEO seat in March. He rejoined Thrive as an adviser in April, setting the table for today’s big news. It has been a true whirlwind for the 17-time NBA champion Lakers the past year — and we’re not just talking about LeBron James leaving and joining the 76ers . There was the Doncic deal, the sale of the team to Walter last year and now this. And “this” came together in just three days. Los Angeles Lakers players Jake LaRavia, left, and Luka Doncic in 2025 Iger has talked for years about owning a major sports franchise. He and Kushner had been part of a group exploring an NBA expansion franchise in Las Vegas. Iger told the Post in an interview today, “We were involved in pursuing the new franchise in Vegas. And while that happened, it was suggested to us that maybe Mark Walter would be interested in selling his stake in the Lakers. And we immediately decided that given the value of the franchise and the iconic nature of the team, that we would be really smart to pursue it. The deal came together in three days.” Angel City FC stakeholder Iger and Kushner, the once-FIFA-touted financial player (and Donald Trump family member by marriage), take a controlling interest in the one-time home of Magic, Shaq and Kobe from Mark Walter about a year after the Guggenheim Partners CEO bought the Lakers from the Buss family at a valuation of $10 billion . While Walter got close to 80% of the franchise, the the Buss family trust retained a 15% interest. According to The Athletic , Kushner owns a minority stake in the Miami Heat, which he will likely have to divest. League rules specify that no one can own interest in more than one team. Given the soaring cost of franchises, NBA owners in 2024 voted to allow private equity groups to buy minority stakes in multiple teams, but not a controlling interest. Kushner also once owned a minority strake in the Memphis Grizzlies. He started Thrive Capital in 2009 with backing from Peter Thiel, according to The Athletic. Iger came on as a minority investor in 2022. Earlier this year, Thrive Capital launched a holding company called Thrive Eternal, whose investments, said Kushner, would be in “iconic franchises and cultural institutions rooted in tradition, identity, and shared experience.” The holding company is, according to The Athletic , the vehicle by which Kushner and Iger intend to buy the Lakers. Thrive Eternal was one of the investors in the controversial recent plan by FIFA president Gianni Infantino to create a $20 billion commercial arm of soccer’s world governing body by selling stakes in the World Cup and other events. That plan was scuttled after widespread outcry in the soccer world and beyond.

articles.title: Jeremy Strong Emailed Mark Zuckerberg To Assure Him He Takes ‘The Social Reckoning’ Role “Very Seriously”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Jeremy Strong Emailed Mark Zuckerberg To Assure Him He Takes ‘The Social Reckoning’ Role “Very Seriously” Andy Cohen Calls Out Paul W. Downs Over ‘Hacks’ Joke At His Expense Alia Shawkat Is “Trying Actively” To Bring ‘State of Grace’ To Streaming, Plan Reunion With Mae Whitman View All August 12, 2026 6:18pm Jeremy Strong reached out to Mark Zuckerberg about playing him in 'The Social Reckoning'. Sony Pictures Entertainment/Wally Skalij/Getty Images While giving his all to his The Social Reckoning portrayal of Mark Zuckerberg , Jeremy Strong reached out to the Meta CEO and Facebook co-founder. The Oscar nominee recently revealed that he emailed Zuckerberg to assure him he takes the “responsibility very seriously,” noting that the tech mogul responded. Strong would not reveal the details of Zuckerberg’s email. “I wrote to him—I’m probably going to give Sony an aneurysm—I sent him an email,” Strong told GQ . “Just to say that I take this responsibility very seriously, and the veracity of it seriously, and I’m approaching it with respect.” Related Stories News ‘The Social Reckoning’ Trailer: Aaron Sorkin Returns To The World Of Facebook News Jesse Eisenberg Turned Down ‘The Social Reckoning’, Aaron Sorkin Says He Was Tired Of Being “Conflated” With Mark Zuckerberg After The Social Network (2010) recounted Zuckerberg’s creation of Facebook and the controversy that ensued, screenwriter Aaron Sorkin returned to write and direct the upcoming sequel, which premieres Oct. 9, focusing on a 2021 document leak that exposed harm Facebook caused on society. Watch on Deadline Noting that “it’s crazy to take this on at all,” Strong explained of the role, “Listen, I know that he is a reviled person and not a popular person in our culture, but I do not think you should have an actor playing him who wants to set out to condemn him.” Jeremy Strong as Mark Zuckerberg in ‘The Social Reckoning’ “It feels incredibly fraught to talk about the movie, to talk about Mark and being the person who is playing Mark and representing Mark in a sense to the world and to posterity; I feel an enormous sense of weight and responsibility,” added Strong. “And listen, my job is to understand and defend his point of view and fight his fight.” In The Social Reckoning , Facebook engineer Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison) goes to Wall Street Journal reporter Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White) with the social media platform’s most guarded secrets. Bill Burr, Wunmi Mosaku, Billy Magnussen and Betty Gilpin also star. articles.title: Bob Iger’s New Magic Kingdom: Fans & Media Wonder If He Can Bring That Disney Sparkle To The Lakers
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Bob Iger’s New Magic Kingdom: Fans & Media Wonder If He Can Bring That Disney Sparkle To The Lakers Lionsgate Stock Falls To 4-Month Low After Activist Investor Pushes AI Agenda Alex Cooper’s Unwell Media Company Valued At $500M After Investment By Patrick Whitesell’s Firm View All August 12, 2026 6:47pm Bob Iger, former Disney CEO and now one of the principal owners of the Los Angeles Lakers Jordan Teller/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images As the new co-owner of the Los Angeles Lakers , Bob Iger brings with him arguably the most significant Hollywood profile of any owner in the history of U.S. major professional sports. The question fans and Angelenos have now is: What kind of Disney magic can he make? Related Stories Executives Bob Iger Buys L.A. Lakers In Record-Setting, $12.5B Post-Disney Move Sports LeBron James Signs With Philadelphia 76ers As “Last Decision”: “I Am So Excited To Energize A New Fan Base” Iger and Josh Kushner unveiled the stunning deal Wednesday morning, saying they pivoted from pursuing an expansion franchise based in Las Vegas to buying the majority stake held by Mark Walter. The whole Lakers negotiation from start to finish took, according to Iger, just 72 hours. In 2025, Walter ended Buss the family’s 46-year dominion over the team by taking control in a deal valuing the Lakers at around $10 billion. It was a new record in U.S. pro sports. A little more than a year later, Iger and Kushner have bought in at a valuation of $12.5 billion, a new record. More than a few eyebrows have been raised about Walter’s entrance and exit from the Lakers given the fact that the billionaire’s corporate empire is currently the subject of a federal investigation. Bill Simmons, founder of The Ringer, a longtime Lakers hater and the head of talk at Spotify, wrote in an X post that “Conspiracy Bill is overheating” after “the most shocking NBA sale in a long time. The Lakers got flipped!” Watch on Deadline A number of fans were stunned by the timing, noting that Walter had steered the Dodgers to two straight titles and seemed a viable longtime owner after the long reign of the Buss family. The Buss family became NBA royalty by presiding over both the “Showtime” run of titles in the 1970s and ’80s with Magic Johnson and Kareem Abdul-Jabaar, and the 2000s-2010s juggernauts featuring Kobe Bryant and Shaquille O’Neal. The Buss family shepherded the franchise capably for decades, but infighting had led to disarray in the front office. The league had also changed. While the Busses were wealthy by nearly any measure, they weren’t rich like the league’s new wave of owners. When Walter came in, Lakers fans were excited to have their very own billionaire in charge. Fans hoped for some facsimile of what Walter has done across town with the Dodgers. The team over in Chavez Ravine has the second-highest payroll in baseball, has invested heavily in beefing up the front office and has won three MLB championships since Walter became majority owner in 2012. And Walter has been investing in the Lakers. In February, he made his most significant change, bringing over the Dodgers’ longtime executive vice president and chief marketing officer, Lon Rosen, as the Lakers’ president of business operations. The franchise’s G-league (or developmental) team was relocated. There were initiatives to bolster the squad’s assistant general manager ranks and its sports science resources. The team also let a number of longtime staffers go last spring. Now, with Walter gone, it is unclear what the team’s direction will be going forward. “We’re not in Kansas anymore,” said Pete Zayas, co-host of the Laker Film Room podcast, after today’s news was announced. “We don’t have the family that had been running it for 40 years. We’re in some different waters for sure.” “Still Sinking In” In an interview with the California Post , Iger didn’t address speculation about what might have motivated the Walter sale. He said the deal “came together in three days,” a remarkably swift timeline. Former majority owner Jeanie Buss, who had agreed with Walter to remain for five years as the team’s governor, is expected to continue for now in that role, Iger said. “We have enormous respect and appreciation for Jeanie, her father and what they’ve contributed to this franchise,” Iger said. The former Disney mogul said the news is “still sinking in” and his role is “very new.” In terms of future plans, he said, “We’re smart enough to know what we know and what we don’t know. It’s just premature to speculate at all about what we plan to do, because frankly, we haven’t made any plans yet. Again, we go into this with an appreciation of who the Lakers are. And we just want to build value from today on.” Iger came on as a minority investor in Kushner’s Thrive Capital in 2022. Earlier this year, Thrive Capital launched a holding company called Thrive Eternal whose investments, said Kushner, would be in “iconic franchises and cultural institutions rooted in tradition, identity, and shared experience” that would could not be easily replaced by digital innovations, but could enhanced by them. That holding company is, according to The Athletic , the vehicle by which Kushner and Iger intend to buy the Lakers. Iger approaches the team’s new era from a fan’s perspective. He has been known for his passion for the NBA and close relationships with prominent players like Chris Paul. In L.A., he is taking over just after the high-profile departure of LeBron James, who headed to Philadelphia in a free-agent deal earlier this summer. That leaves Luka Doncic and Austin Reeves as the team’s primary stars, with a number of questions about the rest of the roster. The Lakers have won 17 total championships. James helped lead them to the one-of-a-kind Covid bubble title in 2020, but their last non-pandemic crown came in 2010. Apart from 2020, their best recent showing in the playoffs has been a Western Conference Finals appearance in 2023 in which they were swept by the Denver Nuggets. Off the court, the team is still one of the league’s most potent money-makers, but there’s plenty of potential to improve the business. According to a recent ranking compiled by Deadline sister publication Sportico , the team’s 2025 revenue was well behind that of the No. 1 NBA franchise, the Golden State Warriors at $833 million. L.A. was also elbowed out by the New York Knicks, which took in $620 million. Crypto.com Arena, the awkwardly-named venue in downtown L.A. once known as Staples Center, is one area where Iger could put his Disney magic to good use. The arena opened in 1999, at a time when downtown was seeing a massive influx in development spending. Today, DTLA’s mojo has ebbed. The NBA’s L.A. Clippers, longtime former tenants at Staples/Crypto.com, opened their own beyond state-of-the-art venue in Inglewood, CA, the Intuit Dome , in 2024. The result? According to Sportico , “The Clippers took the biggest financial leap in 2024-25 in Year 1 of the Intuit Dome at just over $100 million in sponsor revenue, good for second in the NBA.” Iger made his reputation during his time at Disney in part by acquiring Marvel, Fox, Pixar and Lucasfilm, but also by presiding over a successful expansion of the company’s theme park empire. As even Disney super-fans might wincingly acknowledge, he became a master of extracting revenue from the parks . From opening branded areas like Galaxy’s Edge and Avengers Campus to venturing to China with Shanghai Disney to introducing dynamic pricing, Iger proved adept in overseeing experiential businesses. A number of major sports teams, especially in the NBA, have shown that kind of savvy. Surely, a number of moves by the Warriors, from their Rakuten jersey sponsorship to their “Thrive City” mixed-use area around the San Francisco arena they own, have caught Iger’s eye. Rethinking Local Media Then there’s the local media footprint, a key complement to the national NBA rights deals that took effect in 2025. Last year, the Lakers received a hefty $200 million payment from Charter’s Spectrum SportsNet, the regional sports network whose 20-year deal for team rights runs through the 2031-32 season. While the deal is the league’s richest, Walter, according a report last year in Puck, has “shown openness to taking ownership of Spectrum SportsNet away from Charter.” The upside for the cable company is getting the unattractive financials of the RSN off its books. For the former Lakers owner, the appeal was to be able to potentially rework the team’s media plan to take more of an ownership role, as Major League Baseball’s New York Yankees and others do. Iger, as the former overseer of ESPN and the architect of the latter’s recent swap of 10% of its equity for control of NFL media properties like the NFL network, seems to be pretty ideal casting for an owner looking to reinvent TV and streaming. As the RSN model continues to erode, the NBA is among the leagues overhauling its media plan. It is aiming to launch a hub for local rights by the 2027-28 season. ESPN Chairman Jimmy Pitaro, Iger’s former direct report, said at a CNBC conference in June that there is “a local RSN problem that the entire industry is grappling with right now.” The ESPN app, which relaunched in dramatically expanded form a year ago, has been onboarding non-ESPN sports programming like CW game coverage. As leagues grapple with the RSN issue, Pitaro said, “they should be looking for reach, which we can provide.” When Iger returned to the Disney CEO role in 2023 for his second stint, which ended earlier this year when he passed the baton to Josh D’Amaro, his flair for showmanship, on top of his business acumen, was mentioned by many inside the company. That begs the obvious question of how the experience of attending a Laker game might change in the Iger era. Whether they find a new home or remodel the faded Crypto.com, the team has plenty of ways to improve the experience. That said, Laker games have already been an industry staple, with celebrities like Leonardo DiCaprio, Kim Kardashian and Selena Gomez rubbing elbows courtside with industry heavyweights like Jeffrey Katzenberg. As visions of even loftier, star-packed gatherings take flight, some fans haven’t been able to look past the inherent confusion of having one of the most prominent teams in sports change hands twice in 14 months. “How deep are their pockets?” wondered Laker Film Room co-host Darius Soriano. “They just paid an extraordinary amount of money for this franchise, and putting so much money on the table can be tricky. Are you going to follow through on that investment?” Tom Tapp contributed to this report. articles.title: Zurich Film Festival: Peter Farrelly’s ‘I Play Rocky’ & Channing Tatum Starrer ‘Josephine’ Among Gala Titles
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Diana Lodderhose Diana Lodderhose International Features Editor @dianalodderhose More Stories By Diana Zurich Film Festival: Peter Farrelly’s ‘I Play Rocky’ & Channing Tatum Starrer ‘Josephine’ Among Gala Titles Sarajevo Film Festival Director Jovan Marjanović Talks “Vibrant” Lineup, Uptick In Female Directors & Developing Long-Term, “Meaningful” Relationships With Filmmakers Keke Palmer, Jeremy Irons & Jacob Tremblay Projects Heading To TIFF Financing Market View All August 12, 2026 9:00pm Anthony Ippolito as a young Sylvester Stallone in 'I Play Rocky' Amazon MGM The Zurich Film Festival has announced its first selection of gala titles for this year’s edition, which runs September 9 to October 10. Films include the European premiere of Peter Farrelly’s I Play Rocky , starring Anthony Ippolito as Sylvester Stallone, Matt Dillon, Stephan James and more as well as Channing Tatum and Gemma Chan starrer Josephine from director Beth de Araújo. I Play Rocky follows unknown actor Stallone, who is writing a screenplay title Rocky that a studio is desperate to acquire. But Stallone refuses to sell the rights – unless he gets to play the lead himself. Despite numerous setbacks and rejections he remains determined to make his dream a reality: playing Rocky Balboa. Related Stories Trailers 'Josephine' Trailer: Gemma Chan & Channing Tatum's 8-Year-Old Witnesses A Terrible Crime; Sundance Double Winner Gets Release Date Agencies 'I Play Rocky' Star Anthony Ippolito Lands At CAA Josephine follows 8-year old Josephine who witnesses a violent crime and her world is out of joint as she tries to find a way to regain a sense of security. Her emphatic mother (Chan) wants to help her process what happened while her father (Tatum) believes in preparing her for the harsher realities of life, but increasingly finds himself overwhelmed with by the situation. Watch on Deadline Further titles include Olivia Colman comedy Wicker and German productions Love, After All by Andreas Dresen and How Can I Help from Doris Dörrie, both of which will world premiere in Zurich. Here’s the full list: I PLAY ROCKY European Premiere Biography USA, 2026 Director : Peter Farrelly Cast : Anthony Ippolito, Matt Dillon, Stephan James, AnnaSophia Robb, PJ Byrne, Toby Kebbell, Tracy Letts, Jay Duplass JOSEPHINE Drama USA, 2026 Director : Beth de Araújo Cast : Channing Tatum, Gemma Chan, Mason Lily Reeves 111 – ECHOES FROM HALIFAX International Premiere Drama Switzerland, Canada, 2026 Director : Mauro Mueller Cast : Ursina Lardi, Kris Holden-Ried, Djebril Zonga, Fathia Youssouf, Natalie Brown On September 2, 1998, the crash of Swissair Flight 111 off Halifax changes the lives of many people forever: relatives struggle for certainty about their loved ones, helpers try to offer comfort, and the residents of the Canadian coast are confronted with the traces of tragedy. As time passes and questions remain unanswered, the film shows how grief connects, relationships change, and new perspectives emerge. WICKER Comedy USA, 2025 Director : Alex Huston Fischer, Eleanor Wilson Cast : Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, Peter Dinklage, Elizabeth Debicki, Marli Siu, Nabhaan Rizwan An audacious comedic fable about sex, marriage, and the absurdities of social convention, WICKER tells the wholly original love story of an ostracized fisherwoman (Colman) who commissions a husband to be made by the local basketmaker (Dinklage). When her wicker husband (Skarsgård) proves more spectacular than she ever imagined, his soulful spirit and unique prowess awaken something inside her, setting off a wave of jealousy, fascination, and upheaval that threatens the very fabric of village life. COMPANY Mystery Canada, USA, UAE, 2026 Director : Casey Affleck Cast : Nick Nolte, Ben Mendelsohn, Adelaide Clemens, Scoot McNairy, Emily Alyn Lind, Caylee Cowan On a winter night in 1975, a mysterious woman named Evelyn arrives uninvited at a holiday gathering and tells the story of Tom, an aging hermit who rescues a stranded actress during a Colorado blizzard in 1953. To pass the night, the actress recounts an older tale of a farming couple who take in a troubled young drifter as a series of grisly murders spreads fear across the frontier. As the stories intertwine across generations, COMPANY becomes a meditation on grief, vengeance, forgiveness, and the quiet acts of compassion that can heal even the deepest wounds. POSSIBLE LOVE Drama South Korea, 2026 Director : Lee Chang-dong Cast : Jeon Do-yeon, Sul Kyung-gu, Zo In-sung, Cho Yeo-jeong Possible Love follows the intertwined relationship of two married couples facing different paths and hidden desires. Mi-ok (Jeon Do-yeon) lives quietly with her laid-off husband Ho-seok (Sul Kyung-gu) and their young son Cheol until a funeral brings them into the orbit of Ye-ji (Cho Yeo-jeong), a documentary filmmaker chronicling laid-off workers, and her husband Sang-woo (Zo In-sung) – a couple whose affluent lifestyle stands in sharp contrast to their own. When Mi-ok agrees to be filmed, she grows close to Ye-ji, and finds herself uneasily drawn to the unreadable Sang-woo. As their worlds collide, fractures begin to appear in their daily existence. LOVE, AFTER ALL World Premiere Tragicomedy Germany, 2026 Director : Andreas Dresen Cast : Dagmar Manzel, Joachim Król Lore (Dagmar Manzel) and Harry (Joachim Król) have been married for nearly 40 years and there is rarely a moment of silence between them. Old stories, missed chances and the uncertainties of retirement fuel heated discussions. Lore is afraid of growing old and bitter in the garden alongside Harry while he longs for stability and peace. There is only one thing they agree on: Their daughter Gloria has little luck in love. Now, she wants to get married for the third time – this time to a wealthy man who is almost the same age as Harry. IT WILL HAPPEN TONIGHT Romance Italy, France, Spain, 2026 Director : Nanni Moretti Cast : Louis Garrel, Jasmine Trinca, Hippolyte Girardot, Angela Finocchiaro, Melina Åkerman Kvie, Elena Lietti, Andrea Lattanzi, Antonio De Matteo, Nanni Moretti I’ll wait for you, for as long as you want me to. But will it ever happen? BURGUNDY Documentary France, 2026 Director : Michael Dweck, Gregory Kershaw Cast : Enzo Ferraroli, Céleste Kalis, Eric Goettelmann, Patrick Maniere, Guillaume Baroin, Bertrand Devillard Burgundy is one of the world’s most famous wine regions. Through the eyes of novices in hospitality and viticulture, BURGUNDY offers a fascinating glimpse into its unique wine culture, where time-honored traditions live on in rituals centered on luxury and indulgence. Blending documentary and fictional elements, directors Michael Dweck and Gregory Kershaw pay homage to the remarkable and charming people whose zest for life shapes and preserves this unique region and its centuries-old culture. HOW CAN I HELP? World Premiere Drama/Comedy Germany, 2026 Director : Doris Dörrie Cast : Angela Winkler, Laura Tonke, Josef Ellers, Via Jikeli, Eugene Boateng, Zoë Baier Mrs. Winkler has a fall and becomes a nursing case. Her daughter, overwhelmed by her needs, hires a care robot. After some initial resistance, Mrs. Winkler grows quite fond of him. He takes perfect care of her and keeps her entertained – except that he is also supposed to kill her in case her condition deteriorates further. THE HAMMER World Premiere Documentary France, USA, 2026 Director : Simon Wallon Cast : Simon de Pury, Jeff Koons, Marina Abramović, Chloe Wise, Lou Zhenggang A documentary portrait of famed auctioneer Simon de Pury, whose career saw him leading auction houses such as Sotheby’s and Phillips, being the curator of major world collections, an artist, even a DJ, and always being an unavoidable personality “the Mick Jagger of auctions” takes us behind the curtain of the extravagant art market. articles.title: ITN Journalist Exited With “Significant” Payoff After Review Found He Suffered Mental Health Discrimination
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake Jenna Fischer Joins Outpouring Of Support For ‘The Office’ Star Lucy Davis After She Revealed Terminal Cancer Diagnosis After Chaos Of Cruise Vs Pitt AI Deepfakes, Seedance 2.5 Is Now Blocking Hollywood Rip-Offs ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Season 2 Gets Premiere Date View All August 13, 2026 1:00am ITN's headquarters ITN/Matt Freestone EXCLUSIVE : ITN is facing fresh questions about its workplace culture after an external review concluded that a journalist suffered disability discrimination when raising concerns about his working environment, Deadline can reveal. Leo, a pseudonym we are using to protect the identity of the journalist, left ITN in April with a “significant” undisclosed financial settlement after a tumultuous conclusion to his 12-year-long career at the company, where he was once recognized as a rising star and secured Royal Television Society award nominations. ITN is the respected British production outfit behind ITV , Channel 4 and Paramount-owned 5’s news services, as well as hit Netflix documentaries, such as The Investigation of Lucy Letby . But in recent years it has been dogged by questions about its culture, approach to complaints handling, and use of non-disclosure agreements. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals 'Sorry, I Didn't Know's Historic ITV Run Extends To Seventh Season News ITV's Zandland Doc 'Inside Iran: War & Revolution' Goes Undercover During Anti-Regime Protests & Conflict With The U.S. In 2024, a review by law firm Simmons & Simmons concluded that there was “low trust and psychological safety” within parts of ITN, according to a summary seen by Deadline. Some employees complained that they were reluctant to speak out, fearing that it could impact their wellbeing. Watch on Deadline Leo’s story thrusts these issues back into the spotlight, not least because the external HR consultant engaged by ITN to improve workplace conditions and provide management training was deemed to have discriminated against Leo, albeit unintentionally. ITN said the wellbeing of its employees was “paramount,” and that it investigates concerns fairly and has learned from past mistakes. The company strongly refutes the way the events involving Leo have been characterized, but said it could not comment on individuals. ITN did not admit any liability as part of Leo’s exit agreement, per documents seen by Deadline. Leo, who did not sign an NDA after leaving ITN, has a history of mental health issues. He was diagnosed with post-traumatic stress disorder after reporting on the terror attack on an Ariana Grande concert in Manchester in 2017. Then in 2023, he was signed off work and hospitalized with depression. ITN gave Leo access to trauma support and private therapy, but has admitted to shortcomings in handling his mental health after his 2023 breakdown. This included breaching his privacy in July 2024 when an HR executive shared sensitive information about his condition without Leo’s consent. In interviews with Deadline, Leo said the deterioration of his working relationship with a senior colleague sparked a chain of events that led to his departure, including Leo himself facing a gross misconduct investigation. Deadline is not disclosing the identity of the senior colleague or the ITN division in which Leo worked. Leo alleged that the relationship breakdown was exacerbated by a power imbalance that resulted in him becoming isolated at work. This was disputed by other sources familiar with the situation, who did not recognize the power dynamic described by Leo. The sources added that the relationship breakdown also provoked serious concerns about the wellbeing of the senior colleague. ITN facilities In November 2024, Leo wrote an email to his senior colleague detailing his misgivings about their working relationship, as well as expressing concerns to managers and HR. The correspondence triggered an ITN investigation, which was overseen by a representative from People Puzzles, an external HR consultancy drafted in to improve ITN’s people management and complaints procedures. Leo told ITN he did not want or expect the matters to be formally investigated. He feared that the investigation could be weighted in favor of his colleague because of their seniority, despite receiving assurances that this was not the case. The senior colleague was ultimately cleared of wrongdoing, but Leo claimed that the investigation was flawed because of its focus on his mental illness. Leo Subject To “Disadvantages” His subsequent complaint about ITN’s investigation was examined as part of an external review by Kane HR, per a report seen by Deadline. Kane HR concluded that the ITN’s investigation “inappropriately strayed” into a discussion about Leo’s mental wellbeing and its impact on the workplace, instead of focusing on fact-finding. “My view is that [the] employee was subjected to some disadvantages in the investigation process, based on his disability, and it could have been conducted in a fairer and more conciliatory way,” the report said. Kane HR concluded that Leo’s experience was “discriminatory,” though stressed that this was not done intentionally and that no “statutory requirements” were breached by the People Puzzles consultant. The Kane HR report said the original investigation’s recommendations were “comprehensive and reasonable,” but added that there were elements of Leo’s experience that “may have been appropriate to investigate further.” Leo submitted his written statement after the original investigation had closed, telling ITN he was too unwell to meet earlier deadlines set by the People Puzzles consultant. Kane HR said another deadline extension would have been a “reasonable adjustment” given the “knowledge of his ill health.” Once the statement was received, the People Puzzles consultant’s view was that it did not change the outcome of the investigation, which absolved the senior colleague. ITN stands by the findings of the original investigation, despite admitting that the process was flawed. In a June 2025 email to Leo, ITN’s general counsel Zaffrin O’Sullivan wrote: “The company accepts the findings set out in the report and acknowledges and apologises for the instances in which [Kane HR] has found that the original investigation fell short of the standards which you were entitled to expect having raised concerns.” She later told him that it was a “red line” moment for ITN, according to Leo. People Puzzles, which did not respond to a request for comment, is no longer engaged by ITN. Leo Launches Lawsuit; ITN Opens Probe After the investigations, ITN and Leo established a framework for his continued employment, but he argued that the arrangements diluted his role and responsibilities, leaving him isolated and vulnerable to losing his job. Leo’s former co-workers told Deadline that it was a complex situation for all involved. These ITN insiders said the relationship breakdown, and subsequent working framework, created confusion about responsibilities and was difficult to navigate. In December 2025, Leo filed an employment tribunal lawsuit against ITN, claiming discrimination arising from his disability. Within weeks, the company launched its own investigation into Leo’s conduct, citing concerns that he went on a reporting assignment without permission, published an article on Substack without approval, and made a comment to a manager that was perceived as a threat to report his superior to HR. The review concluded that Leo’s actions amounted to gross misconduct and he would face disciplinary action, according to a document seen by Deadline. Leo denied wrongdoing and told Deadline that the investigation felt like a retaliatory “fishing expedition” designed to gather evidence ahead of a potential legal battle. Leo claimed that he was not allowed to call his own witnesses as part of an investigation, which ITN insiders dispute, even though all those interviewed were his superiors. Leo added that he was never shown the terms of reference and the investigation report made no substantive allowances for his mental health or previous experience of discrimination. In a letter to ITN, Leo’s therapist said the investigation had a “profound psychological” impact on the journalist. “Where an individual already experiences the workplace as unsafe, unsupportive, or punitive after raising concerns, the escalation of formal processes can be profoundly destabilising,” she added. Leo’s attorney argued that the ITN investigation was a “further act of discrimination” and was evidence that his working relationship had “irretrievably broken down,” per a letter seen by Deadline. Proposing an exit deal that would involve Leo dropping his lawsuit, the lawyer added: “My client cannot now, in good conscience, remain in a working environment that is making him unwell and poses further risk to his mental health.” Leo left in April with an undisclosed payoff as part of an agreement that settled his lawsuit, but he has continued to raise concerns about his experience. “I just wouldn’t want anyone else to go through this,” Leo told Deadline. “I believed in [ITN], and I believed in its journalistic principles. It was my dream place to work and to then have the experience that I had was just beyond devastating.” ITN insiders shared concerns about the company’s HR processes, but they told Deadline that it would have been a complex situation to navigate, even for an extremely skilled and experienced people management professional. An ITN spokesperson told Deadline: “When a concern is raised we consider it promptly, thoroughly and fairly in view of everyone involved. The wellbeing of all our staff is paramount, and where shortcomings to HR processes have been identified in the past we have learnt from them and always seek continual improvement. While we strongly refute the way these events have been characterised, it would not be appropriate to comment on individuals.” Claudia-Liza Vanderpuije ITN’s culture was a subject of discussion in UK Parliament in March 2025. MP Layla Moran used parliamentary privilege to tell the story of a female employee, who was allegedly suspended after complaining about a “coercive, controlling sexual relationship with an older male editor.” Moran claimed that the woman was prevented from speaking about her experience because of an NDA. More recently, former 5 News presenter Claudia-Liza Vanderpuije sued ITN over allegations of sexism, racial harassment, unfair dismissal, and suffering a detriment due to exercising her whistleblowing rights. The case was settled before going to court, with ITN denying wrongdoing. ITN has since installed Ian Rumsey as its new CEO, replacing Rachel Corp in May. The company’s HR team has also been restructured following the Simmons & Simmons review, while internal employee resources for reporting concerns have been strengthened. articles.title: Marc Turtletaub On His Sprawling Scottish Road Movie ‘Borges and Me’ — Edinburgh
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Marc Turtletaub On His Sprawling Scottish Road Movie ‘Borges and Me’ — Edinburgh Caron Creighton On Capturing The Fight To Save Northern California’s Largest Homeless Encampment With Her Debut Feature ‘Wood Street’ ‘Black Zombie’: Maya Annik Bedward On Her 10-Year Journey To Explore The Political History Of Cinema’s Favorite Monster View All August 13, 2026 1:00am Veteran director-producer Marc Turtletaub returns to feature filmmaking this year with Borges and Me , which screens this weekend in one of the primetime Out of Competition spots at the Edinburgh International Film Festival. Directed by Turtletaub from a screenplay by Oren Moverman, the film follows a young graduate student at the University of St Andrews who embarks on the trip of a lifetime across the Scottish Highlands accompanied by the legendary poet Jorge Luis Borges. The picture is an adaptation of Jay Parini’s popular memoir Borges and Me: An Encounter . Fionn Whitehead and Luis Gnecco lead the film alongside a band of popular Scottish actors, including Alan Cumming, Freya Mavor, John Gordon Sinclair, Morven Christie, Peter Mullan, and Stuart Bowman. Check out a clip from the feature above, and below, you can read our interview with Turtletaub ahead of this weekend’s screenings in Edinburgh. Turtletaub discusses how he stumbled upon Parini’s best-selling novel and how he mounted this large-scale production in 61 locations across Scotland. Turtletaub also teases his next feature project. Related Stories News Supernatural Thriller 'Snapshot' Gets Sales Deal Ahead Of Edinburgh & Frightfest Bows, Watch First Clip Festivals 'Mission' Clip: George MacKay & Rosy McEwen Lead Edinburgh Competition Title DEADLINE: Marc, how did this project come to be? Where did you find the book? MARC TURTLETAUB: We have book scouts. We have other producers send us material. We develop our own. But this one I just found in a bookstore. I was actually on vacation in Hawaii, walked into a bookstore, and saw it. The book was a few years old at that point and looked interesting. I knew a little bit about Borges, but not as much as I do now. I started reading it and fell in love with it. DEADLINE: In all those years, did no one else try to adapt the book? It feels like a ready-made story. TURTLETAUB: There was another team that had tried to put it together, but it hadn’t happened, so they were open to us coming and getting involved. It’s a road movie, so the first thing I did, even before we had the rights to the book, was get in a car and drive from St Andrews up to Orkney. I took the exact route from the book and tried to stay in all the same places. As we were going, I would identify possible shooting locations. DEADLINE: This is a road movie, and it’s rare for films of this scale to be made in the UK. Was it a difficult process to build this production? TURTLETAUB : We make our own movies and then sell them, so we have that big advantage. The film was a co-production between four countries: Holland, Belgium, the UK, and the U.S., so we had an interesting mix of financing. But you’re right, these kinds of movies are rare these days. But we had a great line producer who introduced us to the best crew in Scotland, and having these great Scottish actors join made it a real pleasure. DEADLINE: Yes, this is a great cast. Luis, who plays Borges, is amazing. I believe he is from Chile? TURTLETAUB : Yes, Luis Gnecco. He starred in Neruda , the film about Pablo Neruda, so he seems to specialize in these great writers. I fell in love with his work. He was probably the best-prepared actor I have ever worked with. He read just about everything that had been written about Borges. He found a movie that I didn’t even know existed, which Borges had written. He saw live interviews with Borges. He met someone who knew Borges and interviewed him. In the script, there is a line where Borges says something in Anglo-Saxon, so Luis learned Anglo-Saxon. So that’s the guy that showed up, truly marrying talent with preparation. He was a real treat. And then Fionn Whitehead, who was the lead in Dunkirk , was great as a foil to this wild Luis Gnecco. And then we were able to get all these great Scottish actors: Alan Cumming, Peter Mullan, Freya Mavor, people that were signing on because they liked the project, and we were quite fortunate. DEADLINE: How involved was Jay in the production? TURTLETAUB : He loves filmmaking, and we welcomed him. He was on set every day. In fact, one day we were shooting the scene where Freya Mavor sings a song. Jay was there and, within an hour, wrote the lyrics. So he was a great supporter. The screenplay was written by Oren Moverman, who is a good friend. Oren wrote another movie I made called Puzzle , and he’s going to be working on the next one that I’m going to make. So we have a good relationship. When Jay read the screenplay, he said to Oren, “This is a masterclass in adaptation.” So we knew he liked it, which was important to us. DEADLINE: What’s the next one going to be? TURTLETAUB : The next one is based on a book written by the British author Ben Reeves. It’s called Everything Was Beautiful and Nothing Hurt . It just came out and, in its first week, was on the New York Times bestseller list, so we think it’s quite special. DEADLINE: Marc, you’ve done a lot in your filmmaking career. Is there anything left that you’d like to tick off your list? TURTLETAUB : We really love what we’re doing. I want to continue doing it well. I’ve been able to pass on the leadership of our company to Tim Foley and Michael Clark, and that feels great because one is my son and the other feels like my nephew. We’ve worked together for almost 20 years. And we’re looking at new things as a company. We’re working on a low-cost 3D animation, and we’re excited about that. That’ll be something new for us. This past year we shot an independent TV pilot without a distributor, with Nicole Holofcener directing. It’s called Worried and follows two sisters living in New York. We’re looking forward to lining up a distribution for that. So those are two new things the company is doing, and for me, it’s just about continuing to do what I’m doing and helping support the next generation. articles.title: Marc Turtletaub To Direct Feature Adaptation Of Ben Reeves’ Novel ‘Everything Was Beautiful And Nothing Hurt’

Miikka Skaffari/Getty Images. EXCLUSIVE: Marc Turtletaub will direct a feature adaptation of Ben Reeves ’ novel Everything Was Beautiful and Nothing Hurt . The novel, which landed on the New York Times Bestsellers List in its first week, will be adapted by screenwriter Oren Moverman. Everything Was Beautiful and Nothing Hurt tells the story of Travis, who lives with his cat in a small, gray town. His job is to offer people comfort in their final hours of life, which he does without complaint or judgment. But when Travis meets Dalia, a midwife, and her boisterous eight-year-old daughter Layla, who live across the hall, he begins to understand what it means to be truly alive—and what might be irrevocably lost in death. Related Stories News Marc Turtletaub On His Sprawling Scottish Road Movie 'Borges and Me' -- Edinburgh News Bleecker Street Bets On Ben Kingsley & 'Jules'; 'The Pod Generation', Stephen King Doc Debut As Strike Keeps Talent On Sidelines - Specialty Preview Moverman and Turtletaub have enjoyed a long-standing creative partnership. Moverman wrote Turtletaub’s 2018 film Puzzle and his latest feature, Borges and Me , which debuts this weekend at the Edinburgh International Film Festival. Watch on Deadline Turtletaub revealed his plans to adapt Reeves’ novel during an interview with Deadline , ahead of his trip to Edinburgh. “The next one is based on a book written by the British author Ben Reeves. It’s called Everything Was Beautiful and Nothing Hurt . It just came out and, in its first week, was on the New York Times bestseller list, so we think it’s quite special,” Turtletaub said, adding the film will be shot in the UK. You can read that full interview here . Borges and Me is Turtletaub’s first feature as a director since Jules (2023). The film follows a young graduate student at the University of St Andrews who embarks on the trip of a lifetime across the Scottish Highlands accompanied by the legendary poet Jorge Luis Borges. The picture is an adaptation of Jay Parini’s New York Times bestselling memoir Borges and Me: An Encounter . Fionn Whitehead and Luis Gnecco lead the film alongside a band of popular Scottish actors, including Alan Cumming, Freya Mavor, John Gordon Sinclair, Morven Christie, Peter Mullan, and Stuart Bowman. Borges and Me debuts on Saturday, August 15, at the Edinburgh International Film Festival. The festival ends on August 19. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Andreas Wiseman Andreas Wiseman Executive Editor, Film & International @AndreasWiseman More Stories By Andreas Nicola Coughlan, Charithra Chandran, Kate Winslet & More Join Netflix’s ‘Charlie Vs. The Chocolate Factory’ As Streamer Sets Release Date & 47-Day Theatrical Window Sundance Dark Comedy ‘Run Amok’ Gets North American Deal With Greenwich Entertainment Viral Game ‘Scary Teacher’ Getting Movie Adaptation With Studio Vet Joe Roth Aboard View All August 13, 2026 2:00am Guz And Kiell Will Not Survive Audible EXCLUSIVE : Brit actors, comedians and pals Guz Khan and Kiell Smith-Bynoe have been set by Audible for podcast Guz and Kiell Will Not Survive . Across six episodes, the self-proclaimed survival novices are guided through a series of choose-your-own-adventure survival scenarios taking from the frozen wilderness of Lapland to the Australian Outback. The duo will “make life-or-death decisions as they battle deadly wildlife, extreme weather, and increasingly absurd challenges all without ever leaving the safety of the podcast studio”. Guiding them through each adventure will be survival expert Megan Hine, best known for her work alongside Bear Grylls on Bear Grylls: Mission Survive . According to Audible: “With Guz and Kiell turning every challenge into chaos, from vomiting vultures and volcanic eruptions to sperm whale ‘poonados’, crotch rot and Custard Cream-fuelled survival strategies – making it out in one piece is far from guaranteed.” Watch on Deadline Man Like Mobeen star Khan said of the show, which launches August 13th: “ Who even got me into this? I hope Kiell, expert Megan and the Lord can keep us safe. Ameen.” Ghosts and Stath Lets Flats actor Kiell Smith-Bynoe added: “This Audible podcast proves that surviving isn’t just about having the right skills, it’s about not listening to Guz. Every episode somehow got more chaotic than the last, and I’m still not convinced we’d last five minutes in any of these situations. I had an absolute blast making it.” The friends have previously appeared together on series 15 of Taskmaster and in live improv shows such as Kiell Smith-Bynoe’s Kool Story Bro . articles.title: Disney+ Signs Content Deal With Gary Neville’s The Overlap To Strike Back Against Netflix’s Football Podcast Play
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘Son Of A Critch’: Trailer For Final Season Of Canadian Sitcom Sees Mark Having A Midlife Crisis At 17 Actor & Singer Luke Charles Stafford Launches Dream United Studios With ‘Against The Wall’ Magna Studios Signs ‘20,000 Days On Earth’ Makers Iain Forsyth & Jane Pollard View All August 13, 2026 2:48am Disney+ has signed a podcast deal with The Overlap Disney+ The score is now Disney+ 1, Netflix 1. Disney’s streaming service has struck a deal with former Manchester United footballer and emerging media magnate Gary Neville for podcasts from his Global Studios-owned company, The Overlap . This follows Netflix branching out into football podcasts over the summer by backing the World Cup editions of Gary Lineker’s show , The Rest is Football . The arrangement highlights the growing power of podcasts led by former players, and the desire for global streamers to sign up video-led sports podcasts. The agreement sees Disney+ land 40 new episodes of Neville’s Stick to Football show, with the streamer also getting 50 episodes of new series Stick to United with Wayne Rooney . Disney+ will become headline sponsor on both shows during the nearing 2026/27 season. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'The Lowdown' Gets Season 2 Release Date At FX; First Photos Of Tommy Lee Jones & Betty Gilpin News Alex Cooper's Unwell Media Company Valued At $500M After Investment By Patrick Whitesell's Firm The Stick to Football episodes will run on Disney+, other podcast platforms and The Overlap’s YouTube channel, while Stick to United will be on Disney+, other platforms and The Overlap. Twenty episodes will be exclusive to Disney+ for a “limited time.” Disney+ has also commissioned six exclusive extended-length eps of Stick to United that will feature special guests. Stick to Football is hosted by footballing legends Neville, Jamie Carragher, Jill Scott, Ian Wright and Roy Keane, and sees the group welcome guests to discuss all manner of football matters. Stick to United will see Manchester United record goalscorer Rooney, who was a breakout pundit at the recent World Cup, hosting alongside Mark Goldbridge , the often over-excited and exasperated United fan who has built a huge YouTube following for his views on the team’s performances. They will analyze the English Premier League team’s latest results and biggest talking points. Goldbridge sold his media channels to The Overlap in April, and today he called Stick to United “an historic milestone for fan-led media.” Stick to United will stream weekly from next Tuesday (August 18), while Stick to Football will stream weekly in the UK and Ireland from Thursday (August 20). Neville, co-founder and co-chair of The Overlap, said the “unique partnership that feels right for everyone involved,” and added, “What’s exciting is that we’re not changing who we are. Our community will continue to enjoy our content in exactly the way they always have through YouTube, while at the same time Disney+’s incredible global streaming audience will now be able to discover and enjoy it too.” “As we move into a new era of sports entertainment on Disney+, we’re excited to be bringing one of the UK’s most popular and distinctive sports shows to the platform,” said Sean Doyle, Disney+ EMEA’s VP, Unscripted. “What Gary and the team at The Overlap have created with Stick to Football – and now Stick to United with Wayne Rooney – is truly unique. Adding both shows broadens our local original content offering as we continue to expand into new sports formats, complementing our existing catalogue of drama, comedy, documentary, reality and ESPN on Disney+.” Global, the UK-based radio and audio giant, acquired a majority stake in The Overlap in January. articles.title: Nicholas Hoult Boards ‘Harry Potter’ Season 2 as Gilderoy Lockhart
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rick Porter Plus Icon Rick Porter Television Business Editor rickporter Follow Sign Up View All August 11, 2026 3:31pm Nicholas Hoult Neilson Barnard/Getty Images Logo text HBO ‘s Harry Potter series has locked in a key role for season two. Nicholas Hoult ( Superman, The Great ) has joined the series as Professor Gilderoy Lokckhart, who comes to Hogwarts in Harry’s (Dominic McLaughlin) second year as the new Defense Against the Dark Arts teacher. Lockhart is a key character in Harry Potter and the Chamber of Secrets , the second book in J.K. Rowling’s series and the source material for season two of the show. The character is renowned in the wizarding world for his many heroic deeds, though he’s later revealed as a fraud who took credit for the acts of others after erasing part of their memories. Kenneth Branagh previously played Lockhart in the 2002 Chamber of Secrets film. Related Stories Movies Makeup Oscar Record Holder Recalls Turning Jim Carrey Into the Grinch, Transforming Jacko for 'Thriller' and Playing King Kong Movies Crunchyroll, Sony Nab Makoto Shinkai's Untitled Next Anime Film for Global Release HBO gave an early season two renewal to Harry Potter in May. The show’s first season, officially titled Harry Potter and the Philosopher’s Stone , is set to premiere Dec. 25. Along with McLaughlin, the show’s core cast includes Arabella Stanton (Hermione Granger), Alastair Stout (Ron Weasley), John Lithgow (Albus Dumbledore), Janet McTeer (Minerva McGonagall), Paapa Essiedu (Severus Snape), Nick Frost (Rubeus Hagrid), Rory Wilmot (Neville Longbottom) and Lox Pratt (Draco Malfoy). Francesca Gardiner is the showrunner for season one and executive produces with Mark Mylod (who also directs multiple episodes); Rowling, Neil Blair, and Ruth Kenley-Letts of Brontë Film and TV; and David Heyman of Heyday Films, who produced the eight Harry Potter movies. Jon Brown ( Succession ) is co-showrunner with Gardiner on season two. Hoult broke out in 2002’s About a Boy opposite Hugh Grant. His credits also include Nosferatu, The Menu and four X-Men movies, starting with 2011’s First Class . He’ll next be seen in Amazon MGM’s How to Rob a Bank and the Disney+/Hulu series Mosquito , from The Great creator Tony McNamara. Hoult is repped by UTA, 42, Sloane Offer and Relevant.
