articles.title: Paramount’s Makan Delrahim Says “Everything Is On The Table” In Finding Merger Resolution, Says Leaving California Is A Consideration But Not “Blackmail”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted Paramount’s Makan Delrahim Says “Everything Is On The Table” In Finding Merger Resolution, Says Leaving California Is A Consideration But Not “Blackmail” Kennedy Center Ordered To Pay Jazz Musician Chuck Redd More Than $250,000 In Legal Dispute Over His Opposition To Trump Renaming Tammy Fine To Lead Talent Development For NBC News View All August 11, 2026 5:50pm Screenshot Paramount ‘s Chief Legal Officer Makan Delrahim said that “everything is on the table” when it comes to finding a resolution to a state attorneys general lawsuit seeking to block the company’s proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery . At a Politico conference on Tuesday, Delrahim also defended the company’s consideration of exiting California. California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who is leading the state AGs lawsuit and appeared at the same conference hours earlier, called the threat to leave a form of “blackmail.” “David Ellison was born here, lived here since I moved to this country. I’ve lived here. He’s raising his children here. His intent is to be committed to be in California,” Delrahim said. He added, “There’s a point at which where you have a duty, a fiduciary duty to your shareholders, and those are all the factors you consider. But our goal is to be here.” Related Stories News 'Harry Potter' TV Series Due To Hit HBO In 2027: Everything We Know About The Cast, Who's Creating It, What J.K. Rowling Says & More Legal California AG Rob Bonta Open To Structural Remedies In Paramount-WBD Suit But Calls 30 Movies A Year An "Old, Stale Promise" Delrahim said, “I heard the attorney general say that this was some kind of blackmail attempt for the lawsuit. It is not. When the delay starts costing you know after this merger has been approved from, I believe, 67 countries — European Union, China. Canada, Australia — let’s forget about the DOJ — but all of them have reviewed it this way. But this state seems to view this merger in a different market. You have to take a look at the business environment and look to see what’s best for not only the community, the business, and ultimately, go to the place where you are wanted.” Watch on Deadline Ellison told a group of the company’s executives that he would start the process of leaving the state around Oct. 1 if Bonta did not negotiate a settlement. Paramount faces paying a $7 million-per-day ticking fee to Warner Bros. Discovery for each day that the merger doesn’t close past Sept. 30. But a federal judge last week set the trial for next March, scuttling the company’s plans to close the deal as soon as this summer. California and 11 other states sued to block the merger last month, claiming that it would stifle competition for wide release theatrical film distribution, anticipated big budget blockbusters, and basic cable television channel licensing. With the prospect of a trial delaying the transaction well into next year, Paramount has waged a PR campaign to try to show that the deal has drawn industry support, while Ellison has tried to peg the state AG opposition as about concerns over what would happen to CNN, amid warnings that he would push the network in a Trump-friendlier direction. In a new York Times op ed, Ellison wrote that news organizations require independence, while he said that CNN and CBS News, which Paramount already owns, “are here to tell it straight down the middle.” Delrahim pointed to the Ellison op ed, and said that when it came to CNN, the CEO “wants to bring it back to news.” Bonta, though, denied that the lawsuit was about control of the network, and a mere divestment of the channel would not be a sufficient structural remedy to satisfy the state AGs. Delrahim told the Politico conference, “I take [Bonta] at his word. It’s not about CNN.This is an antitrust case. He’s trying to protect movie theaters and cable operators, as alleged in the lawsuit.” But Delrahim predicted that the AGs would not have a viable case at trial. He pointed to support for the merger from major exhibitors, and when it came to the merger’s impact on cable operators, “it will fall apart because of the market definition.” “There is no such thing as basic cable anymore,” he said. “Combined, if you look at streaming, the two companies will have something like 7% to 11% of the market share.” When Politico’s Alex Burns pressed him on the prospect of selling CNN as a way to “make it easier to get this deal done,” Delrahim responded, “I was born in Iran. I moved here after the 1979 revolution. The single most important thing we have is the First Amendment. not because I’m a religious minority and …think people should be free, but also the First Amendment and free speech. If you start using state powers and wrap yourself around that to actually violate the First Amendment and control of content, that would be the saddest day in this country.” He added, “But having said that, everything is on the table. We would be delighted to engage and discuss about any resolution to get this merger, to get this closing after all this time, in order to repair the industry, create more jobs, bring more jobs and production back.” Delrahim also was asked about the prospect that the company would be investigated by Democrats if they take control of one or more chambers of Congress in the midterms. Rep. Jamie Raskin (D-MD), the ranking member of the House Judiciary Committee, and other Democrats have warned that Paramount would face scrutiny along with other big mergers and efforts to win support from the Trump administration. “You can allege all you want,” Delrahim said. “There is no corruption here.” CEO Threatens To Leave California If Suit Isn’t Settled; AG Calls It “Blackmail” Nicholas Hoult Joins ‘Harry Potter’ As Gilderoy Lockhart For Season 2 ‘Brand New Day’ To Hit $700M U.S. Wednesday; ‘End Of Oak Street’ Due Friday ‘Bourbon & Lies’ Series Based On Books In Works At MGM TV Read More About: 3 Comments

articles.title: California Democratic Gubernatorial Nominee Xavier Becerra Says He Prefers Settlement Of Paramount-WBD Antitrust Lawsuit: “Conference Room, Not Courtroom”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Ted Johnson Ted Johnson Political Editor @tedstew More Stories By Ted California Democratic Gubernatorial Nominee Xavier Becerra Says He Prefers Settlement Of Paramount-WBD Antitrust Lawsuit: “Conference Room, Not Courtroom” Paramount’s Makan Delrahim Says “Everything Is On The Table” In Finding Merger Resolution, Says Leaving California Is A Consideration But Not “Blackmail” Kennedy Center Ordered To Pay Jazz Musician Chuck Redd More Than $250,000 In Legal Dispute Over His Opposition To Trump Renaming View All August 11, 2026 6:23pm Xavier Becerra Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images Xavier Becerra , the Democratic nominee to become the next governor of California, recommended that state attorneys general and Paramount reach a settlement and avoid an antitrust trial over the proposed Warner Bros. Discovery merger. Weighing in for the first time on the lawsuit, Becerra said at a Politico conference on Tuesday, “I hope it settles before court. It is easier to stand in a conference room and settle than it is to stand in a courtroom. I say that having had to stand both in the conference room and in the courtroom. You get way more done in the conference room than you do in the courtroom.” Becerra, the former secretary of health and human services during the Biden administration, served as California’s attorney general from 2017 to 2021. That is the job now held by Rob Bonta , who is leading 12 state attorneys general in their lawsuit to block the transaction. Related Stories News Paramount's Makan Delrahim Says "Everything Is On The Table" In Finding Merger Resolution, Says Leaving California Is A Consideration But Not "Blackmail" News 'Harry Potter' TV Series Due To Hit HBO In 2027: Everything We Know About The Cast, Who's Creating It, What J.K. Rowling Says & More Becerra did not weigh in on the merits of the state AGs’ case, but said, “Having done antitrust cases, these are not easy. They’re a different animal from most litigation. They are very difficult. They are very fact intensive. The law doesn’t keep pace. All I know is this, in terms of what’s going on in this particular case, the entertainment industry is our baby in California. We have to fight to keep it vibrant. If a merger is good, that helps that keeps it vibrant, I’m willing to say, let’s take a look. If that merger undermines the ability of the industry of remaining vibrant, then I’m going to take … a closer look as well. At the end of the day, is it good for the entertainment community in California? Does it benefit California families to have another merger occur? And then, at the end of the day, who will settle it?” Watch on Deadline Asked about reports that Paramount CEO David Ellison has raised the prospect of the company exiting California if no settlement is reached, Becerra said, “Having a major player in the industry leave would not be good. At the same time, I said as well, ‘Is it going to be good for working families?’ Having them leave leave the state is certainly not good for working families. So let’s be adults, not be kids. Conference room, not courtroom.” Earlier, Becerra’s Republican rival, Steve Hilton , blasted the state AG case, calling it “totally politically motivated.” He said that Bonta’s arguments “just don’t add up.” CEO Threatens To Leave California If Suit Isn’t Settled; AG Calls It “Blackmail” Nicholas Hoult Joins ‘Harry Potter’ As Gilderoy Lockhart For Season 2 ‘Brand New Day’ To Hit $700M U.S. Wednesday; ‘End Of Oak Street’ Due Friday ‘Bourbon & Lies’ Series Based On Books In Works At MGM TV Read More About: 8 Comments

articles.title: Mel Gibson Shares ‘Lethal Weapon 5’ Update: “I Think That The Fifth Script Is Better Than All Of The Others”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Rosario Dawson Says She’s “A Reject Of Spider-Man” After ‘Brand New Day’ Cut ‘Daredevil’s Claire Temple Cameo Mel Gibson Shares ‘Lethal Weapon 5’ Update: “I Think That The Fifth Script Is Better Than All Of The Others” Crunchyroll Acquires Makoto Shinkai’s Next Feature Film View All August 11, 2026 6:40pm Danny Glover and Mel Gibson in 'Lethal Weapon 2' Warner Bros. Mel Gibson is sharing an update on the development of Lethal Weapon 5 following years of the actor’s intentions to make the sequel. In a new interview, Gibson gave details on what this fifth installment would look like and where the characters would be after all these years. “The characters are quite different. They’re older. One’s retired. The other one’s on a desk job. He’s putting on too much weight, and it’s low-tech,” Gibson told Collider while attending Fan Expo Boston. “It doesn’t get into the big explosions and all this sort of stuff. But it still has the energy and, I think, drive of a big action film.” Related Stories News Lionsgate Shifts 'The Resurrection Of The Christ' Release Dates; 'Part Two' Moves To 2028 Late Night TV 'SNL' Sketch Has J.K. Rowling, Mel Gibson, Armie Hammer, Ye & More Celebs Claiming They Have Tourette's Following BAFTAs Racial Slur Incident Gibson noted that the film “only harks back” to the previous films in a “minimal way,” and that the new installment in the Lethal Weapon franchise would be “a story all on its own.” Watch on Deadline As far as the action scenes, Gibson said, “It’s a foot chase, right? But it’s kind of filmed like a car chase. So it still has all the elements of what was in the other films, but not nearly so complicated. But it deals more about the people in it.” The actor also said he would “absolutely” want to direct the new film, as that’s what the OG director, Richard Donner, wanted. “Donner, God rest his soul, he said to me in this deep voice, he said, ‘Hey kid, if I drop off the perch, you’ll take this over, won’t you?’ I said, ‘Shut up! You’re not going anywhere.’ And of course he did,” he recalled. “And, you know, when he passed away, I didn’t say anything. But apparently he had told other people that too, so they all came to me and said, ‘You direct it.’ I said, ‘Yeah, okay.’” Gibson said that Donner had been working on the script for the film when he died, saying, “Donner, when he was 90 years old, was working on the fifth, and of course he passed away in the middle. So I got together with the writer, and we completed it thinking, ‘What would Donner do?’ That’s what we were thinking in the room, and I think that the fifth script is better than all of the others. But it’s tied up in some kind of industrial film hell that you can’t extract it from to make it.” Production for the film has not started due to the inner workings of the studio, with Gibson giving insight: “Richard Wenk and I finished the script, and we were going to go into production, but it just never got the wheels under it. I think Warner’s got into some quicksand at that time… so it got buried somewhere, and now I think this David Ellison guy over at Paramount has absorbed or will absorb Warners, or it looks like he will. And maybe, maybe they’ll take the chains off that one, and you might see that in another year or so.” Lethal Weapon is a 1987 action thriller directed by Richard Donner and written by Shane Black, starring Mel Gibson as Martin Riggs and Danny Glover as Roger Murtaugh. The film’s success spawned several sequels, including Lethal Weapon 2 (1989), Lethal Weapon 3 (1992), and Lethal Weapon 4 (1998). A television series of the same name starring Clayne Crawford as Martin Riggs and Damon Wayans as Roger Murtaugh premiered on Fox in 2016 and ran for three seasons. articles.title: Donald Trump Waging $10B Legal War Against BBC On Basis “Doctored” Documentary May Have Been Viewed 285 Times In America
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ Season 2 Gets Premiere Date ‘The Office’ Star Lucy Davis Reveals She Has Incurable Cancer Ari Emanuel’s Mari Agrees Deal To Buy ATG, Owner Of Theater Venues Behind Shows Like ‘Harry Potter & The Cursed Child’ View All August 12, 2026 1:30am Donald Trump is suing the BBC over a 'Panorama' documentary. Getty Donald Trump ‘s lawyers have accused the BBC of a “brazen” attempt to interfere in the 2024 U.S. election on the basis that fewer than 300 Americans may have seen a documentary that misleadingly edited his January 6 speech. Trump is suing the BBC for defamation in Florida for $10 billion, and his amended complaint against the British broadcaster incorporates newly discovered evidence about the viewing figures for the Panorama film, Trump: A Second Chance? , which premiered days before the presidential election. Trump’s new complaint claims that the documentary — which was produced by October Films and spliced together two parts of Trump’s Capitol riots speech — was streamed on iPlayer by “hundreds of individuals” in the U.S., despite it being geoblocked in America. Related Stories News Kennedy Center Ordered To Pay Jazz Musician Chuck Redd More Than $250,000 In Legal Dispute Over His Opposition To Trump Renaming News BBC Joins Working Title's New TV Adaptation Of 'Jane Eyre' Starring Aimee Lou Wood But the evidence was not this emphatic. Watch on Deadline The lawsuit attributes the new information to a deposition of Richard Cooper, the BBC’s director of digital distribution. Cooper revealed that the Panorama film was successfully viewed 570,000 times on iPlayer, but only 0.05%, or 285, of these streams originated from IP addresses that could have been based in America. Some 34 streams appear to have originated from IP addresses that may have been based in Florida, where the case is being heard. During his interview under oath, Cooper was repeatedly clear with Trump’s lawyers that although the BBC’s data “might identify the IP address as being from the United States, that doesn’t necessarily mean to say it originated from the United States.” He added that the Florida IP streams were linked to an internet service provider associated with a cruise ship company. Cooper also qualified that the BBC’s viewing figures were for the “entire period that the documentary was available.” This is important because it is not clear if the 285 potential U.S. streams came in the days leading up to the election, when Trump claims that election meddling took place. The Panorama film was on iPlayer for around a year before being pulled by the BBC. The BBC is defending the lawsuit, but has admitted failings over the Panorama film. The broadcaster has apologized for the Trump edit, with chair Samir Shah describing it as an “error of judgment.” He added: “We accept the way the speech was edited did give the impression of a direct call for violent action.” CEO Threatens To Leave California If Suit Isn’t Settled; AG Calls It “Blackmail” Nicholas Hoult Joins ‘Harry Potter’ As Gilderoy Lockhart For Season 2 ‘Brand New Day’ To Hit $700M U.S. Wednesday; ‘End Of Oak Street’ Due Friday ‘Bourbon & Lies’ Series Based On Books In Works At MGM TV Read More About: Comments

The streamer dropped first-look photos from the set of the upcoming series, which is set to debut in 2027, and announced that Scott Bakula, Logan Marshall-Green and Alex MacIsaac have joined the cast as series regulars. The show’s also added a crop of recurring characters including Bryan Greenberg as Cliff Barnes, Chelsea Fields as Alice Hansen, Patrick Gallagher as principal Montgomery, Alison Araya as Joan Garcia, Aman Smardon as Kai Becker, Krista Bridgers as Frankie Ryder and Ben Cotton as Mr. Marchbanks. articles.title: Chris Evans Teases “Brutal” ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Storyline for Captain America
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 10, 2026 7:03pm Chris Evans Jesse Grant/Getty Images for Disney Logo text There are still several months before Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters, but that didn’t stop Chris Evans from giving fans a little teaser. During a recent Q&A at Fan Expo Boston over the weekend, the actor, who reprises his role as Steve Rogers/ Captain America in the upcoming Marvel blockbuster, said that his character’s storyline is “brutal.” “The Russos love beating up Steve Rogers,” Evans said of the Russo Brothers, who are helming Doomsday . “Their favorite thing to do is to just beat the crap out of him. To them, that’s what makes a hero, and that’s someone who gets punched so many times but still gets up. So they keep finding new ways to kick his butt. And this one was brutal.” Related Stories Movies Disney Predicts 'Spider-Man' Record Opening "Bodes Well" for 'Avengers: Doomsday' Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Soars to $355M for Second-Biggest Opening Weekend Ever In addition to Evans, the upcoming film’s stacked cast includes many Marvel superheroes from the legacy Avengers and X-Men to the Thunderbolts and The Fantastic Four. They’re all expected to team up to face off against villain Doctor Doom, played by Robert Downey Jr. While chatting with People at Comic-Con 2026 last month , directors Anthony and Joe Russo said they knew Downey Jr. was perfect for the villain role once they heard the voice the Oscar winner had crafted for the character. “That was something that Robert surprised us with one day,” Anthony recalled. “You know, we were talking about all the details of the character — the voice, of course, is a key part of it, especially in the mask.” “So one day I think it was in the trailer, we were just sort of talking about some ideas and he broke out into the voice. And we knew at that moment, that was it,” he added. Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters Dec. 18. THR

articles.title: ‘Camp Rock 3’ Director on Bringing the Jonas Brothers Back — and Those Surprise Star Cameos
articles.full_text: Skip to main content From left: Liamani Segura and Malachi Barton in 'Camp Rock 3.' Disney/David Astorga Logo text [This story contains spoilers from Camp Rock 3. ] It’s been 16 years since viewers got their last look at Camp Rock. Disney Channel’s two Camp Rock films, starring the Jonas Brothers and Demi Lovato , were released in 2008 and 2010. They made a star out of Lovato and gave the Jonas Brothers — Kevin, Joe and Nick — even more exposure and fueled their rise to global superstars. Camp Rock and Camp Rock 2: The Final Jam rank among the Top 10 Disney Channel Original Movies of all time. Related Stories TV 'Camp Rock 3' Surprise! Demi Lovato Reprises Role as Mitchie in Disney's Movie TV 'Descendants' Franchise Expands With Movie Featuring Iconic Disney Sidekicks Now, Disney Channel and Disney+ are reviving the franchise with Camp Rock 3, which finds the Jonas Brothers returning as the band Connect 3, who are now looking for a new opening act. Of course, they head back to Camp Rock to discover the next big thing. Hot up-and-comers (and Disney favorites) Liamani Segura ( Descendants : Wicked Wonderland ) and Malachi Barton ( Zombies 4: Dawn of the Vampires ) star in the new movie, along with Lumi Pollack, Sherry Cola, Hudson Stone, Casey Trotter, Brooklynn Pitts and Ava Jean. And Maria Canals-Barrera reprises her role as Connie, mom to Mitchie Torres, played by Lovato in the first two films. From left: Liamani Segura, Hudson Stone, Casey Trotter, Malachi Barton and Lumi Pollack in Camp Rock 3. Disney/David Astorga Veronica Rodriguez (Disney’s The Slumber Party) , who directed the movie, says she made a conscientious effort to strike a balance between keeping the tone of the original films while also updating the sensibility for today’s audience. “Even when I first went out to be the director of this movie, I knew immediately that that was going to be my Mount Everest,” she says. “I needed to make a movie that simultaneously satisfied the new Camp Rockers and the nostalgia campers like myself who grew up with the franchise and know it and love it so much and hold it as a beloved piece of DCOM [Disney Channel Original Movies] canon, just really threading that needle of making a movie that is enjoyable and fun.” She began thinking of the movie as “ Camp Rock Plus. ” “I wanted to take everything we know and love about the original Camp Rock movies and ‘plus’ them up in every way that I could,” which meant everything from the costumes to the characters. “These are kids in the arts,” she continues. “I wanted them to have a personality in how they dressed and their personalities.” From left: Kevin Jonas , Joe Jonas and Nick Jonas in Camp Rock 3. Disney/David Astorga Part of that effort was also reflected in the musical numbers, which feature everything from big group dances to quieter acoustic tunes. “Even the musical numbers, I wanted to ‘plus’ those up a bit and not have off of them just be the kids dancing around the campground,” Rodriguez adds. “I was like, how can I make those feel different and have each one be unique?” To that end, the songs incorporate several musical genres, she notes, which is a reflection of the pop charts themselves that also feature a variety of genres. (The soundtrack will be released Friday, while Barton and Segura also will be performing some of these songs on the upcoming Worlds Collide Concert Tour, featuring stars from the Descendants, Zombies and Camp Rock franchises.) Given how the Jonas Brothers and Lovato’s careers blew up after the release of the first movie, Rodriguez expects the same thing to happen with Segura and Barton, who are already wildly popular with the tween crowd. Segura “is on the Demi [Lovato] track,” she says. “That girl has the voice of an angel and a heart of gold and talent beyond measure.” Barton, meanwhile, is going to be “the next Zac Efron,” she predicts, adding that he learned to play guitar for Camp Rock 3 . “The cast is insanely talented.” Demi Lovato with the Jonas Brothers in Disney’s 2008 musical film Camp Rock . Bob D’amico/©Disney Channel/Courtesy Everett Collection Speaking of Lovato, she makes a surprise appearance in the film, which has been kept top secret until now. We won’t spoil more about her appearance here, but Rodriguez said there were thoughtful discussions with Lovato, who also served as an executive producer, about how to bring Mitchie back while not taking away from the newer generation of stars. “We wanted to find the right balance of how much she should be in the film and what Mitchie’s involvement looked like,” Rodriguez says. “Her character literally says in the movie, to her mom, ‘This isn’t about me, it’s about them. It’s their time to shine. This is the new generation of campers.’ With Mitchie and Connect 3, we wanted them to be ingrained and necessary for the story but also leave enough room and space for the world to fall in love with the new generation of campers.” Another surprise star cameo comes in the form of Zombies franchise alum (and Barton’s co-star in the fourth movie) Milo Manheim , who turns up as a songwriting pro helping to instruct the campers. “Milo passed the Zombies torch to Malachi, and they’re buds,” Rodriguez says. “We were over the moon when it ended up working out for Milo to come play with us. It’s a really fun, meaningful cameo.” She said it was also heartwarming to see Manheim, along with the Jonas Brothers and Lovato, helping to mentor the younger talent on-set, such as guiding them on how to navigate social media. The Jonas Brothers also were executive producers on the movie, and Rodriguez says they were “very hands-on” throughout the process, including the production and creative on a song that Connect 3 performs in the movie. Fans of the original will likely spot some throwbacks to the first two films. Cola, who plays Connect 3’s tour manager, lands a funny line during a hip-hop class that calls back to the original (hint: it has something to do with hats), while Mitchie’s songwriting book introduced in the first film plays a role in the story. In addition, the antagonist of the story, Maddie (played by Ava Jean), was modeled in the vein of Tess (Meaghan Martin) from the original movies, giving “the most lovable mean girl vibes that take us back to the past,” Rodriguez adds. Rodriguez was also happy to bring Canals-Barrera back for a third go-round. The camp’s former head cook and Mitchie’s mom is now the camp director: “She’s the ultimate camp mom.” After the first table read, “everyone in the room loved it and we put more Connie in the movie because she brings such good energy.” From left: Maria Canals-Barrera and Liamani Segura in Camp Rock 3. Disney/David Astorga Today’s audience is quite different from that of 16 years ago. Rodriguez says there was a conscious choice to incorporate what kids today are dealing with, including a scene showing the campers having their phones taken away so they can be more present. “I am a very big proponent of face-to-face communication, hanging out with your friends together, not on devices,” she says. “My hope is that kids watch this, and they like want to go jam with their friends in person and listen to music and sing and dance and just create, create memories. As amazing as technology can be, sometimes just that human-to-human, friend-to-friend, kid-to-kid interaction that can be life-changing.” Rodriguez is excited for fans to watch the movie. “It was such an honor to be able to bring back a beloved franchise like this, and I did not take that responsibility lightly,” she says. “I gave this movie a lot of care and heart and, you know, effort and love. Everyone involved really worked hard and I think succeeded in making a movie that will satisfy all generations. It just feels like pure joy.” Camp Rock 3 premieres at 8 p.m. ET/PT Thursday on Disney Channel and the next day on Disney+. Watch the trailer below. Rodriguez directs from a script by Eydie Faye. The movie is produced by Disney Kids & Family and features choreography by Jamal Sims. Tim Federle executive produces, along with the Jonas brothers, Lovato, Betsy Sullenger, Spencer Berman and Gary Marsh, with a “special thanks” to Alan Sacks for his contribution to the Camp Rock franchise. THR

articles.title: Ann Hui to Receive Busan Film Festival’s Camellia Award
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All August 10, 2026 9:34pm Ann Hui Busan Film Festival Ann Hui , the Hong Kong New Wave pioneer whose films have chronicled the lives of her city’s ordinary and overlooked for nearly half a century, will receive the 2026 Camellia Award at the Busan International Film Festival , presented in partnership with Chanel. The 79-year-old director will accept the prize — awarded to filmmakers who have advanced the standing of women in the industry — at the festival’s opening ceremony on Oct. 6 at the Busan Cinema Center. “In my previous years I felt unwilling to receive such taking-stock prizes because I wished to continue making movies,” Hui said in a statement. “Now that I’m nearly eighty and find it difficult to make a film, I think the prize comes just in time for me to appreciate it more.” Related Stories Movies James Gray Rejects Men Not Being "Allowed to Engage With the Tender Side" Movies Keke Palmer, Deepa Mehta, Jacob Tremblay, and Jeremy Irons Projects Set for TIFF Financing Market Since her 1979 debut The Secret , Hui has directed 27 features and two feature-length documentaries. Her work helped define the Hong Kong New Wave, with films that move across genres but return to her perennial theme — the struggles of everyday life at the margins, portrayed without sentiment: Vietnamese refugees in Boat People (1982), a daughter’s reckoning with her Japanese mother in Song of the Exile (1990), the small dignities of working-class life in The Way We Are (2008), an aging servant and the family she raised in A Simple Life (2011). Hui is already one of the most decorated directors of her generation. She has won best director at the Hong Kong Film Awards six times, more than any filmmaker in the ceremony’s history, and three times at Taiwan’s Golden Horse Awards. Twice — with Summer Snow in 1995 and A Simple Life in 2011 — her work swept best film, director, actor and actress at the Hong Kong awards. In 2020, she became the first female director to receive Venice’s Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement, sharing that year’s honor with Tilda Swinton. She was previously honored in Busan in 2014 as the Asian Filmmaker of the Year. Established in 2024, the Camellia Award takes its name from a flower that is both Busan’s civic emblem and, famously, Gabrielle Chanel’s favorite. Korean production designer Ryu Seong-hie ( Oldboy , Decision to Leave ) was its inaugural recipient, followed last year by Taiwanese actress and filmmaker Sylvia Chang. “I am so happy to return to Busan,” Hui added, “and meet an audience that is among the most savvy and cinematically literate in the world.” Hui will be honored alongside Michelle Yeoh, this year’s Asian Filmmaker of the Year, at a ceremony hosted by Pachinko star Kim Minha. The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15. THR

articles.title: European Broadcast Giant RTL Group Bets on Streaming to Fuel Growth
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All August 10, 2026 11:00pm RTL Group CEO Clement Schwebig Boris-Breuer RTL Group , Europe’s largest television conglomerate, is going full in on streaming. First half figures at RTL, released Tuesday, showed sharp growth in revenues — up 27.2 percent to was up 27.2 per cent to $345 million (€299 million) — in the company’s streaming platforms, including RTL+ in Germany and M6+ in France. The boost made up for declines in RTL’s traditional TV business, where TV advertising revenue fell 4 percent and its production operations, at subsidiary Fremantle , were down 7.7 percent year on year at $964 million (€835 million). (RTL said business at Fremantle would pick up by year end with the roll out of new productions, including its Baywatch reboot ). Related Stories Movies James Gray Rejects Men Not Being "Allowed to Engage With the Tender Side" Movies Keke Palmer, Deepa Mehta, Jacob Tremblay, and Jeremy Irons Projects Set for TIFF Financing Market “Our streaming businesses deliver strong profitability,” said RTL Group CEO Clément Schwebig in a statement. “Sreaming revenue and paid subscriptions continue to grow dynamically. As a result, streaming is now expected to contribute around €100 million ($115 million) to our full-year operating profit.” RTL’s results are the first since it’s acquisition of pay-TV group Sky Deutschland from Comcast closed June 1. The deal will see Sky Deutschland merge with RTL+, creating a streaming operating with 12.4 million paid subscriptions across Germany, Austria and Switzerland, “We are now the clear number three in the German-speaking streaming market,” said Schwebig, who called the Sky Deutschland deal “transformational” for RTL. “We confirm our target to deliver € 250 million ($289 million) in annual synergies within three years. Our transformation strategy is delivering tangible results, and we are executing it with speed and discipline. Including the effects from the Sky Deutschland acquisition, we expect to grow to between €7.1 billion and €7.2 billion ($8.2 billion – $8.3 billion) in full-year revenue with an adjusted EBITA of €725 million ($837 million).” RTL’s Sky Deutschland acquisition is part of a broader wave of consolidation across the European broadcasting market. Last month, Comcast‘s Sky in the U.K. inked a $2.13 billion (£1.6 billion) deal to acquire the media and entertainment (M&E) unit of commercial broadcast giant ITV. Last year, MediaForEurope (MFE), the TV group controlled by the Berlusconi family, took majority control of ProSiebenSat.1, Germany’s number two commercial TV group, adding to MFE’s European network stable, that already includes Italy’s largest broadcaster, Mediaset, and Spain’s No. 1 commercial network Telecinco. The merger mania is on the production side too. On July 9, French production giant Banijay, producers of Peaky Blinders , Big Brother , and MasterChef , joined up with and U.K. production powerhouse All3Media ( The Traitors , Squid Game: The Challenge ) in a deal with an enterprise value of $8 billion. French broadcaster TF1 has reportedly put its production and distribution arm, Studio TF1, on the market. A sale the division, formerly known as Newen Studios, could fetch up to $450 million. And ITV Studios, producers of Love Island and I’m a Celebrity…Get Me Out of Here! , newly independent in the wake of ITV network’s sale to Sky, could also be a takeover target, as well as a potential buyer. All across Europe, the television industry is scrambling to get big quick to avoid dying at the hands of competition from YouTube and the global streaming giants. THR

articles.title: ‘Congo Boy’ Is an Autobiographical and Musical Refugee Drama. Its Director Has More in the Works.
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 11, 2026 12:01am 'Congo Boy' Courtesy of Trigon Film Robert is a 17-year-old Congolese refugee in Bangui, the capital of the Central African Republic (CAR). After his parents are imprisoned, he must care for his four younger siblings while striving to become a musician. That is the story of Congo Boy from director Rafiki Fariala. But it is also his, or at least inspired by his personal story. The landmark co-production by the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the CAR, which world premiered in the Un Certain Regard competition of the Cannes Film Festival, where it won its star Bradley Fiomona Dembeasset the best actor honor in the session, is now unspooling on the big outdoor square in Switzerland, namely the Piazza Grande as part of the 79 th edition of the Locarno Film Festival , on Tuesday, Aug. 11. Related Stories Movies James Gray Rejects Men Not Being "Allowed to Engage With the Tender Side" Movies Keke Palmer, Deepa Mehta, Jacob Tremblay, and Jeremy Irons Projects Set for TIFF Financing Market Congo Boy ‘s cast is led by Dembeasset and also features Christy Djomanda Louba, Pétruche Mbomba, Rosiana Kotozia, Gloria Ambacko and Dieufera Sana. The screenplay was written by Fariala, Tommy Baron and Boris Lojkine. Adrien Lallau handled the cinematography, with editing by César Simonot. The autobiographical film – Fariala is the son of Congolese parents, based in the CAR and a self-taught musician – previously made the 2022 documentary We, Students! , in which he turned the camera on himself and his friends to capture everyday student life at Bangui University. Congo Boy is a production of Mahongo Films in the CAR, co-produced by Kiripifilms in the DRC, which is the company of filmmaker Dieudo Hamadi ( Kinshasa Makambo , Downstream to Kinshasa ), and France’s Unité. You may wonder just how autobiographical the movie is. “It is really my own story, told through Robert, played by Bradley,” Fariala told THR via a translator just before the film’s world premiere. “When you see in the film that Robert is shot at, I was actually shot at.” The same is true for Robert’s stay with a colonel and his participation in a talent show, co-organized by UNICEF, among other things. ‘Congo Boy’ Courtesy of Cannes Film Festival The filmmaker sees his experience as a refugee as something that reflects the lives of many people around the world and is showcased in the film. “My family fled the Congo because there was war there, and when we got to the Central African Republic, war started there, too,” Fariala explained. “They wanted to be in a country that was more at peace to protect their family. So they were thinking of going to Benin and then on to Europe to have some stability for our future. But unfortunately, they had passports and their refugee card that showed a different country, so they got arrested.” After We, Students! was censored in the CAR, he had to go into exile in France, again as a refugee. “We often speak about refugees who want to go to Europe, but there are a lot of people who are refugees within different countries of Africa,” as the film shows, said the director. “And I want to convey that refugees are not beggars. They have to leave their home because this world is really crazy because of human destruction. But the young ones still want to fight; they still have hopes and dreams. I am proud to be a refugee.” How did the director find his cast to tell a very personal story? “We did some street casting,” he recalled, highlighting that he added a French casting director to his Central African Republic crew to find the lead actor. “He’s my double,” emphasized Fariala. “It took months. I started looking into young singers on the music scene, but they lacked charisma. So I went to look for Congolese refugees, and we went to cultural centers in different neighborhoods. At this school at 6 a.m., we auditioned 50 young boys, including Bradley, and he was so different from the others. He was reserved and smiling, but he had something in common with me. He liked to sing and rap, but only in his bedroom, because his father didn’t want to hear anything about art. His father just wanted his son to do well in school, like mine. So I gave him an improv exercise about failing his high school degree, and it was very different from the others.” Fariala was convinced that the young man was the right person to play the lead role. “But I had to talk to his parents, who didn’t agree at first,” he shared with THR . “So I had to be very persuasive.” ‘Congo Boy’ Courtesy of ‘Congo Boy’ – Makongo Films/Unité/Kiripifilms/Karta Film/Canal+ The rest of the cast is also made up of non-professional actors. And many portray their real-life experience, such as soldiers appearing in the film as soldiers, and Fariala’s aunt playing herself. That plays into the filmmaker’s interest in both documentary and fiction, and in mixing the two in his films. “I started out in documentary, but I always like to add a layer of fiction into my documentaries,” he told THR . And Congo Boy is a fictionalized version of his own life, with the reliance on a non-professional cast adding another layer of documentary vibe, he noted. What’s next for Fariala? “For my next projects, whether they are documentary or fiction, I want to keep doing that,” mixing genres, the filmmaker told THR . “I have another documentary that I started filming before Congo Boy . It’s called To Live and is about one year of my life after We, Students! was released and was censored in the Central African Republic and I had to go into exile in France.” What awaits audiences? “I was a bit lost in France,” the creative shared. “I was lonely, and I didn’t know how to talk to people, how to interact, and so I felt homesick. And I filmed myself to live. The camera became my friend; it kept me busy. At the same time, my little sister was sending me footage of the family back home, which helped me really hang in there. So, this will be my next film.” But Fariala has more in the works. “I have written another fiction film which could be a sequel to Congo Boy , because of this character of Robert,” he told THR . “I want to see what happens when he has become a musician and when he becomes famous and how, when he’s accepted in the Central African Republic, he is going to live with success. I want to keep digging into that.” THR

articles.title: ‘The End of Oak Street’: First Reactions
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 11, 2026 1:39am (L-r) Ewan McGregor as Greg Platt and Anne Hathaway as Denise Platt in The End of Oak Street, A Warner Bros. Pictures release. Courtesy Warner Bros. Pictures Logo text Warner Bros. held a series of press screenings for its high concept sci-fi survival feature The End of Oak Street in the last few days, and the early reaction on social media suggests the studio may, finally, have a film to get it out of its box office rut in 2026. The logline for The End of Oak Street reads, “After a mysterious cosmic event rips Oak Street from suburbia and transports their neighborhood to someplace unknown, the Platt family soon discovers that their very survival depends on them sticking together as they navigate their now unrecognizable surroundings.” Related Stories Movies J.J. Abrams on 'The End of Oak Street' Theories and Daughter Gracie's Acting Debut: "I Know How Hard She's Working" Movies Anne Hathaway on Her Jam-Packed Year of Movies and Upcoming Adaptation of Hit Novel 'Yesteryear' Anne Hathaway , Ewan McGregor , Maisy Stella and Christian Convery star as the Platt family. The cast also includes P. J. Byrne and Chris Coy. The film was written, directed and produced by David Robert Mitchell , the filmmaker behind the highly rated 2014 horror film It Follows and A24’s 2018 black comedy Under the Silver Lake . Notably, The End of Oak Street is produced by J.J. Abrams as well as Hannah Minghella, Jon Cohen, Matt Jackson and Tommy Harper. There has been some online chatter that The End of Oak Street is secretly connected to Abrams’ Cloverfield franchise. Alas, Abrams shot down the speculation “The only connection to our Cloverfield movies is that Ewan’s partner is Mary Elizabeth Winstead, who was the star of 10 Cloverfield Lane , who we were very lucky to get to work with and who I adore,” Abrams told The Hollywood Reporter . “So there was that, but other than that, people are just making connections that they happen to see.” Full reviews of The End of Oak Street are embargoed until Aug. 12, ahead of the film’s wide theatrical release on Aug. 14. For Warners, there’s an added pressure for The End of Oak Street to succeed at the box office. The studio had a stellar 2025, when Sinners , A Minecraft Movie , Superman , Final Destination Bloodlines , Weapons and One Battle After Another all made hay at the global box office —and in the case of Sinners and OBAA dominated the Oscars. However, Warners has struggled this year, with The Bride! , Mortal Kombat II and Supergirl all proving to be huge bombs at the box office, with only Wuthering Heights finding any success. articles.title: RTL Boss Clement Schwebig on the Hybrid Future of European TV: “Scale Is Essential”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All August 11, 2026 1:45am RTL Group CEO Clement Schwebig Boris-Breuer Get big or die trying has become the strategy of Europe’s traditional broadcasters. Merger mania is everywhere. Last month, Comcast‘s Sky signed a $2.13 billion (£1.6 billion) deal to acquire British commercial broadcast giant ITV . Last year, MediaForEurope (MFE), the TV group controlled by the Berlusconi family, took majority control of German commercial network ProSiebenSat.1, adding to its pan-European conglomerate that includes Mediaset, Italy’s largest broadcaster, and Spain’s top commercial network Telecinco. The reasoning behind this consolidation is simple. European TV companies, seeing a decline in traditional advertising and fierce competition from streaming companies and online video giants like YouTube, have realized scale matters. If they are not to be wiped out completely, legacy broadcasters need to shift their business online — to digital ad and streaming subscription models — while staying big enough to still be profitable. Related Stories Movies 'Congo Boy' Is an Autobiographical and Musical Refugee Drama. Its Director Has More in the Works. Business European Broadcast Giant RTL Group Bets on Streaming to Fuel Growth RTL Group , Europe’s largest television company, is also playing the merger game. In June, RTL, which owns production giant Fremantle and is itself a subsidiary of German media conglomerate Bertelsmann, closed its acquisition of Comcast’s German pay-TV operation Sky Deutschland, folding it into its RTL+ streaming service. The combined platform, with 12.4 million paid subscriptions, is now the third-largest streamer in German-speaking Europe, behind Netflix and Amazon Prime. In France, where RTL owns commercial channel M6, it is investing heavily in its streaming platform M6+. First-half 2026 figures at RTL, released Tuesday , show how quickly the company is pivoting to streaming. Revenue growth in the division, up 27.2 percent to $345 million (€299 million) made up for the fall off in RTL’s traditional TV business. The shift to streaming is “already far advanced,” says RTL Group CEO Clement Schwebig, “Streaming is no longer an investment story for RTL Group, it is a profitability story.” Speaking to The Hollywood Reporter , Schwebig outlined RTL’s strategy for survival in a transforming TV business — and why he believes consolidation, combined with a hybrid model of free TV, pay TV and streaming, is the only way European media companies can build the scale to compete with the global platforms. “The future is not linear versus streaming,” he says. “The future is exclusive, local content distributed across every platform where our audiences want to spend their time.” RTL is quickly transitioning its traditional free-to-air ad model to streaming. How rapid do you see this transition and what role do you see free-to-air playing in RTL’s business model in the future? The transformation is already far advanced. Streaming is no longer an investment story for RTL Group, it is a profitability story. Our streaming businesses will contribute around €100 million ($115 million) to our operating profit this year. This is a turning point in our operation after years of carefully investing in content and “tech infrastructure,” streaming is now a high-margin contributor and high-growth segment at the same time. Our strategy is to combine the strengths of free TV, pay TV and streaming, of advertising, subscription and distribution revenues into one powerful ecosystem with unmatchable reach. Following the acquisition of Sky Deutschland, we now have 12.4 paid subscriptions in the German-speaking region – this brings us in striking distance to Netflix and Amazon in this market. In June alone, our advertising sales house had a net reach of almost 69 million across all media, reaching 87 percent of all persons in Germany. Linear TV is and will remain the backbone to reach such mass audiences. What are the content implications of this shift – what will the focus of RTL’s acquisition and production spending be going forward? The future is not linear versus streaming. The future is exclusive, local content distributed across every platform where our audiences want to spend their time. That is exactly where RTL is positioned: no other European media company produces so much local content at scale as we do. We have something that very few companies have: brands that speak to our local audiences and create an emotional connection with them – some of them even every day. Think of our news or long-running daily drama such as Good Times, Bad Times . Investing in premium sports is key to strengthening our linear TV channels and gaining users for our streaming services. Just look at the football World Cup 2026: 94 percent of French people watched the competition on M6 or M6+, almost the entire population. A huge figure and powerful demonstration for the strength of our brands. In Germany, the Bundesliga and German Cup competition will continue to excite fans across Sky and [streaming platform] Wow – with some selected matches also broadcast on our flagship channel RTL. The proposed sale of TF1’s production division Studio TF1 has reignited speculation that TF1 could make another bid for M6. How would you view such a bid, and how core is the French network to RTL’s business? Groupe M6 is a highly valuable, strategic asset for RTL Group and one of the best-managed media companies in Europe. We have been one of the founders and a committed shareholder since the launch of M6 in 1987. The long-term success of the company is close to our hearts at RTL. As we said repeatedly over the past years: we continue to believe that consolidation is necessary if European media companies want to compete effectively with global technology and streaming platforms. And we remain convinced that market consolidation will also happen in France sooner or later. Otherwise, the global players will dominate the European markets. I am very confident that Groupe M6 will play a key role in any further consolidation in the French media industry. The management team has taken some big bets to gain audience shares, and they are working out well – most prominently Cyril Hanouna on W9 and the football World Cup this year with record ratings. M6 has the youngest audience among the major French channels, and this makes its programme brands very attractive for advertisers. It shows how successful the management transition to David Larramendy and his team has been. That being said, any significant consolidation move requires a change of the current French media law – and positive signals from the regulators. What is Fremantle’s M&A strategy – are ITV Studios and Studio TF1 (if put up for sale) potential targets? Fremantle’s M&A strategy is very clear. We are focused on IP-driven acquisitions of small and medium-sized production companies that strengthen our position in attractive genres and geographies. We see only limited scale returns for large mergers in the content production space. Large transactions among content producers are often complex and produce limited synergies. As a matter of principle, we do not comment on specific companies or market speculation. Fremantle is one of top three independent production companies worldwide. It combines scale, a highly diversified business model across genres, markets and customers with strong profitability, reaching its target of a 9 percent profit margin this year. With beloved, long-lasting IP such as Got Talent , Farmer Wants A Wife and Baywatch , Fremantle has a proven track record in creating long-term monetisation opportunities through distribution, local adaptations and digital platforms. We are also excited about pursuing new opportunities in adjacent businesses, for example with sports content and in the larger creator economy. THR

articles.title: ‘The State of Us’: Samuel Bottomley Breaks Callum Scott Howells Out of Hospice for One Final Hurrah in Edinburgh-Bound Indie (Exclusive Clip)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All August 11, 2026 3:00am Callum Scott Howells and Samuel Bottomley lead 'The State of Us' Courtesy of EIFF The Hollywood Reporter can unveil an exclusive clip from Ollie Gardner and Jake Harvey’s The State of Us , ahead of its premiere in competition at Edinburgh International Film Festival on Friday. Led by California Schemin ‘s Samuel Bottomley and It’s a Sin breakout star Callum Scott Howells , the British indie follows a boisterous tearaway called Frankie (Bottomley), who is struggling to come to terms with the inevitability of losing his best friend Taylor (Howells) to cancer. Frankie impulsively breaks Taylor out of hospice care for one final night of fun and debauchery, but what promises to be a night of hedonism quickly becomes something much more complicated. Related Stories Business RTL Boss Clement Schwebig on the Hybrid Future of European TV: "Scale Is Essential" Movies 'Congo Boy' Is an Autobiographical and Musical Refugee Drama. Its Director Has More in the Works. In the clip, Bottomley’s character can be seen cajoling Howells’ Taylor into having a drink and letting loose at a house party. On the dance floor, Taylor feels some semblance of relief as he reconnects with his childhood best friend. The characters in The State of Us are loosely based on Harvey’s childhood friendship group, in particular a friend called Jake Andrews, who died from cancer at the age of 18. Harvey and Gardner first met at university before pursuing careers in the arts — Harvey in TV, Gardner in theater — and with this movie, make their feature-length debuts. Co-starring with Bottomley and Howells are Frances Barber, Safia Oakley-Green, Seamus O’Hara, and Duggal Ram. Gardner told THR ahead of the film’s premiere: “I think it’d be quite nice for young men to see this film and see themselves in it from a perspective of, ‘Oh I can joke around and I know where the line is, but I also can really tap into the love that I feel for those male friendships.’ This is one very small seed that we’re trying to [plant] in the discourse of masculinity. We really want to dig into it because it’s such an incredibly complex and complicated theme.” Harvey added that he also hopes the humor lifts audiences heading to watch the film in the Scottish capital. “I think there’s a version of our film which was probably a bit more arthouse, a bit more serious, and more lends itself to that contemporary British type of independent cinema. But actually, [we’re] trying to do something that feels accessible,” he said. “It’s got its jokes and it’s dark humor, [and we hope] that it could actually reach the audience that it needs to speak to.” The 2026 Edinburgh International Film Festival runs from Aug. 14-21, and kicks off on Thursday with Louis Paxton’s The Incomer . Festival director Paul Ridd told THR he thinks it’s their greatest competition slate since they rebooted the event three years ago. “I’ve been very proud of everything we’ve done in 2024 [and] 2025… But this one, I think, is really kind of surpassing expectations.” Take a look at Samuel Bottomley and Callum Scott Howells in a clip from The State of Us below. THR

articles.title: Heritage Monday at the Locarno Film Festival Sees a Future in the Past
articles.full_text: Aug 10, 2026 11:12pm PT Heritage Monday at the Locarno Film Festival Sees a Future in the Past Young people are discovering black and white classics and 'feel the need to go back' to better understand how films were made, according to panelists By John Bleasdale Plus Icon John Bleasdale Guest Contributor Latest Heritage Monday at the Locarno Film Festival Sees a Future in the Past 4 hours ago Zoe Saldaña on Seeing ‘Terminator’ Aged 7, Having the Wrong-Shaped Feet and Wanting to Direct: ‘Give Me That Camera!’ 20 hours ago Protest at the Locarno Film Festival Remembers 60,000 Names of the Dead of Gaza 2 days ago See All Heritage Monday at the Locarno Film Festival Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival/Ti-Press Heritage Monday has become a popular fixture at the industry section of the Locarno Film Festival , reflecting the growing interest in film restoration and retrospective programming. This year’s edition was specifically devoted to the challenge of gaining new young audiences for older films. The panel, moderated by Sung Moon of the Jeonju International Film Festival, featured contributions from Leslie Vuchot of Timeless Cinema from France, Amy Homma from the Academy Museum of Motion Pictures and Academy Collection in the U.S., Arsenal Filminstitut’s Stefanie Schulte Strathaus from Germany and American author and programmer Eddie Muller from the Film Noir Foundation. Related Stories Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech: 'Actually the Greatest Compliment of All' CNN's Kaitlan Collins Was 'Not Surprised' Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech: 'That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office' “When we give the chance to younger people to speak about something, it’s almost never about a recent film,” Vuchot said, citing her experience in running Le Lucernaire cinema in Paris. “It’s about something that’s been transmitted, transferred, and that they want to share as well. […] Young people feel the need to go back, even if it’s from books and stuff, to how films were made, going back to the roots and understanding where filmmakers got their inspiration from.” Popular on Variety For Muller, host of TCM’s “Noir Alley,” the key has been to replicate the mid-20th century, film-going experience, with double features and ushers as part of the atmosphere. A virtuous circle is created as the proceeds from festivals are poured into restoring films which can then be shown at festivals. His role as a host on Turner Classic Movies has also proved a turning point, increasing his visibility. He has brought school classes into his festivals and followed it up with lessons in schools and seen how students who had never seen a black and white film before on the big screen reacted to Humphrey Bogart and Lauren Bacall in “To Have and Have Not.” Muller says: “In a class of 35 students, if you’re lucky, you’re going to connect with six that are really into it, and the other kids are using social media to ignore everything that you’re talking about. But those six are really connecting in a way that will make a difference to their lives.” Despite the ravages of TikTok, Homma argued for pragmatic optimism: “When we’re thinking of our audience, it’s so important for us to try and meet all of our audience members where they’re at, and not assume that they all understand that more cerebral motivation for why we go to a film.” One example to encourage engagement was to bring a real Dalmation — Pogo — to a screening of “101 Dalmations,” with an animator leading live-drawing classes and talking about the techniques used in the film. They also invited Guillermo del Toro to the museum and use the archive to illustrate his talk on films by Alfred Hitchcock. As well as repertory cinemas such as the Academy and Le Lucernaire presenting films, heritage is also proving popular in general distribution. “There’s an urgent need that comes really from the present,” Schulte Strathaus believes. “Heritage film offers so many potential futures, and in a time where we don’t see a future anymore or it’s hard to see a future, we go back into film history, and see all those told and untold and ignored narratives, all those could have beens like those other potential histories that we didn’t know about or that didn’t make it into the present, and that maybe could have led us into a better present.” Some problems were identified, such as the perennial need to secure funding whether from private donors or larger organizations or in a more grassroots way. Likewise, securing and even identifying rights continues to be a problem, which can even extend to subtitles, which might be copyrighted and need to be duplicated, causing unnecessary expenses. The solution proposed was more cooperation and coordination between archives, cinematheques and organizations internationally. Climate controlled archives are closing and even an internationally famous body such as the Motion Picture Academy is being overwhelmed by a growing amount of material while operating with the same number of staff and financial resources. “I’m a forever optimist,” Homma says. “We are seeing more people care about the films.” For Schulte Strathaus, who specializes in avant-garde film, the solution is to build communities who are not just audiences but who can creatively participate in the restorations, either for educational purposes or as artists helping in the preservation of filmmakers’ work. ‘Sholay’ to Make ‘Films in Concert’ World Premiere at London’s Royal Albert Hall Sony’s Indian Version of ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ Hosted by Amitabh Bachchan, Adds Google Gemini as AI Guide (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Gramado Film Festival Launches New Talent Drive
articles.full_text: Aug 10, 2026 11:21pm PT Gramado Film Festival Launches New Talent Drive The inaugural Residency for 60 young filmmakers will offer an intensive program running Aug. 17-19 By Marcelo Cajueiro Plus Icon Marcelo Cajueiro Latest Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities 3 hours ago Luiz Carlos Barreto, Brazil’s Legendary Film Producer, Dies at 98 3 weeks ago Brazil’s Gramado Fest Set to Honor ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello and ‘The Secret Agent’ Standout Maria Fernanda Cândido 3 weeks ago See All Marcio Fraccaroli, Veronica Stumpf and Silvio Guindane will headline masterclasses at the Gramado Residency Credit: Lucas Ramos, Guto Costa The first Residency for Young Filmmakers, a new feature of the Gramado Film Market taking place Aug. 17-19, will count with the participation of 60 filmmakers aged between 18 and 35, selected from more than 200 applications. Participants are required to have work experience on at least one film, mostly in the fields of production, direction, acting, screenwriting, cinematography or sound. Rio Grande do Sul, where Gramado is located, is the state with most participants: 28. The remaining come from the states of Bahia, Goiás, Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, Santa Catarina, Sergipe and Pernambuco, and the Federal District. Related Stories Don Lemon Asks Court to Drop Criminal Charges Against Him Related to Minnesota ICE Protest, Citing Donald Trump's Chronic 'Animus' Toward Journalist Katy Perry Slams Trump Administration for Using Song 'Firework' in Military Strikes Video: 'I Absolutely Do Not Condone It' The intensive three-day program includes a total of 17 sessions in the mornings and afternoons, and the attendance of the Gramado Film Festival ’s evening screenings. The first day features masterclasses on distribution, screenwriting and directing, covering subjects from narrative construction and creative choices to strategies for positioning films in different markets. The day’s program also includes a panel on public policies for the Brazilian audiovisual sector and an event dedicated to music scoring and sound recording. Popular on Variety Over Aug. 18-19, the focus is professional integration, production and changes in the audiovisual market, with panels on true crime, career internationalization, film societies and professional sustainability, as well as masterclasses on audiovisual production and post-production and a case study. The residency concludes with sessions on cinematography and environmental sustainability in productions. Paris Filmes ’ CEO Marcio Fraccaroli and Paris Entretenimento’s producer Veronica Stumpf will conduct the residency’s first masterclass, Distribution: Paths to Finding the Audience. São Paulo-based Paris is Brazil’s leading independent film distributor and a top producer of local pics. “The purpose of this masterclass is to show that distribution goes far beyond screening a film in movie theaters. It’s a strategic stage that begins with decisions about how the work will be positioned, understanding the target audience, developing the communication campaign and choosing the best release window,” Fraccaroli told Variety . “The idea is to share some of our experience to demonstrate how each decision can directly affect a film’s reach, cultural relevance and commercial performance.” Fraccaroli added he hopes to contribute to a conversation about the future of audiovisual distribution in a context of rapid changes in content consumption: “Understanding shifts in the market and developing increasingly intelligent distribution strategies will be essential to expand the reach of films and allow them to achieve their full potential.” Stumpf celebrated the Gramado fest’s decision to launch the residency initiative. “It is essential to discuss and encourage the training of new professionals in order to strengthen the Brazilian audiovisual sector,” she told Variety . “As it is constantly changing, the market increasingly demands knowledge, planning and strategic vision. Training filmmakers, producers and executives who are capable of understanding the entire audiovisual value chain is essential for Brazil to consolidate a stronger, more competitive industry that is prepared to engage with different audiences, both within the country and abroad.” Actor, director, producer, screenwriter and playwright Silvio Guindane will teach the masterclass Directing: Choices That Build the Film. Guindane has starred in dozens of films, telenovelas and series. He broke through as a director with the film “Mussum, o Filmis,” a biopic about comedian and musician Mussum. The feature premiered at the Gramado Film Festival in 2023, taking home awards for film, actor for Aílton Graça, supporting actress for Neusa Borges, supporting actor for Yuri Marçal, original score and the audience award. “Training new filmmakers is fundamental for the market,” Guindane told Variety . “Film is an industrial art because it involves so many people, and a film set is a big thing. But it’s also a handcrafted art. The filmmaker has the role of a conductor, which is to orchestrate talent, to manage, to draw from each department, each person in each department, including and especially the actors, the best they have to give to the characters and to the film as a whole.” ‘Sholay’ to Make ‘Films in Concert’ World Premiere at London’s Royal Albert Hall Sony’s Indian Version of ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ Hosted by Amitabh Bachchan, Adds Google Gemini as AI Guide (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities
articles.full_text: Aug 10, 2026 11:37pm PT Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities The gathering is part of the Gramado Film Market and discusses the audiovisual industry’s role as a development driver By Marcelo Cajueiro Plus Icon Marcelo Cajueiro Latest Gramado Film Festival Hosts the First International Meeting of Cities 3 hours ago Luiz Carlos Barreto, Brazil’s Legendary Film Producer, Dies at 98 3 weeks ago Brazil’s Gramado Fest Set to Honor ‘I’m Still Here’ Star Selton Mello and ‘The Secret Agent’ Standout Maria Fernanda Cândido 3 weeks ago See All Marcelo Pedrazzi, Maria Fernanda Galeano Rojo, Gabriel Portela and Letícia Friedrich, speakers at the Gramado Film Market. Courtesy Gramado Film Festival The First International Meeting of Cities will take place Aug. 12-14 at the Gramado Film Market and will gather municipal-level authorities from such major towns as Medellín, Rio de Janeiro, Porto Alegre, Maricá and fest-host Gramado as well as representatives of Brazilian and Ibero-American organizations to discuss how the creative economy — particularly the audiovisual industry — can contribute to social and economic development. The program will highlight the successful cases of the 2.4-million-strong city of Medellín, Colombia, and Gramado, a tourist town with 40,000 residents in Southern Brazil, said Ralfe Cardoso, general coordinator of the Gramado Film Market. Related Stories Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech: 'Actually the Greatest Compliment of All' Whitney Cummings' Donald Trump Sex Trafficking Joke Was Cut From Mark Twain Ceremony on Netflix; Streamer Says Kennedy Center Axed It Maria Fernanda Galeano Rojo , Medellín’s secretary of economic development, and Karla Valderrama, coordinator of the city’s film commission, will present in a panel the Colombian city’s experience in urban transformation — considered a model for other cities in Latin America — innovation, attracting audiovisual productions, and promoting economic and social development through the creative economy. Popular on Variety As for Gramado, Cardoso said the 54 consecutive annual editions of the film fest were a major driver turning the town into one of Brazil’s best-known tourist destinations. Gramado, in the mountains of Brazil’s southernmost state Rio Grande do Sul, offers European-inspired architecture, a strong gastronomic scene and several entertainment-themed complexes. “The growth of tourism in Gramado is connected to the film festival,” Cardoso told Variety . “It all began 54 years ago. Gramado today ranks as the country’s second tourism destination, behind only Rio de Janeiro. The film festival created that. It’s interesting, because it’s something that began with art.” The 10th edition of the Gramado Film Market will feature panels and pitching sessions, with the participation of execs from major companies such as Amazon MGM Studios, the Globo group’s Globo Filmes and streamer Globoplay , distributors Downtown Filmes, H2O Films and Vitrine Filmes , and Fernando Meirelles’ production company O2 Filmes . The Gramado Film Market’s forum will offer panels on key issues facing the local and international film and TV industries. Letícia Friedrich will present the panel Vitrine Filmes: Sponsorship, Investment, Circulation and Impact. Friedrich, a partner and director of Vitrine, will address how public policy, investment and distribution strategy can work together to strengthen indie cinema. Founded 15 years ago, Vitrine has built to become the leading distributor of Brazilian art features. The company distributed locally Kleber Mendonça’s “The Secret Agent,” which sold about 2.5 million admissions in the country, a spectacular performance for a Brazilian non-comedy art film. The panel’s theme is the company’s Vitrine Petrobras Session, a program sponsored by Brazil’s state-owned oil giant Petrobras. As part of the program, Vitrine has released more than 80 Brazilian films in sessions with affordable ticket prices and organized discussions, training activities and masterclasses in film societies, schools and cultural institutions. “Our project was created to democratize access to independent cinema by promoting Brazilian releases in commercial theaters across all regions of the country,” Friedrich told Variety . “Since 2023, the project has also invested in restoring and re-releasing classics of Brazilian cinema, reaffirming its commitment both to preserving the audiovisual memory and to promoting the country’s cinematic heritage.” Audiovisual public policy specialist Gabriel Portela will take part on the panel Future Perspectives for the Brazilian Audiovisual Industry. He will discuss the sector’s technological transformations, new consumption habits, changing financing models and distribution challenges. “The first question we need to address is developing strategies and policies so that Brazilian films can truly find its audience within the country. We cannot think about the development of our audiovisual industry without a strong domestic market,” Portela told Variety . Marcelo Pedrazzi, director and partner of Quanta, one of Brazil’s leading audiovisual infrastructure and services companies, will participate on the panel Innovations in the Audiovisual Process: Technology, Efficiency and New Production Workflows. He will provide a historical view of the technological evolution since the Lumière brothers’ first dedicated public screenings of moving images in 1895. “Over the past 25 years, the sector has undergone a major wave of transformation driven by innovation and technology. The advent of virtual production has opened the way to unprecedented worlds and new creative horizons,” he told Variety . ‘Sholay’ to Make ‘Films in Concert’ World Premiere at London’s Royal Albert Hall Sony’s Indian Version of ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ Hosted by Amitabh Bachchan, Adds Google Gemini as AI Guide (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments...
