articles.title: Locarno: The Filmmakers Behind ‘Piluk,’ From the National Film Board of Canada, Discuss the Language of Animation
articles.full_text: Aug 10, 2026 11:55pm PT Locarno: The Filmmakers Behind ‘Piluk,’ From the National Film Board of Canada, Discuss the Language of Animation Following the journey of a girl called Piluk, born with wings, the film has its world premiere at Locarno's Pardi di Domani section By Kambole Campbell Plus Icon Kambole Campbell Latest Locarno: The Filmmakers Behind ‘Piluk,’ From the National Film Board of Canada, Discuss the Language of Animation 3 hours ago Marco Bellocchio, Sally Wainwright Win Big at Italian Global Series Festival Which Celebrated ‘Star Trek’ and ‘Lost’ and Lamented Industry Crisis 4 weeks ago ‘Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan’ Recalled by Director Nicholas Meyer 1 month ago See All 'Piluk' directors Elisapie Isaac and Marc Séguin Credit: Éva Maude With a world premiere in the Locarno Film Festival ‘s Pardi di Domani selection of short and medium-length films, the filmmakers behind “Piluk” saw the production as a chance to tell a story with the simplest possible textures: pencil, paper and the human voice. Produced by Marc Bertrand and Jelena Popović of the National Film Board of Canada and directed by multidisciplinary artists and longtime friends Marc Séguin and Elisapie Isaac, “Piluk” was created from over 8,000 drawings using pen, charcoal and pencil and accompanied by a soundtrack of throat-singing. Related Stories Aymar Esse, Director of Locarno Open Doors World Premiere ‘My Father’s Kora,' Explores the Challenges of Queer Identity in Senegal Odd Slice Films Boards Documentary ‘Concrete Land’ Ahead of Locarno Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Piluk’ Courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada “I have the most immense respect for things that can be said with pencil and paper,” Séguin says in an interview with Variety. “ Given all the technology that surrounds us, I still think that not all has been said with paper and pencil. So we wanted to go back to that craftsmanship. I mean, if Eli’s on stage or she records something for this film, it’s her voice. We didn’t want machines to be involved or ask AI to get involved as well, we wanted to just draw it the old-fashioned way.” Popular on Variety The story follows the journey of a girl called Piluk, born with wings on her back, as she crosses the countryside, eventually arriving at an unnamed city, caring for different animals along the way. There’s no dialogue: everything is communicated by its animation and by the expressive vocals of the choral soundtrack. The scratchy, sketchy linework goes for an impression of people and places rather than strictly realistic representation; the backgrounds mostly stripped away. Isaac says that the same principles applied to the soundtrack: the musician, being from an Inuk background, has spoken previously about taking inspiration from traditions of oral storytelling. Isaac says that at first she had been content to collaborate with Séguin in pre-production, but that “[when] it became clear that we’re not gonna overproduce, we’re not gonna over-add,” she began to want to experiment with the human voice. She enjoyed the sense of ambiguity to the way the voices mix with the imagery, that it feels organic this way, Isaac says. “We ended up keeping it very minimalist. What came out is just trying to respect what’s going on in the image and the world.” The idea of allowing room for audiences to project something of their own meaning was important for both the visuals and the soundtrack. “I think that was the purpose,” Isaac says of her approach to the music, “to leave space for people to feel.” To Isaac, lyrics and actual words or even “perfect melody” would be too structured; they wanted unpredictability. Courtesy of the National Film Board of Canada Though Séguin is renowned for his painting and has worked in filmmaking before (as has Isaac — the two have even collaborated before on projects such as Séguin’s 2016 feature “Stealing Alice”), producer Jelena Popović, who took over from Bertrand during the project, points out that both are new to animation as a medium. So it became part of NFB’s responsibility to support the artists in new territory, preserving their voice in the adaptation to working in a new format. This is, in Popović’s eyes, something inherent to NFB’s structure. “We are allies of the artist in a sense that we’re not profit driven, we’re a public money-funded producer and distributor,” she says. Making sure the artists can navigate this new space is but a small part of maintaining a sense of their influence over the story, something which extends to the NFB’s commitment to producing work by Indigenous artists. “The NFB obviously has a commitment to producing work by Indigenous storytellers and artists,” Popović says. “Many other indigenous artists work with the NFB, and hopefully we decolonize the institution through all of this work,” she adds, after listing works by artists such as Terril Calder, Jeff Barnaby and Walter Scott. “So in working with Elisapie and Marc, like any other filmmaker, and especially Indigenous filmmakers, it’s important to preserve this narrative sovereignty of the auteur. We are there to help! We are not there to prescribe anything nor impose anything.” The team of animators at the NFB studio was led by Parissa Mohit (“an amazing filmmaker and animator,” Popović says). “Parissa was their advisor for animation directing, and also the head of the animation team. These amazing exchanges, like the finessing of mise-en-scène and creating that illusion of movement, were really discussed in detail with Parissa and our technical director Eric Pouliot and the rest of our technical experts in-house.” Popović highlights the goal of supporting artists and helping them achieve their specific creative vision, describing NFB as a “creative laboratory.” “Artists come to us with an idea, and we give them a playground to explore in the development phase, and do many kinds of explorations [which] are really not easy to get in the private commercial sector,” Popović says. “We are not based on return on investment.” For Popović, who has also produced shorts such as “Hedgehog’s Home,” “Manivald” and “Bread Will Walk,” the film being made in the way the artists envisioned is the real return on investment — something which stems from a passion and belief in animation as “the sum and the summit of all arts with a capital A.” This is because, as Popović puts it, animation is “using the language of all the visual arts,” folding theater, drama and music into a cinematic language. “At the same time it’s an economical way of storytelling which is painstakingly long to make: you have to start from stereotypes and archetypes because that’s the language you know, and especially in short film animation, you have to adapt yourself to that economy of storytelling.” In their approach to “Piluk,” co-directors Séguin and Isaac have found just that kind of economy: finding the maximum emotional impact with the most minimal of art styles and musical instruments. articles.title: ‘Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO’ Director Kamiyama Kenji Built His New Series Around a Metaphor for AI Fears: ‘Will We End Up Being Used by It?’
articles.full_text: Aug 11, 2026 12:00am PT ‘Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO’ Director Kamiyama Kenji Built His New Series Around a Metaphor for AI Fears: ‘Will We End Up Being Used by It?’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO’ Director Kamiyama Kenji Built His New Series Around a Metaphor for AI Fears: ‘Will We End Up Being Used by It?’ 3 hours ago ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day,’ ‘The Odyssey’ Battle Atop U.K., Ireland Box Office 3 hours ago Boxing Legend Chris John Joins Silver Media Group for Animated Series ‘Dragon’s Dojo’ (EXCLUSIVE) 9 hours ago See All ©SUNRISE Kamiyama Kenji says the alien threat driving his new “Gundam” anime is a direct metaphor for humanity’s uneasy relationship with artificial intelligence. The director, known for “Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex” and “The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim,” tells Variety he built “ Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO ” around that anxiety. The series follows Ray Azumi (voiced by Takeo Otsuka), a war orphan who awakens on the lunar surface as the pilot of the experimental mobile suit Gundam ZERO. The story begins decades after humanity is forced to abandon Earth in the face of a hostile, self-replicating ecosystem born from an alien object’s three revelations: gravity control, faster-than-light communication and cognitive materialization. Humanity marks the years since in a calendar counted from that exile. Related Stories Singapore's First Wuxia Film 'The House on the Moon' Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo 'Decided to Fully Embrace Genre' (EXCLUSIVE) 'Donkey Princess' Review: A Princess Escapes the Kingdom, but Not the Patriarchy, in an Inventive, Shape-Shifting Fairytale Kamiyama explains why he placed Ray in a world where that exile is simply the everyday condition rather than a recent trauma: “As I explored, at the setting stage, the idea that this world too has a time ‘before today,’ I came to feel that rather than spelling out the setting from scratch, it would enrich the story more to let viewers imagine and fill in for themselves what came before today.” Popular on Variety The new setting hinges on those three revelations turning catastrophic. Asked what that premise let him explore, Kamiyama says: “Can we truly master a technology we did not create ourselves, or will we end up being used by it? It is a metaphor for technologies that humanity is already beginning to struggle to handle in reality, such as AI.” When it comes to moving between giant, established mythologies like “Gundam,” “Star Wars” and Tolkien’s Middle-earth, Kamiyama strives to put his own spin on things while also staying true to what the fans want. “I try to prepare surprises while taking the utmost care not to stray from that consensus,” he says. “When that goes well, the sense of sharing the moment with the fans becomes the motivation to keep creating — that’s what I believe.” “Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO” also encompasses the companion video game, “Gundam Rogue Orbit.” “The project actually started from the game first, but the game side had no fixed setting in place, so I built out the world starting from the question of what Gundam fights,” Kamiyama says. He left the game’s mechanics to its own team, reasoning that “games have an appeal that only a game can deliver, the fun that comes from the gameplay and the controls.” To prepare a backstory for “Gundam Rogue Orbit,” Kamiyama had to work out what the monsters were, what they did to Earth and humanity, and how long it took for either side of the coming war to develop a countermeasure like Gundam. “Creating these fine details is, I’d say, both the hardest part and the real thrill of building a science fiction work,” he says. On what keeps pulling him back to stories about societies adapting to systems they can’t control, Kamiyama believes that “anti-war is a universal theme; even as the forms and meanings of war change with the times, it remains timeless.” He extends that idea to the current moment: “The true nature of war looks different from one era to the next. Perhaps it is the unease of the wars unfolding right now.” Building an era untethered from Gundam’s Universal Century or 00 timelines gave him that freedom, he says. On his approach to legacy IP after working with Tolkien and Lucasfilm’s properties, he says, “It was about choosing between what should be carried on and what should be built anew.” Kamiyama also reveals the scale of the world he has built beyond what “RG XARX-ZERO” itself shows. “At the very least, it stretches from 50 years before the point where this story begins to the start of another possible future that could connect to the game’s world 100 years later,” he says. For the science-fiction concepts underpinning that world, including gravity control, faster-than-light communication and cognitive materialization, Kamiyama worked with novelist Toh EnJoe, credited as SF setting supervisor, as an outside arbiter. “He is a master who rearranges words through mathematics, so whether or not to examine meaning became a source of creative inspiration,” Kamiyama says, describing EnJoe’s rulings on which ideas were plausible, needed more thought, or could be glossed over. Asked what he hopes is the first surprise for viewers meeting this world, Kamiyama says: “Gundam’s place within a body of work that has always had giant robots as its protagonists.” The director has spent two decades moving between franchises with devoted fan bases, from his breakout run steering “Ghost in the Shell: Stand Alone Complex” through its two seasons, to co-directing Netflix’s CG reboots of “Ultraman” and “Ghost in the Shell: SAC_2045” with Shinji Aramaki. His theatrical foray into Middle-earth with “The Lord of the Rings: The War of the Rohirrim” reached screens worldwide in 2024, and he now oversees the “Star Wars: Visions” universe as supervising director on its 2026 installment, which extends the story he introduced in “The Ninth Jedi.” “Mobile Suit Gundam RG XARX-ZERO,” produced by Bandai Namco Filmworks with animation from Sola Animation, launches in 2027. ‘Sholay’ to Make ‘Films in Concert’ World Premiere at London’s Royal Albert Hall Sony’s Indian Version of ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ Hosted by Amitabh Bachchan, Adds Google Gemini as AI Guide (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Pacifiction’ Director Albert Serra on His New Film ‘Sixteen Moments of My Life’ and Why He’d Love to Have Directed Elvis Presley
articles.full_text: Aug 11, 2026 12:09am PT ‘Pacifiction’ Director Albert Serra on His New Film ‘Sixteen Moments of My Life’ and Why He’d Love to Have Directed Elvis Presley ‘I want to do a ‘Brigadoon’-style musical comedy,’ Serra tells Variety at Locarno, where ’16 Moments of My Life’ world premieres By John Bleasdale Plus Icon John Bleasdale Guest Contributor Latest Heritage Monday at the Locarno Film Festival Sees a Future in the Past 4 hours ago Zoe Saldaña on Seeing ‘Terminator’ Aged 7, Having the Wrong-Shaped Feet and Wanting to Direct: ‘Give Me That Camera!’ 20 hours ago Protest at the Locarno Film Festival Remembers 60,000 Names of the Dead of Gaza 2 days ago See All Ingrid Caven in Sixteen Moments of My Life. Courtesy of the Locarno Film Festival Don’t call Albert Serra ’s new film, “Seize moments de ma vie” (“ Sixteen Moments of My Life ”), a concert film. Premiering out of competition at the Locarno Film Festival , the film documents a one-off performance by screen legend Ingrid Caven at the Théâtre des Bouffes du Nord in Paris. “I will never shoot a concert unless I’m involved in the music,” Serra told Variety . The band were Molforts, the Catalan musicians who provide Serra’s soundtracks and Caven has been friends with the Spanish director for over fifteen years. Famed for her performances in the sixties and seventies of many European film classics as well as being the muse and frequent collaborator of her sometime husband, Rainer Werner Fassbinder, Caven is also a recording artist and Serra requested that they collaborate together with the musicians writing the music sending it over on CDs and Caven improvising over the music. Related Stories CNN's Kaitlan Collins Was 'Not Surprised' Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech: 'That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office' Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread “Over the years the musicians and Caven wrote 16 songs, going back and forth. All this process, but they didn’t communicate directly. This is the point. They only communicate through the music itself. They didn’t talk.” Popular on Variety Not so much the director as the MC? “I had all these things in front of me, I could hardly see the stage.” This is how Serra also directs his films, such as “Liberté” and “Pacifiction.” “Everything is based on non-communication with the actors. I like when things happen without really working on meanings or on the outcome. Subconscious. Like old school Hollywood, you know, everybody has to do what they have to do, and we don’t need to discuss for hours. This was a similar concept.” The film continues Serra’s interest in performance. His last film, the documentary “Afternoons of Solitutde,” took as its subject a young and celebrated bullfighter and focused intently on him to the exclusion of everything else. So in “Sixteen Moments,” there are no cut-aways to the audience. “You have genius musicians on stage, and you want me to shoot some idiots watching them? No,” says Serra. The music is a mixture of autobiography sung in a way that drifts between opera, cabaret and Edith Piaff. At the very beginning we see Caven coughing before taking the stage. “Every performance is kind of life and death, and it’s unique: it’s fatality. Cinema is perfect for that, because cinema has the same logic. One moment of the film has passed, you cannot grab it, it’s passed. The experience of cinema, it’s the logic of live music or live performance. It has passed, and you cannot recover it. It’s very coherent with this fragility of creating musical life. You know that not everything is perfect. Not everything is under control always. And maybe this is part of the motion and the magic.” Having done a film on bullfighting and a singer, would there be another kind of performance he would like to document? “No, what would it be?” Serra says; then breaks into a grin. “I will do a musical comedy. This is something that has been a lot of times in my mind. I think I will end up doing it because I like this idea of musical comedy that’s positive. The spirit of something that is light: poetic and positive. Nowadays, with all this reality of the war and these problems and frictions and tensions and whatever, I’d like to make a “Brigadoon” style musical. Maximum happiness. The opposite of what I’ve been doing all of my life.” He also says that he wished he could’ve directed Maria Callas and Elvis Presley. “Elvis should have done dramatic roles, and with the right director, he would have been an amazing dramatic actor. And another idea I had was to make light comedies with Maria Callas, because she did only very very dramatic stuff with Pasolini. Very static like this opera and this intensity and this mythological stuff and very heavy. Why not make a comedy with her?” It might not be boasting. Serra’s films have featured some iconic performances, such as Jean-Pierre Léaud as Louis XIV in “The Death of Louis XIV” and Benoît Magimel in “Pacifiction.” Of the latter, Serra says: “It’s the best performance of his career. Whatever people say: no, this is the best performance. I know it. I’m 100% sure.” From Wednesday, Serra is back in the editing suite working on his new film “Out of This World” which he hopes to have completed by the end of the year. “It’s 65% done.” The film stars Riley Keough and F. Murray Abraham as part of an American delegation traveling to Russia in the context of the Ukraine war. “It’s not a war film, it’s about economics. You’ll see what happens in the film, where it goes at the end. It goes to the best scene of recent cinema. This I can tell you. So you will have to wait until the end.” That sounds like a headline. “Yes! And the second headline is ‘You will have to wait until the end.’” Albert Serra Copyright: Oscar Fernández Orengo ‘Sholay’ to Make ‘Films in Concert’ World Premiere at London’s Royal Albert Hall Sony’s Indian Version of ‘Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?’ Hosted by Amitabh Bachchan, Adds Google Gemini as AI Guide (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel Joins Short Film ‘Love Unlimited’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 11, 2026 1:58am PT ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel Joins Short Film ‘Love Unlimited’ (EXCLUSIVE) Frankel will star and also produce alongside his brother Max Mark Frankel for their MarcelMonique Pictures banner. By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest George MacKay, Louisa Harland, Nathalie Emmanuel and Eric Kofi Abrefa Join ‘The Animals’ From ‘Supacell’ Star Calvin Demba (EXCLUSIVE) 29 minutes ago ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel Joins Short Film ‘Love Unlimited’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Pippa Harris and James Wilson to Headline London Film Festival Industry Forum 24 hours ago See All Getty Images Fabien Frankel , currently seen on screens as the dashing, honor-obsessed knight Ser Criston Cole in “ House of the Dragon ,” is ready to take on a very different role. The British actor is set to star in “Love Unlimited,” the debut short drama from actor Olivier Huband (“A Discovery of Witches,” “Becoming Elizabeth”). Frankel will also serve as exec producer under his MarcelMonique Pictures banner, the company he runs with his brother Max Mark Frankel. Max Mark Frankel, who produced last year’s comedy feature “Our Hero, Balthasar,” will serve as lead producer on the project. Related Stories Locarno’s Alliance 4 Development Welcomes Queer Musical, Eco Body Horror and Bruce LaBruce’s Melodrama With Monica Bellucci and Béatrice Dalle 'I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming' Review: An Affecting Trans Relationship Drama Brings Fresh Perspective to the War in Ukraine Written and directed by Hubbard, who also stars, “Love Unlimited” is described as a “small, sincere window into the profound, complex relationship between two old friends — Max (Frankel) and Gabriel (Huband) — as they unknowingly spend a final four days together in Max’s house in the South of France. The film exists in the world of the unspoken, exploring themes of male intimacy, grief and, as the title suggests, the incandescent, enduring power of love.” Popular on Variety “Olivier sent me this script he had written about two best friends who spent their final summer together and we sat in my house and read it together and I found it immensely moving,” said Fabien Frankel, who as well as “House of Dragon” has also starred in “Task” and “The Serpent.” “It’s a subject incredibly close to my brother and I’s heart and we’re proud to get to be a part of it. It’s the first time I’ve acted in something I’ve produced so there are always some nerves that come with that, but I trust Olivier and my brother enough to guide us somewhere really special.” Huband produces with his sister Zara Huband under his Boneyard Films banner. Konstantin Mazov (“Coup de Grâce,” “Rokeby Venus”) has boarded the project as director of photography. Meanwhile, MarcelMonique Pictures have recruited the help of French production company All In Films, founded by Thomas Laget and Julien Floutard, to help bring the project to life. articles.full_text: Aug 11, 2026 2:11am PT RTL Group Posts 3.9% Revenue Rise as Streaming Side Grows, Though Fremantle Continues to Suffer RTL expects Fremantle to pick up by the year's end with the rollout of new shows, including its "Baywatch" reboot By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest RTL Group Posts 3.9% Revenue Rise as Streaming Side Grows, Though Fremantle Continues to Suffer 31 minutes ago Giovanni Tortorici on Working With Monica Bellucci Who Plays an ‘Eccentric’ Aristocratic Matron in His Luca Guadagnino-Produced Film ‘Ketticè’ 3 days ago Cinema Ritrovato Chief Gianluca Farinelli Appointed Artistic Director of Italy’s David di Donatello Awards 6 days ago See All Courtesy of Fox/Sky European media conglomerate RTL Group on Tuesday posted first-half figures showing strong growth in streaming, with revenue up 3.9% to €2.9 billion ($ 3.3 billion), while revenues from its linear TV side and its Fremantle content business were down. The acquisition of pay-TV operation ‌Sky Deutschland from Comcast in June has also increased the group’s revenue base. RTL said it now expects ​2026 revenue of €7.1 to €7.2 billion, ($8.20 ​billion-$8.32 billion), up from its previous ⁠forecast of €6.1 billion to €6.2 billion that it ​issued in March. articles.title: George MacKay, Louisa Harland, Nathalie Emmanuel and Eric Kofi Abrefa Join ‘The Animals’ From ‘Supacell’ Star Calvin Demba (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 11, 2026 2:30am PT George MacKay, Louisa Harland, Nathalie Emmanuel and Eric Kofi Abrefa Join ‘The Animals’ From ‘Supacell’ Star Calvin Demba (EXCLUSIVE) By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest George MacKay, Louisa Harland, Nathalie Emmanuel and Eric Kofi Abrefa Join ‘The Animals’ From ‘Supacell’ Star Calvin Demba (EXCLUSIVE) 11 minutes ago ‘House of the Dragon’ Star Fabien Frankel Joins Short Film ‘Love Unlimited’ (EXCLUSIVE) 43 minutes ago Pippa Harris and James Wilson to Headline London Film Festival Industry Forum 24 hours ago See All Photos supplied by filmmakers Calvin Demba, the British actor, writer and director best known on screen for the Netflix hit “Supacell,” has lined up an impressive cast list for his second short film behind the camera, “The Animals.” George MacKay (“Rose of Nevada,” “Sense and Sensibility”) stars alongside Louisa Harland (“Renegade Nell,” “Derry Girls”), Nathalie Emmanuel (“Game of Thrones,” “Megalopolis”) and Eric Kofi Abrefa (“Supacell,” BMF”) in the project, written and directed by Demba and produced by Tuli Litvak (“Beauty Sleep,” “Fairview Park”). Related Stories Dylan Mulvaney Fires Back After Trump Mocks Her and Kaitlan Collins in White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech: 'Actually the Greatest Compliment of All' CNN's Kaitlan Collins Was 'Not Surprised' Trump Insulted Her in White House Correspondents' Dinner Speech: 'That Happens Pretty Regularly Inside the Oval Office' “The Animals” centers on Miles (MacKay) as he struggles with growing feelings of emasculation and emotional impotency within his relationship with Remona (Harland). An opportunity to reclaim his sense of self arises from another man’s act of heroism during a violent home invasion — but as events spiral out of control, he’s forced to confront the destructive masculine ideals driving him. Popular on Variety “I wanted to make a film that takes a satirical look at gender stereotypes and the role they play in relationships,” said Demba, who made his directorial debut with 2022’s “BabyDolls.” “‘The Animals’ examines masculinity and how it can become performative. It pokes fun at modern relationships and the ways we unconsciously perform gender roles within them, exploring the gap between who we are and who we feel we should be. Tonally, the film is darkly comic, but the violence never feels slapstick. It needed to feel grounded in reality because that threat of violence mirrors the conversations we’re having about masculinity itself.” Added MacKay: “What drew me to the project was the script and the opportunity to work with Calvin. I’m a huge fan of his previous work and wanted to be part of whatever he made next. Working with Cal, and his mix of detail and freedom, was my favourite part of the process. His generosity as a writer and director, and his willingness to share that process, was golden.” “The Animals,” which was shot earlier this year, was filmed on 16mm by Ebba Hult (whose work has screened at Cannes, Telluride, and LFF), edited by Mdhamiri Á Nkemi (“The Last Tree,” “Blue Story”), and graded by Canadian colourist Jodie Davison (“The Revenant,” “The Eternal Daughter”). It is executive produced by BAFTA-winners Mouktar Mohammed (“Supacell”) and Sheila Nortley (“Supacell,” “Stay Close”), Demba and Harland. “This film was a total joy to make because we had such a clever script and such an incredible team, and I loved getting to work alongside George who I have long admired,” said Harland. “The script is what drew me to this role, but I really believe in Calvin as a filmmaker. His stories are rooted in poetry, and I hope to continue working with him on every project he does, whether that’s in front of or behind the camera.” “The Animals” will begin its festival circuit at a BAFTA and Oscar qualifying major festival, to be announced soon. articles.title: Sony Pre-Empts ‘The Ballad Of The Ember Knight’; 14th Century-Set Spec By First-Time Scribes Lands Near 7-Figures
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Fleming Jr Mike Fleming Jr Editor-At-Large @DeadlineMike More Stories By Mike Sony Pre-Empts ‘The Ballad Of The Ember Knight’; 14th Century-Set Spec By First-Time Scribes Lands Near 7-Figures Netflix Plans Epic Survival Story Of Ernest Shackleton In Movie From ‘Adolescence’ Director Phil Barantini & ‘The Revenant’ Scribe Mark L. Smith AI Questions Spoil Book & Movie Heat On Unpublished Debut Novel ‘Call Me, I’ll Hide The Body’ – The Dish View All August 10, 2026 2:18pm L-R: Kieran O'Dea and Brennan O'Dea Courtesy photos EXCLUSIVE : After Christopher Nolan turned Homer’s ancient poem into gold with The Odyssey , maybe Hollywood is ready to take more chances on literate period fare. How else to explain the high level of interest when CAA and Kaplan Perrone went out with the spec script The Ballad of the Ember Knight , a 14th century-set drama that clocked in at 190 pages? When the dust settled, Sony paid near seven-figures to the sibling writing team Kieran and Brennan O’Dea. It is the first time they sold a script. Ember Knight is a medieval epic set against the French and English conflict during the Hundred Years’ War. The hero is a legendary warrior accused of murdering the royal family. To reclaim his standing, he must protect the kingdom’s last surviving prince from the conspiracy that threatens them both. Sony’s Brittany Morrissey and Peter Kang brought it into the studio, and it came without producer attachments. Related Stories Casting Uli Latukefu Lands Villain Role Of Ganondorf In Sony & Nintendo's 'The Legend Of Zelda' Movie News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swings To $42M Tuesday U.S. Box Office Record, Biggest Pic Global YTD With $1.1B How did this become the talk of town at a time when the material market goes into summer slumber? It started with Kaplan/Perrone, which was asked to read the script, knowing full well it would be a hard sell given its length. They flipped for it, CAA got into it, and they took it out. Watch on Deadline While there was flirtation with doing Ember as a longform TV effort because of its length and sweep, the scribes didn’t want to go that route. Nor did they want to cut their work down to the usual length of around 112 pages for a feature script. Sony moved quickly. Who are the O’Dea brothers? They are the middle sons of astronomers. Originally from the East Coast, they grew up in Baltimore and then Rochester before moving to northern Idaho after college. Their storytelling passion was fueled by their late grandfather, who would tell them as bedtime stories works like The Iliad, The Odyssey, Macbeth , WWII, and an errant knight named Sir Kay. It is comforting to know there is still a place for the classics in Hollywood. The brothers are repped by CAA and Kaplan Perrone. articles.title: ‘Pluribus’ Duo Vince Gilligan And Composer Dave Porter On Long-Running Collaboration & That Addictive Main Theme – Crew Call Podcast
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Pluribus’ Duo Vince Gilligan And Composer Dave Porter On Long-Running Collaboration & That Addictive Main Theme – Crew Call Podcast ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Second-Fastest Film To Cross $1B At Int’l Box Office, With Global At $1.67B; ‘PAW Patrol: The Dino Movie’ Opens With $25M Summer Domestic Box Office On A Hot Streak, Will Cross $4B By Monday View All August 10, 2026 2:45pm L-R: Vince Gilligan and Dave Porter Apple TV Of the 18 Emmy nominations for Apple TV ‘s Pluribus , composer Dave Porter can call dibs on three of ’em: for Outstanding Music Composition for a Series, Sound Mixing for a Comedy or Drama Series (One Hour), and Original Main Title Theme Music. It’s a sweet moment for Porter, for after his 18-year collaboration with series creator Vince Gilligan on Breaking Bad, spinoff Better Call Saul and now Pluribus, the Television Academy has finally recognized his nuanced sound, which always pushes the boundary of not only score but also story. Related Stories News Cover Story: Rhea Seehorn Answers All The Big ‘Pluribus’ Questions – Will Carol Blow Up The World In Season 2? News ‘Widow’s Bay’ & ‘Pluribus’ Helped Apple Land Record Emmy Noms, Apple’s Matt Cherniss Says “Quality Over Quantity” Strategy Is Paying Off We talk with the duo on the latest episode of Deadline’s Crew Call podcast about their roots together, their shorthand and philosophy on scoring, and how that 20-second, New Age, harmonized choral main title theme (or “ear wig,” as Gilligan calls it) came about. In that short time span, the music sets the table for the show’s trippy dystopian future where a woman is one of a few untouched survivors in a world where an extraterrestrial virus has turned the majority of Earth’s denizens into peaceful, hive-minded people. It’s no wonder that Porter started his professional career as an assistant to three-time Oscar-nominated minimalist film composer Philip Glass. Watch on Deadline Explains Porter about the melodic, two-part main title performed by Kenya Hathaway: “We’re presenting two sides of this argument. That’s the most interesting part of this show, is all the dichotomies that Vince has created here, and all the ways that we’re hopefully making our audience think and not take a side.” The composer adds, “We love to leave that ambiguity in there if we possibly can, because we want our audience to come to their own conclusions about this amazing world that Vince and our writers have created.” “These two vocal parts: sometimes they’re harmonious, sometimes they’re rubbing against each other in a discordant way, and they don’t seem to fit. And then ultimately, we’re leaving our audience there a little bit unsettled, but curious and hopefully humming a little too.” Says Gilligan about Porter: “[He asks], ‘How do you want the audience to feel? What’s the emotion you’re looking for?’ He always boils it down to that for me. And even then, which I always appreciate, he’s always throwing me a life preserver.” Below is our conversation; listen through to the end as Gilligan speculates how long he sees Pluribus lasting. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Nikki Glaser Signs With WME Alexa Swinton, David Arquette, Wyatt Oleff & Sawyer Spielberg Set For Demolition Derby Drama ‘Wreckless’ From First-Time Feature Filmmaker Kayla Arend CAA Signs Ashley Gill & Grant Gibbs Of Musical Comedy Duo A Twink And A Redhead View All August 10, 2026 2:55pm L-R: Alexa Swinton, David Arquette, Wyatt Oleff and Sawyer Spielberg Jonny Marlow/Ciaràn Maginn/Josh Katz/Bjorn Wallander EXCLUSIVE: Alexa Swinton ( Behemoth! ), David Arquette ( Scarpetta ), Wyatt Oleff ( It ) and Sawyer Spielberg ( Masters of the Air ) are underway on the Minnesota shoot for Wreckless , an indie sports drama marking the directorial debut of Kayla Arend , who’s working from a script she wrote with Mickey Falcone. Set within the male-dominated demolition derby community in rural Minnesota, Wreckless is a father-daughter story about addiction, grief and recovery centered on Joni (Swinton), a reckless teenager who has learned to live with pain, and her father Larry (Arquette), a recovering addict who has spent years trying to outrun his own mistakes. When Joni enters the demolition derby, the father and daughter are forced to confront the past and rebuild their relationship in the most unlikely of arenas. Related Stories Casting Mishka Sets Cast For Debut Feature 'My Boyfriend Is A Demon' Casting 'Scarpetta': David Arquette, Jodi Balfour, William Zabka, Kim Dickens, Killer Mike & Holland Taylor Among Season 2 Cast Additions The film is shooting amidst the real demolition derby community of Rochester, MN, with Oleff playing Atlas, Joni’s magnetic but troubled boyfriend, and Spielberg as Bo, Larry’s neighbor and sponsor. The cast also includes Rochester native Mohamed Khalid Mohamed as Ahmed, Joni’s best friend and co-worker, and other locals. Watch on Deadline A graduate of NYU’s Graduate Film program whose thesis film Leaving Yellowstone was executive produced by Spike Lee, Arend said: “This story is important to me as the child of a man who battled addiction. The unwavering support that I received from this community is something I am eternally grateful for and will never take for granted. I cannot fathom making this film anywhere else. Wreckless is very much a modern portrait of the Midwest that I know and love.” Cast by Barbara J. McCarthy ( Sovereign , Sitting in Bars with Cake ), Wreckless is executive produced by George Hubbard, Teresa Tsai, Timothy Carpenter, John Siff, Inna Swinton and Rolfe Swinton. Clément Bauer ( True Spirit , Sitting in Bars with Cake ), who’s producing for Resonate Entertainment alongside Vic Brandt ( She’s the He ), told us: “Kayla and I both grew up in this pocket of Minnesota, and we knew it was the only place to tell this story, not just to reflect on where we come from, but to shine a light on a community that rarely gets represented on screen.” Best known for roles on the shows And Just Like That… and Billions , Swinton’s film credits include M. Night Shyamalan’s Old , Bradley Cooper’s Maestro and Jake Schreier’s Marvel entry Thunderbolts *. Upcoming, she’ll be seen in Tony Gilroy’s Searchlight drama Behemoth! , set in the world of classical music, which is out December 4. She is repped by Osbrink, Untitled Entertainment and Lichter, Grossman, Nichols. Coming off an appearance in Scream 7 , Arquette’s upcoming slate includes Scarpetta Season 2 for Prime Video, as well as such indies as Wildcard , The Night Driver , The Mess We Made and Killing Hitler . Most recently seen in Karate Kid: Legends and the Apple show City on Fire , Oleff’s also known for his work in the recent It films from New Line; the Guardians of the Galaxy franchise, where he played a young version of Chris Pratt’s Peter Quill; and the Netflix series I Am Not Okay with This . articles.title: Jon Cypher Dies: ‘Hill Street Blues’ Police Chief, ‘Major Dad’ Regular & ‘Masters Of The Universe’ Ally Was 94
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Erik Pedersen Erik Pedersen Managing Editor More Stories By Erik Jon Cypher Dies: ‘Hill Street Blues’ Police Chief, ‘Major Dad’ Regular & ‘Masters Of The Universe’ Ally Was 94 Julianne Moore To Star In New Play ‘Faydra’ Off Broadway Tedde Moore Dies: Teacher In ‘A Christmas Story’ Who Had Dozens Of Other Credits Was 79 View All August 10, 2026 3:27pm Jon Cypher as Chief Daniels in 'Hill Street Blues' (1981-87) and as Man-at-Arms in 'Masters of the Universe' (1987) Everett Collection Jon Cypher , who played Chief Daniels in scores of Hill Street Blues episodes, was He-Man’s chief ally in 1987’s Masters of the Universe , starred on Major Dad and appeared in dozens of other TV series and films over nearly a half-century, died August 3 at his home in Central Point, Oregon. He was 94. His family told local news outlet Ashland News that he died with his wife by his side but did not reveal a cause of death. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries Obituaries James B. Sikking Dies: ‘Hill Street Blues’, ‘Doogie Howser, M.D.’ Actor Was 90 Cypher probably is best known for his role as the politics-savvy and sometimes duplicitous Police Chief Fletcher Daniels in more than 70 episodes of NBC’s 1980s cop drama Hill Street Blues from 1981-87. Although the series created by Steven Bochco-Michael Kozoll never was a big ratings hit — ranking only 27th among primetime series in its first season and never breaking the Top 20 in a three-network universe — its influence was undeniable as critics swooned. The series amassed 26 Emmys, dozens more nominations and was the first show to win four consecutive Emmys for Outstanding Drama Series, from 1981-84. During Hill Street ‘s run, Cypher was cast as He-Man key ally Duncan, aka Man-at-Arms, in the 1987 cult pic Masters of the Universe. Idris Elba plays the character in this year’s reboot starring Nicholas Galitzine. Another big role came around in 1990 when Cypher joined the CBS sitcom Major Dad as Brig. Gen. Marcus Craig for the show’s final three seasons into 1993. But those career-defining parts came a quarter-century or more into his acting career. Born on January 13, 1932, in New York City, Cypher’s first credit was playing Prince Christopher in CBS’ 1957 landmark live telecast of Rodgers and Hammerstein’s musical Cinderella , which starred Julie Andrews and drew more than 100 million U.S. viewers. He then played the first nine Broadway roles, starting with The Disenchanted and including such 1960s productions as The Night of the Iguana, Man of La Mancha, The Great White Hope and 1776 . His final Broadway credit was playing toy story owner Mr. MacMillan in the 1996 production of Big . In the early 1960s, he was cast in the single-season CBS daytime soap Our Five Daughters — which debuted a year after the sitcom My Three Sons — beginning a string of roles in serials for Cypher. He went on to appear on the likes of General Hospital, As the World Turns and Santa Barbara , along with primetime soaps Dynasty, Dallas and Knots Landing. Along the way, he guested on dozens of memorable TV hits from Mission: Impossible, Bonanza and The F.B.I. to The Rockford Files, The Love Boat and Knight Ryder to Hunter, The Commish, JAG, Law & Order, Walker, Texas Ranger and Murder, She Wrote. Cypher’s first big-screen credit was a starring role in 1971’s Valdez Is Coming, playing a powerful rancher who falsely accuses a man of murder and forces the town sheriff (Burt Lancaster) to kill the guy. When the lawman asks for compensation for the fallen man’s widow, Cypher’s Frank Tanner summons a force to battle him. Future Law & Order Emmy winner and DGA Lifetime Achievement Award winner Edwin Sherin directed the film. Cypher would appear in a number of other features during his long career, including Strictly Business and Off the Mark, but TV was his main medium. He also appeared in a number of telefilms such as Elvis & Me, Malice in Wonderland , Night Games and Juan Peron in Evita Peron . His final credit was playing a director in a pair of The Lot episodes in 2001. He also was a singer — his Ashland News obit noted that he sang opera in four languages — and was the author of a book of limericks titled If You’re Not Depressed, You Oughta Be in Therapy. Cypher is survived by his wife of 40 years, Carol Rosin. Information of other survivors was not available. He was to be buried at the Forest Conservation Burial Ground in Ashland, Oregon. articles.title: Chris Carter’s Cut Of ‘The X-Files: I Want to Believe – Vrach Frankenshteyn’ Gets A Release Almost 20 Years Later Amid Ryan Coogler’s Reboot At Hulu

The X-Files: I Want to Believe — Vrach Frankenshteyn is set to premiere on August 14 on Disney+ and Hulu , as the streamer is also working on a reboot by Ryan Coogler. Originally released in 2008, the supernatural thriller was directed by Carter, who also co-wrote it alongside Fran Spotnitz. The X-Files: I Want to Believe was a sequel to the 1998 film and released six years after the main series ended. David Duchovny, Gillian Anderson and Mitch Pileggi reprise their roles as Fox Mulder, Dana Scully and Walter Skinner, respectively. In a case you’d never see on TV, their only lead is a disgraced, defrocked priest claiming to have horrific psychic visions of the crime. Forced to confront the ghosts of their past, the partners must navigate a chilling winter landscape and an even darker human monstrosity. The truth of these crimes is out there somewhere … and it will take Mulder and Scully to find it.” Watch on Deadline The film is a contemporary take on Dr. Frankenstein, and Carter’s cut intensifies the horror elements that were removed from the theatrically released movie to land at a PG-13 rating. Carter’s cut of the film also premieres as Coogler works on a reboot of the sci-fi series . The Oscar winner is writing and directing the pilot, which is set to star Danielle Deadwyler and Himesh Patel as two highly decorated but vastly different FBI agents who form an unlikely bond when they are assigned to a long-shuttered division devoted to cases involving unexplained phenomena. The reboot series is also set to star Amy Madigan, Steve Buscemi, Ben Foster, Devery Jacobs, Lochlyn Munro, Tantoo Cardinal, Joel D. Montgrand and Sofia Grace Clifton. articles.title: ‘Newlyweds’ Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She “Begged” Her Agents To Find Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Comedies Are Primed For Comeback
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say “We Don’t Need An Intimacy Coordinator” On ‘Newlyweds’; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy ‘Newlyweds’ Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She “Begged” Her Agents To Find Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Comedies Are Primed For Comeback Jerry Katzman Dies: Former WMA President Was 89 View All August 10, 2026 4:55pm L-R: Jamie Lee Curtis and Tea Leoni in NBC's 'Newlyweds' Nicole Weingart/NBC) Jamie Lee Curtis had just wrapped a movie when, during the 1988 pilot season, ABC offered her a half-hour multi-camera pilot. She did it and loved it, so she was bummed when the network didn’t pick it up to series that May. Curtis went to do another movie, and, while she was filming, A Fish Called Wanda came out in July 1988, making her an overnight global star. Suddenly, ABC called and told her they wanted to pick up that pilot, which became Anything But Love , a sitcom starring Curtis and comedian Richard Lewis that ran for four seasons. Related Stories News NBC Sets Fall Premiere Dates For ‘Chicago’ And ‘Law & Order’ Shows, ‘The Voice,’ Comedies, New Series & More News Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say “We Don’t Need An Intimacy Coordinator” On ‘Newlyweds’; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy “It was my favorite job I’ve ever had,” Curtis recalled during a panel Monday for the new NBC multi-camera comedy Newlyweds , which she executive produces and recurs on. “And I’m 68 years old, and every single year, all I’ve ever said to my agents is ‘I want to do a sitcom, all I want to do is a sitcom.’ It’s my favorite job, I love the whole part of it, every aspect of it, the dance with the cameras, the idea that you actually get to rehearse something and work it and learn a joke and play it. I just never got to do it, and so I just decided to basically kind of create my own job. I met Gail, and that’s why we are all here.” Gail Lerner is Newlyweds ‘ writer and executive producer. Curtis has done single-camera comedy series over the years, including New Girl and The Bear , but is not a fan of the form. “I’m telling you, I have begged my agents ‑‑ and by the way, I did a single‑camera, which I hate. I mean, great show, New Girl , very funny,” she said. “It’s a good show, but doing it is just like doing a movie. You’ve got a camera crew, and nobody laughs. They are silent, and it’s awful, for me, awful. Single‑camera comedy is not fun.” Jamie Lee Curtis on “begging” to do a multi-cam sitcom after ‘New Girl’ pic.twitter.com/AYjVYbEeZp — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 10, 2026 Like Curtis, Newlyweds stars Téa Leoni and Tim Daly also have multi-camera sitcom experience though for Leoni, it was not love at first sight. “When I did Flying Blind and Naked Truth, they used to hang air‑sickness bags behind all of the sets because I used to hurl before I came out, I used to be so scared,” she said. “In that time since I did that, I missed it, and I realized that I’m old enough, I’m tough, like, I’m good, I can do this, I want to. it’s still a little scary but it is so much fun.” Daly chimed in to “slightly dispute the characterization that people in general think [sitcoms are] old‑fashioned,” noting that young people come to him to talk about his classic sitcom Wings which they had discovered and loved. “So I think that there is an audience; it’s just a matter of us finding them and them finding us, and, hopefully, they will,” he said. Newlyweds is a later‑in‑life love story about a free‑spirited woman (Leoni) and a buttoned‑up professor (Daly) who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship. Curtis plays the professor’s ex-wife, “a bitch,” in her own words. Curtis, an Oscar winner who is married to filmmaker Christopher Guest, spoke about the genesis of the idea for Newlyweds. “The truth of the matter is I met my husband and married him after seeing his picture in a magazine, and we had never spent more than 72 hours together before we got married, I mean at one time,” she said. “I think you can know what we did for the other 70 hours, there wasn’t a lot of talking. We were strangers when we married, and then you wake up one day and go, like, ‘Wow. He really doesn’t talk.'” Continued Curtis, “We have been married for 42 years, thank you very much. But the point is that there’s always been that aspect of my relationship with my husband, we are polar opposites, and that was when we started talking about a later‑in‑life thing that happens to people in their 60s, who hook up and kind of go, ‘You know what, let’s do this.’ There’s something really delicious about watching people figure out life when they are filled in a life with other people, and that’s ultimately what we kind of wanted the show to be.” L-R: Gail Lerner, Jamie Lee Curtis, Bill O’Neill, Tim Daly, Téa Leoni, Emma Meisel and Ignacio Diaz-Silverio during NBC’s “Backlot Pass Day” on Monday at the Universal Studios lot Lerner, who co-created Newlyweds with Curtis, revealed how she and NBC got involved. “Jamie brought me this idea during the pandemic, so we’ve been really generating it for a very long time. And for a million various reasons, it was hibernating for a while, and a lot of people say my project died, but I just knew my project was hibernating,” she said. “And then NBC called in November of 2025 and said, ‘Hey, let’s do that show,’ and we were off to the races.” Lerner gave NBC props for “reinvesting in multi-cam and bringing back Must See TV.” Curtis stressed the fact that Newlyweds is on a broadcast network that is accessible to anyone. “It’s also must-see free TV,” she said. “You have to remember, a lot of people don’t have any money anymore, people are really struggling, and cable and all of the things you have to spend money on. This is network television, and I actually think this whole nostalgia of what sitcoms bring you into your house, things do come around. And my guess is that NBC’s decision to pick up a show that’s going to make a block of comedy on Friday nights ‑‑ ‘Fridays: We Are In Love On NBC’ — I mean, that’s an advertising feed. That’s how you build something.” ‘Newlyweds’ EP Jamie Lee Curtis on NBC taking a chance on sitcoms and their hopes to bring a “feel good” show to viewers pic.twitter.com/HeaPJzObAZ — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 10, 2026 The Friday sitcom block Newlyweds will be part of is anchored by the Reba McEntire comedy Happy’s Place . NBC set a goal this past development season to find a companion for its breakout multi-camera hit, greenlighting two pilots, one of which, Newlyweds, went to series . “The reason we are here is because Happy’s Place became such a happy place, and people wanted to go there that they needed to pair it with a show about love and friendship,” Curtis said. “I just think people want to have a good time in the comfort of their own home, and they want to turn on a network show and have laughs and have feelings. If that isn’t what sitcoms can do well, then I’m not sure what they do. That’s what they do, and that’s why we love them.” With multi-camera comedy in retreat across broadcast, Curtis hopes Newlyweds will help the genre make a comeback that will extend beyond Fridays on NBC. “My guess is then Thursdays are going to start being that, and the next thing you know, NBC is going to look like they were geniuses of bringing back the thing that real people really want, and they want it for free,” she said. “They want to turn their television on and have that level of entertainment and laughter and a good feeling about who we are as a society. And I just think that it’s exciting that we get to do, and we are grateful to NBC for doing it.” Jacob Elordi Circling Ari Aster’s A24 Film Starring Scarlett Johansson Cal AG Bonta Claims Ellison Misinformation, Side Deals In WBD Merger Caitríona Balfe Leads Alfonso Cuarón Horror Series ‘Ascension’ Ordered By Apple TV Second Fastest To Cross $1B WW; Now India’s Biggest Ever Hollywood Pic Read More About: 1 Comments

Just days ahead of the Camp Rock 3 debut, Disney has revealed that Demi Lovato is not only executive producing the franchise’s return but she will also make a cameo in the iconic role. It only makes sense given the callbacks to the original two movies that were already confirmed for the third film, including the return of the Jonas Brothers as Shane, Nate and Jason Gray of Connect 3 and Maria Canals-Barrera as Mitchie’s mom Connie, who is now the camp director. Desperate to find a new opener, they return to their beloved Camp Rock to discover the next big thing. As campers vie for the chance to open for their favorite band, tensions rise and friendships are tested — leading to unexpected alliances, revelations, and romances. Nearly two decades later, Disney says the films have together been watched for more than 535 million hours across linear and streaming. articles.title: Telemundo’s ‘Operación Triunfo’ Carries On With Final Live Show Following Devastating 7.4 Magnitude Quake In Colombia
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Reggie Bannister Dies: ‘Phantasm’ Actor Was 80 Telemundo’s ‘Operación Triunfo’ Carries On With Final Live Show Following Devastating 7.4 Magnitude Quake In Colombia Chris Carter’s Cut Of ‘The X-Files: I Want to Believe – Vrach Frankenshteyn’ Gets A Release Almost 20 Years Later Amid Ryan Coogler’s Reboot At Hulu View All August 10, 2026 5:12pm (L-R) David Bisbal, Ximena Sariñana and Ana Bárbara Telemundo Telemundo ‘s Operación Triunfo Season 1 finale was marred by sadness after the 7.4-magnitude earthquake that struck Colombia on Monday, August 10. The singing competition was to be full of joy as one singer was crowned the winner of the talent show following weeks of arduous work. Although the show is produced for the United States Latino audience, Telemundo produces the talent competition in Colombia. At the top of the finale, host Natalia Téllez acknowledged the recent events that have devastated the country. “Before starting our grand finale full of music and emotions, we want to take a couple of moments to send a big hug to all the Colombians who have been affected by the earthquake that took place this morning,” she said. “Colombia is part of the Operación Triunfo Estados Unidos family, because we produce the program here in RCN’s studios and there’s a big human team that works day by day to make this dream possible.” Related Stories News Adamari López On Importance Of Latino Audiences, Working With Her Daughter & Joining A 24/7 Reality Show Ratings World Cup Final Scores Nearly 63M Viewers Across Fox & Telemundo As Tournament Breaks Ratings Records She continued, “Tonight, our hearts are with all of you; it’s with all the families that are worried or anguished and all those that have lost their loved ones.” Watch on Deadline Judges David Bisbal, Ximena Sariñana and Ana Bárbara were visibly affected by the events that took place in Colombia that have taken the lives of more than 100 people, at the time of this post. According to CNN , the 7.4-magnitude quake had its epicenter in San José del Palmar, about 149 miles west of Bogotá, the nation’s capital. Bogotá is where RCN’s studios are and where Operación Triunfo films. Although the tremor was felt in the country’s capital, no major structural damage has been reported, according to the mayor Carlos F. Galán. While Operación Triunfo ends tonight, Telemundo is also filming the new season of Top Chef VIP , a reality competition set to air on Tuesday, August 11, in the same time slot. articles.title: Reggie Bannister Dies: ‘Phantasm’ Actor Was 80
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Reggie Bannister Dies: ‘Phantasm’ Actor Was 80 Telemundo’s ‘Operación Triunfo’ Carries On With Final Live Show Following Devastating 7.4 Magnitude Quake In Colombia Chris Carter’s Cut Of ‘The X-Files: I Want to Believe – Vrach Frankenshteyn’ Gets A Release Almost 20 Years Later Amid Ryan Coogler’s Reboot At Hulu View All August 10, 2026 8:32pm Reggie Bannister Frazer Harrison / Getty Images / Well Go USA Entertainment Reggie Bannister, actor best known for starring in the Phantasm film series, has died. He was 80. The actor died on Sunday, August 9, in his home in Crestline, his wife, Gigi Bannister told TMZ . According to Bannister’s wife, the actor had been exposed to Agent Orange while serving in the U.S. military during the Vietnam War. Agent Orange is a powerful chemical that kills weeds and acts as a defoliant, which the military used during the war in Vietnam to clear dense jungle and destroy food crops. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Neil Reading Dies: Top UK Entertainment PR Whose Client List Included John Cleese & Lenny Henry Was 56 Bannister also battled with Lewy body dementia and Parkinson’s disease. Watch on Deadline In 1979, Bannister would star in the supernatural horror film directed and written by Don Coscarelli. The film starred A. Michael Baldwin as Mike, a teenager in a small town, as he investigates strange things going on at a local funeral home alongside his older brother Jody (Bill Thornbury) and family friend Reggie (Bannister). The film was followed by four sequels, in which Bannister would reprise his role as Reggie starting with 1988’s Phantasm II , 1993’s Phantasm III: Lord of the Dead , 1998’s Phantasm IV: Oblivion , and 2016’s Phantasm: Ravager . Bannister’s other credits include Silent Night, Deadly Night 4: Initiation (1990), The Demolitionist (1995), Wishmaster (1997), Bubba Ho-Tep (2002), Cemetery Gates (2004), The Mangler Rebor (2005), Last Rites (2006), The Rage (2007), The Quiet Ones (2008), Carnies (2009), Sawblade (2010), Not Another B Movie (2011), The Ghastly Love of Johnny X (2012), Bloody Bloody Biuble Camp (2012), The Obsidian Curse (2016), and Bonejangles (2017). articles.title: Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say “We Don’t Need An Intimacy Coordinator” On ‘Newlyweds’; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Newlyweds’ Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She “Begged” Her Agents To Find Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Comedies Are Primed For Comeback Jerry Katzman Dies: Former WMA President Was 89 Caitríona Balfe Stars In Alfonso Cuarón Horror Thriller Series ‘Ascension’ Ordered By Apple TV View All August 10, 2026 9:23pm 'Newlyweds: (l-r) Tea Leoni as Jeanie, Tim Daly as James Nicole Weingart/NBC NBC did some method casting on its comedy pilot Newlyweds earlier this year, with Tèa Leoni and Tim Daly , who had tied the knot just months prior, tapped as the titular leads in the multi-camera comedy. It marked an on-screen reunion of the duo who also played a husband and wife on the 2014 CBS drama series Madam Secretary. The joint casting was not an accident. “We were kind of sniffing around to play together again,” Leoni said at NBCUniversal’s Backlot Pass event ahead of Newlyweds’ series debut this fall. “We had a lot of fun on Madam Secretary . The world got darker, and we wanted to get lighter. We thought we’ve done this particular medium, and loved it, and we wanted to spend our days together.” Related Stories News 'Newlyweds' Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She "Begged" Her Agents To Get Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Sitcoms Are Primed For Comeback Casting Damon Wayans To Guest Star On NBC's 'St. Denis Medical' Season 3 Premiere In 'In Living Color' Reunion; First-Look Photo Added Daly, “Listen, we spent six years pretending to be married on TV, and I would get to do it again, but we actually are married. It’s a miracle, it’s really fun, it’s cool, and we still like each other.” Watch on Deadline Said Leoni, “It took 12 years, but we got there.” Newlyweds tells the story of a free‑spirited woman (Leoni) and a buttoned‑up professor (Daly) who marry impetuously after a whirlwind courtship. “We’ve been told that we have chemistry, we were told that on Madam Secretary, and, hopefully, we exported that into this show,” Daly said. Added Leoni, “We haven’t lost it.” While they have proven to have an on-screen couple chemistry, being a couple in real life has its advantages too. “One, we don’t need an intimacy coordinator because we are licensed to do whatever we want,” Daly said. Additionally, “We get to start ahead of the game,” Leoni said, giving an example with an exchange between their characters on their first date in the Newlyweds pilot. “I was looking at James, aka Tim, and I can read him, I know where he’s going,” Leoni said. “We just found this moment because ‑‑ maybe that happened somewhere else, but it happens in our life all the time, and it’s fun. It’s really fun to act with someone that you know so well because we are a little ahead with each other. It’s great, we like it.” Daly has the rare distinction of playing the love interest on two multi-camera comedies, NBC’s Newlyweds and Netflix’s Leanne, whose second season premieres later this month. Now that he has his own series, Daly is not sure whether he would continue on Leanne Morgan’s sitcom, where he has been recurring, if it’s renewed for a third season. “Netflix is its own bizarre kind of universe, so I don’t know what they are thinking about or deciding or even if I’m legally allowed to do any more of that show,” he said. NBCUniversal “Backlot Pass Day” (l-r) Gail Lerner, Jamie Lee Curtis , Bill O’Neill, Tim Daly, Téa Leoni, Emma Meisel, Ignacio Diaz-Silverio at the Universal Studios Lot on Monday, August 10, 2026 Newlyweds is created and executive produced by Gail Lerner and Jaimie Lee Curtis, with the Oscar winner also recurring on the show. Curtis was asked about being a boss on the show. “I like to refer to myself as the ‘HBIC,’ head bitch in charge,” she said. “I’m 68 years old, I have wanted to be a boss my whole life. If you ask my children, my husband, they would tell you I’ve been a boss my whole life, but I’ve been waiting my whole life, literally, to be able to manifest ideas and bring what I love about what I do into the workplace I do it in. I’ve been doing it not as a boss for a long, long time, and now I’m a boss, and I love it.” Curtis’ choice of title was clearly by design. When asked what she brings of herself to her role as James’ (Daly) ex-wife, she had a quick response. “I’m really a bitch,” she quipped. articles.title: ‘Sunset P.I.’ Bosses Dan Goor & Luke Del Tredici On Finding Inspiration From ‘Moonlighting’ & ‘The Pitt’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Linda Cardellini Reveals Homage To Betsy Palmer In ‘Crystal Lake’: “A Certain Sweater Makes An Appearance” ‘Sunset P.I.’ Bosses Dan Goor & Luke Del Tredici On Finding Inspiration From ‘Moonlighting’ & ‘The Pitt’ ‘Line Of Fire’s Josh Safran & Peter Krause Tease New NBC Series View All August 10, 2026 10:15pm NBCUNIVERSAL EVENTS -- "Backlot Pass Day" -- Pictured: (l-r) Langston Kerman, Mary Shalaby, Keith David, Jake Johnson, Luke Del Tredici, Showrunner, Executive Producer; Dan Goor, Showrunner, Executive Producer at the Universal Studios Lot on Monday, August 10, 2026 Trae Patton/NBCUniversal NBC ‘s newest comedy Sunset P.I. is coming to TV in February, and creators Dan Goor and Luke Del Tredici teased what’s ahead while on a panel at the network’s Backlot Press Day in Los Angeles on Monday afternoon. They were joined by series stars Jake Johnson, Keith David, Langston Kerman, and Mary Shalaby, Sunset P.I. is a half-hour comedy that centers on Mickey (Johnson), who is smart, cynical, and heartbroken, but trying to pretend he’s not. Mickey is a private investigator with a knack for solving cases and a former LAPD cop whose life imploded three years ago. David plays Mickey’s boss, Garner Taggart, who runs the Garner Taggart PI Agency where his son Mitch (Kerman) and Mickey are the main PIs. Shalaby plays Raya, who also works at the PI Agency. Jane Levy, who was unable to attend the presser, portrays Faye, a smart and resourceful investigative journalist and a force of nature. Related Stories News Téa Leoni & Tim Daly Say "We Don't Need An Intimacy Coordinator" On 'Newlyweds'; Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Her NSFW Title On NBC Comedy News 'Newlyweds' Jamie Lee Curtis On Why She "Begged" Her Agents To Get Her A Sitcom & Why Multi-Cam Sitcoms Are Primed For Comeback The duo, who executive produced the beloved police comedy series Brooklyn Nine-Nine , revealed on the panel that they found inspiration for Sunset P.I. from the hit 80s dramedy series Moonlighting and the critically acclaimed HBO Max medical drama series The Pitt . Watch on Deadline Moonlighting centered on the Blue Moon Detective Agency, formed by Maddie Hayes (Cybill Shepherd) and David Addison (Bruce Willis). The sexual tension between Maddie and David kept viewers on the edge of their seats weekly. SUNSET P.I. — “Pilot” (l-r) Jane Levy as Faye, Jake Johnson as Mickey Wilder “Yeah, we were definitely influenced by Moonlighting . Unfortunately, Jane Levy couldn’t be here today, but the chemistry between Jake and Jane is unbelievable,” shared Goor. “It’s hard to watch, but in a good way. I should not have said that,” he continued with a laugh. “It’s loosely inspired by [ Moonlighting ]. We really like the chemistry between them and the dating and that, but it’s also a hard comedy and an ensemble workplace in the way that Brooklyn Nine Nine is and Parks and Rec. We’re trying the mashup of all the great network television shows we love,” added Del Tredici. The Noah Wyle-led The Pitt is centered on the lives of medical workers at a fictional Pittsburgh hospital. However, the inspiration from this show doesn’t come from the storyline. “We were really inspired by The Pitt , which feels like both a really effective streaming show and also a really effective network show. And we felt like with a PI show, where you can have some overriding plot elements, and also do case-of-the-week things, and do workplace comedy, we are hoping to get the best of both worlds. [Sunset P.I.] is a network show, but we are also conscious of the fact that a large percentage of the audience will stream it,” Goor said. articles.title: Linda Cardellini Reveals Homage To Betsy Palmer In ‘Crystal Lake’: “A Certain Sweater Makes An Appearance”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Linda Cardellini Reveals Homage To Betsy Palmer In ‘Crystal Lake’: “A Certain Sweater Makes An Appearance” ‘Sunset P.I.’ Bosses Dan Goor & Luke Del Tredici On Finding Inspiration From ‘Moonlighting’ & ‘The Pitt’ ‘Line Of Fire’s Josh Safran & Peter Krause Tease New NBC Series View All August 10, 2026 11:30pm Linda Cardellini as Pamela Voorhees in 'Crystal Lake' Peacock The new Peacock series Crystal Lake will welcome a new scream queen in Linda Cardellini , who will play the role of Pamela Voorhees, mother of Jason Voorhees, the infamous serial killer from the F riday the 13th films. Ahead of the streaming series’ premiere on Thursday, October 15, Cardellini and Brad Caleb Kane, writer, showrunner, and executive producer of the series, hosted a panel on Monday afternoon at the NBC Backlot Press Day. “We all know where Pam ends up because she starts all the killing in the first movie. So, what Brad gave me was a beautiful beginning and somewhere to go. There’s an arc there from somebody who means well and is trying to survive. She’s doing the best that she can and fighting hard for things that she thinks are right to [becoming] somebody who then turns out to do all the wrong things. That gives me a lot of places to go. I think that dissent is very necessary,” Cardellini shared. Related Stories News Peacock Launches First Serialized Mobile Game 'Public Eye' News 'Love Island USA' Cements Its Crown As Peacock's Top Original Series The role of Pam has been played by multiple actresses, but the gold standard is Betsy Palmer, the first to play the serial killer mom of a serial killer, in the 1980 film Friday the 13th . Since news of the prequel series broke, there have been questions about how Cardellini will approach playing the character. Watch on Deadline NBCUNIVERSAL EVENTS — “Backlot Pass Day” — Pictured: (l-r) Linda Cardellini, Brad Caleb Kane, Showrunner, Executive Producer at the Universal Studios Lot on Monday, August 10, 2026 “I have, of course, seen what Betsy Palmer did. Then you see a little bit more of it in [ Friday the 13th Part 2]; she kind of comes back as the severed head. The fans love her so much. We even toyed around with the idea of the short hair, but we figured she has 10 years to get there,” she said. Adding, “You can’t duplicate what Betsy did, which was to play this devoted mother. So I can take that and sort of bring that to the early childhood years of Jason’s life. I also think that you don’t get to where Betsy is without really truly loving Jason and getting to know him. That was really important to us going in. And no, you can’t be another Betsy. But I do do a little bit of an homage with a certain sweater that makes an appearance.” The famous sweater Cardellini is referring to is the one worn by Palmer in the original film when Pam was decapitated by a camp counselor. Without giving too much away about the pilot episode, there’s a scene where Cardellini ends up with about a bucket’s worth of blood all over her. Trust me, it’s way more impactful when you watch the scene. The blood pours over her head and face, which, according to Cardellini, required “a lot of cleanups and redos.” “That blood has to fall exactly in the right position for that stunt to work. So there were several ways we did it; for it to really have its full impact on my face, it took a few takes,” she said. Added Kane, “A lot of the gags in the show are very complicated. The special effects gags are very complicated. Linda had to go through a lot, and they’re very hard to reset. We didn’t have a lot of opportunities to do that. And I’d like to give my props right now here in front of all of you to Linda; she nailed it every single time. There was never an, ‘Oh, Linda was not in the right place.’ No, she nailed it every time. So it was a pleasure working with her on these complicated gags because she’s a consummate pro.” Jacob Elordi Circling Ari Aster’s A24 Film Starring Scarlett Johansson Cal AG Bonta Claims Ellison Misinformation, Side Deals In WBD Merger Caitríona Balfe Leads Alfonso Cuarón Horror Series ‘Ascension’ Ordered By Apple TV Second Fastest To Cross $1B WW; Now India’s Biggest Ever Hollywood Pic Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Hong Kong Filmmaker Ann Hui To Receive Camellia Award At Busan International Film Festival
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Becomes Biggest Hollywood Film Of All Time In India; As First Half Box Office Show Signs Of Market Recovery ReelShort On Course To Reach $1BN Revenue & First Profit In 2026 – MPA Report Michelle Yeoh Named As Busan International Film Festival’s Asian Filmmaker Of The Year View All August 11, 2026 12:40am Ann Hui Busan International Film Festival This year’s Busan International Film Festival has named Hong Kong filmmaker Ann Hui as the recipient of the Camellia Award, presented to filmmakers who have made significant contributions to elevating the status of women in the film industry. Hui was a leading figure in the Hong Kong New Wave as a director, screenwriter and producer, making her directing debut with The Secret in 1979. She has continued making films consistently since then, building a body of work that includes 27 feature films and two feature-length documentaries, including multiple award winner A Simple Life , which won Best Actress at the Venice film festival for Deanie Ip’s performance in 2011. Related Stories News Michelle Yeoh Named As Busan International Film Festival's Asian Filmmaker Of The Year News Mouly Surya, Reza Rahadian & Prasanna Vithanage Among Filmmakers Selected For Busan's Asian Project Market Along the way, she has also won Best Director at the Hong Kong Film Awards six times and Best Director at the Golden Horse Awards three times. Both A Simple Life and Summer Snow (1995) achieved the rare feat of sweeping Best Film, Best Director, Best Actor, and Best Actress at the Hong Kong Film Awards. Watch on Deadline Hui has also been presented with Lifetime Achievement Awards at the 2012 Asian Film Awards, Asian Filmmaker of the Year Award at Busan film festival in 2014, and the Golden Lion for Lifetime Achievement at the 2020 Venice film festival. “Underlying Hui’s remarkable career and international acclaim is a singular cinematic vision rooted in compassion and humanity, one that has long captured the complexities of Hong Kong society and the spirit of its times,” said Busan film festival in a statement. “Spanning a wide range of genres, her films chronicle the everyday lives of ordinary people while weaving intimate personal stories into broader social realities. Her nuanced portrayals of women, particularly those often pushed to the margins, have resonated deeply with audiences across cultures and generations.” Hui commented on the award: “In my previous years I felt unwilling to receive such taking-stock prizes because I wished to continue making movies. Now that I’m nearly eighty and find it difficult to make a film, I think the prize comes just in time for me to appreciate it more.” She added, “I am so happy to return to Busan and meet an audience that is among the most savvy and cinematically literate in the world.” Busan partnered with Chanel to establish the award, named after Gabrielle Chanel’s favorite flower, which was last year awarded to Taiwanese actress, director and producer Sylvia Chang. This year’s Camellia Award will be presented at Busan’s opening ceremony on October 6. As previously announced, the festival has also named Michelle Yeoh as this year’s Asian Filmmaker of the Year. articles.title: Fremantle Revenues Slide But Earnings Shoot Up To $69.2M
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse Fremantle Revenues Slide But Earnings Shoot Up To $69.2M L.A. Creator Sachin Kumar Launches Prema Creative Co. With Vertical Comedy Series About Indian-American Actor In Hollywood Sony LIV Confirms ‘Scam 2010’ Production Will Go Ahead Despite Legal Threat View All August 11, 2026 1:07am 'Kill Jackie' AMC+/Fremantle Kill Jackie producer Fremantle saw its half-yearly revenues slide nearly 8% due to drama and film production, but earnings still shot up to nearly $70M. In results released by parent RTL this morning, the London-based company posted revenues of €835M ($963M), down 7.7% on the €905M from the same period last year. RTL attributed the fall to “timing effects at Fremantle’s drama and film business,” with entertainment and documentaries “broadly stable.” Fremantle will see the dip reverse in the second half of 2026, RTL projected, and post “slightly higher” numbers that he previous year due to upcoming productions such as AMC+’s Kill Jackie and Fox’s Baywatch . Related Stories Executives E.W. Scripps CEO Briefs Wall Street On Major Layoffs, Touts AI "Revolution" In Local TV News News Starz Subscriber Levels Climbed In Q2 Despite Price Increase, CEO Jeff Hirsch Says However, Fremantle was one of two units that RTL attributed to a significant increase in earnings across the group. Adjusted EBITA was up from €39M to €60, with the margin widening sharply from 4.3% to 7.2%. This puts Fremantle on track to reach a target margin of 9% for the full year. Watch on Deadline The news comes less than two weeks after Deadline revealed Fremantle had hired Katie O’Connell Marsh to become CEO of its Global Scripted Hub. Her role will be include building out Fremantle’s drama and comedy slate, while improving the revenue take from productions. Days after her hire became public, the Baywatch reboot sold to Prime Video in numerous territories. Fremantle’s latest financials come after RTL implemented cost saving measures at the production house following a strategic review. Part of the move saw Fremantle exit fully-financing films, though it will remain as a co-producer on projects. RTL noted cost reduction plans will continue until 2030 by “optimisation of production costs, simplification of processes [and] reduction of technical costs – driven by AI.” RTL profits rise Overall, Luxembourg-based RTL posted group revenues up 0.1% at €2.9B, with adjusted EBITA coming in at €239M, significantly higher than the €160M delivered in H1 2025. Excluding the impact of buying Sky for €68M, RTL posted group adjusted EBITA up €18M. Streaming revenue, which comes from services such as RTL+ and M6+, was up 27.2% to €299M, with the number of subscribers growing alongside higher pricing in Germany and “rapidly growing” ad money in Germany and France. In total, paid subscriptions for Germany and France – RTL’s biggest two territories – were up 20.7% to 8.7 million. Adjusted EBITA from streaming was €31M and is expected to reach around €100M for the full year, way up on previous guidance to analysts of around €25M-€50M. The result were also the first since RTL on June 1 completed a deal for Sky Deutschland , which posted adjusted EBITA of €61M in H1. RTL noted this would not be indicative of the whole year as June has no production costs attached to the Bundesliga or German Cup football. Once RTL+ and Sky Deutschland merge operations, RTL will have more than 12 million paying subs across in Germany, Austria and Switzerland. “RTL Group delivered a strong first half performance in 2026, driven by rapid streaming growth, gains in both TV audience and TV advertising market shares, and the successful completion of the acquisition of Sky Deutschland,” said RTL CEO Clément Schwebig. “We also demonstrated the unique power of our content and brands, as the coverage of the football World Cup on M6 and M6+ attracted 60 million viewers and generated exceptional digital engagement. “Our streaming businesses deliver strong profitability. Streaming revenue and paid subscriptions continue to grow dynamically. As a result, streaming is now expected to contribute around €100M to our full-year operating profit.” Schwebig, the former Warner Bros. Discovery exec, replaced Thomas Rabe as CEO earlier this year. Rabe remains boss of RTL parent Bertelsmann until later in the year.
