articles.title: ‘House Of The Dragon’ Season 3 Finale: Co-Creator Ryan Condal And Star Emma D’Arcy On Rhaenyra’s Dark Path, The Battle Of Tumbleton And What’s In Store For Season 4
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Justin Kroll Justin Kroll Film Editor @krolljvar More Stories By Justin Gareth Edwards Not Returning For Next ‘Jurassic World’ Movie Bailee Madison & Deon Cole Join ‘Grown Ups 3’ At Netflix ‘X-Men’: Kit Connor Eyed For Cyclops Role In Upcoming Marvel Studios Pic View All August 9, 2026 7:10pm Emma D'Arcy in 'House of the Dragon' Courtesy of HBO SPOILER ALERT: This story contains details from Season 3 episode 8 of House of the Dragon on HBO . “I AM THE PRINCE THAT WAS PROMISED.” These are the words Queen Rhaenyra screams in the Season 3 finale to the people of King’s Landing as she unveils the future prophecy and sets the stage for what is sure to be an eventful final season. Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals ‘House Of The Dragon’ Renewed For Season 4 At HBO News Ryan Condal Extends HBO Overall Deal Through Season 4 Of ‘House Of The Dragon’ & Beyond Sunday’s episode starts with the news of the return of Aegon’s dragon, leading Rhaenyra to not only put a search out for it but also have Daemon move forward with the the attack on Tumbleton. Rhaenyra also makes the drastic decision of relieving Mysaria of her duties as master of whispers and banishing her from King’s Landing. This comes after the the two shared an intimate moment in previous episode. As Ormund Hightower and Daemon Targaryen prepare for the battle of Tumbleton, brothers Aegon and Aemon reunite at Harrenhal to discuss plans on how they will take back the Iron Throne. Watch on Deadline Even after delivering imprisoned Sea Serpent, Daemon denies peace talks from Gwayne Hightower setting the stage for the siege of Tumbleton, living up to the hype for which fans have waited weeks. The bloody battle not only leaves the city in ruins but also sees fiery end to Hightower ironically at the hands of Ulf the White and his dragon, who in the previous episode he had persuaded to cross lines and fight for his side. Ulf ultimately turns on both sides burning the city to the ground as Daemon is force to flee. Back in King’s Landing, Rhaenyra comes to find that her prisoner Helaena has taken her own life but left a parting gift for the queen that foreshadows a potential prophecy of Rhaenyra’s path towards madness. When it came to mapping out not just this season, but Season 4 as well, co-creator and showrunner Ryan Condal said he and the writers mapped out a “superstructure” that gave them an idea of how the series would end, and once that came together plotting the rest of Season 3 was seamless. “We were lucky enough in the breaking of Season 3 because we knew at that point that for sure it was going to be a four-season show that essentially when Sarah [Hess] and I sat down with all the writers, we essentially broke the back of seasons 3 and 4 together, at least in the sort of superstructure of it,” Condal said. “So it was really planning out kind of from here to the end and trying to structure it in a way that had all the peaks and valleys of drama and to keep the pacing and to hit all the big set pieces that we have to hit. Once we kind of laid it all out, it felt like it would be really fun to bookend the season with the two biggest sequences we had ever done. So episode 1, Battle of the Gullet, episode 8, the Battle of Tumbleton.” Rhaenyra makes several decisions in this week’s episode that are establishing a path of no return for the upcoming final season. and it’s hard not to see a similar trajectory to another famous Westeros character whose dark choices led to a tragic end. Emma D’Arcy, who plays Rhaenyra, understands how fans could see parallels between Rhaenra and Daenerys Targaryen from the original Game of Thrones and believes their paths has a lot to do with what the Iron Throne represents for all that seek it. “I think the parallels do call to the greater themes of, of the song of ice and fire universe, which is pride and power and how power corrupts and how far it corrupts — it can change good people into corrupted people,” D’Arcy said. “It can take corrupted people and make them real villains. And other people like this era, it can simply just destroy them.” As for the anticipated battle of Tumbleton, Condal says he drew comparisons to when “the Nazis invaded Paris” while ultimately wanting something that looked and felt like a traditional medieval siege. “So all season long, we’re kind of setting up this, this classic medieval siege, which is really where we wanted to get to,” Condall says. “The concept of that battle was that Ormand had basically done all he could to blunt the threat of Rhaenyra’s greatest power, which is that she has, or had, six dragons under her command at that point. He sees his army as better trained and better suited than the river men that are coming to attack. He knows the ground, he’s inside the city. They have to come over the walls, sacrifice a bunch of their men. So that’s where we all started, and then it was like, ‘OK, well, we need to set to do this in a big location, to build it on, and who are POV characters?’ It was a very, very, very complex thing to fold all together, but we just wanted to do the classic medieval siege. [That was] the elevator pitch for the finale.” With the fourth season also marking the final season of House of the Dragon , Condal says while he saw Game of Thrones as an epic story, he always viewed House of the Dragon as more of tragedy. While he won’t say much about what’s to come, he does hint that the final season will be even bigger then the one we just watched Sunday. “We have we have an incredible season coming, as crazy and big as Season 3 was,” Condal said. “I think Season 4 is going to be even bigger. It’s a great privilege to be able to tell a story and to be able to write the ending and to control when and where that ending happens. This is not a given in making television, certainly. So we’re very excited to get back in and we have new characters and new dragons and new locations that I think are gonna make it a very worthy final season.” Second Fastest To Cross $1B WW; Third Best 2nd U.S. Frame With $145M ‘House Of The Dragon’s Ryan Condal And Emma D’Arcy On Season 3 Finale Now Christopher Nolan’s Highest-Grossing Globally With $1.1B A24’s Anthony Bourdain Biopic ‘Tony’ A Top 2026 Limited Opening Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Mekai Curtis On How ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Finale Sets Up Follow-Up Series ‘Origins’ & Why Kanan Is Misunderstood
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Mekai Curtis On How ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Finale Sets Up Follow-Up Series ‘Origins’ & Why Kanan Is Misunderstood ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Star Patina Miller On Tackling Personal Tragedy While Shooting Series Finale How ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Wraps Up Series After 5 Seasons View All August 9, 2026 8:00pm Patina Miller as Raquel and Mekai Curtis as Kanan Starz SPOILER ALERT: The following reveals major plot points from the series finale of the Starz crime drama Power Book III: Raising Kanan . It’s no spoiler to discuss Kanan Stark’s survival in the series finale of Starz’s Power Book III: Raising Kanan , with even the most casual of fans knowing that Kanan Stark is alive and well in the original Power series. While it’s the closing of another chapter in the Power franchise, there’s still some time to spend with Mekai Curtis as the titular Kanan before going into Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson’s era. But before going into new business, let’s handle old business. Raquel (Patina Miller) was shot and killed in cold blood by Jukebox (Hailey Kilgore) in the show’s final episode. Raq was a surrogate mother to Juke, but when it came down to it, Juke had to avenge her father’s murder at the hands of Kanan. She told her cousin while at the diner that she had killed his mother so as to take everyone that cares about him out of his life. Kanan was rather accepting of the news, something the actor confirms. Related Stories News 'Power Book III: Raising Kanan' Star Patina Miller On Tackling Personal Tragedy While Shooting Series Finale News Starz Subscriber Levels Climbed In Q2 Despite Price Increase, CEO Jeff Hirsch Says “It’s acceptance. That’s the ultimate version of Kanan understanding what Raq taught him at the beginning of the series. Now, more than ever, in Season 5, I think Kanan understands who he is and what he’s done more than ever. When you’ve experienced enough loss and tragedy, there comes a point where you’re going to sit down and just take inventory: you’re going to see where you went wrong, what you did right, where other people went wrong, and how things could have been done differently,” shared Curtis. Watch on Deadline Adding, “Kanan has gotten to have those moments. So, when he finally hears that Mom is gone, he understands. It doesn’t mean it hurts any less, but he understands all the bad he’s done. And for it to be his cousin when he just took out her father, it’s poetic, right? He understands, ‘Okay, I did it.’ It doesn’t mean that I’m proud that I did it, but I did it.” Hailey Kilgore as Jukebox and Mekai Curtis as Kanan Before that moment at the diner, Kanan and Raq met up on a very public street to discuss the hit Stefano (Tony Danza) put on her, amongst other things. The duo opened up like never before. “I wasn’t sure that that was a conversation that was going to happen. So I was casting the line in the wind, ‘No, this is still my mother. I still love this person. These characters, this world, and this show could have been flat and stereotypical if we didn’t add these layers that have you ask questions beyond what you’re seeing. It was really fun to finally have that moment to justify the actions of all of the characters leading up to that, especially for me,” Curtis reflected. He continued, “I feel like Kanan is so misunderstood, especially the younger version of him. You see he’s doing things out of emotion, and he doesn’t know how to articulate himself. But it’s not simply just to be doing it. It’s not simply to ignore the thoughts and the wisdom of the people around him. He’s simply trying to find himself outside of the things that he’s now been shown. He can’t trust in the way that he wants.” Part of that, Curtis explained, was Kanan saying, “You did these things, and it hurt me, and I didn’t know how to say that it hurt me because I was never taught how. But I still love you.” “It was a constant back and forth between Raq and Kanan showing or saying that they love each other, but missing the mark,” he said. “I think they both had different love languages, and they didn’t know how to come together and actually healthily do that until imminent death was in the air.” Playing Kanan across 5 seasons as part of this crazy world of Southside, Jamaica, Queens, the lesson that the actor is taking with him is a pretty special one. “The lesson is love for me. Not to get all preachy about it, but love is patient. It’s kind. It’s giving space when you need it. It’s letting that person come back when they’re ready. It’s ugly. It’s nasty, and that’s everything that you see happen with these characters on the show, but that’s also everything that’s happened behind the scenes,” said Curtis. “I think there’s a rare level of vulnerability and safety that was fostered on this set that allowed us to translate with these characters even more. The lesson for me is: keep your heart open. Keep your heart guarded, but always be open and ready for the things that are around you. Be ready to receive, be ready to give,” he added. Spence Moore (“Ghost”), Charlie Mann (“Tommy”), and Mekai Curtis (“Kanan Stark”) Onto new business, Curtis has already completed work on the first season of the brand new prequel series Power: Origins , a continuation of Raising Kanan , both shows from creator Sascha Penn. Power: Origins will reunite young James St. Patrick (Spence Moore II) and young Tommy Egan (Charlie Mann) with young Kanan. As a quick reminder, teen versions of James and Tommy appeared in the finale of Raising Kanan , played by Maxwell Davis and Andrew Bennett, respectively. At about 13 years old, the boys tried to work with Kanan, but even he had his limits. “That honestly is my favorite part because that is the crossroads that carries through into Origins. You can still see a slight shred of care. Kanan sees himself in these two kids, and while it is exciting, he’s like, “Oh, we can get into all the things.’ It’s still like, ‘Nah, they’re still too young. I’m not gonna be the person that exposes you to whatever is going to bring you back here. We get to see how he still kind of cares and nurtures them in Origins .” Second Fastest To Cross $1B WW; Third Best 2nd U.S. Frame With $145M ‘House Of The Dragon’s Ryan Condal And Emma D’Arcy On Season 3 Finale Now Christopher Nolan’s Highest-Grossing Globally With $1.1B A24’s Anthony Bourdain Biopic ‘Tony’ A Top 2026 Limited Opening Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Justice Smith Promises ‘Heated Rivalry’ Fans To “Take Good Care” Of Harris Drover “If You Give Me A Chance”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By The Deadline Team The Deadline Team More Stories By The Deadline Noah Wyle & Katherine LaNasa To Help Celebrate Writers Guild Foundation’s 60th Anniversary With ‘Star Trek’ Table Read ‘The Write Path’ Seminar For Emerging Writers Returns For Second Year With Insights From ATX TV, SeriesFest, Sundance Institute & The Black List Owl Screenwriting Workshop Taking Submissions For 2027 Program Via The Black List & Athens Film Office View All August 9, 2026 8:18pm Justice Smith at the Deadline Portrait Studio during the 34th Annual Gotham Awards held at Cipriani Wall Street on Dec. 2, 2024 in New York City. Matt Doyle/Deadline The casting of most beloved literary characters in screen adaptation inevitably creates online discourse as fans of the books have their own preconceived notions for what the characters should look like. Heated Rivalry is no exception, with the announcement on Friday that Justice Smith and Charlie Gillespie will play Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, respectively, in Season 2 of the hugely popular series based on Rachel Reid’s Game Changer books, triggering a strong reaction. Smith appeared to address the discourse on his Instagram Story. “I am moved by the support and love I’m getting from fans in my dms, fans who have welcomed me with open arms and who already feel a responsibility to protect me.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News 'Heated Rivalry' Author Appears To Dismiss Negative Reactions To Season 2 Casting News What To Expect For 'Heated Rivalry' Season 2: Everything We Know So Far The protecting part is likely a reference to negative comments posted online, a lot of them pointed at Smith’s casting. “I am honored to play a character that you all care about deeply and I promise that I will take good care of him if you give me the chance,” he wrote, adding, “I am beyond excited for the experience.” The negative online response to the Harris and Troy castings also prompted Reid to remind fans that Connor Storrie and Hudson Williams — now loved around the world for their portrayal of Ilya Rozanov and Shane Hollander, respectively — weren’t an easy sell either. “Thinking about all the people last summer who told me the casting for llya and Shane was wrong and bad…,” Reid wrote on her Instagram Story. Harris Drover and Troy Barrett are the central couple in Role Model, the fifth book in Reid’s bestselling Game Changer series, which is being used as source material for Season 2 alongside the Ilya and Shane follow-up book, The Long Game. Troy is a hockey player on Ilya’s team with a history of bullying, while Harris is the team’s cheerful social media manager, “From the start of the casting process, we knew we were looking for actors who could create something truly special together and bring that same depth and heart to the screen,” Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney and fellow executive producer Brendan Brady said on Friday about the search for Harris and Troy. “Justice and Charlie do exactly that. articles.title: Zurich & El Gouna Film Festivals Strike Strategic Partnership Kicking Off With ‘Dolphins: My Close Encounters’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Zurich & El Gouna Film Festivals Strike Strategic Partnership Kicking Off With ‘Dolphins: My Close Encounters’ Netflix Reunites With Guillaume Canet On Sequel To Hit Action-Thriller ‘Ad Vitam’ James Gray Talks Dream Quality Of Cinema & Approach With Cast: “I’m Not A Good Director Of Actors” – Locarno View All August 10, 2026 1:30am Christian Jungen, Samih Sawiris, Reta Guetg, Amr Mansi, Andrew Mohsen Courtesy EXCLUSIVE: Switzerland ’s Zurich Film Festival (ZFF) and Egypt ‘s El Gouna Film Festival (GFF) have struck a strategic partnership, which will see them collaborate on programming and other initiatives. The alliance will kick off at ZFF’s upcoming 22nd edition, running September 24 to October 4, with the world premiere of feature documentary Dolphins: My Close Encounters , following Swiss marine biologist Angela Ziltener and her decades-long dolphin research conducted in the Red Sea. The film will then get its MENA Premiere at GFF, running from October 15 to 26, just miles from the coastline where Ziltener first began her groundbreaking research. Related Stories News Martin McDonagh To Receive Zurich Film Festival Honorary Award At Gala Screening For 'Wild Horse Nine' News Watermelon Pictures Takes North America For Umm Kulthum Biopic 'El Sett' ZFF entered a new chapter in 2025 following a management buyout led by CEO Christian Jungen. It has seen its star rise in recent years as a launch-pad for fall releases in Switzerland and key stop-off on the awards seasons circuit for international films. It is the second-largest film festival in the German-speaking world, drawing 135,000 visitors in 2025. Watch on Deadline At the same time, it has also forged strong links with other festivals, notably San Sebastian with which it cooperates on industry and festival guests. GFF was launched in 2017 by Egyptian tycoons Naguib and Samih Sawiris in the Red Sea resort of El Gouna created by latter and has risen to become a key date on the MENA fall festival calendar. “Samih Sawiris has been familiar with the Zurich Film Festival for many years, and we’ve had inspiring strategic conversations. Now we are joining forces”, said ZFF CEO Christian Jungen. “This is a true win-win partnership. We can help the El Gouna Film Festival gain access to films and talent while they provide us with invaluable logistical support and guide us on our way to gain new perspectives while navigating the film landscape of Africa and the Middle East. We are excited to collaborate with this dynamic and fast-growing festival.” Sawiris said the partnership would bolster GFF’s founding mission of connecting regional and international film industries at an event showing world-class cinema and fostering dialogue and social impact. “Partnering with a festival as prestigious as Zurich marks an exciting extension of this mission, reflecting a shared commitment to fostering meaningful exchange across outstanding cinema and industry leaders,” said Sawiris. The partners said the new new alliance would also also help connect Middle East and African filmmakers with their European counterparts. “For the better part of a decade, El Gouna Film Festival has worked tirelessly to give filmmakers in this part of the world a platform for them to collaborate and create films that share stories from the region with the rest of the world,” said GFF Artistic Director Andrew Mohsen. “Moreover, we have worked to provide countless opportunities for up-and-coming filmmakers to develop their skills and meet with industry leaders from around the world. This partnership with ZFF will facilitate the creation of synergies with others in the industry from various parts of the world.” “As a film festival, building bridges is one of our key functions,” said ZFF Director Reta Guetg. “We want to connect people who share our beliefs and utilize films as powerful ambassadors of cultural exchange. That is exactly what this new friendship and partnership stands for.” Dolphins: My Close Encounters As the first film presented jointly by the two festivals, Dolphins: My Close Encounters connects Zurich and the Red Sea by focusing on nature: Its protagonist Ziltener has been studying the behaviours of wild dolphin populations in the waters off the Egyptian town of El Gouna for years. Directed by Barny Revill and produced by natural history producer Silverback Films, with Keith Scholey as executive producer, the film traces Ziltener’s more than 15 years diving alongside wild dolphins, slowly gaining a rare window into their lives. What began as a scientific study became something far more personal, as she found herself drawn into the dolphins’ world and faced with a profound question: who was really observing whom? articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Zurich & El Gouna Film Festivals Strike Strategic Partnership Kicking Off With ‘Dolphins: My Close Encounters’ Netflix Reunites With Guillaume Canet On Sequel To Hit Action-Thriller ‘Ad Vitam’ James Gray Talks Dream Quality Of Cinema & Approach With Cast: “I’m Not A Good Director Of Actors” – Locarno View All August 10, 2026 2:00am Al Baraneya Baldr Film-Seera Films-Czar Film EXCLUSIVE: Mad World , the film sales arm of Cairo-based Mad Solutions , has acquired worldwide sales rights to Egyptian drama Al Baraneya ahead of its premiere in Venice parallel section Giornate degli Autori. The debut feature of Dutch-Egyptian filmmaker Ashgan El-Hamus, the film follows the fate of Al Amal, a pregnant young woman living with her extended family in the Egyptian village of Al Baraneya. When the family is offered the chance to sell their land, long-held certainties begin to unravel, leaving Amal torn between the traditions that shaped her and the promise of a different future in the city. Related Stories News Zurich & El Gouna Film Festivals Strike Strategic Partnership Kicking Off With 'Dolphins: My Close Encounters' News Watermelon Pictures Takes North America For Umm Kulthum Biopic 'El Sett' Produced by Frank Hoeve of Amsterdam-based Baldr Film; Kesmat Elsayed of Berlin-based Seera Films, and Eurydice Gysel of Brussels-based Czar Film, Al Baraneya is a Dutch-Egyptian-Belgian-Saudi co-production. Watch on Deadline The acquisition marks Mad World’s second collaboration with Seera’s Elsayed after their collaboration on Mohamed Rashad’s Berlinale 2025-selected The Settlemen t. Amsterdam-based Baldr Film has built an international reputation for championing auteur-driven cinema, with recent credits including the Oscar-nominated documentary Soundtrack to a Coup d’État ; Cannes Grand Prix winner All We Imagine as Light ; Willem van Ewijk’s Venice Giornate degli Autori Best European Film winner Alpha , and Torino Film Festival winner The Garden of Earthly Delights . Al Baraneya is El-Hamus’ feature directorial debut following a series of acclaimed short films, including Birdland . Drawing from her own family’s experiences, she cast her Egyptian relatives alongside actress Reem Amer to create an authentic portrait of family, womanhood, and belonging. “I wanted to tell a story about belonging, womanhood, and the quiet tension between tradition and change through characters whose relationships feel lived rather than performed,” she says of the film. “We’re delighted to bring Al Baraneya to international audiences,” said Alaa Karkouti and Maher Diab, co-founders of Mad Solutions. “Ashgan El-Hamus has crafted a deeply personal and emotionally resonant debut that reflects the richness of Arab storytelling through a universal lens. articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Becomes Biggest Hollywood Film Of All Time In India; As First Half Box Office Show Signs Of Market Recovery
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz ReelShort On Course To Reach $1BN Revenue & First Profit In 2026 – MPA Report Michelle Yeoh Named As Busan International Film Festival’s Asian Filmmaker Of The Year Warner Bros Korea Sets September Release For ‘The Intern’ Remake, Starring Choi Min-sik & Han So-hee View All August 10, 2026 2:24am Spider-Man: Brand New Day Sony/Marvel Spider-Man: Brand New Day is now the highest-grossing Hollywood film of all time in India after taking $10.6M over the weekend for a cumulative $52.8M take. The film, starring Tom Holland and Zendaya, overtook the record previously held by James Cameron’s 2022 Avatar: The Way Of Water after only 11 days of release. Opening in India on July 30, the day before its global release, the film has not faced much competition, although two big local films – Batwara 1947 , starring Sunny Deol, and Nitin Kakkar’s Awarapan 2, starring Emraan Hashmi – are set to open this coming weekend. It’s been a strong summer for Hollywood films in India, with both Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey , which opened on July 17, and Obsession , an early summer release on May 29, reportedly grossing more than the INR1B ($10M) benchmark. Related Stories News Indian Star Sayani Gupta Sets U.S. Feature Debut With 'Arya' News Summer Domestic Box Office On A Hot Streak, Will Cross $4B By Monday Hollywood and other foreign films usually only have a 10-15% share of the Indian market, where local fare dominates. In 2025, international films clocked up a 10% market share with Avatar: Fire And Ash the top-grossing Hollywood film on $26.4M, according to Ormax Media figures. In comparison, the highest-grossing local film last year, Hindi-language action epic Dhurandhar , took $104.8m Watch on Deadline In the first half of 2026, international films had an 8% share, with Obsession grossing around $10M (INR1B) and Project Hail Mary on $9.2M (INR880M). Dhurandhar: The Revenge topped the first half chart with $132m. Overall, India is having an encouraging year at the box office . Ormax Media has reported that revenues for the six months January to June 2026 reached $661.66M (INR63.98B), making it the highest-grossing first half of any year since the pandemic, and surpassing the first half of 2025 by around 10%. Upcoming films include Geetu Mohandas’ Toxic, starring Yash, scheduled for August 26; and Ramayana: Part 1, which is expected for Diwali in November and was recently picked up by Sony for worldwide distribution. Harris, who co-founded Neal Street Productions with Sam Mendes, is currently filming The Beatles – A Four Film Cinematic Event , four separate theatrical biopic films about the British quartet starring Paul Mescal, Joseph Quinn, Barry Keoghan and Harris Dickinson. Mendes is directing the project. Harris will join LFF for a deep dive into her pioneering work, including The Beatles films, as well as discussing the challenges of development and production and her relationship with filmmakers and talent across her career. Her credits include Oscar, Golden Globe and BAFTA winning films Hamnet and 1917 , Oscar and BAFTA nominated Revolutionary Road , British box office hit The Magic Faraway Tree with Andrew Garfield and Claire Foy and Jarhead . Harris is also behind a raft of hit TV productions including Call the Midwife , Penny Dreadful , Britannia , The Hollow Crown and Stuart, A Life Backwards . Related Stories Festivals 'Elsinore' Starring Andrew Scott & Olivia Colman To Open London Film Festival News 'The Magic Faraway Tree': Feelgood Fantasy Pic Based On Enid Blyton Novels Won At UK Box Office With Sequels On The Way Prominent indie producer Wilson, who has been in the business for more than thirty years, will join LFF to discuss his career and bold creative collaborations. He has worked with visionary indie filmmakers to great creative and commercial success on films including Oscar and BAFTA winning The Zone of Interest and Under the Skin , both from Jonathan Glazer, Lynne Ramsay’s You Were Never Really Here , Kaouther Ben Hania’s The Voice of Hind Rajab , Aneil Karia’s Hamlet , Iain Forsyth and Jane Pollard’s 20,000 Days on Earth and Sophie Fiennes’ The Pervert’s Guide to Ideology . Watch on Deadline In the conversation, Wilson will touch on his key career moments from his years at Fox Searchlight Pictures and Film4, where he was a production executive on films such as Sexy Beast and Dancer in the Dark through to the creation of his own company JW Films. “This year our industry programme puts a spotlight on producers and the vital role they play in shepherding artistic visions from their earliest stages through to the screen,” said BFI London Film Festival Director Kristy Matheson. “I’m delighted that industry colleagues will have the opportunity to hear from Pippa Harris and James Wilson – two esteemed producers whose unique creative careers have given us some of the most memorable and critically acclaimed films of recent years.” The 70 th edition of the BFI London Film Festival takes place October 7-18, 2026. The Industry Forum Spotlight and Discussion events take place October 8-15. articles.title: Katie Maloney Wasn’t Interested in Reality TV After ‘Vanderpump Rules.’ Then Came Stassi Schroeder
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 8, 2026 12:00pm Katie Maloney at the 'House of Stassi' premiere in New York. Disney/Arthur Gareev Logo text Katie Maloney wasn’t rushing back to reality television after Vanderpump Rules aired its last season with the original cast in 2024. But then, Stassi Schroeder called. Longtime friends who starred alongside one another throughout the golden years of the Emmy-nominated Bravo series, Schroeder invited Maloney to appear on her new Hulu series House of Stassi after the core cast had been assembled. It’s a topic discussed on the new series, which dropped on the streamer on July 29. During their first onscreen sit-down, a first meeting after a fallout a few years back, at the Belmont (an obvious Vanderpump Rules callback), Maloney gives it to Schroeder straight. Related Stories TV Barbarians at the Gate: How Reality Stars Crashed Hollywood's A-List TV Stassi Schroeder Knew Her Hulu Series Would Cause a Stir: "We Set Out to Make the Realest Show We Could" “You just make your world smaller and smaller and smaller to the point where it’s like if, I don’t know, they didn’t come out of you or they’re not married to you or they’re not on your fucking payroll, they don’t get to be in your life,” Maloney told her friend, cut to a scene of Schroeder, who is an executive producer, uttering, “Damn, this bitch is good. And that’s the type of truth-telling we need on reality TV . I need her to do this show.” Maloney tells The Hollywood Reporter that she wouldn’t have signed up for another reality TV show if it weren’t for “the people that are involved.” She adds, “Knowing Stassi’s history with reality TV and her perspective on it, how she wanted to navigate doing the show was something that I really aligned with.” “Especially coming off of a show like Vanderpump Rules , which was very successful for a long time, but really did kind of, at the end, take a toll on me,” Maloney says, continuing, “I just knew that if I was going to return, it would have to be for something that felt very different, and that absolutely was the case. I just really trusted the producers and the whole production team, and it just was exciting.” Katie Maloney sits down with Stassi Schroeder on House of Stassi. Disney Maloney knew the series was in the works (it was first announced in August 2024, three months before Bravo revealed it was rebooting Vanderpump Rules ), but “never considered [joining the cast] to be an option for a number of reasons.” “I didn’t know where they were in the process,” Maloney explains, adding that she quickly learned they hadn’t started shooting for House of Stassi , and things fell into place. “I don’t know. There was just something that, maybe just innately in my gut, told me like, this is the time ,” she says. A seasoned reality star, Maloney was “cautious” about joining a new show and the cycle that emerges while starring on an active series. “That’s a lot of what I’ve been enjoying away from reality TV, out of the public eye and constant attention,” she says, “but at the same time, I’m pretty used to this, so I have a pretty good handle on it.” She also admits she wasn’t eager to jump at other reality TV experiences after Vanderpump Rules ended. “Obviously, the same production team that worked on Vanderpump Rules worked on The Valley , and I, just through casual conversations, have made it clear that that was not something I’d ever be interested in. But I didn’t really have the interest for a while in participating in reality TV.” Maloney worked with Bravo for over a decade; she was one of three original cast members to remain on Vanderpump Rules for its 11-season tenure before the network rebooted the show. House of Stassi ushers her onto a new network on Hulu and Freeform, which Disney backs. “I’m trying to not compare it constantly,” Maloney says when asked about the differences in starring on a new network. “It’s hard because, like with anything, that’s sort of my only frame of reference. But I’m trying to just treat it like it’s something entirely new that I’ve never been a part of.” Maloney did bring one part of her Vanderpump past over to House of Stassi : an Ariana Madix cameo. “She without hesitation agreed to do it,” Maloney says, explaining that she told Madix she wanted to film at their West Hollywood sandwich shop Something About Her . “I was never going to press [Ariana] or ask her to be part of it beyond that, but I was just happy that she was so supportive,” she says. “Also, we worked so hard to get our sandwich shop open, so it was important that for the first time us filming there, that she was there for that.” On the new series, some House of Stassi castmembers raised their quarrels with Maloney joining their cast. She admits she did not know people like Kristina Kelly and Taylor Strecker had such strong hesitations about her being back around their friend group. “Not prior to going into it. Obviously, I found out quickly that some people had issues,” she says. One comment she was not given a heads up about before the show dropped came from Schroeder’s husband Beau Clark, who said he hoped Schroeder reconnecting with Maloney wouldn’t shift his wife’s behavior. “The only [comment] I had no idea that was said was Beau’s reaction. And obviously Stassi and I having our friendship break that we had, that’s his wife, he’s gonna have her back, but he was pretty passionate in his feelings about me,” Maloney says. “That one stung a little bit too because I’ve always loved Beau and really gotten along with him, so kind of sucked to hear.” Stassi Schroeder, Kristina Kelly and Katie Maloney celebrate the premiere of House of Stassi. Disney/Arthur Gareev A House of Stassi moment of Maloney’s that stuck out was a confessional interview before the season’s disastrous Queen Mary finale dinner party, where Schroeder and Clark’s friends and family brought up concerns about their marriage. “I know how common affairs are and how they happen, and I’ve experienced the beginning stages of it,” she said on the show, sharing her experience of emotional abandonment in her marriage and how she found connection outside of that relationship. Some viewers thought Maloney was speaking about Tom Schwartz’s infidelities in their former marriage, but Maloney confirms she “was talking about myself,” and that “not that many people have caught onto” her admission in the finale episode. “I’ve seen it happen over and over too in people’s lives that I know. If you stop and think about it, five times out of five times, when someone ends their marriage or long-term relationship, the common thing that’s said at the end is, ‘I felt like we were roommates,’” she says. “And that’s when you feel emotional abandonment, and that’s when, and I’m speaking from my perspective on things and other people’s perspectives, but I think that it’s so common.” “It wasn’t necessarily like a singular person or anything,” Maloney adds. “I just was aware so clearly of where I stood emotionally within my marriage and relationship, and some people choose to explore that well out without exiting the relationship armors, because that’s a more difficult thing to do. I recognized that that was my time.” Moving forward with a potential second season of House of Stassi , Maloney says she’d be on board: “I think that would be a lot of fun. I’d love to.” As for what to expect from her, she’d want to “repair and build some of the fractures in the relationships that I have,” while also continuing to grow her friendship with Schroeder. “[I want to] grow my relationship with Stassi from where we are now in this season of life that’s so different than the one that we met each other in,” Maloney says. “I just am excited to see where that goes and takes us.” *** Season one of House of Stassi is now streaming on Hulu. THR

articles.title: Monica Barbaro Teases Luca Guadagnino’s OpenAI Film ‘Artificial,’ Addresses Timothée Chalamet’s Ballet Comments
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 8, 2026 1:35pm Timothée Chalamet and Monica Barbaro Kate Green/Getty Images for The Walt Disney Company Limited Monica Barbaro is in the thick of her rom-com summer — and she’s opening up about what’s next. In a wide-ranging interview with Josh Horowitz on his Happy Sad Confused podcast to promote her new film, One Night Only , Barbaro teased what audiences can expect from Luca Guadagnino ‘s Artificial , the upcoming film about the OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, starring Andrew Garfield. “One day, we would show up, and Luca would be like, ‘This is a — what was the word he used? A zany comedy?’ No. ‘Madcap,’” the actress said. “He would basically be like, ‘This is a madcap comedy.’ Then the next day, he’d be like, ‘It’s a horror story.’” Related Stories Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swinging to Best-Ever 10-Day Start With $143M Second Weekend Movies Luca Guadagnino to Receive Venice Festival's Glory to the Filmmaker Award She added, “Having seen it, I’m like, ‘Yeah, it’s all of it.’ But, to be clear, I don’t think it suffers at all from a lack of tone or confusion of tone. I think, in reality, it kind of is all of that.” In June, Amazon MGM Studios announced it was dropping the feature just months after Amazon entered into a $50 billion investment with OpenAI. Neon later landed the film. Barbaro also discussed Simon Rich’s script, which was inspired by real events. “We were dealing with really challenging material in terms of what we’re saying about people who are alive,” she said. “I feel like this had a particular kind of flavor to it, as far as his films are concerned, because it’s based on real events. I think it’s probably different from the way he might usually work, or our task was so heavily research-based.” Last month, Garfield shared his reaction to the film’s move to Neon with The Hollywood Reporter: “I’m really grateful to Amazon for making the film with us, and I’m also really grateful to Amazon for helping it find a new home,” he said. “I think Neon’s a really, really exciting home for it. I think it’s a really good fit and I’m really excited to release it with them.” Elsewhere in her Happy Sad Confused interview, Barbaro addressed comments made earlier this year by her A Complete Unknown co-star Timothée Chalamet, when he was asked whether audiences still have an interest in slower-paced movies. In his response, he said he wouldn’t want to be involved in an art form that “no one cares about,” citing ballet and opera as examples. “I don’t want to be working in ballet or opera where it’s like, ‘Hey! Keep this thing alive, even though no one cares about this anymore,’” Chalamet said at the time . “All respect to the ballet and opera people out there.” “You’re the first person to ask me about this,” Barbaro said in response to Horowitz. “I can’t possibly know exactly where he was coming from when he said that, but one of the conversations we had on set was about his sister being a dancer, and he was actually saying it from a very hats-off, respect, kind of place.” Barbaro said she interpreted Chalamet’s comments as being more about declining audiences for ballet and opera than a lack of respect for the art forms themselves. “I feel like that was something where he was expressing something in a way that made it sound like it was about respect for the art form, when really I think it is about audiences for that art form. And I do think audiences are dwindling for those kinds of art forms,” she said. Barbaro herself comes from a dance background, having trained in ballet before pursuing acting. “I don’t know that that’s what he was saying, but that’s my personal takeaway. I’m a Gemini. I try to see all sides. I think in a way, there is some truth to that statement in a way that I would like to not lead with offense.” Watch the full interview below. THR

articles.title: Perez Hilton’s Condition “Serious But Stable” Amid Hospitalization, Will Require Surgery
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 8, 2026 3:13pm Perez Hilton Ethan Miller/Getty Images Perez Hilton ’s family is clearing up misinformation about his communication with the media and sharing a new update on his health following his disturbing livestream earlier this week. The celebrity gossip blogger remains hospitalized in Florida, where his condition is “serious but stable,” and he will require surgery in the coming days, according to his family. In a new statement shared on Hilton’s website Saturday, his family confirmed that he remains hospitalized under Florida’s Baker Act, writing, “His communication has been extremely limited and confined to immediate family, medical providers, and others directly involved in his care. He has not communicated with the media or issued any public statements.” Related Stories News Perez Hilton's Children Were Inside Home Minutes Before Disturbing Livestream, Family Says TV Perez Hilton "Reached Out" to Britney Spears, Neil Patrick Harris to Make Amends Before Livestream That Led to Hospitalization The family also clarified that the only credible updates about Hilton’s condition are those published directly on his website, PerezHilton.com. “Perez’s condition remains serious but stable. He experienced significant blood loss and sustained additional injuries that will require surgery in the coming days,” the statement reads. “His treatment and recovery will be a long process. We are grateful that Perez was able to spend time with his mother and sister yesterday.” Hilton’s family also asked for privacy as he continues his recovery and for the media and public to stay away from their property. “We respectfully ask members of the media, paparazzi, content creators, and the public to leave the area surrounding the family’s home and not return,” the statement reads. The latest statement follows an update from Thursday , when Hilton’s family revealed that his children were inside his home just minutes before his livestream. “The events of the past several days have been nearly unbearable for our family. Just minutes before the public livestream incident, Perez’s children, niece, and sister were inside the home,” the family wrote. “When it became clear that Perez was experiencing a severe mental health crisis and harming himself, they immediately fled to protect the children from witnessing any further trauma.” On Tuesday night, Hilton was on a livestream where he was seen covered in blood and appeared to use an object to cut himself repeatedly. Clips of the livestream were re-shared on social media and went viral. Deputies responded to the 48-year-old’s home after the Miami-Dade County Sheriff’s Office received “multiple calls regarding an individual who was livestreaming acts of self-harm on social media.” The following day, Hilton’s TikTok account was banned . Hilton, whose real name is Mario Armando Lavandeira Jr., rose to fame in the early 2000s after launching his controversial celebrity gossip blog. The site was known for publishing tabloid photos, which he captioned with his own “doodles.” THR

articles.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Author Rachel Reid Pushes Back Against Season 2 Casting Criticism
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nicole Fell Plus Icon Nicole Fell Associate Editor nicolemfell Follow Sign Up View All August 8, 2026 5:08pm Brendan Brady, Jacob Tierney, Ksenia Daniela Kharlamova, Dylan Walsh, Hudson Williams, Connor Storrie, Christina Chang and Rachel Reid attend the premiere of 'Heated Rivalry' at TIFF Lightbox on November 24, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario. Harold Feng/Getty Images Logo text Rachel Reid is pushing back against negative comments about Heated Rivalry ‘s latest season two casting . The author, who wrote the novels that the show is based upon, took to Instagram Friday to weigh into online debate about the casting of the characters Troy Barrett and Harris Drover in the upcoming season. It was announced Friday that Charlie Gillespie was cast as Troy, a professional hockey player who is traded to the Ottawa Centaurs in Reid’s source material, while Justice Smith was cast as Harris, the team’s social media manager. “Thinking about all the people last summer who told me the casting for Ilya and Shane was wrong and bad…” she wrote on an Instagram story. Some fans online were criticizing the decision to cast a “skinny” actor to play the character of Harris, who was described as chubbier than the hockey players of the book. Related Stories TV 'Heated Rivalry' Season 2 Finds Its Troy and Harris in Charlie Gillespie and Justice Smith TV 'Heated Rivalry' to Fans: Please Don't Crash the Season 2 Set Harris and Troy’s budding relationship drives Reid’s novel Role Model , the fifth installment of her Game Changers series, which Heated Rivalry the series is based on. “Rachel Reid has given us two beautifully layered characters in Harris and Troy who you can’t help but root for,” showrunner Jacob Tierney and executive producer Brendan Brady said in a release about the casting. “From the start of the casting process, we knew we were looking for actors who could create something truly special together and bring that same depth and heart to the screen. Justice and Charlie do exactly that,” the statement continued. “They immediately connected with the vulnerability and resilience at the core of these characters, bringing an instinctive understanding of who Harris and Troy are.” Ottawa is expected to be the season two home for main character Ilya Rozanov, played by Connor Storrie , who moves to the low-ranking Canadian team. The Russian hockey player made the decision to move to the team in the finale of the show’s first season to be closer to Heated Rivalry ’s other main character and his now-boyfriend, Shane Hollander, played by Hudson Williams . Crave renewed Heated Rivalry for a second season early into the show’s first season run. HBO Max has confirmed it will continue to air the series. The show will begin shooting its second season this month and is aiming for a spring 2027 release . Tierney serves as writer, director and executive producer on the series. Brady and Jayme Alter Wilson serve as executive producers, alongside Lori Fischburg and Liane Cunje as producers. Reid serves as a consulting producer. Mike Goldbach joins season two as co-writer alongside Tierney. THR

articles.title: The ‘One Night Only’ Writer and Producer Have Seen Your Questions and Have (Some of) the Answers
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Hilary Lewis Plus Icon Hilary Lewis Deputy Editor, East Coast hilarylewis Follow Sign Up View All August 8, 2026 5:31pm Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner in 'One Night Only.' Nicole Rivelli/Universal Pictures Ever since the official trailer dropped for the Callum Turner – Monica Barbaro rom-com One Night Only , quickly racking up millions of views on its way to its nearly 40 million total, internet commentators have had a lot of questions about the film’s central premise in which premarital sex is illegal apart from one 12-hour period a year. How is this law enforced? Are people breaking the law? How did this legislation pass? What counts as “sex” under this new mandate? Are marriage (and divorce) rates skyrocketing? What about affairs? Related Stories Movies Monica Barbaro Teases Luca Guadagnino's OpenAI Film 'Artificial,' Addresses Timothée Chalamet's Ballet Comments Movies 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Swinging to Best-Ever 10-Day Start With $143M Second Weekend Rest assured: Some of those questions are answered in the movie, and explanations are starting to trickle out online for those unconcerned about spoilers. Beyond that, One Night Only writer, Travis Braun, who saw his screenplay top the 2024 Black List, has answers, but they’re not all in the Will Gluck -directed Universal movie now in theaters. “I set out to write a movie about the circus that is modern dating, and I thought how fun if we could set that all in one night, and I have answers to those questions, and some of them are in the movie,” Braun told The Hollywood Reporter at the One Night Only premiere earlier this week in New York. Braun said he definitely thought about the specific rules of the film’s alternate reality, framed as three years on from the no-sex act being passed, but didn’t want to get too deep into the politics of the world of the movie. “There’s a big mythology that I’ve built out and then as you develop a movie you start to pare down and you go: What does an audience really care about, and what are they showing up to see? For me the answer is always a love story, romance,” he told THR . “I hope they can come in and we’ll show them how this world functions, and then they can just enjoy the movie and have fun. The whole focus of this was love story and romance first, and the world-building obviously has to make sense and has to be there, but ultimately we weren’t interested in getting into the politics of it. We wanted to tell a story about these two incredible people trying to find love on this crazy night.” Producer Jacqueline Monetta, who brought Braun’s script to Gluck, said they didn’t want moviegoers to have all of the answers. “I had a million questions. I was like, ‘What does this mean? What does this world look like? How do people communicate? What’s different?’ And that’s I think what’s so smart about it,” she said of One Night Only ‘s “big idea, high-concept” premise. “We don’t answer every question in the movie, purposefully, because we want those questions to be had on the car ride home. We want people to keep talking about it and really think about what would this mean for our world, what does it mean for our world now. But I think Will and I were really specific on what questions we wanted to answer.” In a recent Reddit AMA , Gluck also detailed how he and his team approached the world building of the movie while not wanting it to be all about the mandate and offered prospective moviegoers hints for where to find the answers to their questions. “We spent a lot of time talking about the rules of the world, and if you’ve seen the movie, or when you see the movie, you’ll see that the rules of the world and the world building are all in the background,” he said. “It’s on TVs, signage, in thrown-away lines, because we didn’t want to give the world short shrift, but we didn’t want the movie to be about that. It’s another way I want people to see this. If they see it more than once, they’ll pick up so many more rules of the world in the background. A lot of the questions that I’ve been getting after people have seen the movie are actually answered in the movie, which is by design because I want people maybe not to know them. So, yes, it was a tricky tightrope to have them there, but not for the movie to be about it.” Turner meanwhile echoes Braun’s advice for curious prospective moviegoers: “Go see the film!” “You’ll realize pretty quickly what the realm is that you’re working within and it’s a comedy,” Turner says of what inquisitive filmgoers will find. “There are no great political undertones, I don’t think. This is just a place where you can escape for an hour and a half, two hours and enjoy and laugh your head off.” One Night Only is now in theaters. Callum Turner and Monica Barbaro at the One Night Only premiere on Monday. Roy Rochlin/Getty Images for Universal Pictures THR

The song went on to win the Grammy Award for Best Pop Vocal Performance, and its legacy has continued to this day, with “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” topping Billboard’s list of the 500 Best Pop Songs of All Time , among other accolades. “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” was also the name of the well-received 2022 Houston biopic , which starred Naomi Ackie as the music legend. Amazon WATCH THE FILM Whitney Houston: I Wanna Dance with Somebody (Blu-ray) $15.99 $25.99 38% off Buy Now ON AMAZON $3.99 RENT Now oN AMAZON The film is streaming free on Prime Video , though you can also rent it or purchase the movie on Blu-ray (the Blu-ray disc includes a digital code that you can redeem for a download of the film online). articles.title: ‘Objet a’ Explores Desire and Control in an Age When We “Touch Flat Screens More Than Our Lover’s Skin”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 8, 2026 11:03pm 'Objet a' film still Courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G./Schuldenberg Films Ingeborg and Adam are visionary hand surgeons who are bound by love, control and irresistible fixations. Ingeborg, for one, feels compelled to steal objects. Adam longs to become one. But after an accident, their well-choreographed lives suddenly face a force that could upset the careful balance that has long defined their relationship: the enigmatic Gaia. With her arrival, unexpected desires start springing up. With Objet a , her new mind-bending and visceral feature, Berlin-based visual artist and filmmaker Ann Oren ( Piaffe ) returns to Locarno. It is a stylized cinematic exploration of the fragile relationships between humans, as well as humans and nature. And it is likely to make you look and think at control, desire, intimacy, identity – and kleptomania – in a different way. Related Stories Movies Olivia Wilde Says She Fought for 'The Invite' to Get a Cinema Release: "They Bribe You to Not Take Theatrical" Movies Monica Bellucci Plays a Mother Who Yells and Is the "Victim of a Social Role" in Luca Guadagnino-Produced 'Ketticè' Objet a , world-premiering in the international competition of the 79 th edition of the Locarno Film Festival on Tuesday, Aug. 11, stars Aenne Schwarz ( All Is Well , Every You Every Me ) as Ingeborg, Louis Hofmann ( All the Light We Cannot See , The Forger , Dark ) as Adam, and Simone Bucio ( Piaffe , The Ivy ) as Gaia. Georg Friedrich ( Great Freedom ) and Sofia Kokkali ( Our Wildest Days ) also feature. “I’m interested in human desire and how it connects us to other species,” Oren says in a director’s note. “The human body is the starting point for my cinematic language: the more control we have over it, the more we separate ourselves from the natural world.” Oren wrote the screenplay for Objet a with Geoffroy Grison. The cinematography is courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G. ( The Voice of Hind Rajab , A Poet ), with editing by Hansjörg Weißbrich ( Rose , Late Shift ). The film is produced by Schuldenberg Films in co-production with Tarantula, asterisk* and ERT. A theatrical release in Germany through Grandfilm is scheduled for the first quarter of 2027. Oscilloscope Laboratories has acquired the North American rights. Bendita Film Sales is handling international sales. Ahead of the Locarno premiere of Objet a , Oren, Schwarz and Hofmann talked to THR about the serious and fun sides of the production, how they collaborated on its choreography and how timely its themes are if you look close enough. Ann, what gave you the idea for this film and this story? ANN OREN Several things, but what I was starting with was the sense of touch. I make very visceral films. My first feature film, Piaffe , dealt with the sense of sound. I start with the experience of the human body today in order to understand the human condition today. Here, I was thinking about the sense of touch today and what happens when we touch flat screens more than we touch our lover’s skin. A lot of experiences have flattened down to touching this plexiglass most of the day, so what is happening to our fingertips? I think they’re really deprived, and I was imagining zombie-like, hungry fingers – hungry to touch something. And then I had this idea of a couple that is living a very bubbled life and communicating emotionally through objects. ‘Objet a’ Courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G./Schuldenberg Films I am curious, Aenne and Louis, how Ann pitched this project to you. To me as a viewer, Objet a sometimes felt a bit like a dance choreography that was very body-driven and that I could “feel” physically while watching. AENNE SCHWARZ When I read the script, I felt a real longing to become part of this genuinely faraway world, which, at the same time, felt somehow familiar. What was very intense was when Ann talked us through the script. I remember when we all met, she had such a precise and full vision of what she wanted. And then, yes, it was a very physical experience. I experienced it like diving in, and at the same time, you had to hold the line and be very straight because they’re such delicate characters. LOUIS HOFMANN I remember that in our first rehearsal, the term dance popped up quite a few times. The way we moved around one another was, I guess, testing out how near you could be to one another and what distance you could create. I remember that there were only a few moments where the characters would actually touch. But most of the time, it was about playing with the distance between them, creating tension, and playing with that tension. SCHWARZ Yes. The gaze was part of the tension between us. You never lose each other. But sometimes, you are very far and sometimes much closer. It’s always a thin line holding us together. HOFMANN And that longing for the touch is, I think, omnipresent, and that created the tension. Interesting how you both describe this. Now it makes more sense to me why I sometimes felt that you two were almost moving like marionettes. Ann, are you happy if viewers get that sense? OREN Absolutely, because this is exactly the type of work that I’m doing. I see working with actors as being about a very physical performance. There is also the psychology, but what I’m actually interested in is how the characters make decisions, not rationally, but rather through gut feeling. I look at human beings as the species that they are. In everyday life, it happens to everybody that we are compelled to do something, although we don’t really understand why. And I think it’s very exciting for a viewer to see that in a character and see that things are charged with this kind of tension. In the psychoanalytic theory of Jacques Lacan, “objet a” is an unattainable object of desire. Aenne, Louis, were you familiar with this term, or did Ann go through some of this theory? Or was it not really that important to understand such concepts? HOFMANN My girlfriend mentioned it to me. I wasn’t aware of it, but she was. And then during rehearsals, we touched on it a little bit. My character Adam has this desire of wanting to be a desired object for someone else. But then through his journey, he is also developing a sense of what he wants to be for himself. For me, that was a very beautiful journey to go on. ‘Objet a’ film still, courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G./Schuldenberg Films AENNE I saw the title and remembered that a long time ago I studied literature, and Lacan was a topic in one seminar. I remember that I was very excited about it, and so I got a little bit into it. A close friend of mine is a Lacanian psychoanalyst. I felt I had a very intense meeting with this “objet a” myself during filming. The film became this object, in a way. I also wanted to touch it. I also wanted to have it, to own it, and it was also slipping away. So for me, it was a very personal experience with the theme. HOFMANN You mentioned marionettes. I sometimes felt that the way I was being, or we were being directed, I felt so secure and so safe. In Ann’s world that she created, we just kind of obeyed her vision in a very beautiful way. I don’t mean that we had no say in it anymore, because it was quite the opposite. She was still welcoming all of our ideas. Do you remember any examples? HOFMANN When I tried to find the character, I very much went through voice. It was an impulse. I’d read somewhere that the soul of a character is placed in the voice, and I’ve never really gone through that, using the voice in particular to create the character. During rehearsals, I was reading Georg [Friedrich]’s part with Aenne, and I was mimicking, for fun, Georg’s [Austrian] accent and dialect. And then Ann was like: “Wait, I love this voice for you.” And I said: “Hang on, I can’t really have Georg’s voice when being in a film with Georg.” But I then took that placement of the voice, where his voice sits. That’s just an example of how playful we were with one another while being in that very safe and secure environment of Ann’s vision. Ann Oren, courtesy of Björn Melhus Courtesy of Björn Melhus Ann, as a filmmaker, how do you think about colors? I noticed, or maybe I should say “felt,” colors quite a bit in Objet a … OREN This is the bread and butter of my language. I don’t even have to sketch it out. It just comes to me. What would be the color palette of the film, and how does that support the mood that I would like to bring across? For this film, I wanted to reduce colors. Actually, we only have natural colors in the film until, slowly, green becomes the guest and the star color in the film. You have to work very hard to reduce color, actually, especially when you’re shooting outside, and then you slowly introduce it. So when you have a sequence in the end, it’s really ecstatic. So we made sure in the production design and in the costumes that the range was from whites and beiges into the deep browns. The red color was used only in the bedroom … and [in another location] in the background. When I see Adam and Ingeborg within these natural colors, it really makes me think of them a little bit more like animals. I felt the desire inside, or below the surface, of the couple without the characters having to talk about it. Is there a trick to tap into that to make us viewers sense this desire? SCHWARZ With Ingeborg, what I thought was very exciting about her was that her fingertips and her eyes are her sensual organs. And I really tried to dive into these sensations. The crutch she [gets for one of her legs as the film unfolds] became part of my body. It was exciting for me to really open to the world that an object can become so strong. And with Gaia, she also has a sense she never had before, and she can’t control it. That is like an earthquake for her. She goes into a direction she never went before, and she can’t understand it. She basically has things in order. She knows what she wants. She’s very sensitive and delicate, but also very clear in what the object has to do for her. And then this kind of melting starts when her body breaks. When her leg is broken, something breaks into pieces. ‘Objet a’ film still, courtesy of Juan Sarmiento G./Schuldenberg Films HOFMANN I remember that the objects, the crutch, as well as a corset I use, had an immense effect – not only on us but on the whole team. There was a fascination with the beauty of how they were built, and maybe how we got attached to them. We treated them as extended parts of ourselves, and there was this fascination coming from the team as well. I also remember us, as actors, acting differently when we had our objects with us. There was more to us, and it was also kind of between us. This film is about these two people who are symbiotic and living their life in a very symbiotic way, doing everything with one another – working together, living together, loving each other – and then there are these new elements popping up that are so disturbing at first, and so irritating, and so frightening. And then they slowly but surely start to go with those impulses, and they don’t really know where they’re coming from. SCHWARZ One thing that was very special was that this was very playful, and also funny in a way. And that gave us also a lot of freedom. We were having fun. We were laughing. HOFMANN At first, I wondered, “Is this going to become not body horror, but is it all going to be really dark, scary and just full of doom?” But I felt it was quite endearing, and so sweet, no matter how strange these desires might appear to other people. At the end of the day, they are very endearing, sweet desires. And I found the characters so endearing. SCHWARZ Yes, there’s a tenderness. Ann, can you share how you think of rituals as part of your storytelling? OREN That has a lot to do with obsessions with control. You see that with both of them, especially with Adam’s character. He’s obsessed with controlling his body, developing his body, and then he wants his body to also get attention. But the more control we have over our bodies, the more we are disconnected from the natural world that we are a part of. And I think this is a very contemporary condition. The need for rituals, historically, first of all, is that they are relaxing. It doesn’t have to be a religious ritual, but it can be about the things that you have to do in the morning or the things that you have to do before you leave the house. I think that the need for it also has to do with forgetting ourselves and connecting with something larger than ourselves. If in the beginning, the characters are connected to controlling their lives and to objects, towards the end, it opens up to a psychedelic experience that is like ecstasy. And ecstasy has always been a need for humankind. Today, there is a renaissance of psychedelics in the world because we’re so controlled – the need to forget ourselves, to have a moment of ego loss, and to connect to something larger than ourselves. I didn’t want to have a didactic experience for the audience, but rather lure them into something through passion. Speaking of passion, Adam and Ingeborg really try to control that when we first meet them… OREN I built the sexuality between the couple so that they were canceling parts of their bodies; they’re not including their genitals. It’s all about this exchange of the experience of touching and being touched, but in the most clinical way, which makes it absurd and interesting and a very particular choice for the two of them, which makes them suit each other very well. I think we live so bubbled today, and we’re trying to control everything, and it’s becoming about maximizing the length of your life, but you forget to live your life. The film starts with thinking about the human condition, our bubbled life, and what, in a way, leads us to the disaster that we are in right now. We’re living in times of war, climate catastrophe and tech fascism, and it starts from that. So, the film is something very fantastical, and I have very particular characters. But it touches on living in the world right now, and I hope that it’s going to resonate and be absorbed this way. I like to work with ambiguity, so I don’t want a person to come out of the film and be able to describe it with one sentence. That would make it rather boring. THR

articles.title: In ‘Demons,’ Love and Betrayal Become a Metaphor for the Relationship Between Russia and Ukraine (Exclusive Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 9, 2026 1:00am 'Demons' Courtesy of Arthouse Traffic Writer-director Natalka Vorozhbyt ( Bad Roads ) decided to face the Demons to explore the roots of the war between Russia and Ukraine . Now, she is unleashing the Demons at the 79 th edition of the Locarno Film Festival , where the film will world-premiere in the Filmmakers of the Present competition program on Aug. 13. Here is how a synopsis describes the movie: “In the 1990s, Slavik, a homeless drifter from Russia with a blurred past who claims to be a writer, wanders into a remote village in central Ukraine. Nina, a strong and independent woman much older than Slavik, takes the stranger into her home. At first, their strange companionship resembles an unlikely love story. But as their relationship unfolds, love turns into betrayal, and the village begins to reveal its hidden rules — a place where witches may live next door, and the dead sometimes speak with the living.” Related Stories Movies 'Objet a' Explores Desire and Control in an Age When We "Touch Flat Screens More Than Our Lover's Skin" Movies Olivia Wilde Says She Fought for 'The Invite' to Get a Cinema Release: "They Bribe You to Not Take Theatrical" The creator of the film highlights that it unfolds on three interconnected levels. “The first is the relationship between a man and a woman within a traditional society,” Vorozhbyt explains in a director’s statement. “The second is socio-political, where this relationship becomes a metaphor for the relationship between Russia and Ukraine. The third is mystical, exploring the connection between the living, the dead, and the otherworld.” In case you wonder: Nina seems to be the embodiment of post-Soviet Ukraine and the country’s independence. So, you’ll want to look out for any danger to her. Ruslana Pysanka, Aleksey Mitin, Tatiana Stepanova, Ruslan Garmash and Mykola Ponomarenko feature in the cast. Demons was filmed by cinematographer Volodymyr Ivanov, with editing by Milenia Fiedler and Andriy Gulyanych. Celluloid Dreams is handling international sales. THR can now exclusively premiere the trailer for Demons . Don’t expect any exorcizing of demons here! Instead, it is time for a drink and “fire in the belly.” You look confused! To change that, watch the trailer for Demons right here. THR

articles.title: Luca Guadagnino Explains Why He Just Had to Produce Giovanni Tortorici’s Coming-of-Age Drama ‘Ketticè’ in a “Sterile” Italian Film Landscape
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 9, 2026 2:00am Luca Guadagnino at Locarno 2026 Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival/Ti-Press/Edoardo Nerboni Luca Guadagnino didn’t come to Switzerland to share updates on the drama surrounding his OpenAI movie, Artificial , during a meeting with reporters at the 79th edition of the Locarno Film Festival . No, he was in town to sing the praises of a protégé. To be precise, Guadagnino came to Locarno, in Italian-speaking Switzerland, to discuss Ketticè , the sophomore feature of his former assistant, writer-director Giovanni Tortorici ( Diciannove ). The coming-of-age drama stars Salvatore Gallina, Rachele Testagrossa and Monica Bellucci . And yes, the movie’s list of producers includes Guadagnino. Related Stories Movies In 'Demons,' Love and Betrayal Become a Metaphor for the Relationship Between Russia and Ukraine (Exclusive Trailer) Movies 'Objet a' Explores Desire and Control in an Age When We "Touch Flat Screens More Than Our Lover's Skin" Set in Palermo, Sicily in 2012, the era of media mogul-turned-politician Silvio Berlusconi, the movie revolves around Giulio, a listless and dissatisfied 16-year-old who drifts through his days without any enthusiasm for school and no real future prospects. But his encounter with Ketty, a more self-assured peer, offers him an escape from the monotony. The two form a close friendship, which a synopsis describes as “a shared refuge in their search for freedom, far from the judgmental gaze of the adult world.” The film’s title refers to Ketty’s nickname in the Sicilian dialect. Bellucci plays Giulio’s mother in an aristocratic Sicilian family that leaves her feeling oppressed. The cinematography is by Camilla Cattabriga, with editing by Marco Costa. PiperPlay is handling international sales. Guadagnino was asked by reporters about Italy’s rich cinematic history and if his decision to produce Tortorici’s movie was his way of keeping that tradition alive. “Most definitely,” he replied. “I think that we can agree that historically, Italian cinema, from the silent times until the ’70s, generated some of the most important personalities in the history of cinema, but also as an industry, had created a system that was the envy of many other countries. There were many different kind of films being made.” ‘Ketticè’ Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival But then, something happened with “the advent of private TV and the Berlusconi empire,” Guadagnino offered. “It dried [up], and most of what was produced for cinema became TV. Genre was killed. A pretension on authorship became such that the great idea of cinema as authorship became basically people writing scripts and shooting their own scripts so that they could define themselves as authors.” In the end, “the movie industry shrunk and the perspective shrunk and the cinema of Italy became sterile and totally devoid of an idea of language and of an idea of life.” That’s where Tortorici comes in. “So when you meet a personality like Giovanni, who, of course, is an Italian filmmaker working in Italy, but I like to think that he’s a filmmaker, period, when you meet someone that is a complete rarity in the landscape of Italian cinema, you must protect it,” Guadagnino concluded. “You must make sure that every stone is not left unturned in order to give him the means to express himself. For me, introducing films such as Giovanni’s movies is a way to … set up a pavement into the future.” And he emphasized: “It’s about the mindset. The mindset means how you do your stuff, what stories you want to tell, how you understand reality, how you interpret reality. How you run away from falseness is intoxicating for all its truth, all its incredible, vivid reality.” As a producer, Guadagnino shared that he likes to watch a movie and experience it like anyone else in a movie theater. His audience take on Ketticè : “As an audience member, I feel the movie really speaks in a very universal way.” ‘Ketticè’ Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Tortorici said his film explores how institutions, such as school, family and the state, fail kids. “I think the guilty ones are the adults,” he told reporters. “I think they just live in a cultural context of the ultra-capitalist contest and a mediatic world.” Does Tortorici have any vision for his cinematic future after two autobiographically inspired films? “In my next movie, I’m going to explore something that is very far from me,” he offered. “Shooting this movie, I met a lot of people in Palermo, even coming from difficult neighborhoods with difficult life experiences. I find in these stories the possibility to continuing to explore this struggle of young people with authorities.” Continued Tortorici: “I think the big problem of society is the structure of, for example, the family. I think family is the structure that [creates] the next repressed person. So I would very much like to explore these different experiences in all parts of society, family in particular.” THR
