articles.title: ‘Abbott Elementary’ Stars Sheryl Lee Ralph and Janelle James on the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘We’ve Lost Too Many People’
articles.full_text: Aug 8, 2026 3:19pm PT ‘Abbott Elementary’ Stars Sheryl Lee Ralph and Janelle James on the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘We’ve Lost Too Many People’ By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest Andrew Lloyd Webber Is ‘Gutted’ on ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Closing Night: Producing on Broadway Is ‘Unsustainable’ 9 hours ago ‘Abbott Elementary’ Stars Sheryl Lee Ralph and Janelle James on the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘We’ve Lost Too Many People’ 11 hours ago ‘Tony’ Star Dominic Sessa on How Being a ‘Liar’ Helped Him Portray Anthony Bourdain and Why the Film Foreshadows His Later Struggles 17 hours ago See All Getty Images As “ Abbott Elementary ” gears up for Season 6 production in just a few short weeks, stars Sheryl Lee Ralph , Janelle James and Luke Tennie are reflecting on turbulent changes in the industry — from the pending Paramount-Warner Bros. merger to production struggling in Los Angeles. “Any time there is a consolidation, something shrinks, and right now we’re seeing such attrition when it comes to the entertainment industry,” Ralph told Variety on Saturday afternoon at the AAFCA TV Honors held at City Club in Los Angeles. “I don’t want to see too much more shrinking. We’ve lost too many people. We’ve lost too many people outside of this state going to other places.” Related Stories Richard Madden to Star in Hostage Thriller Series 'Trauma' for Prime Video UK, Paramount+ (EXCLUSIVE) 'Stillwater' Series Based on Skybound Graphic Novel Set at Amazon From Greg Berlanti, Carly Wray James, who plays Principal Ava on the award-winning comedy, said she doesn’t pay much attention to the noise surrounding the Paramount merger. Popular on Variety “I really have no idea what it means. I know I still got a job. Hopefully, it results in people continuing to keep their jobs,” James said. “I take it as something I don’t need to worry about.” The AAFCA TV Honors honored the likes of “Abbott Elementary,” “Paradise,” “Spider-Noir” and “Love Story,” along with actors Tracy Morgan, Sterling K. Brown, Lamorne Morris and Erika Alexander, celebrating the best of Black talent and storytelling over the past year. AAFCA’s strong industry ties were underscored by L.A. mayor Karen Bass’ appearance ahead of the upcoming election. On stage, she commended the work that Black creatives are doing as writers, producers and actors amid struggling production rates. “We’re looking at how we reduced the costs on set by reducing the number of city staff,” Bass said of her efforts to bring more production to L.A. “So what I would like to ask you all to do is to tell me, tell our office what more Los Angeles can do, specifically, so that we can continue to flourish.” Reflecting on how “Abbott Elementary” and other Warner Bros. shows provide consistent jobs for local crew, Ralph said: “Hollywood, California, is the birthplace of show business, and too many other cities, states around the country and world are claiming it as theirs. I want it to come back. I want it to stay right here. I want us to come back to the development of real stories, real series, and I would like box office to mean something again soon.” “Abbott Elementary” not only provides consistent work for its award-winning ensemble but also for the hundreds of young kids who work as extras every season. “I have said this to people in the past, but I know for a fact in 10 years, there are going to be kids that were extras or under five in the cast that I’m going to see making films, making movies, creating their own series from YouTube to network to streaming,” Ralph said. “I’m gonna see it because I’m listening to them when they talk on set. There’s some really smart kids on our show. And it’s happening.” Amid an uncertain future, Tennie — who also stars in “Shrinking” and “The Pitt,” which are all filmed on the Warner Bros. lot — feels confident that artists will continue finding a way forward. “There was some sort of weird, strange death at every point in our evolution as TV and filmmakers,” Tennie said, referencing the introduction of color and sound as past inflection points. “People all had their different opinions on where this thing was going to go. And no matter what, whatever people wanted to see most got made. And I truly, in my heart of hearts, believe that.” How Jane Fonda Came to Star in Katie Camosy’s Greenpeace-Produced Directorial Debut ‘Gaslit’ Luxbox Acquires Documentary ‘Life of Jorge Luis Borges’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Let Us Be’ Director Viviane D’Avilla Talks About Shining a Light on Intersex Rights in the U.S.: ‘Their Rights Are Being Taken Away’ Liz Garbus’ ESPN Doc ‘Give Me The Ball!’ About Billie Jean King Will Open Croatia International Film Festival (EXCLUSIVE) Odd Slice Films Boards Documentary ‘Concrete Land’ Ahead of Locarno Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Autlook Boards Barbara Kopple’s ‘Union Town’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Warner Bros. Uses AI Dog Podcast to Promote ‘The End of Oak Street’: ‘Ewan McGregor Was Excellent With Treats’
articles.full_text: Aug 8, 2026 4:41pm PT Warner Bros. Uses AI Dog Podcast to Promote ‘The End of Oak Street’: ‘Ewan McGregor Was Excellent With Treats’ By Jack Dunn Plus Icon Jack Dunn Latest Warner Bros. Uses AI Dog Podcast to Promote ‘The End of Oak Street’: ‘Ewan McGregor Was Excellent With Treats’ 10 hours ago Perez Hilton ‘Will Require Surgery’ After Live Stream Incident, Family Demands Media ‘Cease Photographing Perez’s Children’ 11 hours ago ‘Heated Rivalry’ Author Brushes Off Negativity Surrounding Season 2 Casting 12 hours ago See All Warner Bros.; Dog Pack Warner Bros . has teamed with the AI dog podcast “DogPack” to promote its upcoming sci-fi action film “ The End of Oak Street .” The 90-second podcast clip, hosted by an AI golden retriever named Goldie and an AI French bulldog named Frenchie, features an interview with Starbuck, who plays Anne Hathaway and Ewan McGregor’s dog in “Oak Street.” Starbuck, of course, is also animated using uncanny AI effects. Related Stories 'Bridgette Wrona and the Whisper Creek Murders' Wraps From Little Spark Films; YA Mystery Follows Podcaster Hunting a Serial Killer (EXCLUSIVE) Satyajit Ray's 'Goopy Gyne Bagha Byne' Making to be Chronicled in Srijit Mukherji's 'Maharaja Tomare Selam' In the opening moments of the interview, Frenchie asks Starbuck, “Which one of your human co-stars was the best trained?” Starbuck replies, “Ewan McGregor was excellent with treats. Anne Hathaway matched him there, but she could scratch behind both ears at once. Game over!” Popular on Variety View this post on Instagram The video was shared across the Warner Bros. socials. On Instagram, most of the commenters were excited about the collab, but some took issue with the studio opting to use AI in their promotional material. One commenter wrote, “Billion dollar company using AI. slop.” Another comment with over 400 likes read, “So is this an AI movie or????” From writer-director David Robert Mitchell, “The End of Oak Street” follows a suburban family who must survive a dinosaur horde after their neighborhood is miraculously transported through space-time. Outside of Hathaway and McGregor, cast members include Maisy Stella, Christian Convery, Jordan Alexa Davis and P.J. Byrne. J.J. Abrams produced the film under his Bad Robot banner. During a recent press event, Abrams said that one of the reasons he believed in “Oak Street” is because it’s a high-concept blockbuster anchored by very real family dynamics. He told Mitchell , “The brilliance of what you wrote is that each of the characters has a secret, essentially. Each of the characters has something they’re wrestling with, but they’re a family that you so connect with and so root for and believe in. It’s not a sadistic movie. articles.title: Andrew Lloyd Webber Is ‘Gutted’ on ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Closing Night: Producing on Broadway Is ‘Unsustainable’
articles.full_text: Aug 8, 2026 4:54pm PT Andrew Lloyd Webber Is ‘Gutted’ on ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Closing Night: Producing on Broadway Is ‘Unsustainable’ By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘Abbott Elementary’ Stars Sheryl Lee Ralph and Janelle James on the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger: ‘We’ve Lost Too Many People’ 11 hours ago ‘Tony’ Star Dominic Sessa on How Being a ‘Liar’ Helped Him Portray Anthony Bourdain and Why the Film Foreshadows His Later Struggles 17 hours ago Flo Anthony, Pioneering Page Six Entertainment Journalist, Dies at 74 2 days ago See All Getty Ahead of tonight’s final “Cats: The Jellicle Ball” show, composer Andrew Lloyd Webber is speaking out about how producing on Broadway has become “unsustainable.” “I’m gutted that the wonderful Broadway production of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ is closing today,” Lloyd Webber wrote on Instagram . “I’m immensely proud to have been a part of an incredibly daring production whose cast and creative team broke new ground on Broadway and gave 17 actors their Broadway debut.” Related Stories Marta Kauffman Sets Improvised Sitcom 'DINKS' at Amazon Starring June Diane Raphael, Paul Scheer (EXCLUSIVE) 'Rose Hill' Amazon Series Casts Jake Weary, Sean O’Pry, Hannah Galway, Sadie Dickerson He also took the opportunity to call out the larger issues affecting the industry: “Maybe the show’s closing just might be remembered as the moment that caused everyone involved with Broadway to come to their senses and address the unsustainable cost of producing and running any new show now on The Great White Way, let alone doing new work.” Popular on Variety “The Jellicle Ball” breathed new life into “Cats” by restaging the popular show as a fierce competition between drag performers. Webber’s original show premiered on Broadway back in 1982 and ran through 2000, winning seven Tony awards. In 2019, it was infamously turned into a critically panned film from “The King’s Speech” director Tom Hooper. But despite the Tonys awarding “The Jellicle Ball” three awards for best costume design, best direction of a musical and best choreography, strong reviews and online buzz didn’t stop the show from closing five months before planned at the Broadhurst Theatre. “The Jellicle Ball” started as an off-Broadway production in June 2024. When it premiered on Broadway back in April, the show was initially earning between $900,000 to $1 million a week. But those numbers dropped sharply after “The Jellicle Ball” lost the best revival of a musical Tony Award to “Ragtime.” This isn’t the first time Lloyd Webber has spoken out about the show’s premature end. In July, he wrote on Instagram : “Without action, Broadway risks rivaling Hollywood’s empty soundstages: increasingly dark theatres where bold new work once lived.” “The painful truth is that, with things as they are, bringing almost any new show to Broadway makes little financial sense,” Lloyd Webber continued. “The costs are immense. Creators, writers and directors are often forced to accept minimal royalties simply to get work staged.” Next up, Lloyd Webber and “Sunset Blvd.” director Jamie Lloyd are working on bringing “Evita” with Rachel Zegler to Broadway after its successful West End run. articles.title: Gina Prince-Bythewood Discusses the Worldbuilding of ‘Children of Blood and Bone’ and Praises Author Tomi Adeyemi as a ‘Genius’
articles.full_text: Aug 8, 2026 5:36pm PT Gina Prince-Bythewood Discusses the Worldbuilding of ‘Children of Blood and Bone’ and Praises Author Tomi Adeyemi as a ‘Genius’ Prince-Bythewood and star Thuso Mbedu previewed the Paramount film on opening night of the Martha’s Vineyard African American Film Festival By Aramide Tinubu Plus Icon Aramide Tinubu Latest ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Creator Sascha Penn and Stars Patina Miller and Mekai Curtis on the Deadly Series Finale and ‘Power: Origins’ 1 day ago USA Network’s ‘Anna Pigeon’ Is the Temu Version of ‘Virgin River’: TV Review 2 days ago Prime Video’s Stunning Drama ’Sterling Point’ Elevates the YA Genre Beyond the Mundane: TV Review 4 days ago See All Getty Images for Paramount Pictures For the opening night of the 24th annual Martha’s Vineyard African American Film Festival ( MVAAFF ), “ Children of Blood and Bone ” director Gina Prince-Bythewood and star Thuso Mbedu shared never-before-seen clips of the forthcoming African fantasy film and dished about making the movie. “Obviously films like this don’t get made very often,” Prince-Bythewood told “The View’s” Sunny Hostin during the Q&A. “They say 70% of directing is casting, and that’s what this was. To be able to put together a cast like this. There are no skips. Everybody is amazing. … And as I was working on the script, I started to envision people that I wanted.” Related Stories Stanley Tucci on Why His Emmy-Nominated 'Tucci In Italy' Is Moving to the United Kingdom Next Season Béla Tarr's Legacy to Be Celebrated at Sarajevo Film Festival Based on Tomi Adeyemi ’s acclaimed 2018 novel of the same name, Paramount’s “Children of Blood and Bone” was shot on location in South Africa, which subbed in for the fictional kingdom of Orïsha, where magic has been prohibited. There, the logline explains, “a young woman goes on a quest to reclaim the magic that was violently stolen from her people. She and her brother ally with the daughter and son of the king to fight back against his brutal rule.” Popular on Variety Mbedu (“The Underground Railroad,” “The Woman King”) stars as Zélie Adebola, the young woman in question, who has the power to command the undead. Starring alongside her are Damson Idris as Prince Inan, Amandla Stenberg as Princess Amari, Tosin Cole as Zélie’s brother Tzain and Regina King as Queen Nehanda. Lashana Lynch, Idris Elba, Cynthia Erivo and Viola Davis round out the A-list cast. Mbedu was thrilled to return to her native South Africa to work, and she began preparing for the role — including her stunt training — nearly one year before filming began. “I leaned into the source material a lot,” she said. “I don’t know how many times I read and reread the book, putting it next to the screenplay.” (Prince-Bythewood and Adeyemi share screenplay credit.) “Tomi created a massive world, a huge world,” Mbedu continued. “We don’t have enough hours to put everything on screen. So finding the moments where, even if we’re not seeing it on screen, how am I bringing the reality of the history or the backstory of what we might have meant into the next moment.” Thuso Mbedu, Gina Prince-Bythewood and Sunny Hostin attend the “Children of Blood and Bone” clips and conversations event during the Martha’s Vineyard African American Film Festival in Oak Bluffs, Mass. Arnold Turner/Getty Images for Paramount Pictures Though the film does not debut until Jan.15, 2027, Adeyemi, who also served as an executive producer on the film, recently announced that she will not watch the finished product . On social media, Adeyemi shared that she left the “Children of Blood and Bone” set “hyperventilating and sobbing” and that she is “still being antagonized behind the scenes.” Neither Prince-Bythewood nor Mbedu directly addressed Adeyemi’s claims at MVAAFF, but the director of “The Woman King” did speak positively about the novelist and the world she crafted. “Tomi’s a genius,” Prince-Bythewood said. “It’s a beautiful book, incredible characters. And this time when I read it, I was so connected to Lali’s character. And this young woman who was fighting to bring magic back- and we know what magic means for us. And her resilience, her fight and her search for purpose just spoke to me.” ​ The “Love and Basketball” director also spoke about casting Stenberg as Princess Amari. When the actress’ hiring was announced, there was an outcry over allegations of colorism due to Stenberg’s mixed-race status and lighter skin tone. Additionally, in a now-deleted TikTok video [via the L.A. Times], Adeyemi posted what appeared to be a group chat that included Stenberg. The author wrote, “Do not ever use my name in an interview or video again. Do not text me. Do not call me” and appeared to block the actor. Prince-Bythewood did not address the drama onstage. “I’ve admired [Amandla’s] work since ‘Colombiana,’” Prince-Bythewood told Hostin and the MVAAFF audience. “But I auditioned every young actor for that role of Amari, and Amandla took it, grabbed it.” ​ Though the “Children of Blood and Bone” premiere is still several months away, “The Old Guard” director is content to let the work speak for itself until then. “You’re going to feel every human emotion in this,” she said. “You’re going to be angry, you’re going to laugh, you’re going to cry, you’re going to dance, you’re going to cheer, you’re going to feel hope at the end. And that’s why I hope we go to movies, to feel something, to be moved. So I’m so excited about that. And as we know, these films are rare. I’m so proud of this movie, so excited about this movie and the thing that it can do for us when we see ourselves in this way.” View this post on Instagram Behind the Scenes of Obama’s Acting Cameo in ‘Life, Larry’: Blaming Larry David for His Tan Suit Debacle, Improvising Lines and Ranting About Ketchup Da’Vine Joy Randolph to Star in Indie Dark Comedy ‘Dedicated to Morris Burke’ From Director Will Ropp (EXCLUSIVE) How ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s’ Climactic Fight Scene Secretly Evokes Jean Grey’s Phoenix ‘Baywatch’ Honors Hero 16-Year-Old Lifeguard Ryder Williams During Set Visit (EXCLUSIVE) The Best Hilton Hotels in Hawaii: From a 22-Acre Waikiki Resort to Charming, Boutique Abodes Warner Bros. Whitney Houston is ready to dance with somebody — in Barbieland. Mattel is honoring the late pop icon with a new Barbie Signature doll inspired by Houston’s colorful look from the 1987 music video for “I Wanna Dance With Somebody (Who Loves Me).” The $60 collectible launches Aug. 8 at Target stores and online at Amazon, Walmart, Target and Mattel Creations. Whitney Houston Barbie Buy Now $60 The doll recreates Houston’s instantly recognizable ensemble from the video, complete with a purple tank dress, colorful drop earrings and bright eye makeup. Naturally, she also comes performance-ready with her own microphone stand. Pat Houston, executor of the Estate of Whitney E. Houston and president of the Whitney E. Houston Legacy Foundation, collaborated with the Barbie design team alongside Primary Wave Music, weighing in on everything from the doll’s wardrobe to the singer’s signature glam. Popular on Variety The Whitney Houston Barbie will make its official debut Saturday at the fifth annual Legacy of Love Gala in Atlanta, an event hosted by the Whitney E. Houston Legacy Foundation. Its arrival comes as Houston’s estate continues to celebrate more than four decades since the singer first emerged as one of pop music’s most formidable voices. Released as the lead single from Houston’s sophomore album, “Whitney,” “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” became one of the singer’s defining hits and earned her the Grammy for best female pop vocal performance in 1988. The album itself made history as the first by a female artist to debut at No. 1 on the Billboard 200, while the song was part of Houston’s still-unmatched run of seven consecutive No. 1 singles. The new release joins Barbie Signature’s growing roster of dolls modeled after musicians and cultural icons, which has previously included Tina Turner, Stevie Nicks, Gloria Estefan and Mariah Carey. articles.title: Mahesh Babu’s Look in S.S. Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’ Unveiled
articles.full_text: Aug 8, 2026 10:47pm PT Mahesh Babu’s Look in S.S. Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’ Unveiled By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Naseeruddin Shah, Gurvinder Singh Turn a Village’s Real Grief Into Locarno Competition Title ‘Rehmat’: ‘It’s Important That These Films Get Made’ 2 hours ago Mahesh Babu’s Look in S.S. Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’ Unveiled 4 hours ago Yash’s ‘Toxic’ Trailer Unveils Dual-Role Father-Son Conflict at Core of Gangster Epic 18 hours ago See All Sri Durga Arts/Showing Business Two new character stills of Mahesh Babu from S.S. Rajamouli ‘s “ Varanasi ” were released Sunday to mark the actor’s birthday, showing his character Rudhra on location in Africa. The film’s story spans thousands of years and traverses multiple continents, with locations ranging from Antarctica to Africa to the titular Indian city. Babu plays the dual roles of the protagonist Rudhra and Hindu God Rama, Priyanka Chopra Jonas plays a character named Mandakini and the main antagonist Kumbha is played by Prithviraj Sukumaran. Related Stories Andrew Lloyd Webber Is 'Gutted' on 'Cats: The Jellicle Ball' Closing Night: Producing on Broadway Is 'Unsustainable' Whitney Houston Gets Her Own Barbie, Recreating Iconic 'I Wanna Dance With Somebody' Look The images were shot at the Kilimanjaro and Maasai Mara locations, two of the African settings featured in the film. In one still, Mahesh Babu reclines on a bamboo raft in a jungle setting, dressed in a loose olive-toned shirt and dark cargo trousers, with tousled curly hair and a full beard. The other image shows him in profile against the African savannah, with giraffes and zebras visible in the background. Popular on Variety Mahesh Babu – “Varanasi” Sri Durga Arts/Showing Business Rajamouli described the character’s dual nature in a note accompanying the stills. “Rudhra was born to fulfil a purpose much larger than himself. He carries a destiny he did not ask for. He is witty, he is vulnerable, and he is fierce. That is what Mahesh brought to him. Anyone can play fierce. Very few can play fierce and fragile in the same breath,” he said in an Instagram post . The director also reflected on the Africa shoot itself. “These frames are from our Africa schedule, and the land gave us something no set could. Shooting around Kilimanjaro and in the Masai Mara, I was stunned. There were mornings I felt even the 1.43:1 Imax frame could not hold what was in front of us,” he said. The stills mark the latest in a series of character reveals from the production, following images of Priyanka Chopra Jonas released for her birthday. Babu, who spent a year preparing for the role, underwent three months of Kalari martial arts training solely to adjust his posture for the character’s period-appropriate bearing. “I’m playing Lord Rama’s character, it required posture… you can’t stand like modern characters,” he has said to Variety . He also trained with a track and field team for several months to modify his running style. “When I saw the shot, I was really happy. It was worth it, because that six months of training for that one shot was really worth it,” he said. “The way I walked changed, the way I stood changed, everything changed.” “Varanasi” is Rajamouli’s follow-up to the Academy Award-winning “RRR.” M.M. Keeravani, who won the Oscar for “RRR’s” “Naatu Naatu,” is returning to score the new film. “Varanasi” opens in theaters worldwide on April 7, 2027. articles.title: Naseeruddin Shah, Gurvinder Singh Turn a Village’s Real Grief Into Locarno Competition Title ‘Rehmat’: ‘It’s Important That These Films Get Made’
articles.full_text: Aug 9, 2026 12:22am PT Naseeruddin Shah, Gurvinder Singh Turn a Village’s Real Grief Into Locarno Competition Title ‘Rehmat’: ‘It’s Important That These Films Get Made’ By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Naseeruddin Shah, Gurvinder Singh Turn a Village’s Real Grief Into Locarno Competition Title ‘Rehmat’: ‘It’s Important That These Films Get Made’ 2 hours ago Mahesh Babu’s Look in S.S. Rajamouli’s ‘Varanasi’ Unveiled 4 hours ago Yash’s ‘Toxic’ Trailer Unveils Dual-Role Father-Son Conflict at Core of Gangster Epic 18 hours ago See All © Gurvinder Singh/Vahao Studio The family living in the house that “ Rehmat ” uses as Rashid Ali’s ancestral home lost a son to a drug overdose shortly after Indian filmmaker Gurvinder Singh and his crew first met them. Singh tells Variety , “The actual family that lives there lost their 19-year-old son after we met them for the first time. When I looked at him, the first thought that ran in my mind was that he was on drugs. And he died of an overdose within two months. What else do I need to say? How can that not affect you as a filmmaker planning a film in that scenario. How can you avoid depicting such a state of affairs?” Related Stories 'Robocop' Reboot Series Set at Prime Video 'Stillwater' Series Based on Skybound Graphic Novel Set at Amazon From Greg Berlanti, Carly Wray “Rehmat” has its world premiere in the Concorso Internazionale, the main competition of the 79th Locarno Film Festival . It is the only Indian feature in the section this year and will compete for the festival’s top honor, the Pardo d’Oro. Popular on Variety Adapted from short stories by the Punjabi writer Ajeet Cour, “Rehmat” weaves three narratives set in present-day Punjab around themes of displacement and inherited grief. Singh says the material resonated with him directly through family history. “She has written about many themes, uprootedness being one of them, and she belongs to my grandparents’ generation that migrated from Lahore or other parts of west Punjab to Delhi,” he says. “That was the sort of affinity I had with her stories.” Three decades after he began documenting Punjab’s folk ballads and oral histories, and 15 years after his debut feature “Anhey Ghorhey Da Daan” premiered in Venice, Singh says the film has given him something he didn’t expect. “I never experienced the Partition, but did feel a sense of trauma during the years of militancy and the anti-Sikh carnage in Delhi in 1984,” he says. “Frankly speaking, this film offers me a closure. I feel it has brought out all that I needed to express about the divided land and its people.” The film stars revered Indian thespian Naseeruddin Shah as Rashid Ali, a Punjabi Muslim man whose family left before Partition and who returns to his birthplace after a lifetime in England. Shah says he committed to the role before knowing any of its specifics. “I’d seen and been deeply moved by Gurvinder’s films,” Shah tells Variety . “His cinematic sensibility and his take on the turmoil in his home state made profound statements. I just thought I’d like to be part of such films.” That leap of faith went both ways. Singh says, “I approached Naseer without having written the script, only having a vague outline of the character of Rashid in my mind. His acceptance gave me the possibilities to expand and flesh it, knowing the kind of conviction, intellect and charisma he will bring into it. The responsibility became a flight of imagination. It was a new territory for me.” Of working with Shah on set, Singh says, “I had decided that I would initially observe him in front of the camera and then figure out my approach. But I kept doing that and hardly needed to direct him,” describing how the actor’s “use of the body, gestures, handling of objects” turned Rashid “into his own personal expression.” Shah, who is not Punjabi and does not speak the language fluently, says, “I agree I don’t have the Punjabi heartiness and I don’t look Punjabi. But I think that helped to identify Rashid as an outsider. I don’t speak Punjabi fluently but practice helped.” On the ambiguity of a character who initially introduces himself to the village as God, Shah adds: “A character doesn’t have to be understood by the actor playing him. Actors aren’t psychoanalysts. One must be able to empathize with the character’s situation.” Singh’s preference for long, unbroken takes runs through the film, including the opening shot that establishes Seema’s world. Singh says, “The sense of uninterrupted time that the long take affords, both with the static and the mobile camera, is highly involving for me as a spectator, and my first instinct is to attempt that. But there are scenes where you know it will not be practical or even desirable, hence the montage has to be employed. Both create a different quality of attention and being. And perhaps life is also like that. Our ways of seeing and engaging keep altering.” Shah adds, “I love long takes. It fits beautifully with my stage work. Frankly I don’t believe there’s a great difference between stage and film acting if truth is what you’re looking to find.” Beyond the ancestral house, Singh says the village itself, with its crumbling 19th-century school building and untended lanes, reshaped the narrative during location scouting. Asked how he views Punjab today, Singh says, “Bleak from the perspective of lack of imagination among the youth or those of my generation, not because of any lack of compassion. People are sticking to the glory of ownership of land and the caste they belong to. It has given them a false sense of bravado and entitlement. And the gender discourse is abysmal, especially in the villages. No wonder so many young girls are escaping to the West.” Alongside Shah, the cast includes Suvinder Vicky, Mita Vashisht, Navjot Randhawa and Diya Kamboj, plus the celebrated Punjabi poet Jaswant Zafar, making his screen acting debut at 60 as Harjap. Of casting Zafar, Singh says, “Whenever I have cast a non-actor in a major role, it is fully knowing that the person will play himself or herself on screen. So Zafar became Harjap for me. He has all the natural qualities I had imagined in Harjap and a profound sense of the feelings that he carries, both as a common man and as an intellectual.” “Rehmat” is produced by Singh and Arpana Caur, with Andrei Cosmin Illes and Némésis Srour serving as co-producers. The film is a co-production between India’s Vahao Studio and Paris-based Pavo Films, the outfit Illes and Srour launched earlier this year , with “Rehmat” as its debut project. Shah, whose career stretches back to the parallel cinema movement of the 1970s, says, “My early work prepared me for a film like this. I think Gurvinder has surpassed other contemporary filmmakers in India.” Of the film’s Partition-era subject matter, he says, “I believe it’s important that these films get made. Even if not widely seen now, they will remain as a testament.” Asked what he’s working on next, Singh says, “I am not sure what I want to do after this. I came to the cinema through some conspiracy of the universe. I grew up painting and writing. I am painting again these days.” How Banchi Hanuse’s ‘Ceremony’ Honors Nuxalk History, Healing and Survival Ana Istarú to Appear Alongside Director Daughter Ardélia Istarú in ‘Quemada’ Via Valentina Maurel’s Tres Tigres Label (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Pompeii: Out of Time with Tom Hiddleston’: A Rare Doc That Could Actually Attract a Young Audience How Jane Fonda Came to Star in Katie Camosy’s Greenpeace-Produced Directorial Debut ‘Gaslit’ ‘Let Us Be’ Director Viviane D’Avilla Talks About Shining a Light on Intersex Rights in the U.S.: ‘Their Rights Are Being Taken Away’ Autlook Boards Barbara Kopple’s ‘Union Town’ Ahead of Venice Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Donkey Princess’ Review: A Princess Escapes the Kingdom, but Not the Patriarchy, in an Inventive, Shape-Shifting Fairytale
articles.full_text: Aug 9, 2026 12:42am PT ‘Donkey Princess’ Review: A Princess Escapes the Kingdom, but Not the Patriarchy, in an Inventive, Shape-Shifting Fairytale 'The Wolf House' directors Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña mix media, styles and story worlds for an outwardly whimsical exercise that turns increasingly sober. By Guy Lodge Plus Icon Guy Lodge Film Critic @guylodge Latest ‘Donkey Princess’ Review: A Princess Escapes the Kingdom, but Not the Patriarchy, in an Inventive, Shape-Shifting Fairytale 2 hours ago ‘I Rarely Wake Up Dreaming’ Review: An Affecting Trans Relationship Drama Brings Fresh Perspective to the War in Ukraine 1 day ago ‘The Last House’ Review: Wagner Moura and Greta Lee Bring Conviction to a Suitably Stifling Stay-at-Home Thriller 2 days ago See All 'Donkey Princess' Courtesy by Bendita Film Sales Chilean duo Cristobal León and Joaquín Cociña made a dream nightmare debut with “The Wolf House,” a stop-motion fantasy that turned heads both with its wholly original design — incorporating claymation, puppetry and papier-mâché to palpably handmade but immersively surreal effect — and its trajectory from a seemingly juvenile storybook premise to very grownup recesses of horror and trauma. Their 2024 follow-up “The Hyperboreans” captured fewer imaginations with its dense, narratively abstruse melange of history, psychology and political theory, but still dazzled with technique, adding live-action cinematography to the filmmakers’ varied visual quiltwork. In their beguiling third feature, “ Donkey Princess ,” León and Cociña split the difference between their first two, continuing their singular exploration of hybrid live-action cinema, but fruitfully returning to adult fairytale terrain. Related Stories 'The Last House' Ending Breakdown: Why Is the Family Trapped Inside Their Home? Flo Anthony, Pioneering Page Six Entertainment Journalist, Dies at 74 Premiering in the international competition at Locarno, this is distinctive, aesthetically rich filmmaking that consolidates its helmers’ auteur status, and has the right balance of accessible and avant-garde components to ensure a life beyond the festival circuit — though the substance of its story lingers slightly less in the mind than its remarkable presentation. “Donkey Princess” doesn’t quite match “The Wolf House” for darkly enveloping atmosphere and gnawing emotional impact, but not much does; still, its portrayal of a mythic princess, whose tortured daddy issues follow her even after she’s spirited into the real world, builds to a climax both touching and disquieting. Popular on Variety As suggested by the title, the script (written, like “The Wolf House,” by the directors in collaboration with novelist Alejandra Moffat) riffs on the 17th-century Charles Perrault tale “Donkeyskin” — not one that Disney ever dared touch, giving its discomfiting incest-themed premise, though Jacques Demy gave it delightfully offbeat film treatment in 1970. More downbeat in its whimsy, “Donkey Princess” centers on Princess Diana (“Hyperboreans” star Antonia Giesen), who doesn’t bear any resemblance to her famous British namesake, save for the fact that she’s suffocated by the demands of her very patriarchal kingdom. Said kingdom is realized in a mixture of animated imagery and winningly ramshackle production design by Natalia Geisse: toadstool-shaped castle turrets rendered in what looks like cake frosting, fiberglass mountain formations and forests forged from stray, dry branches, accessorized with the odd flurry of 2D cartoon butterflies and birds. (Fans of the directors’ stop-motion interlude in Ari Aster’s “Beau is Afraid” will spot some familiar landscape textures here.) Tinted in queasy shades of turquoise and puce, it does not look like a world made to last, and for Diana, it isn’t. Guarded obsessively by her father (Francisco Melo) since her mother’s untimely death, she yearns for escape from his clutches; when she meets charming commoner Lalo (Andrew Bargsted), she falls swiftly in love, both with him and the prospect of life outside the royal court. For the King — who really has taken very badly to widowed life, having outlawed love throughout the land — this will not do. Lalo is swiftly banished to an orange-skied hellscape strewn with thorns and vultures: a witty fusion of silhouette animation and tactile set construction. Before he goes, however, he gives Diana a bracelet said to grant wishes across space and time; in short order, she’s transported to the urban bustle of contemporary Chile. There, she and Lalo live together as parallel versions of themselves, also working alongside each other in the pest control business. If this seems a pretty compromised happily-ever-after, there’s also the fact that her father, too, has been teleported to this new realm: an aging invalid stripped of his powers, but still plenty burdensome. That’s not the last dimensional shift in “Donkey Princess,” as Dina is shuffled through various lives and personae, but is never quite free or happy in any of them: The naïve yet despairing time-travel mechanics of Bertrand Bonello’s recent “The Beast” come to mind here, as its various temporal paths do eventually converge into a single, climactic tragedy, with the open-ended possibility of freedom. León and Cociña’s storytelling style can be opaque — the film’s opening salvo, in particular, feels hurried and scrambled — but it gains in grace and clarity, with a concluding shift in register toward near-total realism. That’s the biggest surprise from these most feverishly world-building of filmmakers, even if their most satisfying feature to date remains their most animated one. “Donkey Princess” might lack “The Wolf House’s” intensity of vision and purpose, but it feels an intriguingly transitional work in an oeuvre that could go anywhere from here. ‘Donkey Princess’ Review: A Princess Escapes the Kingdom, but Not the Patriarchy, in an Inventive, Shape-Shifting Fairytale Reviewed at Locarno Film Festival (International Competition), Oct. 7, 2026. Running time: 86 MIN. (Original title: "Princesa Burro") Production: (Chile-France-Uruguay-Netherlands-Germany) A León & Cociña Films, Globo Rojo Films production in co-production with Metonymie, Montelona, Viking Films, Autentika Films. (World sales: Bendita Film Sales, Santa Cruz de Tenerife.) Producer, executive producer: Catalina Vergara. Co-producers: Kim El Moumen, Claire Gadéa, Marleen Slot, Francisco Magnou, Paulo de Carvalho, Naomie Lagadec, Gudula Meinzolt. Crew: Directors: Cristóbal León, Joaquín Cociña. Screenplay: León, Cociña, Alejandra Moffat. Camera: Benjamín Echazarreta. Editors: León, Cociña, Soledad Salfate, Maria Salazar. Music: Jean-Benoît Dunckel. With: Antonia Giesen, Andrew Bargsted, Francisco Melo. articles.title: cast in Season 2
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie ‘Heated Rivalry’ Casts Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie As Harris & Troy; Season 2 Debut Confirmed For Spring 2027 ‘Stuart Fails’ Creators On ‘Big Bang’ OG Return For WGA Strike Roast In Magic-Themed Episode 3 Where Wizards Seek “Residuals For Eternal Spells” ‘Stuart’ Episode 3: Wil Wheaton, Brian Posehn & John Ross Bowie Talk Wizards, Puppies, Penguins, Fireball Fight, Easter Egg & That Shocking Death View All August 7, 2026 10:00am L-R: Justice Smith, Charlie Gillespie, Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie Jonny Marlow; Brindi Tremblay; Sabrina Lantos/Crave Meet Heated Rivalry ‘s newest couple: Justice Smith ( I Saw the TV Glow; Now You See Me: Now You Don’t ) and Charlie Gillespie ( One Night Only, Splitsville, Suze ) are joining returning stars Hudson Williams and Connor Storrie as leads in the upcoming second season of the hugely popular Crave Original series Heated Rivalry , which is confirmed to premiere in spring 2027. Smith and Gillespie will play Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, respectively, the couple at the center of Role Model , the fifth book in Rachel Reid’s bestselling Game Changers series, on which Heated Rivalry is based. Related Stories News What To Expect For ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2: Everything We Know So Far News Upcoming Connor Storrie Projects: From ‘April X’ To ‘Heated Rivalry’ Season 2 Production on Season 2 of the show, which streams on HBO Max in the U.S. and several other territories, started earlier this week in Canada. Watch on Deadline After Season 1 adapted Book 2, Heated Rivalry , which chronicles the budding romance between rival hockey players Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie), while also incorporating elements from Book 1, Game Changer (featuring Scott and Kip), Heated Rivalry creator Jacob Tierney had said that Season 2 will continue Shane and Ilya’s story by tackling Book 6, The Long Game , while also introducing a new couple by taking on Role Model . Troy Barrett is a hockey player on Ilya Rozanov’s team with a history of bullying while Harris Drover is the team’s cheerful social media manager. “Rachel Reid has given us two beautifully layered characters in Harris and Troy who you can’t help but root for,” said executive producers Tierney and Brendan Brady. “From the start of the casting process, we knew we were looking for actors who could create something truly special together and bring that same depth and heart to the screen. Justice and Charlie do exactly that. They immediately connected with the vulnerability and resilience at the core of these characters, bringing an instinctive understanding of who Harris and Troy are.” In Season 1, Shane Hollander (Williams) and Ilya Rozanov (Storrie) are bound by ambition, rivalry and a magnetic pull neither of them fully understood. What began as a secret fling between two fresh-faced rookies evolved into a years-long journey of love, denial, and self-discovery. Like with the casting of Ilya and Shane, Heated Rivalry is going with one American (Smith) and one Canadian (Gillespie) actor for Harris and Troy. Unlike Williams and and Storrie, who were both complete unknowns with a couple of bit parts under their belts when they were cast in Heated Rivalry , Smith and Gillespie are both established actors with movie and TV series regular roles to their names. Smith also had a role in the Jurassic World movie franchise and headlined Netflix’s series The Get Down ; Gillespie, currently seen in One Night Only , additionally starred in Netflix’s Julie and the Phantoms . Heated Rivalry , which became an instant global phenomenon when Season 1 was released in late 2025, is commissioned by Bell Media’s Crave, with the participation of the Canada Media Fund. Tierney is writer, director, and executive producer. Brady and Jayme Alter Wilson serve as executive producers. Lori Fischburg and Liane Cunje are producers, with Reid as consulting producer. Mike Goldbach serves as co-writer on Season 2. The series is produced by Accent Aigu Entertainment in association with Bell Media’s Crave. It is distributed internationally by Sphere Abacus, a Bell Media company, and is available in more than 130 countries. ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Third-Best U.S. 2nd Weekend With $135M-$140M+ Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” By ‘Jellicle’ Closing Tonight Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie Join ‘Heated Rivalry’ As Harris & Troy; S2 Set For Spring Epic Tops $1B Global; Poised To Become Nolan’s Top-Grossing Pic Read More About: 8 Comments

articles.title: Olivia Wilde Talks Fight To Get ‘The Invite’ A Theatrical Release Following Sundance Response: “I Was Passionate About It With A Lot Of Support”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Olivia Wilde Talks Fight To Get ‘The Invite’ A Theatrical Release Following Sundance Response: “I Was Passionate About It With A Lot Of Support” Sigurjón Sighvatsson Talks Rise Of Propaganda Films & Battles To Get David Lynch’s ‘Wild At Heart’ & ‘Twin Peaks’ Off The Ground – Locarno Elisabeth Moss, Daphne Schmon & Ash Mayfair Select 12 Finalists For Wscripted 2026 Screenplay List View All August 8, 2026 9:45am Olivia Wilde Deadline Olivia Wilde has revealed that she was “passionate” about getting a theatrical release for The Invite following the audience response to the comedy at Sundance. “I wanted to investigate this phenomenon that we found at Sundance when we felt the film have that chemical reaction with the audience the first time and it was extraordinary,” she told a press conference at the Locarno Film Festival where the film screens on the Piazza Grande this evening. “I thought, well, this was magic. We have to listen to this… we have to fight for it,” she continued. “If you don’t fight for it, listen, you know this… they bribe you to not take theatrical. It’s a bribe. You get paid more. Not me, not the filmmaker. The financiers will get a lot more money to go to streaming, and you can take that bribe and give that up if that’s where your priorities lie.” Related Stories News Sigurjón Sighvatsson Talks Rise Of Propaganda Films & Battles To Get David Lynch's 'Wild At Heart' & 'Twin Peaks' Off The Ground - Locarno News Felix Randau Reveals Why Claes Bang Was Perfect For The Role Of Himmler's Shady Masseur In 'I Is Another': "If Claes Tells You A Lie, You Want To Believe Him" Wilde thanked producer Megan Ellison at Annapurna for getting on board with her desire to get the film into cinemas, and agreeing to accept A24 ‘s theatrical offer, hinting that the streamers had gone higher. She also credited FilmNation Entertainment , which co-handled the domestic sale with UTA, for securing individual theatrical distributors internationally. Watch on Deadline Olivia Wilde Talks Fight To Get 'The Invite' A Theatrical Release Following Positive Sundance Audience Response: "They bribe you to not take theatrical. It's a bribe. You get paid more… and you can take that bribe and give that up if that's where your priorities lie.” pic.twitter.com/qfVXofMEjg — Deadline (@DEADLINE) August 8, 2026 “But we were really lucky that our financier gave me the opportunity to make this decision, which is something I don’t take lightly. She could have very easily said, no, we’re going to go with the much bigger offer. But I know that she, too, felt this incredible reaction that had happened at Sundance and that it was something worth investing in.” Beyond the audience reaction in Sundance, Wilde questioned the fact that comedy as a genre had come disconnected from cinema audiences. “I really feel that there’s no genre that benefits from the communal experience more than comedy… it’s an ancient part of our culture. As humans, we’ve gathered and told stories and laughed together for thousands of years in different forms, in different ways. “I felt that comedies had been relegated to kind of second tier that didn’t deserve theaters. And the first place we confronted that was really in production… When it came to shooting it on film, I was very passionate about shooting it on 35 millimeter. I hadn’t been able to do that yet. And I thought this is the one I’m gonna really fight for.” Wilde was speaking ahead of a sold-out screening of the film on Locarno’s 8,000 capacity Piazza Grande on Saturday evening. “Today’s very special for me and all of us because I was hoping we would all be seen a few theaters maybe a couple of hundred people in a theater and tonight we’re going to watch it with 8,000 people. I actually can’t believe it. I am in shock.” Since opening on June 26 in the U.S., The Invit e has grossed $23.5 million domestically, and added another $18 million globally across some 30 international territories. Ascot Elite will begin the film’s Swiss rollout on August 13. ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Third-Best U.S. 2nd Weekend With $135M-$140M+ Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” By ‘Jellicle’ Closing Tonight Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie Join ‘Heated Rivalry’ As Harris & Troy; S2 Set For Spring Epic Tops $1B Global; Poised To Become Nolan’s Top-Grossing Pic Read More About: 1 Comments

articles.title: Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Madonna Pays Tribute To Late ‘Ray Of Light’ Producer William Orbit: “Your Music Gave Me A Magic Carpet To Fly On” Morrissey Cancels This Month’s Four-Show Las Vegas Residency Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses” View All August 8, 2026 10:30am André De Shields as Old Deuteronomy in Cats: The Jellicle Ball Matthew Murphy and Evan Zimmerman for MurphyMade Composer Andrew Lloyd Webber is “gutted” that the Broadway production of his Cats: The Jellicle Ball is closing tonight at the Broadhurst Theatre, five months earlier than originally planned. In an emotional message posted on Instagram, Lloyd Webber says he hopes the show’s closing will serve as a warning about “the unsustainable cost” of producing new shows on Broadway. Related Stories Reviews ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Broadway Review: A Queer, Radiant Reinvention Makes A Lasting Memory News ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’ Scores Best Week Ever As Closing Date Nears – Broadway Box Office “I’m gutted that the wonderful Broadway production of Cats: The Jellicle Ball is closing today,” he writes. “I’m immensely proud to have been a part of an incredibly daring production whose cast and creative team broke new ground on Broadway and gave 17 actors their Broadway debut.” He continues, “Maybe the show’s closing just might be remembered as the moment that caused everyone involved with Broadway to come to their senses and address the unsustainable cost of producing and running any new show now on The Great White Way, let alone saying new work.” Watch on Deadline See the message below, along with a note of thanks to fans from the show’s producers who teased “a lot more Jellicle joy to bring to this world” in the days ahead. Today’s message isn’t the first time Lloyd Webber has expressed his disappointment about the early closing. Last month, when the August 8 closing date was announced, he wrote, in part, “As someone who is still as in love with Broadway as I was when I was a teenager, I beg the theatre owners, unions and producers to come together urgently to address what is a crisis coming to a head. Broadway is in dire danger of rivalling Hollywood’s empty soundstages with increasingly dark theatres.” That IG post drew both praise and harsh criticism among commenters. While Sunset Blvd. star Nicole Scherzinger commended Lloyd Webber as “exactly the person” to “help drive the change that’s needed,” others rejected his seeming equating of landlords and union members in sharing the responsibility of Broadway’s financial uncertainties. “So have the audacity to call out out Shubert Organization which has a monopoly on almost half the Broadway theaters,” wrote one of Lloyd Webber’s followers. “Call out their greed. They want producers to cover the rent and the entire operating costs. They want to keep the telecharge fees which they own. How is this allowed?” Wrote a member of a costume crew, “Leave the union workers out of this we deserve to be paid fairly for our work. if you can’t afford to pay us fairly then you can’t afford to produce a show right. Very dangerous to include the unions in this to be honest,” while actor and dancer Neil Haskell wrote, “Most Broadway actors can barely afford to live in the city.” Tonight’s closing will almost certainly have at least one immediate impact: A bump in final-week ticket sales. While the box office report for the week won’t be out until Tuesday, last week’s figures showed Cats: The Jellicle Ball posting its best box office numbers ever as last-chancers scrambled for seats. The production was at standing room only for the week ending August 2, grossing $1,405,709. That’s an increase of $216,278 over the previous week. Regarding today’s message from the composer, at least one famous commenter and Broadway devotee had a suggestion. “Why didn’t alw just fund it himself,” commented Rosie O’Donnell. “he’s a billionaire.” A big fan of the show, O’Donnell did add a “Like” to Lloyd Webber’s message. articles.title: Morrissey Cancels This Month’s Four-Show Las Vegas Residency
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Madonna Pays Tribute To Late ‘Ray Of Light’ Producer William Orbit: “Your Music Gave Me A Magic Carpet To Fly On” Morrissey Cancels This Month’s Four-Show Las Vegas Residency Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses” View All August 8, 2026 12:11pm Morrissey Kevin Winter/Getty Images Morrissey , the ex-Smiths frontman with a penchant for canceling shows, has added to his track record: All four performances of his planned August Las Vegas residency have been scrubbed. The four-show stand at the Wynn Las Vegas’ Encore Theater was set to begin August 14 and wrap up August 19, but ticket-holders received an email yesterday announcing the latest turn of events, according to a report by Deadline sister publication Rolling Stone today. “Hello, we regret to inform you that Morrissey – Live in Concert, scheduled for August 14, 15, 18, and 19 at Encore Theater at Wynn Las Vegas, has been canceled,” the email reads. “Due to unforeseen logistical issues, the scheduled Las Vegas residency cannot take place.” Related Stories News Morrissey Tour To Resume Tuesday After Two Shows Canceled Due To "Credible" Death Threat News Smiths For Sale? Morrissey Puts Stake In Iconic Band Up For Potential Big Bucks Bids The event has been removed from The Wynn’s Entertainment page , and listings on Ticketmaster indicate, “Unfortunately, the Event Organizer has had to cancel your event.” When Rolling Stone broke the story this morning, Morrissey’s official website still listed the shows, but no more: The site’s tour page indicates the next show as Chicago’s Riot Fest on September 19. (The singer is also set to perform on September 26 at New York City’s CBGB Fesival, alongside Patti Smith, Buzzcocks, Bikini Kill and other punk pioneers). Watch on Deadline Morrissey last performed on August 1 in Portugal. As Rolling Stone notes, Morrissey “has become somewhat notorious for canceling or postponing gigs for a wide variety of reasons,” canceling 22 scheduled performances in 2025 alone, with another 10 postponed. Among the stated reasons for the cancellations have been illness, “adverse reaction to a prescription medication,” “sleep deprivation,” “flu” and “reasons completely beyond our control.” Vegas adds “unforeseen logistical challenges” to the mix. ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Third-Best U.S. 2nd Weekend With $135M-$140M+ Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” By ‘Jellicle’ Closing Tonight Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie Join ‘Heated Rivalry’ As Harris & Troy; S2 Set For Spring Epic Tops $1B Global; Poised To Become Nolan’s Top-Grossing Pic Read More About: 5 Comments

articles.title: Madonna Pays Tribute To Late ‘Ray Of Light’ Producer William Orbit: “Your Music Gave Me A Magic Carpet To Fly On”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Madonna Pays Tribute To Late ‘Ray Of Light’ Producer William Orbit: “Your Music Gave Me A Magic Carpet To Fly On” Morrissey Cancels This Month’s Four-Show Las Vegas Residency Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses” View All August 8, 2026 12:44pm William Orbit, Madonna accepting Grammy Award, as seen in her tribute today Instagram screen capture Madonna paid tribute to her late Ray of Light producer William Orbit , saying in an Instagram post that he gave her “a magic carpet to fly on.” “I had an epiphany when I met you and started working with you,” she writes today. “I realized that music did not have to fit into categories or genres. So we created our own.” See the post below. Orbit, who won a Grammy for his work on Madonna’s multiplatinum album Ray of Light and also worked with such other artists as U2, Britney Spears, No Doubt and Blur, died July 23 at the age of 69. His death was announced by his family this week. Related Stories News William Orbit Dies: Grammy-Winning Producer Of Madonna’s ‘Ray Of Light’ Was 69 News Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” About Tonight’s Closing Of ‘Cats: The Jellicle Ball’; Composer Hopes Broadway Will “Come To Its Senses” Madonna’s tribute today is accompanied by footage from the “Ray of Light” song video as well as a clip of them accepting the Best Pop Album Grammy in 1999. Watch on Deadline “Goodbye William Orbit,” she writes. “I had an epiphany when I met you and started working with you. I realized that music did not have to fit into categories or genres. So we created our own. You pressed a magic button inside of me and I fell into a galaxy of unrealized dreams. Your music gave me a magic carpet to fly on and I visited many places. Sad and Joyful. “I sang in ways I’d never sung before,” she continues. “I used words without caring if they made sense or not. In many ways you were my Ray of Light – as was my daughter Lola who was born around this time – I was starting a new chapter, I was choosing another road to walk down – and you were right by my side with your crooked teeth and your genius, way of hearing music. The studio was often church like and I would sit in silence, waiting for your ideas to explode out of your keyboard or your guitar and then I would run with them……….. “I miss those days. Only you could inspire me to write a song like Drowned World or Swim. You were so otherworldly. So singular. “The years passed and I moved on to make music with other people, but I have never forgotten you or the magical time we spent together. Goodbye Billy Bubbles. I was so lucky to have known you and fallen down the rabbit hole with you.” View this post on Instagram ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Third-Best U.S. 2nd Weekend With $135M-$140M+ Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” By ‘Jellicle’ Closing Tonight Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie Join ‘Heated Rivalry’ As Harris & Troy; S2 Set For Spring Epic Tops $1B Global; Poised To Become Nolan’s Top-Grossing Pic Read More About: 2 Comments

articles.title: Melissa Barrera Takes Weekend Off From Broadway’s ‘Titanique’ After She “Lost My Voice” On-Stage
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Obama Blames Larry David For 2014 Tan Suit Debacle In ‘Life, Larry & the Pursuit of Unhappiness’ Finale Matthew McConaughey Performs “Quill” In Scene From ‘The Rivals of Amziah King’ — Watch Jane Schoenbrun On Deconstructing The “Toxic Soup” Of The Slasher Genre In ‘Teenage Sex & Death at Camp Miasma’: “It’s There In The DNA” View All August 8, 2026 1:20pm Melissa Barrera in Broadway's 'Titanique' Evan Zimmerman for MurphyMade As Melissa Barrera enters the final stretch of her Broadway debut run in Titanique , she’s taking a few days off to get her voice and body back into performance shape. On Saturday, the actress who plays Rose DeWitt Bukater in the hit Titanic (1997) musical parody announced that she “lost her voice” during a performance this week and is taking the weekend off to recuperate. “Doing 8 shows a week of a Broadway musical is no joke,” she wrote on her Instagram Story. “After being non-stop since March 26 my body finally told me to take a break. I lost my voice after Wednesday’s show and had to call out Thursday. I did vocal rest and went back in for last night’s show. Related Stories News ‘Titanique’ Star Marla Mindelle Takes Deadline On An Exclusive Tour Of Her Custom-Designed Backstage ‘Diva’s Cabin’ – On The Go With Deadline News ‘Titanìque’ And ‘The Rocky Horror Show’ Extend Broadway Engagements Into Fall “I pushed through because I hate missing shows and missing y’all who travel from all over to see us… But it was mortifying and stressful and by the end of the show I couldn’t even sing, there was no voice left. So I’m taking this weekend off to rest and let my voice come back.” Watch on Deadline Barrera continued, “Gotta listen to our bodies and there is no shame in that, even though it pains me to miss a single second on that beautiful stage. Love y’all. Sorry to miss you. Will also be out Aug 21 and 22 for different reasons. Final TITANIQUE performance Sept 20!” With performances beginning at the St. James Theatre back in March, Barrera made her debut in the original Broadway cast of the musical parody, which was nominated for four Tony Awards, including Best Musical. articles.title: ‘Heated Rivalry’ Author Appears To Dismiss Negative Reactions To Season 2 Casting
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Obama Blames Larry David For 2014 Tan Suit Debacle In ‘Life, Larry & the Pursuit of Unhappiness’ Finale Matthew McConaughey Performs “Quill” In Scene From ‘The Rivals of Amziah King’ — Watch Jane Schoenbrun On Deconstructing The “Toxic Soup” Of The Slasher Genre In ‘Teenage Sex & Death at Camp Miasma’: “It’s There In The DNA” View All August 8, 2026 2:25pm Rachel Reid attends the premiere of 'Heated Rivalry' at TIFF Lightbox on Nov. 24, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario. Harold Feng/Getty Images As Heated Rivalry hits the ice for another season with some new teammates, there’s bound to be some opinions about the casting choices for the book series’ beloved characters. Following the news that Justice Smith and Charlie Gillespie have been cast in Season 2 , author Rachel Reid appeared to respond to negative online reactions to the news that the actors will portray Harris Drover and Troy Barrett, respectively, the couple from Role Model , the fifth book in her bestselling Game Changer series. “Thinking about all the people last summer who told me the casting for llya and Shane was wrong and bad…” wrote Reid on her Instagram Story with a side-eye selfie. articles.title: ‘Monsters Of God’ Slithers Onto HBO: Reptilian Docuseries From ‘Tiger King’s Eric Goode
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew ‘The Work In Progress’ Trailer: Documentary From E.P. Robert Reich Finds Potent Way To “Help Bridge America’s Deepest Divides” TIFF Docs Lineup Revealed: Rapinoe, Said, Love, And A Scent Of Musk Doc Talk Podcast: Director Keith Scholey On His Emmy-Nominated ‘Ocean’ Voyage With The Amazing David Attenborough View All August 8, 2026 2:50pm Tom Crutchfield holds a snake in 'Monsters of God' HBO HBO ’s new documentary series Monsters of God abounds with colorful creatures – and those are just the humans. The five-parter from Tiger King co-director Eric Goode features reptile dealers with a fondness for creepy crawlies and a loose connection to ethical and legal mores. There’s Tom Crutchfield, who loves women with the ardor of Pepé Le Pew but spends most of his time not in pursuit of the ladies but of exotic snakes, lizards, alligators, turtles and whatnot. His arch rival: Hank Molt (aptly named, given that snakes molt), a man who pioneered the shady trade of importing rare and often endangered reptiles to the United States (HBO calls it a “billion-dollar criminal enterprise.”). Related Stories Trailers 'War' First Look & Trailer: Dominic West & Sienna Miller Do Battle In HBO/Sky Divorce Drama Casting 'I Love LA' Adds Taron Egerton, Jamie Chung, Milan Carter & More For Season 2 Reptile dealer Hank Molt in ‘Monsters of God’ Another key Monsters of God character: Anson Wong, a Malaysian “exporter” (to use a polite term) perhaps as cold-blooded as the creatures he rounds up and dispatches around the world. His nickname – “the Pablo Escobar of reptiles.” Watch on Deadline The template for the series is supplied by the 2008 book The Lizard King: The True Crimes and Passions of the World’s Greatest Reptile Smugglers , written by Bryan Christy. The author, who appears in the series and serves as a consulting producer, took part in a panel discussion of Monsters of God Thursday night after HBO screened episode 1 at Vidiots in Los Angeles. He praised Goode and fellow producers for wrangling the reptilian importers, typically a wary group. L-R Executive producer/co-writer Jeremy McBride, moderator Jason Segel, director/E.P. Eric Goode “I know what it took to run these people down, to get people to say ‘yes’ to you coming in their place,” Christy told the moderator, the actor Jason Segel. “And with a camera . I just had a pencil… It’s amazing what they brought together. And they’re celebrating the animals in a way that I hope gets people to care more about this sort of maligned species.” Goode needed no persuading about the beauty of animals like New Caledonian geckos, African bush vipers, Caribbean rock iguanas, and similar Cyclura. He’s been an avid collector since childhood. Eric Goode back in the day with a Southwestern pond turtle. “I have a confession to make,” he said at the Q&A, alluding to his collecting urge. “I’ve been an addict for over 50 years and now I’m still not sober, sorry to say.” The challenge of convincing reptile dealers to appear on camera became evident during the panel discussion, which included Crutchfield and Mike Van Nostrand, both Florida men who have served time behind bars for their activities (in 2022, Van Nostrand was convicted in a scheme to smuggle “illegally-harvested Florida turtles out of the United States and into China, Japan, and other places,” per the Department of Justice). “I didn’t like the Tiger King ,” Van Nostrand stated flatly. “Eric was a little tricky one.” For his part, Crutchfield called Tiger King “one of the weirdest movies I’ve ever seen.” A New Caledonian gecko in ‘Monsters of God’ Along with Tiger King , Goode also directed the 2024 HBO documentary series Chimp Crazy about people obsessed with raising chimpanzees as essentially human children. At the Q&A, he addressed contrasts between Tiger King , Chimp Crazy , and Monsters of God . “Right now, a lot of people are thinking I’m trying to take down the reptile world,” Goode said of Monsters of God . “Yes, I didn’t like people keeping chimpanzees in Chimp Crazy . I wanted laws changed so you couldn’t do that. I didn’t want people having 200 tigers in their backyard [in Tiger King ]. Reptiles are different. It’s nuanced. And as Mike [Van Nostrand] says, if people were breeding more reptiles that may take pressure off of the poachers. And so there’s a lot of gray in this story and it’s not painting anyone with one brush. Law enforcement made a lot of mistakes. We’ve made mistakes. The zoos made big mistakes and we’re all complicit.” An African bush viper in ‘Monsters of God’ Zoos are complicit, the series makes clear, by paying dealers like Molt and Crutchfield to supply them with exotic reptiles knowing full well the wranglers were violating U.S. and international law. Federal officials with the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service don’t seem to come off much better, to judge from episode 1. Nobody’s motives seem 100 percent pure in Monsters of God , self-assessments notwithstanding. “What I really want people to get out of my complete performance from the very beginning to the end,” Crutchfield asserted at the Q&A, “is my great passion and my great love, and more importantly, my great respect for all of these monsters of God that you’re going to see.” Van Nostrand chimed in sardonically, “Are you saying money had nothing to do with it?” “So far,” Crutchfield replied. Fresh episodes of Monsters of God will debut on HBO the next four Thursdays, and stream on HBO Max. Audiences may get hooked, mirroring the obsessional quality of true lizard people. Jason Segel, for one, pronounced himself a fan of the series. “At times it feels like Goodfellas . It feels like Scarface sometimes,” Segel enthused at the Q&A. “I watched every episode over two days and was mesmerized. I can’t wait for all of you guys to see it.” ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Third-Best U.S. 2nd Weekend With $135M-$140M+ Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” By ‘Jellicle’ Closing Tonight Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie Join ‘Heated Rivalry’ As Harris & Troy; S2 Set For Spring Epic Tops $1B Global; Poised To Become Nolan’s Top-Grossing Pic Read More About: Comments

Nicole Rivelli/Universal Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection/Universal Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection While One Night Only is intended as a romantic-comedy, there are some obvious dystopian undertones that audiences can’t ignore. Director Will Gluck recently addressed online comparisons between the Purge franchise and his new Universal rom-com, which is now in theaters, about two New Yorkers (Monica Barbaro and Callum Turner) who meet on the one night a year premarital sex is legal. “I am very aware of the online discourse about this world and this movie being the ‘sex Purge,’ and rightfully so,” he told SlashFilm . “But I don’t want this movie to be about that. And I know I get some blowback going, ‘How could you make a movie about this not being about that?’ Because I love exploring characters and situations. Related Stories Reviews ‘One Night Only’ Review: Callum Turner And Monica Barbaro Charm In A Madcap Rom-Com Where Premarital Sex Is Limited To A Single Day Of The Year News Universal Warns “If We Don’t Act Now, Love Will Leave Theaters Forever” — But Says There’s “Hope” For The Rom-Com In Will Gluck’s ‘One Night Only’ Gluck added, “Whenever us humans get put in situations, no matter how or why the situation happens, we still have to be humans and get through the day. articles.title: Jane Schoenbrun On Deconstructing The “Toxic Soup” Of The Slasher Genre In ‘Teenage Sex & Death at Camp Miasma’: “It’s There In The DNA”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Obama Blames Larry David For 2014 Tan Suit Debacle In ‘Life, Larry & the Pursuit of Unhappiness’ Finale Matthew McConaughey Performs “Quill” In Scene From ‘The Rivals of Amziah King’ — Watch Jane Schoenbrun On Deconstructing The “Toxic Soup” Of The Slasher Genre In ‘Teenage Sex & Death at Camp Miasma’: “It’s There In The DNA” View All August 8, 2026 6:30pm Hannah Einbinder in 'Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma' (2026) Mubi/Courtesy Everett Collection With their latest directorial outing, Jane Schoenbrun used subtle pieces of nostalgia to deconstruct the slasher genre. The Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma writer/director explained to Deadline that they wanted to create “a mindset where you can really enjoy something scary,” noting the frequent symbolism of candy and junk food as providing an atmosphere “that’s actually safe” while diving into a horror movie or exploring sexuality after trauma. “There is this idea that if it gets too real, you can turn it off, that you’re exploring something dangerous, doing it in a way that’s actually safe,” said Schoenbrun, who is non-binary . “Which in my experience of coming into my sexual identity post-transition, kind of required some gummy candy on hand. What I mean by that is, even if we’re going to be exploring scary and vulnerable and potentially embarrassing, triggering parts of ourselves, we trust each other well enough to know that at any moment, we can be like, ‘Let’s stop, we gotta just eat some fucking gummies.'” Related Stories News ‘Teenage Sex And Death At Camp Miasma’ Trailer: Hannah Einbinder & Gillian Anderson Lead Jane Schoenbrun’s Meta Return To Feature Filmmaking News ‘Teenage Sex and Death At Camp Miasma’ Director & Cast Set ‘Secretary’ Live Reading In Schoenbrun’s latest film, Hannah Einbinder stars as queer director Kris, who is tapped to helm a new installment of the long-running Camp Miasma horror franchise. While courting Billy Presley (Gillian Anderson), the actress who played the “final girl” in the original film, to reprise her role, the pair spirals into a psychosexual frenzy as the slasher’s killer, Little Death (Jack Haven), comes to life. Watch on Deadline Acknowledging the problematic trans representation of horror films like Psycho (1960), Sleepaway Camp (1983), The Silence of the Lambs (1991) and Texas Chainsaw Massacre: The Next Generation (1995), Schoenbrun admitted the genre has been “catnip to me since I was 10 years old,” and they jumped at the chance to direct their own. Jane Schoenbrun attends the ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ premiere on Aug. 5, 2026 in New York City. “So many slashers do have this sense of humor, and even if they’re not overtly meta like the Scream movies are, they’re so aware of their own tropes and the sort of rituals … And I just loved that from a young age and loved all of the little rituals within it, and so, getting to make my own is just like play and joy,” they explained. “But it also felt like the perfect way to talk about sex and to talk about my experience as a trans person post-transition, learning how to come into a sexual identity that I could feel comfortable within, because so many of these movies are obviously deeply engaged in gender and sexual roles, and these movies have so much to say for better or for worse about deviants,” said Schoenbrun. “It is there in the DNA of the slasher genre that these movies are talking about fear and desire, gender and sexuality, normativity and deviance. And that’s all swimming in the toxic soup of the genre, so I wanted to remake it in my own language.” Read on about Jane Schoenbrun’s love letter to the slasher genre with Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma , now playing in theaters. DEADLINE: It was really fun to see the slasher genre through your eyes. Tell me about finding inspiration in that genre and “final girls.” JANE SCHOENBRUN: I mean, it was the easiest thing in the world because it’s just one of those genres that has been catnip to me since I was 10 years old. I just raided the horror section of the video store as a kid from an age when I really shouldn’t have been doing that, like in 5th grade, I watched in the span of about one week, every Nightmare on Elm Street movie. I think that I was always drawn to movies and really anything entertainment where it felt forbidden in some way, like the thing on the tape, how is that even allowed? And that’s the thing that I love about a lot of my favorite slashers. Don’t get me wrong, I love like brutal ones, like I love Texas Chainsaw , that’s a nasty movie at its core, and that’s what’s so special about it. But so many slashers do have this sense of humor, and even if they’re not overtly meta like the Scream movies are, they’re so aware of their own tropes and the sort of rituals of, OK, what’s the most outrageous way that like these like dumb kids can get killed? But watching it, it’s not about fear a lot of the time, it’s about joy and celebration. And I just loved that from a young age and loved all of the little rituals within it, and so, getting to make my own is just like play and joy. But it also felt like the perfect way to talk about sex and to talk about my experience as a trans person post-transition, learning how to come into a sexual identity that I could feel comfortable within, because so many of these movies are obviously deeply engaged in gender and sexual roles, and these movies have so much to say for better or for worse about deviants, whether that be Norman Bates or Buffalo Bill or Sleepway Camp or Jason, Michael Myers, Leatherface in drag. It is there in the DNA of the slasher genre that these movies are talking about fear and desire, gender and sexuality, normativity and deviance. And that’s all swimming in the toxic soup of the genre, so I wanted to remake it in my own language. ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ (2026) DEADLINE: I’m curious about the symbolism of all the processed junk food and the chandelier of wrappers. SCHOENBRUN: The junk food in the movie, I forget when it found its way in there. It’s like so much of the movie is about, like I said, ritual, about being in a mindset where you can really enjoy something scary, whether that be Kris [Hannah Einbinder] in bed, with, you know, with Raisinets and the popcorn, watching a schlocky horror movie, or the two characters learning how to be present and enjoy sex after a lot of trauma. There is this idea that if it gets too real, you can turn it off, that you’re exploring something dangerous, doing it in a way that’s actually safe. Which in my experience of coming into my sexual identity post-transition, kind of required some gummy candy on hand. What I mean by that is, even if we’re going to be exploring scary and vulnerable and potentially embarrassing, triggering parts of ourselves, we trust each other well enough to know that at any moment, we can be like, “Let’s stop, we gotta just eat some fucking gummies.” DEADLINE: And one thing I really love—I just feel like it’s a theme in your work—is how it depicts the way media and entertainment influence us. Why does that inspire you? SCHOENBRUN: I think it comes from a fascination and sensitivity to the complex relationship between what we think of as fiction and what we think of as reality, which we tend to, as a society, think of as pointing in one direction. Like, reality dictates fiction, not vice-versa, but when you actually look at the way the world works, it’s like one echoes off the other. And I think a complicated, sometimes terrifying and sometimes beautiful way, where the fiction, the cultural norms, the things we grow up looking at on our screens, the roles that we’re told people play, they kind of inspire us to create reality. There’s something liberating when you start thinking in that way. I think it’s a way of thinking that we as a culture, could do a lot more of. To think about the idea of fiction inspiring reality just as much as reality is inspiring fiction, is a potential path to liberating us from this hellscape that they’re telling us is the only way the world can be. Gillian Anderson in ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ (2026) DEADLINE: And I know you have the Secretary reading. Tell me what it’s been like prepping for that and why you all chose that movie. SCHOENBRUN: I mean, that was such a huge influence on on Miasma . There just aren’t that many fun and funny movies about deviant sex. And just the way that movie is like feather light while talking about really raw and taboo things, it is just really inspiring to me. And the dynamic between those two main characters is definitely one that had a lot of influence on on Kris and Billy’s [Gillian Anderson] relationship in Miasma . And it’s already to me a very queer movie in its way, but having Gillian reading the James Spader part and Hannah reading the Maggie Gyllenhaal part, I think it’s just gonna be like a very unique joy. Honestly, we’ve been prepping a little bit, but I think it’s just gonna be about getting up there and feeling the chemistry of it all, and just letting these folks who we have all gotten to know each other really, really well, but we haven’t actually done anything wacky and creative like that in a while, like as a reunion, it’s gonna be a real blast, I think. ‘Brand New Day’ Eyes Third-Best U.S. 2nd Weekend With $135M-$140M+ Andrew Lloyd Webber “Gutted” By ‘Jellicle’ Closing Tonight Justice Smith & Charlie Gillespie Join ‘Heated Rivalry’ As Harris & Troy; S2 Set For Spring Epic Tops $1B Global; Poised To Become Nolan’s Top-Grossing Pic Read More About: Comments
