articles.title: ‘The Blacklist Was a Plague’ — Locarno Retrospective Curator Ehsan Khoshbakht Talks About What We Can Learn From the Intolerance of the Past
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 11:00pm PT ‘The Blacklist Was a Plague’ — Locarno Retrospective Curator Ehsan Khoshbakht Talks About What We Can Learn From the Intolerance of the Past By John Bleasdale Plus Icon John Bleasdale Guest Contributor Latest ‘The Blacklist Was a Plague’ — Locarno Retrospective Curator Ehsan Khoshbakht Talks About What We Can Learn From the Intolerance of the Past 5 hours ago Lucca Comics and Games, Europe’s Answer to Comic-Con, Sees 3% Rise in Attendees 9 months ago Hideo Kojima Talks ‘Death Stranding 2’ and the Importance of Connection: ‘It’s Not Connection With Headshots and Shooting Each Other’ 9 months ago See All Dalton Trumbo in '10 Hollywood Commie Writers Arraigned' Courtesy of UCLA One of the most shameful episodes in Hollywood’s history is being examined in a new retrospective to screen at the Locarno Film Festival : Red & Black: Hollywood Left and the Blacklist. Speaking to Variety , the retrospective’s curator, Ehsan Khoshbakht , speaks about the inspiration for the program, which features the work of directors, writers and stars such as John Garfield, Joseph Losey, Dalton Trumbo , Dorothy Parker, Richard Wright and Charles Chaplin . Related Stories Disney's Next Big Thing: Malachi Barton on 'Camp Rock 3,' Doomscrolling on TikTok and Not Hiding His Faith in God Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread What was your starting point for the retrospective? I have often wondered why someone who could have lived a life of comfort would instead fight for the Republicans in the Spanish Civil War, as the screenwriter Alvah Bessie did. Or why filmmakers such as Joseph Losey and Cy Endfield at the height of their success would leave their families, and end up working in Mexico, England or Italy, often forbidden even to use their real names. Trying to understand that inner compulsion — not to name names — became the starting point. Popular on Variety ‘España otra vez’ written by Alvah Bessie Courtesy of Mercury Films Did you see contemporary resonance in your program? My reaction was to intolerance and hysteria in the arts. This is not a right-versus-left program. It’s about what happens when the media are abused and misused; when smear campaigns and fear-mongering prevail over rationality and dialogue. There were films such as “Salt of the Earth,” whose Mexican actress was forcibly removed by immigration officers in the middle of production and deported. The blacklist caused serious health problems, tore families apart, drove people to suicide, and prevented some potentially great films from ever being made. It was a plague. So, it is a bitter irony that 80 years later, Dr. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment the other day. Is it ever going to stop? Every film in the program responds in some way to one of the ugly excesses of the world now, and to the destructive policies of the current administration in the U.S. I didn’t select the program according to that criterion. It is just a painful and frightening coincidence. How did exile change the way the filmmakers worked? They were forced to adapt to filmmaking modes and industries that were alien, smaller and less streamlined. This introduced what I see as a brilliantly eclectic combination of European style and taste with American sensibility and dynamism. Losey’s “Stranger on the Prowl,” with its unusual and effective blend of neorealism and the man-on-the-run theme, is one example among many. Jules Dassin explored his previously unexamined fascination with the psychosexual. Both filmmakers went on to contribute to a modern cinematic language that could not have developed in America. Others, like Bernard Vorhaus, simply crashed out. ‘Mission to Moscow’ by Michael Curtiz Courtesy of BFI/Warner Bros. What films are you particularly excited about? I’m excited about some of the films for various reasons: some because they are key blacklist films that hadn’t been screened before, even in major retrospectives. For instance, the pro-Soviet and frankly embarrassing “Mission to Moscow,” which is a Hollywood film that depicts Stalin as a fair-minded, brilliant leader! Then there are some films that haven’t been screened in this particular context, such as “España otra vez,” the first Spanish film made under the Franco dictatorship to deal explicitly with the Spanish Civil War from the point of view of the defeated side — the Republicans. It’s in the program because it was written by and starred one of the Hollywood Ten, Alvah Bessie. ‘The Intimate Stranger’ Courtesy of BFI Another super-rare film is “The Intimate Stranger,” by Joseph Losey. Perhaps, the most self-conscious meditation on the blacklist. This film was impossible to show for decades. Losey’s son, Gavrik, will be in Locarno to introduce it. There are nearly thirty 35mm prints in the program, and for some of them to be seen in original format is a chance of a lifetime. The retrospective seems to hold a special place of esteem in Locarno among festival-goers. Other contemporary festivals allocate their worst venues to classic films, if they show them at all. Locarno gives us their best venue, the superb GranRex. I cannot think of any other film festival in the world that would allow me to select 50 titles — mostly in 35mm prints — edit a book of newly commissioned essays by leading scholars from around the world, and produce a podcast. I think it matters to our director, Giona Nazzaro , to go deeper into the history of cinema. He’s an avid cinephile. As for our partners, UCLA Film & TV Archive, Cinémathèque suisse and the BFI have all provided us with essential support. This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity. The 79th Locarno Film Festival runs over August 5-15. articles.title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Is Both a Promising Reboot and a Tedious Sequel: TV Review
articles.full_text: Aug 5, 2026 12:00am PT ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Is Both a Promising Reboot and a Tedious Sequel: TV Review By Alison Herman Plus Icon Alison Herman TV Critic aherman2006 Latest ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Is Both a Promising Reboot and a Tedious Sequel: TV Review 4 hours ago Ariana Grande May or May Not Be Struggling. We Can Talk About It Without Trying to Shame Her 17 hours ago ‘Rick and Morty’ Spinoff ‘President Curtis’ Plays It Safe, but Keeps the Sci-Fi Franchise Cruising: TV Review 1 week ago See All Courtesy of Apple TV Anyone with even the vaguest understanding of the profit motive can understand why Apple TV sports comedy “ Ted Lasso ” has returned three years after its poorly received — yet still widely watched — third season seemed to close the book on its story. A streaming service continuing to milk one of its few major hits doesn’t prohibit the result from being enjoyable; if the first three seasons of “Ted Lasso” are effectively one (overlong, especially toward the end) sports movie, then Season 4 is its perfectly routine sequel. And in a genre filled with redemptive second chances, “Ted Lasso” could use one of its own. If a show has the chance to correct for mistakes like overindulgence and bloat, why not take it? Related Stories Disney's Next Big Thing: Malachi Barton on 'Camp Rock 3,' Doomscrolling on TikTok and Not Hiding His Faith in God Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread Season 4 introduces a premise that gives Jason Sudeikis’ titular American-football-turned-British-football coach a chance at both a fresh start and a return to old stomping grounds. Two years after Ted walked away from AFC Richmond and took his signature mustache back to Kansas City, team owner Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham), marketing chief Keeley (Juno Temple) and operations head Leslie Higgins (Jeremy Swift) arrive stateside with an offer he can’t refuse: coaching the club’s brand-new women’s team, who begin their existence as the underdogs — specifically, Greyhounds — their male counterparts once were. Given the cultural bias against women’s sports leagues, they’ll likely remain so even if they succeed. Popular on Variety The concepts of class reunion (Ted goes back to London and gets the gang back together!) and clean slate (Ted takes on a new challenge!) are somewhat at odds. Sure enough, Season 4 is far more enjoyable as the latter than the former — even as “Ted Lasso” keeps privileging nostalgia and tired subplots over its best chance at a renaissance. Tanya Reynolds of “Sex Education” is a welcome addition as Alice Chilton, a coach whose constant scowl and clipped severity make her a well-suited foil for Ted’s sunny optimism until she inevitably warms to it. But, at least in the five episodes provided to critics out of an eventual 10, she’s pretty much the only new character who feels fully established, because “Ted Lasso” refuses to make room in the ensemble by sidelining (or is it touchlining?) old ones. Like Sudeikis, actor Brett Goldstein remains a creative force behind the camera, which may explain why his churlish then player, now coach Roy Kent remains such a presence despite the pivot away from his men’s squad. But while foregrounding Rebecca and Keeley makes sense given the renewed focus on women in sports, Roy and Keeley’s on-again, off-again romance lost its allure several seasons ago. Figures like Roy and Ted’s longtime deputy Beard (series co-creator Brendan Hunt) would be better deployed as occasional cameos, yet they remain load-bearing — and space-occupying — protagonists. The consequences can border on the absurd: a major decision by Ted’s ex-wife Michelle (Andrea Anders) is sped through rather than shown from her perspective; an episode hinges on a team problem with cliques that’s only depicted onscreen far too late. Until then, we’re mostly told about it by other characters with longer tenures. Contributing to the sense of overcrowding is an otherwise welcome development: no single episode of the first five clocks in at over an hour, the way so much of Season 3 did. “Ted Lasso” is not for everyone; the blindingly earnest social consciousness and relentless positivity some find so grating remain firmly in place. (Feminist commentary was never the series’ strong suit, and centering the women’s team prompts more of it than ever.) But Season 4 reigns in some excesses and offers glimpses of fresh new faces: a walk-on player who’s also a single mom; a goalie who refuses to wear gloves; a new mentor for Rebecca, played by comic legend Tracey Ullmann. If only the show would clear the field for them. ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Is Both a Promising Reboot and a Tedious Sequel: TV Review Production: Warner Bros. articles.title: Disney, TikTok Strike Content-Sharing Deal Aimed at Boosting Short-Form Programming on Disney+
articles.full_text: Aug 5, 2026 3:00am PT Disney, TikTok Strike Content-Sharing Deal Aimed at Boosting Short-Form Programming on Disney+ By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Disney, TikTok Strike Content-Sharing Deal Aimed at Boosting Short-Form Programming on Disney+ 1 hour ago Paramount Q2 Profit Dips, With Streaming Boost Offset by TV Declines 15 hours ago Jimmy Fallon is Nearly Last Late-Night Host Standing Amid Summer Hiatus 2 days ago See All Getty Images; Courtesy of Disney Disney is going long on short-form content. The entertainment giant struck an alliance with TikTok that will have creators on the popular quick-hit video service making shorts tied to characters and stories from Marvel, Pixar, Star Wars, FX and more. The resulting pieces from creators who opt-in to the program will be available on both TikTok and on Disney+ in the form of “Verts,” the company’s vertical video products. Related Stories Disney's Next Big Thing: Malachi Barton on 'Camp Rock 3,' Doomscrolling on TikTok and Not Hiding His Faith in God Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread “This collaboration creates a new bridge between the stories we tell and the creativity they inspire, giving creators a bigger stage to share what they’ve made, and audiences more to discover on Disney+ every day,” said Asad Ayaz, Disney’s chief marketing and brand officer, in a statement. Popular on Variety The agreement will launch in the U.S. in coming months, and the companies intend to move it to other markets around the world. Financial terms were not disclosed. It’s no secret that younger people are watching shorter videos with more frequency, including TikTok vignettes, Facebook Reels, even “whip-around” sports shows like NBC Olympics’ Gold Zone and NFL Red Zone. The format is driving conversations around everything from wellness to food to pop culture. Many prominent advertisers are also investing in it, with big-spending companies including Procter & Gamble and JCPenney creating “microdramas” and “microcontent.” Disney has telegraphed its interest for months. It already introduced “Verts” to ESPN’s direct-to-consumer streaming service, and unveiled plans for short-form video to surface on Disney+. “Short form and creative content, they’ve exploded in the past few years, and it’s an area we’re focused on because we have deeply committed fans who, you know, love our brands and our franchises and characters, and they want to engage with them in this new way,” said Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro, speaking during a May call with investors. “This is specifically important when we think about Gen Alpha, obviously, the newest generation of Disney fans. What we’re doing is we’re experimenting with short-form content in a variety of ways.” The TikTok alliance might fill in for a previous ambitious project that was ultimately scrapped. Disney in December unveiled a three-year deal with OpenAI that would have allowed users of the company’s generative-video Sora platform to generate short, user-prompted social videos using a set of more than 200 masked, animated or creature characters from Disney, Marvel, Pixar and Star Wars, as well as costumes, props and vehicles. Disney planned to make a $1 billion equity investment in OpenAI, and receive warrants to purchase additional equity. The project, however, was ultimately scrapped after OpenAI decided to shut Sora down. Now TikTok will help Disney move further into the emerging field. Both companies will administer a “Disney Creator Ambassador Program” that will give certain users incentives and access to events and career development. TikTok creators will gain access to assets related to hundreds of films and series from Disney’s vast library, and fans will be able to take part in a Disney-centered experience on TikTok that will be refreshed regularly. “Together with Disney, we’re bringing the authentic creator expression of the TikTok community to Disney+, inviting audiences to experience the shared creativity that makes fandom so powerful,” said Dawn Yang, global head of entertainment for TikTok, in a statement. There is some hope that allowing Disney intellectual property to fuel TikTok pieces will have a halo effect for Disney’s films and programs. Nearly half of respondents on a survey commissioned by TikTok and conducted by Ipsos, a market-research firm, said that discovering entertainment content on TikTok spurred them to go on to watch a movie or show on a streaming service or traditional TV. In January 2026, under a deal brokered by the Trump administration, ByteDance sold a majority stake in TikTok’s U.S. business to non-Chinese investors , including Oracle, Silver Lake and Abu Dhabi’s state-owned investment firm MGX. Beijing-based ByteDance retains 19.9% of the joint venture; the deal brought ByteDance and TikTok into compliance with the U.S.’s TikTok divest-or-ban law that went into effect in January 2025. ‘Heated Rivalry’ Success Sparks New Publishing House From Gay Adult Entertainment Giant Falcon | NakedSword (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Industry,’ ‘Widow’s Bay’ Lead 2026 TCA Awards Nominations Future Debuts at No. 1 With ‘The Real Me,’ as Rolling Stones and ‘Heated Rivalry’ Soundtrack Also Bow in Top 10 Connor Storrie Scores First Emmy Nomination Despite ‘Heated Rivalry’ Not Being Eligible ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Hacks,’ ‘Pluribus,’ ‘The Pitt’ Among Top Nominees for LGBTQ Critics’ Dorian TV Awards ‘Heated Rivalry’ Funko Pops Are Here: Shop the New Shane and Ilya Collectibles Ahead of Season 2 Loading comments... articles.title: Alba Rohrwacher-Starrer ‘A Common Story’ Gets Boarded by True Colours Ahead of its Venice and Toronto Premieres (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 5, 2026 3:05am PT Alba Rohrwacher-Starrer ‘A Common Story’ Gets Boarded by True Colours Ahead of its Venice and Toronto Premieres (EXCLUSIVE) By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Alba Rohrwacher-Starrer ‘A Common Story’ Gets Boarded by True Colours Ahead of its Venice and Toronto Premieres (EXCLUSIVE) 31 minutes ago ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Lands Biggest Opening Weekend in Middle East Box Office History 23 hours ago CNN Appoints Stefano Pozzebon as Rome Correspondent, Boosting European Coverage (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All Courtesy True Colours Italian sales company True Colours has taken world sales outside Italy on first-time director Anna Foglietta’s marriage drama “A Common Story” (“Una Storia”) starring Alba Rohrwacher , ahead of its bow in Venice and Toronto. Foglietta is an actress-turned director best-known to international audiences for her role in Italy’s smash hit “Perfect Strangers” that earned her a David di Donatello nomination. She also served as the official emcee of the 77th Venice International Film Festival. Related Stories 'The Odyssey' Breaks Records With Massive Debut at U.K. and Ireland Box Office Imax China Prepares Full 'Odyssey' Rollout Across Nearly 800 Screens as CEO Cites the 'Christopher Nolan Effect' (EXCLUSIVE) “Common Story” is the tale of Erika, played by Rohrwacher – whose credits include Pablo Larraín’s “Maria” and who served on the 2025 Cannes competition jury panel – and Mauro, played by Guido Caprino (“The Art of Joy”) whose simple life in the countryside is disrupted when their daughter Irene leaves to go to university abroad. Their house feels empty, and the balance on which this couple had based their lives seems to crumble. “This profound, intimate crisis will push them to really look at one another and understand if and how they can transform themselves and, consequently, their love,” says the synopsis. Popular on Variety “Common Story” will world premiere in September at Venice’s Horizons section, followed by a North-American launch in Toronto’s Discovery section. Foglietta’s directorial debut is produced by Italy’s HT Film, Indigo Film, Tenderstories and Blu One Lab with support from RAI Cinema and HBO Max also on board. BIM Distribuzione will release the film in Italy. “ This marks the beginning of an international journey we’re proud to embark on with True Colours, which shares our faith in a film that, thanks to its author’s vision, manages to delve with extraordinary sensitivity into the depths of everyday life,” said HT Film’s Viola Prestieri. Commented True Colours chief Elliot Gustin: “For the past 10 years, True Colours has consistently worked to discover and promote new Italian filmmakers. Anna is clearly one of the most talented voices of her generation and, with ‘A Common Story,’ she succeeds in portraying the crisis faced by a couple and a woman with great tenderness and sensitivity.” “We are delighted to be supporting this unique new female voice around the world, starting with the Venice and Toronto film festivals,” he added. Other titles on True Colours’ 2026 slate comprise Dario Albertini’s family drama “Armony,” starring Valerio Mastandrea and Asia Argento, that is launching from Locarno’s Piazza Grande; Susanna Nicchiarelli’s upcoming “Happy Days” with Riccardo Scamarcio (“Modì”) and Carlotta Gamba (“Portobello”); and Paolo Civati’s doc “Masters” which portrays nine prominent filmmakers including Jane Campion, Tim Burton, and Martin Scorsese. ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Industry,’ ‘Widow’s Bay’ Lead 2026 TCA Awards Nominations ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Hacks,’ ‘Pluribus,’ ‘The Pitt’ Among Top Nominees for LGBTQ Critics’ Dorian TV Awards Hudson Williams Confronts Autograph Hounds Who Followed Him Home in Viral Video: ‘Please F—ing Leave’ ‘Heated Rivalry’ Success Sparks New Publishing House From Gay Adult Entertainment Giant Falcon | NakedSword (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Heated Rivalry’ Creator Asks Fans to Not Crash Season 2 Filming: ‘Please Give Our Cast and Crew the Space They Need’ Connor Storrie Scores First Emmy Nomination Despite ‘Heated Rivalry’ Not Being Eligible Loading comments... articles.title: ‘The Mummy’ Poster Ads Banned From London Underground After Advertising Watchdog Cites ‘Distressing’ Imagery
articles.full_text: Aug 5, 2026 3:11am PT ‘The Mummy’ Poster Ads Banned From London Underground After Advertising Watchdog Cites ‘Distressing’ Imagery By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Cannibalism Comedy-Horror ‘Ali & Ben’s Spicy Meats,’ Starring Amir Nafis, Signs Abnormal Studios for Worldwide Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 10 hours ago Cate Blanchett, Nina Hoss on the Friendship Driving ‘Elektra/Persona’ at London’s National Theatre: ‘There’s a Lot of Masking and Unmasking’ 14 hours ago Tokyo’s TIFFCOM 2026 Expands IP Market, Adds AI and Anime Conferences 22 hours ago See All ©Warner Bros/Courtesy Everett Collection The U.K. Advertising Standards Authority has ruled that outdoor poster ads for “Lee Cronin’s The Mummy ” breached its code by presenting an image that gave “a realistic impression of a dead child,” while clearing companion TV and streaming spots for the same campaign. The ASA investigated four issues stemming from several complaints about ads for the Warner Bros Entertainment U.K. Ltd. cinema release, seen in April this year. The regulator upheld one complaint and rejected the other three in a ruling published Aug. 5. Related Stories Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread Disney's Next Big Thing: Malachi Barton on 'Camp Rock 3,' Doomscrolling on TikTok and Not Hiding His Faith in God “The ASA received 30 complaints, many of whom believed the ads were distressing for children and adults,” the ASA said. Popular on Variety Posters on the London Underground and at outdoor sites showed a close-up of a mummified female figure with grey, ashen skin, cracked lips and one eye swollen shut, wrapped in material resembling a shroud and inscribed with hieroglyphic-style symbols. The ASA said the figure’s features gave “a realistic impression of a dead child” and that the material wrapped around her added to that impression. Because the posters ran in untargeted locations, including on the London Underground and at a site visible from a children’s nursery, the regulator concluded the imagery was likely to distress young children who saw it. It ruled the posters unsuitable for outdoor display in that form, finding them in breach of CAP Code rules 1.3 and 4.2. Warner Bros. had argued the poster’s neutral expression, open eye and absence of a sarcophagus or restraints were deliberate choices meant to reduce distress, and noted the studio’s outdoor buying policy of keeping horror titles at least 100 metres from schools – a standard that does not extend to nurseries. The ASA ordered that the poster ads “must not appear in the form complained of” and directed Warner Bros. to keep future marketing likely to frighten young children away from places where they would see it. The ruling cited BCAP Code rules 1.2, 4.1, 4.10, 5.1 and 32.3, and CAP Code (Edition 12) rules 1.3, 4.1 and 4.2. The ASA rejected a separate complaint that the posters trivialized child loss or ongoing global conflicts, finding that text identifying the image as promotion for a film provided sufficient context, even if some viewers found it distasteful. Variety has reached out to Warner Bros. Discovery for comment. The campaign also included a TV ad and a matching Prime Video ad depicting a family receiving a call about a daughter who had gone missing eight years earlier, with the father questioning what she was doing in a 3000-year-old sarcophagus. On-screen text read, “Some Things Are Meant to Stay Buried.” Both ran with a post-7:30 p.m. scheduling restriction cleared by Clearcast. The ASA found the TV and streaming ads were unlikely to cause serious distress and that their scheduling restrictions were sufficient to limit exposure to young children, rejecting complaints that they should have been kept off air later or targeted more precisely on Prime Video. It also noted Clearcast’s data showing an average children’s index of 31 across the TV placements – well below the industry baseline of 100 that represents typical child viewership, indicating the actual child audience was low. articles.title: Disney Streaming Profit Doubles in June Quarter, Company Shifting Consumer Products to Studios Division
articles.full_text: Aug 5, 2026 3:36am PT Disney Streaming Profit Doubles in June Quarter, Company Shifting Consumer Products to Studios Division CEO Josh D'Amaro also outlines use of new AI tool for Disney's parks team By Jennifer Maas Plus Icon Jennifer Maas TV Business Writer @jmaasaronson Latest Disney Streaming Profit Doubles in June Quarter, Company Shifting Consumer Products to Studios Division 22 minutes ago Why Parents Are Still Afraid of Video Games After 50 Years and How a Gaming Nonprofit’s New Workshops Are Trying to Help 2 days ago ‘Talking Tom & Friends: World’ Kids’ Mobile Game Launches The Smurfs Crossover (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago See All ©Walt Disney Co./Courtesy Everett Collection Disney posted mixed results for the June 2026 quarter, as Disney+ and Hulu continued to boost profits and the theme parks division turning in solid performance. And Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro revealed his latest move to restructure the media conglomerate’s operations: He’s moving most of consumer products out of Disney Experiences and into the entertainment unit. In a letter to shareholders accompanying the earnings results Wednesday, Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro said that starting in the first quarter of fiscal 2027 (which runs October-December 2026) Disney will be moving “much” of its consumer products business results from the experiences segment to the entertainment segment. That means that sales for merchandise for “Avengers: Doomsday,” for example, would fall under entertainment revenue and put the bulk of the consumer products biz under Disney Entertainment’s studios group. The consumer products business accounted for $1.1 billion in revenue this quarter, the strongest year-over-year growth in five years. Related Stories Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread Disney's Next Big Thing: Malachi Barton on 'Camp Rock 3,' Doomscrolling on TikTok and Not Hiding His Faith in God “We believe this shift will have strategic and operational benefits by bringing the monetization of our IP through consumer products closer to the studios that create that IP,” D’Amaro, who previously ran Disney Experiences before stepping into the CEO job in March , wrote in the letter to shareholders. “Additionally, we believe this presentation will better reflect the returns our Entertainment segment is generating from the content it produces and make our Entertainment segment more comparable to peer reporting methodologies.” Popular on Variety On the streaming front, revenue from Disney+ and Hulu was up 11% for the April-June quarter, to $5.53 billion — and operating income in the entertainment streaming segment more than doubled, to $712 million, compared with $329 million in the year-earlier period. Disney said overall streaming subscription revenue was up 15%, to $4.7 billion, and ad sales increased 3%. The company no longer discloses total subscriber figures on a quarterly basis. In the letter, D’Amaro also outlined some AI developments at the company, including the Parks division’s recently implemented large-scale use of Disney’s proprietary AI tool, J.A.R.V.I.S. “We made our J.A.R.V.I.S. AI tool available to our more than 2,000 Imagineers earlier this year, giving them instant access to over 70 years of institutional knowledge,” D’Amaro wrote. “We’re using AI-powered digital twins and simulation tools to design and stress-test new attractions, including leveraging these tools for the Abu Dhabi park. And we’re applying AI to simplify the booking and planning journey for our guests, while equipping our cast members with AI-assisted tools to better serve guests in the moment.” Disney continued to tout the blockbuster success of “Toy Story 5” in the latest quarterly earnings results, revealing the film’s release has also led to the franchise as a whole reaching more than 2 billion hours streamed on Disney+ and record consumer products sales. Overall, Disney reported net income of $2.63 billion on $25.2 billion in revenue, with adjusted EPS of $2.06 (up from $1.51 with the exclusion of income tax and one-time impairment and severance charges) for the quarter ended June 27. Revenue was up 7% year over year while net income increased 28% (without those favorable exclusion, income was down 48%) for the period, which is Disney’s Q3 of fiscal 2027. Wall Street analysts on average forecast earnings per share (EPS) of $1.85 on $25.4 billion in revenue for the three months ended June 30 (Disney’s Q3 of fiscal 2026), according to data provider LSEG. Total segment operating income was up 21% to $5.6 billion. Free cash flow came in at $3.1 billion. Following recent layoffs , D’Amaro noted that Disney remains “highly focused on reducing costs across the enterprise to create incremental capacity to invest for growth and are evaluating a variety of levers, including reductions in labor and SG&A.” The CEO says the company is “mid-stream in this work” and “will provide future updates on our progress.” Previously, Disney had set an $8 billion goal for share repurchases in fiscal 2026, which ends in September. With the confirmation of the sale of Disney’s 50% stake in A+E Global Media to an affiliate of co-owner Hearst, Disney said it will use the approximately $1.2 billion in cash from the sale to increase its total share repurchases for the year to at least $9 billion. Disney took a $812 million impairment charge during the quarter due to its investment in A+E. Severance costs for the quarter were $88 million. Overall, Disney’s entertainment segment (which includes film and TV studios and networks as well as the streaming business) revenue was up 6% to $11.3 billion for the quarter. The division continued to receive a boost from the acquisition of a large stake in Fubo last fall, which it combined with the Hulu live TV business. The addition of Fubo contributed a 4% lift in subscription and affiliate fees revenue, which was up a total of 12%. Ad sales for the entertainment division were down 1% on lower rates. Content sales decreased 6% due to a decrease in TV/video-on-demand and home entertainment distribution sales. On the movie front, Disney praised “Toy Story 5” for surpassing $1 billion in global box office, bringing the franchise’s lifetime global box office to more than $4 billion, while downplaying recent releases “Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu” and the live-action “Moana” movie, both of which “underperformed our box office expectations,” Disney said. ESPN revenue for the quarter was up 4% to $4.5 billion. Ad sales increased 5% on higher impressions. Operating income declined 17% to $858 million, a larger drop than the 14% that Disney previously estimated due to a double-digit percentage increase in programming expenses, including the timing of new rights agreements, on the close of the NFL Network deal. “Contributing to the lower-than-expected operating income were four-game sweeps in early rounds of the NBA Playoffs and the impact of a network carriage dispute,” Disney said. Disney Experiences, which currently houses theme parks, cruises and consumer products, saw June quarter revenue of $10 billion (up 10%) and operating income of $3 billion (up 20%). Attendance at Disney domestic parks grew 3% from April-June. Disney World in particular experiencing a “stand-out quarter, with healthy core attendance increases from domestic tourists and annual passholders, and effective summer promotions and new experiences that further supplemented growth,” though Disney notes it has “continued to face headwinds from international attendance at our domestic parks.” For the July-September quarter, the company expects total segment operating income of approximately $4.9 billion, with the inclusion of financial results from a 53rd week of operations. “Our strong fiscal Q3 results and reiterated full-year outlook reinforce our confidence that we are uniquely well positioned,” D’Amaro said in the letter to shareholders. “Decades of IP investment have built deep fan connections that translate into strong financial results. Our accelerating global guests growth at Experiences, ‘Toy Story 5’s’ theatrical and consumer products success, and strong ESPN viewership gains all helped expand our consumer reach this quarter. Together, our results show a unique ability to engage consumers at scale, both digitally and physically, even amid macro uncertainty.” Also Wednesday, Disney struck a content deal with TikTok that will let the app’s creators (initially in the U.S.) make shorts tied to characters and stories from Marvel, Pixar, Star Wars, FX and other properties. The resulting creator videos will be available on both TikTok and on Disney+ in the form of “Verts,” the company’s vertical video format. ‘Heated Rivalry’ Success Sparks New Publishing House From Gay Adult Entertainment Giant Falcon | NakedSword (EXCLUSIVE) Hudson Williams Confronts Autograph Hounds Who Followed Him Home in Viral Video: ‘Please F—ing Leave’ Future Debuts at No. 1 With ‘The Real Me,’ as Rolling Stones and ‘Heated Rivalry’ Soundtrack Also Bow in Top 10 ‘Heated Rivalry’ Creator Asks Fans to Not Crash Season 2 Filming: ‘Please Give Our Cast and Crew the Space They Need’ ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Industry,’ ‘Widow’s Bay’ Lead 2026 TCA Awards Nominations ‘Heated Rivalry’ Funko Pops Are Here: Shop the New Shane and Ilya Collectibles Ahead of Season 2 Loading comments... articles.title: Prateek Kuhad to Make Feature Film Acting Debut in Marginal MediaWorks, D36 and Jugaad’s ‘Drowning,’ Directed by Dar Gai (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 5, 2026 4:00am PT Prateek Kuhad to Make Feature Film Acting Debut in Marginal MediaWorks, D36 and Jugaad’s ‘Drowning,’ Directed by Dar Gai (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Cannibalism Comedy-Horror ‘Ali & Ben’s Spicy Meats,’ Starring Amir Nafis, Signs Abnormal Studios for Worldwide Sales (EXCLUSIVE) 10 hours ago Cate Blanchett, Nina Hoss on the Friendship Driving ‘Elektra/Persona’ at London’s National Theatre: ‘There’s a Lot of Masking and Unmasking’ 14 hours ago Tokyo’s TIFFCOM 2026 Expands IP Market, Adds AI and Anime Conferences 22 hours ago See All Marginal MediaWorks Prateek Kuhad , the Indian singer-songwriter known for hits including “Cold/Mess” and “Kasoor,” will make his feature film acting debut in “ Drowning ” (“Doobna” in Hindi/Urdu), Marginal MediaWorks has revealed. Directed by Dar Gai and shot on location in New Delhi, the film marks Marginal’s first fiction feature produced in South Asia, in partnership with Los Angeles-based label D36 and Mumbai-based Jugaad Motion Pictures. Related Stories Becoming Tate McRae: The Pop Sensation on Navigating Fame, Treating Work Like ‘a Fantasy’ and Getting Taylor Swift’s ‘Amazing’ Sourdough Bread Disney's Next Big Thing: Malachi Barton on 'Camp Rock 3,' Doomscrolling on TikTok and Not Hiding His Faith in God Kuhad plays Tarush, an indie musician in Delhi who lands one breakout hit and then can’t escape the grip of a criminal record label boss. Marginal founder and CEO Sanjay M. Sharma is producing with the company’s head of film, Milan Chakraborty, D36 co-founder and CEO Abhi Kanakadandila, and Jugaad co-founders Dheer Momaya and Gai, from a story the group developed jointly. Popular on Variety “The film is like if the Safdie brothers mixed John Carney’s ‘Once’ and Lars von Trier’s ‘Dancer in the Dark’ in the blender that is the contemporary music scene in Delhi,” Sharma said. For Kuhad, the project grew out of an earlier collaboration with Gai, who directed the video for his song “Cold/Mess.” “Ever since Dar directed the video for ‘Cold/Mess’ I hoped we would find more ways to work together,” Kuhad said. “So when Abhi and Sanjay brought the idea for a film inspired by my song ‘Drown,’ I was immediately intrigued.” Kuhad’s “Cold/Mess” reached No. 1 on Spotify India and was featured on former U.S. President Barack Obama’s year-end playlist; the Gai-directed video was later named Rolling Stone’s Music Video of the Year. His third album, “Full Moon Chamber,” arrived July 10 via Atlantic Records, following a run of sold-out headline tours across North America, Europe, the U.K., Asia and the Middle East. He is repped by CAA and Big Bad Wolf India, with Everyday Rebellion handling worldwide management. Gai’s credits include “Three and a Half,” which streams on Netflix worldwide after a stellar festival run; her second film, “Namdev Bhau: In Search of Silence,” played at Busan, BFI London and Palm Springs. Jugaad’s “Last Film Show” was shortlisted for the international feature Oscar. “With Doobna, I wanted to make a film that feels like life right now: real, funny, tragic, chaotic, and impossible to escape, impossible to press a reset button,” said Gai, a Ukrainian native long based in Mumbai. Kanakadandila, whose D36 roster spans South Asian-descent artists in the U.S., U.K., India and Pakistan, framed the film as a response to a gap he sees in how the region’s music culture reaches screen. “India has a singular relationship between music and cinema, but there’s a fundamental mismatch between the spirit of the contemporary scene and the format of traditional Bollywood,” he said. The film is the anchor of a South Asia-focused push within Marginal’s broader international slate, which also includes projects in Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Thailand, Europe and Canada. “This is a trillion dollar market, two billion people, more English speakers than the United States itself, and the fastest growing, digitally connected, and largest youth population in the world,” Sharma said. “Just as we’ve seen Korean culture, food, fashion, music and cinema resonate around the world, a similar wave is coming from South Asia.” Marginal has produced more than a dozen features in just over five years, including Tribeca 2025 Audience Award runner-up “The Rose: Come Back to Me,” Tribeca Jury Prize winner “Cypher,” and the recently released horror title “Camp.” Hudson Williams Confronts Autograph Hounds Who Followed Him Home in Viral Video: ‘Please F—ing Leave’ Future Debuts at No. 1 With ‘The Real Me,’ as Rolling Stones and ‘Heated Rivalry’ Soundtrack Also Bow in Top 10 ‘Heated Rivalry’ Funko Pops Are Here: Shop the New Shane and Ilya Collectibles Ahead of Season 2 ‘Thunder Point’ Heats Up as Fremantle, Bell Media and ‘Sullivan’s Crossing’ Showrunner Bring Robyn Carr’s Next Series to the Global Market: ‘It’s “Friday Night Lights” Meets “Virgin River”’ (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Heated Rivalry’ Success Sparks New Publishing House From Gay Adult Entertainment Giant Falcon | NakedSword (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Heated Rivalry,’ ‘Industry,’ ‘Widow’s Bay’ Lead 2026 TCA Awards Nominations Loading comments... Shooting on the ten-part show will take place on Prince Edward Island and in Toronto, with Canadian producer Sphere Media attached. The creator-showrunners are Dane Clark ( Suze , One More Time ), and Linsey Stewart ( Workin’ Moms , North of North ). Logline on the series is as follows: “ This Summer Will Be Different , based on the beloved novel by Carley Fortune, is a simmering, sun-soaked romance set across multiple summers on Prince Edward Island about Lucy, a young woman navigating her 20s and her first real love with her best friend’s brother, the one person she was never supposed to fall for.” Related Stories Legal Producer Adds Defamation Claim To Lawsuit Against Netflix Over Theft Of Hard Drive Of World War II Espionage Pic 'Fortitude' News Idaho College Murders Doc Series Grabs Attention On Netflix; 'Ransom Canyon' Season 2 Off To Slow Start Exec producers are Clark, Stewart, Fortune and Jennifer Kawaja and Elise Cousineau for Sphere, the maker of Netflix limited series Wayward . Watch on Deadline “When Carley first entrusted us with her captivating book, we knew we had to find the right team to deliver to her passionate fanbase,” said Danielle Woodrow and Tara Woodbury, Netflix’s Directors, Content in Canada in a statement. “Developing this project with Dane, Linsey and Sphere has been a dream and we couldn’t have found better partners to bring this love letter to both Toronto and Prince Edward Island to the screen.” Fortune added: “I fell in love with Prince Edward Island first in the pages of L.M. Montgomery’s Anne of Green Gables and again when I visited with my best friend in my early twenties. I’m thrilled to bring this sweeping love story to the screen with Netflix and to transport audiences to the glittering shores and windswept beaches of PEI.” Netflix has been steadily upping its number of Canadian originals, which the streamer has linked to domestic viewing in Canada increasing 20% in 2025. articles.title: second corporate shift
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie The Summer 50-Something Female Friendships Took Over Streaming With ‘Five Star Weekend’ & ‘Ride Or Die’s Surprise Success Disney Closes $1.2 Billion Deal To Sell A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst Viola Davis Stars In ‘Ascent’ Thriller Series Ordered By Paramount+ From John Logan View All March 16, 2026 1:45pm (L-R) Dana Walden and Debra OConnell Disney/ABC Dana Walden , incoming President and Chief Creative Officer of The Walt Disney Company as of Wednesday, has revealed the new leadership structure of Disney Entertainment. She laid out the changes Monday in a memo, which you can read below. In addition to television, which she oversaw; film, which she took over in her new role; and direct-to-consumer, which she co-ran with Disney’s film chief Alan Bergman , Walden’s purview now will include Games and Digital Entertainment, previously under incoming Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro, which will become part of Disney Entertainment, with Sean Shoptaw now reporting to Walden. Related Stories Executives Debra OConnell Sets Direct Reports, Including Craig Erwich Who Adds 20th Television Oversight Executives Disney Names Josh D’Amaro CEO, Dana Walden President & Chief Creative Officer Bergman and Shoptaw are members of Walden’s new leadership team of direct reports that also includes Debra OConnell , John Landgraf , Joe Earley and Adam Smith . Watch on Deadline There had been questions whether Bergman would stay on as Chairman of Disney Entertainment, Studios, under Walden. He will, as the two are said to be getting along great, and he also will continue to share oversight of Direct To Consumer (Disney+ and Hulu) with her. RELATE: Disney’s Josh D’Amaro On “Surreal” Moment He Was Asked To Be CEO; Incoming Chief Bonds With Dana Walden, Bob Iger At Town Hall With Walden expanding her turf as Disney President and CCO, there also had been a lot of speculation whether she would elevate one of her senior executives on the TV side to streamline the operation and reduce the number of her direct reports. She has, and that is OConnell, previously President, ABC News Group & Disney Entertainment Networks, who has been named to the newly created role of chairman of Disney Entertainment Television . OConnell now will be in charge of the television brands, including ABC Entertainment, Disney Branded Television, Hulu Originals, National Geographic Content and creative for 20th Television and 20th Television Animation, in addition to her current duties overseeing ABC News and the ABC Owned Television Stations. Her promotion only slightly impacts Landgraf, who remains Chairman of FX and will continue reporting directly to Walden and maintain oversight of Onyx Collective. He no will longer oversee Nat Geo, a brand that joined his portfolio in 2023. The network over the last couple of years pulled out of original scripted programming, Landgraf and his team’s top area of expertise. There will be a change for Eric Schrier , President of Disney Television Studios, who will report to Earley, having previously reported to Walden. DTC President Earley now will serve as Co-President of the division with Smith as both report to Walden. Earley heads content strategy for DTC, which explains Schrier’s alignment with him. Schrier serves as Head of Global Original Television Strategy, overseeing the development and production of international shows for Disney+, which is expected to be his priority going forward.

articles.title: Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘This Summer Will Be Different’ TV Adaptation So Far
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘This Summer Will Be Different’ TV Adaptation So Far ‘Wizards Beyond Waverly Place’ Season 3 Release Guide: How Do The Episodes Roll Out? ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Come Out? View All August 4, 2026 5:54pm L-R: Sophie Nélisse as Lucy Ashby, Roby Attal as Felix Clark, Francesca Reale as Bridget Clark for the start of production of 'This Summer Will Be Different' Amanda Matlovich/Netflix Another Carley Fortune book adaptation will soon be making a splash onto the small screen. Netflix ’s television adaptation of Fortune’s This Summer Will Be Different has found its main cast after receiving the greenlight in March of this year . The project continues in the current of success of Prime Video’s Every Year After , based on Fortune’s debut novel Every Summer After , which recently received a Season 2 renewal at Prime Video’s inaugural Obsessed Fest. Related Stories Books ‘Every Summer After’ Author Carley Fortune Details Involvement In Prime Video Adaptation: From Casting Sue To Future Of Her Literary Barry’s Bay Books 10 Major ‘Every Year After’ Book Changes From Carley Fortune’s Novel ‘Every Summer After’ For everything we know about the This Summer Will Be Different show heading to Netflix, read on. Watch on Deadline When will Netflix’s This Summer Will Be Different come out? There is no release date yet, as the show is in early stages of production. Has This Summer Will be Different started production yet? Yes, Netflix and author Carley Fortune revealed that the series has started production on Prince Edward Island, home of Anne of Green Gables . Who is in the cast of Netflix’s This Summer Will Be Different ? Deadline broke the news of the main trio’s casting, led by Sophie Nélisse ( Heated Rivalry , The Book Thief , Yellowjackets ) as Lucy Ashby. Next came the announcement of Roby Attal ( The Sex Lives of College Girls, The Haunting of Bly Manor )and Francesca Reale’s ( Stranger Things , Do Revenge ) casting as Clark siblings, Felix “Wolf” and Bridget . When Netflix unveiled the start of production, they also revealed that six actors had been added to round out the cast in recurring roles: Jordan Rodrigues as “Miles Lam,” Jude Wilson as “Zach”, Natalie Brown as “Christine”, James Tupper as “Ken”, Tom Barnett as “Peter” and Celia Owen as “Joy”. What is This Summer Will Be Different about? First published in 2024, Fortune’s third novel follows Lucy Ashby (Nélisse) as she drops everything at her florist job to come to the aid of her best friend Bridget (Reale), who gets cold feet about her upcoming wedding. The problem is, Lucy has a history with Bridget’s brother Felix (Attal) after a one night stand the night they met on PEI years ago. Bridget has three rules for Lucy’s trips to PEI, and the third is that Lucy not fall in love with Felix. Lucy and Bridget have been best friends since they began living together after college. Netflix’s logline calls the adaptation “a simmering, sun-soaked romance set across multiple summers on Prince Edward Island about Lucy, a young woman navigating her 20s and her first real love with her best friend’s brother, the one person she was never supposed to fall for.” Who else is behind Netflix’s This Summer Will Be Different ? Dane Clark ( Suze , One More Time ) and Linsey Stewart ( Workin’ Moms , North of North ) serve as creators and showrunners as well as executive producers. Author Carley Fortune will also executive produce alongside Jennifer Kawaja ( Sort Of, Wayward ), Elise Cousineau ( Cardinal , Small Achievable Goals ) and Sam Levine ( Small Achievable Goals , The Z Suite ) for Sphere Media. Directors are Karen Maine ( Yes, God, Yes , Nobody Wants This ), Jasmin Mozaffari ( Ginny & Georgia , Firecrackers ), Fab Filippo ( Sort Of , Save Me ). Does Carley Fortune have other book adaptations in development? Yes, Fortune’s One Golden Summer , which serves as a sequel of sorts to Every Summer After , will provide source material for Season 2 of Prime Video’s Every Year After . Her second novel, Meet Me At The Lake is in development with Netflix and Archewell Productions.

articles.title: Samantha Morton On Why She “Hasn’t Worked For A Year” Since ‘The Odyssey’ & Why She Was “Sad” & “Hurt” After Getting “Fired” From ‘Her’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando ‘The Odyssey’ Extends Run At Alex Theatre After Becoming Highest-Grossing 70MM Exhibitor Who Had Not Screened A New Movie In 35 Years Samantha Morton On Why She “Hasn’t Worked For A Year” Since ‘The Odyssey’ & Why She Was “Sad” & “Hurt” After Getting “Fired” From ‘Her’ Ariana Grande Says Upcoming Break Was “Not A Reactive Or Impulsive Thing” & Something Planned Although “Boundaries, They Need To Be Set” View All August 4, 2026 7:01pm Samantha Morton Roy Rochlin / Getty Images Samantha Morton is opening up about not working after filming Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey . In a new interview, Morton revealed she had been out of work for a year following her role of Circe, a witch and goddess on the island of Aeaea, in the epic film. “I haven’t worked for a year since making The Odyssey ,” Morton said on the Happy Sad Confused podcast, noting that she has “really good agents and a manager.” She continued, “But at the end of the day, I’m 49. I do believe I’m a good actor, [but] there are other good actors out there. Do you know what I mean? So, the politics of the industry has changed massively.” Related Stories News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' With $360M Is Now Biggest Opening Ever At Domestic Box Office - Monday AM Update News Universal Becomes First Studio To Conquer $4B+ At Global B.O. YTD As 'Odyssey' Heads For $1B WW Morton also revealed what it was like to be cut from Spike Jonze’s Her , the role that ultimately went to Scarlett Johansson. She’s incredibly evocative.” The 2013 film revolved around Theodor Twombly, played by Joaquin Phoenix, who develops a relationship with the voice assistant. Morton read Samantha’s lines on set with Phoenix, but they were replaced with Johansson’s voice in post-production. Morton recalls she was “sad,” adding, “It does hurt when you’re fired from something or before it. I don’t know. What I’d have wished for was another chance in a booth to do an American accent. In April, Deadline reported she would star in the rescue thriller Love and War , which is set to be directed by Lisa Mulcahy, who will also co-write the script alongside Elisabeth Gooch. Furthermore, Morton is also set to star in Amazon’s crime thriller, Dirty , alongside Phoebe Dynevor. The series follows trainee Detective Eva Bennett, played by Dynevor, who returns to Manchester and joins a new homicide investigation run by her fearsome estranged mother – the legendary Detective Chief Inspector Lois Mercer, played by Morton. As they navigate their complicated relationship and long-buried truths resurface, Eva starts to uncover Lois’ crimes, forcing an impossible choice between justice and blood. articles.title: Big-Bucks-Generating Disney Consumer Products Unit Shifts To Studio Umbrella
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Tom Tapp , Dominic Patten August 4, 2026 8:02pm In Disney ‘s second corporate shift to the entertainment tent in six months — and just before CEO Josh D’Amaro leads its Q3 earnings report tomorrow morning — the company unveiled plans to to move its revenue-rich Consumer Products division. The shift seeks to create “cohesion across the entire Disney ecosystem and extending the relevance of our franchises for generations,” according to a joint memo today from Thomas Mazloum, chairman, Disney Experiences and Alan Bergman , chairman, Disney Entertainment Studios. To that end, Disney Consumer Products will travel from the Experiences division to Disney Entertainment — specifically under the company’s Studios umbrella. Related Stories Executives Dana Walden Unveils Her Disney Entertainment Leadership Team Spanning Film, TV, Streaming & Games; Debra OConnell Upped To DET Chairman News Disney Closes $1.2 Billion Deal To Sell A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst “Disney Consumer Products will shift the majority of its businesses to Disney Entertainment, sitting within the Studios, beginning October 2026,” the C-Suite duo wrote. “This evolution reflects how these businesses operate today and strengthens that model by more directly linking our consumer products businesses with the creative and business teams behind the content.” The duo said the reorg was a “work in progress.” Watch on Deadline Essentially putting the people who create Disney’s IP in the same room as the people who create products based on that IP, the synergy may not be sexy, but it sure as Hell is a very big deal — if for the sheer size and cash involved if nothing else. DCP-licensed products did $63 billion in retail sales in 2025. With about two months to go before it all is locked in, details are scant about who the internal merger of sorts will work. We do know that Lisa Baldzicki, who was named DCP prez in the spring, will continue in her role. Baldzicki succeeded Tasia Filippatos as the latter became President of Disney Parks International just after D’Amaro became CEO in March. On a practical level, today’s DCP announcement looks to be the rare case of a corporate meld where the amount likely redundancies — read: layoffs — is minimal. Today’s move marks the second time this year a division that used to sit under now CEO D’Amaro in his former Disney Experiences capacity has shifted to Disney Entertainment. Sean Shoptaw, EVP, Games and Digital Entertainment’ and his entire’s division moved over in March . Of the new partnership between DCP and the company’s content creators, Mazloum and Bergman observed, “At its best, this work happens when storytelling, commerce and experiences come together from the very beginning, creating cohesion across the entire Disney ecosystem and extending the relevance of our franchises for generations.” Disney Consumer Products is the world’s top licensor. DCP, today’s memo notes, is “outperforming its nearest competitor by nearly three to one.” The rest of the top five is made up of Authentic Brands Group ($36 billion), People Inc.($27 billion) NBCUniversal ($20 billion), and Hasbro ($17.5 billion). L.A.’s historic Alex Theatre will continue to exhibit the fantasy epic through August 20, 2026, following audience demand. The Odyssey was the first-run movie at the theater since Terminator 2: Judgment Day in 1991 — 35 years ago. The theater recently underwent systems upgrades, including the installation of 70mm film projectors, which welcomed audiences to the special engagement of The Odyssey on July 17. “We’re incredibly grateful to the people of Los Angeles and to film lovers from across Southern California for making our presentation of The Odyssey in 70mm such an extraordinary success,” said Miles Williams, Artistic Director of the Alex Theatre. “The response from audiences has been overwhelming and a wonderful reminder of how much people still value the shared experience of seeing a great film together.” Williams continued, “I’d also like to thank Universal Pictures for recognizing the important role historic theatres continue to play in Hollywood’s cinematic legacy and for partnering with the ALEX to be part of this landmark release. We’re honored to have been part of bringing this film to audiences, and we look forward to welcoming them back for many more unforgettable movies.” Watch on Deadline Nolan’s The Odyssey is close to crossing the $1 billion mark in the global box office, sitting at $911 million after three weekends. The filmmaker shot the entire film in Imax 70mm, which made moviegoers seek the large screens to experience the movie how Nolan intended. articles.title: Gregg Sulkin Says “It Took Three Seconds” To Return To Mason Greyback For ‘Wizards Beyond Waverly Place’ Finale: “All I Had To Do Was Look At Selena”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Katie Campione Katie Campione Senior TV & Labor Reporter @katie_campione More Stories By Katherine Idaho College Murders Doc Series Grabs Attention On Netflix; ‘Ransom Canyon’ Season 2 Off To Slow Start Jewish Film Institute Reveals 2026 Grant Recipients & San Francisco Jewish Film Festival Award Winners ‘Stranger Things,’ ‘Bluey’ & ‘The Pitt’ Dominate Streaming TV In H1 2026; Peacock Rates High With Unscripted Originals View All August 4, 2026 11:03pm Wizards Beyond Waverly Place Disney SPOILER ALERT! This post contains details from the final season of Wizards Beyond Waverly Place . Gregg Sulkin can rest easy knowing there’s a universe out there where Alex Russo and Mason Greyback are still together. “I mean, I think, in my heart, Alex and Mason are always endgame,” he recently told Deadline after a brief role reprisal as the fan-favorite werewolf and Alex’s former flame for the Wizards Beyond Waverly Place conclusion. “So, storyline wise, I think it’s more in the heart than on the page, and I think all the fans around the world will resonate with that,” he added. “But, of course, delighted to be back on the show. Delighted to work with Selena again. It’s very special to be on back on set in my first American home.” Related Stories News 'Wizards Beyond Waverly Place' Season 3 Release Guide: How Do The Episodes Roll Out? News 'The Devil Wears Prada 2' Achieves Biggest Live-Action Movie Premiere On Disney+ & Hulu Since 'Deadpool & Wolverine' Sulkin makes a delightful, if limited, appearance in the second of four episodes alongside former co-stars Selena Gomez and Jennifer Stone, also known as Alex’s human best friend Harper Finkle. Watch on Deadline As viewers know by now, Wizards Beyond follows Alex’s daughter Billie (Janice LeAnn Brown), whom she shares with former dark wizard Damian Penwulf. But that’s in the real world. In this world, Alex is still living with Harper and is dating Mason, who Harper believes is about to stop by with plans to propose. But, when he gets there, he reveals something else. Mason can’t propose, because he’s dead. Through Mason’s revelations, we learn that Alex has been in some sort of limbo state after throwing herself through a dimensional rift to save her family at the end of Season 2. He and Harper are there only to guide her back to her family. “I felt like there was only one person who was going to do that, and thankfully, they chose Mason,” he said. “I think Mason has always been Alex’s rock.” It’s been more than a decade since the Wizards of Waverly Place finale, and still Sulkin supposes “it took three seconds” to slip back into character. “All I had to do was look at Selena, and it was like, ‘Okay, cool, we’re back,'” he said. “I think, when you have such a special bond with people on a professional and personal level, it’s very easy to slip back into it.” Wizards Beyond has brought back many of the characters from the original Disney Channel series, which ran from 2007 to 2012, so it has always begged the question of whether these important characters would return in some capacity. While Alex and Mason were dating at the end of Wizards of Waverly Place , the continuation establishes early on that Alex has married someone else. Wizards Beyond follows Alex daughter Billie (Janice LeAnn Brown), who she shares with her husband and former dark wizard Damien Penwulf. In large part, the series follows Billie as she unwittingly works to help make her family whole again. Whatever the canon may be, Sulkin remained open to returning throughout Wizard Beyond ‘s short three-season run and had an inkling that the writers would find a way to eventually make sense of a return for Mason. “It was just a matter of fitting in the perfect slot for my character to come back, whilst also giving space for the new show to breathe, whilst also paying respect to my character, [and] Selena and I’s characters’ relationships,” he continued. He hoped the stars might align. “And thankfully, they did.” It’s certainly a brutal end for a beloved original character, but luckily in this universe death doesn’t feel quite so permanent. “I think the amazing about wizards, and when you’re dealing with magic, is that anything can happen,” Sulkin reassured audiences, adding “this was a a chance to say goodbye for now.” He says he’ll “never say never” to future opportunities for Mason’s return, should the franchise spawn again. “The show gave me so much, so I feel like it would be very inconsiderate of me to not want to return the favor to the fans and also the channel for believing in me.” Judge Sets WBD Merger Trial For March; Streaming Fuels Mixed Q2 ‘Brand New Day’ 2nd Fastest To $1B WW; Record U.S. Monday With $47M Female Friends In Their 50s Drive Summer Success Of ‘Five Star Weekend’ & ‘Ride Or Die’ Numan Acar Joins Pic As Kevin J. articles.title: Jason Sudeikis Sets Up ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4: “It’s Getting Back To Doing What He Loves”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Rebecca Rittenhouse Cast In Hulu’s Cable Guy Pilot ‘Colin From Accounts’ Sets Premiere Date For Third & Final Season Mary Holland Joins DC’s Jimmy Olsen ‘Superman’ Spinoff Series View All August 5, 2026 12:00am SPOILER ALERT: The following reveals major plot points from Apple TV ‘s Ted Lasso Season 4 premiere. It’s been more than three years since we caught up with Ted Lasso ( Jason Sudeikis ) and all his fabulous friends and loved ones back in Season 3. Following a hiatus, the Apple TV series Ted Lasso is back, and it’s like he was never gone. Well, almost. When we reconnect with Ted in Episode 1, he’s back in his hometown of Kansas City, after leaving his life in London behind to be closer to his son Henry (Grant Feely). Ted is now working at Fowch’s Fine Foods, a local grocery store, ringing people up at the register. Related Stories News 'Ted Lasso' Season 4 Release Schedule: When Do New Episodes Come Out? News Juliette Lewis On If 'Cape Fear's Crystal Or Max Is "More Psychopathic," Martin Scorsese's Lasting Support & Season 2 Hopes: "We Will See" Unbeknownst to him, three people from his past are coping with the heat outside his house: Rebecca (Hannah Waddingham), Leslie ( Jeremy Swift ), and Keeley (Juno Temple). When Ted sees them, he opens his front door and does a leap into the air (photo below), sharing his joy over their reunion. Famished, Ted takes the trio to a local BBQ spot where they pig out and catch up on what they’ve been up to. Amid the small talk and Rebecca spilling BBQ sauce all over her delicates, she reveals the real reason they are there: she wants Ted to coach their new women’s team. Ted is a little surprised but not really, and a little unsure of how to respond to her generous offer. Jason Sudeikis as Ted Lasso in Apple TV’s ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 After catching Henry’s soccer match, Rebecca, Leslie, and Keeley head back to the U.K. without Ted, who declined the coaching job offer. However, all hope is not lost. When he gets home, he looks at all his mementos from the Richmond days and reminisces about those moments amongst friends. Taking a shot in the dark, he texts his ex Michelle (Andrea Anders), who is with Henry, and both agree to join Ted for a new adventure in England. Ted is chuffed to bits at the prospect. “When we first meet him, he’s really just dad-ing it up. He’s taken a part-time job, and he clearly didn’t blow the money he made while being the head coach of a Premier League team for three seasons. He’s hiding out a little bit, and slowly puts the pieces together of a different way to go about this familiar situation from the inside out,” shared Sudeikis with Deadline, which can be seen in the video above. He added, “So then it’s getting back to doing what he loves, which he was depriving himself of for one reason or another. That’s open to interpretation. I have my theories.” Even though Ted is going back to coaching, this will be his first time training women. The team, which viewers will officially meet next week in Episode 2, consists of Boots (Jude Mack), the cheeky twin sisters Niamh (Aisling Sharkey) and Siobhan (Rex Hayes), Margy (Mercedes Assad), and her girlfriend Mady (Annelise Heywood). There will also be a few other new faces that will be introduced in Episode 3. Before Ted arrives in England, the ladies will have been trained by Assistant Coach Alice Chilton (Tanya Reynolds), a lovely and devoted leader who lacks self-confidence. Jeremy Swift, Hannah Waddingham, Juno Temple and Jason Sudeikis partake of the BBQ in Kansas City Of the new experience of working so closely with the women on the team, Sudeikis remarked, “Coaching women for the first time in his life… arguably, he has a complicated relationship with women. He’s certainly not practiced in mentoring and coaching. It’s similar to being a fairly new father of a young girl; you don’t necessarily know what to do, what you can do, what you’re allowed, what’s appropriate…” Sudeikis later added, “Because I was once a boy and I’ve, at this point in this journey, not been a girl, I’m guessing a lot of times. Girls are very good at making you wonder while you’re guessing, which I appreciate at this point in my life. I think Ted, for a guy who lives in the questions, is getting answers from areas he never expected.” Earlier in the episode titled “Home,” while still in Kansas City (Missouri or Kansas, you decide), Leslie took a break from the group to visit the American Jazz Museum. Unfortunately, it was closed for a private event. Lucky for him, there was another option right next door: the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum. The gentleman selling the tickets convinced Leslie to consider his second choice. Not really being into baseball, Leslie was hesitant, but he went in anyway. He learned a lot about some of the greatest Black players of all time, with a large focus on Satchel Paige. Swift commented on the scene, “It’s an unexpected journey because he wants to go to the jazz museum, and it’s a little lesson for him about struggle in sport and overcoming it. Big shout out to Milan Carter, who I did the scenes with, who is just a really beautiful actor, fantastic. I loved working with him. Also, a big shout out to Declan Lowney, who directed that first episode. He’s been on the show since the beginning, and he’s a superb director. A lot of fun to work with.” For anyone planning to visit Kansas City, both the American Jazz Museum and the Negro Leagues Baseball Museum are real institutions that can be visited. Next week, Ted crosses the pond. articles.title: Locarno Film Festival Head Giona A. Nazzaro Talks Mission To Liberate Spectators In The Age Of The Algorithm As 79th Edition Kicks Off
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Scores Biggest All-Time Middle East Opening Weekend Amid Stunts & Drone Shows Toronto Unveils Wavelengths & TIFF Classics Lineups With Films By Angela Schanelec, Radu Jude, Denis Côté & Lisandro Alonso TIFF Centrepiece To Showcase 54 Features With Kamila Andini’s ‘Four Seasons In Java’ & Avi Nesher’s ‘Our Loves’ Among World Premieres View All August 5, 2026 12:57am L-R: Isabella Rossellini, Giona Nazzaro, Zoe Saldaña and James Gray Getty Images/Michael Buckner/Deadline The Locarno Film Festival opens today with the world premiere of French directorial duo Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh’s The Green Eyes in front of 8,000 spectators on the lakeside town’s Piazza Grande. The opening ceremony will also see Isabella Rossellini feted with the festival’s Excellence Award, with further honorees across the festival including Darren Aronofsky, Virginie Efira, James Gray, Asia Argento, Rick Baker, Zoe Saldaña and producer Sigurjón “Joni” Sighvatsson. Other star guests include Olivia Wilde with her $40M box office breakout The Invite ; Monica Bellucci in the role of the aristocratic mother of a troubled teenager in Giovanni Tortorici’s Luca Guadagnino produced drama Ketticè and Claes Bang in post-WW2 intrigue I Is Another , all of which play on the Piazza Grande. Related Stories News 'Bruton:' Biopic About Man Who Briefly Escaped Prison During 10 Year Sentence Lands Sales Rep Ahead Of Locarno Debut News James Gray To Receive Locarno's Honorary Career Pardo Award With the issue of migration into Europe hitting the headlines this past week after tens of thousands of people attempted to cross without permission from Morocco into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, The Green Eyes is a timely opening film. Watch on Deadline Set in the Landes in southwestern France, it follows 11-year-old Chaya whose brother goes into a mysterious deep sleep when their family is served with deportation papers. The drama takes its cue from so-called resignation syndrome, a state first observed in Sweden in the 1990s among the children of asylum seekers, which researchers suggested was sparked by trauma and a sense of powerlessness. “The opening film is crucial. It’s like the opening beat of a concert,” says Locarno Film Festival Artistic Director Giona A Nazzaro. “We wanted to share with the audience in Locarno that we’re fully aware of what’s going on in the world, but at the same time that we think we can tackle what’s going on through the tools of cinema, storytelling, imagination and fantasy,” he continues. The Piazza Grande lineup traditionally showcases more accessible fare while independent world cinema competes for the Golden Leopard in the International Competition and edgier works by mainly but not only emerging directors are showcased in the Cineastes of the Present sidebar. Nazzaro says he is not keen on making a distinction between “so-called public films” and “cinema for the highbrow few”. “The real challenge today is to create a possibility where different forms of cinematic art can coexist with the same rights and dignity in the same public space of festival,” he says, adding his dream is to liberate spectators from preconceived viewing choices,” he explains. “It’s a kind of dream to regain cinema as a freedom that can’t be predicted through algorithms or consumer habits… my aim is not to shape the program within the expectations of how cinema should be consumed today but rather create a space where cinema can be experienced as a discontinuation, or an interruption… welcome to Locarno, where your algorithm does not work anymore,” he continues. Nazzaro says the diversity of the Locarno program builds on his work at Venice Critics’ Week, which he headed from 2016 to 2020. “We aimed to welcome new filmmakers in Venice like Helena Wittman ( Drift ), Bertrand Mandico ( The Wild Boys ), Anna Eriksson ( M ), who were completely out of the box back in the day, and now have become, luckily, more established names,” he explains. “What we try to say with a curated diversity is that obviously we have a limited number of slots, but we try to pick differences not only in subjects and stories, but also in the approach to the cinematic form.” He gives artist Beatrice Gibson’s first feature At Night in the Cineastes of the Present, following six women traversing Paris after dark, as an example of a film ticking these boxes. “It’s an outstanding film that tackles issues of identity and power representation, even in contexts and circumstances where you think we have moved on… it is extremely eloquent in the way it points to some of the very crucial crossing points of our contemporary conversations about where we are right now,” he explains. Nazzaro highlights recent Cineastes of the Present success stories such as Sophy Romvari’s Blue Heron , which won Locarno’s First Feature Award, and then played in Toronto’s Centrepiece sidebar, clinching the Best Canadian Discovery Award, and the well-travelled Golden Leopard winner Sweetheart by Margherita Spampinato. “Our DNA has always been about discovering new filmmakers, new talents, new possibilities for cinema. Locarno is one of the places where you can really dive into the possibilities for the art form today,” he says. Under Nazzaro’s watch, Locarno has also welcomed pictures like Sony Pictures’ action-comedy Bullet Train starring Brad Pitt, but in a trend seen across the European festival circuit this year studio pictures are absent at this edition. He suggests it is a sign of the times. “I’m a huge fan of North American cinema and what Hollywood used to stand for. I’m not oblivious to the changes, the industrial, financial, and structural transformation that the whole studio system is going through. I’m not even sure if there is still something like a studio system, not in the sense or way that we used to know it,” he says. “That said, the collective intelligence of the Hollywood system is very much alive and expresses itself through unique artists such as Tom Cruise, and we’re also seeing how the system can work for an auteur like Chris Nolan and The Odyssey .” “It’s always very risky to say definitively what is going on with the studios, because the strength of that system, whatever that system has become, is that it has in its DNA the capacity, the possibility, the opportunity to contradict itself at all times. Just a couple of weeks ago, we were all discussing Backrooms , which I think is extremely brilliant, and Obsession ,” he continues, noting Locarno feted the latter’s executive producer Jason Blum with its Raimondo Rezzonico Award in 2022. The U.S. is represented this year selection by Gray’s Paper Tige r and Wilde’s The Invite on the Piazza Grande as well as Greek American director Erin Vassilopoulos’s New Jersey and New York City-set drama Destroy All Girls in Cineastes of the Present. Restored versions of David Lynch’s Wild at Heart , Kevin Costner’s Dances With Wolves and Martin Scorsese’s Taxi Driver will also play on the Piazza Grande. This year’s retrospective entitled ‘Red & Black – Hollywood Left and the Blacklist’ explores the filmmakers and films who fell victim to McCarthyism. Restored by Zurich-based laboratory Cinegrell in collaboration with the Locarno Film Festival, the new 4K version of Dances of Wolves i ncorporates 30 minutes of previously unseen footage extending its duration to just under four hours. Nazzaro suggests that while Costner’s revisionist Western epic may seem naïve today, it still represents an antidote to current U.S. politics. “It’s like saying, ‘Ok, the hippies in Laurel Canyon were completely naive and stoned out of their heads most of the time but then came the 80s, and I’d rather go with the hippies than with the yuppies. You know what I’m saying?” he explains. Currently tied up with the next instalments of Horizon – An American Saga , Costner is not scheduled to attend, but Nazzaro hopes the late night screening will be a cinephile event nonetheless, with at least a handful of spectators staying to the end in the small hours of the morning “We’re aware of the time but the aim is to create an experience from which people might say, ‘I was there’. We’re not expecting 8,000 people to be there waiting for the sun to come up with the end credits but that’s the idea,” he says. He recalls attending a screening of the 216-minute version of Michael Cimino’s Heaven’s Gate with the director in attendance in Venice in 2012. “The director of the festival in Venice at the time [Alberto Barbera] had this very late night screening and was saying, “Guys, you have to see this film because the film will not be existing anymore. So, it was packed,” recounts. “This is different. We’re bringing something back to life. The idea of going with that kind of film through the night with that kind of length is to say something very simple: you can win whatever night it is we are living through with the light of cinema.” Judge Sets WBD Merger Trial For March; Streaming Fuels Mixed Q2 ‘Brand New Day’ 2nd Fastest To $1B WW; Record U.S. Monday With $47M Female Friends In Their 50s Drive Summer Success Of ‘Five Star Weekend’ & ‘Ride Or Die’ Numan Acar Joins Pic As Kevin J.
