articles.title: Walt Disney Company & TikTok Ink Global Short-Form Content-Sharing Deal
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony Walt Disney Company & TikTok Ink Global Short-Form Content-Sharing Deal TriCoast Worldwide & Vitagraph Set Fall Release For Malcolm McDowell & James Paxton Western ‘Last Train To Fortune’ Brittany Snow Joins Lionsgate’s ‘The Housemaid’s Secret’ View All August 5, 2026 3:00am Disney The Walt Disney Company and TikTok today announced a global deal that will allow social media content creators and fans to access and use memorable scenes from Disney movies and shows. The new pact, which will pilot in the US in the coming months with other markets to follow, will bring a collection of curated Disney-centric fan-created content from TikTok to the Disney+ app. At launch, short-form videos from participating creators who opt-in to the program will live on both TikTok and Disney+ verticals. The shorts will feature characters and stories from Disney’s brands including Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, FX and more. Related Stories News Big-Bucks-Generating Disney Consumer Products Unit Shifts To Studio Umbrella News Disney Closes $1.2 Billion Deal To Sell A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst TikTok will offer their creators access to assets from Disney’s vast library. The TikTok videos will be refreshed regularly to engage Disney+ subscribers, so as to stimulate fan conversations, communities, and engagement. The TikTok deal with the Mouse House comes on the morning of Disney’s Q3 earnings call, and in the wake of news last night that the media conglomerate was moving its Disney Consumer Products unit from the Experiences division to Disney Entertainment which is under the Studios umbrella. Watch on Deadline “The best storytellers are fans first,” said Asad Ayaz, Walt Disney Company Chief Marketing and Brand Officer in a statement. “That has always been true at Disney, and today, fans are celebrating our stories in entirely new ways. This collaboration creates a new bridge between the stories we tell and the creativity they inspire, giving creators a bigger stage to share what they’ve made, and audiences more to discover on Disney+ every day.” “Creators are at the heart of everything we do at TikTok. Their creativity extends the life of films and shows into conversations that fans discover and share,” said Dawn Yang, TikTok’s Global Head of Entertainment. “Together with Disney, we’re bringing the authentic creator expression of the TikTok community to Disney+, inviting audiences to experience the shared creativity that makes fandom so powerful.” Through the jointly-run Disney Creator Ambassador Program, Disney and TikTok will enable top-notch creators to unlock special rewards and provide them with increased profiles, access to exclusive events and career development pathways. It’s a means for Disney to build relationships with the next generation of creative talent. According to internal TikTok data, fans shared an average of 6.5 million film and TV-related posts on the social media portal daily last year. Additionally, nearly half of surveyed viewers said they went on to watch a movie or TV show on a streaming service or television after discovering entertainment content on TikTok. In December 2025, Disney planned a $1 billion investment in OpenAI and a three-year licensing deal to let fans generate short videos using over 200 Disney, Pixar, Marvel, and Star Wars characters on Sora. The big-bucks investment looked to reset the IP battle between artificial intelligence and Hollywood by permitting iconic characters from Frozen , Star Wars and the Marvel multiverse to be used on the generative AI video app, Sora. However, in March, OpenAI pulled the plug on Sora. articles.title: Edinburgh Television Festival Advisory Chair Adam Hawkins Urges Industry To “Embrace Change” In Confab’s Final Year In Scotland
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse ‘The Artful Dodger’ Renewed For Final Season At Hulu & Disney+ Nimrat Kaur, Roshan Mathew & Pavan Malhotra Star In ‘Job Trafficking’, Prime Video Series About Industrialized Online Scams Fremantle Hires Katie O’Connell Marsh As Global Scripted Chief View All August 5, 2026 3:00am Adam Hawkins is the advisory chair for the final Edinburgh Television Festival Getty, Netflix “If this Edinburgh is all about embracing change and embracing the future, then maybe we should do the same with the festival.” That’s the verdict from Adam Hawkins , the advisory chair of the final ever Edinburgh Television Festival , which is held later this month in Scotland’s capital. In an interview with Deadline, the Netflix UK Director of Documentary Series urged the industry to keep an open mind about the future of the festival, which is in 2027 transferring to Greater Manchester in England after 51 years in Edinburgh. The UK television industry, which gathers annually for the event to talk shop and frequent the local ale houses, remains very divided between those who think moving the venue away from Edinburgh is a disaster given the number of agents, producers and creatives in town for the Fringe Festival in August, and those who say the costs have simply become too high to remain a diary date for many – especially those climbing the ladder. Watch on Deadline Related Stories Books Everything We Know About Netflix's 'This Summer Will Be Different' TV Adaptation So Far Legal Producer Adds Defamation Claim To Lawsuit Against Netflix Over Theft Of Hard Drive Of World War II Espionage Pic 'Fortitude' Basic hotel rooms cost an average minimum of $300 per night, with pricier options nearing $700 during the month, but many producers have come for years and see Edinburgh as a crucial moment to take the temperature of their buyers and counterparts. “I’ve always loved going to Edinburgh,” says Hawkins, who worked for the likes of The Tinder Swindler producer Raw before joining Netflix in 2022. “It’s a great buzzy place at this time of year, but Manchester is also an incredibly vibrant city and I think the buzz will probably be the same.” Hawkins – who saw Jeremy Paxman deliver the annual James MacTaggart Lecture in 2007 during his first visit to the event – is known for greenlighting the likes of Victoria Beckham , Robbie Williams and the upcoming Being Gordon Ramsay at Netflix, and worked on the streamer’s first daily World Cup soccer show, Gary Lineker ’s The Rest is Football over the summer. Hawins concurs with Deadline’s read that the corridors of Edinburgh International Conference Centre provide a unique flavor of the local business. “It feels like you’re in the middle of the British TV industry, like an amazing chance for a snapshot,” he says. “Even though I’m the advisory chair this year, I’m hopeful I’ll get the chance to just wander around, as I do think that there is a moment of taking the temperature and seeing everyone together. That’s the magic, isn’t it?” We were speaking prior to my International TV Co-Editor, Max Goldbart, breaking the news that it might not be curtains after all for Edinburgh. Screen Scotland, the body that represents the interests of the Scottish film and TV industry, commissioned a piece of work earlier this year examining what a new fest might look like. Interestingly, Rowan Woods, the former creative boss of the Edinburgh TV Fest, is leading on the work as an indie consultant. It’s a sign that at least some of the local industry disagrees with the TV Foundation’s decision to move the event and of a desire to keep tradition going. A veteran of the UK biz, Hawkins says no other local or international TV event generates the same “electricity in the air” as Edinburgh and adds that if Manchester can recreate that atmosphere, “Then the [new festival] will be a roaring success.” Final edition highlights Michaela Coel delivered the annual MacTaggart lecture in 2018 So what exactly is Manchester going to follow? For starters, YouTube’s VP of EMEA, Pedro Pina, will be stepping onto the same plinth the likes of Paxman, James Murdoch, Michaela Coel and Mark Thompson have done before. His MacTaggart Lecture, which is considered a bellwether for the state of the industry, will likely talk about YouTube’s increasingly important role in British broadcasting – earlier this year it passed the BBC in monthly audience reach for the first time. The shift towards creators, most of whom rely on YouTube as their platform – will also be a hit topic, especially as many remain concerned how that is upending traditional production. Hawkins says the booking is reflective of the changing shape of the biz – one that has been inundated with consolidation such as the Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery saga, disruption from AI and new money-making models. “Being part of the festival is solidifying that they are are television,” he says. “They’re not something else, they’re not outsiders and they’re not the newcomers. They are very much part of the furniture now and it is important TV industry sees that, and it’s important they play their part in that. They’re calling themselves television. We must treat them like that.” Hawkins’ employer, Netflix, has faced the same questions of intention. His response is that “none” of the Netflix commissioning team in the UK is American. “We are knitted into the fabric here, and we spend huge amounts of money,” he adds. “Us being a part of it and me leading on it is reaffirming we are part of the British landscape.” Netflix can, of course, point to the fact that it discovered the Richard Gadd play on which hit series Baby Reindeer was based, during an August in Edinburgh. “We are firmly rooted here, and we are passionate defenders of the British TV industry as well,” says Hawkins. Richard Gadd first performed ‘Baby Reindeer’ in Edinburgh Bar Apple TV, every major broadcaster and streaming spending in the UK will feature across ten Spotlight Sessions, including YouTube for the first time. One recurring criticism with the format is that they can be used a promo sessions rather than substantive content, but Hawkins refutes this, saying media outlets’ hunt for headlines is at odds with what they are actually achieving. “Edgier talking points are not interesting to most TV producers,” he argues. “They just want to know how to sell their next show and how to be successful. I’m hopeful people will leave those sessions with a clearer understanding.” There will also be off record, peer-to-peer sessions to give delegates face time with major commissions, as part of Hawkins’ determination to give producers more access to decision makers. Also notable is the first public appearance of BBC Director General Matt Brittin, a former Google boss who replaced Tim Davie earlier this year. “He has only just got his feet under the table,” says Hawkins. “I am sure he will hit the ground running, so he might have some interesting announcements, but it will be kind of like Pedro in a way – he’s at the ‘getting to know you’ stage. He is an interesting choice as somewhat an outsider to the BBC, and people want to know what he is all about, and what his priorities are. I’m glad he chose the festival.” Before that, BBC journalist Ros Atkins will return for a third year in a row to open the festival on Tuesday, August 25, with his trademark fast-paced, data-driven assertions of issues facing he industry. Further journalism heavyweights Cathy Newman, Susanna Reid and Clive Myrie will discuss truth in an age of misinformation, while Hawkins will introduce broadcaster Amol Rajan for his Alternative MacTaggart. Hawkins will also be on stage interviewing former footballer, broadcaster and Goalhanger co-founder Gary Lineker about the “third act of his career” – quietly building a media empire after spending six weeks with him in Times Square during the World Cup recording the Rest is Football podcast. YouTuber, podcaster and BAFTA presenter Amelia Dimoldenberg – “a TV star who is naturally part of the new generation” – will also be in conversation to discuss on her career and Gary Oldman will receive a Global Icon Award and look back on six seasons of Apple TV cop drama Slow Horses . SNL Masterclass ‘Saturday Night Live UK’ One of the more well-attended sessions will undoubtedly be the SNL UK Masterclass , which will bring together the on-screen performers, producers and Sky commissioning executives behind the show. Initially met with consternation and scorn upon its announcement by a skeptical industry, the remake of the famed NBC sketch show’s first season was broadly considered a success by its ending earlier this year. A second, expanded season has been ordered and Sky is hoping it will become part of the British industry fabric, with many of Season 1’s clippable segments doing the rounds on social media each week after broadcast. Jack Shep, whose portrayal of a smouldering Princess Diana was arguably the viral moment of the first run, will appear on stage alongside the likes of fellow performer Ania Magliano, writer Daran “Jonno” Johnson, lead producer James Longman and Sky unscripted commissioning chief Phil Edgar-Jones. “Even though it is a decades-old heritage brand, it works because of the clips,” says Hawkins. “In some ways, it is clip-first, program-second. It is as much about the new wave of television as anything else. I’m really excited about that.” Amid the excitement around announcements, Hawkins – who is working alongside Edinburgh TV Festival Managing Director Campbell Glennie and new Head of Editorial Niall Flanagan on the event this year – knows there will never have been such apprehension heading into an August in Scotland. Not only is the future south of the border, but the industry is facing unprecedented disruption and a continuing financial problem. “Things are changing, and I don’t think they will go back,” he says. “Some people want to turn the clocks back ten years, but I’m hopeful there will be excitement and that people are up for the challenge. We have the best TV industry in the world, in my opinion, and we can meet the moment. The only way to be right now is up for the challenge, and while there will be nerves in the industry, I’m hopeful this is a nervous excitement. As for how the future in Manchester shakes out, Hawkins – who did not play a role in the selection process – provides an honest assessment. Could, Deadline asks, the foundation that runs the TV Festival look back on this decision in five years and consider it a mistake? “Hard to know,” replies Hawkins. “I have no idea, and the proof will be in the pudding. Honestly, knowing how hard they work on it and how much they care, I’m sure it will be a success.” Hawkins is embracing the change, the question is if the industry embraces it with him. articles.title: Eli Roth Admits ‘Ice Cream Man’ Features Generative AI After He “Mispoke” About Using The Technology
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake ‘The Artful Dodger’ Renewed For Final Season At Hulu & Disney+ ‘Baywatch’ Reboot Beaches At Amazon Prime Video Across Europe, India & Canada The Show Will Go On Without Ariana Grande: ‘Sunday In The Park With George’ Producers Plan For Musical Without ‘Wicked’ Star View All August 5, 2026 3:11am ‘Ice Cream Man’ Valerie Flores/The Horror Section Ice Cream Man features a scoop of AI. That’s the revelation from horror director Eli Roth after he admitted to adopting the technology in a “few scenes” of the slasher film, despite initially saying that animated sequences were brought to life traditionally. In an interview on Monday, the Hostel helmer was asked if he used artificial intelligence in Ice Cream Man scenes featuring a Fleischer Studios-style animation that entrances kids and transforms them into killers. “I have an animation background and I drew it,” Roth initially told website Polygon. “I worked with an animation team and I wanted it to look and feel like — there’s an old Mickey Mouse cartoon where he goes to a haunted house and there’s brooms and dancing skeletons and this kind of flowing dancing stuff and the jittery style of the animation. So I drew the loop cycles and the styles. Then I had some animators help kind of make it a little more fluid, and I worked with an artist to give it a bit of an old-timey jittery feel. But I sat there and I drew out the frames that I wanted.” Related Stories News 'Ice Cream Man' Review: Eli Roth Blends 'Home Alone' And 'Hostel' For Over-The-Top Unrated Bloodfest News 'Ice Cream Man' Review: Eli Roth Blends 'Home Alone' And 'Hostel' In Over The Top Unrated Bloodfest In Search Of A Story It was later revealed that Ice Cream Man ‘s credits included a mention of Dark Half, an AI visual effects company. Confronted with this, Roth issued a statement to Polygon clarifying his original remarks in the interview. Watch on Deadline “I misspoke. AI was used in a very small portion of a few scenes in the film,” he said. “It was an opportunity where technology and creativity came together to help bring my vision for the film to life.” Roth was not specific about whether his clarification referred to the animated sequences in Ice Cream Man . Deadline has contacted his rep for comment. Ice Cream Man opens on August 7. articles.title: Disney Earnings Buoyed By ‘Toy Story 5’, Theme Parks, Streaming Profit; Books $100M Tariff Refund
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jill Goldsmith , Dade Hayes August 5, 2026 4:05am Toy Story 5 Disney Disney ’s Josh D’Amaro stepped out with solid numbers and some news in his first full quarter as CEO. Toy Story 5 drove studio revenue, theme parks saw an uptick in attendance, and streaming profits more than doubled for the three months ended in June. Total operating income for Disney’s fiscal third quarter jumped 21% $5.6 billion, beating Wall Street forecasts, as did adjusted EPS (of $2.06 a share, up from $1.61). Revenue of $25.2 billion rose 7% from the year earlier. The fiscal Q3 numbers follow confirmation of Disney’s planned sale of its 50% interest in A+E Global Media to an affiliate of co-owner Hearst for $1.2 billion in cash. The media giant is moving its consumer products business under Studios from the lucrative division’s longtime home in Experiences. And it unveiled a global, short form content sharing partnership with TikTok this morning. Related Stories News David Ellison Says Paramount Is "Absolutely Open" To Settling WBD Antitrust Suit, But "We Will Win At Trial" News Disney Closes $1.2 Billion Deal To Sell A+E Global Media Stake To Hearst The quarterly numbers and full-year outlook “reinforce our confidence that we are uniquely well positioned,” said D’Amaro, who took the reins from Bob Iger in March. “Decades of IP investment have built deep fan connections that translate into strong financial results. Our accelerating global guests growth at Experiences, Toy Story 5 ‘s theatrical and consumer products success, and strong ESPN viewership gains all helped expand our consumer reach this quarter.” Watch on Deadline He’ll be hosting a call with analysts at 8:30 am ET. Disney’s three sprawling divisions are led by Entertainment, which posted profit of $1.7 billion, up 64%, on revenue of $11.3 billion. The company cited the June 19 theatrical release of Toy Story 5 , which has surpassed $1 billion in global box office, as well as The Devil Wears Prada 2. Disney acknowledged that Star Wars: The Mandalorian and Grogu and live action Moana (in fiscal 4Q) underperformed at the box office but noted their other contributions to the flywheel like a new Mandalorian-themed Millennium Falcon: Smuggler’s Run at Disneyland and Walt Disney World , and retail sales. “We expect the live-action Moana to be a strong title on Disney+ , building on the success of the original film … and extending the reach of the franchise, which now includes three films, a themed area at EPCOT, and a robust global merchandise business.” Disney doesn’t furnish streaming subscriber numbers anymore but said SVOD operating income more than doubled to $712 million from $329 million on revenue of $5.5 billion, up 11%. Subscriptions fees rose 15% (9% from more subscribers, 3% from higher rates and 1% from a favorable foreign exchange impact). Advertising nosed up 3% (impressions were higher, rates lower). Disney also sounded a bit like Netflix as it talked up an emerging international programming slate with Rivals Season 2 on Disney+ in the U.K. and Ireland, The Perfect Crown in Korea and Dear Killer Nannies in Latin America. The company plans to triple the number of Disney+ local original series over the next three years. “Our ambition is for Disney+ to become the digital centerpiece of the Walt Disney Company,” D’Amaro’s letter said. “We aim to evolve Disney+ into a comprehensive membership ecosystem. By integrating high-value, always-on benefits with our storytelling, we can reach more fans, deepen engagement, and increase subscriber retention. These product enhancements will also allow us to further segment the market, increasing our addressable opportunity over time. We expect to begin introducing elements of this vision in Spring 2027.” Disney+ Q3 churn declined worldwide and Disney said it passed an important milestone in “app unification” allowing Hulu standalone and bundle subscribers to link profiles, watch history, and manage subscriptions on Disney+. At Experiences, profit rose 20% to over $3 billion on almost $10 billion in revenue. Global guests grew 4% and attendance at domestic parks rose 3%. WDW saw healthy core attendance increases from domestic tourists and annual passholders.Forward bookings remain robust. That should reassure investors who were spooked by softer attendance at Universal’s domestic parks when Comcast reported earnings last month. Theme parks average per capita ticket revenue rose 5%. Disney noted continued, but moderating, headwinds from international attendance at domestic parks. It cited strong attendance growth at Disneyland Paris following the opening of World of Frozen. Overall, it anticipates a quarter of global guest growth in the current fiscal Q4 despite consumer softness in Asia. Q3 was the first full quarter with Disney’s two newest cruise ships, the Disney Destiny and Disney Adventure. Disney said it recorded approximately $100 million in a tariff refund for the quarter, reversing out tariff payments earlier in the fiscal year. Apple last week reported a $2.19 billion tariff refund for the June quarter. Sports, led by juggernaut ESPN, saw profit of $853 million, down 17% on higher programming and production costs, on $4.5 billion in revenue. Disney cited contractual rate increases, costs for new sports rights and an impact from the timing of rights costs recognition as a result of the NBA contract renewal. Contributing to the lower-than-expected operating income were four-game sweeps in early rounds of the NBA playoffs and the impact of a network carriage dispute. Disney was likely referring here to the resolution terms of a fight with YouTube TV in late 2025. After unlocking a selection of ESPN content on Disney+ domestically in 2024 and expanding it globally since then, the letter said, the company plans to deliver a more robust subset of games for Disney+ subscribers beginning this fall anchored by additional college football simulcasts. The service will also continue simulcasting college football pregame show College GameDay . articles.title: ‘Ice Cream Man’ Review: Eli Roth’s Small-Town Horror Flick Is for Diehard Slasher Fans, and Absolutely No One Else
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All August 3, 2026 8:00pm Ari Millen in 'Ice Cream Man.' Valerie Flores/The Horror Section If you’re looking up the credits for Ice Cream Man on IMDB, you might as well skip past director/co-screenwriter Eli Roth and the extensive cast list. Because the real stars of this ultra-gonzo horror film are the folks in the makeup department, especially prosthetics designers Steve Newburn and Adrien Morot (the latter an Oscar winner for his work on The Whale ). Sure, Roth came up with the story and co-wrote the screenplay. But his efforts would have been for naught if you didn’t fully believe the sights of young children dismembering their parents’ bodies or playing games of tetherball and tag with human heads. Not to mention the tug of war using human intestines. Related Stories Business 'Terrifier' Actress Had Deal for 1 Percent of Profits. A Court Will Decide If That's for One Movie -- Or the Whole Series Movies 'Hershey' Biopic Trailer: Finn Wittrock, Alexandra Daddario Struggle to Make Affordable Chocolate If all of that sounds like a euphoric cinematic experience, then this the film for you. It’s certainly the film for its auteur, who conceived the idea more than two decades ago and has been trying to make it ever since. Since the major studios passed on his idea about a townful of kids turned into crazed, murderous zombies, Roth formed his own company, The Horror Section, to distribute his labor of love. Not surprisingly, the film is being released unrated. Ice Cream Man The Bottom Line Catnip for gorehounds. Release date : Friday, August 7 Cast : Ari Millen, Benjamin Byron Davis, Eli Roth, Karen Cliche, Dylan Hawco, Sarah Abbott, Shiloh O’Reilly, Kiori Mirza Waldman, Charlie Zeltzer, Charlie Storey Director : Eli Roth Screenwriters : Eli Roth, Noah Benson 1 hour 26 minutes The film doesn’t feature a particularly complicated scenario. The strange-looking driver of a weirdly decorated ice cream truck driving through the sort of idyllic American small town painted by Norman Rockwell distributes his frozen wares to the local children, and they promptly turn into homicidal little creatures staring blankly into space and sporting severely discolored lips. They go after their adult prey with such demonic enthusiasm it makes you wonder why George Romero never thought of the idea, a sort of “Bugsy Malone of the Living Dead.” One hopes Roth has gotten his worst instincts out with this effort, which, considering that it comes from the maker of such films as Cabin Fever , Hostel and Thanksgiving , is saying something. The silent, perpetually smiling ice cream truck vendor, played chillingly by Canadian actor Ari Millen ( Orphan Black ), is certainly a creepy figure who could give Art the Clown in the Terrifier movies a run for his money. Except that the Ice Cream Man is less a psycho killer than an evil enabler, one whose frozen treats turn otherwise normal children into pint-sized killing machines displaying remarkable ingenuity in their methods of slaughter. The Ice Cream Man does pitch in at times, including serving a teacher’s scooped-out brains to him in a cone. The little darlings, who include a girl who walks around the neighborhood holding her mother’s severed head like a trophy, display the usual playfulness of summer campers. They also seek to swell their ranks by force-feeding the ice cream to any fellow children who haven’t yet been infected. Their carnage — exemplified in a lengthy, virtuosic sequence in which they attack the adult teachers and employees at their grade school with frenzied abandon — includes the sort of gruesome playground activities involving severed body parts that makes one hope the child actors had recourse to on-set psychiatric counseling. There’s a backstory of sorts, told by a local priest (Benjamin Byron Davis) and involving a travesty of justice followed by revenge facilitated by a necromancer. But it almost seems unnecessary, since the film’s true raison d’etre is demonstrating the amazing talents of its prosthetics designers, who have created such a relentless series of horrific bodily images that it’s easy to imagine blood-crazed audiences applauding them like musical numbers. The reliance on practical effects rather than the CGI employed by so many current horror films at least proves refreshing. The visuals are also packed with throwaway jokes, including one drive-by decapitation that should be accompanied by a rim shot, and deadpan visual flourishes like a crow pecking out the eyes of a corpse in the foreground of a shot. There have been plenty of horror movies involving murderous children over the years, such as Village of the Damned and its sequel and, of course, Children of the Corn . But Roth doesn’t hide his desire to outdo them all with this effort that can only be described as sick and twisted. And I’m sure he’ll take that as a compliment. Full credits Production: The Horror Section, MCT Studios Distributor: The Horror Section Cast: Ari Millen, Benjamin Byron Davis, Eli Roth, Karen Cliche, Dylan Hawco, Sarah Abbott, Shiloh O’Reilly, Kiori Mirza Waldman, Charlie Zeltzer, Charlie Storey Director: Eli Roth Screenwriters: Eli Roth, Noah Benson Producers: Eli Roth, Kate Harrison Karman, Christopher Woodrow, Raj B. Singh Executive producers: Jon Schnaars, Holly Adams, Kevin Frakes, Nasir Jones, Peter Bittenbender, Matt Maclellan, Andre Coutu, Connor Digregorio, Eli Massillon, Lorenzo Antonucci, Ash Avildsen, Phil Hunt, Compton Ross, Jeremy Ross, Geneva Wasserman, Feng Ren, David Edwards Director of photography: Simon Shohet Production designer: Peter Mihaichuk Editor: Matt Lyon Composers: Brandon Roberts, Snoop Dogg Costume designer: Jenifur Jarvis Casting: Stephanie Gorin 1 hour 26 minutes THR

articles.title: Ariana Grande Wants to “Clear the Air” About Upcoming Break From Public Eye: “Not a Reactive or Impulsive Thing”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 3, 2026 8:42pm Ariana Grande at the 2026 Golden Globes. Christopher Polk/2026GG/Penske Media via Getty Images Ariana Grande is offering some clarifications for her fans after it was revealed on Sunday that she will be “taking a step back from visibility” after her Eternal Sunshine Tour wraps. The singer-actress took a moment during her concert on Monday night at the United Center in Chicago to “clear the air about a few things.” “Sometimes when a story comes out that’s not directly from me, things can get a little blown out of proportion, so I just wanted to speak to my fans directly tonight because I love you so much,” Grande began, via videos shared on social media. “The announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing. It was something that I have decided. A plan that I had quietly made a long time ago. It was a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place. And I want you to know that many things can be true at the same time.” Related Stories Music Atarashii Gakko! on Their New Album 'From Tokyo With Love' and Their Global Evolution Music St. Vincent Wraps Orchestra-Backed Tour With Cinematic Hollywood Bowl Show “I heard that my fans were worried that negativity was ruining things for me, but I just have to say that could not be more the far opposite. This is not what that is. And I just want to be very, very clear, multiple things can be true at the same time: boundaries need to be set, human beings can need a break sometimes and also, this can be and will continue to be the greatest experience of my professional and creative life,” she continued, drawing loud cheers from the audience. “No matter what noises exist out there, nothing will ever be able to distort my reality or be real to me or louder to me than this love that we share, or even how it feels to make art with the people that I love and respect.” “This is what I will always take with me and carry with me, because the rest of that shit is not mine to carry so I don’t carry it. And I wanted you to hear that from me. I needed to get out here and differentiate that from my truth for all of you because I love you and this tour has been the most healing, beautiful, corrective, magnificent, special experience of my life,” Grande concluded. @chris HER PUTTING HER PHONE IN HER BOOT AT THE END ☠️ we love uuuu @arianagrande #arianagrande #eternalsunshinetour ♬ original sound – Chris Olsen The Wicked star’s new comments came a day after The Hollywood Reporter learned that she will be stepping back from the public eye after her tour concludes on Sept. 1, following her 10-show residency in London. “She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” a statement shared with THR read. “This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.” THR also learned that Grande dropped out of the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park With George , which is set to open next summer. The “petal” singer has had a busy few years , between starring in Wicked: For Good and Wicked , the latter of which earned her an Oscar nomination for her role as Glinda. She’s also released two albums over the last two years, including 2024’s Eternal Sunshine and Petal , which dropped last month . Grande next stars in Focker-in-Law , hitting theaters on Nov. 25. THR

articles.title: Cabo Verde Looks Beyond the World Cup, Ivory Coast Gets Animated, Zimbabwe Has Ambition: A Chat With Locarno Open Doors Film Producers
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 4, 2026 12:01am Locarno Open Doors Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors Open Doors , the Locarno Film Festival ‘s co-production platform and talent development program for filmmakers from equity-seeking communities and regions where artistic expression is at risk, is ready for its 2026 edition . It is its second that is putting a spotlight on African cinema . The Open Doors Producers program supports producers in their efforts to build sustainable careers and cross-border networks, bringing to the Swiss city six participants. They are Tapiwa Chipfupa of Ambidextrous Pictures in Zimbabwe, an EAVE alumn who recently launched the international training and mentorship program Audiovisual Entrepreneurs Laboratory (AVEL); Adja Mariam Mahre Soro from the Ivory Coast, or Côte d’Ivoire, who leads Studio Kä, an animation studio she founded in Abidjan; Natasha Craveiro from Cabo Verde, whose company Korikaxoru Films produced Omi Nobu , which featured in the Open Doors Screenings at Locarno 2025; veteran Mamounata Nikiema of Pilumpiku Production in Burkina Faso; Nigerian producer David Ikeata of Vox Cinematic Films; and Rua Osman from Sudan, whose Helomur Picture has been behind such festival favorites as Goodbye Julia (Cannes, 2023). Related Stories TV Disney+ Sets Release Date for Season 2 of Hit Thriller Series 'Made in Korea' Music Phil Collins Reveals He Nearly Died During 2024 Hospitalization After Years of Alcohol Abuse Yanis Gaye, a French-Senegalese creative producer, co-founder of the boutique production houses Goree Cinema in Senegal and Strange Fruit Production House in France, also co-founded Yetu (Un)Limited, a multi-venture African film studio. At Locarno, he serves as head of studies at Open Doors. And he connected THR with some of the producers attending this year’s edition. “It’s interesting because you see a lot of territories represented that you would think have a lot of challenges in terms of infrastructure and local industry itself,” he explained about the Open Door 2026 participants. “But this is where you actually see the resilience and the most innovative models. Because you have to be bold in a way that allows you not just to produce content, but also to shape your own ecosystem.” Continued Gaye: “The nature or the profile of the African producer is much closer to an entrepreneur and social entrepreneur. … It’s about working on multiple things at the same time, so usually those producers and their companies tackle many verticals at the same time.” Running Aug. 5-10, the Open Doors program offers hands-on training, mentoring and networking, along with public screenings and events during the Locarno Film Festival and its industry arm Locarno Pro . Before they all dive into a busy week in Switzerland, THR talked to Soro from the Ivory Coast, Zimbabwe’s Chipfupa and Craveiro from Cabo Verde about what projects they are currently working on and what they expect from the Open Doors experience in Locarno. What’s your hope for the Open Doors experience? NATASHA CRAVEIRO I am really, really happy that I will get this opportunity to be in Locarno to meet people, to be in this program that is so very well designed, and they are so attentive to our needs. My expectation is to meet people with whom we can collaborate and who get to know Cape Verde from another point of view that is not the football [FIFA World Cup] point of view. Not that it’s not a good opportunity. People still have the name [of our country] in their heads. It’s a good opportunity to say, yes, we have football, but we do have cinema too. TAPIWA CHIPFUPA Like Natasha, I am extremely excited. The online program has been really awesome for me already. It has been curated for me or around me. So, I already have so much that I’ve learned. I’ve gotten to know the other producers a little bit, so I’m really excited to actually see them face-to-face and to have more discussions. The program they’ve outlined to us for Locarno looks so exciting. I feel that if we apply ourselves, we’ll be able to develop it into something so much bigger. So, I’m feeling really privileged. Tapiwa Chipfupa of Ambidextrous Pictures in Zimbabwe Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors ADJA MARIAM MAHRE SORO I’m also very happy to be part of this program and to be selected. We do animation, which is not necessarily the kind of work and projects for which they used to have producers in Open Doors. I was curious to see how our reality can fit with the program, and online, it was already very, very interesting. So I look [forwward to] Locarno and will just follow the flow, meet new people, make good experiences and enjoy the moments. Are you bringing specific projects to Locarno? SORO I am coming with a young adult animated series. That is not something that we used to have coming from Africa for a global audience, with taekwondo and murder and many things in it. So I’m curious to see how the the producers at Locarno who focus more on feature films see this kind of opportunity. CRAVEIRO I’m also coming with projects, two hybrid features. And I am looking, of course, for financing, for co-producers. Both are talking a lot about our reality in Cape Verde. One is more related to environmental protection and the worries we have now that we are seeing tourism exploding. We are getting more worried every day. And of course, we are happy for the World Cup, but it’s an extra worry for us because we know we are not even prepared for the numbers of tourism we have already. The other project is about the post-colonial Cape Verde. It’s a country that doesn’t talk about the colonial traumas. And that is sticking with us generation after generation, 50 years after our independence [in 1975 from Portuguese colonial rule]. Natasha Craveiro of Korikaxoru Films in Cabo Verde Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors CHIPFUPA I’m coming with a supernatural thriller based in a village. It’s about a young girl who defies the patriarchy and tradition to ultimately become the unlikely savior of the village. I am obviously looking for financing partners, people who are interested in developing a short as a proof of concept. But I’m also in the process of trying to contribute to the local ecosystem here in Zimbabwe, as our industry is still really developing. I’ve been developing some initiatives for which I would really love to find people to partner with. The first one is a producers’ lab that is already supported by Berlinale Talents, and I am looking for ways to continue that and keep that alive. And recently, I started an initiative for young women and girl creatives in the film and art sector. Locarno is an opportunity not just to showcase our films, but to look at how else we can help or we can contribute to the development of the continental sector as well. CRAVEIRO We do have these kind of projects too because we are also still struggling to build a healthy ecosystem. We have the Cine Club project because we feel that the audience needs to be educated, and you have to go get them. We have so we have the Cinet Club. Our company also has this academy through which we try to help young people who have an idea to transform it into a project. And we do have this festival that we started last year. So, I’m also looking for partners who are interested and who can help us to take these steps, these baby steps that we need to take. Adja Mariam Mahre Soro of Studio Kä in Ivory Coast Courtesy of Locarno Open Doors SORO In Côte d’Ivoire, until last year, it was a real challenge. There was a real gap between what we know about animation and what our government knew about animation. They had to understand that we need to build an ecosystem to have talents who know how to make animation, we need to have schools, we need to have a real ecosystem. But now they have started to understand it. For example, I have the chance to collaborate with the Ministry of Communication on an animation school pilot for 25 young animators and see how that can be a way to improve our schools that already exist and their curriculum. Last year, we also signed a treaty of co-production with Belgium, and we are also having a conversation with Canada. So there is movement now. We also have an event in November where we invite Japan in Côte d’Ivoire to talk about animation, so there is a real desire to do something in Côte d’Ivoire. THR

articles.title: Alan Ritchson on What He Learned About Fame From Working With Arnold Schwarzenegger
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All August 4, 2026 12:55am Alan Ritchson Kierra Thorn/Getty Images Alan Ritchson took a break from his Reacher duties to star opposite Arnold Schwarzenegger in the upcoming holiday film The Man With the Bag. Directed by Adam Shankman and due to hit Amazon Prime Video on Dec. 2, the family comedy casts Schwarzenegger as Santa Claus who goes on a journey to retrieve his magic bag after its stolen. In order to get it back, he turns to his naughty list on which he finds a former thief, played by Ritchson, who comes along for the expedition. After filming with the action icon, Ritchson said he was the one who left with a valuable gift. “It was a treat,” the Reacher star told Dax Shepard and Monica Padman on a recent episode of Armchair Expert. “He taught me a lot about how gratitude should manifest in the life of somebody dealing with fame.” Related Stories TV Amanda Ip, Jay Baruchel, Ciara Bravo and Kevin Durand to Star Opposite Alan Ritchson in 'Reacher' TV Alan Ritchson Breaks Silence on Motorcycle Fight, Calls it "Scariest" Experience of His Life Ritchson said he’s transitioning to a part of his life and career where he’s aware of “how present fame is and how toxic and intrusive” it can be, not only for him but his wife, Cat, and their young boys. But he was able to watch how Schwarzenegger moved through the world and dealt with his own fans while on set and off, and that helped him shift his perspective. “I worked with Arnold, who deals with this on a degree that I will probably never experience,” he explained. “He’s dealt with it for decades on a degree that I can’t quite understand. He stops for everybody. We would be in the middle of a scene in a diner and people would be banging on the glass because our lockup wasn’t tight enough. They’re like, ‘Oh my God, will you take a picture with us?’ [He says], ‘Oh, be right there. Come outside and take a picture with us.’ He has no problem. He makes time for everybody. And so I look at that and I’m like, ‘Cat, if this is his attitude, I have no excuse.’ … He showed me something really interesting in the way that he approaches life and his lot in life. And I really deeply admire how he treats people.” Schwarzenegger and Ritchson filming a scene for Man with the Bag in New York on Jan. 15, 2025. Jose Perez/Bauer-Griffin/GC Images/Getty Images THR

articles.title: Amazon Picks Up ‘Baywatch’ Reboot Internationally
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All August 4, 2026 2:00am The cast of 'Baywatch' at the 2026 Fox Upfront Ben Hider/FOX. ©2026 FOX Media Amazon Prime Video is hitting the beach. Amazon has snatched up multiple international territories for the upcoming Baywatch reboot , picking up the hot lifeguard adventure series for much of Europe, including France, Germany, Italy, and Spain, as well as for Canada, Latin America and India, among other territories. As part of the deal, Amazon will also license the complete Baywatch back catalogue, including all nine seasons of the original Baywatch, and seasons 9 and 10 of the show, which was rebranded Baywatch Hawaii in the same territories. (Not included, though, are the two seasons of the less-fondly-remembered spin-off series Baywatch Nights .) Related Stories Business Think the Paramount-WBD Mega-Deal Has Nothing to Do With the Locarno Film Festival? Think Again! Movies Cabo Verde Looks Beyond the World Cup, Ivory Coast Gets Animated, Zimbabwe Has Ambition: A Chat With Locarno Open Doors Film Producers The new Baywatch stars Stephen Amell alongside Jessica Belkin, Shay Mitchell, Hassie Harrison, Thaddeus LaGrone, Noah Beck, and Brooks Nader. Matt Nix ( Burn Notice , The Gifted ) serves as showrunner and executive producer alongside executive producers McG, Michael Berk, Greg Bonann, Doug Schwartz, Dante Di Loreto and Mike Horowitz. McG ( Charlie’s Angels ) will direct the series premiere episode. The reboot is billed as a celebration of the original series “re-energized” for a new generation . The original Baywatch , starring David Hasselhoff, was canceled after its first season on NBC, but survived through syndication and became a massive global hit. At its peak, it was the most-watched show in the world, airing in over 200 countries and reaching more than a billion viewers every week. In addition to Anderson, the show launched the careers of actors such as Carmen Electra, Jason Momoa and Yasmine Bleeth. Fremantle and Fox Entertainment are producing the show. The first 12-episode season will debut on Fox in January 2027 and on Prime Video later in the year. Fox Entertainment Global holds all domestic distribution rights. Fremantle is handling all international sales and brokered the Amazon deal. “We’re thrilled to be partnering with Prime Video to bring the new Baywatch to audiences across multiple territories, while also giving fans the opportunity to revisit the original series they know and love,” said Michela Di Mondo, executive vp, distribution, Canada & international at Fremantle, in a statement. “Few shows have made as big a splash or had such lasting cultural impact…This is just the beginning of what we believe will be an exciting new chapter for Baywatch .” THR

articles.title: Think the Paramount-WBD Mega-Deal Has Nothing to Do With the Locarno Film Festival? Think Again!
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 4, 2026 2:00am Locarno Pro 2025 Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival/Ti-Press The planned Paramount Skydance acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD) is sure to make global waves across various parts of the film industry landscape. In fact, it already has, being the topic of debate on film studio lots, at sector players’ headquarters, in social meet-ups across the industry and, yes, also at film festivals, such as the recent Karlovy Vary fest. The 79th edition of the Locarno Film Festival in Switzerland is also ready to take on the big issue of consolidation and its fallout, along with other hot-button sector topics, at its 2026 Locarno Pro industry program . Related Stories TV Disney+ Sets Release Date for Hit Thriller Series 'Made in Korea' Music Vicki Wickham, Influential 'Ready, Steady, Go!' Talent Booker and Producer, Dies at 87 “There are some earthquakes that are shaking up the infrastructure of the global industry,” which plays into this year’s program, Markus Duffner , director of Locarno Pro , tells THR . So, among other themes, he and his team thought: “Let’s see what happens with the merger of Paramount and Warner. Let’s see what happens with everything that AI can do, as groundbreaking technologies will change the industry.” News of the Paramount-WBD earlier this year came up as the team was in the thick of planning this year’s Locarno Pro program. “We don’t have a crystal sphere, but when we were putting together [the plans for Locarno Pro opening session] StepIn, the Paramount merger news came out,” Duffner recalls. “And we said, ‘Wow, what does it mean with all we’re talking about? But in the end, we felt it’s actually coherent with what we were already dealing with.’ So it’s not something brand new. It’s really a symptom of everything we were dealing with and discussing already.” Locarno Pro, which will once again mix educational, business and networking opportunities, runs Aug. 6-11 this year as part of the Locarno festival, which takes place in the Swiss lakeside town Aug. 5-15. “The 2026 edition of StepIn will explore how power structures, human capital, politics, AI and data-driven systems are reshaping the future of independent cinema,” Marcello Paolillo, the StepIn project manager, explains in a brochure. “The first roundtable will focus on the unprecedented pressures that independent cinema is facing today, including the influence of global streaming platforms on creative choices, the increasing use of algorithms, data and AI in decision-making, and the rapid concentration of power through mergers and industry consolidation.” After all, the Swiss festival’s industry strand is all about exploring challenges and how to address them with an eye on the future. “Locarno Pro is the platform which identifies, anticipates, and addresses the challenges faced by the European film industry, through an open space for dialogue on innovation and social impact, and through a concrete investment in the next generation,” Duffner highlights in a preview of this year’s edition on the Locarno Pro website. “Today’s talents are the leaders, producers, and filmmakers who will shape the coming era of film. This is why Locarno Pro is not a market like any other: it is the place where those who believe in cinema as an art form and a driving force for change find the tools to make it possible.” THR

articles.title: Serena Rossi to Receive Venice Fest’s Passion for Film Award
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Scott Roxborough Plus Icon Scott Roxborough Europe Bureau Chief sroxborough Follow Sign Up View All August 4, 2026 2:30am Serena Rossi Courtesy of the Venice Film Festival Italian actress Serena Rossi will receive the Campari Passion for Film Award at the 83rd Venice International Film Festival, organizers unveiled on Tuesday. Rossi will accept the award on Sept. 10 during a ceremony in the Sala Grande at the Palazzo del Cinema, ahead of the out-of-competition premiere of Scherzetto ( Trick ), directed by Mario Martone. Rossi stars in the film alongside Toni Servillo, Lorenzo Perrotta, Leonardo Lidi, Giovanni Ludeno and Gianluca Di Gennaro. In a statement, Rossi said returning to the Lido to receive the honor was “a true honor,” adding that passion and the search for an authentic connection with audiences had guided her career. She said presenting Scherzetto at this year’s festival alongside Martone, Servillo and the cast made the occasion “even more special.” Related Stories Movies Cabo Verde Looks Beyond the World Cup, Ivory Coast Gets Animated, Zimbabwe Has Ambition: A Chat With Locarno Open Doors Film Producers TV Disney+ Sets Release Date for Season 2 of Hit Thriller Series 'Made in Korea' The prize, presented in collaboration with the artistic direction of the Venice Film Festival , recognizes film professionals for their contribution to cinema and their creative work. Previous recipients include editor Bob Murawski, cinematographer Luca Bigazzi, composer Terence Blanchard, production designer Marcus Rowland, costume designer Arianne Phillips, production designers Tonino Zera and Paola Comencini , and director Gus Van Sant. Venice artistic director Alberto Barbera said Rossi had built a career across film, television, music and voice acting, highlighting her work in a range of genres and formats. Rossi first came to prominence on Italian television with roles in series including Il Commissario Montalbano and Adriano Olivetti , before expanding into film with credits including Song ‘e Napule , Ammore e malavita , Lasciami andare and Io sono Mia , in which she portrayed singer Mia Martini. More recently, she has starred in the Rai series Mina Settembre , Netflix’s The Children’s Train and Non abbiamo bisogno di parole , and Disney’s Uonderbois . She also hosted the opening and closing ceremonies of the 78th Venice Film Festival in 2021. The 83rd Venice International Film Festival runs Sept. 2-12. THR

articles.title: Mary Rivera, Ned’s Grandma in ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home,’ Dies at 82
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 4, 2026 2:42am Mary Rivera Sony Pictures Mary Rivera, the Filipina actress who played Ned’s grandma (or lola) in Spider-Man: No Way Home , has died. She was 82. She died April 15 in Honolulu, Hawaii. TMZ reported that Rivera had suffered a stroke before her death. Rivera was born in Iloilo Province, in the Philippines on June 2, 1943. She attended the University of San Agustin in Iloilo City and graduated in 1964 with a degree in education. After college she worked for the radio station Kanlaon Broadcasting System. It it unclear when she moved to U.S., but she lived in Hawaii before her death and had worked as a teacher and was a retired church missionary. Related Stories Music Vicki Wickham, Influential 'Ready, Steady, Go!' Talent Booker and Producer, Dies at 87 TV Scott Hylands, Star of TV's 'Night Heat' on Both Sides of the Border, Dies at 83 A non-professional actor, Rivera won the part of Ned’s lola after sending an audition tape to producers of No Way Home , who had placed an ad on Facebook looking for a Filipina performer aged 50-90. In an interview with the Philippines’ Star FM Baguo , Rivera said that her daughter Angela Kelly had seen the Facebook ad and urged her to audition. Rivera said that she had quoted lines from The Grapes of Wrath in her audition tape. Rivera only appears in one scene in No Way Home , but it has become iconic for various reasons. In the scene Rivera plays Ned’s (Jacob Batalon) grandma, and then Ned and MJ (Zendaya) realize they can use Doctor Strange’s ring to create portals. It is the scene where Andrew Garfield and Tobey Maguire’s versions of Spider-Man appear for the first time in Tom Holland’s dimension, also marking their first appearance in the Marvel Cinematic Universe. The appearance of the actors was famously a big secret before release of the film and fans across the global went wild in cinemas when they make their entrance. The scene was also notable for Filipino representation on screen, featuring two Filipino characters — Batalon is a Filipino-American born in Hawaii — including one who speaks significant parts of her dialogue in Tagalog, a first for a major Hollywood blockbuster. Rivera told Star FM Baguo that there was a “swelling in my heart,” when director Jon Watts told her she could speak in her native tongue to forcefully admonish the Spider-Men for messing up her kitchen. In an interview with Hawaii Public Radio , Rivera’s daughter Angela Kelly spoke about her mother’s role in No Way Home and what it meant to the family. “It’s been an amazing adventure. To us, she’s just my mom. But to the rest of the world, she’s Ned’s Lola,” Kelly said. “It’s humbling really, because never before in cinematic history really has there been a place for the Filipino language and culture. They did a really good job with paying attention to the details of our culture.” Rivera is survived by her husband, Alejandro Rivera; children, Carmela Jones (Jay), Paul Rivera (Leilani), Edwin Rivera, Angela Kelly (Jaime); 11 grandchildren and 4 great grandchildren. THR

Related Stories Movies Cabo Verde Looks Beyond the World Cup, Ivory Coast Gets Animated, Zimbabwe Has Ambition: A Chat With Locarno Open Doors Film Producers TV Disney+ Sets Release Date for Season 2 of Hit Thriller Series 'Made in Korea' Eisenberg returns to the London Film Festival following the premiere of A Real Pain in 2024, which nabbed him an Oscar nomination for best original screenplay. “I am both honored and honoured to be bringing The Debut to the 70th BFI London Film Festival,” joked Eisenberg about the U.S.-U.K. spelling. “What a wonderful thrill to be the closing night gala, and I can’t wait to share the incredible performances by the cast with a London audience.” Kristy Matheson, artistic director of the BFI London Film Festival, added: “We are thrilled to welcome writer-director Jesse Eisenberg back to the LFF to close the 70th edition of the festival with his deliriously funny and heartfelt film, The Debut . The 70th instalment runs from Oct. 7-18. Lionsgate will release The Debut in U.K. cinemas on Jan. 15, 2027. THR

articles.title: Spotify Hits Milestone of 300 Million Premium Subscribers
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 4, 2026 4:15am Photo Illustration by Chris McGrath/Getty Images Audio streaming giant Spotify posted a second-quarter revenue gain and ended June with 300 million paying premium subscribers, up from 293 million as of the end of March and slightly above the forecast 299 million, “reflecting … year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter growth across all regions.” The company described this as “a milestone no audio streaming service has ever reached.” Monthly active users (MAUs) grew to 777 million, slightly below the projected 778 million, from 761 million in the previous quarter. Revenue growth for the quarter accelerated to come in at 14 percent, or 15 percent on a constant currency basis, to get the company to €4.8 billion ($5.5 billion), in line with its forecast. Operating income hit €655 million ($754 million) in the second quarter, exceeding management guidance and up 61 percent from the year-ago period despite a 3 percent increase in operating expenses, “driven by temporary investments in marketing and cloud/AI spend.” Related Stories Music Vicki Wickham, Influential 'Ready, Steady, Go!' Talent Booker and Producer, Dies at 87 Movies 'The Green Eyes,' Inspired by Resignation Syndrome, Opens Locarno With a Story Told From a Refugee Child's Perspective to "Try to Revive Empathy" Profitability has been in the investor spotlight after price increases and cost cuts. Spotify shares dropped more than 4 percent in pre-market trading. “We have a scale that few companies in history have reached, a business that is healthy and compounding, and opportunities only we are positioned to pursue,” said co-CEO Alex Norström. “Spotify lives across your whole day — the commute, the workout, studying, gaming, the dinner table, and sleep. At our scale, that is rare… Our position gives us an opportunity space as wide as our users want it to be.” Added co-CEO Gustav Söderström: “Investor Day described where we believe Spotify is going in the future. This quarter demonstrated that we are already building that future: better engineering, faster shipping, new products and new ways for users to engage. We are still in the very early stages of what is possible and will continue to have a high bar for investments.” He concluded: “Our job remains the same: understand the technology early and deeply, and turn it into something people love. Creating value for our stakeholders.” For the third quarter, Spotify predicted 305 million premium subs and 788 million MAUs, as well as operating income of €​670 million and revenue of €​5 billion. “Our business performed well in the second quarter, led by strength in subscribers and profitability,” Spotify said. “Overall, we view the business as well positioned to deliver improved growth and margins in 2026 as we reinvest to support our long-term potential.” THR

articles.title: Hwang Bo-reum, Lee Geum-yi Among Authors in Busan Story Market’s 2026 Selections
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 12:33am PT Hwang Bo-reum, Lee Geum-yi Among Authors in Busan Story Market’s 2026 Selections By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Dominates U.K. and Ireland Box Office With Massive Launch 41 minutes ago Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago See All Photo by Sasha Don The Busan Story Market (BSM) has unveiled 25 official selections for 2026, including international bestseller Hwang Bo-reum and two-time Hans Christian Andersen Award finalist Lee Geum-yi, drawing on original IP from four Asian countries. BSM is part of the Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the official market of the Busan International Film Festival (BIFF). Among the Korean selections is “My Upstairs Neighbors” by Hwang Bo-reum, the author behind the international bestseller “Welcome to the Hyunam-dong Bookshop,” and “Chasm of Sorrow” by Lee Geum-yi, whose more than 50 published books and international translations have made her one of Korea’s most recognized children’s and young-adult authors. The lineup as a whole comprises 15 titles from Korea and four each from Taiwan and Japan, alongside two from Indonesia. Related Stories 'Matchbox' Trailer: John Cena Stars in Toy Car Action Movie From Apple TV Margot Robbie, Mark Ruffalo, Daisy Ridley, Omar Sy Projects Lead Venice Immersive Lineup Genres and narratives range widely this year, spanning stories that explore universal emotions and relationships, including life and death, family, growth, love and loss, through fresh genre settings, alongside plot-driven works built around hidden agendas and fixations that take unpredictable turns. Popular on Variety BSM operates as a marketplace connecting film and audiovisual adaptations of original IP, drawing from books, webtoons, web novels, video games and other formats, with content platforms and IP holders worldwide. The official selections take part in pitching sessions and one-on-one business meetings aimed at secondary rights deals and adaptation collaborations. For the Korean IP selection, BSM fielded 138 submissions from 83 companies this year, ultimately choosing 15 titles from 13 companies: nine books, two webtoons, two web novels and two stories. Books make up more than half the Korean lineup, though the selections stay broadly balanced across formats and genres. The titles pair crowd-pleasing categories, among them romance, mystery, fantasy and family drama, with less conventional hooks, including parallel worlds, out-of-body experiences and science fiction, touching on themes from generational communication and family bonds to individual lives set against their times. The selection ranges from emotionally driven human dramas to AI-inflected fantasy, genre-blending historical romance, period pieces and hybrid concepts. BSM’s Taiwanese IP selection, conducted annually with the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), yielded four titles from four companies, one apiece drawn from books, webtoons, web novels and comics. Each centers on a high concept distinctive enough to convey its identity in a single line, using fantasy settings not merely for spectacle but to work through emotional terrain that includes bereavement, remorse, early romance, ties between family members and coming of age, positioning the titles for adaptation across film, drama series and other formats. Four Japanese IPs from four companies, one book and three comics, were chosen through the Visual Industry Promotion Organization (VIPO). The selections lean on layered characters and relationships built around secrets and obsessions, with stories shifting in unpredictable directions as hidden truths surface or unlikely individuals form bonds across boundaries. Indonesia’s two selections, both comics from two separate companies, were picked from a shortlist of 10 Indonesian original IPs that had been presented at the 2025 JAFF Content Market, an initiative run by the Jogja-NETPAC Asian Film Festival Market (JAFF Market); the pair emerged after a round of pitches and meetings centered on adapting the properties for film and audiovisual formats. Both took home the JAFF Content Market Award Goes to ACFM 2026, earning them a spot in this year’s BSM lineup. JAFF Content Market has since evolved into JAFF IP Connection for 2026, and one of BSM’s selected Korean IPs will be invited to that program following talks with JAFF Market representatives. The Yogyakarta, Indonesia program runs Nov. 28-30, continuing the two-way exchange of original IP between BSM and JAFF Market. BSM runs alongside APM at ACFM, which takes over Exhibition Center 2 at BEXCO in Busan for four days starting Oct. 10, with the 25 selections set to connect with industry professionals through BSM Pitch & Match sessions and further business meetings exploring IP expansion and adaptation opportunities. ACFM is the official market of BIFF and is held in Busan every October. The 2025 edition, ACFM’s 20th, drew industry professionals from 55 countries – 3,024 of them, alongside 1,222 registered companies – with on-site attendance reaching a record 30,006. The Sales Market tallied 8,438 business meetings, generating an estimated $71.1 million in transactions. The 31st Busan International Film Festival runs Oct. 6-15, with the 21st ACFM held Oct. 10-13. articles.title: Haugesund New Nordic Films Unveils French Focus Including a Case Study on ‘Ibelin,’ From ‘The Imitation Game’ Director Morten Tyldum (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 12:45am PT Haugesund New Nordic Films Unveils French Focus Including a Case Study on ‘Ibelin,’ From ‘The Imitation Game’ Director Morten Tyldum (EXCLUSIVE) French prodco Les Valseurs will pitch two out of four French projects selected for the Nordic Co-Production Market By Annika Pham Plus Icon Annika Pham Latest Erik Poppe’s ‘Beloved’ to Open Haugesund: ‘All Eyes Are on Norway,’ Says Festival Chief Tonje Hardersen 1 day ago DR Sales Closes With WDR/Arte, VRT, NRK in Multi Buyers Pact on Norwegian Wildlife Doc ‘Frost Without Snow and Ice’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 months ago U.K. Heavyweight Doc Player Jane Ray Boards Argentina’s ‘The Nights’ by Ana Bovino Ahead of ECAM Forum (EXCLUSIVE) 2 months ago See All 'All the Softness in the World' Courtesy of Les Valseurs New Nordic Films , the Norwegian International Film Festival’s industry confab in Haugesund, has announced the program for its first ever French Focus, set up to foster partnerships and co-productions between France and the Nordic countries. The event, due to run Aug. 25-28, is organised by New Nordic Films in partnership with the Institut Francais de Norvège, the French Ministry of Europe and Foreign Affairs, France’s National Center for Cinema ( CNC ) and promotional body Unifrance . Related Stories Margot Robbie, Mark Ruffalo, Daisy Ridley, Omar Sy Projects Lead Venice Immersive Lineup 'Matchbox' Trailer: John Cena Stars in Toy Car Action Movie From Apple TV Headlining the French Focus is a pitching session on Aug. 26 at the Nordic Co-Production Market of four French films in development, of which two are produced by pedigreed producer Les Valseurs , a Cannes Un Certain Regard Jury Prize winner this year for “ Elephants in the Fog ” and Un Certain Regard top prize winner in 2025 for “ The Mysterious Gaze of the Flamingo .” Produced by Les Valseurs co-founder Damien Megherdi, “Borderline” is the feature length spin-off of Yves Piat ’s Oscar and César nominated short film “Nefta Football Club,” while “All the Softness in the World” is an ambitious animation project by Turkish artist Ayçe Kartal whose short film “Wicked Girl” was the first animation short to scoop the Grand Prix in Clermont-Ferrand in 2018. Popular on Variety Two other directorial debuts make the cut: the creative documentary “Boutès” by Jeanne Géli and Loïs Szymczak, produced by Womanray’s Marielle Tricoire, co-producer of Jim Jarmusch’s “Father Mother Sister Brother” and “Temporary Lives” by Syrian-Norwegian filmmaker Wessam Hachicho, produced by Respiro Productions (“In the Nguyen Kitchen”). Besides the four-title pitch, the French Focus will include a panel on co-production opportunities between France and the five Nordic countries, and a case study on the anticipated “ Ibelin ” by Norwegian-born Morten Tyldum, mostly famed for the Oscar-winning “The Imitation Game.” The biopic about online gamer Mats Steen – starring Charlie Plummer, Stephen Graham, Toni Collette, and Bill Nighy – is currently in production for France’s Vendôme Pictures, Pathé, and Norway’s Neby-Tyldum AS. “I am incredibly happy that we are finally able to have a French focus in Haugesund,” said Gyda Velvin Myklebust, head of New Nordic Films. “French cinema is well-known internationally for high artistic quality, and we in the Nordic region have also recently made a strong mark internationally,” she added, referring to “Sentimental Value”’s Oscar win for Best International Feature, the first ever for Norway. “France and the Nordics have highly talented and ambitious filmmakers, and we believe our French focus will give wind to a French-Nordic wave of co-productions and creative collaborations between our countries.” For Kjersti Mo , CEO at the Norwegian Film Institute (NFI) the French Focus reflects “a growing recognition that European film depends on stronger international collaboration.” “France has one of Europe’s strongest film cultures and most developed production ecosystems, while the Nordic countries bring distinctive stories, strong creative talent and considerable international experience,” Mo added. “These different strengths are precisely what can make the partnerships valuable,” said the NFI chief, who also underscored that “international collaboration is a central priority” in the institute’s new strategy. Speaking to Variety, Michel Plazanet, CNC director of international affairs, pointed out that “the Nordic countries, which traditionally co-produce extensively among themselves, are now “seeking additional partners, particularly in France, as this opens up numerous opportunities: access to funding (such as “Aide aux Cinémas du Monde,” regional co-production funds, Arte, and SOFICA), distribution advantages (French sales agents have an excellent reputation, and French co-productions gain easier access to the Cannes and Annecy festivals), and better access to the French theatrical market, the largest in Europe, especially for arthouse cinema.” Conversely the Nordics offer clear advantages for French producers, Plazanet said, as the region boasts “robust institutions, substantial and diverse public and private funding, and reliable professionals accustomed to international co-production.” Aide au Cinéma du Monde So far 20 Nordic projects have received backing from the ACM including three Cannes entries from Joachim Trier (“Sentimental Value,” “The Worst Person in the World,” “Louder than Bombs”), and two from Tarik Saleh (“Eagles of the Republic,” Boys from Heaven”). Denmark, Norway, and Sweden are the most active [co-production] countries, but Iceland also performs very well, given its very small population,” Plazanet said. Among the French Focus attendees, Julie Billy, founder of Paris-based June Films, was just granted ACM support for the Icelandic project in production “A Favour” by Grímur Hákonarson (“Rams”), and is developing a project with Norway’s Eye Eye Pictures (“Fjord,” “Sentimental Value”). “The French Focus comes at exactly the right moment,” said the producer, also interested in creators – notably from the Sámi community, “whose perspectives are unique and increasingly important on the international scene.” “I would love to see Norway as a minority co-producer in more French productions, and of course the other way around,” added Eye Eye Pictures co-founder Andrea Berendsen Ottmar who also hopes the French Focus will “inspire, so that we can help each other to think outside the box in terms of how we structure and finance our projects. Independent producers all over Europe need to stand together and support each other, and forums like this are very valuable in that sense,” she observed. As noted by Plazanet, the French Focus plays within a series of French/Nordic industry events, multiplied in the last two years, that peaked in 2025 with the Visions Nordiques Festival in Paris. Next on the CNC’s top agenda is “an institutional alignment on key European issues, notably the transposition of the AVMS Directive and platform obligations.” The Norwegian International Film festival, running Aug. 22-28, will platform eight French films in its section French Touch. Drilling down on the four French projects lined-up for the Nordic Co-Production Market “Bordeline” (“Sur la ligne,” Yves Piat) Produced by Daniel Megherbi, Les Valseurs Feature debut from the director of the 2020 Oscar-nominated short film “Neftah Football Club who has sketched out ideas from his short, together with writer Alaa Eddine Aljem (“The Unknown Saint”). The story turns Hishem, on a customs officer on the Algerian-Tunisian border, who encounters Tesla, a donkey lost in the desert with headphones over his ears, with a bag of cocaine on his back. Producer Megherbi who co-produced with the Nordics Nepalese pic “Elephants in the Fog,” a Cannes’ Jury Prize winner, believes “Bordeline”’s deadpan, absurd humor, “somewhere between Elia Suleiman and the Coen brothers,” will resonate well with Nordic partners and the general audience. Public backers on board include the CNC, Région Nouvelle-Aquitaine and ICEC in Spain via Spanish co-producers Sumendi and BTeam Pictures. Filming is pencilled for April-May 2027. “All the Softness in the World” (“Toute la douceur du monde,” Ayçe Kartal) Produced by Damien Megherbi, Les Valseurs Turkish animation filmmaker Ayçe Kartal and Megherbi reunite on the helmer’s feature length debut after his multi-awarded short film “Wicked Girls,” an Annecy Jury Prize) winner. Set in 1950, the story follows the young Levon who has grown up posing as a girl, to be protected from an ancient family vendetta. In his search for his true identity, Levon lands in Paris in the world of Haute Couture where he begins to recover a sense of self through creativity. “I want to explore, through [Levon] an alternative history of fashion, one rooted in survival, not spectacle,” said Kartal in a statement. “At Haugesund, we hope to find a Nordic co-producer who understands what we’re trying to achieve with this project. It’s an ambitious, innovative piece of adult animation, and we want a partner who’s genuinely excited by that,” said Megherbi who’s secured development support from the CNC and Hauts-de-France region. “Boutès” (Jeanne Géli, Loïs Szymczak) Produced by Marieke Tricoire, Womanray A liife-affirming documentary in which forensic pathologist Jeanne Géli turns filmmaker to capture the frailty and beauty of life, as her partner Loic Szymczak, an Olympic diver and visual artist, suddenly fights for his own life, upended by a malignant brain tumor. Together they move towards one act of faith-a performative dive in the heart of Paris. “This film is, above all, a love story. We are making it to transform the reality of illness into poetic material,” said the co-directors. Womanray founder Tricoire, who bridges luxury brands with film and served as co-producer on Jim Jarmusch’s Golden Lion winner “Father, Mother, Sister, Brother,” said she signed up for New Nordic Films when she found out that the founder of the extreme sport Døds diving (Death diving) was born in Norway. The project co-produced with Hutong in France, is currently shooting, with a delivery pencilled for 2028. “Temporary Lives” (Wessam Hachicho) Produced by Amélie Quéret, Respiro Productions Wessam Hachicho, a graduate from Oslo’s Westerdals film school and a former cinematographer in Syria, draws from her own uprooting experience to tell the story of a Syrian teenager refugee in Oslo and his estranged father as they seek asylum in Norway. “Beneath the [film’s] political context lies an intimate story about unresolved trauma, family bonds and the sacrifices parents and children make for one another,” said Hachicho. The film also asks how institutions shape individual lives, as every decision the characters make becomes a negotiation between survival, dignity, and hope.” Queret, who met the rising filmmaker at the Less is More Lab, said she was blown away by Hachicho’s script and “clear artistic identity.” In Haugesund, she will be looking for a Norwegian co-producer and access to Nordic funds. Filming is due to start in 2027.
