articles.title: Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 1:59am PT Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Dominates U.K. and Ireland Box Office With Massive Launch 41 minutes ago Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago See All Tabernacle Street Films/Unscripted Co Acclaimed Bengali cinema actor Parno Mittra is stepping behind the camera as a producer for the first time with “ The Music Teacher ,” a British-Indian short film starring Raima Sen that begins principal photography this month in Kolkata. The project is co-produced by Tabernacle Street Films (U.K.) and Unscripted Co (India), the production banner Mittra is launching with this film. Written and directed by Shrimoyee Chakraborty, “The Music Teacher” is her first Bengali narrative film, following her documentary “Spirit of the Wildflower” and her work as creator and presenter of “India Bites.” Chakraborty also produces for Tabernacle Street Films, alongside Mittra’s producing role for Unscripted Co. Editor Aarti Bajaj, known for her work on “Jab We Met,” “Rockstar,” “Highway,” “Tamasha,” “Sacred Games,” “Jubilee” and “Amar Singh Chamkila,” comes aboard as co-producer. Related Stories James Gunn Gave ‘Big Brother 28’ Star Rick Devens a Cameo in ‘Man of Tomorrow’ but He ‘Had to Cancel’ Margot Robbie, Mark Ruffalo, Daisy Ridley, Omar Sy Projects Lead Venice Immersive Lineup Sen takes the title role, with Niranjan Mondal, who appeared in “Laughtersane,” rounding out the cast. Popular on Variety Inspired by Chakraborty’s mother, “The Music Teacher” is set in North Kolkata and centers on a young man struggling with depression who finds a path back to life through a teacher of Rabindra Sangeet, the genre of songs composed by Nobel laureate Rabindranath Tagore that remains central to Bengali culture. The film is billed as a tribute to Rabindra Sangeet and the educators who have preserved Bengal’s cultural heritage across generations, exploring resilience and human connection. Mittra has spent more than two decades building a career as one of Bengali cinema’s most established actors, with credits including “Doob (No Bed of Roses),” “Rajkahini,” “Apur Panchali” and “Ranjana Ami Ar Ashbona.” “‘The Music Teacher’ embodies the kind of cinema I want Unscripted Co to champion – stories that are deeply rooted, emotionally resonant and capable of travelling across cultures,” Mittra said. “After more than two decades as an actor, producing this film marks an exciting new chapter in my creative journey. As our first production, this project represents the beginning of the vision I have for Unscripted Co, and I couldn’t have asked for a more inspiring team to bring it to life.” “‘The Music Teacher’ is my love letter to my mother, to Rabindra Sangeet and to Kolkata,” Chakraborty added. “It’s an incredibly personal story, and I’m honored to be making it alongside such an extraordinary team.” “I’ve spent my career helping shape stories in the edit room, and producing feels like a natural extension of that journey,” Bajaj said. “‘The Music Teacher’ is intimate, deeply moving and profoundly human. articles.title: Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 2:00am PT Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Dominates U.K. and Ireland Box Office With Massive Launch 41 minutes ago Singapore’s First Wuxia Film ‘The House on the Moon’ Unveils Clip Ahead of Locarno Competition Bow: Director Nelson Yeo ‘Decided to Fully Embrace Genre’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Raima Sen, Shrimoyee Chakraborty, Aarti Bajaj Team on Parno Mittra’s Producing Debut ‘The Music Teacher’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago See All Momo Film Co. Singapore has never really had a wuxia feature film – though the genre was a fixture of local television in the late 1980s and early 1990s, when a wave of wuxia serials cast actors like Li Nanxing and Zhu Ming. Nelson Yeo is closing that gap with “ The House on the Moon ,” a lunar reimagining of the Chang’Er myth landing in Locarno’s international competition. Variety is exclusively unveiling a clip from the film, ahead of its world premiere. Related Stories Margot Robbie, Mark Ruffalo, Daisy Ridley, Omar Sy Projects Lead Venice Immersive Lineup 'Matchbox' Trailer: John Cena Stars in Toy Car Action Movie From Apple TV Wuxia is the Chinese genre of sword-fighting heroes and martial fantasy that has powered everything from King Hu’s classics to Wong Kar-wai’s “Ashes of Time.” Popular on Variety “It was quite ambitious when we first started having this idea of picking wuxia,” Yeo tells Variety . “For this one I decided to fully embrace genre and see where the film can take us.” Yeo has a habit of returning to Locarno. He attended the festival’s Filmmakers Academy in 2018, then premiered his 2023 debut feature, “Dreaming & Dying,” there, where it won the Filmmakers of the Present Golden Leopard and the Swatch First Feature Award. Three years on, he’s back for a third time. “I’m super glad to be back in Locarno,” Yeo says. The film reimagines the legend of Chang’Er, the moon goddess, and her husband, the archer Hou Yi, picking up the story after Chang’Er ascends to the moon and setting her on a journey to its dark side alongside a bandit from Earth. For Yeo, the appeal was less about honoring the myth than filling in what it leaves out. “The original myth has always been so simple,” Yeo says. “As a kid, you can pretty much recite the whole story in a couple of lines and people will get it. But then at the same time, you always wonder what are these characters really going through? What are their emotions like?” He points to Peng Meng, the disciple mentioned only in passing in the traditional tale, as the character who benefited most from that expansion. “It’s just a very basic foundation,” Yeo says. “So I felt like I have more, I can take more liberties in terms of like building the character.” Even so, he adds, the story remains centered on its heroine: “Chang’Er is traveling to the dark side of the moon throughout the film, but essentially, it’s about a journey inside herself and finding herself again and finding her own voice, in fact.” That affinity for late-1980s and 1990s wuxia runs deep. Yeo grew up on Hong Kong genre cinema and the wuxia television serials that were once a fixture of Singaporean TV, and he cites Tsui Hark’s “Zu: Warriors From the Magic Mountain” as a touchstone alongside Wong Kar-wai’s “Ashes of Time.” But reviving that language now came with practical headaches. “Sourcing for the props was a nightmare,” Yeo says. “And in terms of location wise, because Singapore being such a modern city, we had a lot of trouble finding proper locations to shoot the film.” Those constraints pushed part of the production to Taiwan, Yeo’s first time filming there. “It was quite an eye opener in terms of how things are done there,” he says. The Taiwan leg also brought him into the orbit of Lee Kang-sheng , the Taiwanese thespian and longtime Tsai Ming-liang regular, a collaboration Yeo calls a highlight of the production. “He’s amazing because he’s a one-take wonder,” Yeo says. “Everything that he does on the first day is just perfect. And I’m so fortunate to work with him.” The film’s tonal balance owes much to its bandit character, written to speak Singlish and cast, Yeo says, to give audiences an entry point among a story otherwise populated by immortals. “I really wanted that character to be the one that the audience can really relate to,” he says. “After all, he a mortal in among all these immortals. He’s the closest to the audience.” The role also reshaped the film’s register. “The original character that was written was much darker and the film was much darker,” Yeo says. “I felt like having this different element, this slightly more comedic character, lightens things up a little bit.” Shot partly through virtual production, “The House on the Moon” pushed Yeo toward tools he still regards with caution. “First and foremost, I feel like virtual production is a game changer,” he says. “At the same time, it’s not so accessible to independent filmmakers because of the inherent cost of it.” He’s warier still of artificial intelligence’s growing role in production. “Nothing beats being on the real locations, having the actors interact with the space,” Yeo says. “There’s so much more room for creative freedom on set in terms of blocking or improv. Working with a cast and crew spanning Singapore, Taiwan and beyond, including a German visual effects team and an Indonesian composer based in Berlin, was, Yeo says, a deliberate widening of his usual process. As for what the film’s Locarno premiere means to him, Yeo would rather audiences approach it without a map. “I guess just to give in to their senses and not go in with any expectations,” he says. “The plot maybe on the surface it sounds really complicated, but as long as you follow the characters’ emotions, I think you’ll be fine.” Whether “The House on the Moon” spins off into a franchise remains an open question for Yeo. “If it happens, if it happens,” he says. “I won’t force it. I won’t force myself to make a sequel of the film.” He’s already looking elsewhere: a horror project he’s drafted, and “Black Sun,” a film he’s been trying to get made for more than a decade. “The House on the Moon” is produced by Tan Si En, Wendy Lie and Kuek Shee Heng for Momo Film Co (part of Fremantle), and Aview Images, in co-production with Weydemann Bros., 9LB Film, KawanKawan Media and Widewall Pictures. It is financed by the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA). The film’s proof of concept secured support from the VP Innovation Fund by Singapore’s IMDA. Parallax Films holds worldwide exclusive sales rights (excluding German speaking territories, Taiwan, and Singapore) and non-exclusive rights for all other regions in Southeast Asia. The film stars Lim Shi-An, Dominick Rustam, Harry Chang and Akira Huang, with a special appearance by Lee Kang-sheng. articles.title: ‘Gagarine’ Directors Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh Talk ‘The Green Eyes’ as Kinology Announces First Sales: ‘Dreamers Know No Borders’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 2:45am PT ‘Gagarine’ Directors Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh Talk ‘The Green Eyes’ as Kinology Announces First Sales: ‘Dreamers Know No Borders’ (EXCLUSIVE) By Marta Balaga Plus Icon Marta Balaga Latest ‘Gagarine’ Directors Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh Talk ‘The Green Eyes’ as Kinology Announces First Sales: ‘Dreamers Know No Borders’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Locarno’s StepIn Focuses on ‘Power, People, Data and the Future of Film’: ‘The Counter-Algorithm Is a Human Being Who Gives a Damn’ (EXCLUSIVE) 1 week ago Locarno’s First Look Section Reveals Six Uruguayan Titles, From Family Stories to Drama About Desire That ‘Persists Across Oceans’ 3 weeks ago See All 'The Green Eyes' 2026 June Films – Haut et Court – Les Films du Fleuve - Hobab – France 3 Cinéma Having boarded as the sales agent of Locarno Film Festival ‘s “ The Green Eyes ,” Kinology has pre-sold “The Green Eyes” to Benelux (Cinart), Switzerland (Filmcoopi), Turkey (Chantier) and the former Yugoslavia region (MCF). Distribution in France will be handled by Haut et Court, one of the film’s producers. Directed by Fanny Liatard and Jérémy Trouilh – also known for “ Gagarine ” – the film will open this year’s Locarno’s Film Festival on Aug. 5, playing at Locarano’s Piazza Grande. Related Stories 'Matchbox' Trailer: John Cena Stars in Toy Car Action Movie From Apple TV James Gunn Gave ‘Big Brother 28’ Star Rick Devens a Cameo in ‘Man of Tomorrow’ but He ‘Had to Cancel’ “Fanny and Jérémy are among the most inspired and inspiring French filmmakers today, and Kinology couldn’t be happier to be part of their magnificent comeback after the wonderful ‘Gagarine’,” said its founder and CEO Grégoire Melin, noting their “unique blend of social and magical realism.” Popular on Variety The film is produced by June Films and Haut et Court and co-produced by Les Films du Fleuve and Hobab. In “The Green Eyes,” Liatard and Trouilh follow little Chaya, who lives with her family in the Landes region in France. But when they learn they’re being evicted, her older brother Nour falls into a mysterious sleep. “We first learned about ‘resignation syndrome’ five years ago, through a photography exhibition featuring two sisters affected by this condition,” Liatard and Trouilh told Variety . “These little girls were sleeping side by side, locked in a deep sleep ever since their family’s request for asylum had been denied. Those images deeply moved us. When we realized that hundreds of children had been affected by this condition, we wondered what these young children, trapped in their sleep, were dreaming about. That was the starting point for our desire to tell a story from a child’s perspective and dive into the dreams of a little girl who will do everything she can to wake her big brother up.” Liatard and Trouilh decided to answer Variety ’s questions together. “We do everything together,” they admitted. “We’ve been working as a directing duo for over 10 years now, and we feel lucky to be able to share this journey together. We still don’t divide up the work.” Thorough research was important in order to address this disease in the film. “It truly exists, even if we then venture into the realms of fiction and magic. We met doctors who specialize in this disease and young people who have awakened from it, sometimes after several years of deep lethargy. These powerful testimonies conveyed to us the sheer strength of these children.” They also inspired the resilience of Chaya and Nour’s. “In our story, Chaya never loses hope of saving her brother, and it is thanks to the love that binds them and the power of her imagination that she succeeds.” Douae Butarbuch M’Zaouki, Sayyid El Alami, Anamaria Vartolomei, Arcadi Radeff, Omar Al Jbaai star. Liatard and Trouilh combined reality and fiction in their award-winning “Gagarine,” where a boy who wants to become an astronaut tries to save his home from demolition. “We love to explore reality without being realistic! Diving into the imagination and our characters’ dreams allows us to explore their emotions in a very visual way.” In “The Green Eyes,” the Landes forest, where they filmed, is already “magical in itself.” “There’s this lighthouse standing in the middle of the pine forest, and a little village covered in sand. It’s a paradise for these children, but also the place where all their traumas are replayed,” they said. They also praised Guillaume Laurant (“Amélie,” “I Lost My Body”), who joined them as a screenwriter. “He shared some of the magic of his vision with us.” “It’s always a major challenge for us to strike the right balance between realism and magical elements. On the one hand, it was important to ground the film in real everyday life, and the archive footage helps us connect with the reality of the syndrome. On the other hand, we wanted to delve into Chaya’s imagination until the boundary between dream and reality gradually blurred.” They enjoy focusing on younger protagonists who are not afraid to dream. “Dreamers know no borders; they invent the worlds of their choice. These worlds are refugees, and when reality becomes too violent, they can serve as escape routes,” they noted. “It’s true that children and teenagers often find it easier to immerse themselves in their imaginations. But it’s also the hearts of adult dreamers that we hope to reach.” Mary Beth Barone on Her Debut Netflix Special ‘Galaxy Brain,’ Wanting to ‘Offend the Correct People’ and ‘Overcompensating’ Season 2: It’s ‘Sadder but Also Funnier’ Lee Chang-dong’s Venice and Toronto-Bound ‘Possible Love’ Sets Theatrical Release Dates Ahead of Netflix Bow Netflix Hit With $105 Million Suit After Losing Copy of Nicolas Cage WWII Film Anne Sweeney Resigns From Netflix Board Netflix Paid $587 Million for Ben Affleck’s AI Startup InterPositive ‘Myron Bolitar’ Series Adds 10 To Cast, Including Melissa Benoist, Bebe Neuwirth, Jamie Hector, Quincy Isaiah Loading comments... articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 3:01am PT Spotify Notches 300 Million Premium Subscribers Music streamer's Q2 2026 subscription revenue increases 15% and ad revenue ticks up 1% By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest David Ellison Says Opposition to Paramount-Warner Bros. Is Over His Control of CNN, Claims He Will Not ‘Bend Newsrooms to My Views’ 15 minutes ago Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% 4 days ago Disney Expected to Sell 50% Stake in A+E to Hearst for More Than $1 Billion 5 days ago See All Getty Images Spotify ‘s Premium customers grew to 300 million in the second quarter of 2026, after the music streamer gained 7 million paying subscribers, exceeding its previous guidance. Total monthly active users, including those on the free, ad-supported tier, stood at 777 million as of the end of Q2. That slightly undershot previous guidance of 778 million, which the company attributed to ongoing “product optimizations” in the quarter. Related Stories David and Larry Ellison Sued by Paramount Investor Alleging 'Illegal' Side Deal With Donald Trump to Secure U.S. Approval for Warner Bros. Takeover Warner Bros. Discovery Sues Amazon, Accusing It of 'Lawless Employee Shopping Spree' Including Poaching HBO Veteran Pia Barlow For Q2, the company reported revenue of €4.78 billion, up 14% and in line with its forecast. Operating income came in at €655 million and gross margin hit an all-time high of 33.4% (above previous guidance of €630 million and 33.1%, respectively). Net income was €545 million, compared with a net loss of -€86 million in the year-ago period. Popular on Variety Subscription revenue in the quarter grew 15% to €4.33 billion, while ad revenue inched up 1% to €446 million. Spotify said the improvement in gross margin in Q2 was driven by Premium gains (as revenue growth outpaced music costs net of marketplace programs, audiobooks costs and video podcast costs). On the ad-supported side, gains were driven by “favorable podcast and tax impacts, which more than offset music costs” and other costs of revenue. For Q3, Spotify expects revenue of €5.0 billion, operating income of €670 million and gross margin of 32.9%. It projects Premium subscribers of 305 million and total monthly active users of 788 million (implying the addition of approximately 11 million net new MAUs in the quarter). Spotify called out the launch of new initiatives in Q2 including Reserved in the U.S., which gives an artist’s most dedicated fans exclusive early access to concert tickets, and Personal Podcasts, letting users generate personalized AI-powered audio episodes. On Tuesday alongside the Q2 earnings results, Spotify announced a new agreement with Merlin for Spotify’s upcoming fan-made covers and remixing tool, which gives artists on labels under Merlin’s Spotify agreement the option to participate. As previously announced, Spotify’s tool will launch as a paid add-on, which “will create an additional revenue stream for participating artists,” the streamer said. Spotify co-CEO Alex Norström said in announcing the results, “We have a scale that few companies in history have reached, a business that is healthy and compounding, and opportunities only we are positioned to pursue. Spotify lives across your whole day — the commute, the workout, studying, gaming, the dinner table, and sleep. At our scale, that is rare… Our position gives us an opportunity space as wide as our users want it to be.” Co-CEO Gustav Söderström added, “This quarter demonstrated that we are already building that future: better engineering, faster shipping, new products and new ways for users to engage. We are still in the very early stages of what is possible and will continue to have a high bar for investments… Our job remains the same: understand the technology early and deeply, and turn it into something people love. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro 1 day ago See All Matt Infante Jesse Eisenberg is set to bring the curtain down on the 70th edition of the BFI London Film Festival with the U.K. premiere of his next feature as director. “ The Debut ,” a musical comedy starring Julianne Moore , Paul Giamatti, Halle Bailey and Havana Rose Liu, will close the 2026 festival on Oct 18 at London’s Royal Festival Hall, with Eisenberg and his cast, which also includes Bernadette Peters, Colton Ryan, Lilli Cooper, Maulik Pancholy and Bonnie Milligan, expected to attend. Popular on Variety “I am both honored and honoured to be bringing ‘The Debut’ to the 70th BFI London Film Festival,” said Eisenberg. “What a wonderful thrill to be the closing night gala, and I can’t wait to share the incredible performances by the cast with a London audience.” Added Kristy Matheson, BFI London Film Festival artistic director: “We are thrilled to welcome writer/director Jesse Eisenberg back to the LFF to close the 70th edition of the festival with his deliriously funny and heartfelt film, ‘The Debut.’ With its knockout performances and brilliantly sharp script, we’re excited to share this film, which will have audiences in its thrall and renewed by the joyous and soulful power of cinema.” “The Debut” will premiere at the Toronto International Film Festival and will be released in the U.S. by A24 on Dec. 11. articles.title: David Ellison Says Opposition to Paramount-Warner Bros. Is Over His Control of CNN, Claims He Will Not ‘Bend Newsrooms to My Views’
articles.full_text: Aug 4, 2026 4:02am PT David Ellison Says Opposition to Paramount-Warner Bros. Is Over His Control of CNN, Claims He Will Not ‘Bend Newsrooms to My Views’ By Todd Spangler Plus Icon Todd Spangler NY Digital Editor xpangler Latest David Ellison Says Opposition to Paramount-Warner Bros. Is Over His Control of CNN, Claims He Will Not ‘Bend Newsrooms to My Views’ 26 minutes ago Spotify Notches 300 Million Premium Subscribers 1 hour ago Sony Pictures Revenue Drops 13% in June Quarter, Music Segment Sales Jump 21% 4 days ago See All Getty Images; CNN Paramount CEO David Ellison said he believes the antitrust litigation filed by 12 states and the Writers Guild of America isn’t about market share but about “whether I can be trusted as a steward of Warner’s CNN .” Ellison, in an op-ed published by the New York Times Tuesday, noted, “There has been speculation about my politics, my loyalties, my intentions.” He reiterated his pledge that CNN would remain independent under a merged Paramount- Warner Bros. Discovery and that its journalists “will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve — not to any party or cause.” Related Stories David Ellison Addresses Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Delay Amid State AGs' Lawsuit in Staff Memo: 'The Facts and the Law Are on Our Side' How Strong Is the Democratic State AGs' Lawsuit Aiming to Block Paramount's Warner Bros. Takeover? “Unfortunately, I can’t give anyone a view into my heart and mind, but I can share this: I have regularly voted for candidates of both parties; I hold some views that would be called conservative and others that would be called liberal, just like most Americans; and when it comes to our news operations, I do not aspire to lead these companies to bend their newsrooms to my views. I believe that news should be based on facts and truth,” Ellison wrote. Popular on Variety The Paramount chief continued, “Great news organizations like CNN and CBS News are here to tell it straight down the middle. That requires newsrooms that reflect the whole world, not one side of it. And it requires independence. Our journalists will continue to answer to the facts and to all the people they serve — not to any party or cause. These were founding principles for both CNN and CBS News, for legends like Ted Turner and Edward R. Murrow, and it is exactly that kind of independence that has always fueled the greatness of ‘60 Minutes.’” Ellison said he has not heretofore publicly weighed in on the litigation aimed at blocking the Paramount-WBD merger because “I believe that anyone who oversees a news organization — I am chief executive of Paramount, which owns CBS — shouldn’t put a finger on the scale, especially on matters involving his own company.” So “when California’s attorney general, 11 other state attorneys general and, a day later, the Writers Guild of America sued to stop the deal, I stayed quiet. I quickly learned such restraint has costs. While I was silent, others were happy to write my story for me. No more.” In the new business, Ellison wrote, “There is much ground to recover.” He cited the latest polling from Gallup that found 28% percent of Americans “trust the news — the lowest ever recorded.” “The temptation is to say the problem lies elsewhere. Our obligation is to look inward and say: We can do better. We are in a moment when Americans trust few institutions, but journalists haven’t always helped their case by refusing to engage with critiques,” Ellison wrote. Ellison had hoped to have closed Paramount’s $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery by now. Instead, he’s facing a protracted legal fight that threatens to push the consummation of the merger into 2027 — or derail it altogether. The 12-state coalition alleges a combined Paramount-Warner Bros. will unlawfully reduce competition in the basic cable and theatrical distribution markets. The WGA’s lawsuit argues that it will also harm the marketplace for writers. Last Friday, Paramount Skydance asked a judge to schedule its upcoming antitrust trial beginning Nov. 4, 2026 , while the states and the WGA asked for the trial to commence April 5, 2027. The parties are awaiting the judge’s ruling on the trial date. There’s been speculation that the states might drop their suit if Paramount agreed to spin off CNN. But California attorney general Rob Bonta, who is leading the state AGs’ lawsuit to block the merger, has denied this. “Spinning off one channel from a media conglomerate is not a sufficient remedy to protect consumers and preserve competition in the film and television industry,” Bonta said in a July 15 post on X. Separately, last month a Paramount shareholder sued David Ellison and his tech billionaire father Larry Ellison, alleging they cut an “illegal” deal with President Donald Trump to secure U.S. governmental approval for the takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. In return, according to the lawsuit, the Ellisons offered “the opportunity to improperly funnel cash” to the president by settling his legal claims against CNN, and they allegedly promised that CNN anchors whom Trump does not like would be fired after the WBD takeover. In response, a Paramount spokesperson said in part, “This lawsuit recycles allegations that have already been reported and already addressed. As we’ve said consistently: no commitments from either David or Larry Ellison have been made to any government body, State AG, or federal agency regarding the future of CNN or any other news property, other than the goal to deliver truth-based journalism.” Ellison, in the NYT op-ed, said the lawsuits filed by the states and the WGA “imagine a Hollywood that no longer exists — an industry ruled by a handful of legacy studios.” Echoing points Paramount has made previously, Ellison said that if you add up every hour Americans spend watching TV, a combined Paramount-Warner would account for less than 20% of all watch time — “competing every day against Netflix, Amazon, Apple, which are all companies whose resources dwarf ours.” If you add in viewing of YouTube’s user-generated content, Paramount-WBD’s share would be around 13%. He said a combined Paramount-Warner Bros. would account for just 18% of the domestic box office over the past 12 months and only 22% on average over the past two years. “Those are not the numbers of a company that can dictate what audiences watch or what writers get paid,” Ellison wrote. That’s why “I believe this fight is not really about market share,” but about control of CNN, Ellison said. If it were about Paramount-WBD’s market power, he argued, “it wouldn’t have been reviewed or approved by regulators reflecting 65 countries, including the United States, the European Union and China.” A combined Paramount-Warner Bros., Ellison wrote, will reinvigorate the entertainment industry. “Hollywood is losing ground to technology platforms whose algorithms reward the loudest voices. The work is leaving, especially from California — where I grew up and where I’m raising my family — draining the deepest pool of creative talent ever assembled,” he wrote in the Times op-end. Ellison also called out “commitments we have made for the proposed Paramount-Warner,” to release 30 theatrical films a year; 170 television series annually, “for our own platforms and for our competitors’”; and more than $30 billion in annual content investment. “I understand that promises from an executive in the middle of a merger invite skepticism. So judge us by the year we just had,” the exec wrote. “Since I took over Paramount, we have nearly doubled our theatrical slate from eight films last year to 15 and greenlit 40 new or returning series for Paramount+, our streaming service. You can expect 90 series from our television studios in 2026. We raised our content investment by $1.5 billion. We did that before the deal was signed and any lawsuit was filed, because making more is the whole point of the company we are building.” Ellison concluded his op-end with this: “Hollywood’s story can have a happy ending only when we connect with our audience. It’s the audience — the American people — who have the final say in whether a movie succeeds or fails, whether a news organization thrives or withers and therefore whether our industry succeeds or fails. I want to build a company with the strength and resources to deliver for those audiences who turn to us, for the storytellers who rely on us and for the country that dreamed this all up.” Netflix Inks Exclusive Deal for Video Episodes of Vox Media Podcasts ‘Unexplainable,’ ‘Switched on Pop’ About 300 Netflix Titles Used Generative AI This Year, Company Reveals Netflix Among Parties in Early Talks to Buy Letterboxd: Report LISTEN: Netflix, Disney+ and Amazon Fight in France Over Streaming Quotas and Theatrical Windowing Rules Chloe Fineman Among Four Cast in ‘Myron Bolitar’ Series at Netflix Netflix Orders ‘Monopoly’ Competition Series With $2 Million Dollar Prize Loading comments... articles.title: ‘Late Fame’ Review:  Willem Dafoe And Greta Lee Superb In Wonderful Indie Film About Art And Rediscovery In A New York Long Gone
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Pete Hammond Pete Hammond Awards Columnist/Chief Film Critic @DeadlinePete More Stories By Pete ‘Late Fame’ Review: Willem Dafoe And Greta Lee Superb In Wonderful Indie Film About Art And Rediscovery In A New York Long Gone ‘Ice Cream Man’ Review: Eli Roth Blends ‘Home Alone’ And ‘Hostel’ In Over The Top Unrated Bloodfest In Search Of A Story ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Review: Tom Holland And Zendaya Forge A Challenging Path Forward In Dark And Thrilling New Chapter From Marvel Superhero, Spider-Man View All August 3, 2026 4:59pm Late Fame Killer Films Late Fame , which premiered a year ago this month at the Venice Film Festival, is a gem. It is a movie about, among other things, discovery and rediscovery. It may be a year after critics first saw this movie that I am only just discovering now as it begins its theatrical engagements, but if ever there was a beguiling and enlightening film hiding in plain sight, it is this one from director Kent Jones ( Diane) and Oscar-nominated screenwriter Samy Burch ( May December). Related Stories News 45 Of The Most Anticipated Movies Of 2026 News The 63 Movies That Have Made More Than $1 Billion At The Global Box Office Based on Arthur Schnitzler’s 1890’s novella, Burch has modernized it and changed the Vienna setting to New York City’s Soho district, a once-bustling enclave for artists and poets and now something quite different. Ed Saxberger ( Willem Dafoe ) has worked for the post office for 37 years, but in the late ’70s he was a published poet with a brief dance with notoriety, a couple of articles written about his modest paperback, now relegated to the back shelves of a dusty private bookstore, if you can even find it there. Meyers ( Edmund Donovan ), the leader of a young group of men with respect for those who came before and whose little salon competes with “influencers” tied to their iPhones in the same space, indeed has discovered Saxberger and intends to make him the group’s next project, an excavation of greatness somehow passed over but ripe for renewal. Setting out to find Saxberger, he encounters this modest man whose current social interactions are with blue-collar colleagues at the local bar and a peaceful existence in his humble apartment. Friends only know Ed as a fellow postal worker, certainly not as a man who once wrote poems with the gift of Frost. But that was another life, another time, and so when Meyers invites Ed to his group it is met with some resistance. He can’t even fathom how this guy even could find his book, much less want to praise it. Watch on Deadline Nevertheless he shows up, and thus begins his relationship with the self-called Enthusiasm Society, a gathering of twentysomething admirers, if not much else, who call themselves intellectuals and reject technology in favor of art and poetry. Indeed their recognition of him as a kind of genius eventually wins over Ed, who begins to remember the love for creativity that once drove his life in a very different era, a lost New York where art was prized. And there also is Gloria ( Greta Lee ), the older female friend of the Enthusiasm Society, an actress and singer and somewhat tragic if flamboyant personality whom they also have latched on to. Ed finds something in common with her, even if they are the exact opposites in demeanor. By her very nature she begins to light up his life, especially when she agrees to perform his poetry at a show the Society is going to produce, one advertising new poetry from this lost genius. What makes this film work as well as it does, even if inspired by material from well over a century ago, is first and foremost a truly splendid cast. Dafoe continues to be a miracle of an actor, never overplaying his hand here and believably embodying a man resigned to a different life than what might have been — a richly talented writer of long ago suddenly reawakened after putting it all in the past. His skepticism is real and so is his awareness that these newfound admirers may not see him for who he really is and what his poetry is really about. Lee, so fine in a wide variety of roles from Past Lives to The Morning Show , is superb as a woman playing a role in life as well as piano bars. Fortunately she is no stereotype here as Gloria is a genuine talent herself, an exceptional performer as she proves singing Brecht and Weill’s “Surabaya Johnny” in a beautiful moment with Ed in the audience recognizing he is also seeing someone deserving of late fame herself. Unfortunately she has demons, and Lee is truly stunning in a role that runs the gamut. Donovan is perfect as the leader of a group who essentially adopts artists for their own sense of worth. Burch’s brilliantly witty, biting and all-knowing screenplay never satirizes these characters or looks down on them in a movie Jones and his exceptional actors have blessed with sheer humanity and grace. Producers are Pamela Koffler, Christine Vachon, Mason Plotts, Danny Roberts H.S. Naji, Jackie Langelier, Taylor Shung and Ethan Lazar. HBO Max and DCS declined to comment for this story. She is currently in production on The Earliest Show , a TV series from Amplify Pictures. She is repped by Atlas Artists, Paradigm Talent Agency, and Ziffren Brittenham. articles.title: ‘Ice Cream Man’ Review: Eli Roth Blends ‘Home Alone’ And ‘Hostel’ For Over-The-Top Unrated Bloodfest
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Pete Hammond Pete Hammond Awards Columnist/Chief Film Critic @DeadlinePete More Stories By Pete ‘Late Fame’ Review: Willem Dafoe And Greta Lee Superb In Wonderful Indie Film About Art And Rediscovery In A New York Long Gone ‘Ice Cream Man’ Review: Eli Roth Blends ‘Home Alone’ And ‘Hostel’ In Over The Top Unrated Bloodfest In Search Of A Story ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Review: Tom Holland And Zendaya Forge A Challenging Path Forward In Dark And Thrilling New Chapter From Marvel Superhero, Spider-Man View All August 3, 2026 8:00pm Ice Cream Man The Horror Section Taking a cue from the likes of Jason, Freddy, Leatherface, Michael Myers, Chucky, Candyman, and countless others, Horrormeister Eli Roth has now realized a 20 year dream to give the same fame in the genre to the Ice Cream Man in the simply titled new film, Ice Cream Man. That’s right. Roth hopes to immortalize the guy who drives around neighborhoods in that musical ice cream truck, the one kids have flocked to ever since wheels were invented. What he has created is just another excuse for mind-numbing graphic terror, but unfortunately has forgotten to provide much of a plot to keep us hooked. The filmmaker felt no studio would touch his vision of unfiltered gross-out dismemberings and the movie is being released unrated and under the moniker of The Horror Section, a new distributor Roth has created to put it into theatres. Related Stories News 'Ice Cream Man' Review: Eli Roth Blends 'Home Alone' And 'Hostel' In Over The Top Unrated Bloodfest In Search Of A Story Documentary 'Death Boom' Review: Eli Roth & Leonardo DiCaprio Among Producers Of Docu Warning Baby Boomers To Be Ready: The End Is Coming, And It Is Not Pretty - Tribeca Festival Essentially the director is taking the idea of seeing kids unleashed to invoke whatever pain they can possibly muster on adults ala Home Alone but making it so gross-out bloodletting that it would get an NC 17 if a rating were slapped on it. What Roth, and his longtime screenwriting partner Noah Belson have concocted is an unfleshed-out idea that is just left with the flesh. Watch on Deadline Opening on a typical sunny summer day in a fictional American small town called Bayleen Bay, we see a little league game in progress when an Ice Cream truck comes rolling in and the propreitor, a man with a creepy smile begins handing out free samples to all the kids. What a nice gesture. Uh, not. The ice cream man has revenge on his mind because as we will later discover via flashbacks, he was bullied and battered years earlier by the other kids in the town, leading to a miserable life. Now he is back, those kids are now the parents of a new generation that unknowingly is being weaponized thru his ice cream in order to have them kill their parents and everyone else over the age of 12. This is a man serving up double scoops of terror but the children are doing his bidding while he approvingly looks on. When these kids march into the school the next day like zombies with colorful flavors of ice cream smeared across their mouths, the grown ups do not know what they are in for but about 15 minutes into what appeared to be just a nice idyllic film, all hell breaks loose and these kids one by one start chainsawing off heads, some unmentionable parts, legs, arms, hands , feet – you name it. They find new inventive uses for daddy’s power tools, make jumpropes out of guts, serve up scoops of the school principal’s brains, and well, you get the picture. Chopping up their parents and teachers has never been so much fun as these kids take command gleefully and with joy as the ice cream man (actor Ari Millen in a dialogue-less performance) leads the band. If all this sounds like your kind of entertainment, I suggest you check in with your therapist. Roth is pretty gleeful himself, a director who has taken the genre to the limits in movies like 2002’s Cabin Fever, 2005’s torture porn Hostel , and the 2023 holiday horror flick Thanksgiving which was the feature film realization of a ludicrous fake theatrical trailer in Quentin Tarantino’s Grindhouse, but here he is really stretching the limits of taste, no doubt intentionally. Unfortunately the timing is off as this underdeveloped concept looks like a bad attempted imitation of last summer’s far superior Zach Cregger directed smash hit Oscar winning Weapons which had a similar idea of a whole town’s kids being mysteriously weaponized. Ice Cream Man feels like a (very) low budget attempt to capitalize and exploit, even if Roth has waited 20 years to get it made. Also it seems ill-timed since this year has also seen smart reinventions of the horror genre with the likes of Obsession and Backrooms finding critical acclaim and huge audiences. With this film though we are just back to basics with no ambition beyond finding ways to tear the human body apart that somehow we haven’t seen before. There is even one kid carrying around his severed mother’s head like a stuffed teddy bear. Sweet. Now it does appear Roth and company are going for laughs in some ways, the absurdity of it all, and I must confess it works in one scene with a priest hiding from the ice cream man and delivering complex instructions to three kids who have thus far avoided the curse so they can break the spell and end this holy terror: “You kill the siren, you cut the Necromancer’s head off, he’ll be wearing a ceremonial cloak, but do not remove the hood, find the ice cream man and remove the hood, make the ice cream man look into the Necromancer’s eyes, that will kill him”. Got all that? No spoiler alert on if the kids succeed in this daunting task, but it does all end with a spirited rap tune written and sung by none other than Snoop Dogg. “I Scream. You Scream. We Scream. ICE CREAM!” Producers are Roth and Kate Harrison Karman. articles.title: Mary Egida Rivera Dies: ‘Spider-Man: No Way Home’ Actress Was 82
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ariana Grande Says Upcoming Break Was “Not A Reactive Or Impulsive Thing” & Something Planned Although “Boundaries, They Need To Be Set” Geno Segers Apologizes After Being Fired From ‘Hadestown’ Over Transgender Comments: “I Accept Full Responsibility For My Words” ‘Chicago Fire’s Dermot Mulroney Says “It’s Bitter To Have To Leave” NBC Series After Two Seasons View All August 3, 2026 8:12pm Mary Egida Rivera Sony Pictures Mary Egida Rivera, actress who portrayed Ned’s Lola on Spider-Man : No Way Home , has died. She was 82. Rivera, who played the grandmother of Ned Leeds (Jacob Batalon) in the 2021 film, died after suffering a stroke. According to an obituary online , Rivera “passed away peacefully on April 15, 2026, in Honolulu.” Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Producer Amy Pascal On How Destin Daniel Cretton’s Vision Made The Difference, Franchise’s Future & A 007 Update TMZ reported news of Rivera’s death on Monday, August 3, with the family telling the outlet the actress was placed on life support after suffering a stroke. The doctors did not have a positive prognosis for Rivera if she ever returned from the coma, and with that information, “the family made the difficult decision to remove her from life support.” Rivera’s obituary notes that “she was very proud” after she was cast in Spider-Man: No Way Home as the Filipino grandmother. She shared a scene with Batalon, Zendaya, Tobey Maguire, and Andrew Garfield. Watch on Deadline The family told TMZ that she “lived a good life” and it was her family who encouraged her to audition for the role in the Sony Pictures film where she was able to speak in Tagalog. In Rivera’s memorable scene, Batalon and Zendaya open a portal hoping to get to Tom Holland’s Peter Parker, but instead uncover a multiverse of Peters. Garfield first appears in the scene with Zendaya’s MJ asking him to prove he’s Spider-Man, to which he crawls on the ceiling. Ned’s Lola then asks Garfield’s Peter to remove a cobweb from the ceiling, to which he obliges. Rivera is survived by her husband, Alejandro Rivera; children, Carmela Jones (Jay), Paul Rivera (Leilani), Edwin Rivera, Angela Kelly (Jaime); 11 grandchildren and 4 great-grandchildren. articles.title: Ariana Grande Says Upcoming Break Was “Not A Reactive Or Impulsive Thing” & Something Planned Although “Boundaries, They Need To Be Set”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Armando Tinoco Armando Tinoco Staff Writer @armietinoco More Stories By Armando Ariana Grande Says Upcoming Break Was “Not A Reactive Or Impulsive Thing” & Something Planned Although “Boundaries, They Need To Be Set” Geno Segers Apologizes After Being Fired From ‘Hadestown’ Over Transgender Comments: “I Accept Full Responsibility For My Words” ‘Chicago Fire’s Dermot Mulroney Says “It’s Bitter To Have To Leave” NBC Series After Two Seasons View All August 3, 2026 8:34pm Ariana Grande Christopher Polk / PMC / Getty Images Ariana Grande is making it clear that her upcoming break was not a reaction to anything and was planned in advance. During a performance at the United Center in Chicago on Monday night, Grande took a moment to address the audience and speculation around her persona. “So basically, the announcement that was made yesterday was not a reactive or impulsive thing,” she told her fans at the Chicago stop of the Eternal Sunshine Tour . “It is something that I had decided to plan that I had quietly made a long time ago and it’s a decision that was made from a thoughtful and empowered place.” Related Stories News Ariana Grande Exits West End’s ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Revival Amid “Ongoing Public Scrutiny” News The Show Will Go On Without Ariana Grande: ‘Sunday In The Park With George’ Producers Plan For Musical Without ‘Wicked’ Star Grande noted that “many things can be true at the same time,” adding , “I want to share this because I heard that my fans were worried that negativity was ruining things for me, but I just have to say that could not be more the f*** opposite. Honestly, this is not what that is. And I just want to be very, very clear: Multiple things can be true at the same time. Yes, boundaries, they need to be set. Human beings can need a break sometimes. And also, this can be and will continue to be the greatest experience of my professional and creative life.” Watch on Deadline She continued, “No matter what noises exist out there, nothing will ever be able to distort my reality or be more real to me or elaborate to me than this love that we share. The rest of that sh** is not mine to carry, so I don’t carry it. I need to get out here and differentiate that from my truth for you all because I love you and this tour has been the most healing, beautiful, corrective, magnificent, special experience of my life.” Grande’s clarification comes after the star dropped out of the West End’s Sunday in the Park with George revival amid “ongoing public scrutiny” over her physical health following the release of the “Petal” music video. In a statement to Deadline , Grande’s team said, “Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour. She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily and then taking a much-deserved break from public facing work and appearances which has lead to endless, ongoing public scrutiny. This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.” Watch part of Ariana Grande’s speech in the video below. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Stewart Clarke Stewart Clarke More Stories By Stewart Matt Stein Joins Pocket.watch From Philo Shadowbox Takes On Management Of New York’s Historic Kaufman Astoria Studios Douglas Stuart, Marlon James & Elizabeth Strout Among 13 Authors On The Booker Prize Longlist; Organizers Say 2026 Selection “Rewards Risk” View All August 4, 2026 2:07am Fabian Tobias is set to replace Christiane Ruff ITV Studios, Stefan Gregorowius ITV Studios has hired Fabian Tobias from EndemolShine Germany. He will run ITV Studios Germany and replace Christiane Ruff who will retire in spring 2027 after a long stint running the production business. ITV Studios Germany makes the local versions of hit shows including I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here , The Voice and The Chase , as well as recent breakout format The Werewolves . Ruff has been running the German business for 13 years and will retire next spring. Filling her shoes, Tobias will report to Lisa Perrin, Managing Director, International Production, based in London. He launched shows including The Masked Singer , Beauty and the Geek and Lego Masters locally while running the German business. Watch on Deadline As MD of ITV Studios Germany, he will oversee creative strategy, production, and the development of new shows for the international market, as well as the acquisition of third-party formats. He has worked for ITV Studios previously, as a Senior Producer on its local versions of I’m A Celebrity…Get Me Out of Here and Hell’s Kitchen from 2013-2014. “I am thrilled that Fabian has decided to join us at this pivotal moment for the industry,” Perrin said. “His dynamic leadership, brilliant client and talent relationships, and deep experience of the German market will be invaluable as we evolve the business.” As Ruff prepares to depart, Perrin added: “Whilst Christiane continues as Managing Director into 2027, I want to take this moment to thank her for what will be an incredible 13 years. articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Jake Kanter Jake Kanter International Investigations Editor @Jake_Kanter More Stories By Jake ‘Baywatch’ Reboot Beaches At Amazon Prime Video Across Europe, India & Canada The Show Will Go On Without Ariana Grande: ‘Sunday In The Park With George’ Producers Plan For Musical Without ‘Wicked’ Star ‘Have I Got News For You’ Producer Says BBC “Nervous” About Trump Jokes Amid Lawsuit: “I Wish The BBC Would Calm The F*** Down” View All August 4, 2026 3:00am 'Baywatch' cast Brooks Nader, Thaddeus LaGrone, Hassie Harrison, Stephen Amell, Livvy Dunne, Jessica Belkin, Shay Mitchell and Noah Beck Ben Hider/FOX Reach for your red lifebuoy; Baywatch is heading back to Europe and beyond. Fox’s reboot of the 1989 drama has been picked up by Amazon Prime Video across Italy, Germany, France, Spain, Portugal, Benelux, Switzerland, Austria, Turkey, Canada, Latin America, and India. The deals, brokered by Fremantle , follow Sky acquiring Baywatch in the UK and Ireland . Baywatch, which wrapped its original 11‑season run 25 years ago, returns in January next year with 12 new episodes. Prime Video will also stream the complete Baywatch back catalogue. Watch on Deadline Related Stories News Fremantle Hires Katie O'Connell Marsh As Global Scripted Chief Casting Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation 'You Are Here' For BBC & Starz The new Baywatch series stars Stephen Amell in the lead role of Hobie Buchannon, alongside Jessica Belkin as Charlie Vale, Shay Mitchell as Trina, Hassie Harrison as Nat, Thaddeus LaGrone as Brad, Noah Beck as Luke, and Brooks Nader as Selene. articles.title: ‘I Is Another’ Trailer: Claes Bang Stars As Heinrich Himmler’s Double-Dealing Massage Therapist In Locarno-Bound Drama
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie First Look At Josh Henderson In Cold Case Thriller ‘Bulldogs’ As Filming Gets Underway In L.A. Demían Bichir & Danny Ramirez Join U.S.-Mexico Border Doc ‘Desert Angel’ As Executive Producers Gavin Leatherwood Joins ‘It Happened One Summer’ As Filming Gets Underway In New York View All August 4, 2026 4:20am EXCLUSIVE: Felix Randau’s post-World War Two drama I Is Another , starring Claes Bang as Heinrich Himmler’s controversial massage therapist Felix Kersten, world premieres at the Locarno Film Festival this week and Deadline can reveal the trailer. The historical drama delves into the conflicting accounts around Kersten’s conduct during World War Two. The late physiotherapist claimed he used his relationship with Himmler to save the lives of 60,000 Jewish people in the final days of the war and also claimed he had used his influence to help stop a plan to deport the entire Dutch population to Eastern Europe. Related Stories News Richard E. Grant & Dominic West Among Cast Set For Dark Comedy 'The Man Who Stole Portugal' -- Cannes Market News Beta Cinema Post Deals On Berlinale Award-Winner & Austrian B.O. Hit 'Four Minus Three' His accounts have been challenged since and mystery still swirls around the truth of what really happened. Watch on Deadline Randau delves into Kersten’s story through an imagined 1952 train trip from Germany to Oslo, where the therapist was hoping to receive the Nobel Prize. On route, he is accosted by journalist Hedda (Valerie Pachner) who demands a one-on-one interview with Kersten, during which she presents evidence suggesting he was far from being on the right side of history. A psychological game of cat and mouse ensues. Randau was last in Locarno with his 2017 film Iceman about the fight for survival of a Neolithic clan in the Ötztal Alps more than 5,300 years ago. I Is Another is produced by Ostlicht Filmproduktion (Marcel Lenz, Claritta Kratochwil) in co-production with WEGA Film (Veit Heiduschka, Christian Bachmann, Julia Heiduschka), in collaboration with Mitteldeutscher Rundfunk, BR, and Arte. articles.title: Sally Field Won Her First Emmy for 1976’s ‘Sybil’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Mikey O'Connell Plus Icon Mikey O'Connell Senior Entertainment Editor View All August 2, 2026 11:00am Sally Field (left) as Sybil and Joanne Woodward as Dr. Cornelia Wilbur in Sybil, the NBC TV movie that gave Field the first of three Emmys. “The televised novel has hit a new plateau,” wrote THR’s Richard Hack. NBCU Photo Bank/NBCUniversal/Getty Images Sally Field boasts a trio of Emmys. With her nominated performance as Tova Sullivan in the Netflix adaptation of Shelby Van Pelt’s Remarkably Bright Creatures — you know, “the octopus book” — she could easily snag a fourth. But statuettes are a lot like being smitten: You never forget your first time. For Field, that came courtesy of 1976’s Sybil . Not yet 30, the actress transformed herself from goofy TV sweetheart ( Gidget, The Flying Nun ) into a serious and layered performer by playing a woman suffering from dissociative identity disorder — and the 16 multiple personalities that came with her diagnosis. Related Stories TV Charlie Hunnam Adopted Kittens While Filming 'Monster' to Decompress From "Darkest Realm" of Playing Ed Gein TV How Rufus Sewell Found a TV Role Worth Staying For Reviewing the telepic at the time, THR ‘s Richard Hack wrote that Field “dominates the screen, switching from personality to personality like a sparrow hopping from branch to branch in a maple.” In the end, the two-night NBC special received a total of four Emmys and a nomination for Joanne Woodward, who played the title character’s psychiatrist. The impact on Field’s career was immediate. She’d be seen on the big screen, riding shotgun with Burt Reynolds in Smokey and the Bandit within a year of Sybil premiering. (Field has since won two Oscars, for Norma Rae and Places in the Heart .) But Sybil ‘s true legacy may be in how it shifted the face of a misunderstood diagnosis from Norman Bates doing mommy cosplay in Psycho to a young actress who was and remains one of the most likable (really!) women in Hollywood.
