articles.title: Nancy Guthrie Case Haunted by Sheriff’s Department’s Possible Mistakes
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 2, 2026 11:20am Pima County Sheriff, Chris Nanos, speaks to the media on Feb. 3, 2026, in Tucson, Arizona. Jan Sonnenmair/Getty Images As the investigation into Nancy Guthrie ‘s kidnapping case crosses the six-month mark, a new report from The Wall Street Journal is highlighting possible mistakes by the sheriff and lead investigators. The Pima County Sheriff’s Department, led by Chris Nanos, has been overseeing the investigation after Savannah Guthrie ‘s mom was reported missing on Feb. 1. As of Aug. 2, Nancy hasn’t been found and there have been no arrests in the case. After reviewing personnel files obtained in public records requests and conducting interviews with current and former county and federal officials and people close to the case, the WSJ has found that there were concerns from the start of the investigation, including who Nanos appointed head of homicide, Sgt. David Stivers. Related Stories TV Savannah Guthrie Issues Emotional Plea for Answers in Mom Nancy's Disappearance After Release of Ransom Notes TV Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie Case Releases Ransom Notes: "She Perished Shortly After She Was Taken" According to personnel records, Stivers was reprimanded two months before Nancy was kidnapped for “poor judgment,” as he was blamed for delays securing crime -scene evidence in a homicide case. The charges in that case were ultimately dropped for insufficient evidence, The Journal reported. When it came to Nancy’s case, people familiar with the investigation said Stivers and his detectives ignored the dried blood on her front porch for hours after they arrived on Feb. 1, suspecting that the blood came from some unrelated cause. “They failed to seal off the property with police tape to protect sensitive crime-scene evidence, allowing reporters, livestreamers, and Amazon and pizza delivery drivers entry to the porch,” the WSJ wrote. After undergoing DNA analysis, the blood samples were later confirmed to be Nancy’s. It’s now believed to be connected to her kidnapping. The WSJ later reported that Nanos promoted Stivers to lieutenant in July. The new role will reportedly take effect in September. Lt. Heather Lappin — Nanos’ opponent in the November 2024 election, where he was running for reelection (he ultimately won after a recount) — told The Hollywood Reporter in February that Nanos had removed some of the department’s best detectives because they supported her election campaign. “A lot of the Guthrie case is just consequences of his really bad decision-making, the years of decimating his units,” she told THR at the time. “Three of our best homicide detectives, probably in [all of] southern Arizona, were removed from Homicide because they supported me [in the election].” People familiar with the matter also told the Journal that Nanos put Lappin on administrative leave weeks before Election Day and sidelined deputies who had supported Lappin after being reelected. The department’s senior pilot, who had backed Nanos’ challenger in the election, was also demoted to patrol duty days before Nancy’s kidnapping following a workplace complaint. This led to more delays in the investigation on Feb. 1, as the department struggled for hours to find a flight deputy to operate its search-and-rescue plane, a $1.7 million Cessna surveillance aircraft, equipped with both infrared and zoom-lens cameras. Flight data reviewed by The Journal showed that by the time the plane got up in the air to begin its search, it was getting too dark to use its zoom-lens cameras. The WSJ said that Nanos has disputed its findings. “I can assure everybody that we are working hard every day with all of our partners,” the sheriff said, including “corporate America,” which has “offered up some assistance with some of the brightest minds in this country.” He added, “This case is not cold.” THR has also reached out to the Pima County Sheriff’s Department for comment. In addition to coming under fire from his own department, as Nanos was accused in March of hiding an extensive disciplinary record , the sheriff has also been criticized by Federal Bureau of Investigation Director Kash Patel. Neither Nanos and Patel has announced any further breaks in Nancy’s case, despite the latter also promising early on to lead the charge on the federal side. In May, during an interview on Sean Hannity’s Hang Out with Sean Hannity podcast, Patel accused Nanos of sidelining FBI agents early in the investigation. “For four days, we were kept out of the investigation,” he said. The sheriff pushed back against those claims in an interview, stating that there weren’t any delays. If Patel “really believes that we tried to block them or keep them out of this or not share things,” Nanos said, “I, 100 percent, want him to call me because that’s the furthest from the truth.” According to The Journal , Nanos said he has never spoken to Patel. Throughout the case, Savannah has continued to take to social media , pleading for answers in her mom’s disappearance. On Saturday, after Nanos released a pair of ransom notes initially sent to the CBS affiliate in her home city of Tucson, Arizona, the Today co-anchor asked that anyone with information come forward. “We are begging for help. We are desperate. We need someone to come forward,” Savannah wrote on Instagram. “Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognizes the writing in the ransom demand notes. Someone has noticed something different, strange, troubling or just unusual — perhaps with someone they deeply love. Perhaps they are afraid to come forward. Perhaps they are conflicted. Perhaps they are angry or upset for being in this situation. There is a way out — to tell what you know. You can do so anonymously. The reward is available.” The Pima County Sheriff’s Department said the notes “purport to have been written by kidnappers.” The second note, which was sent to the CBS affiliate on Feb. 6, stated that Nancy “perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now.” Authorities said they decided to share the ransom notes publicly in hopes that someone recognizes “distinctive patterns of word choice, syntax and phraseology that reflect the writer’s unique linguistic style.” THR

articles.title: Ariana Grande to “Step Back From Visibility” After Tour Ends Amid “Ongoing Public Scrutiny”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 2, 2026 1:12pm Ariana Grande Monica Schipper/Getty Images Ariana Grande is planning to take a step back from the public eye after the Eternal Sunshine Tour wraps, including dropping out of Sunday in the Park with George . This decision comes after the Grammy-winning singer has faced a wave of online commentary surrounding her health and body over the last year. Most recently, discussions intensified after the release of her new music video for her song “Petal,” with many fans pointing out her noticeably thinner appearance in the footage. “Ariana will be taking a step back from visibility after she completes the Eternal Sunshine Tour,” her rep shared in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter on Sunday. Her tour concludes on Sept. 1 after her 10-show residency in London. Related Stories Music K-pop Girl Group IVE is Ready for Their Next Big Adventure Music Sam Fender and Olivia Dean Have the Longest-Running No. 1 in U.K. History “She looks forward to finishing the tour and ending it on a high note, both healthily and happily, and then taking a much-deserved break from public-facing work and appearances, which has led to endless, ongoing public scrutiny,” the rep added. “This tour has been a beautiful experience for her. She loves her fans and has loved every minute of this tour so much.” Grande has been booked and busy the last few years , filming Wicked and Wicked: For Good , which released in 2024 and 2025, respectively. She had also been campaigning for awards for both films, ultimately earning a best supporting actress Oscar nomination for her role as Glinda in the first film. On the music side, she dropped her seventh studio album, Eternal Sunshine , in 2024, before heading out on a 3-month-long tour starting in June. She also just released her eighth studio album, Petal , at the end of July. A source close to the singer also told THR that her new album is “a fight song.” They added that it’s an “anthem about the love-hate relationship with the public and their toxicity. This album is not about any romantic partner or breakup in that way.” Grande next stars in Focker-in-Law , opposite Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller, which hits theaters on Nov. 25. It’s unclear if Grande plans to participate in the film’s upcoming press tour. The “hate that i made you love me” singer was also set to appear, opposite her Wicked co-star Jonathan Bailey, in the West End revival of Stephen Sondheim’s Sunday in the Park with George . However, THR confirmed Grande will no longer be participating in the project, which opens at London’s Barbican Centre next summer. The production will cast another lead to replace Grande. “Following this evening’s announcement from Ariana Grande’s team, we can confirm that she has decided to step back from Sunday in the Park with George ,” Empire Street Productions shared in a statement. “We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support. The production will open at the Barbican in summer 2027 as planned, and casting will be announced in due course.” People was first to report the news of Grande stepping back from visibility after the tour. Caitlin Huston contributed to this report. THR

articles.title: Morgan Wallen’s Year-Old Album Manages to Climb Back Atop the Charts
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All August 2, 2026 2:26pm Morgan Wallen performs onstage for the 16th Annual Darius and Friends St. Jude Benefit at Ryman Auditorium on June 2, 2025, in Nashville, Tennessee. Jason Kempin/Getty Images for ABA Morgan Wallen ‘s I’m the Problem is back on top of Billboard ‘s albums chart, the publication reported on Sunday, more than a year after the country star first released the project in May 2025, and over seven months since the album last reached number one back in January. I’m the Problem managed to best both Olivia Rodrigo ‘s eight-week-old You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love and Charli XCX ‘s brand new Music , Fashion, Film in one of the tightest chart races of the year so far. Wallen earned 80,000 units this week, while Rodrigo’s LP, which topped the charts for two weeks this summer, came in with just under 80,000 units. Charli’s Brat follow-up, meanwhile, opened with 78,000 units. Related Stories Music Ariana Grande to "Step Back From Visibility" After Tour Ends Amid "Ongoing Public Scrutiny" Music K-pop Girl Group IVE is Ready for Their Next Big Adventure While I’m the Problem hasn’t hit No. 1 since January, it’s been a chart monster overall, staying in the top 10 since its release over a year ago. It’s one of two top 10 albums for Wallen, with his 2023 album One Thing at a Time clocking in at seven this week. I’m the Problem has spent 63 weeks on the Billboard albums chart, while One Thing at a Time has racked 178 weeks. Wallen’s number one return comes as the singer released his latest song, “Been by Now,” last Friday. The question now becomes where that song will land on Monday’s new Hot 100 chart. Through all his controversies, Wallen remains the biggest streaming act in a country boom that’s also propelled the likes of Zach Bryan, Luke Combs and Ella Langley, the latter of whom currently has three songs in the top 10 on the Hot 100, including song of the summer contender “Choosin’ Texas.” For Rodrigo, You Seem Pretty Sad for a Girl So in Love has logged its fifth consecutive week at number two after spending its first two weeks atop the chart. For Charli, Music, Fashion, Film opens with a similar debut to Brat, which debuted with 77,000 units back in 2024. THR

articles.title: John Oliver Says Taco Bell Has the Moral High Ground Over Trump Administration Amid “Explosive Diarrhea” Parasite Crisis
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kimberly Nordyke Plus Icon Kimberly Nordyke Managing Editor, Digital View All August 2, 2026 9:59pm 'Last Week Tonight With John Oliver' Courtesy of HBO As four more U.S. states saw a breakout in cyclospora cases, linked to contaminated lettuce, John Oliver decided to weigh in on the parasite causing “debilitating explosive diarrhea” across the country. A total of nine states have now reported cases of cyclospora, which has been attributed to shredded iceberg lettuce sources by Taylor Farms. And according to recent data, almost 2,000 people in those states got sick after consuming the lettuce at a Taco Bell restaurant. Overall, it’s estimated that there are nearly 12,000 cases, with that number expected to grow. Related Stories TV John Oliver Talks New "Prospective Business Daddies" and Colbert Support Group and Reveals HBO Contract Extension (Exclusive) TV David Jenkins' 'Booster Gold' DC Series Not Moving Forward at HBO On Sunday’s Last Week Tonight , Oliver played a news clip in which the reporter advised viewers dining at a restaurant to “ask the source of their lettuce or … eat cooked vegetables instead” to avoid getting sick. Responded Oliver: “Yeah, the best advice they have for you right now is to basically play lettuce detective at every restaurant. And what are you really expecting them to say? ‘Oh shit, we actually get it from Sam’s Parasite Barn. We were hoping no one would ask.’ ‘Cause let’s be honest, your server doesn’t know where the restaurant sources their lettuce. Their main concern is that the bartender they fucked last week stopped working Mondays, and their manager won’t release next month’s schedule unless everyone goes to a poetry night, so why not give them all a break and just order soup.” Oliver then played another news clip in which the reporter said the symptoms include “debilitating, explosive diarrhea” that can last for weeks. The new clips also featured three people who had the illness describing their pain as “unbearable” and “horrible.” One noted that some folks are hoping to get the parasite to lose weight: “No, you don’t,” she said. Noted Oliver “Of course you don’t. Nobody should be looking at the people who pooped so weird that they made it onto the news and think, ‘It should have been me.'” Citing another news report, Oliver quoted an epidemiologist who described the illness’ symptoms as “uncontrollable and it’s very liquid. If you’ve seen pictures from cholera wars where the patients are on gurneys and the gurney has a hole where your butt goes and there’s a bucket underneath the hole, it’s very similar.” Said Oliver: “No offense, but I don’t think that epidemiologist should be allowed to give statements anymore. We were looking for something like, ‘It’ll cause digestive issues,’ not ‘Taco Bell made American shit so hard and wet they need assless beds like a 19th century poop ward.'” As Taco Bell sales dropped, the company put out a statement to reassure consumers: “We want you to hear it from us. We take your health and safety seriously and have removed all affected Taylor Farms lettuce from Taco Bell stores. So go ahead and enjoy your Taco Bell today. You always got us. We always got you. See you in the drive-through.” “No, you fucking won’t,” Oliver quipped. Oliver did give credit to Taco Bell for at least addressing the problem, while then turning to President Donald Trump and U.S. Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. for creating a situation wherein authorities are not able to respond as effectively as in years past. He noted that the Food and Drug Administration “has been underfunded for decades now,” but under the Trump administration, the FDA has lost 20 percent of its staff, and the Centers for Disease Control has lost 25 percent of its staff, including eight of its 11 scientists who track food parasites. “Wait, only three people now?” Oliver asked. “That is clearly not enough. It really feels like we shouldn’t be able to fit the CDC’s entire parasite tracking team comfortably onto a porch glider.” Oliver noted that the day after Kennedy said the crisis was under control, the FDA announced it was investigating a new outbreak. “It does say something pretty grim about America, that when it comes to acting swiftly to prevent a public health threat, the current government just lost the moral high ground to fucking Taco Bell,” Oliver quipped. The Last Week Tonight host ended the segment with a parody ad for Taco Bell that started: “Hey America, we at Taco Bell want you to know we care about your health and safety.” It continued: “We know that because of our food, many of you have been shitting your brains out in a way that we never intended because Taco Bell’s always prided itself on two things: having the wettest food in America and only giving you the regular normal level of diarrhea. That’s why we’ve temporarily removed lettuce from our food, so while you’re powering through our Mexican food adjacent menu, including our, oh Jesus Christ, Sausage Crunchwrap Supreme, you can feel confident that you’re avoiding one narrow definition of gastrointestinal disease. Again, we’re not promising you won’t get regular diarrhea from it. And you’ve seen our food, right? There’s something on the menu called Diablo Dusted Chicken Nuggets, OK? We’re just saying, we’ll try not to give you the kind of diarrhea that’ll put you on the news.” THR

articles.title: Locarno Pro Takes on the Big Issues: AI, “Algorithms and Consolidation Versus Creative Freedom”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 3, 2026 12:01am Markus Duffner Courtesy of Locarno Film Festival Locarno is not “just” about the discovery of new film gems and the celebration of the art of cinema. It’s also about discussing and conducting business, about addressing the challenges facing the industry and about networking to enable all of that. So, while people can explore new and classic cinema during the 79th edition of the Locarno Film Festival , running Aug. 5-15, the Swiss fest’s Locarno Pro industry program returns with a spotlight on the big issues of the day and the future, along with much more, during its 15th edition, taking place Aug. 6-11. Related Stories Movies 'The Days Off' Is a "Love Letter to That Internet That No Longer Quite Exists" (Locarno Trailer) TV Scott Hylands, Star of TV's 'Night Heat' on Both Sides of the Border, Dies at 83 The 2026 program of panels and keynotes will kick off with the traditional StepIn session, which will this year explore how power structures, politics, AI and data are reshaping independent cinema. Also returning is Open Doors, the co-production platform and talent development program for filmmakers from regions where artistic expression is at risk. After all, Locarno Pro also sees itself as a talent incubation and training platform. This year marks the second year with a f ocus on Africa , with the spotlight being put on six projects in development, six producers and five directors. Plus, in partnership with ACAU – Agencia del Cine y el Audiovisual del Uruguay, L ocarno Pro’s First Look initiative for works-in-progress will showcase six Uruguayan films currently in post-production. The networking platform Match Me! and co-development program Alliance 4 Development also return, as do the classic film program Locarno Heritage and programs targeting young industry professionals in the U30 think tank. Among the innovations this year is the launch of a Locarno Pro podcast and the inaugural Open Doors Connect program, which “allows foundations, film institutions, and organizations to join by sponsoring an industry professional, opening up new financing models, markets, and collaborations rooted in global equality.” Markus Duffner , director of Locarno Pro in his sixth year, expects around 2,000 accredited industry guests to attend this year, with around three-quarters of those coming from Europe. Among the attendees are an estimated 800 producers, 350 buyers, about 100 sales agents and 300 film festival programmers. Ahead of all the debates and networking, Duffner took time to talk to THR about the return of the Locarno Investment Community for its second year, the choice of Uruguay, the hot issues in focus and why AI will be touched on throughout the program. After its debut last year, the Locarno Investment Community is back for its second edition. Why does this offering make so much sense, and what was the experience and feedback like last year? In the first year of the investment community, we had about 40 private investors of different profiles – from private banks to philanthropic organizations, mostly from North America. Then there were European funds that are investing not only in projects but also in companies and slates. And there were also private individuals who are curious about how to invest in culture and in film in particular. We organize this in partnership with Oxbelly, which is developing talented scriptwriters, but also bringing in their ambassadors and philanthropic investors from the U.S. So, we created the program together, and last year, it was like the pilot edition with some closed-door sessions. For this year’s second edition of the Locarno Investment Community, we will have around 45 investment players coming, and we will have a stronger program for them to also network and mingle with our talent. It’s an added value for both the Swiss industry and for the European industry in Locarno. So, I think it’s something that’s here to stay for us. Are any participants from last year returning or are they all new? I would say 25 percent are coming back, and then we have added new layers. It will also always depend on the films that are selected for the festival. We’re different from Sundance Catalyst or the Cannes Investorx Circle . We are really an informal platform. We create networking opportunities with all the lunches, one-to-one meetings and closed-door sessions, which are useful for both networking reasons, but also for training, education and mentoring for both the investors and our talent. And everything in Locarno Pro is tailor-made and custom-made based on the profile of the people who are coming, so that we don’t waste anyone’s time. We think about who sits where at which table at lunch or why this person should meet with that person. Once you get to Locarno, we take care of you, and that’s unique. And innovation is key. It’s not copy-paste. We stop and look at what our industry needs. The idea is to innovate our Locarno Pro platform because of the state of the traditional financing system. Everybody is worried about what’s going to happen in the future. This year continues that. Tell me some more about those future concerns, please. There are some earthquakes that are shaking up the infrastructure of the global industry. Let’s see what happens with the merger of Paramount and Warner. Let’s see what happens with everything that AI can do, as groundbreaking technologies will change the industry. I’m not even talking about generative AI and the creative element, but what’s happening in the industry with those tools. Innovation is important for us. And for us, innovation is also about bringing new players to our platform. It’s our duty to offer new options to talents, filmmakers and producers. How do the connections you enable lead to results? We are pretty realistic. It’s not that the connections we create are leading to immediate results, but our incubation works, and we have some success stories, such as Flow , the Oscar-winning animation . This year, we also won a Silver Bear in Berlin [for best screenplay] with Nina Roza , which was one of our first-look works-in-progress from Canada last year. In the Piazza Grande program this year, we have a film called The Chilean , which is co-produced by an Italian and a Chilean producer who met in 2017 in Locarno in our Match Me! [networking offering]. They even got a small grant from Ticino [which is the Swiss region that Locarno is part of] and got to shoot a few days in Locarno, so for me this is like the perfect story to show how Locarno Pro plays a role. Probably, this film wouldn’t have been made if it wasn’t for the platform we created. How does Locarno fit into the annual schedule for film investors? Investors either have funds, mostly smaller funds, or they can allocate $1 million a year, and they come to Locarno looking at the festival calendar. They have Venice and Toronto coming up, and then they have a few other smaller markets for potentially another $400,000 or so to invest. If you invest $100,000-$150,000 in each film, you’re scouting for projects. And there are some funds that need to spend their money by the end of the year. So for them to come to Locarno increases the potential for them to find a project. If we have 85 talents, and we match them based on their profile, there is a good chance. Uruguay is the focus of this year’s first look works-in-progress showcase at Locarno Pro. How did you choose the country? What we do when choosing a country is secure a partnership with a local institution to allow us to get the full picture of every country. And we work with this local partner a year in advance, or even a year and a half in advance. When we chose a focus on Spain, we were looking at post-COVID politics, and saw that the Spanish government invested so much money into cultural recovery after COVID that we thought, let’s do something with Spain. Within a couple of years, they must have a boom in projects and a lot of good films with commercial and festival potential. Similarly, if you look at the Latin American landscape, given the current political situation in Argentina, I think Uruguay and Brazil now are the two thriving countries that are able to invest a lot in minority co-productions as well as majority co-productions. They have a very thriving industry at the moment. Uruguay, especially if you look at its proximity to Argentina and how it can compensate for that, is really interesting. And in talking with ACAU – Agencia del Cine y el Audiovisual del Uruguay, we felt this is a really good moment to focus on Uruguay. This year’s six works-in-progress from Uruguay are a really diverse selection in terms of genres, in terms of geographical regions and in the way they are shot. They provide a really nice picture of Uruguay today. In this year’s Locarno Pro panel discussions and keynotes, what are some of the key overarching themes? We’re having over 50 speakers this year. StepIn, which is our thought-provoking kick-off event every year, [film industry data analyst] Stephen Follows is going to talk about our main topics, which will be reflected across the rest of the Locarno Pro program, which is: “Power. People. Data.” – and the future of them. He will address “Fear, Lies, and the Illusion of Control.” We were thinking of our core themes even before the [Paramount-Warner Bros. Discovery] merger news, and then we said: “Okay, this is a question of power, of course, but at the same time, it’s a question of the algorithm, so data.” There is subscription fatigue or fatigue of the algorithmization of products and content that is available not only online but also in cinemas nowadays. Tell me a bit more about that and other themes! Studios use algorithms to decide what to finance, to develop, and all that. Stephen Follows has been vocal about this. But for us, he will do a special intro. Our program will also focus on gender equality nowadays in the industry and what it means to distribute a film today. And, of course, how to finance them will be a topic. We’ll talk about films versus formula – algorithms and consolidation versus creative freedom. That is not AI per se, but there is a lot of AI in there. We will think a lot about why cinema still matters and what it means to release a film. There is a little bit of activism in it, but we can see that fewer films are doing huge box office, and others are flopping, so this is a market trend that has been changing. This year, we’ll also talk about the cost of inclusion. Who can afford to be in this industry? Things are changing so fast. Our ambition is not to find a solution, but to look at risk and opportunity, and maybe anticipate the market trends ahead. But the time horizons have changed. Before the pandemic, StepIn was aiming at five-year predictions. Now, the industry is moving so fast, with all the tech disruption, the market and all the politics, that if we can predict what happens next year or in two years, I would say we are doing a good job. For the first time, we will also do a podcast of about an hour with the topics in focus. And AI will be a topic across the Locarno Pro sessions and events? On all [panels and sessions], more or less, there is at least one person who is thinking about and covering AI. Everything is influenced by AI these days, including financing, distribution and sales. And since there is no legislation yet on a European level to create precise rules, so we want to allow for conversation and dialogue. We invite policymakers and members of film institutes too, who can then relate takeaways to their ministries of culture or the European Parliament so they understand what key players are going through. Film restorations have also been a key part of Locarno Pro… Yes, we have a full-day Heritage Monday dedicated to new restorations we present. We restore two films a year. This year, it was a Senegalese film from Safi Faye, Letter From My Village , and Dances With Wolves , the Academy Award winner by Kevin Costner, which will be shown in a second screening in the Piazza Grande on Friday night. Restoration really goes to what Locarno’s mission is, including finding new audiences for classic films and giving them a new commercial life. THR

articles.title: Woody Harrelson to Receive Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at Bosnian Film Festival
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All August 3, 2026 1:28am Woody Harrelson Mark Seliger/SFF U.S. star Woody Harrelson will be honored with an award at this year’s Sarajevo Film Festival in recognition of his contribution to cinema. He’ll receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at the Bosnian festival, joining fellow 2026 recipients Emily Watson (also president of the Sarajevo jury ), Asghar Farhadi , and the recently announced Diego Luna . Harrelson has earned three Oscar nominations, including best actor for The People vs. Larry Flynt and best supporting actor for The Messenger and Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri . He accrued more critical acclaim for starring in Ruben Östlund’s Palme d’Or winner Triangle of Sadness . Related Stories Movies Locarno Pro Takes on the Big Issues: AI, "Algorithms and Consolidation Versus Creative Freedom" Movies 'The Days Off' Is a "Love Letter to That Internet That No Longer Quite Exists" (Locarno Trailer) “Woody Harrelson is one of those actors you believe in even in the most improbable roles, while at the same time you can easily imagine him as someone you might spend time with every day,” said Jovan Marjanović, director of the Sarajevo Film Festival. “That remarkable ease of performance is, in fact, one of the hardest qualities to achieve on screen, yet he delivers it film after film. His talent, charisma, and boldness serve as an inspiration to many future generations. It is our great honor to present him with the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.” In honor of Harrelson, Michael Winterbottom’s 1997 film Welcome to Sarajevo , which premiered at Cannes and was also screened at the third-ever Sarajevo Film Festival later that year, will be screened for audiences. The film examines the war in Bosnia in the mid-1990s, and the role of journalists in its media coverage. It is based on journalist Michael Nicholson’s book Natasha’s Story . The screening will take place at the Coca-Cola Open Air Cinema as part of the Open Air program. He next leads Apple TV’s Brothers alongside Matthew McConaughey, premiering Sept. 23, and stars opposite Kristen Stewart in Quentin Dupieux’s Full Phil , which debuted at Cannes this year. He recently wrapped Netflix’s The Cackling of the Dodos with Sam Rockwell and is producing a documentary on Austin’s iconic Armadillo World Headquarters . Harrelson also wrote, directed and starred in Lost in London , the first feature film shot in a single continuous take and broadcast live to theaters. His television credits include Cheers , True Detective and The White House Plumbers . The 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival will run Aug. 14-21. THR

articles.title: In ‘Donkey Princess,’ a Young Royal Travels Through Worlds – and Film Genres – in Search of Love (Exclusive Trailer)
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 3, 2026 2:30am 'Donkey Princess' film still Courtesy of Benjamin Echazarreta Cristóbal León and Joaquín Cociña, the Chilean filmmakers who have made a name for themselves with The Wolf House and The Hyperboreans , as well as collaborators of Ari Aster , will world premiere their third feature film, Donkey Princess ( Princesa Burro ), in the international competition program of the 79th edition of the Locarno Film Festival on Friday, Aug. 7. As was the case with their first two feature films, their new movie is an ambitious cinematic ride. And it comes in the form of an envelope-pushing fairy tale. Related Stories Movies Woody Harrelson to Receive Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at Bosnian Film Festival Movies Locarno Pro Takes on the Big Issues: AI, "Algorithms and Consolidation Versus Creative Freedom" The Donkey Princess focuses on Diana, the princess of an ancient kingdom, whose father, King Arthur, has forbidden love. That is why, when Diana falls in love with Lalo, the King simply banishes him. “Using a magical bracelet, Diana travels to other worlds in search of her love,” explains a synopsis. “Discovering that her father manipulates her decisions, she must face her fears and change her destiny.” The travels that Diana embarks on allow León and Cociña to use the places she visits as a way to explore different film periods and genres. “Diana travels through parallel worlds where each universe transforms the film’s genre,” the creative duo explains in a directors’ note on the Locarno website. “The film brings this constant mutation of realities into live action, where fantasy reshapes everything.” The cast is led by Antonia Giesen and also features Andrew Bargsted and Francisco Melo. Alejandra Moffat co-wrote the screenplay for Donkey Princess with the directors. The movie, featuring cinematography by Benjamín Echazarreta, was edited by Soledad Salfate, Maria Salazar, León and Cociña. Bendita Film Sales is handling international sales. “ Donkey Princess is our way of reimagining the history of fantasy cinema: a film that engages with this tradition while presenting our own vision of the genre,” León and Cociña highlight in a directors’ statement. “In The Wolf House , The Hyperboreans and in our short films, we have explored worlds where dreams and nightmares dominate the materiality of space, generating universes in constant construction, mutation and destruction. In Donkey Princess , we take these ideas and adapt them into a fiction feature film performed entirely by actors. The story is loosely inspired by the tale Donkeyskin , as recorded in writing by [Charles] Perrault and later adapted for the screen by Jacques Demy.” But there is really no way to get a feel for a film by León and Cociña other than to watch it. THR can now exclusively premiere a trailer for Donkey Princess . So, check it out right here – and get ready to have your mind blown. THR

articles.title: Sarajevo Unveils Open Air Program, Including Diego Luna’s ‘Ashes,’ ‘Minotaur’ and ‘No Good Men’
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lily Ford Plus Icon Lily Ford @lilyfordtweets Follow Sign Up View All August 3, 2026 3:48am 'Minotaur' Cannes Film Festival Sarajevo Film Festival has unveiled its Open Air program, with films such as the Cannes-premiering Minotaur and Diego Luna ‘s Ashes set to screen at the fest’s largest venue, the Coca-Cola Open Air Cinema. Paweł Pawlikowski’s Fatherland , starring Hanns Zischler and Sandra Hüller, will open the section at the Bosnian film festival, with Danis Tanović’s 2001 film No Man’s Land set to close it. The movie takes place in 1993, during the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina. By a twist of fate, Čiki, a soldier in the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, finds himself trapped in the same trench as Nino, a Bosnian Serb soldier. Related Stories Movies In 'Donkey Princess,' a Young Royal Travels Through Worlds - and Film Genres - in Search of Love (Exclusive Trailer) Movies Woody Harrelson to Receive Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at Bosnian Film Festival Also premiering in the program is Luna’s film about two siblings forced to leave Mexico and head to Madrid to reunite with their mother, who had left a few years earlier to chase a better future. When they arrive, however, the bitter, suffocating reality that awaits them proves far harsher than imagined. Luna spoke to The Hollywood Reporter at Cannes about the making of the film and why it was a deeply personal project. Also screening is Andrey Zvyagintsev’s Minotaur , another feature from Cannes, following a successful company director called Gleb , who finds himself under siege from mounting corporate pressures and an increasingly unstable world. The collapse of his carefully ordered life accelerates towards violence. The Berlinale opener No Good Men from Shahrbanoo Sadat is also set for a Sarajevo premiere. It focuses on Naru, the only camerawoman at Kabul’s main TV station, who struggles to keep custody of her three-year-old son after leaving her husband, a serial cheater. Convinced no good men exist in her country, Naru is caught off guard when Qodrat, Kabul TV’s most respected journalist, gives her a career opportunity. Among other movies premiering in this section are Annemarie Jacir’s Palestine 36 , Rodrigo Sorogoyen’s The Beloved , and Michael Winterbottom’s 1997 film Welcome to Sarajevo , in honor of the recently announced Honorary Heart of Sarajevo recipient Woody Harrelson . Also on Monday, the Sarajevo Film Festival unveiled its Open Air Premiere program, which brings together the most anticipated new films from the region of the former Yugoslavia. These movies are screened at UNIQA Open Air Cinema Stari Grad, and the best film — selected by audiences — will receive the Prix Cineplexx. Among the features in this selection are Miroslav Terzić’s 3 Weeks After , Miha Hočevar’s Hidden People , and Marijana Jankovic’s Home . Igor Jelinović’s Honey Bunny will screen, as will Darko Štante’s The Lost Son , Predrag Ličina’s The Virus of Pathological Kindness , and Hari Šečić’s The Widower , about a 62-year-old electrician who was raised and lives in a patriarchal society. When his daily routine changes after the sudden death of his wife, Enisa, Mirsad tries to get used to a life without her and soon realizes that he took her for granted. The 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival will take place Aug. 14-21. THR

articles.title: Christopher Nolan China Interview Goes Viral Over Frank Views on Critics, Christian Themes in ‘The Odyssey,’ Being a “Bard for a Civilization at Dusk”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 3, 2026 4:55am Christopher Nolan Josh Telles/PMC Despite The Odyssey giving up the throne to Spider-Man: Brand New Day at the box office, Christopher Nolan continues to make news, this time for a press tour interview he did in China that got deeply philosophical about art, history, storytelling, modern film criticism, and the appearance of Christian conceptions of atonement in his soon-to-be billion-dollar blockbuster. Speaking to Chinese podcaster and political philosophy lecturer Zhong Shu in Beijing, which first appeared on China’s Bilibili video platform, the British filmmaker has something of a hard break from the usual interviews he’s done on The Odyssey’s globe-spanning press tour. There were no games, no soft-ball or rushed questions about his favorite moments from the production or anecdotes about the actors, instead Zhong’s interview was one of the rare ones where the filmmaker was probed about his personal philosophy and worldview and how that informed the making of The Odyssey . Related Stories Movies Sarajevo Unveils Open Air Program, Including Diego Luna's 'Ashes,' 'Minotaur' and 'No Good Men' Movies In 'Donkey Princess,' a Young Royal Travels Through Worlds - and Film Genres - in Search of Love (Exclusive Trailer) As such, it was perhaps no surprise that the interview has gone viral as it gave us a fascinating insight into the thinking of arguably the world’s most popular filmmaker at the peak of his powers. Here are some key takeaways and highlights. “Bard of a civilization at dusk.” Zhong began the interview, which was conducted in English, by describing Nolan as a bard of the modern age, as Homer was a bard of Ancient Greece and then describing the latter’s poem as a celebration of war and victory, whereas Nolan’s adaptation of The Odyssey is most certainly the oppposite, reflecting more the current day. Zhong followed up by asking the director, due to the tone of his film, whether he was a “bard of a civilization at dusk?” “I think that’s a really interesting point, a really interesting question,” Nolan said with a laugh. “I mean underlying the main part of the point is this 400-year-or-so gap between the events that Homer is describing when Homer’s story was written down, or first received by readers and audiences. That’s a pretty interesting gap, and for me, I don’t think I’m completely at odds with the way Homer is telling the story. When you look at it from a sort of historical perspective and the reason is — and what I got interested in as I adapted it — is that Homer’s writing about an era before his, he’s writing about an era hundreds of years before. His audience viewed it as being more advanced than theirs. So they were a civilization on the rise, but they were trying to get back to where they had been 400 years before. So that idea of a cycle, that idea of, as you say, a civilization at dusk. I think it’s there in the poem, it’s subtle. But when you look at the history as well… when they would unearth these walls of old palaces that were crumbled, they called them Cyclopian walls because they thought only a giant could have built such grand walls. They had this idea of the greatness of this past civilization. And so I became interested by that collapse, what they call the catastrophe, the Bronze Age collapse. What happens between the events of the Trojan War and Homer.” He added, “I think [those themes are] something that from a modern perspective is frightening and interesting and I think for me it partly comes out of having worked on Oppenheimer before this, which is very much a film about the end of the world, about the end of and collapse of civilization, ultimately. So I think yeah I definitely carried that sensibility into this adaptation of The Odyssey .” Concepts of atonement. Zhong then moved on to the concept of “atonement” in Nolan’s film, saying that such a concept doesn’t exist in Ancient Greek culture, or language, or in Homer’s poem. She asked directly whether the filmmaker had “Christianized The Odyssey ” and further why atonement was so important in the film. “I wasn’t too conscious of how I was approaching it philosophically other than I really honed in on the idea of what’s termed ‘xenia,’ said Nolan. “In the film we call it Zeus’s Law for simplicity, but it’s that idea of mutual respect – that I treat you the way I want to be treated. And in their theology it’s because you might be a god in disguise. I really drilled down on that, and I started to realize that for me a lot of what’s interesting about the interaction of history and mythology is this idea of the ‘sea peoples’, the idea of the people from the sea who were thought to have precipitated the Bronze Age collapse. It’s one of the great mysteries of history: who were they? But the idea that really a violation of xenia, a violation of Zeus’ Law — which is what the suitors are doing in the palace — that really is the [breaking] of Zeus’ Law that is causing this difficulty and this damage. “I think the idea of atonement in a way is what we bring as viewers to the story,” Nolan added. “I don’t know whether there really is atonement in the film, or whether we just feel that catharsis or that’s the process we’re seeing in the final meeting that we’ve waited for between Odysseus and Penelope. But I think in a way we maybe bringing our more modern sensibility to that. Insofar as [atonement is] there, it’s not a deliberate attempt to Christianize it, but it’s an outgrowth or it’s a natural conclusion of burrowing in on this philosophical idea of what happens when you break Zeus’ Law.” Modern film criticism, storytelling and tropes. Circling back to Homer’s poem, and how it celebrates the great men of history, Zhong then probed Nolan on whether his adaptation “apologizes” for this sense of greatness to suit modern sensibilities. “Is [ The Odyssey ] a story of apology that demands repentance, and reflection and self-criticism?, asked Zhong. I think that when you’re talking about storytelling, you’re always in conversation with the expectations of the audience,” Nolan began his considered reply. “So, it really is an energy that’s brought from the audience as well as an energy that’s put forward from the story itself. When you’re characterizing somebody, and the trite version of this, or the criticism that is often leveled at movies in general, is, ‘oh, the character has to be made sympathetic’ — so the character is manipulated in different ways or changed in different ways. And that’s a fundamental flaw of film criticism in a way, or storytelling criticism, because to be able to identify the mechanism does not invalidate the mechanism. And that’s a real problem in criticism today because people have this idea that: because I can understand why the story affects me the way it is, therefore, it didn’t work. That’s not how storytelling works. When we create a heroic figure in a story as storytellers, we have to be mindful of the energy that the audience brings to that story and the interaction between our intention and the way the audience receives that. And the fact that mechanism is identifiable to people doesn’t invalidate it. Part of that mechanism is saying, ‘are we going to treat greatness as an absolute or coming from a democratic or… more idealized philosophical state that we live in, in today’s world, where we want to view people as equal. Do we have to apologize for that greatness? And the answer is yes, we do, or the audience rejects the greatness, and that is part of the mechanism. Once again, the fact that the mechanism is identifiable doesn’t mean that it’s invalid or shouldn’t be used.” Later in the interview Nolan returns to his views of modern “amateur” film criticism. “When I was talking about film criticism, I was talking more about amateur film criticism than professional film criticism, because professional film criticism tends to understand the necessity for the mechanisms. So you’re looking at a lingua frana of storytelling created by Hollywood for the last 100 years that is very effectively universal and so it is its own language, and that language is understood by people all over the world, which is what’s incredible about it. And it is a very accessible modern language of storytelling and it has certain rules. It has conventions, you can break those conventions, you can bend them. You can move them, but you have to be aware of them the whole time. As I say, I’m thinking more of amateur criticism when I say that people who, because they feel they’ve identified the mechanism, they feel that it invalidates it. That can be true of certain elements and film grammar, and film language evolves with that. “So when a trope becomes too familiar to an audience, then it has to be changed. But we do, as filmmakers, avail ourselves of that common language. We build on that understanding that our audience has seen many films. And that they understand that language. So, you’re playing with that language. It’s the language of genre. It’s the language of audience sympathy. It’s the language of clarity and of narrative direction and how you guide people through a story.” Nolan then linked his point about “mechanisms” to his film Memento . “You can’t completely have a tabula rasa; you can’t throw everything away. You have to make your choices in terms of ‘how am I orienting the story?’ So for example, one of my first films, Memento , was a story that I structured in reverse chronologically. But what I retained was a very clear and simple three-act structure. So the structure of the film as it’s received by the audience is very very conventional. But the chronology is unconventional. And so those are the choices you make. That’s one example where you say, ‘Okay, I need this to be extremely familiar underneath so that I can change what’s on the surface.’ And that’s a continual mechanism that’s evolving.” THR

articles.title: China Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Swings to Massive $121 Million Five-Day Opening

The tentpole project has grossed $121.3 million in the Middle Kingdom in its first five days of release. $19 million of this came from Imax, which makes it the highest-grossing Imax opening weekend in the “Spider-Man” franchise for China. articles.title: Korea Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut
articles.full_text: Aug 2, 2026 11:25pm PT Korea Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Zee Shareholders Approve $330 Million Capital Raise Before Indian Regulator Bars Company From Markets 3 hours ago Massive Attack Addresses Singapore Concert Aftermath in New Statement 5 hours ago Korea Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut 6 hours ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Superhero blockbuster “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ” has delivered a huge opening at the South Korean box office during the weekend of Jul. 31–Aug. 2. According to data from KOBIS, the tracking service operated by the Korean Film Council, the web-slinging sequel generated a colossal $16.9 million from 2,252,930 admissions over the three-day frame across 2,409 screens, capturing an overwhelming 80.63% share of total weekend revenue. Since launching wide on July 29, the tentpole has pulled in a cumulative gross of $25 million from 3,384,147 total admissions. Of this, Imax accounted for $2.4 million, making it the highest grossing Imax opening weekend of all time in the territory. Related Stories 'Sunday in the Park with George' Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On 'As Planned' After Ariana Grande Exits Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage The arrival of the superhero juggernaut ended the two-week streak of local sci-fi survival thriller “ Hope ,” which moved to second place. The Na Hong-Jin -directed epic starring Hwang Jung-min, Zo In-sung, Jung Ho-yeon, Michael Fassbender , and Alicia Vikander brought in $2.4 million from 335,810 admissions over the frame. The film has now accumulated a total of $31 million from 4,110,550 admissions since its July 15 launch. Popular on Variety “Minions & Monsters” finished in third place, adding $434,409 from 65,245 ticket buyers over the weekend frame. The film has raised its total to $5 million from 713,940 admissions. “Moana” was in fourth place in its fourth weekend of release, collecting $252,794 from 37,122 admissions. The oceanic adventure has reached a total local gross of $7.4 million from 999,949 admissions. “Toy Story 5” placed fifth, adding $222,465 from 31,874 admissions. The family blockbuster has now amassed a cumulative South Korean gross of $20.9 million from 2,912,210 total admissions since its mid-June debut. Faith-based animated feature “David” took sixth place, generating $167,794 from 25,013 admissions over the frame, pushing its haul to $1.7 million from 263,378 viewers. Local animated sequel “Teenieping: Legend of the Whale Heartstone” landed in seventh place ahead of its official release, bringing in $177,482 from 20,986 admissions across preview screenings. Directed by Kim Soo-hoon, the musical fantasy sequel to the 2024 hit animated film follows Princess Romi and her fairy companion Heartsping as they dive into an ocean journey to rescue Queen Velita from deep-sea creatures. Including early previews, the family film has collected $215,104 from 26,494 tickets. Tomoaki Fujino’s “What Should We Have Done?” debuted in eighth place, pulling in $116,603 from 16,009 admissions over the weekend. The acclaimed documentary captures a 20-year personal chronicle of a family struggling with severe mental illness and social isolation. Since its Jul. 29 premiere, the release has grossed $170,552 from 24,008 viewers. Local psychological thriller “The Eyes,” directed by Yeom Ji-ho and starring Shin Min-ah and Kim Nam-hee, took ninth place with $55,396 from 7,364 admissions, stretching its overall local cume to $11.1 million from 1,537,378 tickets. Rounding out the top 10 was the Japanese anime feature “Dream Animals The Movie,” which added $30,263 from 4,719 admissions over its second frame to bring its gross to $262,973 from 41,996 ticket buyers. The overall market collective gross for the weekend was $20.8 million, making it the biggest weekend of the year, soaring above last week’s $8.2 million. articles.title: Erik Poppe’s ‘Beloved’ to Open Haugesund: ‘All Eyes Are on Norway,’ Says Festival Chief Tonje Hardersen
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 1:00am PT Erik Poppe’s ‘Beloved’ to Open Haugesund: ‘All Eyes Are on Norway,’ Says Festival Chief Tonje Hardersen Cristian Mungiu, Nikolaj Coster-Waldau and Anders Danielsen Lie are some of the star names attending the Norwegian Int. Film Festival at Haugesund By Annika Pham Plus Icon Annika Pham Latest Erik Poppe’s ‘Beloved’ to Open Haugesund: ‘All Eyes Are on Norway,’ Says Festival Chief Tonje Hardersen 4 hours ago DR Sales Closes With WDR/Arte, VRT, NRK in Multi Buyers Pact on Norwegian Wildlife Doc ‘Frost Without Snow and Ice’ (EXCLUSIVE) 2 months ago U.K. Heavyweight Doc Player Jane Ray Boards Argentina’s ‘The Nights’ by Ana Bovino Ahead of ECAM Forum (EXCLUSIVE) 2 months ago See All Credit: Helge Skodvin, Paradox, SF Studios After the World Cup where Norway made a splash with its wealth of soccer talent – led by Erling Haaland and Martin Ødegaard – the Nordic nation will be showcasing some of its biggest film talents at the 54 th edition of the Norwegian International Film Festival in Haugesund, running Aug. 22-28. Out of 84 feature length and 20 short films in the program, 22 Norwegian features and 15 shorts made the cut, including “ Beloved ” (“Kjærast”) by acclaimed Oscar-shortlisted Erik Poppe (“The Kings Choice,” “A Thousand Times Goodnight,” “ The Emigrants ”). The drama, repped internationally by Reinvent Yellow , will have its world premiere in the picturesque Norwegian coast town Aug. 23, as its opening film. Based on the only original screenplay by Nobel Prize-winning author Jon Fosse, the film stars Leo Magnus de la Nuez (“Beforeigners”) and Kristi-Helene Giæver Engeberg (“War Sailor”) as Asle and Gerd, who live an idyllic life with their son in a small Norwegian coastal town. But soon their perfect love is put to test, as Asle, a sailor, is inexorably drawn by the call of the sea. Related Stories Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey’s ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Revival Delays Ticket Sales Until Fall Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage Festival director Tonje Hardersen said “Beloved’ is the perfect opener. “Poppe opened the festival two years ago with “ Quisling – The Final Days ;” he’s a true Haugesund regular, and Jon Fosse was actually born in Haugesund, so we’re thrilled to have them with us with a powerful film, set in the dazzlingly beautiful Western Norwegian landscape.” Popular on Variety “Beloved” is a love story full of the unspoken, tenderness, and mystery, unmistakably Jon Fosse,” said Poppe before adding: “We live in a time where much of what we see on film and series depicts cynicism and human distance. Perhaps the most radical thing we can do now is to tell stories about closeness and hope.” The pic is produced by Poppe’s regular partner Finn Gjerdrum of SF Studios ’ banner Paradox. Another hotly anticipated new Norwegian film, picked for the closing gala, is “The Murder of Benjamin,” based on the real-life murder of Benjamin Hermansen, a 15-year-old boy of mixed Norwegian and Malian heritage, who was brutally murdered by a neo-Nazi in 2001. Repped by TrustNordisk , the drama is helmed by Ingvild Søderlind, credited for Netflix’ “Royalteen: Princess Margrethe” and “Battle: Frestyle.” Seasoned Thomas Robsahm (“The Worst Person in the World,” “Lovable”) produces for Nordisk Film Production Norway. “It’s a strong film that follows the dramatic racially-motivated murder that happened 25 years ago. For me it was yesterday, but the younger generation doesn’t know about it which is why it’s key to highlight it at Haugesund,” said Hardersen. Cracks in Norwegian society The festival chief noted that cracks in Norwegian society is a predominant theme this year, tackled as well in Jørgen Nordby’s Norwegian doc-feature “The Voice That Vanished,” a world premiere. The pic follows local artist Helene Bøksle and the traumatic experience of having her vocals from the game “ Age of Conan” used by the July 22, 2011 mass murderer Anders Behring Breivik in his propaganda videos. Then in Cristian Mungiu ’s Palme d’Or winner “Fjord,” one of a handful Cannes competition entries secured by Hardersen (with “Fatherland,” “Parallel Tales” and “The Beloved”), it’s the turn of Norway’s child protection system to come in for scrutiny. “I’m really curious to see how the film will go down at the very first screening with a national audience,” said Hardersen. Mungiu will walk the Haugesund red carpet Aug. 25, when his Cannes winner opens New Nordic Films, the festival’s industry sidebar and biggest Nordic Film Market of the year, together with the twin event Nordic Film Market at Göteborg. As underscored by the fest honcho, “Fjord” stars Renate Reinsve who toplines Haugesund’s other local pick “ Butterfly ” by Itonje Søimer Guttormsen, and the Oscar winner “Sentimental Value.” Screening at the Amanda Nominees sidebar, Joachim Trier’s family drama has a chance to make history at the Norway’s Amanda national film awards if he coverts all its 12 nods into wins Aug. 22 at Haugesund’s Festiviteten Concert Hall. Besides Mungiu, A-list talent expected take in “Game of Thrones”’ Nikolaj Coster-Waldau , a producer together with Norway’s Kristian Landmark on the Greenlandic-set documentary “Qajaq Man,” and local household name Anders Danielsen Lie (“The Worst Person in the World”), whose performance as jazz legend Bill Evans in the Berlin Silver Bear winner “ Everybody Digs Bill Evans ” enthused critics, including Variety’s . Danielsen Lie will be honored at Haugesund alongside film and theatre actress Anne Marie Ottesen, when their names will be added to the festival’s Walk of Fame at a ceremony Aug. 22. Among the festival’s top non-competitive sections, the Nordic Focus will screen 10 new titles including Finnish chiller “Nightborn” and Danish gothic gay romance “ No Rest for the Wicked ” which scooped two top awards each at the recent Fantasia Film Fest; Haugesund’s parallel children’s festival Cinemagi will open with the Norwegian kids movie “Back To Tottori,” sequel to Silje Salomonsen and Arild Østin Ommundsen’s 2021 Amanda winner “Sisters: The Summer We Found Our Superpowers.” All Eyes on Norway “Our cinema is strong, and after the World Cup, all eyes are on Norway. We’re enjoying a unique momentum with which to further boost our films and country as a film nation. However, our audiovisual sector as a whole is still struggling, with many people losing their jobs,” commented Hardersen, who said the topic of how to strengthen the Norwegian industry in the next decade will be one of the main themes of Haugesund’s Film Policy Conference on Aug. 23. “We’re not part of the E.U. and don’t want to be left out when the E.U. launches its flagship [2028-2034] AgoraEU program,” she said. As for the Norwegian International Film Festival which she has headed since 2015, Hardersen is pleased to announce that it has consolidated its brand in 2026 by expanding its footprint to Stavanger, the Rogaland region’s largest city and Norway’s oil capital. The Stavanger Festival’s soft launch last March sold more than 10,000 tickets and boosted the Norwegian International Film Festival’s overall visitors by 30%. “As Stavanger’s first film festival, we tapped into the large expat community working in the oil business and university students. It was a great experience,” said Hardersen. “Government support to our festival is based on our ability to renew ourselves, and the Stavanger film event was also a way to give back to our key backer, the Rogaland County.” Would she be tempted in the future to move the must-attend industry showcase New Nordic Films to Stavanger, four times the size of Haugesund? “No”, she said. “The beauty and uniqueness of Haugesund is its small size. You run into everyone. This two-city Norwegian film festival allows us to keep cinemas active in our region, to build new audiences and for our staff to be employed all-year round.” Massive Tribeca Fest Data Leak Exposes Jennifer Lawrence, Robert De Niro and More Celebs’ Contact Info; Meet the Man Who Discovered the Files Robert De Niro Expected in Rome for 50th Anniversary Screening of Bernardo Bertolucci’s Historical Epic ‘Novecento’ ‘Tribeca 25,’ Documentary From ‘Valentino: The Last Emperor’ Director Matt Tyrnauer and Tribeca Studios, Will Look at Festival’s History (EXCLUSIVE) Madonna on Technology Ruining the Concert Experience: ‘Put Your F—ing Phones Down and Connect’ Tribeca Festival Condemns Palestinian ‘Dog Rape’ Joke Made on ‘The Wedding Entertainer’ Red Carpet: ‘Human Suffering Should Never Be Mocked’ Jodie Foster Says Martin Scorsese and Robert De Niro ‘Couldn’t Stop Giggling’ While Teaching Her How to Unzip a Fly on ‘Taxi Driver’ Set: ‘They Were Just So Nervous’ Loading comments... articles.title: Woody Harrelson to Be Honored at Sarajevo Film Festival
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 1:01am PT Woody Harrelson to Be Honored at Sarajevo Film Festival Festival to screen Michael Winterbottom's 1997 film 'Welcome to Sarajevo' By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest Woody Harrelson to Be Honored at Sarajevo Film Festival 4 hours ago FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan 2 days ago Gary Oldman, ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker and ‘Barbie’ Producer Robbie Brenner Among Toronto Market Speakers 3 days ago See All Courtesy of Mark Seliger Woody Harrelson will be awarded the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo at the 32nd Sarajevo Film Festival in recognition of his “outstanding contribution to the film industry and an exceptional acting career,” the festival said Monday. The news follows announcements over the weekend that the festival would close with a newly restored version of Bosnian director Danis Tanović Oscar-winning film “No Man’s Land,” 25 years after its premiere at the Cannes Film Festival, and that Bosnian actor Emir Hadžihafizbegović would also receive the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo. Related Stories Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage 'Sunday in the Park with George' Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On 'As Planned' After Ariana Grande Exits Jovan Marjanović, director of the festival, said Harrelson is “one of those actors you believe in even in the most improbable roles, while at the same time you can easily imagine him as someone you might spend time with every day.” Popular on Variety He added, “That remarkable ease of performance is, in fact, one of the hardest qualities to achieve on screen, yet he delivers it film after film. His talent, charisma and boldness serve as an inspiration to many future generations.” Illustrating Harrelson’s versatility and prowess as an actor, the festival cited his Oscar nominations for “The People vs. Larry Flynt,” “The Messenger” and “Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri,” and his performance in Ruben Östlund’s Palme d’Or winner “Triangle of Sadness.” To coincide with the award, the festival will screen Michael Winterbottom’s 1997 film “Welcome to Sarajevo.” The festival described the film as a “powerful examination of the war in Bosnia in the mid-1990s and the role of journalists in its media coverage.” It is based on journalist Michael Nicholson’s book “Natasha’s Story.” Harrelson stars alongside Stephen Dillane and Marisa Tomei. Harrelson will be seen next in Apple TV’s “Brothers” alongside Matthew McConaughey, which premieres Sept. 23, and also appears opposite Kristen Stewart in Quentin Dupieux’s “Full Phil,” which premiered at Cannes this year. He recently wrapped Netflix’s “The Cackling of the Dodos” with Sam Rockwell. The festival will run Aug. 14 to 21. Quentin Tarantino Plans to Retire After His Next Movie. articles.title: Action Man Movie, Based on Iconic British Toy Originally Inspired by ‘G.I. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 1:28am PT Action Man Movie, Based on Iconic British Toy Originally Inspired by ‘G.I. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission 2 hours ago Action Man Movie, Based on Iconic British Toy Originally Inspired by ‘G.I. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro 4 hours ago ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return 2 days ago See All Mainframe Entertainment/Hasbro / Action Man — the iconic British action figure that first launched in 1966 — is getting the movie treatment. Variety has confirmed that an Action Man film is being developed by U.K. powerhouse studio Working Title alongside Hasbro , who own the licence and whose own G.I. Joe toyline the original Action Man was based on. The script for the project is being written by LA-based U.K. filmmaker Simon Hatt, known for his work at Marvel including as an exec producer on “Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 3,” and “X-Men ’97” co-writer Anthony Sellitti. Related Stories Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage 'Sunday in the Park with George' Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On 'As Planned' After Ariana Grande Exits Producing is Jeremy Latchem, another former Marvel exec whose credits include “Dungeons & Dragons: Honor Among Thieves,” “Spider-Man: Homecoming” and “Avenger: Age of Ultron.” Popular on Variety Action Man, launched in the U.K. by Palitoy, was originally based on Hasbro’s 1964 G.I. Joe figure, but later models gave it a more local look and feel, with uniforms and accessories reflecting British armed forces. It was reintroduced in 1993, based on the G.I. Joe Hall of Fame figure of that time, while in 2006 Hasbro licensed reproductions of a variety of the original Action Man figures to celebrate its 40th anniversary. Action Man did get its own animated cartoon series, but this was only available on video in the U.K. due to broadcasting rules regarding advertising to children. G.I. Joe, meanwhile, has already had three live-action movies, starting with 2009’s “G.I. Joe: The Rise of the Cobra,” which grossed $302 million worldwide, followed by “G.I. Joe: Retaliation” ($375.7 million) in 2013 and the 2021 reboot “Snake Eyes,” which made just $40 million off a budget between $88-110 million. A fourth film, “G.I. Joe: Ever Vigilant,” was in development but has since stalled. articles.title: Zee Shareholders Approve $330 Million Capital Raise Before Indian Regulator Bars Company From Markets
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 2:02am PT Zee Shareholders Approve $330 Million Capital Raise Before Indian Regulator Bars Company From Markets By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Zee Shareholders Approve $330 Million Capital Raise Before Indian Regulator Bars Company From Markets 3 hours ago Massive Attack Addresses Singapore Concert Aftermath in New Statement 5 hours ago Korea Box Office: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Captures 81% Market Share in Colossal Debut 6 hours ago See All ZEE Entertainment Enterprises Limited/Getty Images Shareholders of Indian media giant Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd. approved a promoter group fund infusion worth INR3143.5 crore ($330 million) and a new employee stock option plan at an extraordinary general meeting, a day before India’s securities regulator barred the company and two of its top executives from the market. The Mumbai-headquartered media and technology company said its shareholders backed a preferential issue of 249,485,563 warrants to a promoter group entity, priced at INR126 ($1.32) each. A warrant gives its holder the right to convert it into a company share at a later date, at a price fixed now. Once exercised, the promoters’ stake will grow to 23.79% of the company. Related Stories Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey’s ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Revival Delays Ticket Sales Until Fall Ariana Grande to Take ‘Step Back From Visibility’ After Tour Ends Amid ‘Public Scrutiny,’ Drops Out of ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Musical Shareholders also cleared the “Truly Yours” employee stock option plan, under which 37,422,835 stock options with a face value of INR1 ($0.01) each will be granted to eligible employees of Zee and its subsidiaries, in one or more tranches. Popular on Variety R. Gopalan, chair of Zee Entertainment Enterprises Ltd., thanked shareholders for their support. “This approval is a clear reflection of the shareholders’ belief in the Company and its management,” Gopalan said. “The board firmly believes that robust growth capital coupled with enhanced promoter alignment, will serve as key enablers in ensuring long-term profitability in a dynamic business environment.” A day after the shareholder vote, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) – the country’s capital markets watchdog – issued an order barring Zee from the securities market for two months and barring chair emeritus Subhash Chandra and managing director and CEO Punit Goenka from the market for 12 months each. SEBI also imposed penalties totaling INR1.48 crore ($155,000), split between INR30 lakh ($31,000) on Zee, INR58 lakh ($61,000) on Goenka and INR60 lakh ($63,000) on Chandra. The order concerns the pledge of a Zee-owned property in Hyderabad, used in December 2018 to secure INR726 crore ($76.1 million) in loans for four entities linked to Essel Group, the promoter group associated with Chandra and Goenka. SEBI found the pledge was never disclosed to or approved by Zee’s board or audit committee, and determined that Chandra and Goenka had used the company’s asset to shield borrowings tied to their own family-controlled entities. A company spokesperson said Zee was reviewing the order with legal counsel and did not expect it to affect the fund-raising exercise. “The company would like to clarify that pursuant to the regulatory approvals received from the stock exchanges and from its esteemed shareholders at the Extraordinary General Meeting conducted on 31st July 2026, it will further take all required steps to successfully complete the fund-raising exercise, which is aimed at strengthening its financial foundation, and will also continue to work towards creating value for its stakeholders,” the spokesperson said. The order is the latest in a long-running SEBI probe into Zee’s promoters. The regulator first barred Goenka and Chandra from holding managerial or directorial roles at listed companies in June 2023, over allegations of fund diversion. The Securities Appellate Tribunal set aside that order that October, but the scrutiny continued to shadow Zee’s proposed $10 billion merger with Sony Pictures Networks India, which collapsed in January 2024 . Chandra later accused SEBI’s then-chair of scuttling the merger. In the two years since, Zee has cut roughly 15% of its workforce and expanded into sports broadcasting, striking a deal with FIFA in June for Indian broadcast and streaming rights to the 2026 and 2030 World Cups and 37 other tournaments through 2034. The newly approved capital is earmarked for that broader push, with the company directing the funds toward sports, acquisitions, digital content, artificial intelligence and microdrama through fiscal 2029, with sports receiving the largest share. articles.title: ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On ‘As Planned’ After Ariana Grande Exits
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 2:46am PT ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On ‘As Planned’ After Ariana Grande Exits By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’ 2 hours ago ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On ‘As Planned’ After Ariana Grande Exits 3 hours ago ITV Sees ‘Solid’ Results in First Half of 2026, Reports $26 Million Loss Due to Fast Food Advertising Regulations 3 days ago See All Getty Images for Universal Pictu The London production of “Sunday in the Park With George” is set to go ahead as planned despite Ariana Grande exiting the show . The Stephen Sondheim revival, which also stars Grande’s “Wicked” co-star Jonathan Bailey , was scheduled to premiere at London’s Barbican next summer with producers set to launch ticket sales after Grande completed the last leg of her “The Eternal Sunshine Tour” on Sept. 1 in the U.K. Related Stories Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey’s ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Revival Delays Ticket Sales Until Fall 'Sunday in the Park with George' Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On 'As Planned' After Ariana Grande Exits However, on Sunday night reps for the actress said Grande will be “taking a step back from visibility” after she completes her tour — which includes dropping out of the play. Popular on Variety But the show must go on and a rep for producers Empire Street Productions tells Variety : “The production will open at the Barbican in summer 2027 as planned, and casting will be announced in due course.” Grande was set to star as both Dot and Marie in the revival opposite Bailey as painter George Seurat, offering “Wicked” fans a rare opportunity to see the film’s stars together live on stage. “Sunday in the Park With George” is directed by Tony and Olivier Award winner Marianne Elliot, with design by Tom Scutt. Auditions for the ensemble have been taking place in London this summer. Producers for the show said they “wish [Grande] nothing but the best,” adding: “We know this cannot have been an easy decision, and she makes it with our complete understanding and support.” In recent years fans have expressed increasing concern for Grande, particularly in regards to her physical appearance. The actor and singer previously disclosed she was diagnosed with PTSD after a suicide bomber killed 22 people, including a number of children, at her concert in Manchester in 2017. Aside from “Sunday in the Park With George,” Grande’s only other publicly-known commitment is a role in upcoming Robert De Niro and Ben Stiller comedy “Focker-in-Law,” which is set to bow over Thanksgiving. It is unclear whether Grande will still participate in the film’s publicity tour.
