articles.title: ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 2:51am PT ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘Peaky Blinders’ Helps U.K. Region Land Official Production Hub Status From British Film Commission 2 hours ago Action Man Movie, Based on Iconic British Toy Originally Inspired by ‘G.I. Joe,’ in Development With Working Title and Hasbro 4 hours ago ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return 2 days ago See All ©Netflix/Courtesy Everett Collection “ Peaky Blinders ” may have given closely clipped back and sides haircuts a new lease of life, but it’s now helped a region of the U.K. land official backing as a center for high-end productions. The British Film Commission has announced that the West Midlands, home to the city of Birmingham and where “Peaky Blinders” is set and shot, has been named the U.K.’s eighth official regional production hub for scripted inward investment for film and high-end TV. Related Stories Ariana Grande and Jonathan Bailey’s ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Revival Delays Ticket Sales Until Fall Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Leaking Unreleased Music and Footage According to the Commission, having served as production base for “Peaky Blinders,” the feature film “The Immortal Man” and the as-yet untitled “Peaky Blinders” spin-off series, the region has now fulfilled the criteria needed to receive official hub status. Popular on Variety The West Midlands joins South-West England (Bristol); North-West England (Manchester and Liverpool); Yorkshire (Leeds); Northern Ireland (Belfast); Scotland (Glasgow and Edinburgh); Wales (Cardiff); and London & South-East England as an official production hub, lending its strength to a UK-wide offer which contributed £5.8 billion ($7.8 billion) to the UK economy in 2025. “As Tommy Shelby of the Peaky Blinders once said, ‘when you plan something well, there’s no need to rush.’ The growing success of the West Midlands as a U.K. production hub certainly bears this out. Over the course of nearly 15 years, the region has steadily grown in strength and stature, building skills, infrastructure and reputation,” said Adrian Wootton, Chief Executive of the British Film Commission. “With the West Midlands becoming an official regional production hub, our offer to the global film and TV industry now spans the length and breadth of the U.K.: wherever you base your production, you’re within a stone’s throw of world-class facilities, crew and talent, with access to one-of-a-kind locations and some of the world’s most stable, transparent and generous tax incentives.” The two upcoming “Peaky Blinders” spin-off series are being film at the recently opened in Birmingham’s Digbeth Loc. Studios, which was founded by show creator Steven Knight . “I’m thrilled that the West Midlands has been recognised as a fantastic place to make film and TV,” said Knight. The opening of Digbeth Loc. Studios is an important part of that ambition, providing a home for world-class film and television production in the heart of Birmingham. We are at the beginning of a journey, and we’ve got off to a great start. The West Midlands is always ambitious, and we believe we will create a global content making industry in our neighbourhood.” In addition to the region’s new hub status, the BBC previously announced plans to establish its future regional headquarters in The Tea Factory in Digbeth . articles.title: CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’
articles.full_text: Aug 3, 2026 3:35am PT CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’ By K.J. Yossman Plus Icon K.J. Yossman @KJYossman Latest CBS News Correspondent Trevor Phillips Says Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss ‘Will Either Change the World or Crash and Burn’ 2 hours ago ITV Sees ‘Solid’ Results in First Half of 2026, Reports $26 Million Loss Due to Fast Food Advertising Regulations 3 days ago Jared Leto Documentary Director on Exposing Sexual Misconduct Allegations and the ‘Mystery’ of Why He Hasn’t Been Held Accountable 4 days ago See All Getty Recently appointed CBS News correspondent Trevor Phillips has given a typically forthright assessment of his new boss, Bari Weiss . “Bari and her team have a huge tanker of a network news organisation to turn around, and they are assembling a little team on the bridge,” he told The Daily Telegraph . “The great thing about her is that she’s one of those people who will either change the world or crash and burn. But when they crash and burn, it’s in technicolour.” Related Stories Ariana Grande to Take ‘Step Back From Visibility’ After Tour Ends Amid ‘Public Scrutiny,’ Drops Out of ‘Sunday in the Park With George’ Musical 'Sunday in the Park with George' Producers Confirm Summer 2027 Show Will Go On 'As Planned' After Ariana Grande Exits Phillips, who has been a correspondent for the U.K.’s Sky News since 2021, was handpicked by CBS News editor-in-chief Weiss to join the Paramount-owned network as senior global affairs correspondent . He will also join “60 Minutes.” A veteran writer and broadcaster as well as a former politician, Phillips was previously chair of the U.K.’s Equality and Human Rights Commission and in 2022 was knighted for his services to equality and human rights . Popular on Variety He is set to move across the pond this summer to take up the new role at CBS. “You know, I’m 72. It’s a great adventure,” he said of Weiss’s offer. “And who turns down adventures if someone is willing to take a chance on you?” To mark the move, Phillips gave a wide-ranging interview to the Telegraph, in which he gamely discussed some of the controversy that has swirled since Weiss was appointed to her role last year. “In the U.S., the controversy has been framed as, ‘CBS News is becoming anti-woke’. But that’s not what Bari is about,” Phillip said. “She has her own views, some of which I’m sympathetic to, some of which I’m not, but her point is that the media should be heterodox. There should be a variety of voices.” He wouldn’t comment on rumors that reporter Holly Williams, who works in CBS News’ London bureau, had been taken off an interview with right wing politician Nigel Farage in favor of Phillips, but said: “What’s interesting in politics now is this current of thought, represented by Farage, Giorgia Meloni and Marine Le Pen, which essentially says the way we have done conventional politics is bust in a new world, and we need to do things differently. We keep trying to fit it into the old Right/Left duopoly, and I don’t think that’s quite right. The interviews I’m interested in doing will include that group [of leaders].” “I’m not the smoothest presenter on television or reader of the autocue, but I guess they think that I manage the chaos [of live guests] well,” Phillips added. “Broadcast journalism has, to some extent, become the creature of entertainment. We need to return to the business of reporting. To put it in its crassest terms, the story needs to come before the reporter. Despite a previously announced Season 2 renewal , the series officially has been canceled at Disney+ , Deadline has confirmed. Yahya Abdul-Mateen II, who stars as the titular super-powered actor Simon Williams, said in a statement that he’s “glad we got to be a part of something cool” as he thanked fans for their “genuine love” they’ve shared over the show, which has earned him an Emmy nomination for Outstanding Lead Actor in a Comedy Series. “Word just dropped that Wonder Man won’t be coming back for Season 2,” he wrote on Instagram. “(And if you don’t knowww, now ya knoww!) That’s life, right? Everything will shake out. I wanted to say thank you to everybody who WATCHED the show, ENJOYED the show, and SHARED that they enjoyed the show in some way or other.” Related Stories Cancellations and Renewals Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Eulogizes ‘Wonder Man’ After Surprise Cancellation: “That’s Life, Right?” Cancellations and Renewals 2026 TV Cancellations Photo Gallery: Series Ending This Year & Beyond Abdul-Mateen continued, “The show worked. And that’s my favorite thing about it. I could see it on the faces of the Youtube reactors (because I watched along with y’all this time. Shoutout to y’all) and I can see in the messages I get saying how the show reminded some of you not to give up, and I feel it in the genuine love shared when I bump into some of you all during the day. So, thinking of you all today. I’m glad we got to be a part of something cool. Thank you for watching… And uhh… See you at the EMMYS.” Season 1 launched with all eight episodes on January 27, bringing in 618M minutes viewed in its opening week, per Nielsen. That put it at No. 8 among streaming originals for the week of January 26-February 1, though the title appeared to skew older with 41% of viewing concentrated in the 35-49 age range — more than any other Top 10 title that week. Marvel ordered a Season 2 in March with Yahya Abdul-Mateen II expected to return as Simon Williams and Ben Kingsley back as Trevor Slattery. While the series no longer is moving forward, it’s not a death knell for the characters themselves, who still can appear within the MCU at any time.

articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Dancing With The Stars’: ‘DWTS: Juniors’ Alum Kamri Peterson Joins Season 35 Troupe Gregg Araki Is “Not A Big Supporter” Of AI, But Found It Useful For Editing This ‘I Want Your Sex’ Scene: “Literally Insane” Christopher Nolan Calls Out “A Real Problem” In Amateur Film Criticism View All August 2, 2026 10:34am Simon O'Connor of OModest Mouse performs on stage during Audacy Beach Festival on Dec. 4, 2021 in Fort Lauderdale, Florida. Jason Koerner/Getty Images for Audacy Modest Mouse has cut ties with guitarist Simon O’Connor following accusations of sending inappropriate DMs to a minor. On Friday, the band announced that Les Savy Fav’s Seth Jabour will join them on the tour accompanying their eighth studio album An Eraser and a Maze , which kicks off Tuesday, Aug. 4 in Ojai, California. “Simon O’Connor will not be joining us on the upcoming tour,” Modest Mouse prefaced in a statement on Instagram. “The good news is that Seth Jabour of Les Savy Fav will be jumping in to play guitar. We look forward to being out there with you all.” Related Stories News Seth Rogen Maintains He Has "No Plans" To Work With James Franco Again: "Nothing Has Changed" News Aziz Ansari "Would Love To Finish" Scrapped 'Being Mortal' After Bill Murray Alleged Misconduct Last weekend, a Reddit user claiming to be 17 and “following Simon for a few years,” recounted an incident that allegedly happened when she was 16, sharing screenshots of inappropriate memes and messages O’Connor appeared to have sent. Watch on Deadline “Late at night I checked stories and I spam liked whatever it was Simon had put on his story,” she recalled. “He came into my DMs and sent me an erotic image (to say the least) while giving me the excuse he had been partying or whatever, continuing to message me. My age is the first thing in my bio. I reached out to several people within the indie music fandom and nobody with a platform cared. I think more people should know about this. I’m hesitant to put screenshots here but I do have them!” View this post on Instagram O’Connor broke his silence the next day with a statement on Reddit. “Hey, Simon here. I would just like to address some of the conversation on this thread that has come to my attention. Firstly, I would like to just state that I unequivocally oppose any sexual behavior towards minors, as a human and a parent it disgusts me,” he started. “Throughout my adult life, there has been a person who has popped up from time to time with the intention of, for lack of a better term, messing with me. This person creates multiple social media accounts and deletes them… but always posts similar photos that I often recognize from previous accounts,” he explained. “After a long night, I picked my phone up to discover that a similar profile had been interacting (‘likes’ to be specific) with some of my instagram posts and stories. I assumed that this was the same person I had dealt with before and, with poor judgement, I decided to reach out with a tasteless meme, a sticker that read ‘Simon calls your bluff,’ and an attempt to indicate that I recognized the ‘barrage of likes’ and similar photo content from the previous profiles…. Almost a ‘gotcha.’ After a few minutes, I realized that I had made a mistake and this was not the person who I had dealt with before. I unsent the messages and immediately ceased communication. “I’m genuinely sorry to the person who received those messages. They didn’t deserve to be put in that position, and I’m sorry for the stress and attention this has brought them. I know some people will choose not to believe me, and I understand that. I can’t change what’s happened. All I can do is tell the truth, take responsibility for my mistake, and apologize,” added O’Connor. O’Connor, who previously toured with MGMT, joined Modest Mouse on guitar and backing vocals in 2021, first appearing on An Eraser and a Maze , which the band released on June 5. Getty It was the best of times at the box office, and it was the best of times. No worst times as the entire North American marketplace hit a record $428.99M weekend for all pics per Rentrak thanks to the $355M second best ever domestic opening of Sony/Marvel Studio’s Spider-Man: Brand New Day . We knew it was bound to be a record for the U.S./Canada B.O. and it could be higher by tomorrow morning if Brand New Day takes down Avengers: Endgame ‘s all-time domestic opening record of $357.1M. That was the last time in the final weekend of 2019 that the domestic box office had a record overall weekend marketplace record with all titles totaling $402M. Post Covid, the best weekend so far for all movies was July 21-23 when Barbie and Oppenheimer opened fueling a $311.3M North American marketplace (now the fifth best ever among all top grossing domestic weekends). Related Stories News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Powers To Amazing Second-Best Global Opening At Box Office With $927M WW; 'Odyssey' Nearing $1B WW News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Nearly Topples 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M All-Time U.S. Weekend Record - Sunday AM Box Office Update This weekend is +246% from the same weekend a year ago when Fantastic Four: First Steps led the box office in its second frame. Watch on Deadline Year to date, the North American box office stands at $6.19 billion for the Jan. 1-Aug. 2 period , +15% from a year ago. “This now sets up a tremendous month of August, and the likelihood of a $4 billion summer and a $10 billion year just went up exponentially with this milestone summer weekend,” says Rentrak Head of Marketplace Trends, Paul Dergarabedian. The U.S./Canada box office hasn’t seen double digits at the annual box office since pre-Covid 2019 when it ended with $11.4 billion. At this point in time in 2019, the annual box office stood at $7 billion. Summer for the first weekend of May through EOD today stands at $3.57 billion which -1% behind 2019’s heat wave at the same point in time which rang up $4.8B. Michael O’Leary, CEO of exhibition lobby org Cinema United was doing donuts this morning in the parking lot, celebrating the mega box office record: “Moviegoers across generations made this weekend one for the record books. Our industry is at its best when there is something for everyone to see on the big screen, and this year we are seeing what happens when the innovation and creativity on display in amazing movie theaters across the country and around the world is combined with a great slate of films.” The beautiful eruption of theatrical comes at a time when there’s been fears about two studios merging, Paramount and Warner Bros, that marriage of historical landmarks put on hold for 11 months in a pending federal antirust lawsuit with state AGs. Theatrical waves a strong flag at a time when Netflix’s stock at just over $71 a share has hit near 12-month lows; the impression that streaming is becoming more commonplace in people’s lives, not the dominant form of entertainment it was during Covid. Sony didn’t just give us the second best opening ever with Spider-Man: Brand New Day at $355M domestic, $927M WW, but they also recently announced that they were reopening L.A. legendary box office and cinema juggernaut, the Cinerama Dome and Hollywood Arclight in early 2028. Part of Grande’s break includes Sunday in the Park , but a source noted she “cannot wait to support the brilliant team bringing this project to life.” Last December, Deadline’s Baz Bamigboye reported that Grande and Bailey were thinking of re-teaming on a production of Sunday in the Park with George , with Empire Street Productions and London’s Barbican Centre confirming the next month that they’d be staging the musical with the pair, set for a summer 2027 opening. The show’s producers were previously holding off on ticket sales until after Grande’s tour concludes on Sept. 1 at London’s O2 Arena. Last month, Deadline confirmed that Grande will no longer appear in Season 13 of American Horror Story due to scheduling conficts with the 41-show tour that kicked off June 6 in Oakland, California. articles.title: Christopher Nolan Calls Out “A Real Problem” In Amateur Film Criticism
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Dancing With The Stars’: ‘DWTS: Juniors’ Alum Kamri Peterson Joins Season 35 Troupe Gregg Araki Is “Not A Big Supporter” Of AI, But Found It Useful For Editing This ‘I Want Your Sex’ Scene: “Literally Insane” Christopher Nolan Calls Out “A Real Problem” In Amateur Film Criticism View All August 2, 2026 1:49pm Christopher Nolan attends 'The Odyssey' premiere on July 11, 2026 in Mumbai, India. Aalok Soni/Getty Images for Universal Pictures With Letterboxd at the palm of our hands, everybody truly is a critic these days, much to Christopher Nolan ‘s annoyance. The 2x Oscar winner recently unpacked “a real problem” with amateur film critics today, explaining there is a “very accessible modern language of storytelling” that they don’t see as necessary to filmmaking. “The criticism that’s often leveled at movies in general is, ‘Oh, the character has to be made sympathetic, so the character is manipulated in different ways or changed in different ways,'” he told Beijing, China podcast host Zhong Shu . “And that’s a fundamental flaw of film criticism in a way, or storytelling criticism. Because to be able to identify the mechanism does not invalidate the mechanism. And that’s a real problem in criticism today.” Related Stories Culture Joyce Carol Oates Defends Christopher Nolan & 'The Odyssey' Against Emily Wilson, Other Critics News Greek Prime Minister Congratulates Christopher Nolan On 'The Odyssey' Nolan continued, “Because people have this idea that, ‘Because I can understand why the story affects me the way it is, therefore, it didn’t work.’ That’s not how storytelling works. So, when we create a heroic figure in a story, as storytellers, we have to be mindful of the energy that the audience brings to that story and the interaction between our intention and the way the audience receives that. And the fact that that mechanism is identifiable to people doesn’t invalidate it.” Watch on Deadline With his latest film The Odyssey following that storytelling format through Homer’s ancient epic, to the tune of nearly $1B and counting, Nolan explained that amateur film critics need “to understand the necessity for the mechanisms.” Here is my interview with Christopher Nolan: are you a bard for a civilization at dusk? pic.twitter.com/dQION5v6bl — Yiyang Zhuge (@ZhugeYY) July 31, 2026 “So, you’re looking at a lingua franca of storytelling created by Hollywood for the last hundred years that is effectively universal. And so, it is its own language, and that language is understood by people all over the world, which is what’s incredible about it,” added Nolan. “And it is a very, very accessible modern language of storytelling, and it has certain rules, it has conventions. You can break those conventions. You can bend them. You can move them. But you have to be aware of them the whole time. “I’m thinking more of amateur criticism, because they feel they’ve identified the mechanism, they feel that it invalidates it. That can be true of certain elements, and film grammar, film language evolves with that. So when a trope becomes too familiar to an audience, then it has to be changed. But we do, as filmmakers, avail ourselves of that common language. We build on that understanding. Our audience has seen many films and they understand that language,” he said. Despite a lively online discourse around Nolan’s latest, The Odyssey currently holds a solid 94% critic rating and a 97% audience score on Rotten Tomatoes. The Odyssey follows Odysseus (Matt Damon) through the incredible trials and mythical encounters he faces on his decade-long journey home to wife Penelope (Anne Hathaway) and son Telemachus (Tom Holland) after the Trojan War. The film also stars Zendaya, Robert Pattinson, Charlize Theron, Lupita Nyong’o, Jon Bernthal, Benny Safdie, John Leguizamo, Elliot Page, Himesh Patel, Bill Irwin, Samantha Morton, Jesse Garcia, Will Yun Lee, Rafi Gavron, Shiloh Fernandez, Mia Goth, Travis Scott and more. articles.title: Gregg Araki Is “Not A Big Supporter” Of AI, But Found It Useful For Editing This ‘I Want Your Sex’ Scene: “Literally Insane”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Dancing With The Stars’: ‘DWTS: Juniors’ Alum Kamri Peterson Joins Season 35 Troupe Christopher Nolan Calls Out “A Real Problem” In Amateur Film Criticism Ariana Grande Exits West End’s ‘Sunday in the Park with George’ Revival Amid “Ongoing Public Scrutiny” View All August 2, 2026 3:40pm Chase Sui Wonders and Cooper Hoffman in 'I Want Your Sex' Magnolia Pictures With his first movie in more than a decade, Gregg Araki found himself working in a whole new era of Hollywood to bring I Want Your Sex to the big screen. Discussing his new erotic comedy thriller, now playing in theaters, the co-writer and director explained to Deadline how AI tools were particularly useful in post-production on one scene of dialogue filmed with stars Cooper Hoffman and Chase Sui Wonders on a mini golf course next to a freeway. “For me, one of the coolest things is the technology is so advanced now and it really makes it so filmmaker friendly,” he explained. “I remember talking to Rick Linklater about this; back in the old days, when I was making Three Bewildered People [ in the Night ] and he was making Slacker , it was really just fucking hard to make a movie, just technically hard with 60 millimeter and loading magazines and torn sprocket holes and tape slices, and all of the stuff that we had to go through. You had to be kind of a crazy obsessive person to even try to make a movie.” Related Stories Festivals ‘I Want Your Sex’s Cooper Hoffman & Chase Sui Wonders On Why Their Unhinged Threesome Scene “Felt Tragic” — Sundance Studio News Gregg Araki Reveals ‘Now Apocalypse’ Season 2 Was Written For Starz, Mirrored Show’s Cancellation: “So Prophetic” Araki continued, “Whereas now, with the technology and the crazy sensitive cameras and iPhones and all of the software, all the things you can do—I’m not a big supporter of AI in terms of replacing actors and writers, but in terms of the tools you can do in post, there’s stuff that we did in I Want Your Sex . We shot that entire mini golf scene literally next to a freeway. It’s so loud in the rough cuts and stuff, but with tools that are available now in post, it’s like you can hear crickets whenever we’re mixing it. It was literally insane the way these things can work, and the same with the editing stuff, it’s amazing. The effects, all that stuff is really being kind of revolutionized in a way that makes all of that stuff accessible to indie lower budget filmmakers.” Watch on Deadline With the success of indie films like Obsession serving “shocks to the system” of a big-budget, IP-driven industry, Araki is “excited for the future” of Hollywood. Co-writer/director Gregg Araki on the set of ‘I Want Your Sex’ “It’s just crazy times, everything’s so upside down. And for indie film too, it’s really hard to get distribution. It’s hard to get indie film finance, but it’s always been hard, so it’s always a struggle, different struggles,” explained Araki. “I’m personally kind of excited for the future, I think. I do think that a lot of the old formulas aren’t really working anymore. I think Hollywood’s really sort of scrambling—it’s kind of like the Titanic, people just kind of running around. So, the rules are really being rewritten.” Co-written by Araki and Karley Sciortino, I Want Your Sex stars Olivia Wilde as dominatrix Erika Tracy, an artist and provocateur who enlists her assistant Elliot (Hoffman) as her sexual submissive. articles.title: Phil Collins Says He Nearly Died From Alcohol Abuse:  “I Was Very Lucky”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Tom Tapp Tom Tapp Deputy Managing Editor More Stories By Tom RFK Jr. Clashes With CNN’s Dana Bash About Covid, Fauci, Vaccines & Autism Phil Collins Says He Nearly Died From Alcohol Abuse: “I Was Very Lucky” ‘Dancing With The Stars’: ‘DWTS: Juniors’ Alum Kamri Peterson Joins Season 35 Troupe View All August 2, 2026 6:44pm Phil Collins on stage with Genesis for the band's final tour in 2022 Thomas Coex/Getty Images “I’ve been sick, I mean very sick,” Phil Collins said last year in an interview with MOJO magazine. Now, the Grammy winner is offering details about that illness, especially about his battle with alcohol. Collins has been open about his medical struggles in recent years , previously revealing that he suffers from Type 2 diabetes and complications from a 2007 spinal injury. In January, the former Genesis drummer noted he was under 24-hour care and has also said that he could no longer hold his drum sticks properly without feeling pain, even taping his sticks to his hands to get through later gigs. He also experienced kidney issues and underwent five operations on his knee. Related Stories News Rock & Roll Hall Of Fame Class Of 2026: Phil Collins, Iron Maiden, Billy Idol, Luther Vandross, Celia Cruz, Wu-Tang Clan & More News Phil Collins Says He Does “Contemplate” Performing Live Again: “I Can’t Really See It Happening, But I’m Healthier Now Than I Had Been For Quite A While” Those kidney issues, it seems, were related to his abuse of alcohol. Watch on Deadline In a new interview with the Sunday Times, Collins detailed just how bad it got. “My kidneys were packing up, my organs were just seizing up,” Collins said of being admitted to the hospital in late 2023, about a year after his last tour with Genesis. “People were coming to say goodbye. But I don’t remember them coming. I didn’t have no idea this was going on. They were all worried that they wouldn’t see me again. It could all have gone so terribly wrong.” The Oscar winner had previously said he “spent months in the hospital.” Now, he has revealed that he almost didn’t make it out. “There were some decisions to be made about, ‘Do we keep Phil on life support?’ kind of thing,” he said. “I was very lucky to have come out of that,” said Collins. “Needless to say, I haven’t had a drink since.” Collins is set to be inducted into the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame as a solo artist on Nov. 14 at Los Angeles’ Peacock Theater. He was previously inducted as a member of Genesis. Nimrat Kaur ( The Lunchbox , Dasvi ), Roshan Mathew ( Choked , Kappela ), Kavya Trehan ( The Royals ) and Pavan Malhotra ( Tabbar , Fouja ) will take on lead roles in the eight-episode Hindi-language series, which is from Select Media Holdings and Chalkboard Entertainment . Prashant Nair ( Umrika , Tryst with Destiny ) is the director and Pratik Khanuja, Sameer Chand, Vikesh Bhutani and Shujaat Saudagar are the producers. Coming out of the Amazon streamer’s Indian office, the show explores ‘pig butchering,” scams that involve perpetrators spending weeks or months building fake trust and false intimacy with victims online before draining them of money. Prime Video is billing it as a “gripping survival drama that exposes the dark machinery behind one of the world’s fastest-growing criminal enterprises.” Prime Video remains one of India’s more popular streaming services, and has rolled out a significant originals strategy through series such as Paatal Lok , The Traitors , Dupahiya , Mirzapur , Farzi and The Family Man and movies including The Mehta Boys , Maja Ma and Ammu . The service announced a huge slate of originals earlier this year, though Job Trafficking had not be unveiled at that time. In May, Amazon merged India free streamer MX Player with Prime Video, which it claimed created the country’s largest streaming service. This effectively marked the end of the Amazon M X Player brand. articles.title: Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Woody Harrelson Honor & 25th Anniversary Screening For Oscar Winner ‘No Man’s Land’
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Melanie Goodfellow Melanie Goodfellow Senior International Film Correspondent @mel_goodfellow More Stories By Melanie Australia’s ‘Better Man’ & ‘Eden’ Production House Forte Corp Pictures Hires Former Matchbox Exec Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Woody Harrelson Honor & 25th Anniversary Screening For Oscar Winner ‘No Man’s Land’ ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker, Gary Oldman, Mattel Studios President Robbie Brenner Join TIFF Market Talks View All August 3, 2026 1:48am Woody Harrelson Mark Seliger The Sarajevo Film Festival will honor Oscar-nominated actor Woody Harrelson at its upcoming 32nd edition later this month. Harrelson will receive the festival’s Honorary Heart of Sarajevo Award in recognition of his outstanding contribution to the film industry and acting career, following in the footsteps of recent recipients such as Stellan Skarsgård, Paolo Sorrentino, Meg Ryan, Alexander Payne and Lynne Ramsay. “Woody Harrelson is one of those actors you believe in even in the most improbable roles, while at the same time you can easily imagine him as someone you might spend time with every day,” said Sarajevo director Jovan Marjanović. Related Stories Festivals Diego Luna To Receive Honorary Heart Of Sarajevo Award Festivals Sarajevo Film Festival Unveils Full Competition Lineup “That remarkable ease of performance is, in fact, one of the hardest qualities to achieve on screen, yet he delivers it film after film. His talent, charisma, and boldness serve as an inspiration to many future generations. It is our great honor to present him with the Honorary Heart of Sarajevo.” Watch on Deadline Harrelson has historic links to the festival as co-star of Michael Winterbottom’s 1997 film Welcome to Sarajevo , which premiered at Cannes and then also screened at the 3rd Sarajevo Film Festival, less than two years after the end of the siege of the city. The film – a powerful examination of war in Bosnia in the mid-1990s and the role of journalists in its media coverage – will screen in the festival once again as part of the open air programme. Harrelson played ego-driven American reporter Jimmy Flynn. Harrelson has earned three Academy Award nominations, including Best Actor for The People vs. Larry Flynt and Best Supporting Actor for The Messenger and Three Billboards Outside Ebbing, Missouri , and starred in Ruben Östlund’s Palme d’Or winner Triangle of Sadness . He next leads Apple TV’s Brothers alongside Matthew McConaughey, premiering September 23, and stars opposite Kristen Stewart in Quentin Dupieux’s Full Phil , which premiered at Cannes this year. He recently wrapped Netflix’s The Cackling of the Dodos with Sam Rockwell and is producing a documentary on Austin’s iconic Armadillo World Headquarters. Harrelson wrote, directed and starred in Lost in London , the first feature film shot in a single continuous take and broadcast live to theaters. An Emmy Award winner for his iconic portrayal of Woody Boyd on Cheers , his television credits also include True Detective and The White House Plumbers . He has also distinguished himself on stage as an actor, writer and director, starring in the Broadway revival of The Rainmaker , the West End’s On An Average Day and Night of the Iguana , and directing his own off Broadway production Bullet for Adolf , which he cowrote with Frankie Hyman. In other Sarajevo news, the festival announced over the weekend that it will also be laying on a special 25th anniversary screening of a restored 4K version of Danis Tanovíc’s 2001 Oscar-winning feature No Man’s Land exploring the absurdity of war through the prism of the Bosnian War. The Sarajevo Film Festival runs from August 14 to 21. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Singapore’s Wave Films Taps Former Cambodian Broadcasting Chief Dave Ulmer To Drive U.S. Expansion Mouly Surya, Reza Rahadian & Prasanna Vithanage Among Filmmakers Selected For Busan’s Asian Project Market Korean Box Office Up 42% In 2026 H1, Driven By ‘The King’s Warden’ & Other Local Hits; ‘Project Hail Mary’ Tops Imports View All August 3, 2026 1:49am Yukino Kishii plays the character Makiko in her 20s & 40s Wowow EXCLUSIVE: Japanese broadcaster Wowow has announced that it’s producing a live-action series based on Riku Onda’s best-selling mystery novel The Aosawa Murders (Eugenia) , set to star Yukino Kishii , known internationally for her role in recent Cannes title All The Lovers In The Night . The six-episode series is scripted by Naoko Adachi ( What Did You Eat Yesterda y?) with Go Furukawa ( Kaneko’s Commissary ) as lead director. Hayato Kawai, whose credits include Disney+ series Gannibal , also directs. The series will premiere on Sunday, November 8, airing and streaming weekly on Wowow. Related Stories News Anne Watanabe & Jasper Pääkkönen To Lead Japanese-Nordic Noir Series 'Blood & Sweat' For Wowow, Nelonen, ICS Nordic & Boat Rocker Studios News 'Bye Bye, Earth' Anime Will Be Joint Production By Sony Pictures Japan, Crunchyroll, Wowow The story opens with a mass poisoning at the home of a prominent family in a Japanese coastal city and follows the impact of the event on a novelist, who was among the first at the scene and later wrote a book about the case; a blind girl who was the family’s sole survivor; and a writer investigating the case. Watch on Deadline Yukino Kishii, in her first role for Wowow, plays the role of Makiko Saiga – a woman who witnessed the mass poisoning at the age of eleven and later wrote a novel about it – and who freely changes her voice and manner of speaking depending on whom she is talking to Wowow has also revealed first-look photos of Kishii in this challenging role (see above) – showing her playing the character in two different time periods: in the 1980s when as a twenty-something Makiko went from door to door listening to the people whose lives the case had upended; and in the 2000s, now in her forties, when she is confronted about the truth of the case by a freelance writer. In addition to All The Lovers In The Nigh t, which premiered in Cannes Un Certain Regard and has sold widely internationally, Kishii’s credits include Small, Slow But Steady (2022) – for which she won several acting honours including Best Actress at the Japan Academy Film Prize – and Japan-Taiwan co-production Sinsin And The Mouse . Kishii commented on her casting in the series: “I had been reading Onda-sensei’s novels since junior high school, so the offer made me very happy – and put just as much pressure on me. When I heard the scripts would be by Naoko Adachi, who always renders the world from so many angles, I felt that with her I might be able to dive into this story.” Published in English as The Aosawa Murders , Onda’s 2005 novel Eugenia won the 59th Mystery Writers of Japan Award for Best Novel, and has sold a cumulative 380,000 copies in Japan. The novel has been translated into six languages (English, German, French, Spanish, Italian and Korean) and was selected as a New York Times Notable Book of 2020; featured among The Guardian’s best recent crime and thrillers of 2020; and won first place in the international category of the German Crime Fiction Prize in 2022. Naoko Adachi, who has adapted the novel, is one of Japan’s most highly regarded screenwriters. In addition to TV Tokyo hit series What Did You Eat Yesterday? , her credits also include NHK morning drama Welcome Home, Mone and upcoming historical drama Gyakuzoku no Bakushin . She also previously worked with Kishii on NHK’s Farewell Hospital (2024) and Farewell Hospital 2 (2026). Takeo Kodera, a producer for Kadokawa, which published the original Japanese version of the novel, brought the project to Wowow, which produced with the cooperation of Kadokawa Daiei Studio. Masaki Yamada, Chief Producer at the Drama Production Department of Wowow’s Content Production Division, said he was attracted to the work because: “The question is not ‘who did it?’ but ‘why do people go on being driven mad and damaged by this case?’’ — and there is that sense that the reader is somehow participating in the story.” Commenting on the adaptation, Onda said: “Since publication in 2005 I had received many offers to adapt the novel, including from overseas, so for the adaptation to be decided in the book’s 20th-anniversary year – just as the complete edition was published – is deeply moving.” Adachi commented: “I feel Eugenia is a story that drags readers and viewers out of the safe seat of the ‘bystander’. You are pulled into the case whether you like it or not, and as the story goes on you can no longer say for certain that what you saw is the truth exactly as you saw it.” Wowow is handling international rights to the series and will be presenting it to buyers at the upcoming TIFFCOM and ATF markets in Tokyo and Singapore later this year. articles.title: ‘Where Is Austin Tice?’: BBC & NPR Team On Podcast Unravelling The Story Of Journalist Who Disappeared In Syria In 2012
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Opens To $355 Million U.S. & $927M Worldwide, Second Best Start Of All Time At Box Office Read the full story By Max Goldbart Max Goldbart International TV Co-Editor @Goldbart1 More Stories By Max International Insider: Netflix’s $500M Zombie Gamble; The New Scottish Fest; Ngozi Onwurah On ‘Welcome II The Terrordome’ Alan Cumming-Backed Block The Merger Submits Evidence To UK Culture Sec; Argues WarnerMount Will “Directly Impact UK Documentarians’ Ability To Tell Diverse Stories” FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal View All August 3, 2026 4:00am BBC EXCLUSIVE: The BBC and NPR are teaming on a podcast about kidnapped American journalist Austin Tice . Josh Baker ’s Where is Austin Tice? sets out to answer questions in real time about the man who many consider to be the longest captive American journalist in history. The podcast, a rare co-pro between the BBC and NPR, will be on NPR’s Embedded feed from September 8 and will simultaneously comprise the third season of Baker’s I’m Not a Monster series for BBC Sounds and World Service. It will be hosted by Baker and investigative journalist Sara Obeidat. Related Stories News Jared Leto Allegations Are "Bellwether" Moment For MeToo In Hollywood, Says Producer Behind Explosive BBC Documentary Casting Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation 'You Are Here' For BBC & Starz Tice disappeared in Syria more than a decade ago and remains one of the biggest missing person cases of our time. His mother Debra insists her son is alive and has led a tireless campaign to bring him home — a campaign that continues to this day. He is thought to have been kidnapped by Syria’s regime led by the now-deposed Bashar al-Assad, making him the longest captive American journalist in history. Baker and Obeidat penned a BBC News investigation on the website last year that confirmed he was imprisoned by the Assad regime. Watch on Deadline The pod retraces Tice’s journey, allowing the audience to experience the investigation as it unfolds. It differs from the previous two seasons of I’m Not a Monster in that those cases were not unravelling in real time. The first series explored America’s Sam Sally, a mother who entered ISIS territory with her husband and children, and the second Shamima Begum, who joined ISIS as a teenager before trying to regain her British citizenship. Both have won numerous awards. “It is rare in journalism to have the chance to do work that might offer something tangible to a family while also showing the stark reality of the Syrian regime’s brutal dictatorship,” said Baker. “That possibility has driven us throughout — alongside a responsibility to the Syrians who trusted us with their stories and are still searching for answers about their own missing relatives.” Embedded senior supervising editor Katie Simon added: “When Josh and Sara first came to us with this story, we knew it was a rare opportunity to showcase immersive reporting about one of the most secretive regimes. The Austin Tice story gives us the chance to step into a once-hidden Syrian prison system and begin to piece together a play-by-play of Austin’s timeline from the moment he goes missing. It’s also a chance for two public media powerhouses to come together and make something new and meaningful in longform narrative journalism.” The podcast is written, showrun and presented by Baker and investigated and produced with Obeidat. It is series-produced by Simon Maybin and produced by Lucy Burns, with Clare Fordham as series editor for BBC News Long Form Audio. It was commissioned by Daniel Clarke for BBC Radio 4 and BBC Sounds. At NPR, the podcast was edited by Robert Little, who leads NPR’s Investigations team and Embedded ’s showrunner Simon. It was produced by Monika Evstatieva. The EP for Embedded is Irene Noguchi. BBC Studios is distributing the series. Jimmy Mulville , the Hat Trick Productions founder, has claimed that the BBC is “nervous” that Trump will accuse the UK broadcaster of malice if he is upset by jokes on its iconic topical comedy show. Mulville, who has been making Have I Got News For You for more than a quarter of a century, urged the BBC to remain calm in the face of threats from Trump. On the same episode, Mulville joked that David Ellison and his family had “bought an apartment up Trump’s ass a long, long time ago, and that’s where they live” as they attempt to close Paramount’s takeover of Warner Bros. The 500,000 square-foot campus in Astoria, Queens, is an historic studio facility where classic film and TV hits including Goodfellas and Sesame Street filmed, as well as contemporary shows including Succession and Just Like That , and movies including The Devil Wears Prada 2 . Today, the landmark studio comprises 11 soundstages and 325,000 square-feet of office and production support space. Shadowbox takes on management of Kaufman Astoria after a tumultuous period at the studios. In April, Deutsche Bank filed a foreclosure complaint against Kaufman Astoria Studios and its then owner Hackman Capital Partners, alleging a default on a $340 million loan that was due to be paid last fall. It starts managing the studios, which were originally built in the 1920s as the home of Paramount Pictures, from today. “We want to welcome producers to this incredible studio to be enriched by its history and the storytellers that have come before them at the same time as offering a top-tier customer service to meet the demands of today’s production needs,” said Mike Mosallam , Chief Operating Officer, Shadowbox Studios. He added: “Our team is looking forward to working with the on-lot staff to thoughtfully integrate the Shadowbox Studios standards of excellence. Whatever the production, we will work in partnership to make it seamless.” Shadowbox already runs studios in the U.S. and internationally. Shadowbox Atlanta is a nine-soundstage complex that has been home to Jumanji and Godzilla: King of Monsters . In the UK, there is Shadowbox Shinfield, an 18-soundstage facility that has played host to Star Wars: The Acolyte and Ghostbusters: Frozen Empire . It is currently developing a 10-soundstage complex in Queensland, Australia. articles.title: Charlie Hunnam Adopted Kittens While Filming ‘Monster’ to Decompress From “Darkest Realm” of Playing Ed Gein
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Beatrice Verhoeven Plus Icon Beatrice Verhoeven Awards Editor bverhoeven Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 10:30am Charlie Hunnam has earned Golden Globe, Actor, Critics Choice and Emmy nominations for his portrayal of Ed Gein in Monster: The Ed Gein Story. Photographed by Beau Grealy Charlie Hunnam didn’t hesitate to take on the role of serial killer and body snatcher Ed Gein in Ryan Murphy’s Monster: The Ed Gein Story. That is, until he started researching the horrific crimes that were committed. “Being confronted with some of those images of the crime scenes, I really started to get afraid of the darkness and what it was going to be like to inhabit that,” Hunnam tells THR . Then he got access to Gein’s medical records, which shed light on the factors that led to his declined mental state, marking a turning point for Hunnam. Thirty pounds lighter, with a prosthetic eyelid, a higher vocal octave and months of mental preparation, Hunnam became Gein. His dedication to the role scored the 46-year-old actor his first Emmy nomination, following Golden Globe, Actor and Critics Choice Award nods. Overall, the Netflix limited series received a total of seven Emmy nominations, including two for makeup, prosthetic and nonprosthetic. Related Stories TV How Rufus Sewell Found a TV Role Worth Staying For TV John Oliver Talks New "Prospective Business Daddies" and Colbert Support Group and Reveals HBO Contract Extension (Exclusive) Hunnam talks with THR about his first conversations with Murphy, committing to Gein’s voice and his most challenging scene. How much did you know about Ed Gein before signing on? I know a lot about other facets of the world of crime, like the Mafia and the Mexican drug war, but I don’t know as much about the serial killer subgenre and did not know anything about Ed Gein prior to my first meeting with Ryan, which I didn’t even know was to discuss Ed Gein. I thought it was just our mutual friend Max Winkler [who directed and executive produced the show] putting us together because they worked [together] a lot and Ryan had been asking Max a lot of questions about me. … We ended up having a three-hour, pretty engaged discussion about storytelling in general, but specifically more and more about the story he was telling. And then, at around the three-hour mark, he just sort of turned around and said, “I think you should play him. What do you think about that?” By that point, I was so taken with Ryan as a person. I was enjoying the conversation and being in his presence so much that before I knew what I had done, I said, “Yeah, that sounds like a great idea.” Did you have any hesitation playing Ed? Initially, I didn’t. The scripts weren’t available for a long period of time because that first meeting when I agreed to do it, Ryan was just breaking the first episode, and so then I set about wanting to learn everything I possibly could about Ed Gein and doing research on my own terms, and that ended up being the only moment in the process that was filled with fear and doubt because all of the texts that have been written about Ed are these pretty grotesque, sensationalized accounts of all the brutality and horrendous details of the things that he did, which were just terrible, and being confronted with some of those images of the crime scenes, I really started to get afraid of the darkness and what it was going to be like to inhabit that. There was a moment where I felt like maybe I’d made a mistake, and I was waking up in the middle of the night, really fearful of it, and just anticipating the process to be sort of pitch black. Then, there was a turning point where I was able to access his medical records, because he was incarcerated in a mental health facility for 30 years and did these biannual reviews, and the transcripts of all of those were not somebody else’s account who was sort of reveling in the darkness and depravity of the subject matter. It was a human being grappling with the regret of his actions and trying to understand why he did what he did, and trying to unravel this incredibly complex relationship with his mother [played by Laurie Metcalf]. And that brought me back to the original conversation I had with Ryan — that what he was trying to explore was what makes a human being into a monster. Charlie Hunnam as Ed Gein with Suzanna Son, who plays Gein’s girlfriend Adeline Watkins in the Netflix series. Courtesy Of Netflix I’d love to talk about your physical transformation. I was in fairly decent shape but wasn’t aware of just how thick I was. About three and a half weeks before we started shooting, I had my first costume fitting, and then being in those clothes, it was a really anxiety-inducing experience because I just didn’t feel like I looked right. When I put those clothes on, I realized I was so much bigger, fuller and healthier looking than Ed was. That was this horrendous moment where I thought, “Oh fuck, I’ve got to lose an enormous amount of weight.” I dropped 30 pounds in that three and a half weeks. … One of the things that I felt from the research that really had an impact on Ed was this eye that he had that had been described as a very flabby lid that hung over and gave him this somewhat tragic look in some angles and somewhat sinister in other angles. I thought it’d be a really great tool. So to Corey [Castellano], our wonderful makeup artist, I expressed that I wanted to do that eye, but we ran into a bit of a roadblock with Ryan, who just felt like it was going to be distracting unless it was done flawlessly. Then there was going to be an enormous amount of postproduction at great cost to make sure it was always fixed any time it didn’t look perfect, but I don’t think he necessarily knew just what an expert Corey is in his field, and so we did three tests of that before we finally convinced Ryan to let us do it. How long were you in the makeup chair for every day? We started at about an hour and a half, and then we got that down to about 45 minutes towards the end. You know, we did it once, and the application just got faster and faster. But you know, our wonderful hair department are pretty sort of obsessive, compulsive perfectionists, and so they also wanted to cut my hair every day. I got a haircut every single day just to make sure that the whole thing was tight and correct. What about the mental preparation? Your partner said that you spoke in the voice at home. Yeah. I didn’t think there were any recordings [of his voice]. I actually found a recording, but not until a week before we started to shoot. So a lot of that was invention. The starting point was understanding the consequence of being isolated and having no social group and only having interaction with one person, and then that person, his mother, telling him every day of his life that she hated him, that he wasn’t born the daughter that she wanted. We’re all looking for acceptance, validation and love. I knew that later on in his life, a lot of the more bizarre areas of his behavior were an effort to become the thing that he thought that his mother wanted him to be, but I thought that the voice would be an interesting way to demonstrate that, and so just playing around in that higher vocal range and trying to be the daughter that he knew that his mother wanted him to be. Then I got the tapes and was like, “Oh my God, it’s nothing like how he actually spoke.” Some of the actual range and intonation I had intuited, I’d sort of gotten right, but he had a very deep and folksy type of rhythm to his voice. But at that point, I was committed, and so we just decided to go for it. Hunnam in the third installment of Monster . Courtesy Of Netflix You talking about how his mother treated him, that’s the whole debate of nature vs. nurture, right? If you look at genetics, what the scientists are starting to understand now, and I’m certainly no scientist, is that it’s really about epigenetics. It’s like, a predisposition is definitely not the same as a predetermination, and it’s almost impossible to understand genetics outside of environment. And so you might have a predisposition to do something, but unless that is triggered by some sort of trauma or collection of events that are presented in your environment, it’s not necessarily going to manifest. And my sense was, Ed, he certainly had mental illness. He had dissociative personality disorder, which was presumably developed later in life as a consequence of trauma, but he was born with schizophrenia, and then there’s also all of the trauma, the isolation and the abuse, and it also seemed like he probably had some sort of psychological stunting that he probably had the mental age of somebody more like 12 or 14, which I don’t know if that was [something] that he was born with, or if it was a consequence of arrested development due to some big trauma in his life. Which scene was the most challenging for you? I was very excited by this idea that at the heart of the show is going to be a sincere exploration of mental illness. There tends to be one scene in any given show or movie that is the sort of thesis [or] mission statement, and to me that was the scene when Ed gets his diagnosis in episode seven, and so that scene always felt more important, that we were really going to define and declare who Ed was, at least through our prism of understanding. That was the one that was the ticking time bomb in the back of my mind, where I just kept thinking, “I can’t fuck this one up. This is the opportunity to articulate everything that I think that I know about this character,” and I was really scared to do that scene. I [read] it the first time, and then decided I was just going to not look at it too much. … We did two takes, but Max only used the first take in the show. Did you add your own improv to any of the other dialogue or did you pretty much stick to the script? Ryan was so kind and generous to me. Early on, he called me and said he was so happy that I was doing the show, and he said, “I really just get a sense from you that you’re going to go all the way with this, and I want to give you all of the latitude and authority to be able to make this your own. So, I’d like you to come on and actually be an executive producer and not just a vanity credit, but work with Max and actually operate in a producorial capacity on the show,” because he knew that I produced a few things, actually, like hands-on, really produced. A lot of actors get credits with absolutely no producorial responsibility, and I myself have received that before, and always feel a little guilty about it because producing is a really hard job. But that’s all to say that Ryan gave me huge latitudes to make it my own, and their dialogue is so damn good that there was never really any reason to go off book. But I did find myself just having such a good time being inside that character, which is crazy to say because I was really hyper aware of that it was a real person. We have a lot of responsibility in that, and he also did terrible things and there were really terrible real life consequences to a lot of human beings that came into contact with him. But at the same time, there was something in really wanting to challenge myself and just surrendering to having the experience of being that person, that felt artistically really satisfying and kind of liberating. It was like so far away from me that I was able to sort of get lost in it, and would find the creative process enjoyable. That I thought that I knew so much about him, had such a clear idea of my perception of him that I was able to just play in the scenes. And so I did end up improvising quite a lot while also trying to honor the material that was so good. Did you ever have to decompress after a scene? I adopted a couple of kittens while I was in Chicago for the second half of it, and I was staying in a really nice hotel. I mean, not all the time because we were out in the middle of nowhere, and some of the accommodation was like truly horrendous. But while we were in actual Chicago, I was staying at the Four Seasons because Max, the director, had a friend there who got a decent rate, and I wanted to be close to Max because I knew we’d be talking a lot. So I had this like really lovely room in the Four Seasons, and they were so kind to me. And I came home one day, I’m like, “listen, I know this is a wild card, but like, I just adopted these two kittens. Can I can I keep them in my room?” And they were like, “Yeah, tell us anything you need.” I’m a very serious pet owner. I had to hire a cat sitter because obviously I work 14, 15 hours a day. I wasn’t going to just leave them alone for that period of time, and so then I had a cat sitter with them for like eight hours. They went from the streets to really coming up in life and living that Four Seasons life with a full time cat sitter playing with them. So I would go home from the darkest realm and just literally play with kittens for three hours. What is your response to people calling true-crime shows like this sensationalism? I’ve not had to answer that question very much, and sort of gratefully so. I think Ryan gets asked that question a lot, and I would say probably my media training would say that’s a question for Ryan, but that’s not my answer. I would say, we are tasking ourselves with finding the truth of the human condition, and it’s not necessarily my job to judge the value or potential consequence of it. I think it’s my job, if we’re going to tell a story like this, to really sincerely find the truth of it, and that was an obsession. I have a horrible memory, so I would not claim this at the moment, because even 18 months past the experience, I’ve forgotten a lot. But like, I would have taken the Pepsi Challenge against any other Ed Gein scholar in the world going into this. I read everything . I read all of his court documents, all of his medical history, every single book that’s been written on him. I watched all of the movies. I only say that in there’s a fine line between sensationalism and finding the truth, and I never wanted to tip over into sensationalism. To me, the obsession was like, let’s find the truth of who this guy was, and then let the audience decide how they feel about him. I couldn’t afford to have really any strong judgment. I did initially go into all of the research, I was so repelled by it, but I just kept moving forward, and trying to just learn as much as I could, and then try to bring that truth to bear with as little judgment as possible. This story first appeared in a July stand-alone issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine. To receive the magazine,

articles.title: Netflix’s New Releases Coming in August 2026
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 12:00pm Clockwise from top left: 'The Last House,' 'Mourinho,' 'The Whisper Man,' 'Tires,' 'MLB Field of Dreams,' 'My Brilliant Career,' 'Ricky Gervais' Alley Cats' and 'Outer Banks.' Netflix A potty-mouthed project from Ricky Gervais; Wagner Moura and Greta Lee trapped indoors; a behind-the-memes look at Jose Mourinho; a third season of Shane Gillis’ popular workplace comedy; a return to the Field of Dreams; a helping of Aussie period drama; the final chapter of OBX ; and a star-studded crime thriller top-lined by Robert De Niro are among the new film and TV highlights to hit Netflix in August. Netflix regular Ricky Gervais returns with a new project on Aug. 7, the adult animated comedy Alley Cats. The British comedian really divides opinion (some think he’s a genius talking truth-to-power and others a frightful bore who owes a lot of his reputation to the writing skills of Stephen Merchant). THR is not really making any judgements here, but we know Alley Cats will likely attract a lot of views as it features Gervais’ trademark foul-mouthed humor. The premise isn’t all that deep, its a bunch of feral alley cats swearing a lot. Each to his own. Related Stories Business Anne Sweeney Steps Down From Netflix Board Business Netflix Sued For $105 Million After Hard Drive of Unreleased Nicolas Cage Movie Was Stolen From Its Office Aug. 7 sees the release of the intriguing sci-fi thriller The Last House . Directed by French filmmaker Louis Leterrier ( Now You See Me and Fast X ) and written by Matthew Robinson ( Love and Monsters ), the film stars Greta Lee and Wagner Moura as a couple who with their two children find themselves trapped inside their house due to a looming threat and must band together to find a way out. The Special One is back on top! Jose Mourinho is about to start the new soccer season as coach of Real Madrid and just ahead of his debut at one of most famous club sides in the world we have a three-part documentary about the living legend. From the team behind Beckham , Mourinho hits Netflix on Aug. 11, and captures the remarkable story of soccer coach who has won everything there is to win in Portugal, England, Spain and Italy and also has side hustle in creating viral memes (he’s the guy behind this and the phrase, “If I speak I am in big trouble.”). The doc features interviews with the likes of Sir Alex Ferguson, John Terry, Iker Casillas, Zlatan Ibrahimović, Didier Drogba, Marcelo, Samuel Eto’o, Javier Zanetti, Frank Lampard, Petr Čech and more. Comedian Shane Gillis’ time in the spotlight continues apace with the much-anticipated release of the third season of his series Tires on Aug. 13. The workplace comedy, that unsurprisingly takes place in a struggling Pennsylvanian tire shop, isn’t overly complex but is undoubtedly one of the funniest things on Netflix at the moment. Gillis and co-creators Steve Gerben, John McKeever have put together a great cast of oddball characters, including Stavros Halkias’ Dave and Thomas Haden Church’s Phil Jacobs. Other recurring performers include Andrew Schulz and Matt McCusker. The critics weren’t impressed but the audience loved it. If you don’t think too hard about it, you’ll have a great time. Also on Aug. 13, we have Netflix’s big live sports event of the month, the MLB Field of Dreams 2026. If you’re unfamiliar with the special game, the MLB plays a regular season game in a ballpark adjacent to Field of Dreams in Dyersville, Iowa. Yes that Field of Dreams , from the 1989 film starring Kevin Costner. It’s a bit gimmicky but fun nonetheless. This year the Minnesota Twins take on the Philadelphia Phillies. It’s all happening on Aug. 13, as we have another pick, this time our international pick of the month, the Australian series, My Brilliant Career. Some people maybe familiar with the Miles Franklin novel, others with Gillian Armstrong’s 1979 film adaptation starring Judy Davis and the late Sam Neill, which has become something of an urtext for Australian New Wave cinema and feminist cinema. This new six-episode adaptation, developed by Liz Doran, stars Philippa Northeast as the Sybylla Melvyn, a precocious 17-year-old living in rural Australia in 1900 who wants to become a writer. Alas her plans are disrupted by romance with Harry (Christopher Chung). On Aug. 20th, the Outer Banks saga comes to a likely epic conclusion, with the launch of the fifth and final season of the popular action/mystery teen drama. OBX , as the kids call it, has been something of a star factory for Netflix, producing the likes of rising stars Chase Stokes, Madelyn Cline, Madison Bailey, Jonathan Daviss and more, and the cast are back for one more run around with the final season in which the Pogues find themselves stranded in Morocco still mourning the death of one of their best friends and still trying to win their freedom. At the end of August, on the 28th to be precise, Netflix releases its most starry original feature film, James Ashcroft’s The Whisper Man. The crime thriller is based on Alex North’s bestselling book, and tells the story of a widowed crime writer looking for his abducted son, and asks for help from his estranged father, who also happens to be a retired former police detective. Together they “discover a connection to decades-old case of a convicted serial killer known as “The Whisper Man.”” The cast is genuinely the biggest draw for this project as it includes Robert De Niro, Michelle Monaghan, Adam Scott, Michael Keaton, John Carroll Lynch, Hamish Linklater, and Owen Teague. The film was written by Ben Jacoby and Chase Palmer. Movies added to Netflix in August include About Last Night…, Anaconda, Annie, Are We Done Yet?, Bride of Chucky, Cult of Chucky, Curse of Chucky, Seed of Chucky, Child’s Play 2, Child’s Play 3, Clueless, Daddy Day Camp, Daddy Day Care, Elysium, The Fast and the Furious, 2 Fast 2 Furious, The Fast and the Furious: Tokyo Drift, Fast Five, Fast & Furious, Fast & Furious 6, Furious 7, Field of Dreams, The Hitman’s Bodyguard, The Hitman’s Wife’s Bodyguard, Holmes & Watson, Marie Antoinette, Mile 22, Minions, National Security, Nightcrawler, Party Girl, Selma, Something’s Gotta Give, Speed, Speed 2: Cruise Control, Tears of the Sun, The Mortal Instruments: City of Bones, Zero Dark Thirty, Swiss Army Man, M3GAN, The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, The Shallows, Smurfs: The Lost Village, Eighth Grade, Five Nights at Freddy’s 2, Sing and Ingrid Goes West.
