articles.title: Savannah Guthrie Issues Emotional Plea for Answers in Mom Nancy’s Disappearance After Release of Ransom Notes
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 1, 2026 12:58pm Savannah Guthrie and her mother, Nancy Guthrie, on the ‘Today’ set. Nathan Congleton/NBC Savannah Guthrie shared another emotional message Saturday morning, marking six months since her mother, Nancy Guthrie , went missing, as authorities continue to search for answers in the case. Her post came after the Pima County Sheriff’s Department released two ransom notes allegedly sent by her kidnappers shortly after Nancy’s disappearance in hopes of generating new leads. Guthrie shared a photo of her mother, 84, alongside a lengthy caption, writing, “Six months ago, someone took her out of her bed in the dead of night. We have lived every moment, every breath, and every heartbeat in agony and despair ever since. Every day, we wake up and try to be strong and go on — because that’s what our joyful and resilient mom taught us to do.” Related Stories TV Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie Case Releases Ransom Notes: "She Perished Shortly After She Was Taken" TV The Reporter Who Won't Give Up on the Nancy Guthrie Kidnapping Story “But make no mistake — our hearts are in ruins. Cam and Kristine, Annie and Tommy, Mike and me — we spend every waking moment thinking of her, longing for her, looking for her,” she continued. “There is a hole inside us that can never be filled. There is an ache that cannot be softened. And there is a determination in us that cannot be quenched — to find out what happened to her, so that we can give her the dignity of a proper goodbye — a celebration of her remarkable life that she so deserves.” The Today co-anchor went on to plead for anyone with information to come forward, emphasizing that a reward remains available. “We are begging for help. We are desperate. We need someone to come forward,” she wrote. “Someone knows something. Someone suspects something. Someone recognizes the writing in the ransom demand notes. Someone has noticed something different, strange, troubling or just unusual — perhaps with someone they deeply love.” Savannah added, “Perhaps they are afraid to come forward. Perhaps they are conflicted. Perhaps they are angry or upset for being in this situation. There is a way out — to tell what you know. You can do so anonymously. The reward is available. There is a way to end this situation and do the right thing.” She concluded by asking for continued support as her family searches for answers. “We will never stop looking for answers — and we will never stop looking for the light,” she wrote. “We will always be hoping and praying and believing in the best of our world — in spite of circumstance. This is what our faith makes possible. Please. Bring her home.” Nancy was reported missing on Feb. 1 after authorities said they believed she was abducted from her home outside Tucson, Arizona. She was last seen the evening of Jan. 31. Earlier this week, the Pima County Sheriff’s Department released two ransom messages that were purportedly sent by those who kidnapped Nancy to KOLD-TV shortly after she disappeared. The first, delivered Feb. 2 and addressed to Savannah, claimed Nancy was “safe but scared” and demanded between $4 million and $6 million in Bitcoin for her release. A second note, emailed to the station’s tips line on Feb. 6, claimed the kidnappers “did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition,” adding, “She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this and hope you can all find peace. We are truly sorry.” Investigators have not announced any arrests or identified an official suspect. The initial deadline for the first ransom demand was Feb. 5 ($4 million), while a second demand set a deadline of Feb. 9 ($6 million). Messages of support poured into Guthrie’s comments from celebrities including Kristin Chenoweth, Ross Mathews, Monica Lewinsky, Karen Fairchild and Today With Jenna & Sheinelle co-host Jenna Bush Hager. See Savannah’s full post below. View this post on Instagram THR

articles.title: Vincent Pastore, the Mobster “Big Pussy” on ‘The Sopranos,’ Dies at 80
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 1:47pm Vincent Pastore Michael Loccisano/Getty Images Vincent Pastore, the Bronx-born actor who portrayed Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero, the mob informant who winds up sleeping with the fishes, quite literally, on The Sopranos , has died. He was 80. Pastore was found dead by Steve Villano, the actor’s self-described “right-hand man,” in his Bronx home on Saturday, he told The Hollywood Reporte r. He apparently died in his sleep, he added. The son of a real-life wiseguy, he said, Pastore made a living running and owning bars and nightclubs for two decades and didn’t get into acting until he was 42. Yet by the time he was done, he had appeared in nearly 200 movies and TV projects — most often as an Italian American bad guy — and twice in singing roles on Broadway. Related Stories Movies Richard L. O'Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer, Dies at 96 General News Angela Wales Kirgo, Longtime Writers Guild Foundation Executive Director, Dies at 78 After landing bit parts in films including Martin Scorsese ‘s GoodFellas (1990) and Brian De Palma ‘s Carlito’s Way (1993), Pastore was impressive as the right-hand man of Alan Arkin ‘s mob boss in the comedy The Jerky Boys (1995) and as the caporegime Angelo Ruggiero opposite Armand Assante in the acclaimed 1996 HBO telefilm Gotti . Sopranos creator David Chase hired him for the role of Sal — the character wasn’t even known as Big Pussy yet — soon after he auditioned for the HBO drama in 1998. It came down to Pastore and Johnny “Roast Beef” Williams, the actor recalled in 2022 on Chazz Palminteri’s podcast . The gregarious Pastore said he “did his research” and discovered that “Big Pussy was a real guy in Jersey. He was tall and thin, out of Newark, he was friends with Frankie Valli, and there was a Little Pussy, [who] wound up being the rat in the family,” he noted. Why was the guy nicknamed Big Pussy? “Because he was a cat burglar, like Cary Grant ,” Pastore said. After Sal gets nabbed by the FBI on The Sopranos , he chooses to become an informer to avoid life in prison. He is soon sniffed out, however, and his fate is sealed when he appears to Tony ( James Gandolfini ) as a talking fish in a dream . On the second-season finale, “Funhouse,” Sal is gunned down on a boat by Tony, Paulie ( Tony Sirico ) and Silvio ( Steven Van Zandt ) and dumped overboard. Pastore, who had appeared in 21 of the show’s first 26 episodes, was extremely popular with viewers; he would show up four more times in flashbacks or dreams through the series’ 2007 conclusion. Even though he was no longer on one of TV’s hottest shows after getting whacked, he said he looked at the bright side as he was flying to Los Angeles for the first time to make a movie, Deuces Wild (2002). “I was 50 years old … and I’m on a plane and I’m going to work,” he told Palminteri. Vincent Pastore with Sopranos castmate Tony Sirico in 2012. Eric Reichbaum/Everett Collection Pastore was born in the Bronx on July 14, 1946. His father, John, was a bookmaker who had to give up that business in order to get married — the family of his future wife Natalie insisted — but resumed making loans when he retired from his job as a school custodian. The family lived in an apartment above a social club in New Rochelle, New York. After graduating from New Rochelle High School in 1964, Pastore enlisted and spent three years in the U.S. Navy and attended Pace University, where he switched his major from business to drama. But when he couldn’t find acting work, he focused on the club business around New York, starting in 1967. (He owned the Crazy Horse in New Rochelle and also drove a limo.) One night, actor brothers Matt Dillon and Kevin Dillon were at a place with him while The Pope of Greenwich Village was playing on the TV. “Matty said, ‘You could do the work that these guys are doing,’ pointing to [future Sopranos co-star] Frank Vincent and Tony Musante ,” he remembered. Pastore was hired to appear in the Sylvester Stallone -starring Gangster , directed by William Friedkin , but the project never went forward. He then made his professional acting debut in True Love (1989), starring Annabella Sciorra and Aida Turturro. Casting director Ellen Lewis saw him in that and put him in GoodFellas , and he was in Penny Marshall ‘s Awakenings in 1990, too. Pastore worked for Marshall again in Riding in Cars With Boys (2001) and with other top directors in Woody Allen’s Manhattan Murder Mystery (1993), Andrew Bergman’s It Could Happen to You (1994), Scott Kalvert’s The Basketball Diaries (1995), Sidney Lumet’s Night Falls on Manhattan (1996), Jim Abrahams ‘ Jane Austen’s Mafia! (1998), Norman Jewison ‘s The Hurricane (1999), Jon Favreau ‘s Made (2001), Guy Ritchie ‘s Revolver (2005) and Luc Besson ‘s The Family (2013). He was a leading man in the indies A Tale of Two Pizzas (2003), Heaven’s Messenger (2008), Dough Boys (2008) and Pizza With Bullets (2010) and still active recently, with a turn in the Neil Bogart biopic Spinning Gold (2023). On the small screen, Pastore sparkled in the 1997 CBS miniseries The Last Don , starring Danny Aiello , and showed up on everything from Law & Order , The Practice and Everybody Hates Chris to Blue Bloods , The Neighborhood , Gravesend and the soap operas One Life to Live and General Hospital . He participated in 2007 on Dancing with the Stars but withdrew after a week; was a contestant in 2008 on Celebrity Apprentice ; pitched a product that holds money, a “Broccoli Wad,” in 2011 on Shark Tank ; launched his own brand of tomato sauce; played in a rock band; had a podcast, Fuhgeddaboudit With Vinny Pastore ; and toured around the world with Michael Imperioli and Steve Schirripa in Talking Sopranos . Pastore did lots of stage work, and on Broadway he played Amos Hart in the 2007-08 revival of Chicago and the mob kingpin Nick Valenti in 2014 in Bullets Over Broadway . He studied acting at the HB Studios coming up and in recent years taught a workshop there. In 2014, he was diagnosed with prostate cancer. Survivors include his daughter, Renee; a sister, Sally; and a brother, Johnny. THR

articles.title: Vin Diesel Says ‘Fast Forever’ Is the “Best Script” He’s Read in Decades: “I Am Still Crying”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 1, 2026 3:54pm Vin Diesel at 'The Fast and the Furious' 25th Anniversary photocall at the 2026 Cannes Film Festival. Andreas Rentz/Getty Images for Universal Pictures Vin Diesel is very pleased with the script for the 11th Fast & Furious film. Diesel took to Instagram on Saturday to share that he’s read the script for Fast Forever , which is slated to release in theaters in 2028 from Universal . In a caption accompanying a trailer for the upcoming theatrical re-release of the original The Fast and the Furious , racing back into theaters on Aug. 21 for its 25th anniversary, the actor wrote: “I just read the Fast Forever script by [Michael Lesslie]. It is the best script I have read in decades. I am still crying.” Related Stories Movies Joyce Carol Oates Defends 'Odyssey' Against Translator's Viral Slam: "Crude Language of MAGA Folks" Movies 'The Odyssey' Holds Strong for Big Second Weekend of $87M, Passes $600M Globally He added, “When March 17th 2028 comes… you will thank God you got to see the first one in the theaters this summer.” Fast Forever will follow 2023’s Fast X, directed by Louis Leterrier. A sequel to Fast X was originally expected to open in theaters in spring 2025 before being delayed. The film starred franchise regulars Michelle Rodriguez, Tyrese Gibson, Ludacris, Jordana Brewster and Sung Kang, alongside Jason Statham, John Cena, Helen Mirren, Charlize Theron, Jason Momoa, Brie Larson and Alan Ritchson. Diesel, who is best known for portraying franchise leader Dominic Toretto, announced in February 2024 that the next film would serve as the finale . Last year, the actor revealed at FuelFest , an automotive event organized by Paul Walker’s brother Cody Walker, that the next movie would mark a “return to the car culture, to the street racing.” He also teased a reunion between Dom and the late Paul Walker’s character Brian O’Conner. “That is what you’re going to get in the finale,” Diesel said. Walker, who played Brian throughout the franchise, died in a car crash on Nov. 30, 2013, at age 40. Furious 7 was still in production at the time, so his remaining scenes were completed using CGI, archival footage and his brothers Caleb and Cody Walker as stand-ins. Fast & Furious franchise has grossed more than $7 billion worldwide. Peacock is also developing a TV series based on the films. View this post on Instagram THR

articles.title: Scott Hylands, Star of TV’s ‘Night Heat’ on Both Sides of the Border, Dies at 83
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Mike Barnes Plus Icon Mike Barnes Senior Editor mikebarnes4 Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 4:24pm Scott Hylands Courtesy Everett Collection Scott Hylands, who starred as the cynical Det. Kevin “O.B.” O’Brien on the 1980s cop show Night Heat , the first Canadian original drama series to simultaneously air in the U.S., has died. He was 83. Hylands died July 29, his son, Luke Hylands, announced . A longtime resident of Salt Spring Island in British Columbia, he was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukemia in October 2021. The Canadian actor had portrayed his share of villains and heavies in guest spots on U.S. television for about two decades when he returned north to star as a good guy — finally! — in Night Heat , filmed in Toronto. Related Stories TV Vincent Pastore, the Mobster "Big Pussy" on 'The Sopranos,' Dies at 80 Movies Richard L. O'Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer, Dies at 96 On the documentary-style series, conceived by onetime New York City detective Sonny Grosso — who with partner Eddie Egan helped bring down the “French Connection” drug-smuggling ring in the 1960s — Hylands portrayed the veteran cop O’Brien alongside Jeff Wincott as his younger, hot-headed partner, Frank Giambone. Meanwhile, Allan Royal played Tom Kirkwood, who writes about the pair in his “Night Heat” newspaper column (he’s also the series’ narrator). Each episode represented one shift in the show’s unnamed city and was shot between the hours of 6 p.m. and 4 a.m. The series ran for four seasons and 96 episodes, from January 1985 through January 1989, on CTV in Canada and in late night on CBS. (It often out-rated Johnny Carson’s Tonight Show in some markets.) From left: Jeff Wincott, Allan Royal and Scott Hylands in a promotional photo for ‘Night Heat.’ Alliance Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection Scott Hylands Douglas was born on Feb. 27, 1943, in Lethbridge, Alberta. His mother, Ruth, was a nurse and a math teacher; his father, Walter, was killed in action in 1945 during World War II. He attended Shawnigan Lake Boys School on Vancouver Island, graduated from the University of British Columbia in 1964 and then headed to New York, where he landed the lead in a 1965 off-Broadway production of Billy Liar . After several years in San Francisco with the American Conservatory Theater, he made his onscreen debut by starring as the deranged ex-boyfriend in Daddy’s Gone a-Hunting (1969), directed by Mark Robson and written by Lorenzo Semple Jr. and Larry Cohen . He spent the 1970s showing up in the films Slipstream (1973), Earthquake (1974) and The Boys in Company C (1978) and on episodes of such series as The Streets of San Francisco , Kung Fu , Harry O , Police Woman , Cannon , Medical Center , Baretta , Wonder Woman and Police Story and in the 1978-79 miniseries Centennial . After Night Heat ended its run, Hylands worked on such shows as NYPD Blue , The X-Files , Due South , Stargate SG-1 , The Outer Limits , V , Once Upon a Time and Wynonna Earp . Perhaps most notably during this stretch, he played Ennis Stuccy, the stepfather of Carrie Coon’s Department of Homeland Security agent Gloria Burgle, on the third season of FX’s Fargo in 2017. In addition to his son, survivors include his wife of 36 years, Veronica, and his daughter, Rebecca. “I was lucky to have worked with him on my first big acting job,” Wincott told the Toronto Sun in 2021. “He taught me a lot. He was always prepared, professional, and he cared deeply about doing good work, a lesson and example I carried with me throughout my career.” THR

articles.title: K-pop Girl Group IVE is Ready for Their Next Big Adventure
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content K-pop girl group IVE. Courtesy of Starship Entertainment It’s a Tuesday in early spring, and the young women in IVE are gathered in what appears to be a warehouse turned studio near L.A.’s Arts District for a Vevo Studios shoot. The performers gather around a monitor playing back their most recent take. They watch the screen intently as makeup artists and hair stylists give quick touch ups. Earlier this year, the girl group put out their second studio album, Revive+ . The six-member outfit, comprising members Yujin, Wonyoung, Gaeul, Rei, Liz and Leeseo, kicked off their new era with the pre-release single “Bang Bang,” one of the two songs they’re performing for Vevo. Related Stories Music Sam Fender and Olivia Dean Have the Longest-Running No. 1 in U.K. History Music Grammys CEO "Saddened" Over BTS Decision to Not Submit for Awards There’s little downtime, with the group performing several takes of them singing and dancing live for the cameras, but the members of IVE find a few moments of rest. In those moments, they look less like the global superstars they undoubtedly are, and more like the young women they also are — playing with their phones and chatting amongst each other during their brief breaks. “We’re so enthusiastic,” says Wonyoung about being in Los Angeles. It’s hours later, and we’ve gathered in the basement of Live Nation’s Beverly Hills office. “We really love working in L.A., so we’re really happy.” At just 21 years old, Wonyoung has been an active K-pop idol for eight years, having won popular Korean music competition series Produce 48 at the age of 14 and joining the temporary girl group Iz*One, alongside fellow IVE member and the group’s leader, Yujin. The now-22-year-old was only a year older than her. IVE had plenty going for themselves as group when their first single “Eleven” was released in 2021 — two K-pop veterans with Wonyoung and Yujin, a powerhouse vocalist with the now 21-year-old Liz, a skilled rapper and songwriter with now 23-year-old Gaeul, a charismatic and charming rapper with the now 22-year-old Rei and an adorable singer and youngest member with the now 19-year-old Leeseo. It should come as no the surprise the group was a near-instant success. The group dominated domestic charts and toured the world, but they’re still getting new experiences, much like this Vevo shoot. “This is the first time that we’ve done anything like this in the U.S.,” Rei says. The rapper, perhaps IVE’s most online member, admits she’s watched other performances from the series online and the studio was smaller than she expected it to be. “We’ve done a lot of performances in Korea and filmed videos of ‘Bang Bang’ a lot,” she continues. “But it was a special performance.” Now, the group is back in the U.S. for their Show What I Am world tour, which lands Saturday (Aug. 1) in L.A. The group will return to the Kia Forum after last performing at the arena in 2024. The group comes back with new performances, including solo stages from each member — a continuation of the group’s decision to each have a solo song on Revive+ . Below, IVE speaks with The Hollywood Reporter about their latest music, touring, the realities of being a K-pop idol and what they’ve learned from one another. Can you tell me about your most recent single “Bang Bang? ” GAEUL “Bang Bang” symbolizes a new start for us, just like the title of our album, Revive+ . Do you feel a pressure to try new things ever? WONYOUNG More than a pressure, we really feel excited and like [there’s] a happy virus thing inside of us. [It’s] really less [about pressure] and more that [these] six girls can do it. Rei, Gaeul, Jang Wonyoung, An Yujin, Leeseo and Liz of IVE attend the media showcase for IVE’s second full-length album ‘Revive+’ on February 23, 2026 at YES24 Live Hall in Gwangjin-gu, Seoul, South Korea. HLL/Imazins via Getty Images You’ve been together for a while now. Do you feel anything has shifted for you as performers or as people? Does being an idol get any easier for you as time goes on? LIZ Inwardly, I don’t feel much different from when I was a student. I think because we did have to start working earlier on, we were able to reflect on that and learn new things. Leeseo, I’m particularly interested in hearing your experience with this. A lot of people your age are just starting to think about what the rest of their life looks like. You’ve already had a career for quite a long time now. How are you feeling about where you’re at right now? LEESEO Sometimes I do want to live a normal life like other people my age, but I feel like with the five members I have, this team, is just so fun. I’m really glad that I’m in IVE. I’m really satisfied with the music and the vibe of our group, so I’m really excited for the future. Your music has definitely evolved alongside you. Do you ever feel any anxiety or any excitement about trying new things? Do you have worries about losing the spark of what makes your music work for you if you try these new things? YUJIN Especially with “Bang Bang,” I was kind of worried because it really was a new genre that we haven’t tried before. But it got so much more attention and love than we thought [it would], so I think it’s worth it. We try hard to make our performances better and better, so I feel proud. Success tends to come with more eyes on you, whether that be fans or the general public. You’re young women — a lot of people are given more grace be young and do things, but everything you do is often looked at pretty critically. Do you ever feel misundersood? Do you ever wish people could see you differently? LIZ Something that I would want to do if there wasn’t so much pressure is freely travel and go about my everyday life. But with all the love that we receive, there’s risks that inevitably come with it, so I think it’s something that we have to accept. Many people can think what they want and they have their own impression of what IVE is. But if you end up caring about all of those opinions, then you can’t live your own life. We try not to care too much about what these other people think and just keep going. GAEUL There’s a lot of misunderstandings and some things can not be in our favor, but we still try our best in our own way. We believe that if we just keep doing what we want to do, then we’ll be able to go our own way. IVE members Rei, Gaeul, Jang Wonyoung, An Yujin, Leeseo and Liz. The Chosunilbo JNS/Imazins via Getty Images) Is there anything about how you all are together that would surprise people? WONYOUNG Maybe audiences see us on stage or during performance and [think] we’re [just] professional. But we’re just six girls or high school girlies, so that’s a fun part [of us people don’t get to see]. All versions of IVE might be a surprise, in a good way, because we’re just girls. You’re getting ready to go back out on tour. What does preparation look like? YUJIN I have such a good memories from our last tour. I really had fun, so I’m looking forward to it. I’m preparing a lot of medicine, so I don’t get a cold. Is there something your teammates have made you better at over the years? REI When we practice, we definitely give advice to help each other. For me, personally, during our debut there were a lot of things I didn’t know. Especially just Korean language-wise, so the members have really helped me. I’m the only foreign member, so sometimes it was a little bit lonely for me. But the members really took care of me. That really warmed my heart as the years went on. Last year, when KPop Demon Hunters was really popular, you posted a video of you doing the “I Am” choreography to “Golden.” That was very cute, why did you decide to do that? WONYOUNG We felt like there was a little coincidence between that song and our song, “I Am.” We felt like we could relate to that song, so we just made a cute video of our choreography and the Demon Hunters song. It was a good thing because people loved that set. When you’re preparing for a comeback or a tour, what’s the most important thing for you all? WONYOUNG Our health. Our health is the most important thing always, so we just try to get a lot of sleep and a lot of food. THR

articles.title: Gavin Newsom Reportedly Concerned About State Antitrust Suit Against Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 1, 2026 4:46pm California Gov. Gavin Newsom Heather Diehl/Getty Images Governor Gavin Newsom is concerned about the antitrust lawsuit filed by 12 state attorneys general led by California against Paramount ‘s $111 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery, and what it will mean for the entertainment industry, according to The Wall Street Journal . In a Friday report, sources told the WSJ that Newsom has said if the merger is blocked due to the lawsuit, state employment will suffer. The outlet also notes that “Newsom’s office has encouraged Attorney General Rob Bonta’s office, which has independent authority to file such suits, to find a resolution out of court.” Related Stories Movies 'Barbie' Sequel Stalled as Warner Bros. Tries to Reach Deals With Greta Gerwig, Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling TV Taylor Sheridan Returning for an On-Camera Role in 'Lioness' Season 3 Reps for Newsom and Bonta declined the WSJ ‘s requests for comment; The Hollywood Reporter also reached out to California’s governor for comment. On July 13, the states filed a lawsuit alleging that the merger would combine two of Hollywood’s top five studios, which would lead to higher prices, less movies in theaters and a decrease in the variety and quality of content. “There is no debate here: This merger will snuff out competition, drive up prices, diminish content quality, and produce fewer movies and shows each year,” said California Attorney General Rob Bonta at a press conference at the time. The filing of the suit led to a temporary pause on the merger, ruled by U.S. District Judge Araceli Martínez-Olguín on July 20; that temporary restraining order was subsequently extended on July 23. One day later, Paramount agreed to hold off on the acquisition until the court makes a decision of whether or not the deal violates antitrust laws. In a court document filed on July 24, Paramount said they will not consummate the acquisition until June 2027 or five days after the court issues a ruling on the case, whichever is earlier. Alongside California, Arizona, Colorado, Connecticut, Massachusetts, Minnesota, Nevada, New Jersey, New Mexico, New York, Oregon and Washington are involved in the suit. While organizations including Cinema United have shown support for the suit and actors Benedict Cumberbatch, Alan Cumming and Benedict Wong called on the U.K. to block the Paramount–Warner Bros. merger, Newsom is not the only democratic power player to reportedly push for a settlement. On Monday, Ari Emanuel, WME executive chairman and CEO of TKO, wrote an op-ed for the WSJ in support of Paramount’s acquisition of Warner Bros. “When government officials manipulate markets to reach political outcomes, antitrust stops protecting competition and starts threatening it,” Emanuel wrote. “The attorneys general should drop this case and get back to enforcing the laws as they are written. Let Hollywood creatives get back to trying to rip each other’s heads off at the box office, in streaming, online and everywhere else we compete. It’s what we’re best at.” THR

articles.title: ‘Wonder Man’ Star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II Reacts to Marvel Series Cancellation: “See You at the Emmys”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All August 1, 2026 5:00pm (L-R) Simon Williams/Wonder Man (Yahya Adbul-Mateen II) and Trevor Slattery (Sir Ben Kingsley) in Marvel Television's 'Wonder Man.' Suzanne Tenner/Marvel Television Logo text Marvel ‘s Wonder Man star Yahya Abdul-Mateen II is speaking out after the Disney+ series was un-renewed . The streamer picked up the series for a second season in March before reversing course and canceling the renewal on Thursday. The decision came as a surprise after Wonder Man had a solid debut on Disney+ in late January, drawing 618 million minutes of viewing time during its premiere week, according to Nielsen’s streaming ratings. While the show fell out of the top 10 original streaming titles after that, it continued to earn positive reviews from critics and audiences. Abdul-Mateen also received an Emmy nomination for his performance of the title character. Related Stories Movies Mahershala Ali Confirms He's Not Doing Marvel's 'Blade': "They Didn't Want to Do It" Movies Sadie Sink's Secret Role in 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Finally Revealed Following the cancellation, Abdul-Mateen took to Instagram to share his reaction. “Word just dropped that Wonder Man won’t be coming back,” he wrote in the caption. “That’s life, right? Everything will shake out.” The Candyman actor continued, “I wanted to say thank you to everybody who WATCHED the show, ENJOYED the show, and SHARED that they enjoyed the show in some way or other. The show worked. And that’s my favorite thing about it. I could see it on the faces of the Youtube Reactors (because I watched along with y’all this time. Shoutout to y’all) and I can see in the messages I get saying how the show reminded some of you not to give up, and I feel it in the genuine love shared when I bump into some of you all during the day. So, thinking of you all today. I’m glad we got to be a part of something cool.” View this post on Instagram He concluded his post: “Thank you for watching… And uhh… See you at the EMMYS.” Abdul-Mateen is nominated for best actor in a comedy series alongside Steve Carell ( Rooster ), Matthew Rhys ( Widow’s Bay ), Jason Segel ( Shrinking ) and Martin Short ( Only Murders in the Building ). Wonder Man co-creators Destin Daniel Cretton ( Spider-Man: Brand New Day, Shang-Chi and the Legend of the Ten Rings ) and Andrew Guest had also been set to return for a second season. They executive produce alongside Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige, Louis D’Esposito, Jonathan Schwartz and Brad Winderbaum, head of Marvel Television and Marvel Animation. Guest also served as showrunner, while Cretton directed several episodes. Ben Kingsley, X Mayo, Demetrius Grosse, Zlatko Burić, Arian Moayed, Olivia Thirlby, Dan Donohue and Kameron J. Meadows rounded out the cast. THR

articles.title: Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman Make Surprise Appearance at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Kirsten Chuba Plus Icon Kirsten Chuba Events Editor kirstenchuba Follow Sign Up View All August 1, 2026 9:01pm Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman promote "Practical Magic 2" during CinemaCon on April 14 in Las Vegas. Ethan Miller/Getty Images Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman are getting an early start on spooky season. The duo made a surprise appearance at a Cinespia screening of their beloved 1998 movie Practical Magic on Saturday night, arriving to screams from the crowd at Hollywood Forever Cemetery. “[ Practical Magic ] is [the] perfect movie to show at a cemetery,” Bullock said to the crowd, as Kidman added, “Thank you for all your support for getting this second film made that’s coming to you very soon.” They also introduced the sequel’s new additions in Joey King and Maisie Williams, sharing a toast among themselves and the audience. Related Stories TV Taylor Sheridan Returning for an On-Camera Role in 'Lioness' Season 3 TV A 10-Year-Old Budding "Hollywood Reporter" Gets Her First Red Carpet Experience, Interviewing the Stars of 'L.O.L. Surprise! The Next Headliner' The night helped stir up excitement ahead of the upcoming sequel , which sees Bullock and Kidman reprising their roles as orphaned sisters Sally and Gillian Owens. In the original, the two — raised by their witch aunts Aunt Jet (Dianne Wiest) and Aunt Franny (Stockard Channing) — embrace witchcraft after avoiding it most of their lives. The sisters work to learn how to use their powers to ward off a curse that threatens women in the family from finding love, and leaves men they fall in love with dead. Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman make a special appearance at a @cinespia screening of #PracticalMagic , alongside their sequel costars Joey King and Maisie Williams pic.twitter.com/kc3kRD0xNZ — The Hollywood Reporter (@THR) August 2, 2026 In Practical Magic 2 , set 25 years later, Bullock’s character now has two daughters — played by King and Williams — who have their own witchy abilities. King’s character discovers dark family secrets that plunge the Owens family into a crisis, and the women must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel them once and for all. Wiest and Channing have also returned for the follow-up, alongside other new additions Lee Pace, Xolo Maridueña and Solly McLeod. The Perfect Couple ‘s Susanne Bier directed the film, which hits theaters Sept. 11. Bullock and Kidman are producing the sequel alongside Denise Di Novi, who was also behind the 1998 movie. Practical Magic is also returning to theaters for one night only, on Aug. 11, in preparation for the new film. THR

articles.title: ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 12:16pm PT Critics Pick ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary Penny Lane's enchanting film turns the story of Flaco into a true-life nature fairy tale that's like the greatest children’s novel E.B. White never wrote. By Owen Gleiberman Plus Icon Owen Gleiberman Chief Film Critic @OwenGleiberman Latest ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary 14 hours ago ‘Tony’ Review: Dominic Sessa Gives His First Movie-Star Performance in Matt Johnson’s Tasty Biopic About the Young Anthony Bourdain 4 days ago ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Review: Tom Holland Returns in a ‘Mature’ but Arduous Adventure That for All Its Good Action Is Trying Too Hard 5 days ago See All David Lei “ Wild Inside ” is an enchanting movie, and a haunting one too. It’s a documentary about Flaco, the owl who escaped from the Central Park Zoo and spent a year living in the wilds of New York City. Since that story was widely covered when it happened in 2023, turning Flaco into an international media sensation, you might think: Why do I need to see a documentary about it? The answer is that Penny Lane, the gifted director of “Wild Inside,” has told this tale in a revelatory way, building it like an imagistic storybook from the ground up. From the moment that Flaco, on the evening of February 2, 2023, first appeared on a sidewalk near the corner of 50th St. and Fifth Avenue, standing there as still as a statue, he was surrounded by people filming and photographing him — civilians on their phones, then nature photographers, amateur and professional. Working with the editor Hannah Buck, Lane uses their endless archive of images to craft a true-life nature fairy tale. “Wild Inside” feels like the vérité version of the greatest children’s novel E.B. White never wrote. Related Stories 'Family Guy' Casts Kieran Culkin to Play the Devil in New Halloween Special for Hulu 'Ebenezer' Trailer: Johnny Depp Transforms Into Grouchy, Snowball-Throwing Scrooge As you watch the movie, Flaco becomes a true character , though there’s nothing cute about him, and the film has a philosophical ambiguity that takes you by surprise. It’s a movie about freedom and captivity, but it doesn’t have a simple or reductive message. Flaco, who lived in the Central Park Zoo for 13 years, escaped when someone cut the wire mesh on his cage. He was a Eurasian eagle-owl, a species that doesn’t exist in America, and when you look at him, he really is the living incarnation of the classic, mythological… owl . He’s stunningly beautiful, with big orange eyes set inside a regal head, and a body of tan and black and orange feathers that makes it appear that he’s wrapped inside the most luxurious comforter on earth. His wingspan is awesome (nearly six feet wide), but when Flaco is just standing there, which is most of the time, he does indeed look wise and inscrutable. To know what’s going on in that head, you have to read his actions. Popular on Variety The day after he made his first appearance on that midtown sidewalk, Flaco flew to Central Park and lodged himself high up in a tree near the south end of the park, just opposite the Essex House. What would happen to him? Representatives of the Central Park Zoo planned to recapture him, and they set about the task armed with mosquito nets, trying to tempt Flaco with food — the dead white lab rats he had eaten every day for 13 years. But Flaco wasn’t interested. He just stayed up in that tree. How would he survive? Tentatively, then with more confidence, he began to fly down into the park and hunt the real live New York City rats that roam there. His muscles grew stronger; his predatory instincts came to the fore. Within two weeks, he was living like a wild animal, though one who was so accustomed to being around humans that he had a way of standing on a branch as if it were his throne. The Central Park Zoo people gave up on trying to capture him. It’s only natural that the story told by “Wild Inside” triggers our liberal impulses. We think: Yes! Flaco is alive in the wild! He’s in a better place. The movie taps into what’s noble and valid and genuine about those feelings. Some of us actually have an aversion to zoos. Personally speaking, from the earliest age, I couldn’t stand them. I found staring at wild animals in captivity to be inexpressibly sad . Flaco is the animal hero who triumphs over the system of “benign” incarceration, becoming the apex predator of Central Park. And the more he thrives, and gets elevated to a kind of critter superhero status (Seth Meyers on his late-night show: “Every New Yorker dreams of moving out of their tiny shitty apartment into a nicer neighborhood. And Flaco Shawshanked out of that cage and did it!”), the more he becomes a symbol of what freedom means. After a number of months, he moves from Central Park to the East Village, and then to the Upper West Side, where we see him standing on air conditioners, and at times on elevated stone carvings in a way that’s very Batman. Residents will encounter him perched on the air conditioner just outside their apartment, staring in. From the outset, however, there are warnings in the other direction. Within a week, Flaco had triumphed over the doubters who feared that an owl raised in captivity wouldn’t have the strength or stamina to survive in the outside world. Yet it isn’t quite that simple. There have long been owls and hawks who live outside of zoos in New York, and there’s a fate that awaits them. They eat rats and mice, and in doing so they absorb the rodenticide that’s in the bodies of those creatures. Should Flaco have been recaptured and returned to his tiny environment within the Central Park Zoo? In the documentary, several knowledgable observers say that that would have been the most humane scenario — that had it happened that way, Flaco would be alive today, and would likely have lived for another 30 to 40 years. The probability of that is indisputable. What’s haunting about “Wild Inside” is that it inspires us to root for Flaco’s freedom, for the fullness of his life , in the spirit of “It’s better to burn out than to fade away.” Yet the ending that he comes to haunts us as well. He dies one day, out of the blue, by colliding into the wall of an apartment courtyard; that’s because his strength had been weakened by the rodenticide. What was the right choice? Maybe there was no right choice. “Wild Inside” is so moving because we’re stirred by the creature Flaco was, and it’s the story he lived that made him that creature. ‘Wild Inside’ Review: The Story of the Central Park Owl Becomes a Moving and Haunting Documentary Reviewed at IFC Center, New York, July 31, 2026. Running time: 96 MIN. Production: An HBO Documentary Films release of a Sandbox Films, Spinning Nancy production. Producers: Gabriel Sedgwick, Nickolas Hasse. Executive producers: Jessica Harrop, Caitlin Mae Burke, Lisa Heller, Nancy Abraham, Tina Nguyen, Julie Parker Benello, Patty Quillin. Crew: Director: Penny Lane. Camera: Naiti Gámez. Editor: Hannah Buck. Music: Carolina Eyck. With: Flaco, MJ Ansbro, David Barrett, Edmund Berry, JP Borum, Sheryl Checkman, Louise Bergmann, Mark Elliott, Anke Frohlich, Owen Klessel, David Lei, William Murray, Eitan Raitses, Juan Rosado, Jason Sander, Meg Spectre, Javier Torres. articles.title: Vincent Pastore, Who Played ‘Big Pussy’ on ‘The Sopranos’, Dies at 80
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 1:55pm PT Vincent Pastore, Who Played ‘Big Pussy’ on ‘The Sopranos’, Dies at 80 By Jack Dunn Plus Icon Jack Dunn Latest Vincent Pastore, Who Played ‘Big Pussy’ on ‘The Sopranos’, Dies at 80 14 hours ago Marvel, ‘Star Wars’ and DC’s Biggest Fans Discuss Why Their Favorite Franchises Are Struggling: ‘I’m Still Waiting for “Blade”’ 3 days ago Joyce Carol Oates Defends ‘The Odyssey’ and Slams Translator for Scathing Review: ‘Speaks in the Crude Language of MAGA Folks’ 3 days ago See All WireImage Vincent Pastore, who is best known for playing Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero on HBO’s “ The Sopranos ,” has died, according to TMZ . He was 80. Pastore was a key player on the first two seasons of “The Sopranos,” and helped deliver one of the mob drama’s most iconic moments. In the show, Big Pussy was part of Tony Soprano’s (James Galdofini) most trusted inner circle, until he started wearing a wire for the FBI. In the Season 2 finale, Tony, along with Silvio (Steven Van Zandt) and Paulie (Tony Sirico), makes the difficult decision to kill him off while out on a boat. articles.title: ‘It: Welcome to Derry’ Creator Says Season 2 Will ‘Not’ Shy Away From the ‘Horrible’ Cultural Themes of the 1930s: It’s the ‘Heart of Our Story’
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 2:29pm PT ‘It: Welcome to Derry’ Creator Says Season 2 Will ‘Not’ Shy Away From the ‘Horrible’ Cultural Themes of the 1930s: It’s the ‘Heart of Our Story’ By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘It: Welcome to Derry’ Creator Says Season 2 Will ‘Not’ Shy Away From the ‘Horrible’ Cultural Themes of the 1930s: It’s the ‘Heart of Our Story’ 13 hours ago Vin Diesel Says ‘Fast Forever’ Has the ‘Best Script I Have Read in Decades’: ‘I Am Still Crying’ 15 hours ago Richard L. O’Connor, Emmy-Winning Producer and ‘The Muppet Movie’ Executive, Dies at 96 17 hours ago See All Brooke Palmer/HBO As horror fans eagerly await the next chapter in Pennywise’s (Bill Skarsgård) horrifying reign of terror, “ It: Welcome to Derry ” co-creator Andy Muschietti has shared some details on the current status of Season 2. “We’re very excited, we’re in the writers’ room right now,” Muschietti confirms to Variety . The new season will take place in 1935, centering around one of the interludes in Stephen King’s “It” novel — the Bradley Gang Massacre. As recalled in the book, a group of outlaws hides out in the town of Derry while fleeing the FBI, robbing and murdering store owners and causing all-around chaos. It takes place 27 years before the first season of “It: Welcome to Derry,” which follows the mystery surrounding a young boy gone missing amidst a Cold War military plot. Related Stories Judge Pauses Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Paramount Agrees to Postpone Warner Bros. Merger Until After Antitrust Trial “There’s gonna be a lot of that depression-era hustling in the air in our characters. Everybody’s trying to get by and survive the circumstances. They are gonna do crazy things,” Muschietti says. “And of course, the social, cultural, horrible things that were happening in the era, too. We’re not going to skip those. [They are the] very center and the heart of our story.” Popular on Variety While “It” fans have become accustomed to the franchise’s focus on the horror that lurks underneath images of suburban comfort and kids riding bicycles, Muschietti says Season 2’s aesthetic will differ: “In this case, on the surface, Derry is a graveyard almost. It’s a carcass of something because people are depleted, poor, tired, jobless, homeless. The kids don’t have a suburban, comforting life. They’re in a very different situation. Some of them are orphans or runaways, and so the environment is pretty bleak. But there’s always the aspect of hope that is always there, burning, and it’s what keeps our new group going.” Going back another 27 years gives Muschietti and his creative team, including co-creators Barbara Muschietti and Jason Fuchs, more of a canvas to play with; after all, the ’30s interlude in King’s original novel doesn’t take up much of the overall story. But the family bloodline will help fans connect the different timelines. “There will always be the connection, there’s a family tree that appears,” Muschietti explains. Muschietti began exploring the world of Derry and Pennywise in the 2017 hit film “It” and its 2019 sequel “It: Chapter Two.” He previously told Variety of his three-season plan for “Welcome to Derry,” exploring the time periods of 1962, 1935 and 1908, respectively, with an interest in King’s interludes: “I realized there was a hidden story there, and that Stephen King was leaving crumbs that could guide us somewhere. It’s a story told backwards.” But the horror director and screenwriter still has his eyes set on adapting other King stories. “I cannot talk too much about it because some of them are [active] projects. One that I did touch that’s not a current project, but I would love to go back to at some point is ‘The Juant,’ which is a short story that blew my mind when I read it. I was 14 or something,” Muschietti says of the short story in King’s “Skeleton Crew” collection. “It just completely shattered me.” “It: Welcome to Derry” Season 1 is currently streaming on HBO Max. ‘X-Men’ Star Famke Janssen Says Marvel ‘Made a Mistake’ By Not Asking Her to Return as Jean Grey in ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ ‘Get Kevin Feige on the Phone’: Yahya Abdul-Mateen II on Taking Control of His Marvel Offer and What’s Next for ‘Wonder Man’ Robert Downey Jr. Says ‘Avengers: Doomsday’ Figured Out How to Make Marvel Movies ‘Not Be a Letdown’ After ‘Infinity War’ and ‘Endgame’ Sadie Sink’s ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Role Is So Secretive That She Didn’t Have an Audition and Never Saw the Script Until Flying to London ‘Heartstopper Forever’ Trailer: Kit Connor and Joe Locke’s Love Story Wraps Up in Netflix Movie Ryan Reynolds Says There Will ‘Eventually’ Be Another ‘Deadpool’ Movie: ‘There’s a Few Really Deep Cuts That I Think Are Missing’ Loading comments... articles.title: Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock Surprise Fans at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening in Hollywood Forever Cemetery for L.A.’s Cinespia
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 9:30pm PT Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock Surprise Fans at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening in Hollywood Forever Cemetery for L.A.’s Cinespia 'Practical Magic 2' stars Joey King and Maisie Williams led a 'Midnight Margaritas' toast By Angelique Jackson Plus Icon Angelique Jackson angelique814 Latest Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock Surprise Fans at ‘Practical Magic’ Screening in Hollywood Forever Cemetery for L.A.’s Cinespia 6 hours ago ‘Barbie’ Sequel Stalls as David Zaslav Won’t Approve Bigger Salaries for Ryan Gosling and Margot Robbie 18 hours ago Jon Bernthal on His ‘Brotherly Dynamic’ With Tom Holland in ‘Spider-Man’ and ‘The Odyssey,’ and Why Punisher Is Peter Parker’s ‘Cautionary Tale’ 2 days ago See All Getty Images for CinemaCon Sandra Bullock and Nicole Kidman made a surprise appearance at a screening of “ Practical Magic ” on Saturday night in L.A. Attendees came to the place, the Hollywood Forever Cemetery, for magic — and many, many Midnight Margaritas — but few expected an appearance by the Owens sisters themselves to introduce the 1998 cult classic. “Thank you so much for coming out tonight. Perfect movie to show in a cemetery,” Bullock, who stars as Sally Owens, said over the crowd’s roar of enthusiasm. “We should also thank the spirits that are floating around us as well because you’re on their seats.” Related Stories AMC Theatres Chief Adam Aron Pushes for Paramount Warner Bros. Merger, Says 'Thanks, but No Thanks' to State AG’s Blocking Deal Paramount Skydance Agrees to Link Merger Antitrust Case to Pre-Existing Paramount+ Subscriber Suit Kidman, who plays Gilly, added: “Thank you for all your support for getting this 2nd film made that’s coming to you.” Popular on Variety Then, Bullock introduced the “next generation” of Owens sisters: Joey King and Maisie Williams, who play Sally’s adult daughters in Warner Bros.’ sure-to-be-spellbinding sequel, in theaters Sept. 11. The duo sauntered on the screen with margaritas in hand. “To the coven,” Kidman said, proposing that the crowd — clad in all types of 90s witchy attire, from flowy black robes and pointy hats “Practical Magic” t-shirts — raise their glasses. “Maisie and I are so excited to be joining the coven as Kylie and Antonia,” King told the crowd. “We really hope you enjoy the new movie as much as we did making it.” View this post on Instagram “Practical Magic 2,” directed by Susanne Bier, “returns to a world steeped in moonlit mischief and powerful ancestral magic, as the Owens sisters must confront the dark curse that threatens to unravel their family once and for all in a must-see cinematic event of fun, magic and mayhem.” The new movie follows 28 years later, as Sally bakes cakes and avoids men, while Gilly attracts men named Chad on Tinder. But the Owens family’s 300-year-old curse carries one generation forward, striking Sally daughter Kylie’s and her lover (Xolo Maridueña), who gets hit by a car while bicycling with several bouquets of roses. Kylie is determined to reverse the curse by any means necessary, forcing Sally and Gillian to band together to keep her away from the darkness and break the spell for good. Lee Pace also stars in the film, with Stockard Channing and Dianne Wiest returning and Frances and Jet Owens, Sally and Gilly’s aunts. Akiva Goldsman and Georgia Pritchett wrote the script for the sequel, which is based on the 2021 novel “The Book of Magic” by Alice Hoffman, the fourth in her “Practical Magic” book series. Denise DiNovi, Bullock and Kidman produced the Warner Bros. film. Andrew Kosove, Broderick Johnson, Donald Sabourin and Hoffman serve as executive producers. The special “Practical Magic” screening was part of Cinespia ‘s annual lineup of exhibitions at the Hollywood Forever Cemetery. The outdoor screening series, which is celebrating its 25th anniversary, has “The Mummy,” a double feature of Mia Goth’s “X” and “Pearl,” “Coming to America” and a 40th anniversary showing of “Labyrinth” scheduled for the month of August. Cinespia is presented by Amazon MGM Studios and Prime Video. articles.title: ‘Hacks’ Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 11:58pm PT ‘Hacks’ Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First Awards Circuit Podcast: Also on this episode, Variety TV critic Aramide Tinubu shares her summer TV picks and Emmy nomination hot takes. By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest ‘Hacks’ Stars Hannah Einbinder and Paul W. Downs on the Legacy of ‘Hacks’ and Which Character Needs a Spinoff First 4 hours ago John Oliver Extends His HBO Contract to Continue ‘Last Week Tonight’ Through 2027 2 days ago ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Producers on Episode 2’s Surprise Kaley Cuoco Cameo as an Alternate Penny 2 days ago See All Getty Images for HBO Max Hannah Einbinder says working with Gillian Anderson on the new film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma” has actually given her a new perspective on the end of “ Hacks ” and its legacy. “Doing all this press with Gillian for the movie, she talks about ‘X-Files’ constantly,” Einbinder tells Variety ‘s Awards Circuit Podcast . “She’s asked about it constantly. It’s made me feel like, ‘oh, I’m gonna talk about “Hacks” for the rest of my life!’ I’m so happy that will always be something that I can come back to and meditate on and express gratitude for. When you are a part of something that has a deeply connected base of people who love it, that stays.” Related Stories Why I'm Suing to Block the Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger (Guest Column) Court Hears Argument on States' Move to Pause Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger Meanwhile, given how many photo shoots and events Paul W. Downs and his “Hacks” co-star Megan Stalter seem to show up at, why isn’t there a Jimmy and Kayla spinoff in the works? Popular on Variety “I would love for it to happen, and I have said this: You know we had a very specific plan for the way we wanted to end the story in the finale,” he says. “It’s such it’s so much pressure to deliver a satisfying ending … so, even to the last minute, even though we had this plan for a long time, we were like, ‘Should we stretch it out? Should we do two half seasons?’ But in the end, I’m so happy we stuck to our guns, and it resonated with people the way that it did. And because of that, I don’t I don’t want anything else to come after. I want that to be the last thing people remember.” When grilled about “Jimmy and Kayla,” he adds, “getting to play these characters and having these characters evolve as much as they have over the five seasons has been so gratifying that it’s terrifying to think there won’t be more between the two of us. But I think it would have to be something different.” OK … we’re getting somewhere. So what might a “Hacks” spinoff look like? “There’s so many characters in the show that if we could do a universe, I want to see Mayor Jo in her first election. I want to see Marty coming to to Vegas in the ’70s.” Einbinder likes the Mayor Jo idea. “‘Better Call Saul’ vibes,” she says. “Her just being a fucking absolute criminal. Are you kidding? I’m in the freaking seats with the popcorn on that one.” Give it time. Maybe we’ll wear them down! But for now, we’ve got Downs and Einbinder on this week’s Awards Circuit Podcast, where they talk more about the “Hacks” ending and what they’ve got in store next. Plus, they take the 10 Questions quiz! But first, on the Roundtable, Variety TV critic Aramide Tinubu joins us to give some of her summer TV picks and hot takes on the Emmy noms. Listen below! He might be a bit biased, but Downs raves about Einbinder’s part in the upcoming slasher film “Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma,” which opens August 7. “I’ll give you the review,” he says. “This is a pull quote now from Variety . Absolutely beautiful, absolutely terrifying and absolutely funny. And Hannah is a revelation. She is such a star. I’m not even kidding. The stuff that she does, her range being on display yet again in this is really impressive.” As for Downs, Lucia Aniello and Jen Statsky, the trio has a number of projects in the works — including one in development with Kaley Cuoco — although she’s busy on something else right now, so schedules will have to align for their project. And then the trio also has another project they’re working on for HBO. “I can say it’s a it’s a limited series,” he says. “It’s an hourlong limited. I can say that. So it’s a slight tone shift, but there’s definitely going to be humor.” Einbinder says she’d be game to join them again for this next project. “I told Paul, Jen and Lucia that I want to be their non-problematic Rob Schneider. I just want to pop up in everything they do forever.” Meanwhile, Einbinder says she’s still thinking a lot about her time on “Hacks,” and how she found a video that she recorded for herself in Season 1. Now it feels like a bit of a time capsule: “It was in my trailer, and the sound is pretty muffled, and it’s kind of a shitty video, but I just was kind of reflecting, like kind of a diary, and one of the things that I said was ‘I think these people are going to mean so much to me.’” Einbinder’s come a long way in those six years since “Hacks” first became a reality. “Most nights when I get into bed and feel the relief of making it back to my bed at the end of a long day, I go, ‘wow.’ I just am filled with gratitude. This experience has made so much possible for me in every conceivable way. On an emotional level, obviously we have a very strong bond. When I was auditioning for Ava initially, I was opening for other comics on the road. That went away because of COVID, and the job I had before that was working at a coffee shop, and that also went away. I was just really, ‘I actually don’t know what I’m gonna do.’ And so just on every level, [this success] has never been lost on me.” 10 QUESTIONS WITH HANNAH EINBINDER and PAUL W. DOWNS: 1. Childhood nickname: Einbinder: “‘Pud,’ short for ‘Pudding.’ My parents called me that.” Downs: “‘Chubb.’ I think it came from my love of pasta and pizza. I think it honestly came from my love of Swiss Miss. I would take Swiss Miss packets with half and half, and I would make like a sludge that I would drink. It was my version of child cocaine, I guess.” 2. Something you loved as a kid but can’t believe you were into it now: Downs: “I used to kind of collect these, they were basically little figurines that were like a dragon or an Excalibur or a wizard, and they were on amethyst. They were sold at a kiosk at the Rockaway Town Square Mall, and I was into these bizarre — I don’t know what that is. Fantasy figurines. They were also very like Sedona. You know, they were very like hippie figurines. I can’t believe I was so into that” Einbinder: “I have done so much inner child work that I have love and affection for the things that I maybe was into. I took baton. I had a baton unit. I was very into baton at one time. I did baton classes. I learned from a stripper named Heather. Thank you, Heather. She taught baton on the side. She was like, ‘I do flaming baton at my where I dance,’ and we were like, ‘We want to come see you dance, Heather!’ And she was like, ‘It’s not for kids.’” 3. Go-to Karaoke or sing-in-the-shower song: Einbinder: “‘What’s Up,’ by 4 Non Blondes.” Downs: “‘All I Wanna Do’ by Sheryl Crow. It’s a real crowd pleaser.” 4. Give me an alternate title for your show: [Not asked] 5. What’s your secret talent? : Downs: “I can give a good massage.” Einbinder: “I can create a bubble ring underwater. Or a smoke ring. I can do that too. But that’s featured in the show ‘Hacks.’” 6. Favorite ice cream flavor : Downs: “As a kid, I loved strawberry. Now I want like a like a dark chocolate double fudge chunk.” Einbinder: “Mint chip.” 7. The one item you couldn’t live without : Einbinder: “Cell phone.” Downs: “I was gonna say toothpaste. You really want toothpaste.” 8. What TV show in all of history do you wish you were a cast member of? : Einbinder: “‘Sopranos,’ ‘Mad Men.’” Downs: “Some of my favorite shows like ‘Arrested Development’ or ‘Succession’ or ‘Fleabag,’ I don’t know that I want to be on those shows. I think I want to be on ‘Friends.’ I think I would have had a blast.” 9. Fictional character you most admire : [Not asked] 10. Your favorite piece of advice : Einbinder: “‘Faster and funnier.’” Downs: “I’ve uttered those words. You know what else I uttered recently, and I’m taking a great piece of advice that Maya Angelou gave to Oprah, which is when someone tells you who they are, believe them the first time. I think that’s a really good piece of advice.” Variety’s “Awards Circuit” podcast, hosted by Clayton Davis, Jazz Tangcay, Emily Longeretta and Michael Schneider, who also produces, is your one-stop source for lively conversations about the best in film and television. Each episode, “Awards Circuit” features interviews with top film and TV talent and creatives, discussions and debates about awards races and industry headlines, and much more. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Anthony D'Alessandro Anthony D'Alessandro Editorial Director/Box Office Editor @AwardsTony More Stories By Anthony ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat ‘Avengers: Endgame’ $357M Weekend Record – Saturday AM Box Office Update ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’s $309 Million Promo Partner Campaign Is A Hollywood Record ‘The Odyssey’ Passes ‘Oppenheimer’s $330M U.S. Lifetime B.O. In 13 Days Before ‘Spider-Man’ Swings In – Box Office Update View All August 1, 2026 7:51am Tom Holland as Spider-Man Sony Pictures SATURDAY AM: This weekend, it’s a game of Marvel trying to beat Marvel at the weekend box office. Spider-Man: Brand New Day continued to post an all-time record opening day/previews yesterday with $168M , feasibly outstripping the previous first day record owned by Avengers: Endgame ($157.4M). Still, there’s isn’t a unison of opinion out there that Brand New Day will take down Avengers: Endgame ‘s all-time opening record of $357.1M. Some believe it boils down to Sunday where a $5M swing is possible . Sony is calling their 3-day weekend at $325M , which is a wonderful second-best ever start in North America, but others think the opening here is closer to $350M+ . If Brand New Day gets above $105M today, then it has a better shot of beating Avengers: Endgame ‘s start. Brand New Day came close to having a better pure Friday than Avengers: Endgame after you back out previews, $96M to $97.4M. Avengers: Endgame went on to do $109.2M on its Saturday which was +12% from its pure Friday. That Russo Brothers directed movie eased -17% on Sunday and the thinking is that Brand New Day is down between -10% to -15% on Sunday from Saturday. Watch on Deadline How is walk-up business? Very similar to No Way Home ‘s. In Screen Engine/Rentrak PostTrak exits, 33% said they bought their tickets same-day for Brand New Day, which is not far from No Way Home ‘s 35%. However this winds up, of course, it’s the biggest ever domestic opening for Sony, stratospheres above Spider-Man: No Way Home’s $260.1M. It’s also a record start for director Destin Daniel Cretton, Zendaya and the second best for Tom Holland after Endgame. PLF screens have caught 24% of Brand New Day ‘s weekend in its web with 3D accounting for 17% of the gross so far. Unlike Odyssey, Brand New Day, especially given its family appeal, doesn’t need to live or die on PLF with the masses taking it in on 2D screens. As far as audience exits, Brand New Day is looking real similar to No Way Home : A definite recommend of 88% (versus previous pic’s 90%) in PostTrak exits, its fourth A CinemaScore among the Holland Spider-Man (to No Way Home ‘s A+), biggest demo remains 18-24 at 36% (vs No Way Home ‘s 42%), with a 61% to 39% male-female split (vs previous pic’s 62%/38%). Broken out, men over and under 25 showed up at 30% apiece while women under 25 were next at 21%, followed by women over 25 at 18%. Diversity demos are 36% Caucasian, 28% Hispanic and Latino, 20% Black, 10% Asian American and 6% Native American and other. The 18-34 set reps 63% of Brand New Day ‘s moviegoers versus No Way Home ‘s 68%. Over 35 demo grew with Brand New Day at 21% versus No Way Home ‘s 15%. Of those who went, 58% told PostTrak that it was part of a franchise they love, 47% said it looked fun and entertaining, 41% went for the cast as a whole, 39% went for Holland and 29% went for Zendaya. Brand New Day is playing everywhere but best in South, South Central and West. The Regal Irvine Spectrum is the movie’s top grossing venue with more than $385K. The fact that Brand New Day is reaching record levels sans Imax provides more hope for Disney with Marvel Studios’ Avengers: Doomsday at Christmas given how Imax is committed to Warner Bros/Legendary’s Dune Part Three. While we don’t have an official update on international, over in China, Brand New Day is easily No. 1 this weekend with over $71M since yesterday after a Wednesday opening. There was a gap in the Holland Spider-Mans in the Middle Kingdom. No Way Home wasn’t cleared to play, hence there wasn’t a legal way to watch the movie. The previous pic there in 2019, Far From Home, opened to a reported $95M (not accounting for currency swings and inflation). How is Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey doing in the shadow of a behemoth like Brand New Day ? Very well, thank you, with a $51M third weekend, -43%, the best third frame the Oscar winning filmmaker has ever seen at the domestic box office. Running cume is $396.5M for the Universal theatrical release at 3,861 theaters. When does Odysseus wrap up his journey stateside? The outlook is a half billion for the latest Nolan, which if that happens would be his second highest grossing movie after Dark Knight ($534M domestic). As we told you, for all movies, this is a record weekend ahead of the final April weekend of 2019 when Avengers: Endgame led all pics to $402M. Current estimate is $434M, +262% from the same frame a year ago when Disney/Marvel’s Fantastic Four: First Steps led in its second frame, and +195% from last weekend’s $147.3M. No doubt about it, theatrical is alive. 1.) Spider-Man: Brand New Day (Sony) 4,487 theaters, Fri $168M, 3-day $325M-$350M+ /Wk 1 2.) New York and LA locations had ok numbers, we hear. The result here is similar to Neon’s Nic Winding Refn genre title, Her Private Hell, last weekend which opened to $538K at 675 (but is dropping to around a second weekend of $36K at 147 sites for a running ten-day cume of $842K). 9. Evil Dead Burn (New Line) 642 (-1,743) theaters, Fri $150K (-82%), 3-day $527K (-81%), Total $31.2M /Wk 4 10. Obsession (Foc) 430 (-773) theaters, Fri $140K (-71%) 3-day $450K (-71%) Total $262.7M /Wk 12 FRIDAY MIDDAY UPDATE: Sony/Marvel Studios’ Spider-Man: Brand New Day is heading for an all-time record opening day (including previews) between $167 million-$173 million . That easily would kick the first day/preview opening record of Avengers: Endgame ($157.4M) to the side, not to mention the U.S./Canada debut here is well ahead of Spider-Man: No Way Home ‘s first Friday/previews of $121.96M. This is according to industry sources, not Sony right now. Related Stories Reviews ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Review: Tom Holland And Zendaya Forge A Challenging Path Forward In Dark And Thrilling New Chapter From Marvel Superhero, Spider-Man News ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Los Angeles Premiere Red Carpet Photos: Zendaya, Tom Holland, Sadie Sink & More Some would like to call an opening domestic record ahead of Avengers: Endgame ‘s $357.1M, but we’re not there yet. Could be. But best estimate at this point in time is north of $330M at 4,487 theaters, which of course would make it the second-best opening at the North American box office ahead of No Way Home ‘s $260.1M in 2021. If by some chance a hurricane wipes out several theaters and Brand New Day falls back to $280M — c’mon, that’s an awesome opening, and $20M ahead of No Way Home ‘s start. That said, I’m hearing the hourlies here for Brand New Day are pulling ahead of No Way Home ‘s. It ain’t stopping.

Animal control officials, along with the Los Angeles County Department of Regional Planning, conducted the search of the property that the officials suspected was being used as a kennel operation with more than 100 dogs present. (Subsequent reports indicate there were as many as 200 dogs on the property.) “The warrant allows us to lawfully access the property and verify compliance with County codes,” the department said in a statement to press. “Our priority is the safety and well-being of both the animals on the property and the people who may be working or residing here. In the written caption accompanying the video, Blair wrote, “The animals are good in lieu of our surprise visit in 105° heat! With as busy as we all are in animal rescue and saving lives from the hot deserts and abandoned animals and shelters, everyone’s emails and social media are overloaded! “Turns out,” she continues, “we just have some paperwork to do and some diagrams but as everybody knows, I’m looking to move so I can be more educational and help more animals. O’Connor, 'On Golden Pond' movie poster Courtesy Richard L. O’Connor , an Emmy-winning TV producer and a studio executive in charge of production on such films as On Golden Pond, The Muppet Movie and Raise The Titanic, died July 22 in Palm Desert. He was 96. His death was announced by his family. A cause was not disclosed. A long-time resident of the Mendocino Coast, O’Connor won an Emmy Award for Outstanding Children’s Program for producing the 1989 NBC TV movie A Mother’s Courage: The Mary Thomas Story starring Alfre Woodard. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News Jean-Pierre Dorléac Dies: Emmy-Winning ‘Battlestar Galactica’ & ‘Somewhere In Time’ Costume Designer Was 83 Born in San Francisco with his twin brother Don on January 7, 1930, O’Connor and his twin served together in the United States Marine Corps in the Korean War from 1950-1951, and after college Richard began pursuing a career in Hollywood. He landed a job in the mail room at CBS Television City, the start of a career in show business that would eventually including producing and working as a studio executive. Watch on Deadline His four-decade studio production career includes such TV and movie credits as On Golden Pond (1981 ); The Muppet Movie (1979) ; Movie, Movie (1978) ; Friendly Fire (1979); and Raise The Titanic (1980). As a producer, O’Connor’s credits include TV movies and episodes of such TV series and limited series as Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman (1993), Amerika (1987), A Death in California (1985), Fatal Vision (1984) and Angels in the Endzone (1997), among others. He is survived by wife Brona; daughters Kathleen, Triglia and Karen; stepchildren Kate, Marc and Matt; four grandchildren, two great-grandchildren and one great-great-grandaughter. articles.title: Donald Trump Disagrees “100%” With U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro On Reflecting Pool Damage, Writes  “VANDALS!”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Donald Trump Disagrees “100%” With U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro On Reflecting Pool Damage, Writes “VANDALS!” Richard L. O’Connor Dies: Emmy-Winning Producer, Exec In Charge Of ‘On Golden Pond’, ‘Muppet Movie’ Was 96 Linda Blair Says Search Of Her Reported Kennel Operation Was About “Paperwork” View All August 1, 2026 10:29am Reflecting Pool, David Hearn Getty UPDATE, with Trump statement: President Donald Trump is sticking with his go-to explanation of vandalism for the peeling lining of the Reflecting Pool that U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro has concluded was the result of the no-bid contractor’s botched installation. On Truth Social today, Trump writes, “I disagree 100% with Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia, on the Reflecting Pool. I don’t know what she was thinking? To me, it was a pure case of VANDALISM, that included the grass, which had a big 86 47 emblazoned in giant letters on it, and other elements of the surrounding area. There may have been some contractor difficulty, but the major damage was caused by VANDALS! President DJT”. Related Stories Sports FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal News ABC Says Comments Overwhelmingly Favor License Renewals Despite FCC's "Ongoing Retaliation Campaign" To Punish Network Over Trump Coverage Trump, in the post, is conflating the Reflecting Pool damage with an apparent marking of the number 8647 on the nearby National Mall last month. No evidence has been presented that the two situations were connected. Trump maintains that the number is an assassination threat. Watch on Deadline PREVIOUS: Contradicting claims made repeatedly by President Donald Trump, U.S. attorney Jeanine Pirro now says she will seek to dismiss a felony charge against former Olympic canoeist David Hearn who had been accused of ripping up a small square piece of new blue lining from the renovated Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool. In a motion filed Friday evening, federal prosecutors conceded that damage to the pool was “the result of a botched installation and not vandalism.” In the build-up to the Trump-renovated pool’s intended July 4 unveiling, the new blue lining began peeling as the water turned green with algae bloom – the very problem the Trump-ordered restoration project was to have fixed. Just last month following Hearn’s indictment on July 2, Pirro stated that prosecutors had “tremendous evidence” of Hearn’s guilt and that he faced up to 10 years in prison. Hearn has consistently denied the accusations. The cost of Trump’s pool renovation has ballooned to more than $14 million. Yesterday, federal prosecutors blamed the contractors hired by the the Interior Department on a no-bid contract for the mess, saying that the renovation itself had caused “widespread damage” to the lining. Pirro now accuses he Interior Department of misleading prosecutors on key facts, including that the Department withheld evidence that the lining had begun to peel within two days of the project’s completion. Pirro said the Department had insisted that “nearly all of the damage” had been the work of vandals. Pirro’s new stance on the matter marks a significant break from her usual lockstep siding with Trump. The former Fox News on-air personality said in her motion last night that contractor Atlantic Industrial Coatings rushed “to complete the [renovation] project prior to events associated with the America 250 celebration.” Trump had repeatedly said the newly blue pool would be unveiled before the July 4 celebration. “Given all of this newly discovered information,” Pirro writes, “it is difficult to attribute the widespread damage to the Reflecting Pool to vandalism.” Of the seven people that had been arrested on vandalism charges in connection to the pool, only Hearn was charged with felony destruction of property. A trial was supposed to have started September 28. On Friday, lawyers representing Hearn said in a statement that the dismissal of charges “does not erase the abuse of government power in arresting and charging a patriotic American who did nothing wrong. The government’s approach was ready, fire, aim. The administration owes Mr. Hearn an apology.” Samara Weaving Lands Emma Frost Role In Disney/Marvel’s Reboot Pic Vincent Pastore Dies, ‘The Sopranos’ Cast Reacts Netflix Mountaineer Nirmal Purja Dies In Avalanche Dermot Mulroney To Leave NBC Drama ‘Chicago Fire’ Early In Season 15 Read More About: 27 Comments

articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Greg Evans Greg Evans NY & Broadway Editor @GregEvans5 More Stories By Greg Nirmal Purja Dies In Avalanche: Celebrated Mountaineer Featured In Netflix Documentary ’14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible’ Was 43 Donald Trump Disagrees “100%” With U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro On Reflecting Pool Damage, Writes “VANDALS!” Richard L. O’Connor Dies: Emmy-Winning Producer, Exec In Charge Of ‘On Golden Pond’, ‘Muppet Movie’ Was 96 View All August 1, 2026 11:09am Nirmal Purja (2023) Andreas Rentz/Getty Images Nirmal Purja, the British-Nepali mountaineer whose renowned career was featured in the 2021 Netflix documentary 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible , died in an avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan on Thursday, July 30, his company has confirmed. He was 43. Purja was one of 10 people killed in the tragedy. Related Stories Obituaries 2026 Deaths Photo Gallery: Hollywood & Media Obituaries News ‘14 Peaks’ Producer Noah Media Group Ups Legal Boss To COO Elite Expeditions, Purja’s company, said in a statement, “Today, it is with profound sadness and immense heartbreak that we confirm that Nirmal “Nimsdai” Purja, tragically lost his life following the avalanche on Broad Peak. We have also received confirmation that other members of the expedition sadly did not survive. Today, we mourn not only Nims, but every life lost in this tragedy.” The statement, posted on Instagram – read it in its entirety below – continued, “The world has lost one of mountaineering’s greatest climbers, a leader who inspired millions through his courage, humility and unwavering belief that human potential is far greater than we often imagine.” Watch on Deadline Purja’s brother Kamal later said in a statement, “It is with the heaviest heart that I share the devastating news that my beloved younger brother, Nirmal ‘Nimsdai’ Purja, and the other climbers are no longer with us. Although our hearts are broken, we are incredibly proud of you. Your legacy will live forever.” Born in Nepal and later serving in the British army, Purja was best known for his 2019 accomplishment of scaling the world’s 14 highest peaks in just over six months. “It has been a grueling but humbling six months,” he said at the time, “and I hope to have proven that anything is possible with some determination, self-belief and positivity.” The 14-peak adventure was chronicled in the Netflix film 14 Peaks: Nothing Is Impossible (see the trailer below). “The biggest strength I have is that I have no fear,” the indefatigable Purja says in the trailer. In a statement, Nepal’s Prime Minister Balendra Shah said that “the tragic death of six Nepalese and four other foreign climbers, including world record holder Nirmal Purja, in the Karakoram mountain range of Pakistan, has shocked us. The history of their courage, dedication, and contributions will always remain inspiring.” Purja served in the British military for 16 years and was awarded an MBE in 2018 for his achievement in extreme high-altitude mountaineering. Purja, who lived in Hampshire, England, is survived by his wife and and three-year-old daughter. Complete information on survivors was not immediately available.
