articles.title: Vincent Pastore Dies: ‘The Sopranos’ Star Was 80
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Nellie Andreeva Nellie Andreeva Editor-In-Chief @DeadlineNellie More Stories By Nellie Vincent Pastore Dies: ‘The Sopranos’ Star Was 80 ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Creators On Episode 2 Surprise OG Star Return & “Breaking Up” Beloved ‘Big Bang Theory’ Couple ‘Stuart Fails To Save The Universe’ Stars On Stuart’s Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off… What About Gary? View All August 1, 2026 1:08pm Vincent Pastore Kristina Bumphrey via Getty Images Vincent Pastore , known for playing mobsters in film and TV, most notably Salvatore “Big Pussy” Bonpensiero on HBO’s The Sopranos , has died. He was 80. The veteran actor was found dead in his Bronx residence today, Aug. 1, by a neighbor. Pastore’s manager had not heard from him for three days though, according to a close friend, the actor’s driver had spoken to him on the phone Friday night. The death is believed to be from natural causes and is not being investigated by the medical examiner. Born in the Bronx on July 14, 1946, Pastore fought in the Vietnam war before graduating from Pace University with a degree in drama. While working as a limo driver, he met Matt and Kevin Dillon who went to see him in a community play he was doing, and The Entourage star Kevin helped him get his first break. Related Stories News 'Stuart Fails To Save The Universe' Stars On Stuart's Bold Move In Episode 2 As His Relationship With Denise Takes Off... What About Gary? Cancellations and Renewals 'Wonder Man' Canceled After 1 Season At Disney+ After minor parts in early 1990s movies such as Goodfellas, Carlito’s Way and Men of Respect , Pastore rose to prominence with his roles in the 1995 feature The Jerky Boys: The Movie and the 1996 HBO TV movie Gotti , in which he appeared alongside future Sopranos co-stars Tony Sirico, Frank Vincent, and Dominic Chianese. It was David Chase’s 1999 drama The Sopranos that gave Pastore his signature role, Big Pussy, Tony Soprano’s (James Gandolfini) longtime best friend and mob enforcer turned FBI Informant whose murder became one of the Emmy-winning series’ most memorable scenes. ‘The Sopranos’ Season 1 cast, from left: Tony Sirico, Steven Van Zandt, James Gandolfini, Michael Imperioli and Vincent Pastore HBO Pastore’s extensive feature credits also include Mickey Blue Eyes, Two Family House, Riding in Cars with Boys, Witness to the Mob, Deuces Wild, Mafia!, Serving Sara, This Thing of Ours, Shark Tale, Bachelor Party Vegas, Once Upon a Time in Brooklyn, Money Train, A Brooklyn State of Mind, The Deli, Spinning Gold and Guy Ritchie’s Revolver. In TV, Pastore was a frequent guest star on Law & Order and had major roles on The Practice, Son of the Beach, Queens Supreme, Hawaii Five-0, Wu-Tang: An American Saga, the daytime drama One Life to Live and the miniseries The Last Don II . He most recently was a series regular on Gravesend and guest starred on Yellowjackets . During the 2000s, Pastore was a fixture on reality television with appearances on Celebrity Apprentice, Celebrity Family Feud, Dancing With the Stars, Shark Tank and Celebrity Fit Club . He also hosted The Wiseguy Show on SiriusXM and performed with the band The Gangster Squad. “Vinny was a great guy, he would help anyone and was very charitable,” Pastore’s longtime manager Bob McGowan said. Pastore is survived by his daughter, Renee, son-in-law and granddaughter. articles.title: ‘A Life Illuminated’: Of Bioluminescence, Mysterious Sea Creatures, And A Woman Scientist’s Groundbreaking Quest
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Matthew Carey Matthew Carey Documentary Editor, Awards @mattcarey More Stories By Matthew Emmy Contender Judd Apatow On “Piss-Your-Pants” Funny Mel Brooks, His Nikki Glaser Collab, And That Seth Rogen-Anne Hathaway ‘Knocked Up’ Story Chris Hemsworth’s Wild State Boards ‘Learning To Fly’, Ultra Marathon-Themed Documentary From Award-Winning Director Max Lowe Doc Talk Podcast: Director Sara Dosa On Her Oscar Contender ‘Time And Water’, Elegy For Iceland’s Disappearing Ice View All August 1, 2026 4:33pm Dr. Edie Widder (right) below the ocean surface in 'A Life Illuminated' Sandbox Films Director Tasha Van Zandt went to great lengths to make her documentary A Life Illuminated – and to enormous depths. More than 3,000 feet, in fact. Van Zandt descended over half a mile to the ocean floor in a submersible to film the work of pioneering marine biologist Dr. Edie Widder , who has observed and studied more deep ocean phenomena than perhaps anyone alive. Her discoveries have “transformed how we perceive life in the deep sea,” the filmmaker writes. “[Widder] began her career at a time when the deep sea was considered a dark, empty void. But Edie dared to look diﬀerently. Through her courage, curiosity, and her lens, she revealed the ocean as a glowing, dynamic world.” Related Stories Documentary ‘A Life Illuminated’ Clip: Take Plunge With Undersea Explorer Edie Widder In TIFF World Premiere Documentary Documentary Sandbox Films, XTR Team On ‘A Life Illuminated,’ Feature Doc On Pioneering Marine Biologist Edie Widder Widder has uncovered a once-hidden “language of light” – dazzling bioluminescence that pervades ocean depths. Watch on Deadline A bioluminescent jellyfish seen in the North Atlantic Ocean. Reinhard Dirscherl/ullstein bild via Getty Images “Edie actually says, ‘Because so much of our ocean world is bioluminescent and the ocean is so vast, bioluminescence may be the most common form of communication on our planet,’” Van Zandt said at a Q&A Wednesday that followed a screening of her film in Santa Monica, CA, a short distance from the Pacific. “’What is this language we don’t understand?’” It took the development of submersibles capable of withstanding tremendous atmospheric pressures to enter that sunken water world. But something more was required to reveal the life forms and their activities so far below the surface – truly innovative thinking that has been the hallmark of Dr. Widder’s scientific career. She led the invention and design of multiple devices to “enable unobtrusive deep-sea observations,” as noted by the Ocean Research & Conservation Association (ORCA), which Widder founded. Dr. Edie Widder earlier in her career. Sandbox Films As the documentary explores, Widder developed an “eye-in-the-sea” system to remotely monitor deep ocean marine life. It uses far-red illumination, which she understood wouldn’t bother creatures in the depths because most of them don’t perceive infrared light. Widder also created an “electronic jellyfish,” an ingenious optical lure aimed to tempt sea creatures into camera range. By deploying one of the lures, she became the first person to capture video of a giant squid alive, a multi-tentacled animal trying to make a dinner of the faux jellyfish. “In 2012, I, along with the rest of the world, saw this first footage of a live giant squid in its natural habitat,” Van Zandt recounted. “And I was transfixed by it, but it wasn’t until years later that I started to really sit with the question of who was the person behind the camera and how did this [footage] come to be? And so, in 2020, I reached out to Edie Widder for the first time. And on our very first conversation, she started to share how that was just one of hundreds of discoveries she had made in this quest to transform how we see our ocean planet. And that is when the spark for this film began.” A submersible deep below the ocean surface in ‘A Life Illuminated’ Sandbox Films Eventually, Van Zandt took the plunge with Dr. Widder. “When I was able to dive with Edie, we saw things that likely no one has ever seen before, even beyond this film that we couldn’t even capture on camera because it was so faint to the human eye. And it was remarkable,” the director said. “There are incredible creatures in our oceans that we can’t even begin to fathom how to even look for yet. So, it was completely life-changing.” For decades now, Widder has been documenting the light show created by marine animals that mix chemicals in their bodies to generate bioluminescence. Van Zandt structures the film around the scientist’s mission to capture the flashback effect (her white whale, as Edie describes it), an attempt to see how bioluminescent creatures respond when they’re flashed with light from an otherwise darkened sub. It was a daunting task for Van Zandt and director of photography-producer Sebastian Zeck to try to reveal that experiment. (L-R) Producer-director Tasha Van Zandt and producer-director of photography Sebastian Zeck at the Toronto International Film Festival on September 7, 2025. Gareth Cattermole/Getty Images for IMDb “Filming in the deep sea in complete darkness from a submersible is a huge technical challenge, but everything sort of came together on that very last dive,” Zeck explained at the Q&A. “We used these specialized cameras provided by Canon to film that [flashback effect] sequence. Light sensitivity in photography is measured in what’s called ISO. Normally in a daylight setting, we’re shooting at ISO 800 or so. The sequence at the end of the film, we shot at ISO 100,000. So, that gives you a sense of the sensitivity required.” The attempt by humans to communicate with marine animals may evoke, for some, a classic Steven Spielberg film about first contact with extraterrestrials. “It really felt like all of the [marine] life was kind of responding in this fantastical way and truly felt like Close Encounters ,” Van Zandt marveled. “We flashed the lights, everything flashed back. And it felt like we were in the center of the Milky Way, but with blue glitter all around us. It was glowing and sparking. And just like the 4th of July — like [Edie] describes from her first experience. But then in the distance, we were seeing things that the camera couldn’t even capture. There was life swooshing and sweeping and this glowing golden, amber-colored creature that we don’t even really know what it was that was off in the distance. And also something fascinating is that the camera picked up this little creature called a tomopterid worm, which glows kind of a golden orange color that flashed along with all of the blue bioluminescence we were seeing.” Sandbox Films A Life Illuminated , from Sandbox Films and XTR, premiered at the Toronto International Film Festival last September, going on to screen at the Camden International Film Festival in Maine, Hot Springs Documentary Film Festival in Arkansas, CPH:DOX in Copenhagen, SFFILM’s Doc Stories and many other festivals in the U.S. and abroad. It began its theatrical run on July 24 at DCTV Firehouse Cinema in Manhattan and the documentary opens Sunday at the Roxie Theater in San Francisco (where Van Zandt and Zeck are based). The 12:50 p.m. Roxie screening on Sunday will be followed by a Q&A moderated by oceanographer Sylvia Earle. With its spectacular imagery of bioluminescent creatures, not to mention a giant squid measuring somewhere between 2-4 storeys tall, this is a film that demands to be seen on the big screen. That’s the closest most of us will ever come to observing the astounding sights Edie Widder has witnessed for decades. Van Zandt says she regards her protagonist as an inspiration. “Going into the [final] dive… one of my greatest fears was how would I respond, if I would feel fearful, if I would panic. And she kept saying to us, ‘Just focus on curiosity instead of fear.’ And when we went down on the dive, that was really the guiding factor. There were definitely moments where I had to say, ‘Curiosity over fear, curiosity over fear,’” Van Zandt recalled. “This lifetime of seeing things no one’s ever seen before and breaking depth limits and just so many courageous moments that she’s lived through has really instilled in her this incredible grounded-ess. It’s really remarkable.” Samara Weaving Lands Emma Frost Role In Disney/Marvel’s Reboot Pic Vincent Pastore Dies, ‘The Sopranos’ Cast Reacts Netflix Mountaineer Nirmal Purja Dies In Avalanche Dermot Mulroney To Leave NBC Drama ‘Chicago Fire’ Early In Season 15 Read More About: Comments

articles.title: Scott Hylands Dead: ‘Night Heat’ & ‘Fargo’ Actor Was 83
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $168M U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn Vincent Pastore Tributes: ‘The Sopranos’ Alums Jamie-Lynn Sigler, Michael Imperioli & More Remember “Kind-Hearted Brother” Scott Hylands Dead: ‘Night Heat’ & ‘Fargo’ Actor Was 83 CBS News Correspondent Nikki Battiste Joins NBC’s ‘Early Today’ As Anchor: “A True Homecoming” View All August 1, 2026 5:01pm Scott Hylands in 'Night Heat' (1985-89) Alliance Entertainment/Courtesy Everett Collection Scott Hylands , the actor known for playing Detective Kevin “OB” O’Brien in Night Heat , has died. He was 83. The Canadian actor died on Wednesday, July 29, his cinematographer son Luke Hylands announced in a statement memorializing his “forever hero and best friend” on social media. “Husband, Father, Actor, Director, Writer, Storyteller, Friend, and lover of life,” he wrote on Instagram . “I am heartbroken to share the news that my Dad Scott has passed away Wednesday night. Myself and my family are still trying to process this horrible loss.” Related Stories Documentary 'A Life Illuminated': Of Bioluminescence, Mysterious Sea Creatures, And A Woman Scientist's Groundbreaking Quest News CBS News Correspondent Nikki Battiste Joins NBC's 'Early Today' As Anchor: "A True Homecoming" Luke continued, “There simply are not enough words I can say about you right now. You are my forever hero and my best friend. Always and forever. I love you. Goodbye Dad. xo” Watch on Deadline Born Feb. 27, 1943 in Lethbridge, Alberta, Canada, Scott Hylands Douglas was raised in British Columbia, where he studied zoology at University of British Columbia before transferring to theater arts. After college, he pursued acting in New York City, where he made his off-Broadway debut as the lead in a 1965 production of Billy Liar . He also performed with the American Conservatory Theater in San Francisco for several years before his onscreen debut in Daddy’s Gone A-Hunting (1969). View this post on Instagram He went on to appear in films like Operation Snafu (1970), Fools (1970), Slipstream (1973), Earthquake (1974), Bittersweet Love (1976) and The Boys in Company “C” (1978), as well as shows like Griff , Kung Fu , The Magician , Wonder Woman , Police Story , The Waltons and Hart to Hart . Upon returning to Canada in the ’80s, Hylands landed the role of Detective Kevin “OB” O’Brien in the the CTV/CBS police crime drama Night Heat from 1985 to ’89. The actor was also known for playing Father Travis in ABC’s V (2009-2011). Over the years, Hylands also appeared on shows like NYPD Blue , The Outer Limits , The X-Files , Stargate SG-1 , Supernatural , Fargo , Heartland and Wynonna Earp , as well as films like Rememory (2017) and Elsewhere (2019). Scott Hylands is survived by wife Veronica, son Luke and daughter Rebecca. The Hollywood Reporter was first to break the news of Hylands’ death. articles.title: Sam Fender and Olivia Dean Have the Longest-Running No. 1 in U.K. History
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All July 31, 2026 1:36pm Sam Fender and Olivia Dean Samir Hussein/WireImage Sam Fender and Olivia Dean have made history, as the duo has set the new U.K. record for longest run atop the U.K.’s singles chart with their song “Rein Me In,” which has now spent 19 weeks at No. 1, the U.K.’s Official Charts Company announced on Friday. Fender and Dean took the throne from the late Frankie Laine, who’d held the record for over 70 years as his 1953 hit “I Believe” spent 18 weeks atop the chart. “Completely lost for words, thank you so much to Olivia Dean and the fans for making this song the juggernaut that it is,” Fender told the Official Charts company on Friday. “Can’t believe we broke the U.K. record!” Related Stories TV FIFA Boss Infantino Under Fire Over World Cup Sell Off Plans Movies Filmsaaz and Neozoon: Meet Filmmakers With Pseudonyms - and Political Movies - at Locarno “Rein Me In” first made its way onto the U.K. single chart in June of 2025, steadily making its way up the ladder before finally reaching the top this past February. From then, it enjoyed the top spot for 19 non-consecutive weeks, only getting interrupted by Harry Styles’ “American Girls,” Olivia Rodrigo’s “Drop Dead,” Ariana Grande’s “Hate that I Made You Love Me” and Taylor Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You.” “Rein Me In” managed to outlast Shakira and Burna Boy’s global smash “Dai Dai,” which is the anthem to the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Ella Langley’s “Choosin’ Texas,” arguably the biggest song of the year in the U.S., reached a new peak at No. 3. Stateside, “Rein Me In” currently sits at 69 on Billboard’s Hot 100 chart. Dean has two top 10 songs in the U.S. herself with “So Easy (To Fall in Love)” and “Man I Need.” THR

articles.title: Sheriff in Nancy Guthrie Case Releases Ransom Notes: “She Perished Shortly After She Was Taken”
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All July 31, 2026 1:58pm Pima County Sheriff Chris Nanos spoke to the media on Feb. 3 in Tucson, Arizona. Jan Sonnenmair/Getty Images Chris Nanos, the sheriff in the Nancy Guthrie kidnapping case, has released a pair of ransom notes initially sent to the CBS affiliate in her home city of Tucson, Arizona. The second of the two notes states that Nancy has “perished.” The notes “purport to have been written by kidnappers,” the Pima County Sheriff’s Department wrote in a press release timed to the six-month anniversary of Nancy’s disappearance . The first note was sent to KOLD-TV 13 News on Feb. 2; Nancy was last seen alive on Jan. 31. Addressed directly to Savannah Guthrie , the first ransom note demands $4 million-$6 million (depending on date of deposit) in Bitcoin for her safe release. It says Nancy is “safe but scared.” Related Stories TV The Reporter Who Won't Give Up On the Nancy Guthrie Kidnapping Story News Nancy Guthrie Ransom Notes Were All Reportedly Fake “Her life is in your hands,” the first note states. The note’s final line offers two details as proof of its legitimacy: “She had a white smart watch on the floor of the foot of her bed and the white flood light in the backyard was destroyed.” Nancy Guthrie is the mother of Today show co-anchor Savannah Guthrie. She was 84 years old at the time of her disappearance. On Feb. 6, a second email sent to the same news outlet’s Tips line states that Nancy has died and “is buried in nature.” The initial deadline for the ransom deposit ($4 million) was Feb. 5; the second deadline ($6 million) was Feb. 9. The second note reads, in full: “Guthrie Family, We did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition. We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this and hope you can all find peace. We are truly sorry.” Nancy had a serious heart condition and was without her medication. The ransom notes are posted below. The first Nancy Guthrie ransom note. Pima County Sheriff’s Office The second Nancy Guthrie ransom note. Pima County Sheriff’s Office The Pima County Sheriff’s Department says it is sharing the ransom notes now for the first time publicly in hopes that someone in the public recognizes “distinctive patterns of word choice, syntax and phraseology that reflect the writer’s unique linguistic style.” “They also provide valuable insight into the person’s mindset, motives and the evolution of their tone over time,” the press release continues. “As with the unidentified male depicted in the video, we believe these distinctive linguistic characteristics may be recognizable to someone who knows or has interacted with the notes’ writer. A friend, family member, coworker, classmate or acquaintance may recognize these patterns of expression and possess information that could help identify the individual responsible.” Doorbell videos of the suspected kidnapper were released to the public on Feb. 10. THR

articles.title: Bravo VP Talks Amanda’s TV Future After ‘Summer House’ Exit, West’s Departure and ‘In the City’ Season 2: “I’m Optimistic”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Andy Cohen with the 'In the City' season one cast. Charles Sykes for Bravo Logo text “Summer should be fun — and summer will be fun,” Kyle Cooke said while closing out the In the City reunion earlier this week. And Bravo is indeed having a busy summer after wrapping the first season of In the City , the Summer House spinoff following a group of friends — including Lindsay Hubbard , Kyle Cooke, Amanda Batula , Danielle Olivera and more — as they navigate friendships, relationships and careers in New York City. Filmed immediately after Summer House season 10, the series captured Amanda and Kyle’s marriage before the pair announced their split in January after 10 years together and four years of marriage. Related Stories TV 'In the City' Reunion Concludes With Part Two: How to Watch 'Summer House' Spinoff's Cast Sit-Down Online TV 'In the City' Reunion Recap: Lindsay and Whitney's Heated Exchange, Amanda Reveals She and West Haven't Said "I Love You" During part two of the reunion, Amanda confronted Kyle and alleged she recently learned he had been unfaithful during their marriage, while Kyle claimed Amanda nearly hit him after he woke her up one morning. The pair also revisited Kyle’s comments from the Summer House reunion about their lack of intimacy, ultimately acknowledging their incompatibilities while reiterating they still care deeply for one another as they continue navigating their divorce. Amanda also found herself in the hot seat with Danielle Olivera, apologizing for calling her a “homewrecker” earlier in the season. Andy Cohen also pointed out the contrast between Amanda’s apology to Danielle and her more defensive exchange with Ciara Miller during the Summer House reunion, where Amanda addressed her relationship with Ciara’s ex and fellow Summer House star, West Wilson. In a conversation with The Hollywood Reporter, Josh Brown, Bravo’s vp of current production, who was in the control room during the In the City reunion, breaks down the episode’s biggest moments, shares where things stand with a potential second season of the spinoff — now one of Bravo’s top three most-watched freshman series of the past five years — discusses Carl Radke’s possible future on the series and offers updates on Summer House season 11, including the show’s new house following the departures of Amanda and West. *** Things picked up where they left off last week with Lindsay and Whitney’s heated exchange. Was there anything that we didn’t see, and did they really leave the reunion still on bad terms? For sure, there’s more material, but there were no more twists and turns that viewers didn’t see. Viewers definitely got a true picture of what happened at the reunion. I don’t know if they left on bad terms, but I would call it unresolved terms. I think there will be more to work out in their friendship in real life. Lindsay was quite activated the whole reunion, as we know and love her for. The same with her conversation with Danielle. Was it surprising that maybe things were still left on an unresolved note? I was not surprised. I actually thought it was hopeful by the end, at least in my opinion. I work on Summer House as well, and I’ve worked on that series since the beginning. We’ve seen so many twists and turns in the Lindsay and Danielle friendship. So many ups and downs about so many different subjects. From when one of them was in a relationship and one of them was not, to when they were each in relationships, and now both moms, which is fascinating. So, I will never count either of them out to try and work out their friendship. They’ve had a long history together, and personally, I think it’d be great to see them continue to get to a good place. Lindsay had called out Danielle for not being as open in front of the cameras about her relationship. Could that impact her returning to the series? That wouldn’t affect how we move forward with Danielle in a future season. It’s more something for Lindsay and Danielle to work out, and if others in the cast take issue with anything, it’s more for them to work out as a friend group. What is your take on the color of Danielle’s dress to Yvonne’s wedding reception? Was it pink? Was it white? Did production warn her to maybe choose something else to wear? Well, by coincidence, I happened to be at that scene, and I will say that colors are not my specialty. ( Laughs. ) It looked — it was borderline. Let’s put it that way. In some light, it looked pink, and in some light, it looked a little bit closer to white. So, I could see both sides. What did you think about Whitney and Kenny’s performance at the reunion and how they held their own — especially in their arguments with Lindsay? I think that everyone gave great effort at the In the City reunion overall. I was proud of the cast. This was a first season. We don’t always have reunions in first seasons of Bravo series, and we had a very veteran cast in Kyle, Amanda and Lindsay. Even Danielle is extremely veteran. Then we had someone like Andrea, who’s kind of in the middle of experience. We had some very, very new cast members, and I feel like the cast did great in terms of how they did at the reunion. So we’re happy with it. There was discourse surrounding Amanda’s performance at the Summer House reunion , and she addressed it at the In the City reunion. What was her energy like that day? Did you notice a shift where she approached this differently? I did notice a huge difference from the minute each reunion started. I think Amanda was very scared at the Summer House reunion. I think she was not sure what it was going to be like and knew she was going to be asked a lot of tough questions by some of her fellow castmates about certain things that happened in that friend group. Here on In the City, there were a lot of questions for Amanda, but they were ultimately about the In the City friend group, her marriage and the fallout so the subjects and the stakes of the conversations were really different and I think she felt that going into each reunion, so I do think you saw a very different Amanda in each reunion. She seemed more relaxed here for sure. Amanda had a big reveal when it came to Kyle; she said she found out recently that he was unfaithful in their marriage. He seemed to be shocked by that. Was there anything that viewers didn’t see with that conversation? I think that was surprising to everyone, both, you know, her and Kyle’s fellow castmates and to producers behind the scenes. There wasn’t more information given at the reunion that viewers didn’t see. Andy said that Amanda’s apology to Danielle was very sincere and remorseful, and that it would have gone a long way with Ciara. Was it surprising to see her apologize to Danielle like that? Do you think that will change how some viewers perceived her from the Summer House reunion? I don’t know if it will change how they perceive her. I really don’t. I think viewers would appreciate that she apologized to Danielle. I was not surprised that she apologized to Danielle. I think what I was maybe more surprised about was the lack of a true-feeling apology to Ciara. I think that was surprising to everyone behind the scenes back at the Summer House reunion. Kyle Cooke, Ciara Miller, Andy Cohen, Amanda Batula and West Wilson at the Summer House season 10 reunion. Jocelyn Prescod/Bravo Moving forward, if In the City gets a second season, how do you think it will play out with Kyle and Amanda’s dynamic? Can they both be on the show? That is a very good question. I think, like Summer House, we approach things organically, and so we have to go by the facts on the ground, so to speak. I really don’t know what would happen if we are to get a season two. The one thing I would say is that, as viewers have seen on Summer House and In the City, both Kyle and Amanda are making a sincere effort to be friends post-marriage, even though they’re still technically married. They both really care about each other. I think viewers felt that at the reunion. What’s the status of season two right now? Have you heard anything? It’s too early to say. We just finished airing the season, and we’re really happy with the performance of the series in its first season. Bravo just released a big announcement about ratings in the past week or so, and In the City was included in that touting its performance for season one. So I’m optimistic. A few days after In the City’s reunion filmed, it was announced that West was leaving Summer House . Two weeks after that, it was announced that Amanda was leaving Summer House . What is Amanda’s future on TV? Could she still be part of a future season of In the City? Could we see West join? If I’m being honest, I think it’s too early to talk about that. We just finished airing the season, but we always approach things organically and by the facts on the ground. So, anything’s always possible, but there’s no plans for anything at this time about anything I should say, just because we’re still reacting to finishing airing the season. We’re getting our heads around where we go from here, so it’s too early to talk about casting for season two. Have you had any talks with Amanda about whether she’d even want to return to TV in the future? I have not — we have not. It’s just too soon to be talking about that. We are so appreciative of everything she’s done so far, and we really care about her. But it’s just too early to be having any talks like that. It’s premature. When do you think that process for In the City will start? I would say by the end of the summer for sure. We’ll definitely know a lot more within a month. Fans have been begging for Carl to be on In the City as a cast member. Is that something that you’d be open to? We obviously love Carl, and he made an appearance on In the City. In the City, I think, is a very different subject than Summer House. It’s about people who are sort of on the edge of leaping into a big adult decision, and they’re not quite sure which way to go on it, which is very different than Summer House. And so, I would say for anyone, that would have to be part of the equation that we factor in on the show in terms of their bigger participation on the show for Carl or anyone else. But Carl, of course, is a very organic part of the group, even In the City cast. So, if there’s a reason and if it feels organic, we always love Carl. After everything that’s happened with Summer House , is there anything that you learned from these experiences that you’ll apply to either the next season of Summer House or a potential second season of In the City? This was the ultimate sign of how willing this cast is to really talk about what’s really going on in their real lives. Obviously, last season was a very tough season in a lot of ways. Or really, it was the fallout from the season. It wasn’t necessarily things that happened on Summer House that were as tough, but it was what happened after the season and the reunion. The fact that we are back on Summer House the very next summer for another season, obviously, we’ve had some changes on the show in terms of who’s there, but the fact that we’re back with our forecast and moving forward and having a really fun, exciting summer says a lot about this group and the real friendships that are approaching over a decade for some of them. We hope to build that in a very separate way on In the City, should we get a green light. We want this real friend group that hangs out 12 months a year and not just showing up for filming. So, if that cast is willing to go there, we’re hopeful. West has said that his exit was mutual. Is that correct, or is there anything you can share about that? Yeah, I mean, especially with something like Summer House, it has to be the right fit. It has to feel real because they’re housemates. This is not like a house reality show where we bring in 10 strangers and see what happens when these 10 strangers get to know each other. This is a real friend group and an organic friend group, and so if someone doesn’t fit organically in the group, there’s sort of nothing that can be done. I’m sure West quickly recognized that. I’ve not spoken to him about this, but I would guess that he would not be interested in pushing his way into any friend group. He wants to live his life as well. Was it similar with Amanda, where it felt like there was just too much damage done and things couldn’t return to how they were with the group? Yeah, that’s exactly what I would say. Most episodes, every morning, they have to wake up and have breakfast together. You can’t have breakfast with someone that you don’t want to be there — it doesn’t make any sense for a show about a Hamptons house share. Obviously people will go through their ups and downs and their conflicts, and maybe once in a while, I’m sure a cast member is thinking, “Wow, I really wish I weren’t facing this person over my omelet right now.” But in the end, they have to have breakfast together. So, it’s going to feel forced if it’s not an organic friend group of people who, at their core, like each other as friends. Is it true there’s a new house for Summer House season 11? We can say that we’re not in the same house as last season. That’s true. So I think that’s great. It’s a new chapter. It was a wonderful house that we had for years, but I don’t know how the cast would have felt being back in that same house. We decided to get a different house way before this scandal and news broke, but I’m very grateful that we did make that decision because I think it would have been tough for them, some of them, emotionally, to be back in the same house. Can you tease anything about how Ciara is doing this summer? Here’s what I would say: I’m the biggest Ciara fan. So I’m a cheerleader for her in life, including Summer House, but also everything else she’s doing. I feel like Ciara is living her best life, and I think people are going to see a lighter, really fun Ciara who’s not weighed down as much by the conflicts of Summer House past. It’s going to be a really fun summer for her and for us. *** All episodes of In the City season one and 10 seasons of Summer House are streaming on Peacock. Check out all of The Hollywood Reporter’s In the City coverage here and Summer House here . THR

articles.title: Tom Corson Promoted at Warner Music After Latest C-Suite Shake Up
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Ethan Millman Plus Icon Ethan Millman Music Editor View All July 31, 2026 3:03pm Armin Zerza and Tom Corson Gonzalo Marroquin/Getty Images; Presley Ann/Getty Images Warner Music Group COO and CFO Armin Zerza is stepping down from his role, the company announced on Friday, noting that the executive has decided to leave for “personal reasons.” Warner Records COO Tom Corson will replace Zerza WMG’s as COO, and the company is starting a search for its next CFO. Zerza “will remain available to the company through the end of the fiscal year to ensure a seamless transition,” WMG said. Louis Dickler, WMG’s SVP, Global Controller and Chief Accounting Officer will serve as interim CFO while the company looks for a replacement. It’s a sudden departure for Zerza given that he joined the record company just over a year ago in April of 2025, and he was given the joint role as COO as well just over two months ago. Zerza’s successor will be WMG’s fourth CEO since 2023. Longtime CFO Eric Levin retired in 2023, succeeded by former ESPN and Disney executive Bryan Castellani before Zerza’s appointment in 2025. “Armin has been an instrumental leader and member of the executive team during a crucial period of growth and transformation,” WMG CEO Robert Kyncl said in a statement. “We thank Armin for his outstanding business and financial leadership and enduring contributions to WMG, and we wish him all the best.” Corson , meanwhile, is one of the most respected record executives in the music industry. Before joining Warner, he was the president and COO of RCA Music Group. With Warner Records CEO Aaron Bay-Schuck, the duo led a respected turnaround for the storied label, garnering a reputation in the record business for a strong artist development system with stars like Zach Bryan, Benson Boone and Sombr . With Corson moving to the corporate posting, following the transitional period, Bay-Schuck will helm Warner Records alone. “It’s an honor to step into this role during such a transformative era for both our company and the industry at large,” Corson said in a statement. “A huge thanks to Robert for the opportunity, as well as to Aaron and the Warner Records team for the unforgettable run. I’m looking forward to building on our momentum, turbocharging operations, and creating even more impactful opportunities for our incredible artists and songwriters worldwide.” As Kyncl said of Corson’s appointment: Tom is one of the most dynamic, respected, and effective executives in the music business, and a fierce champion of talent. Together with Aaron, he’s helped architect Warner Records’ resurgence, and we’ll leverage his vision, disciplined execution, and deep experience across the entire company as we continue to deliver for our artists and songwriters while achieving our top and bottom line goals.” THR

articles.title: John Galliano to Take Spotlight at Met Gala and Costume Institute Exhibition 16 Years After Antisemitic Rant
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Chris Gardner Plus Icon Chris Gardner chrissgardner Follow Sign Up View All July 31, 2026 5:28pm John Galliano attends Vogue's Forces of Fashion Conference at Milk Studios in New York on Oct. 12, 2017. (Photo by Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images) It’s official: John Galliano has been selected for a career-spanning exhibition at the Metropolitan Museum of Art in 2027. The move to give Galliano’s work a coveted spotlight in the Met’s Costume Institute — an exhibition that serves as the centerpiece for the annual Met Gala , one of the world’s most watched and obsessed-over red carpet events — makes him the third living designer to receive a solo exhibition at the Met. The honor was previously bestowed upon Yves Saint Laurent (in 1983) and Rei Kawakubo (in 2017). Related Stories Lifestyle Disney and Old Navy Team Up for New Haunted Halloween Line of Cozy Flannels, PJs and Totes Lifestyle Womenswear Designer Rosie Assoulin Teams With Target to Deliver Luxury for Less That means his entire career, from runway highs to antisemitic lows, will fall into focus at the Met. It will cover the start at his namesake label before he segued to culture-shifting work at Givenchy and later, Dior, where he led the famed house for nearly 15 years as creative director from October 1996 through March 2011. More recently, he has led Maison Margiela from 2014 through 2024. And it will not shy away from his firing by Dior when video footage surfaced showing an inebriated Galliano making antisemitic remarks in a Paris café. The tirade not only led to a professional downfall and a retreat from public life for approximately two years, Galliano was found guilty by a Paris court of public insults based on religion, race, and ethnicity. He received a fine and was forced to pay damages and court fees. Galliano’s retreat, well-detailed in reports, interviews and a documentary, included meeting with Jewish leaders, rabbis and receiving blessings from groups like the Anti-Defamation League. Per today’s news — as detailed in a press release and an exclusive report from The New York Times’ Vanessa Friedman — the Met’s exhibition is not meant to present “a conventional narrative of disgrace and redemption” but rather “how aesthetic achievement, ethical accountability and institutional recognition intersect.” In addition to his accountability for the drunken tirade, Galliano has also said recovery has been key to this new chapter of his life after alcoholism and drug addiction caused turmoil in the previous era. “John Galliano has exerted a profound influence on fashion over the past four decades,” offered Max Hollein, The Met’s Marina Kellen French director and CEO, in a statement. “His work brings historical inquiry, artistic imagination, theatrical expression and technical experimentation into dynamic relation. Drawing upon the depth of The Costume Institute’s scholarship and the breadth of The Met’s collections, ‘John Galliano: Horizons’ will offer an expansive examination of his creative practice while attending closely to the historical, cultural and ethical circumstances through which his work is understood.” Per NYT ‘s Friedman, the decision did not come easily or expeditiously. She reports that Galliano, Met Costume Institute curator Andrew Bolton, Vogue global editorial director Anna Wintour (a longtime Galliano champion), and a “handful of influential rabbis and Jewish leaders in New York City” met for a closed-door meeting in May to discuss the possibility of a Galliano exhibit. Friedman reported that it was “one of several such meetings” held with Jewish leaders over the past year. According to a press release, Galliano’s exhibit will be divided into three sections, “Bearings,” “Horizons” and “Atlas of Transformation.” It will be accompanied by a catalog penned by Bolton, published by The Met and distributed internationally by Yale University Press. “Every Galliano collection begins as a journey among things separated by time, place, or medium: portrait and posture, silhouette and story, memory and material,” per Bolton in a press release. “‘Horizons’ approaches fashion as a form of cartography, mapping not territories but affinities, tensions, and transformations. It traces how images become ideas, ideas become material, and material becomes emotion. Yet a horizon reveals not only what lies before us, but also where we stand. The exhibition therefore considers both how Galliano has remapped the world through fashion and how his conduct, its consequences, and changing cultural values have reshaped our understanding of his work.” Galliano is now designing for Zara under a two-year deal to “re-author the brand’s archive” by “deconstructing and reconfiguring them into new seasonal expressions and creations.” His first collection is expected in September. Galliano poses with models at his Christian Dior haute couture show in Paris on July 6, 2009. (Photo by Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images) Galliano and Charlize Theron at the Met Gala at New York’s Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 1, 2006. (Photo by Peter Kramer/Getty Images) THR

articles.title: Taylor Sheridan Returning for an On-Camera Role in ‘Lioness’ Season 3
articles.full_text: Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 31, 2026 6:07pm Zoe Saldaña and Taylor Sheridan in season two of 'Lioness.' Lauren Smith/Paramount+ Logo text Taylor Sheridan is getting back out in front of the camera. The creator of Lioness , as well as Landman , Mayor of Kingstown , Tulsa King and Yellowstone and its spinoffs, has a surprise on-camera role in season three of the Paramount + spy thriller, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. “He’s involved. I mean, he has a role, which is great. And the show’s better for it when he plays a role,” Thad Luckinbill told THR of Sheridan’s balancing acting with writing and producing his many television series. “He’s a great character, and he kills it. So, I love when he comes in and plays with us.” Related Stories TV A 10-Year-Old Budding "Hollywood Reporter" Gets Her First Red Carpet Experience, Interviewing the Stars of 'L.O.L. Surprise! The Next Headliner' Movies 'The Magic Faraway Tree' Team on Bringing a 1940s Family Adventure Into the Modern Era THR also reached out to Paramount for comment. While Luckinbill, who plays Kyle McManus, a field-active CIA paramilitary officer and old friend of station chief Joe (Zoe Saldaña), couldn’t say much more about what Sheridan’s role would entail, he did reveal they share scenes together. Sheridan previously appeared as CIA officer Cody Spears in a cameo during season two . It isn’t unfamiliar territory for Sheridan. Before becoming one of television’s most prolific creators, he appeared in series including Sons of Anarchy and Veronica Mars , in addition to onscreen roles in Yellowstone and 1883 . Whether it’s in front of or behind the camera, Luckinbill said he still gives every part his full attention. “He’s so real. Whether he’s an actor, writer, director or a producer, he’s still the same guy,” Luckinbill, who co-starred with Sheridan in 2018’s 12 Strong , said. “He’s gonna give you the same opinions, and he cares the same about the product. So it doesn’t really change. He is who he is and you get it. He’s full access.” Matt Gerald, who plays Army Delta Force operator Cody J, teased that the stakes are “incredibly high, if not the highest yet.” “It starts with a bang. It’s nonstop throughout the entirety of the season — and it ends with a bang.” As for the behind-the-scenes training, Gerald explained, “We started with some weapons training with some of our top military class, some of the best coaching forces guys on the planet that we were lucky enough to train with. They put us through some close quarter combat stuff. So shooting a variety of weapons, training, movement stuff, a lot of explosions, breaching doors. We did it all.” He added, “In a time where there’s a lot of war going on in the world, we’re asking our soldiers to risk life and limb, to be able to get an understanding of the things they do when they go to work every day, it’s highly rewarding.” Per Paramount+, here’s the official season three logline : “Hidden networks, foreign operatives and personal betrayals collide. Joe (Saldaña) walks the line between duty and home as unseen forces circle her world. Patterns appear where they shouldn’t, names vanish and paths rearrange. Guided by Kaitlyn (Nicole Kidman) and Westfield (Michael Kelly), Joe confronts enemies operating in the shadows, leaving her to reckon with a war that now reaches into every part of her life.” Lioness season three premieres Sunday on Paramount+. THR

articles.title: FIFA Boss Infantino Scraps World Cup Sell Off Plans After Backlash
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All July 31, 2026 6:20pm President Gianni Infantino holds the FIFA World Cup winner's trophy. Sam Hodde/Getty Images After announcing plans earlier this week for FIFA to sell off a stake in the World Cup to private investors, the president of the global soccer governing body, Gianni Infantino , has announced he’s pulling those plans. “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed. And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders,” Infantino said in a statement on Friday. Related Stories TV FIFA Boss Infantino Under Fire Over World Cup Sell Off Plans Business Opposition Grows to FIFA World Cup Sell-Off Plan “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” he continued. “Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.” The proposed plan would have consisted of FIFA setting up a new entity, FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), that would bundle soccer associated money-making operations while a significant stake would be sold to private investors. 20 percent of the company would have been sold to Thrive Capital, an invest group run by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law, Jared Kushner. Backlash was immediate, with European soccer body UEFA saying on Thursday that if the plan went through, it would boycott FIFA events , including the World Cup . Three of the four semi-finalists of the 2026 men’s World Cup hailed from Europe, including this year’s champion, Spain . Earlier this week, U.K. Prime Minister Andy Burnham released a statement online that read, “football does not belong to investors. It belongs to the people who fill the stands and who stand on the touchline week in, week out, rain or shine. The World Cup is not a product. It is the greatest competition in world sport, and it was never anyone’s to sell. Dress the deal up however you like. Once you have sold a piece of it, you have sold out.” Infantino’s statement continued, “Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.” THR

articles.title: How Jack Haven Found “Innocence” in ‘Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma’ Slasher Little Death
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content Jack Haven. Courtesy It might seem a bit jarring to hear that an actor “took a sweetness” from a character called Little Death, but Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma ’s Jack Haven found an innocence to the slasher in Jane Schoenbrun ’s latest feature. “It’s someone who isn’t killing because of a wicked and cruel instinct, but sort of just because of inevitability and curiosity,” the 31-year-old tells The Hollywood Reporter . In Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Misasma , a young filmmaker, played by Hannah Einbinder , is preparing to reboot a slasher franchise, Camp Miasma, which found Haven’s Little Death terrorizing and killing teen campers. Add the ultimate final girl, played by Gillian Anderson , and it’s an unbeatable formula. Related Stories Movies With 'Camp Miasma,' Hannah Einbinder Is Back in Another Complicated Cross-Generational Relationship Movies Karlovy Vary Fest Adds Cannes Winner 'Fjord' and 'Teenage Sex and Death at Camp Miasma' “I like a character that just doesn’t quite know how human things work, but is interested in playing with them,” Haven explains. “[There’s] an innocence and a total inability to control the people around them in a manipulative way. This character has a deep power that’s a deep centered power, but has no interest in the social dynamics.” The actor gained recognition for their role in Netflix’s Atypical , along with roles in films like Bill and Ted Face the Music . They’ve also waded into the filmmaking waters in recent years. In Camp Miasma , Haven reunites with Schoenbrun after the pair worked together on the director’s acclaimed feature I Saw the TV Glow. “Jane is one of those rare and sacred collaborations that I just feel it’s intergalactic when I get to work with them,” Haven says. “I feel a great freedom when I’m with Jane,” they continue. “When I’m talking to Jane about creating something because they have a really unlimited imagination and they can travel through dimensions.” The actor says they’ll always work with Schoenbrun when the opportunity’s presented. Adds Haven, “I pack myself and I’m ready at the door.” Below, Haven digs into the film premiering at Cannes, working as a filmmaker and the Camp Miasma sequence that the actor found to be their most physically challenging scene ever. What drew you into the movie? I would’ve said yes to anything that Jane asked me to do, but they described the character as the slasher killer in a helmet with a slobbering tongue, and I was totally in. What was the Cannes experience like? I wish I was mentally stable enough to enjoy something like Cannes, but unfortunately I’m not. The best part was that I knew it was a good thing in my mind. Probably in my body, I knew it was a good thing. My mind turned invasive species mode and was running through the rainforest, trying not to get caught. It’s like, you know that scene in The Beach when Leonardo DiCaprio goes into video game mode and he’s being chased? It’s like that level of paranoia for some reason is elicited by environments in which capitalism and film are making out. I just, something about it, I run. But seeing everyone’s hard work, this beautiful group of people with the purest souls on earth being celebrated in this way was just magnificent. Also, my mom came, and it was really special to be there with her because she’s a longtime artist. It was just amazing to see it through her eyes. How do you work through getting over that in your own head? I’ve just been working on transcending it. It’s totally an ego thing because it’s like, first of all, no one really gives a shit about anyone else. At the core of every interaction is pure love, and we know that celebrity culture is done. I think it’s hilarious that we’re still dealing with these dynamics because we know they’re not real. Seeing a movie like Camp Miasma at Cannes, people just enter this state of bliss because they are in the imaginary dimension, even if just for a moment. For some reason, that’s what we like to pay for. We like to pay for things that glitter like the imaginary, like magic. This is the way our world is built right now, it won’t always be built like this and it hasn’t always been built like this, but that’s the mental gymnastics I have to do, which honestly should be quite easy because as I said, it’s all love. You recently did your first feature as a director, right? Can you tell me a bit about what that process of transitioning to filmmaking has been like? Yes, I have two features actually, but only one is available to see. The first one I made on my iPhone, and it was really because one of my close friends, Peter, he’s 73 and he had liver cancer, so he was dying. He’s the star of the film, so I wanted to make it as quickly as possible. He got the liver transplant halfway through and he survived, and so we finished the film with him. The second film, my good friend Clyde gave me money to buy a better camera. I wrote a script for that one. The first one was improvised, and that one was more produced. Then editing it is obviously hell. My best friend Mina Walker scored the movie. We’ve just finished that one. Now, I’m writing the third one. We’re going to shoot in August and September, [and it’s] is a comedy. I believe Jane said in the director’s notes that the one shot killing spree scene was the most proud they’ve been about anything they’d made. I’d really love to hear about that scene in particular. Jane had a shot by shot with them as Little Death. It [was] made at the camp before we started shooting. It was just an iPhone edit, which I hope gets released someday. But I can’t take really any credit for it. I know what my body is doing, and it’s like 3 a.m., and I do what I must do. The hardest part was probably the camera that was strapped to me. What was that like? I read it was very heavy. I don’t even know how heavy it was, but it felt like it was as heavy at least as me. It felt like the shadow self, honestly. It was balancing that. But the camera assistant, Emma, was holding the camera, and then there were sandbags on the back so it was counterbalanced, but it’s still… The fight choreographer, stunt choreographer, Maja Aro, had this really particular movement that we practiced so much, so I knew what I was doing. The pieces were all there, but it’s still probably the hardest thing I’ve had to do as an actor, just in terms of physical intensity. The stunt people in the background, they were doing such hard work because they were throwing themselves against the wall and then falling to the rhythm of the stabs. We did it maybe eight times, and still on the last take, I screamed afterwards because I forgot something. But I guess we got it. What did you feel like seeing the scene? Totally blown away. As with the whole film, as with all of Jane’s work. Even when Jane describes something or describes an idea for a film, that’s unlike anything. It really feels like a feeling of your grandmother telling you a story as a child, it’s that wonder. THR

articles.title: ‘Barbie’ Sequel Stalled as Warner Bros. Tries to Reach Deals With Greta Gerwig, Margot Robbie, Ryan Gosling
articles.full_text: × Skip to main content By Lexi Carson Plus Icon Lexi Carson Associate Editor View All July 31, 2026 8:03pm Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling in 'Barbie' Courtesy of Warner Bros. Entertainment The Barbie sequel has hit a roadblock on its way back to Barbieland. Warner Bros. has until December to reach a deal with the stars of the 2023 film, Margot Robbie and Ryan Gosling , as well as director and co-writer Greta Gerwig , before the rights revert to Mattel, according to a report from the New York Times . The studio has been negotiating with the principal talent for months, offering them a share of the profits if the film reaches certain box office milestones. The outlet also claims that Warner Bros. Discovery CEO David Zaslav declined to approve the proposed deal because he believed it was “too generous.” Related Stories Movies Gary Oldman, Curry Barker, 'Barbie' Producer Robbie Brenner to Keynote Toronto Film Festival Lifestyle Mattel's Collectible 2026 Barbie Holiday Doll Channels Festive Representation in Red The Times went on to report that a Warner Bros. spokesperson disputed that characterization, saying talent representatives declined an offer made in May and have not yet submitted a counteroffer. “We have a rights deal with Mattel in place and have made a series of big offers to try and finalize deals to make the next Barbie film,” studio co-chairs Pam Abdy and Michael De Luca said in a statement. “Unfortunately, we have been unable to reach an agreement thus far.” The Hollywood Reporter reached out to Warner Bros. for comment, and they had nothing further to add. Gerwig and her Barbie co-writer Noah Baumbach have had an idea for Barbie 2 for a couple of years. THR first reported in 2024 that the couple was in the “early stages” of developing a story for the sequel. Barbie was a massive hit with audiences and critics, grossing $1.5 billion worldwide and earning eight Oscar nominations, winning one for best original song (“What Was I Made For?” by Billie Eilish and Finneas O’Connell). Upon its release in July 2023, the film also became a cultural phenomenon thanks to its marketing campaign, signature pink aesthetic and simultaneous release with Christopher Nolan’s Oppenheimer , dubbing the name, “Barbenheimer.” THR

articles.title: John Oliver Extends His HBO Contract to Continue ‘Last Week Tonight’ Through 2027
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 2:18pm PT John Oliver Extends His HBO Contract to Continue ‘Last Week Tonight’ Through 2027 By Michael Schneider Plus Icon Michael Schneider Variety Editor at Large franklinavenue Latest John Oliver Extends His HBO Contract to Continue ‘Last Week Tonight’ Through 2027 13 hours ago ‘Stuart Fails to Save the Universe’ Producers on Episode 2’s Surprise Kaley Cuoco Cameo as an Alternate Penny 1 day ago Banijay Americas CEO Ben Samek to Oversee Merged Banijay/All3Media Operations in the U.S. 1 day ago See All HBO Max John Oliver is staying put for now at HBO, no matter whom his “business daddy” might end up being next year. The “ Last Week Tonight With John Oliver” host has extended his contract with the network through the end of 2027, Variety has confirmed. But perhaps because of the ownership uncertainty, Oliver’s extension is only for one year, vs. its usual three-year pickups. Oliver has been vocal on “Last Week Tonight” about his concerns over Paramount Skydance’s proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery: “Yeah, not great news,” he said in a March episode . “In fact, if I may quote anyone who’s ever accidentally sat on their Roku remote, I’m in Paramount now … how the f-ck do I get out of here?’” Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House When news of Paramount’s desire to take over Warner Bros. first emerged last September, he also had this to say: “Please stay the f-ck away from us. You are not my real business daddy, and you never will be!” At the time, Oliver was critical of Paramount’s settlement with the Trump administration over its baseless lawsuit against CBS’ “60 Minutes.” He has also been critical of Bari Weiss’ takeover of CBS News. Popular on Variety Oliver resumed new episodes of “Last Week Tonight” this week after a summer hiatus , and spent much of the show dissecting Donald Trump’s latest doings — potentially also putting him in the crosshairs of the Trump-friendly Paramount Skydance owners. “Last Week Tonight” was last renewed for three years in December 2023, bringing the show up to this year and its Season 13. “Over the past decade, John and his exceptional team have combined deep research and intelligence with cutting humor to tackle a broad range of subjects, both widely discussed and unconventional,” Casey Bloys, chairman and CEO, HBO & Max Content, said in a statement at the time. “Last Week Tonight” first launched in 2014 and is now in its 13th season. The show has scored 28 Emmys; last year it won the scripted variety series and variety writing categories (where it has dominated for the last eight years). The show also has two Peabody Awards, five Critics Choice Awards, two GLAAD Media Awards, six Writers Guild Awards and eight consecutive PGA Awards. “ Last Week Tonight With John Oliver ” is produced for HBO by Avalon and Peyance Productions; executive producers are Oliver, Tim Carvell, Liz Stanton, Jon Thoday and James Taylor. Director is Paul Pennolino. THR first reported the news of Oliver’s deal extension. Loading comments... articles.title: Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman Used Pain Scale Ratings to Prep BDSM Scenes in ‘I Want Your Sex’: She ‘Hit Him Really Hard and’ It Was ‘Only a Seven or Eight’
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 2:34pm PT Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman Used Pain Scale Ratings to Prep BDSM Scenes in ‘I Want Your Sex’: She ‘Hit Him Really Hard and’ It Was ‘Only a Seven or Eight’ By Anna Tingley Plus Icon Anna Tingley Latest Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman Used Pain Scale Ratings to Prep BDSM Scenes in ‘I Want Your Sex’: She ‘Hit Him Really Hard and’ It Was ‘Only a Seven or Eight’ 13 hours ago You Can Now Land New York’s Toughest Restaurant Reservations Through DoorDash 14 hours ago How to Stream Shark Week Live Online Without Cable 5 days ago See All Cooper Hoffman had never filmed a sex scene before signing on to Gregg Araki’s erotic thriller “ I Want Your Sex .” So when he arrived on set for the first time and found himself surrounded by ball gags, stilettos, whips, chains, dildos and strap-ons, a few first-day jitters were understandable. “Even if you’re nervous to do it, you’re gonna do it,” Hoffman told Variety at the film’s Los Angeles premiere on Tuesday night. “Because there’s no reason to not do anything in this life just because you’re scared.” Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Still, how does an actor prepare to strip naked, slip into a maid’s outfit and get spanked with a leather whip? This is just one of many, many kinky situations Hoffman encounters as Elliot, a meek, wide-eyed college graduate who enters into a sadomasochistic relationship with gallery owner Erika Tracey (Olivia Wilde). Popular on Variety Increasingly, the answer comes in the form of an intimacy coordinator — a role that Araki, long known for embracing provocative themes, employed for the first time on this project. The profession, which officially unionized with SAG-AFTRA in 2024, has become an increasingly standard presence on film and television sets. Intimacy coordinator Yehuda Duenyas likens the job to that of a choreographer or stunt coordinator. “If someone is going to get their head blown off, people are like, ‘Go grab the goo gun, get the exploding head with the squibs in it, press the button and boom.’ No one really bats an eye about violence,” he says. “But when it comes to intimacy, everyone gets kind of squishy and weird.” “There are so many things to look after with intimacy scenes that no one really sees,” he continues. “It’s the same way that, with a stunt, you’re not seeing the padding or the fake hits. It just looks real, but you know there’s a lot of movie magic happening behind the scenes.” That movie magic is put to work throughout the film, which uses high-intensity montages to establish the pair’s dom-sub dynamic: Elliot crawling across the floor in pink silk lingerie, taking a spanking in a maid’s outfit, standing fully nude as a hot-pink dildo is lubed up overhead and, during a threesome-gone-wrong, getting handcuffed to a St. Andrew’s cross with a towel stuffed in his mouth. “He might have been terrified, but it wasn’t, ‘I’m terrified, I don’t want to do this.’ It was, ‘I’m terrified, and I do want to do this,'” Duenyas says of Hoffman. “He was more like, ‘Yeah, yeah, it’s the scariest thing I’ve ever done. Let’s do it.'” Below, Duenyas talks about how he prepared Wilde and Hoffman for their most intense on-screen moments, the most challenging scenes to shoot and the film’s overall messaging on sex and experimentation: There are multiple high-intensity montages that establish the nature of Olivia and Cooper’s dom-sub sexual relationship. What would surprise people about what goes into shooting scenes like that? With those montages specifically, we had moments where we would say, “Okay, I’m hitting you this hard. What is that on a scale of one to 10?” Cooper would say, “That’s a zero.” She’d say, “Really?” Then she would go harder, and he’d say, “Okay, that’s a two. That’s a three. That’s a five.” Olivia realized, “I can hit you really hard, and it’s only registering as a seven or an eight.” We had a bunch of little things like that so they could, number one, have a language for communicating about the physicality and, number two, feel like they could talk about what was happening while also making it look good. ©Magnolia Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection Gregg told Variety that Olivia came onto the set with much more experience doing nude scenes, while Cooper was “terrified.” What was your process for making him more comfortable from the beginning? If you’ve ever gone skydiving, you might be terrified, but you really want to go skydiving. You’re there to do it. Or, if you’ve ever jumped off a cliff into water or stood on a high diving board, you’re on top of that thing to do it, even though you’re scared. So, yeah, he might have been terrified, but it wasn’t, “I’m terrified, I don’t want to do this.” It was, “I’m terrified, and I do want to do this.” Is someone terrified because they’re thinking, “This is a no for me. This is a hard boundary, but I’m involved in this thing and I already said yes, so what am I going to do?” Are they biting their nails or is it, “I’m fucking terrified. Let’s do this really well. How are we going to do this?” That was Cooper’s stance. I wouldn’t say he was terrified. If you’ve ever talked to him, he’s super cool and very together. He was more like, “Yeah, yeah, it’s the scariest thing I’ve ever done. Let’s do it.” It was very matter-of-fact. He approaches almost everything he does by diving headfirst into it in this really beautiful way. He’s an incredible performer. How did the dom-sub type of sex scenes differ from the more traditional sex scenes you’re used to working on? Sure, there are differences, but in terms of the way we approach intimacy coordination as a craft, it’s not that different. Olivia had also done a lot of research. Everyone brought what they knew and the type of story they wanted to tell. Gregg obviously did as well. In this particular film, we’re dealing with these very specific, blurry and complicated power dynamics. That’s the story. The story shows up in their relationship, their work lives and their sexual lives together. What was so fun was finding the character of their intimacy together. Every intimate scene we work on has a different type of character, and that was the character for this one. Is it different? Yes. BDSM and these kinds of lifestyle scenes, if you want to call them that, are different from something like a “Heated Rivalry” scene. It’s a different type of intimacy, but we approach it the way we would approach anything else. ©Magnolia Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection I’m guessing one of the main differences is how many props are involved. What was the most challenging scene to work on? The threesome scene, from a blocking and camera-angle perspective, took a minute to figure out. When I say “a minute,” we had a really compressed shooting schedule. We shot all the intimacy within the first five days. We did all of that stuff upfront. Also from an intensity perspective, that scene required a lot. There was a lot to work out. It wasn’t, “Oh my God, this is so hard.” It was a puzzle to put together in terms of the traffic patterns, the handcuffing and how to get out of the handcuffs quickly. Are we fiddling with keys, or are we just getting out of them? There are a lot of little details. Which details are you going to skip for the sake of the story, and which details are you going to keep in to maintain the flavor and the vibe of the story? All of the restraint scenes needed a little more care. Getting an actor into restraints on the St. Andrew’s cross wasn’t that complicated of a scene. But when you have to shoot it from three angles in three different ways, and an actor is strapped to a St. Andrew’s cross, can they get out easily if they need to pee? Gregg recently talked to Variety about Gen Z’s attitude towards sex and what he hoped to accomplish with this film. What are your thoughts on this mission statement? Gregg wants people to go out and argue. He really wants people to argue about it and say, “Well, I thought it was this,” or, “I thought it was that,” or, “I think that’s bullshit,” or, “I think that’s true.” He wants those conversations. I love Gregg, and I’ve loved his work over the years. He has contributed so much. I learned about intimacy through watching Gregg Araki films as a young person. I feel like we owe him for his contribution to intimacy in cinema. He has contributed so much to the film canon. Where would we be without those pieces he has made and the work he has put in? I can’t speak for Gen Z, and I don’t know whether Gen Z is having less or more sex. But I hope people see this film and want to take a chance on love, take a chance on experimentation, take a chance on feeling something and allow themselves to be taken to a place they haven’t been before.
