articles.title: ‘Cape Fear’ Creator Nick Antosca on That Shocking Final Sequence and Making Big Changes From Scorsese’s Version
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 3:00pm PT ‘Cape Fear’ Creator Nick Antosca on That Shocking Final Sequence and Making Big Changes From Scorsese’s Version By Daniel D'Addario Plus Icon Daniel D'Addario Chief TV Critic DPD_ Latest Evan Rachel Wood Says ‘It’s Sad’ Not to Be Asked Back for ‘Practical Magic 2’ After Offering to Return: ‘It Seems Like They’re Not Following the Book’ 4 days ago ‘Am I Supposed to Be a Comedian?’: Donald Trump’s Bizarre White House Correspondent’s Dinner Speech Had Few Laughing 6 days ago How ‘Cape Fear,’ Apple TV’s Timely Adaptation, Became Summer’s Grisliest Hit 1 week ago See All SPOILER ALERT: This story contains spoilers for “The Executioners,” the finale of “ Cape Fear ,” now streaming on Apple TV . In the final moments of “Cape Fear,” Anna Bowden realizes that she’ll never truly be free of the man who’s been stalking her family. The Bowden family has defeated Max Cady (Javier Bardem), the ex-convict who blames Anna (Amy Adams) and her husband Tom (Patrick Wilson) for his incarceration, in an epic battle during which he invaded their home, placed Anna and Tom on “trial” for colluding against him and threatened their children Natalie and Zack (Lily Collias and Joe Anders). Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House During that intense confrontation, Anna stunned Max with evidence she obtained at his family’s houseboat that his sister Crystal (Juliette Lewis, who also starred as a different character in the 1991 film version of this story) actually committed the murder for which Max was convicted, having killed Max’s pregnant wife, ripping the unborn fetus from her body. Max’s child actually lived, growing nearly into adulthood while Max spent his life mourning him; in a bitter irony, Max killed him in the chaos that ensued at the Cady family boat at the start of the finale. It’s our definitive proof, too, that Max never did what Tom, as prosecutor, put him away for, and Anna, as defense attorney, didn’t block. For all his crimes against the Bowdens, Max began his legal journey as an innocent man. Popular on Variety Javier Bardem in ‘Cape Fear.’ (Apple TV) By the time he’s defeated, Max seems utterly broken; the last we see of this seemingly invulnerable agent of chaos is his sputtering out water on the Bowdens’ deck, ready to be apprehended by the authorities. But the family’s victory is only conditional. After Anna declares, “Let him die in a cage,” sparing Max’s life, we jump ahead in time to a backyard barbecue, echoing the one that, in happier times, opened the series. Back then, the Bowdens were surrounded by friends, but here, it’s only the four family members, trapped in their fortress. We see Natalie watching a true-crime influencer’s video shot just outside their front door before she joins the rest. As Tom prepares their meal, he glances nervously over his shoulder, toward the pool where he nearly died; Zack sits in eerie silence while his parents force bonhomie, joking about keeping the secret of how good his cheeseburgers are. After Tom refers to Anna as a “psychopath” for ordering her burger without cheese, lettuce, or bun, she declares, “Guilty” — and the verbal reminder of just what they’ve suffered through, and how similar they may be to the guilty psychopath they defeated, overcomes Anna’s defenses. She looks over her shoulder, her face beginning to twist in agony and fear, as the film suddenly shifts to a bright-red filter: End of series, though not of Anna’s psychological journey. Nick Antosca created this version of “Cape Fear” — the third onscreen adaptation of John D. MacDonald’s novel “The Executioners,” following big-screen takes in 1962 and 1991 — and co-wrote the finale. He spoke to Variety via Zoom about that shocking final sequence, the revelation of Max’s innocence and what lies ahead for all the Bowdens, including the daughter who may very well be the product of Anna and Max’s years-ago coupling when they were lawyer and client. I was genuinely struck by the final scene of the series, in which the family is speaking in a sort of coded language that they understand implicitly — and we see just how haunted Anna is. Will the family always be haunted, do you think? The Bowden family will always be haunted by Max Cady and the memory of what happened during this story. The 1991 movie has always struck me in terms of its ending narration, where Juliette’s [Lewis’ character] goes, “And then we never spoke of it again,” basically. You’re just like, Yeah, but I bet you thought about it — still thinking about it today. I wanted our version of that energy. That moment when Tom looks over his shoulder — there’s no sound in the mix motivating that. They’re just going to be looking; they’re going to be hearing things. Lily Collias in ‘Cape Fear.’ (Apple TV) Before Natalie joins the family, she’s fiddling with an envelope from a DNA-testing service that she hasn’t opened yet. One wonders, will she ever open it? One does wonder that. She’s also — very intentionally, it’s barely seen, there’s no close-up of it — wearing an ankle bracelet, too. They’re all going to be dealing with the aftermath of stuff that’s gone on, and they’re probably going to have to sell that house, because I don’t know that they’re going to be allowed to practice law in Georgia in the immediate future. I always imagined that coda — that they would be trying to recreate the first scene, where they’re by their pool and having a barbecue, and things are safe and good. The fact that the series ends with Natalie’s parentage still unresolved feels like a real conversation-starter. Do you have in your mind an answer to the question of who Natalie’s father is? Yes, I do. And you wrote with that in mind. Yes. As a viewer I could go either way! I’m glad. It’s interesting that the finale takes place in the Bowden family home, as opposed to, as in the films, on the boat. In a way, Cady’s intrusion into the home feels even more charged. A lot of people asked as we were getting the last scripts in, or even before, “Is the climax of the show going to be a fight on the storm in the houseboat?” I always felt that we needed to go to the houseboat. But it felt like the conclusion of this version of the Bowden story belonged in the domestic space, so we were to bring the storm to them, and put the trial in their own home. That’s what it felt like it needed to be — and that fight in the pool should feel elemental and primal. We’re in the middle of a hurricane, but it’s their home. Amy Adams in ‘Cape Fear.’ (Apple TV) The violence is really gnarly in the final confrontation. I think of myself as pretty strong-stomached, and I really couldn’t watch the scene where Max convinces a drugged Zack to almost bite his own tongue off. That was one of many shots where we spent a lot of time in the editing room being like, “How many frames of this should we show? How much is too much?” That and the head-smash within the prison in Episode 2. One of the more fun experiences I’ve had in the editing room was being in the edit on that with Martin Scorsese on FaceTime with me, going over it, saying, “Yeah, roll the cut a couple frames, right before the head starts to explode.” Just calibrating, you know, to the exact frame, like how we were going to smash that skinhead’s head. I’m curious about the decision to have the Bowden family spare Max’s life. It’s a departure from the 1991 version. In the 1962 version, he lets him live. We were deciding between those two potential endings. In that moment, the Bowdens are clinging to a last shred of social order and moral order that they believe themselves to be part of. They don’t want to kill a man in front of their children. You could argue that, of all the terrible decisions the Bowdens make throughout this season of television, not killing Max is one of the worst decisions that they could make. From a sheerly pragmatic point of view, they will, of course, always wonder if he’s found his way out of prison and is just around the corner! He’s almost certainly going to prison for a long, long time; he has done a lot of verifiably bad stuff. But if somebody else made the show and I’m watching it, I’m going, “Kill him! Please!” Amy Adams and Patrick Wilson in ‘Cape Fear.’ (Apple TV) The previous versions depicted a Max who maybe should not have been found guilty of their crimes due to mitigating circumstances, but were not literally innocent. This Max, we realize, simply did not do the crime for which he was convicted. It flips the story on its head. So he was wrongly convicted of this murder, but he was a really bad guy in general, and prison narrowed and sharpened that darkness within him. It’s all directed right toward the people he blames. It’s interesting that you talk about the evolution of previous Maxes. In the book, he’s not even the client. He’s just a guy Sam saw committing a crime and testified against him — that’s it. Once you get to the ‘91 version, he was his actual client. That was [screenwriter] Wesley Strick’s innovation, which I think is really brilliant. Each innovation takes the moral complexity to a different level. Early in the episode, Anna provokes Max into choking her in public by declaring that he killed his wife and showing compromising videos of his communications with a past mistress. He’s giving a press conference, and she says just the right things to enrage him. It felt in that moment as if she had an intuitive sense of what buttons to push to get him to drop the facade of control. Can you talk about odd bond and mutual understanding they share? They had a bond, to some degree, in the past, and she’s had to hold herself back for most of the series. Once all is lost for her — at the end of Episode 8, where all of her family is scattered to the winds and locked away, and she’s started drinking again, there is a kind of freedom in that. She goes on her adventure in Episode 9, she gets the information, and then she’s able to use that as ammunition at the beginning of Episode 10. It’s because she has nothing to lose anymore, so she’s able to let loose and press all of his buttons. Before that, she still has the veneer of civility holding her back. Having known my share of attorneys, I also recognized in her a desire to use logic and reason to puzzle her way out of Max stalking her. It seemed to me she triumphed when she started playing according to Max’s own terms. The Bowdens are frustrating for a while, because they want to believe that they’ve got it under control. But I think it’s the case that — like, in your own life, you don’t want to believe things are as bad as they are. Would you move right away? Would you uproot your family and get out? I don’t think you would do that instantly. It’s hard to make big moves in life, sometimes, until it’s too late. Moving is really hard! At the beginning of Episode 3, there’s a scene where random people come into their backyard, and Tom just goes out to talk to them. When we were writing that episode, we were thinking “What are the things that make it feel like your space is permeable? Like you’re under threat?” Around that time, I was at my house, and I walked out into my backyard, and there were some people there. It was just like the show, although I don’t have a castle in Georgia. I was like, “What are you doing here?” and we had this crazy conversation. Later, when the police came, they were like, “Why did you just go up and talk to people who were in your yard hanging out? When that happens, call the police.” But I don’t know. You don’t necessarily think about your own life in the way you would if you were watching characters on TV. You don’t take action that way sometimes until you’re like, Oh, yeah, I guess that really was a threat. I think among the most powerful elements of the series is that the Bowdens are slow to take action in part because they think of themselves as fundamentally good, despite some lapses in the past. Max thrusting his perspective at them forces them to consider how different they really are from Max — that’s very potent. There’s an energy of collective guilt and “No, no, I’m a good person” that feels like part of the culture of modern-day America. That came by osmosis into the show. Do you think the Bowdens are bad people? I think they’re complicated people. They’re very flawed people. This interview has been edited and condensed. articles.title: ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 4:14pm PT ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles 'It's the hardest movie I've ever had to make,' director Jeff Wadlow says. By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down 11 hours ago ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles 11 hours ago ‘Big Brother 28’ Contestant Jason Breaks Down That Explosive Tea Party and Not Letting Kamu ‘Bully’ Him: ‘Isn’t It Interesting How the Six People in Power Were So Threatened by a Drag Queen?’ 16 hours ago See All Courtesy of Amazon Studio When “The Devil’s Mouth” director Jeff Wadlow met the cast of his bloody shark movie, he made one thing clear. “‘Listen, this is going to be the most physically demanding job you’ve ever had. Not just because of the stunt work and all the underwater work, but the fact that when you have a simple dialogue scene, you’re going to be treading water,'” Wadlow recalls telling Kathryn Newton , Lana Condor and the rest of the ensemble. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Written by Aja Gabel and Myung Joh Wesner, “The Devil’s Mouth” was named to the Black List back in 2019. Newton and Condor lead the cast as Sara and Max, two best friends whose friendship is tested after they get trapped in a freshwater cave — along with the rest of their college buddies, played by Gavin Casalegno, Tommi Rose and Nico Hiraga — while taking a trip to Thailand. Popular on Variety Of course, things get complicated when a bull shark enters the scene. In order to prep for the intensive shoot, the actors spent two weeks treading water, doing breath holds and training with real kayaks. Besides one stunt where Newton’s character had to hop off a 35-foot cliff into a shallow pool of water, all the actors were game to do their own stunts — safely, of course. “All the rock climbing, diving, underwater work, breath holds, getting dragged around on winches, that was all them,” Wadlow says. Known for helming lower-budget horror films for Blumhouse like “Imaginary,” “Fantasy Island” and “Truth or Dare,” Wadlow was first approached about directing the film during a meeting in which he was laser-focused on pitching his dream “G.I. Joe” trilogy. He had some hesitations when, instead, the words “shark movie” were mentioned. “I said, ‘I really don’t want to just do a shark movie unless there’s something new,'” Wadlow recalls. Then when he heard about the one-location aspect of the film, his creative juices began flowing, and he worked with Gabel and Wesner to rewrite the script. “Now we’re talking about an intersection between the shark movie genre and the claustrophobic horror movie,” he says. “I was blown away by how good it was because the character dynamics were complex and interesting. There’s a really nuanced investigation of female friendship.” Below, Wadlow breaks down casting Newton and Condor against usual type, how his team built 13 sets on two soundstages to pull off the illusion of an endless cave in Thailand, and why “The Devil’s Mouth” is “the hardest movie” he’s made to date. Talking about casting this friend group, what made Kathryn and Lana perfect for this central dynamic? What’s funny about casting this film is both Kathryn and Lana thought they should be playing the other part. And you can kind of see it! Having made the movie, I only see Kathryn as Sara, and I only see Lana as Max. But on the page, the characters were sort of similar to characters that they had played before. I ultimately think that made the movie so much more interesting because it forced Kathryn to stretch and grow and define a quieter character to play. She normally plays really out-there dynamic characters, and Sara’s got an internal journey; Lana usually plays like the good girl, this was a chance for her to play someone with a little more bite. They both really rose to the challenge and did it together. They became best friends while we were making the movie. We shot this whole thing in Thailand. Thailand is so far away from America that if you leave from the East Coast, you go through the Middle East, and if you leave from the West Coast, you go through Japan. It’s literally on the opposite side of the planet, and so there were no long weekends going home. Once we were there, we were all there, and it was a Thai movie. There were about less than a dozen Westerners working on it. How did you go about finding the cave? What were the biggest logistical challenges to filming inside? It’s the hardest movie I’ve ever had to make. I mean, in 85% of the movie, the characters are swimming in water. Movie cameras in water do not get along, as we all know! And just like casting this movie, I had this crazy curveball at the last minute where it was written for Mexico and we were going to shoot in the Dominican Republic. I was 10 days away from leaving and the studio calls me up and says, “Hey, some sound stages and a crew just became available in Bangkok. Can you shoot Thailand for Mexico?” And I was like, “Well, that’s bonkers. What are you guys talking about? That would be so challenging and I don’t really see the point.” And on top of that, I’m allergic to peanuts! I can’t go and spend six months in Thailand, I will probably die. I’m being serious, I go into anaphylactic shock, and they’re like, “We’ll get you a second assistant whose only job will be to feed you, make you dinner reservations, keep you alive and get your driver, in addition to your U.S. assistant!” I started thinking about the soccer team that got lost in the flooded cave system in Thailand, and how that was a part of our collective consciousness at the time and really in the zeitgeist. And I started doing some more research on freshwater cave systems in Thailand, and it started to feel a little bit more dangerous — a little bit more off the beaten path, a little bit more exotic, and I thought that would increase the credibility of what transpired. If it was just a system that tourists went to all the time in Mexico, for them to have gotten into this kind of trouble seemed a little less plausible. It also seemed like help would be there a lot sooner. But suddenly, you start setting it in a remote part of Thailand, it just feels further, more out the realm of these characters’ normal worlds. How did you approach filming the caves and meet the challenge of this one location? I wanted there to be this increasing sense of claustrophobia, so I started really wide and big. I wanted to make the trip look awesome and fun, and the location seem beautiful and appealing. I didn’t want the audience to ever go like, “Why are these people on this trip? This seems like a bad idea.” I wanted it to be obvious why they’re on the trip. It’s an amazing place to visit. Then I wanted to go into real caves that were mysterious and beautiful and not foreboding at all. I wanted the audience on the adventure, so I found real freshwater caves where rescue divers train. And then once they go around the corner, I went on a soundstage because shooting this movie in a real cave would be impossible. Forget just the lighting — the stunt work and safety issues would be massive. So once they’re in the cave system, we’re on a soundstage. We built a 120-foot long, 70-foot wide cave set and flooded it with five feet of water. We had one other set that was like 60-by-70 feet that had 15 feet of water. Between those two sets, I shot every cave. So we had 13 sets on two stages. It was just about turning them over and being really creative. Alec Hammond, my production designer, is just a mad scientist. We figured out how to shoot every square foot of every rock and make it look like it’s a different cave just by using lighting tricks and key set-pieces that we would turn or rotate. It was really difficult. There are multiple scenes where they swim off the set and they just swim back onto the same set. What were some of the biggest considerations for filming and lighting the underwater sequences? The lighting was really challenging because you want it to feel dark, but it can’t be darkness, right? We wanted to use the headlamps to motivate light, but you couldn’t really use them because if you tilted them down or got them anywhere near the lens, the lens would just flare out. We did a lot of experimentation with the headlamps. James Kniest, my director of photography, is also very good at his job. We ended up building these custom headlamps where we can control the luminance. But also we could angle them. And we would often yell from monitor like, “Hey, Lana, two clicks up!” And the cast knew that meant tilt it up, two clicks. And if you really study the movie, most of the time their headlamps are not pointed anywhere useful. But you see the light glowing, and in your mind it kind of motivates a general fill — that allowed us to come in with movie lights and get an exposure. I do think it works. I mean, if you study it, it falls apart pretty quickly. Ultimately, it was a digital system. It was much more about all the stuff that went around the cameras — the underwater housing, the HydroFlex, all those systems that we were using. That was another massive challenge with this film because I couldn’t use a dolly, couldn’t use a steadicam. I couldn’t even do handheld shots because when the camera is in water, even at water level, it has to be in the HydroFlex underwater housing. That weighs 120 pounds alone. You’re not doing a handheld shot, you got to use buoyancy to keep it up. I basically had to learn an entirely new cinematic language. I couldn’t use long lenses. I brought in Pete McCaffrey, who’s this legendary New Zealand camera operator, and he was just on the technocrane all day everyday. That was the only way I could really get the camera in and do some more traditional moves. But even those are impossible because you can’t drop marks in the water! How do the actors know where to go? In addition to getting to work with the local crew, what were some of the biggest benefits of filming in Thailand? As far as the actual economic incentives, the cost of living is much lower over there. We got a lot more bang for our buck. At a certain point, the cost of living can price a movie out of an area. If you’re having to pay a certain wage so people can live in that area, the studios only want to invest a certain amount of money in a movie. You can’t just physically make the movie there. And so sometimes, I thought a little bit about, “Alright, well we’re paying less than we would elsewhere. How do I feel about that?” And it was explained to me that this was a film industry hungry for projects. These were outstanding wages given the cost of living in that area and they were thrilled to have the work. So that’s how I wrapped my head around it. I really embraced Thailand as a character in the film and tried to make it feel like we couldn’t have shot the movie anywhere else. It wasn’t just about economic incentives or labor costs or equipment costs. The industry is really excited right now about the success of films like “Obsession” and “Backrooms” from younger directors. What do you make of these conversations happening in horror spaces? I mean, it’s just hard. It’s always going to be hard to get movies made. It’s not like Disney made “Obsession,” or Netflix made “Backrooms.” It’s not like major studios are embracing this kind of filmmaking. These are filmmakers that fought like hell to get their movies made, and I’m so happy that they’re enjoying this kind of success. I don’t think it’s going to make it any easier, though, to make movies. It might make it a little bit easier for Curry Barker to make his movie, obviously. But that’s the exception. That’s not the rule. I don’t think you’re going to see major studios chasing down young filmmakers who have had success with a couple YouTube shorts to make wide releases. Maybe I’m cynical, but I just don’t see that happening. I think it’s still going to be hard. It’s almost always going to be hard, and it’s hard for a reason because it tests you, and for that reason, only people who can really do it are able to keep doing it. “The Devil’s Mouth” is now streaming on Prime Video. articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 4:47pm PT ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down By Matt Minton Plus Icon Matt Minton mminton@variety.com Latest ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Leaks Online: Millions Watched Bootleg Before It Was Taken Down 10 hours ago ‘The Devil’s Mouth’ Director Breaks Down His Bloody, One-Location Shark Movie, Those ‘Demanding’ Stunts and Why Kathryn Newton and Lana Condor Wanted to Switch Roles 11 hours ago ‘Big Brother 28’ Contestant Jason Breaks Down That Explosive Tea Party and Not Letting Kamu ‘Bully’ Him: ‘Isn’t It Interesting How the Six People in Power Were So Threatened by a Drag Queen?’ 15 hours ago See All ©Sony Pictures/Courtesy Everett Collection While Marvel fans are expected to turn out in droves to see “ Spider-Man: Brand New Day ” in theaters this weekend, a high-quality bootleg of the film leaked on X, with millions of people having viewed it. Posted by an account named Fredrick Bryan at 6:05 a.m. PT, the leaked video reached 5.9 million accounts and counting, with over 143,000 people liking the post and 10,000 people resharing before it was taken down around 3:25 p.m. PT. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Several other X accounts also posted copies, though most didn’t last long on the platform. Studios typically send infringement notices to those posting unauthorized copies, though it can be difficult to keep ahead of the volume of posting for the most popular new films. Popular on Variety Sony had no comment. “Brand New Day” is far from the first big-budget film to leak online. Last week, Christopher Nolan’s tentpole “The Odyssey” leaked on X with its own high-quality bootleg. It reached 2.1 million views within two and a half hours and was eventually taken down with a notice. The account itself was suspended as well. Addressing “The Odyssey” leak, Universal issued a statement to Variety on Sunday: “We became aware of the unauthorized posting of the film and immediately initiated takedown protocols. We take copyright infringement seriously and will pursue all appropriate remedies to protect our content and intellectual property rights.” Regardless of the leak, “Brand New Day” is already doing exceptional business at the box office. It made a record-breaking $72 million in previews, including Tuesday early access screenings — the most of any movie in history. That placed it above “Avengers: Endgame,” which grossed $60 million in Thursday previews. “Brand New Day” sees the return of Tom Holland as the famous web-slinger, with Emmy-winner Zendaya returning as MJ. The cast also includes Sadie Sink in a mystery role, Jon Bernthal and Jacob Batalon. ‘Chimney Town: Frozen in Time’ Sells Wide Across Europe Ahead of Annecy French Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Berlinale Title ‘Members of the Problematic Family’ to Open Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Javier Bardem Politely Warned ‘Cape Fear’ Co-Star About Grabbing Her Hair During Attack Scene and Apologized in Advance: ‘I’m So Sorry, My Love’
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 6:00pm PT Javier Bardem Politely Warned ‘Cape Fear’ Co-Star About Grabbing Her Hair During Attack Scene and Apologized in Advance: ‘I’m So Sorry, My Love’ By Antonio Ferme Plus Icon Antonio Ferme Latest ‘Obsession’ Star Inde Navarrette Confirms Meeting With ‘X-Men’ Director Jake Schreier and Would Love to Play Mystique 18 hours ago ‘The Odyssey’: What Academics Are Saying About Christopher Nolan’s Epic 2 weeks ago Why Aren’t There More Imax 70mm Screens for ‘The Odyssey’? ‘It’s Not Practical,’ Company Says 2 weeks ago See All Getty Images In 2007, Javier Bardem delivered one of the century’s most chilling performances as Anton Chigurh in “No Country for Old Men.” Nearly two decades later, he’s proved once again he could convincingly play a sociopath, reimagining the vengeful murderer Max Cady on Apple TV +’s hit summer series “ Cape Fear .” Cady was previously played by Robert Mitchum in 1962 and Robert De Niro in 1991, but the brilliance of Bardem’s performance lies in the long stretches of perceived stillness, heightening the tension of the cat-and-mouse game he plays with the Bowden family, which star Lily Collias described as “a lot of fun” but “sometimes very jarring.” “We’re playing cat and mouse, and then the cameras turn off, and I still feel like a mouse,” Collias told Variety at the “Cape Fear” finale screening in New York. “And he still feels like Tom from ‘Tom and Jerry.’” Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Collias plays Natalie Bowden, the daughter of Anna (Amy Adams) and Tom (Patrick Wilson), two lawyers who Bardem’s Cady blames for his incarceration. After 10 episodes of buildup, the series finale depicts an epic battle in which Cady invades the Bowden’s home, placing Anna and Tom on “trial” for colluding against him and threatening their children. Popular on Variety “[Episode] 10 felt almost like a play,” Collias said. “It was just the family and him in the house, and we were doing the most insane things and laughing so hard off camera. It felt like such a joy that it was actually a beautiful time.” Before filming one violent sequence in which Cady grabs Natalie by the hair, Collias says Bardem politely apologized in advance and made sure she felt comfortable with the physicality. “We would go through such weird circumstances, it’s little things that make me still giggle to this day,” Collias said. “In Episode 10, there’s one point where he has to grab me by my hair, and before the scene, he’s like, ‘I’m so sorry, my love. Is it OK if I just — I’m going to grab you like that?’ I’m like, ‘Yeah, that’s fine.’ Then we start rolling and I see this thing coming up to me and I’m like, ‘What the fuck?! Well, OK, that’s your job!’” When asked about filming the intense finale scenes, Bardem smirked, explaining how he’s learned to lean into the “play” involved with acting as he’s gotten older. “For me, it’s more about a game,” Bardem said. “You use your imagination to jump in and step out of it. I respect everybody’s process, as long as those processes respect other people’s processes. For me, the fun part is to really be part of a group of people that imagine things that don’t exist, and they create it together based on the fact that it’s all a big lie.” Berlinale Title ‘Members of the Problematic Family’ to Open Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (EXCLUSIVE) ‘Chimney Town: Frozen in Time’ Sells Wide Across Europe Ahead of Annecy French Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan
articles.full_text: Jul 31, 2026 11:41pm PT FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan By Leo Barraclough Plus Icon Leo Barraclough International Features Editor LeoBarraclough Latest FIFA Chief Gianni Infantino on the Ropes as He Ditches Controversial $20 Billion Private Investment Plan 4 hours ago Gary Oldman, ‘Obsession’ Director Curry Barker and ‘Barbie’ Producer Robbie Brenner Among Toronto Market Speakers 23 hours ago World Cup Boycott Backed by All 55 UEFA Countries as Asian, North and Central American, Caribbean Members Oppose FIFA Stake Sale 1 day ago See All Courtesy of Getty Gianni Infantino , the embattled president of soccer’s governing body FIFA , has abandoned his controversial plan to create a $20 billion company, FIFA Forward Enterprise, that would control the commercial rights to its events, principally the World Cup. In a statement released late Friday, Infantino said it had “become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place.” Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House The survival of Infantino, who is up for re-election for a fourth term as president at the FIFA Congress in March, is now in doubt. Popular on Variety Infantino said, “Our purpose has always been – and will always be – to unite and improve. Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game.” The climbdown by Infantino follows a threat by European countries, represented by the continent’s soccer governing body UEFA, to boycott all FIFA events, including the World Cup, if the plan moved forward. Opposition to Infantino’s plan had also come from Concacaf, which governs soccer in North, Central America and the Caribbean, and the sport’s governing body in Asia, the Asian Football Confederation. Resistance to the plan had also come from within FIFA. Carlos Cordeiro, Infantino’s senior adviser on global strategy and governance, resigned over the issue, saying the proposal was “a bad deal” for soccer and would “mortgage” its future. Then on Friday, the organization’s chief operating officer Kevin Lamour said its own administration had been “deceived” about the project. Lamour described the plan as “the project of one person,” and said, “the time has now come for [soccer’s] political leaders to ask themselves the right questions and make the right decisions.” Lamour added that he had a duty of loyalty to “certain values” and supporting his colleagues. “If that means I lose my job, then so be it. I will understand and respect that decision. At least I’ll sleep well tonight.” Under Infantino’s proposal, each FIFA member country would have received an initial payment of $20 million and a doubling of their annual stipend to $5 million. This would have been partially funded by the sale of a roughly 20% stake in FIFA Forward Enterprise to an investor group led by Thrive Eternal. Thrive Eternal is run by Joshua Kushner, whose brother Jared Kushner is married to President Donald Trump’s daughter Ivanka. articles.title: ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 2:17am PT ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘The Inbetweeners’ Reunion Movie in the Works at Netflix With Original Lead Cast to Return 1 hour ago ‘The Odyssey’ Craze Continues as New BFI Imax Screenings Sell Out in Under 30 Minutes (EXCLUSIVE) 19 hours ago Irish Indie Film ‘Lemonade,’ Starring Barry Keoghan, Reveals First Images and Plot Details (EXCLUSIVE) 21 hours ago See All Everett Collection “ The Inbetweeners ” — the hit Brit teen comedy series from the late 2000s that spawned two successful spin-off films — is officially back. A reunion movie is now in the works at Netflix , Variety has confirmed, with the original lead cast of Simon Bird, Joe Thomas, Blake Harrison and James Buckley understood to be attached, although final deals are yet to be finalized. The news comes less than a year after rights holders Banijay U.K. revealed that it had struck a deal with “The Inbetweeners” creators Iain Morris and Damon Beesley and their Fudge Park Productions that, at the time, they said “paves the way for the return of the hit comedy title.” But it was then unknown in what shape or form — and on what platform — that return would look like. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House Netflix, it seems, has fallen for the show’s famed foul-mouthed library of hilariously puerile quotes. Popular on Variety Originally broadcast on E4 in the U.K. between 2008 and 2010, “The Inbetweeners” follows the misadventures of suburban teenager Will MacKenzie (Bird) and his friends Simon Cooper (Thomas), Neil Sutherland (Harrison) and Jay Cartwright (Buckley) at the fictional Rudge Park Comprehensive as they navigated school life, friendship, male bonding, lad culture and failed sexual encounters. It was originally conceived as a more realistic counterpoint to fellow hit Brit teen show “Skins,” showcasing an adolescence that is awkward and — as Morris suggested at the time — mostly “crap.” After three seasons, two hit movies followed, released in 2011 and 2014 respectively. The first set a record for the biggest opening weekend for a U.K. comedy at the time of its release with the sequel also breaking box office records. “Incredibly exciting to be plotting more adventures for our four favourite friends (ooh friends),” Morris and Beesley said after the news that “The Inbetweeners” would return in 2025. Netflix declined to comment. ‘Chimney Town: Frozen in Time’ Sells Wide Across Europe Ahead of Annecy French Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Berlinale Title ‘Members of the Problematic Family’ to Open Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Massive Attack Duo Banned From Singapore Over Palestinian Flag Display
articles.full_text: Aug 1, 2026 2:26am PT Massive Attack Duo Banned From Singapore Over Palestinian Flag Display By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Massive Attack Duo Banned From Singapore Over Palestinian Flag Display 1 hour ago Oscar-Qualifying Bengaluru International Short Film Festival Expands to 10 Arenas, Adds AI and Dance Competitions (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago ‘Harry Potter and the Cursed Child’ Celebrates 10 Years as Longest-Running Two-Part Play in Modern West End History – Global Bulletin 2 days ago See All Getty Images Both members of Massive Attack have been permanently barred from re-entering Singapore after unfurling a Palestinian flag during the British trip-hop group’s concert in the city-state, according to a joint statement from the Singapore Police Force and the Infocomm Media Development Authority (IMDA). The statement said police investigated both band members for “their actions of support for a political cause and unfurling of a foreign flag” during the show at The Star Theatre on July 29. Following the investigation, and in consultation with the Attorney-General’s Chambers, police administered stern warnings to both men for offences under Section 3 of the Foreign National Emblems (Control of Display) Act 1949 and Section 16 of the Public Order Act. Related Stories Jalen Brunson Talks Taylor Swift’s Wedding, Giving Back and Whether the Knicks Will Visit the Trump White House “Both men will also be banned from re-entering Singapore,” the statement said. Popular on Variety According to the statement, the event organizer had acknowledged the licensing conditions attached to the concert beforehand, but both band members held up a “foreign flag” onstage during the performance, with one shouting “Free Palestine.” The IMDA said it is investigating a possible breach of several licence conditions, including one barring performers from displaying flags tied to any cause, and will act once that inquiry concludes. The regulator added it will not approve any future application for the band to perform in Singapore given the entry ban. The concert was the band’s only scheduled Singapore date on its current tour, with video of the flag display circulating widely online alongside footage of the crowd joining in chants of “Free Palestine.” The two men are Massive Attack’s founding members, Robert “3D” Del Naja and Grant “Daddy G” Marshall, who make up its current touring lineup; authorities did not name them in the statement. Singapore maintains strict rules on the public display of foreign flags and emblems without a permit, framing the laws as necessary to protect the country’s racial and religious harmony. The joint statement reiterated that position, with authorities saying they “take a serious view of acts which could potentially harm the racial and religious harmony in Singapore” and urging the public, including foreigners, “to refrain from importing foreign politics” into the country. “The peace and harmony between different races and religions in Singapore should not be taken for granted, and we must not let external events affect our society,” the statement said. Massive Attack has been among the more vocal acts in music in its support for Palestinian causes. Del Naja was arrested earlier this year during a demonstration in London tied to Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the U.K. Variety has reached out to Massive Attack’s representation for comment. ‘Chimney Town: Frozen in Time’ Sells Wide Across Europe Ahead of Annecy French Premiere (EXCLUSIVE) Berlinale Title ‘Members of the Problematic Family’ to Open Indian Film Festival of Melbourne (EXCLUSIVE) Loading comments... articles.title: Whips & Wilde Vs Webs As ‘I Want Your Sex’ Debuts With ‘Spider-Man’ — Specialty Preview
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Jill Goldsmith Jill Goldsmith Co-Business Editor More Stories By Jill Apple TV Viewership Hit All-Time High In June Quarter; Tough Comps With ‘F1: The Movie’ Slow Growth In Services Tim Cook’s Swan Song At Apple Sees Quarterly IPhone Sales Surge, Highflying Stock Dip Cinemark, Marcus CEOs On Box Office Rebound: Younger Audiences, Longer Windows, Balanced Mix Of Films View All July 31, 2026 2:00pm 'I Want Your Sex' Magnolia Pictures Raunchy comedy I Want Your Sex starring Olivia Wilde as an artsy dominatrix and Cooper Hoffman as her muse is spinning some R-rated counter programming to Spider-Man: Brand New Day . The Gregg Araki film from Magnolia Pictures, which world premiered at Sundance ( see Deadline review ), hits about 700 theaters. Its Rotten Tomatoes Certified Fresh at 91%. Hoffman stars as fresh-faced Elliot who lands his first post-college job with renowned artist, icon and provocateur Erika Tracy (Wilde). His fantasies come true as Erika taps him to become her sexual muse, but he soon finds himself way out of his depth. With Mason Gooding, Chase Sui Wonders, Daveed Diggs, and pop star Charli XCX playing against type as Elliot’s uptight girlfriend. Related Stories News 'Hadestown: The Musical', 'Motor City', Films By Nicolas Winding Refn, Hirokazu Koreeda, More In Indie Rush - Specialty Preview News Sundance Award Winning Doc 'American Pachuco: The Legend of Luis Valdez' Starts Rollout In Rare 'Odyssey' Weekend Debut - Specialty Preview I Want Your Sex played two dozen U.S. festivals after Park City including Seattle, Chicago Critics, NewFest Pride, Provincetown, Frameline and Outfest, and partnered on screenings with Assistants vs. Agents and dating apps Grindr and FEELD, among others. Watch on Deadline Araki joined Charli XCX for a Q&A in L.A. last week that was live streamed globally to YouTube on the day of her new album (Music, Fashion, Film) launch. Janus Films is presenting Kiyoshi Kurosawa’s historical mystery The Samurai And The Prisoner at Film at Lincoln Center and IFC Center in New York and the Landmark Nuart in L.A. Kurosawa will be in NYC for the first time in over a decade for six sold-out Q&As (and for a sold-out special appearance in Toronto next week). The film premiered at Cannes and has grossed nearly $10 million in Japan, a career peak for Kurosawa. Janus will expand it nationally throughout August. The adaptation of Honobu Yonezawa’s 2021 prizewinning novel set in 16th-century Japan follows Lord Murashige Araki (Masahiro Motoki), who finds himself besieged within the walls of his own castle after rising up against the tyrannical Nobunaga Oda (Bando Shingo). Isolated, he is confronted with a series of mysterious crimes that shatter the fragile order of his court. At 95% with RT critics (off 43 reviews). IFC Entertainment is re-releasing Richard Linkatater’s groundbreaking 2014 Boyhood on 110 screens. Filmed over 12 years with the same cast, it stars Ellar Coltrane as Mason, who literally grows up on screen before the audiences’ eyes. Ethan Hawke and Patricia Arquette are his parents and Lorelei Linklater his sister. IFC’s Motor City is sticking around at 600 locations in week 2 (down from 1,600) after a solid opening. Limited release : Yashaddai Owens’ debut feature Jimmy from Strand Releasing, starring Benny O. Arthur as a young James Baldwin arriving in Paris, opens at the IFC Center. In honor of Baldwin’s 102nd birthday, a celebratory screening Sunday (Aug. 1) at 6:30 will be followed by a conversation with the director and filmmaker Barry Jenkins. The impressionistic, black-and-white feature premiered at Telluride in 2024 and the New York Film Festival. Unusual environmental documentary A Paradise Lost by Laurie Sumiye debuts at DCTV Firehouse in NYC for a weeklong run. The film combines animation with live-action footage to explore an unprecedented 1979 legal dispute that saw the rare Palila bird native to Hawaii sue the state to prevent its extinction amidst threats of climate change and fire. During the court case (Palila v. Hawaii) to establish habitat protections for American endangered species, a stuffed Palila sat at the plaintiffs table, and the film from Blooming Ink Pictures is narrated from the bird’s POV. Won the Best Social Justice and Environment Documentary Award at the Festival De Cine Antigua in Guatemala and has also screened at the Hawaii International Film Festival, the DisOrient Asian American Film Festival in Oregon, the Santiago Wild Film Festival in Chile, the EcoFrames Environmental Film Festival in Greece, and the SCINEMA International Science Festival in Australia. Another brave bird: Penny Lane’s Wild Inside about NYC’s beloved owl Flaco opens at the IFC Center via Sandbox Films and HBO Documentary Films. In February of 2023, the male Eurasian eagle-owl, the largest species of owl in the world, was discovered missing from his cage at the Central Park Zoo in Manhattan. articles.title: Wendell Pierce & Erika Woods Break Down Shocking ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Series Penultimate Episode
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Rosy Cordero Rosy Cordero Associate Editor, TV @SocialRosy More Stories By Rosy Wendell Pierce & Erika Woods Break Down Shocking ‘Power Book III: Raising Kanan’ Series Penultimate Episode Dermot Mulroney To Leave ‘Chicago Fire’ Early In Season 15 Rebecca Hall Officially Joins Netflix Series Based On Dan Brown Novel ‘The Secret Of Secrets’ View All July 31, 2026 2:07pm Wendell Pierce & Erika Woods in Power Book III: Raising Kanan' Season 5 Episode 7 Starz SPOILER ALERT: The following reveals major plot points for Starz ’s Power Book III: Raising Kanan Season 5 Episode 7. With only one episode to go for the series finale of the hit Starz crime drama Power Book II: Raising Kanan , there’s no doubt that there are plenty of bodies yet to be piled up. In last night’s episode—the penultimate of the series—fans witnessed the end of three lives that were mostly unexpected. As I reported this morning, following the early season death of Lou (Malcolm Mays), Raising Kanan killed off his brother Marvin (London Brown) in Episode 7. This ending was not fully a surprise, as the character had accepted his fate and had plans put in motion to protect his daughter Jukebox (Hailey Kilgore). Read Brown’s true post-mortem to learn more about what was going on in Marvin’s head and what could’ve been should he have survived . Related Stories News 'Power Book III: Raising Kanan' Says Goodbye To Major Series Character In Season 5: "I Wish We Could've Gotten One More Season" Casting Claire Foy & Matthew Macfadyen To Lead David Nicholls Novel Adaptation 'You Are Here' For BBC & Starz What I didn’t note in that story is that there were two more significant deaths. Last night, we also said goodbye to Snaps ( Wendell Pierce ) and Pop (Erika Woods), two agents of chaos who joined the fold in Season 3. They were murdered by Juke in a surprise twist following the revelation that they were behind Famous’ (Antonio Ortiz) death in Season 4. Watch on Deadline Pierce and Woods spoke to Deadline about Snaps and Pop’s demise, what it’s like playing a couple as a real-life couple, and why it was perfect that they were shot to death by Juke. DEADLINE: What was the initial attraction for you both to play Snaps and Pop? ERIKA WOODS: Getting to work with Wendell Pierce definitely made it very attractive. I mean, duh. [ Laughs ] For me, that was that was first and foremost. And then getting to play someone on the other side of law, since I’ve always played law enforcement. Getting to play someone so devious and delicious and methodical-it was really challenging and, most of all, fun. WENDELL PIERCE: I just wanted to be a part of the world. They are very specific in the way they develop characters and populate the world of the Power universe. That’s a very rare thing. So, any sort of good writing is always attractive. DEADLINE: When I announced your castings, I learned you are a real-life couple. What was it like working together? WOODS: It was really fun and a great learning experience. And just like with any coworker, it was a great collaboration with not just Wendell, but our nephew Breeze [Shameik Moore] and all the other great characters in the universe. It was the icing on the cake. PIERCE: You do the work as normal. You try to be a great collaborator and be there for your scene partner. And since we know each other really well, it really helps develop the characters a little deeper. DEADLINE: One of my favorite elements of this couple was how they dressed and carried themselves. The costumes were all top-notch. Did you enjoy that as well? WOODS: Yes, it was the other character in the universe; our wardrobe, led by Tsigie White, was another collaborator for us. I absolutely loved it. It helped shape our characters. PIERCE: It lets you know who you are. The clothes are just another variable that lets you know who the character is as a part of the character development. And Tsigie is a great designer. Everything was custom. I really think the work that she did is worthy of awards because people always take it for granted that costuming is not easy, especially when it’s a contemporary show. It really is very specific, very inventive, very creative work with different fabrics. We became known for dressing alike and complementing each other so much so that our characters have become one of the leading characters for Halloween. DEADLINE: Did either of you take anything home as a memento? PIERCE: I did. I had such great hats. I took several hats. You know, the red ostrich and brown leather and all of that. So I have a collection of a few of the hats. WOODS: I definitely did take a pair of boots. Really nice vintage boots that I loved. DEADLINE: Focusing on Episode 7, we all say goodbye to Snaps and Pop after Jukebox murders them. Why was she the right person to kill them? WOODS: I think with Juke it was the element of surprise, which I think was perfect, because Kanan [Mekai Curtis] might have been the obvious choice. I think to have Juke and her discretion and being so methodical, we had no idea we were being followed. She outgained us in the end. I thought that was just genius writing, and very well played. PIERCE: Ultimately, when you are in the game, you always have to have your head on a swivel and watch your back. But it’s almost impossible for anyone to be absolutely perfect. With as long as we have been in the game, and as the OGs, we let our guard down. It takes that one moment of indiscretion and relaxation that puts you in jeopardy. That’s the lesson that’s learned. You pay the consequences for the lifestyle that you lead, and as the saying goes, no one gets out of this life alive. DEADLINE: With the loss of Marvin, Snaps, and Pop, how do you think it will affect the game? PIERCE: The thing I love about the Power Universe is we play with time. This was a prequel set before the original Power, and next we’re seeing Origins , how others come on. We spoke for two seasons about Breeze before we even saw him. So there are opportunities to go back and discover how these people got involved in the game, and what made them an OG. There are flashbacks [on the show]. We saw Lou after he was dead, and we saw scenes leading up to his death. There’s still a lot of history about Snaps and Pop that we don’t know. Snap, Crackle, and Pop. Who’s Crackle? DEADLINE: Wait a minute, there’s a Crackle? WOODS: Yep! PIERCE: You’ll have to wait and see. DEADLINE: It has to be DefCon. PIERCE: We’ll have to wait and see. And what was our relationship with DefCon? Who is DefCon? WOODS: Huh? It would be nice to reveal that in Origins , don’t you think, Rosy? I think that would be a very nice reveal because I can neither confirm nor deny. PIERCE: Ultimately, you have to pay the consequences for your actions. So that’s the lesson in what happens to these characters in this episode. What you do in the dark will ultimately come to light, so you best be careful. There, but by the grace of God, go I. What happened to me can also happen to you. DEADLINE: So what you are teasing is that you both could come back as flashbacks in Power: Origins ? PIERCE: Anything is possible. articles.title: ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Post-Credit Scene Explained: What’s Next For Tom Holland’s Peter Parker?
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi All The Songs In ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’: From Tame Impala To Steve Lacy ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Post-Credit Scene Explained: What’s Next For Tom Holland’s Peter Parker? Sadie Sink’s Role In ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Explained View All July 31, 2026 2:46pm Peter Parker/Spider-Man (Tom Holland) works at his desk in Columbia Pictures' SPIDER-MAN™: BRAND NEW DAY. Jay Maidment It looks like Tom Holland ’s spoiler of yore — teasing Spider-Man in space for Avengers: Infinity War (2018) alongside the Guardians of the Galaxy (2014) cast — can take on new meaning with the post-credit scene at the end of Spider-Man: Brand New Day . There is just one short snippet after all of the credits have rolled in the movie, so be prepared to settle in all the way until the songs in the film are listed. Related Stories News Sadie Sink’s Role In ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Explained News Amy Pascal On Tom Holland’s Spider-Man & Tom Hardy’s Venom Crossover: “We Have Hope” The bookend of the film shows Ned’s (Jacob Batalon) Spider-Man tracker app interface with a voice alerting the user to a new location for the webslinger. The mask icon that denotes Spidey’s location on a pixelated GPS map, that looks like older videogames, pinpoints the superhero somewhere in space. The playful post-credit bit is followed by Marvel ’s signature text declaring that Spider-Man will return, but not naming which title he will appear in next. Avengers: Doomsday , coming December 18, 2026, could include him if viewers consider the post-credits scene from Thunderbolts* which also teases the arrival of other superheroes in space. Watch on Deadline Ned (Jacob Batalon) works on his Spidey Tracker in Columbia Pictures SPIDER-MAN™: BRAND NEW DAY. Photo by: Jay Maidment That teaser hinted at the meeting of the New Avengers and The Fantastic Four after Yelena Belova’s (Florence Pugh) iPad runs a threat scan of outer space and alerts her of an unidentified craft, an extradimensional ship, entering the orbit of Earth-616. Viewers of Fantastic Four: The First Steps will recall that the film is set on Earth-828, and the spaceship in the Thunderbolts* post-credit scene looks awfully familiar, so it seems that the quartet will join forces with Avengers and New Avengers, or, jokingly, knockoff Avengerz. The projectile rotates to show its blue-backed number four emblazoned on the side. Furthermore, one post-credit scene of Fantastic Four: The First Steps (2025) teases Dr. Victor von Doom (Robert Downey Jr.) meeting Franklin, Sue Storm (Vanessa Kirby) and Reed Richards’ (Pedro Pascal) baby. This interaction was prefaced by “Four Years Later” in the signature Marvel post-credit text. Sue leaves the couch where she is reading to Franklin to get another book for him, and she returns to see the toddler touching an unmasked Doom’s face, but from an angle that only shows his hooded silhouette, holding the silver mask he usually dons. Back to the Thunderbolts* post-credit scene, a dynamic similar to Captain America: Civil War (2016) could be developing because Yelena, Buckey Barnes (Sebastian Stan), John Walker (Wyatt Russell), Ava Starr aka Ghost (Hannah John-Kamen) and Alexei Shostakov (David Harbour) are lamenting how the new Captain America Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie) is filing for copyright of the name, Avengers vs. their squad, the New Avengers.

articles.title: Ransom Notes Released In Nancy Guthrie Case In Hopes Of Generating New Leads
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Denise Petski Denise Petski Senior Managing Editor More Stories By Denise Ransom Notes Released In Nancy Guthrie Case In Hopes Of Generating New Leads Billie Eilish Concert Film ‘Hit Me Hard And Soft’ Gets Paramount+ Release Date Martha Plimpton & Silvia Dionicio To Return For Season 2 Of HBO’s ‘Task’ View All July 31, 2026 3:15pm Savannah, Nancy Guthrie (inset); Nancy Guthrie's home Feb. 9, in Tucson, Ariz AP/Getty Images Sheriff’s officials have released two ransom notes allegedly sent by those who kidnapped Nancy Guthrie from her Arizona home earlier this year. The Pima County Sheriff’s Department released the notes in hopes of generating new leads in the case. Related Stories News Savannah Guthrie Posts New Video As Authorities Continue Investigation Into Mother’s Disappearance: “We Will Never Give Up On Her” News Savannah Guthrie Speaks On Latest News Of Missing Mother: “We Are In Agony” The first note was sent a day after her disappearance from someone who claimed they have her, and that “she is safe but scared” and would not be released until payment, $4 million in bitcoin, is received, according to the full messages released by the Pima County Sheriff’s Department and the FBI Phoenix Field Office on Friday. The note, addressed to her daughter, Today co-host Savannah Guthrie , said she would be held for a maximum of seven days. The second note, sent Feb. 6 to Tucson news outlet KOLD, states that Guthrie died shortly after she was taken. Watch on Deadline “We did not fully grasp the seriousness of her physical condition,” the note reads. “We never intended to hurt her, that was not our intention. She perished shortly after she was taken. We believe it was heart related. She is buried in nature now. Nothing you could have done could have changed the outcome. We want your family to know this and hope you all can find peace. We are truly sorry.” Investigators believe that someone who knows or has interacted with the writer of the notes — including a friend, family member, co-worker, classmate or acquaintance — may have information that could help identify the person responsible and may have chosen to stay silent because of personal relationships, or safety concerns, and are urging them to come forward. The 84-year-old Guthrie went missing from her home near Tucson early February 1. The FBI has said her disappearance is being investigated as a kidnapping for ransom. Anyone with information is urged to contact 1-800-CALL-FBI (1-800-225-5324). The Guthrie family is also offering a $1 million reward for the return of their mother. articles.title: John Galliano Announced As Subject Of 2027 Met Gala And Costume Institute Exhibition
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Robert Lang Robert Lang Photo Editor/Arts & Culture Writer More Stories By Robert Denis Villeneuve & Vija Celmins Announced as 2026 LACMA Art+Film Gala Honorees ‘Romy And Michele’ Sequel Begins Production With Original Costume Designer Mona May The Frontier Lives On: Why MoMA Is Revisiting Hollywood’s Greatest Westerns View All July 31, 2026 3:25pm Anna Wintour and John Galliano at the Dior fashion show as part of Haute Couture Spring/Summer 2026 held at the Musée Rodin Swan Gallet/PMC The Metropolitan Museum of Art said Friday that John Galliano will be the subject of its landmark spring 2027 Costume Institute exhibition, John Galliano: Horizons , with the annual Met Gala set to celebrate the acclaimed British designer’s influence on fashion while also confronting the controversy that reshaped his career. Related Stories Culture Met Gala 2026 Photos: Best Of The Red Carpet From Beyoncé, Madonna, Rihanna, Sabrina Carpenter And Teyana Taylor To Janelle Monáe Culture Met Gala 2025 Photos: Best Of The Red Carpet Galliano becomes just the third living designer to receive a solo exhibition at The Met, following Yves Saint Laurent in 1983 and Rei Kawakubo of Comme des Garçons in 2017. Opening in spring 2027, the exhibition marks the first major museum retrospective to examine the full breadth of Galliano’s four-decade career, bringing together garments, accessories, sketches, research books, archival materials and toiles that trace his creative evolution from his celebrated 1984 Central Saint Martins graduation collection through his tenures at Givenchy, Christian Dior and Maison Margiela. Drawing extensively from the Costume Institute’s collection — the largest holding of Galliano’s work in the world — the exhibition culminates with his acclaimed Spring/Summer 2024 Maison Margiela Artisanal collection, hailed by many critics as one of the defining couture presentations of the decade. Watch on Deadline John Galliano poses with models during the Christian Dior Haute Couture fashion show for A/W 2009-10 on July 6, 2009, in Paris. Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images Beyond celebrating Galliano’s creative achievements, the exhibition also will directly examine the racist, antisemitic and anti-Asian remarks that led to his dismissal from Christian Dior and his namesake label in 2011, as well as his conviction by a Paris court for public insults based on race, religion, ethnicity or origin. Organizers say the exhibition will explore the relationship between artistic achievement and ethical accountability, rather than presenting a traditional narrative of downfall and redemption. “John Galliano has exerted a profound influence on fashion over the past four decades,” said Max Hollein, The Met’s Marina Kellen French Director and CEO. “His work brings historical inquiry, artistic imagination, theatrical expression and technical experimentation into dynamic relation. Drawing upon the depth of The Costume Institute’s scholarship and the breadth of The Met’s collections, John Galliano: Horizons will offer an expansive examination of his creative practice while attending closely to the historical, cultural and ethical circumstances through which his work is understood.” The exhibition is curated by Andrew Bolton, Curator in Charge of the Costume Institute, who has chronicled Galliano’s career through scholarship and previous exhibitions. Stevie Nicks wore a custom look designed by John Galliano for Zara at The 2026 Met Gala Michael Buckner/Penske Media via Getty Images “Every Galliano collection begins as a journey among things separated by time, place or medium: portrait and posture, silhouette and story, memory and material,” Bolton said. “ Horizons approaches fashion as a form of cartography, mapping not territories but affinities, tensions and transformations. It traces how images become ideas, ideas become material and material becomes emotion. Yet a horizon reveals not only what lies before us but also where we stand.” He added that the exhibition will examine “both how Galliano has remapped the world through fashion and how his conduct, its consequences and changing cultural values have reshaped our understanding of his work.” John Galliano and Charlize Theron attend the Metropolitan Museum of Art Costume Institute Benefit Gala: Anglomania at the Metropolitan Museum of Art on May 1, 2006, in New York City Evan Agostini/Getty Images The exhibition will unfold across three thematic sections. The opening movement, “Bearings,” presents a chronological overview of Galliano’s career while directly addressing the events surrounding his 2010 and 2011 conduct, his dismissal from Dior, his treatment for substance addiction and the continuing evolution of his public legacy. The second gallery, “Horizons,” explores the designer’s enduring inspirations — from history and geography to art, performance and storytelling — revealing how disparate cultural references are transformed into richly imaginative collections. The final section, “Atlas of Transformation,” offers an unprecedented look inside Galliano’s creative process through original research books, sketches, fittings, toiles and finished garments, illustrating how concepts evolve into some of fashion’s most celebrated designs. The exhibition has been organized by Bolton with the assistance of Costume Institute staff Stephanie Kramer and Emily Mushaben, with exhibition design by 1009. John Galliano’s Paris Fashion Week Womenswear Spring/Summer 2016 on October 4, 2015 Pascal Le Segretain/Getty Images As is tradition, John Galliano: Horizons will serve as the centerpiece of the 2027 Met Gala, where the fashion industry’s biggest names are expected to interpret the exhibition’s themes on the museum’s iconic steps. The gala’s official dress code, co-chairs and host committee will be announced at a later date. The announcement follows a string of recent Costume Institute exhibitions spotlighting influential designers and fashion movements, but John Galliano: Horizons is poised to become one of the museum’s most closely watched exhibitions for its willingness to examine both extraordinary artistic innovation and the enduring questions surrounding legacy, accountability and cultural memory. The show will be on view at The Met Fifth Avenue from May 9, 2027-January 9, 2028.
