articles.title: Juliette Lewis On If ‘Cape Fear’s Crystal Or Max Is “More Psychopathic,” Martin Scorsese’s Lasting Support & Season 2 Hopes: “We Will See”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Home Improvement’s Patricia Richardson Reunites With TV Sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Taran Noah Smith: “My Other Boys” ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Is X’s Latest Bootleg Leak, Gets Millions Of Views Before Taken Down Lorde Pauses Lollapalooza Show As Multiple Fans Pass Out View All July 31, 2026 4:25pm Juliette Lewis as Crystal Cady in Apple TV's 'Cape Fear' Apple TV SPOILERS: This post contains details about the Cape Fear , Season 1 finale episode “The Executioners” With another twisty-turny ride down Cape Fear reaching an end, Juliette Lewis was thrilled to have a chance to return to an important title from her youth, from a new perspective. The Oscar-nominated actress, who plays convicted killer Max Cady’s (Javier Bardem) sister Crystal in the Apple TV series, praised series creator Nick Antosca for giving her “so much to play” as a mentally disturbed figure from the sociopathic character’s past. The role comes 35 years after her breakout performance as public defender Sam Bowden’s (Nick Nolte) daughter Danielle in the Martin Scorsese -helmed 1991 feature adaptation of John D. MacDonald’s 1957 novel The Executioners . “But that was what was exciting, is that me coming back would be in a character that goes toe-to-toe with Max Cady, with our new Max Cady, and that they have this deep history, where you don’t know who the lion is and who the mouse is at any given time,” Lewis told Deadline. “And that she really gets under his skin and vice versa.” Watch on Deadline Related Stories News ‘Cape Fear’ Series Creator “Always Wanted” Juliette Lewis To Star In Reboot News Juliette Lewis Makes Surprise ‘Cape Fear’ Cameo After Starring In 1991 Movie — Plus Francesca Scorsese Following their work together on Hulu’s 2019 limited series The Act , Antosca came to Lewis with a “three-page backstory” for the character of Crystal Cady, which Lewis said “was so rich with drama,” including the big twist revealed in Friday’s Season 1 finale episode “The Executioners”. After Max served 17 years for killing his pregnant wife Melissa, whose unborn baby was taken from the scene, his former attorney Anna Bowden (Amy Adams) learns the truth. Crystal (Lewis) escaped from the mental institution where she was committed, killing Melissa and taking the baby to raise as her own. Max Mattern as Luke and Juliette Lewis as Crystal Cady in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ “It’s so funny, because series work is a little bit different than film,” noted Lewis. “You often take a part, and you don’t know what’s coming, and they often don’t wanna tell you because they’re trying to keep these little nuggets secret from online and outward. But Nick, thank God, was such a good collaborator because he told me [from the beginning]. Lewis added, “I need to know because I like to create what it is I’m not showing, and I like to know where we’re going. And so, I knew all the things. I knew how savage she was from the very beginning, but of course I am who I am. I’m not gonna telegraph that. We wanna really make a real kind of psychopath. It’s like who’s more psychopathic, her or Max Cady? You decide.” And although the finale sees Max shoot Crystal and Luke (Max Mattern) and throw them into the hull of a burning boat, without realizing the young man is his own son, Lewis thinks a second season could provide another twist to that storyline. “Well, we will see. I hope to have a second season, because I know a little stuff about the second season,” teased Lewis. “But that’s what’s exciting about Nick, the show creator’s writing. It’s always twists and turns. It’s always to get you going in one direction as an audience and then, jaw-dropping. He really had fun creating that as a noir and a thriller. What’s behind this door? And it’s never what you expect.” Robert De Niro and Juliette Lewis in ‘Cape Fear’ (1991) (MCA/Courtesy Everett Collection) Following her Academy Award-nominated performance in the 1991 movie, which starred Robert De Niro as Max Cady, Lewis has found the experience “so meaningful” for bringing her back to Scorsese, who executive produces the series along with Steven Spielberg. “It’s a piece of my history and my career. It’s sort of my birthplace. It’s like my creative origin story is Cape Fear ,” said Lewis. “And then Scorsese, I consider one of my first and most important teachers. He validated me early on when I was an introvert and I had no articulation of my process, but I had a very strong point of view and instincts, and he knew early on to validate that and give me encouragement where I needed and so that I could be the adventurous, daring performer that I hope people think I am, but that I try to be. And making choices and not playing it safe, that’s because I had a Scorsese early on who gave me encouragement and gave me the floor. I kind of say metaphorically, he gave me the dance floor and the space to create. He didn’t damper these ideas.” Read on about Juliette Lewis’ return to Cape Fear , all episodes of which are now available to stream on Apple TV+ . DEADLINE: I really enjoyed the character of Crystal Cady and what she adds to the Cape Fear story that has been told multiple times now. JULIETTE LEWIS: Oh, thanks. DEADLINE: Tell me about how Nick [Antosca] approached you for the role and how it came full circle from your last time in Cape Fear . LEWIS: It was really amazing because I had worked with Nick [on Hulu’s The Act ]. We wanted to do something together. We had a general meeting and he pitched the idea … “I’m thinking about doing Cape Fear , but as a series. And I have some strong ideas about it.” And I was intrigued. That was pre-pandemic, I think 2019. It went away, and then I saw Amy Adams’ name and Javier Bardem attached. And because Hollywood can sometimes be a brutal place, I thought the ship had sailed without me. And so, I was like, “Oh gosh, should I reach out to Nick to say, hey, you remember the meeting we had, and you actually said you wanted me to be a part of it?” Anyway, two days later, he gave me an offer. He said, “No, I was keeping it a surprise. I was about to offer you this role.” And he had about a three-page backstory. The backstory was so rich with drama, and there was just so much to play. Even if you’re given a sentence, when you have such a strongly written backstory in a series, it makes the creation of a character really easy, because normally in series, you don’t. You just get one script and then some idea, but Nick is so thorough in his character development, and so that’s what’s exciting about working with him. But the short story is, I thought I wasn’t a part of it, and Nick had a part for me all along, and he kept his word. And he’s so smart, because I think people were really excited by my involvement. Juliette Lewis in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ (Hopper Stone/Apple TV+/Courtesy Everett Collection) DEADLINE: Tell me about reuniting with Martin Scorsese as the executive producer now. Did that bring up any memories from working on the movie? LEWIS: The whole thing is so meaningful for me because it’s a piece of my history and my career. It’s sort of my birthplace. It’s like my creative origin story is Cape Fear . When I became worldwide, people knew of me in this way on a global scale. You know, luck of the draw, I had no idea that that’s the impact it would have. And then Scorsese, I consider one of my first and most important teachers. He validated me early on when I was an introvert and I had no articulation of my process, but I had a very strong point of view and instincts, and he knew early on to validate that and give me encouragement where I needed and so that I could be the adventurous, daring performer that I hope people think I am, but that I try to be. And making choices and not playing it safe, that’s because I had a Scorsese early on who gave me encouragement and gave me the floor. I kind of say metaphorically, he gave me the dance floor and the space to create. He didn’t damper these ideas, because a lot of times early on, some people you work with, they just want a robot. And I was fortunate enough to work with the auteurs of American cinema who really validated my voice. And so, I always come to the table, trying to bring it something fully realized. But anyway, the short story is to say, gosh, it’s so important that that Scorsese gave it his blessing. I wasn’t on the table read, because I came in a few episodes later, but I’ll be seeing him shortly. I’ve seen him over the years. DEADLINE: Like you said, Crystal is just such a well fleshed-out character, and she’s really so fun to watch and kind of unsettling. Tell me about her dynamic with Max, that weird sibling dynamic and the effect she has over him. What it was like working with Javier on that? LEWIS: I’m so glad that reads. I haven’t seen the series, so I don’t know ever what edit they use and stuff. I’ve only heard about it, so people are telling me what we intended happened. But that was what was exciting, is that me coming back would be in a character that goes toe-to-toe with Max Cady, with our new Max Cady, and that they have this deep history, where you don’t know who the lion is and who the mouse is at any given time. And that she really gets under his skin and vice versa. And then also just on a pathology point, I was intrigued by playing a stalker, like stalker energy, obsession, obsessiveness—but they don’t know. They think they’re justified in everything they’re doing. She would never think she’s a stalker or somebody who’s obsessed. She’s just doing what she thinks is right and what is necessary. People don’t speak about acting this way, but I speak of it that it’s energy work, like I’m an energy worker, and what I mean by that is I’m conjuring energy. So that’s why some of my roles, I want people to feel it on a visceral level. But even when she comes in the first scene and she shows up at the bar where [Max] is sitting, and then they go in the cigar room, he brings her there. But even to show up, I wanted to have such a strong energy that’s so intimidating, but it’s veiled by, “I wouldn’t hurt anybody. I’m so sweet.” You know, sweetness and light. So, I love that dichotomy. I love the friction of the contradiction of what you show and what you conceal. It’s really exciting in character work for me. DEADLINE: Yeah, it was really fun to watch as well. Juliette Lewis in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ (2026) Apple TV LEWIS: But just to experience Javier as Max Cady—my first scene with him was when I saw him on the sidewalk, and I’m in the green coat. And He was just so exciting. He’s all the things. He’s all the things you want from a Max Cady, seductive, charismatic, dangerous and enticing. DEADLINE: Yeah, he’s always fun to watch as a bad guy, but he seems very sweet and charming in real life. LEWIS: Well, that’s the thing is, he really has a gift. Because I was in scenes, one inch apart, and when he puts that veil over his eyes, a veil of darkness, it’s something to behold. It’s really powerful, and so it was really exciting for me to work with him. We both respect each other so much, and we could just dance, metaphorically speaking. The couple scenes we have that are super intimate, almost face to face, just a half inch apart, it’s pretty electric. I hope it came off exciting. DEADLINE: Oh yeah, absolutely. And one part that I was really struck by was the reveal that Crystal killed Melissa and stole the baby. What was your reaction to first reading that? LEWIS: It’s so funny, because series work is a little bit different than film. You often take a part, and you don’t know what’s coming, and they often don’t wanna tell you because they’re trying to keep these little nuggets secret from online and outward. But Nick, thank God, was such a good collaborator because he told me. I need to know because I like to create what it is I’m not showing, and I like to know where we’re going. And so, I knew all the things. I knew how savage she was from the very beginning, but of course I am who I am. I’m not gonna telegraph that. We wanna really make a real kind of psychopath. It’s like who’s more psychopathic, her or Max Cady? You decide. Juliette Lewis in Apple TV’s ‘Cape Fear’ DEADLINE: Yeah, and it was also just tragic finding out that he killed Adam after he was so heartbroken that he had lost him in the first place. LEWIS: Well, we will see. I hope to have a second season, because I know a little stuff about the second season. But that’s what’s exciting about Nick, the show creator’s writing. It’s always twists and turns. It’s always to get you going in one direction as an audience and then, jaw dropping. He really had fun creating that as a noir and a thriller. What’s behind this door? And it’s never what you expect. DEADLINE: Well, that’s exciting to hear because honestly, when Max threw them down below the boat, I could tell they weren’t totally dead yet, so they could have gotten out of that fire. LEWIS: Yeah, exactly. articles.title: FIFA Scraps Controversial Plan To Turn World Cup Into Commercial Enterprise
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Patrick Hipes Patrick Hipes Executive Managing Editor More Stories By Patrick Tournament Of Roses Organization And Its Rose Parade Sign With UTA Movie Academy Re-Elects Lynette Howell Taylor As President Michael J. Fox To Receive TV Academy’s Bob Hope Humanitarian Award At This Year’s Emmys View All July 31, 2026 6:20pm FIFA president Gianni Infantino Getty Images FIFA on Friday said it would not move forward with a plan to create a $20 billion commercial arm of soccer’s world governing body by selling stakes in the World Cup and other events to private investors. The proposal had been met by a wave of criticism by several soccer confederations from the time it was proposed just days ago, with major groups repping Europe, Asia and the Americas condemning the plan that would have radically restructured the global non-profit organization. Related Stories Sports FIFA Set To Lose Vote Over Controversial Private Investment Plan After Europe, Asia & Americas Reject Proposal News Donald Trump, As Expected, Awarded New FIFA Peace Prize At World Cup Draw “Having listened carefully to all the views, it has become clear that the project has created divisions of a nature that, regardless of the level of support, are no longer in the interest of the objective set out in the first place,” FIFA president Gianni Infantino said in a statement released Friday evening. “Our purpose has always been — and will always be — to unite and improve. As a result, this proposal will not proceed.” Watch on Deadline Statement attributable to the FIFA President The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed. And more so, as we said… — FIFA Media (@fifamedia) July 31, 2026 The plan, which Infantino announced Tuesday and contingent on a member vote, came on the heels of the summer’s wildly profitable 2026 FIFA World Cup hosted by the U.S., Mexico and Canada. The proposal would have created a commercial arm called FIFA Forward Enterprise, which was being valued at $20 billion. FFE would operate the commercial side of the sport as a dedicated business, with profits shared with member associations like UEFA (Europe), CONCACAF (the Americas, which includes the U.S.) and Asia (the AFC). The World Cup is not a commercial enterprise, but FFE would allow it to be exploited by private investors. FIFA had said it would be the controlling shareholder, but that it had hoped to raise $4.2 billion by “carefully selecting long-term investors who will purchase minority, non-controlling interests.” Thrive Capital, an investment firm led by Joshua Kushner, the brother of President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner, was among the investors approached, per reports. Reactions to commercializing the men’s and women’s World Cups and other major tournaments like the Club World Cup were swift. UEFA — home to World Cup winner Spain as well as semifinalists England and France and six of the eight quarterfinalists — said all 55 of its member states will boycott the World Cup if FIFA enacted the plan to sell stakes in the tournament to private investors. “The World Cup cannot be treated as an investment product. It is one of football’s greatest sporting legacies,” it wrote after its membership voted in an emergency meeting Thursday. “It has been built over generations by players, national teams and supporters across every continent. No part of it should ever be surrendered to private investors. The World Cup is not for sale.” CONCACAF and its 41 members also formally opposed the plan Thursday, questioning “the need for private equity investment to fund new and existing FIFA Forward programs following the most profitable FIFA World Cup in history.” The AFC joined in opposition earlier today. The number of countries in the three federations is more than 140, well above the majority needed to reject the plan required ratification. “The FIFA Forward Enterprise project was intended to provide a basis for further strengthening our FIFA Member Associations and our sport worldwide, especially in those countries where support is most needed,” FIFA said in its statement tonight. “And more so, as we said from the outset, to do this only if a majority of the FIFA Member Associations were in support and always subject to a consultation process with them, the FIFA Council, the Confederations and wider stakeholders.” It added: “Moving forward, my intent is to bring all interested parties back together in the coming days and weeks in the spirit of shared interest in our game, and with the objective to continue growing football everywhere, particularly in those countries that mostly need our support.” The next major tournament on the FIFA schedule is the 2027 Women’s World Cup next summer in Brazil. The next men’s World Cup is in 2030 co-hosted by Spain, Portugal and Morocco. articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Home Improvement’s Patricia Richardson Reunites With TV Sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Taran Noah Smith: “My Other Boys” ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Is X’s Latest Bootleg Leak, Gets Millions Of Views Before Taken Down Lorde Pauses Lollapalooza Show As Multiple Fans Pass Out View All July 31, 2026 6:32pm 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Courtesy of Sony Pictures As Tom Holland’s summer blockbusters take over the big screen, X has spoiled yet another one of the actor’s theatrical releases. Following the leak of a high-quality bootleg of The Odyssey on X last week, Spider-Man: Brand New Day was leaked Friday morning on the Elon Musk-owned social media platform, with the movie reaching millions of accounts before it was taken down later that day. Deadline has reached out to Sony for comment. Despite the brief leak, Friday marked a record-breaking opening day for the Sony/Marvel Studios sequel, projected for $167M-$173M, which bests Avengers: Endgame ‘s $157.4M opening day in 2019. Watch on Deadline The latest leak comes after a high-quality bootleg of The Odyssey made its way to X last weekend, also garnering millions of views before Universal took action and “immediately initiated takedown protocols.” Since buying Twitter and rebranding it as X in 2022, Musk has allowed X Premium subscribers to share videos up to four hours long, making it possible for users to release entire pirated feature films. articles.title: ‘Home Improvement’s Patricia Richardson Reunites With TV Sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Taran Noah Smith: “My Other Boys”
articles.full_text: Skip to main content Dismiss News Banner Breaking News 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' Sets All-Time First-Day High With $167M+ U.S., Could Beat 'Avengers: Endgame' $357M Weekend Record Read the full story By Glenn Garner Glenn Garner Associate Editor @xoxo_glenn More Stories By Glenn ‘Home Improvement’s Patricia Richardson Reunites With TV Sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas, Taran Noah Smith: “My Other Boys” ‘Spider-Man: Brand New Day’ Is X’s Latest Bootleg Leak, Gets Millions Of Views Before Taken Down Lorde Pauses Lollapalooza Show As Multiple Fans Pass Out View All July 31, 2026 8:06pm Zachery Ty Bryan, Patricia Richardson, Taran Noah Smith, Tim Allen and Jonathan Taylor Thomas in 'Home Improvement' Bob D'Amico/Touchstone Television/Courtesy Everett Collection Although any hopes of an onscreen reunion might be pointless, the cast of Home Improvement appears to be keeping close in real life. Patricia Richardson , who starred as matriarch Jill Taylor in the ABC sitcom for its eight-season run from 1991 to 1999, reunited with her onscreen sons Jonathan Taylor Thomas and Taran Noah Smith this week. “My other boys,” Richardson captioned a selfie with Thomas and Smith, who played sons Randy and Mark, alongside Zachery Ty Bryan as oldest boy Brad. Related Stories News Tim Allen Says ‘Home Improvement’ Reboot Is “Stuck” Because Of Onscreen Sons’ “Personality Problems” Casting ‘Home Improvement’ Reboot Not Right For Patricia Richardson The reunion comes after their former TV dad Tim Allen said a potential reboot is stuck due to “ personality problems ” with the actors who starred as the sons. Watch on Deadline “They keep talking about how it could move forward, but they get stuck [because] there are some personality problems right now with the boys,” Allen told Us Weekly in June. “They’ve got their own issues. I always thought it would be cool if it was a story about them. That’s a little challenging right now, to put it mildly.” View this post on Instagram While Richardson has noted that Thomas and Smith no longer act , Bryan is currently serving 16 months in a California prison, due to several probation violations, following multiple DUIs and a domestic violence charge. Richardson said “it was so weird” hearing Allen say in the press that the cast was all onboard for the reboot, despite him never coming to her, noting she “would not want to” return regardless.
